sections.heading: Reading your child's school before you buy anything
paragraphs: Three questions about the school will tell you more about what tutoring should do than any conversation with a tutor. The first is who teaches the course and what their subject background is. A computer science specialist teaching Digital Society produces technically confident students who write thin contextual analysis; a humanities specialist produces the opposite. The gap you need filled is whichever one the school is not covering.

The second is how the cohort is sized and timetabled. A class of three in an awkward option block gets less practice, less peer comparison and fewer marked pieces than a class of eighteen, simply because of how teaching time works. Those students need the tutor to act as a second teacher rather than as a top-up, and the honest version of that plan is more sessions, not the same number with more enthusiasm.

The third is the school's own deadline structure for the inquiry project. The internal deadlines are set by the school, not by the IB, and they usually sit weeks earlier than the IB's own upload dates so teachers have marking time. Families regularly come to us two weeks before an internal deadline expecting project support and discover there is no time left for the choice that actually determines the mark.

A note on the regulator, because parents ask what it covers. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which also publishes inspection outcomes; in Dubai that function sits with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, in Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. A school's published inspection rating tells you about the institution. It tells you nothing about one small option subject, which is why the three questions above are better value than the report.

sections.heading: Honesty rules in a course about artificial intelligence
paragraphs: Digital Society is the only Diploma subject where students study generative artificial intelligence as content and are simultaneously tempted to use it as a shortcut on the assessed work. That tension needs a plain answer rather than a nervous one. The inquiry project must be the student's own work. Using a generative tool to produce text, analysis or structure that is then submitted as the student's own is academic malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the tutor who suggested it.

Where such tools are legitimately useful, the condition is disclosure and the school's own policy. Most schools in Abu Dhabi now publish one, and it is normally more restrictive than students assume. A tutor's job here is to be clear about the boundary rather than vague: teach the skill, discuss the context, challenge the question, give written feedback on the student's draft, and leave the production of the work to the student. We keep a record of what was reviewed and what was advised, which protects the student if the question is ever raised.

The same honesty applies to the tutoring market itself. Services selling finished IB coursework exist in this market and advertise openly; our own competitor research found one offering completed internal assessments at a fixed price. What is being sold there is a malpractice finding with a receipt attached, and it can cost a student the whole Diploma.

On permits, the position is checkable. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat quoted figures with caution. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules also bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which rules out the arrangement families most often think of first.

faqs.question: How can we judge a Digital Society predicted grade when the course is this new?
faqs.answer: By getting a second, consistent reading. With few cohorts behind the subject and sometimes only three or four students in a class, a school's internal mark is an estimate rather than a position in a distribution. What helps is one external marker who marks the same student's timed writing against the published command terms, repeatedly, over several weeks. That produces a trend rather than a snapshot, and a trend is what you can take back to the school in March if you think the prediction is wrong. A single second opinion on a single piece of work is almost as uninformative as the original.

faqs.question: My son is excellent with technology but stuck on a 4 in Digital Society. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the course does not award marks for knowing how systems work. It awards them for making a claim about a digital system in a named context, supporting it with specific evidence, and following the consequences for identifiable stakeholders. Technically fluent students write detailed explanations and then stop, which satisfies the content and leaves the concept and context unaddressed. The fix is structural rather than intellectual: name the concept, locate it in a real context, use the technical material as evidence in as few words as the claim needs. Most students apply that within three or four marked answers.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi systems make good inquiry project contexts?
faqs.answer: Ones your child can observe directly. The emirate's unified government services platform, the automatic number-plate toll system on the approaches to the island, the smart parking scheme, autonomous vehicle trials that have run on Yas Island, the technology cluster on Al Maryah Island and the low-carbon district at Masdar City are all digital systems with named stakeholders and published information. The reason to prefer them over a global platform is evidence quality: a student can describe the real interface, the real friction and the real data being collected, and supported specifics are what the criteria reward.

faqs.question: What is the Higher Level extension in Digital Society, and how is it practised?
faqs.answer: It asks students to analyse challenges in digital society and the interventions proposed to address them. The common failure is writing an opinion piece. What earns marks is treating an intervention as an object of analysis: naming it and whoever proposed it, stating a claim about its effect, giving evidence with a source and a date, and tracing the consequences for named stakeholders. Because it is a habit rather than a body of content, it needs short repeated practice over weeks and cannot be revised the weekend before. We run it as its own strand with separate marking from about ten weeks out.

faqs.question: Is Digital Society the right choice if my daughter wants to study computer science at university?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. Digital Society is a Group 3 individuals and societies course about the effects of digital systems; Computer Science is the Group 4 course where students program and build. Many engineering and computing degrees want mathematics and a science, and some name Computer Science specifically. Check the published entry requirements of the universities on her list, including the UAE institutions, before choosing. Taking both is possible in some Abu Dhabi timetables and is a strong combination for anything involving technology policy, product work or law. Treat admissions pages as the authority, not general advice.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Digital Society inquiry project without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may teach what the criteria reward, discuss candidate contexts, challenge a question that is too broad to support, explain how evidence should be sourced, and give written feedback on a draft the student has produced. A tutor may not supply the investigation, rewrite passages into their own prose, or hand over a structure with content filled in. The student must write their own project. We keep a record of what the tutor reviewed and advised, which is useful if the school ever asks how the work was supported, and it is the only version of coursework support that is safe for the student.

faqs.question: Can my child use AI tools while studying a Diploma course about AI?
faqs.answer: For learning, within the school's own published policy and with disclosure where required. For producing assessed work, no. Submitting text, analysis or structure generated by a tool as the student's own is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student. Most Abu Dhabi schools now publish an AI policy and it is usually stricter than students assume, so read the school's version rather than relying on general advice. A tutor should be explicit about this boundary rather than vague, and should be teaching the student to produce the reasoning themselves, which is the thing the examination will test anyway.

faqs.question: There are hardly any past papers. What will my child practise on?
faqs.answer: A practice bank built for the purpose. Four sources do the work: the school's own assessments, which match the teacher who sets the prediction; released and specimen material, used sparingly because there is little of it; questions written to the published command terms, which give volume and let a tutor target one weak concept; and current reporting on digital systems, which supplies unseen stimulus. The student's own project context can also be re-examined through different concepts to produce a dozen distinct questions. Everything written is marked against the criteria rather than compared to a nonexistent archive of boundaries.

faqs.question: Does the teacher's subject background change what tutoring we need?
faqs.answer: Significantly, and it is worth asking the school. A computer science specialist teaching Digital Society tends to produce students with strong technical explanation and thin contextual analysis; a humanities specialist tends to produce the reverse. The gap you are buying support for is whichever side the school is not covering, and a tutor who diagnoses that in the first session saves a term of generic revision. It also tells you what kind of practice to prioritise: concept and context work for the technically strong, content precision for the strong writers.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a stalled inquiry project usually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect, if the problem is the question, and many more if the problem is the evidence. A project stuck because the question is too broad can often be rescued in two or three sessions, since narrowing a question is a single skill applied once. A project where the student has written at length on a context they cannot get evidence for is a harder rebuild, because the work already done may not be reusable. That asymmetry is the argument for spending on the choice of context early rather than on polishing late.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around Abu Dhabi school hours and the Ramadan timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the Ramadan question should be settled before the month begins. School hours shorten and evenings restructure around Iftar, so a 5pm slot stops working; sessions typically move to post-Iftar times from around 8.30pm, or to weekend mornings for timed papers needing an uninterrupted stretch. Since Ramadan currently falls inside the revision term for the May session, this affects the most valuable weeks of the year. Families who agree new timing in advance keep their rhythm; the ones who improvise usually lose several weeks of the best revision time available.

faqs.question: Why is online better than finding somebody near Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: Because the binding constraint in this subject is scarcity, not distance. Very few teachers in the Gulf have taken Digital Society cohorts through to examination, and searching within a short drive narrows the pool to whoever lives nearby, usually a generalist. Online matching keeps the specialism and removes travel from both the price and the calendar, which is what makes a 7.30pm midweek slot possible at all. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE homes; every lesson here runs live over video, one-to-one, with screen sharing for stimulus material and marked work.

faqs.question: Does an online Digital Society tutor need a UAE tutoring permit?
faqs.answer: If they are tutoring from inside the UAE, yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any figure quoted to you is speculation. It is a reasonable question to ask any tutor, and the MoHRE service page sets out how the permit is applied for.

faqs.question: My child's school has only three Digital Society students. Can tutoring carry the course?
faqs.answer: It can carry most of the teaching, provided the plan is honest about the hours. A very small cohort in an awkward option block gets less practice, fewer marked pieces and no peer comparison, so the tutor has to sequence content, set and test reading and mark regularly, rather than top up a well-taught course. That is more sessions than a support arrangement, not the same number delivered harder. Registration, internal deadlines and submission stay with the school, so ask the coordinator for the project deadline structure before the first session.

That is what the free trial lesson is for, and it happens before any payment. Send a timed answer, a class piece and the current predicted grade, tell us whether the papers or the inquiry project is the worry, and we will match an Abu Dhabi student with a Digital Society specialist for live one-to-one online lessons in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: A new subject, no revision shelf, and what that means for a parent
paragraphs: Digital Society replaced Information Technology in a Global Society and was first examined in 2024. That single fact changes what tutoring in this subject is for. In Mathematics or Chemistry, a parent buys explanation of settled content against a decade of published resources. Here there is no decade. There are few workbooks, little accumulated exemplar material, and in many schools a first or second cohort whose teacher is learning the assessment alongside them. What a family is actually buying is a method for generating the student's own material and a reader who knows what the marks reward.

The subject is built on three interlocking things. Concepts, including change, identity, power, space, systems, expression, and values and ethics, are the analytical lenses. Content areas, running from data and algorithms through computers, networks, media, artificial intelligence and autonomous technologies, are the technical substance. Contexts, including cultural, economic, environmental, health, political and social, are where the two meet in the real world. Every question in the subject is some combination of the three, and an answer that names none of them is an opinion piece.

That structure makes the assessment unusually predictable once a student sees it. A question will give a scenario and ask for analysis, and the moves are always the same: identify the content area involved, choose the concept that illuminates it, locate the context in which the impact lands, bring a real-world example with a date and a source, and then weigh the claim. Students who learn that sequence stop being at the mercy of whichever topic comes up, because the sequence works on any of them.

The real-world example is the part parents rarely hear about and the part that decides grades. Digital Society is assessed on analysis of actual developments, which means a student needs a stock of examples they can describe accurately, date, and attribute. Nobody can revise that from a textbook, because the examples are current. The practical answer is a file, built from the first week of DP1 and added to weekly: the development, the date, the source, the content area, the concept, the context, the contested claim. That file is the revision material, and a tutor's main job is to make it exist.

Lessons for UAE families run live online, one to one, with a shared screen. There are no home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. In this subject the format is almost the point. The material under discussion is on a screen anyway: a policy document, a dataset, a platform interface, a news report with a date on it. The tutor and student annotate the same artefact, and the annotated version goes into the example file rather than into a notebook that gets lost.

programmes.description: Assessed by written papers drawing on the concepts, content and contexts framework, an internally assessed inquiry project on a question of the student's own choosing, and at Higher Level an additional component based on pre-released material about a digital challenge. The subject rewards analysis of real developments rather than technical skill.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools introduced this course recently, so a number of local students are in a first or second cohort. The practical consequence is a shortage of marked exemplars inside the school, which is exactly the gap that makes external marked feedback valuable here in a way it is not in a long-established subject.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP design and individuals and societies both feed this course: design supplies comfort with systems and prototyping, individuals and societies supplies the habit of investigating an issue from several perspectives. Neither requires a student to attribute a current example to a dated source, which is the discipline Digital Society grades.
programmes.countryNote: Students coming through an Abu Dhabi MYP cohort usually arrive technically confident and analytically loose. They can explain how a recommendation algorithm works and will write about its effects without naming a single real platform, policy or date. The first few sessions are spent converting general knowledge into sourced, specific evidence.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students taking Digital Society as a Diploma course sit identical components, and the career-related study often connects directly: a student on a business or technology pathway encounters the same questions about data, automation and platforms in a workplace setting.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, CP students with placements in technology or government-services organisations have unusually good access to primary material for the inquiry project. The caution is confidentiality: anything used in an assessed report must be publicly available or cleared, and that needs checking with the school rather than assumed.

programmes.name: Extended Essay in Digital Society
programmes.description: A 4,000-word investigation of a digital-society question. The subject-specific risk is choosing something so current that the only available literature is reporting, leaving the student with no scholarship to engage and no settled analysis to test their own argument against.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi students have strong local material here, from government digital services to the emirate's artificial intelligence research institutions, and much of it is documented in published policy. Supervision from a tutor is coaching and feedback on drafts the student has written; no part of the submitted text comes from anybody else.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-digital-society-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the components and neighbouring courses Abu Dhabi families raise alongside Digital Society, with the specific demand each one makes.

subjects.name: Concepts
subjects.levels: HL and SL, throughout the course
subjects.description: Change, identity, power, space, systems, expression, and values and ethics, used as analytical lenses rather than as topics. An answer that applies a concept consistently to a real example reaches the upper bands; an answer that mentions the concept in the opening line and abandons it does not.

subjects.name: Content areas
subjects.description: Data, algorithms, computers, networks and the internet, media, artificial intelligence, and robots and autonomous technologies. Enough technical accuracy is required to describe how something works; the marks are for what follows from how it works, not for the description itself.

subjects.name: Contexts
subjects.description: Cultural, economic, environmental, health, human knowledge, political and social settings in which digital developments land. Students often analyse an impact without locating it in a context, which makes the analysis generic and caps the mark.

subjects.name: Inquiry project
subjects.description: The student poses a real-world question, investigates it with sources, and reports the findings within a tight word limit, supported by selected material. The commonest loss is a question too broad to answer with the evidence actually gathered.

subjects.name: Higher Level extension
subjects.description: An additional component built on material released before the examination about a digital challenge and possible interventions. Because the material is known in advance, preparation is a research task rather than a revision task, and students who treat it as the latter are underprepared.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Frequently confused with Digital Society by families choosing options. Computer Science assesses programming and computational thinking; Digital Society assesses analysis of digital developments in society. A student who wants to build systems should take the former.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Overlaps usefully on platforms, data as an asset and automation in operations. The distinction to maintain is that Business wants a recommendation for an organisation, while Digital Society wants an analysis of impact across stakeholders and contexts.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Supplies the vocabulary for analysing platform markets, network effects and the economics of data. Students taking both write stronger answers on the economic context, provided they resist importing diagrams into a Digital Society answer.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Digital Society supplies some of the best available TOK material on technology, knowledge and the reliability of digitally mediated information. The human knowledge context in this subject and the TOK essay reinforce each other directly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Helps substantially with the data content area, because a student who can read a distribution and a correlation can interrogate a claim made from a dataset rather than accepting it. Useful preparation for the evidence handling the inquiry project requires.

sections.heading: What a new subject means in practice, and what to buy instead of a revision guide
paragraphs: Digital Society was first examined in 2024, which puts it in a different category from every other Group 3 option. The accumulated apparatus that surrounds an established subject does not yet exist in the same depth: few workbooks, limited exemplar material in circulation, and in many schools a department teaching its first or second cohort. None of that reflects on the teaching. It describes an information gap, and a family deciding how to spend money on support should understand where that gap actually is.

It is not in explanation. Most students understand how a recommendation system or a data broker works, often better than the adults around them. The gap is in evidence and in structure: a stock of real developments the student can describe accurately with a date and a source, and a reliable sequence for turning one of those into an analysis the mark scheme recognises. Neither can be bought as a product. Both can be built, week by week, and that is the honest description of what tutoring in this subject does.

The table below sets out what does and does not exist for a student in this subject, because it changes what a parent should ask for. A tutor offering to work through a revision guide has misunderstood the course. A tutor who asks in the first session what is already in the student's example file, and how it is organised, has understood it exactly. The same question is worth putting to the school: how many cohorts have sat the subject, and is there any marked work from a previous year that current students can see.

sections.heading: Concepts, content and contexts: the sequence that answers any question
paragraphs: The framework is the subject's best feature, because it makes the assessment predictable. A question presents a scenario and asks for analysis or evaluation. The reliable sequence is five steps: name the content area involved, choose the concept that illuminates what is at stake, locate the context in which the consequences land, attach a real example with a date and a source, and then weigh the claim against an alternative reading. Done in that order, the answer has a shape before the student has decided what to say.

Most lost marks come from skipping steps two and three. A student writes competently about how facial recognition works, asserts that it raises privacy issues, and stops. The concept of power is doing no work in that answer, and no context has been chosen, so the analysis is generic enough to apply anywhere. The same material, routed through the power concept in a specified political or health context, with one dated example, reaches a different band entirely.

The fifth step, weighing against an alternative reading, is what separates evaluation from description. Digital developments almost always distribute benefits and costs unevenly, and an answer that identifies who gains, who bears the cost, and what the trade-off is being made for will outscore an answer that is simply critical. Students arrive with strong instincts about technology, often negative ones, and the instinct is less useful than the analysis. The table below maps the recurring combinations so a student can see what a well-formed question looks like.

sections.heading: The example file: the revision resource the subject does not sell you
paragraphs: This is the practical core of the page. Because Digital Society is assessed on analysis of actual developments, a student needs examples they can state accurately, date, and attribute to a source. There is no book of these, because by the time one is printed the examples are old. The working solution is a file maintained from the first weeks of DP1, with a fixed entry format, reviewed for coverage rather than volume. Students who have one walk into the examination with material; students who do not rely on whatever they can half-remember.

The entry format matters more than the tool used to keep it. Each entry records the development, the date it happened, the source where it was documented, the content area it belongs to, the concept it illustrates, the context in which the impact landed, and the claim that is actually contested about it. That last field is the one students omit and the one that makes the entry usable, because an example without a contested claim attached is a fact rather than evidence.

Coverage is checked periodically against the framework rather than the calendar. A file with fourteen entries about artificial intelligence and none about networks or media is a file that will fail on half the paper. Every few weeks the file is read against the content areas and contexts to expose the gaps, and the next fortnight's additions are chosen to fill them. That is unglamorous work and it is the single highest-return habit available in this subject, which is why it occupies part of every session rather than being set as homework and forgotten.
bullets: Fixed entry format: development, date, source, content area, concept, context, contested claim

sections.heading: The inquiry project: your own question, and a word limit that punishes breadth
paragraphs: The internally assessed component asks the student to pose a real-world question, investigate it using sources, and report what they found within a tight word limit, supported by selected material. The current limit is in the region of 1,200 words of report; confirm the exact figure and the current criteria with your child's teacher, because this subject is new enough that documentation is still bedding in and a stale number here would be actively harmful.

Two failures dominate. The first is a question too broad for the evidence a student can actually gather, such as asking whether artificial intelligence is good for employment. No report of this length can answer that, so the result is a summary of other people's opinions. A workable question is specific about the technology, the setting and the group affected, and it is answerable from sources the student has in hand before they commit to it. Testing the question against the available evidence is the decisive hour in this component.

The second is treating the word limit as a constraint on the findings rather than on the description. Students spend their count explaining how the technology works, which they know well, and arrive at the analysis with a few hundred words left. The mark is for the investigation and what is concluded from it. A word budget set before drafting, with description kept to the minimum the argument needs, is the practical control. Feedback from a tutor is comment on drafts the student has written, naming the criterion; no portion of the submitted report comes from anybody else.
bullets: Be specific about the technology, the setting and the affected group
Test the question against sources you already hold before committing
Keep description minimal; the marks are in the investigation and conclusions
Confirm the current word limit and criteria with your child's teacher

sections.heading: Higher Level: the pre-released challenge is a research task
paragraphs: Higher Level candidates sit an additional component built on material the IB releases ahead of the session, concerning a digital challenge and the interventions that might address it. Because the material is known in advance, this component behaves unlike any other examination on the Diploma. It cannot be revised in the usual sense and it can be prepared almost completely, which makes it the best value for preparation time in the whole subject.

The preparation is a mapping exercise. Who are the stakeholders in this challenge, and what does each of them want. What interventions are available, and who proposes them. What does each intervention cost, who bears that cost, and what is the evidence that it works. Where do the interventions conflict with each other. A student who has that map, with sources attached, can write about the challenge from any angle the paper takes.

Two things go wrong. Students read the pre-released material, find it interesting, and do no research around it, arriving with the content but no evidence. Or they research extensively and never write to time, so the first timed attempt happens in the examination. The sequence that works is research first, then the map, then timed writing against several possible question framings. Three timed attempts on different framings is usually enough, and they should happen weeks rather than days before the session.

There is a scheduling implication for families. The release date is set by the IB and communicated through the school, so the preparation window is fixed and known in advance rather than negotiable. Booking support for this component after the window has opened wastes part of it, because the research has to come before the writing. Ask the Diploma coordinator when the material is expected, count back six to eight weeks from the session, and place the sessions inside that stretch rather than in the general run-up to examinations.
bullets: Known material means the component can be prepared almost entirely
Map stakeholders, interventions, costs and conflicts, with sources attached
Research first, then write to time on several possible framings
Three timed attempts, weeks before the session rather than days

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi as documented digital-society material
paragraphs: Examples drawn from the student's own setting mark better than examples borrowed from elsewhere, provided they are documented rather than observed. Abu Dhabi supplies several that are. The UAE appointed a minister of state for artificial intelligence in 2017, which is a verifiable fact about the governance of technology rather than a general claim about innovation. The emirate hosts a university dedicated to artificial intelligence research in Masdar City. Government services are delivered through a unified digital platform, and a national digital identity system is used to access them.

Each of those serves a different part of the framework. A national digital identity system is the clearest available case for the identity concept in a political context: it concentrates convenience and raises real questions about inclusion for people who cannot or will not enrol. A unified government services platform illustrates systems and space, because it reorganises where a transaction physically happens. A dedicated artificial intelligence research institution and a technology start-up programme illustrate change in an economic context, with published material behind both.

The discipline is the same as everywhere else in this subject: name the source, record the date, and state what is contested. A local example used promotionally is worth nothing, because the evaluation marks require a trade-off. A local example used analytically is worth more than a borrowed one, because the student can describe it accurately and is less likely to repeat a half-remembered detail. Where a student has access through a family member or a work placement, anything used in an assessed report must be publicly available or cleared with the school first.
bullets: The UAE appointed a minister of state for artificial intelligence in 2017
A national digital identity system is strong material for the identity concept
Unified government service platforms illustrate systems and space

sections.heading: Generative tools, honesty, and the boundary that matters most in this subject
paragraphs: Digital Society students are the most likely on the Diploma to be using generative artificial intelligence tools, and the most likely to be studying them as course content at the same time. That makes the academic-honesty question concrete rather than theoretical, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a warning. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own. Where a generative tool has been used, it must be acknowledged in the way the school and the IB require, and it cannot be presented as the student's own writing or thinking.

The practical guidance we give is simple and it is about where in the process a tool sits. Using a tool to find material that is then checked against a primary source is research. Using one to generate text that goes into a submission is not acceptable, and in this subject it is also self-defeating: the assessed quality is specific, dated, attributed evidence, and generated prose is characteristically unspecific, undated and unattributed. The examiner's complaint and the honesty rule point in the same direction.

A tutor's boundary is identical to the one in every other Diploma subject, and our tutors state it to the student in the first session. A tutor teaches the framework, challenges a question, interrogates an example, explains what a criterion rewards, and comments on drafts the student has written. A tutor does not author any part of a submitted report, supply sentences to insert, or hand over finished work. Providers selling completed coursework are selling a malpractice risk that falls on the candidate. Official subject guides and papers are referenced and linked at source, never redistributed as downloads. Check your school's own policy on acknowledging tool use, because schools implement the requirement differently.
bullets: Submitted work must be the student's own, with any tool use acknowledged as required
A tool used to find material that is then verified is research; generated text is not
Generated prose is weak in exactly what this subject grades: specific dated evidence
No part of a submitted report comes from a tutor

sections.heading: Practical questions before you book, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Four questions are worth asking any tutor for this subject. How many Digital Society students have you taught through to assessment. What would you do with my child's example file in the first session. Will feedback name the criteria in writing. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. The first two will quickly separate someone who knows this course from someone who has read its syllabus, and the last is a legal matter that applies to anybody tutoring privately in this country.

On the permit: it was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students, and that tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here. MoHRE's service page lists application through its smart app, website and e-services system, a two-working-day completion time, and no fee.

Two more things a parent should know before paying anybody. The schools regulator in this emirate is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools; Gulf News has reported that its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tuition of students enrolled at their own school, which is worth verifying on adek.gov.ae. And IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, operates no office in the UAE, and publishes no tariff: market rates for a Diploma specialist here, read from providers' own pages in October 2026, run roughly AED 150 to AED 450 an hour online, and our own terms are quoted after the free first lesson.
bullets: Ask how many Digital Society candidates a tutor has actually taken to assessment
Ask what they would do with the example file in session one

process.title: Tell us the cohort, the level and the project stage
process.description: The first message that helps names the level, how long the school has offered the subject, whether the inquiry project question is settled, and for Higher Level whether the pre-released material has arrived. A first-cohort student with an unsettled question needs a different first session from a second-year student preparing the challenge component.

process.title: Free first lesson spent on evidence
process.description: One 50-minute online lesson in one subject at no charge, with no card details taken. The tutor looks at whatever examples the student already has, shows what a properly documented entry looks like, and writes one short analysis from it. That is usually enough to show whether the method is going to help.

process.title: A plan with the file at the centre
process.description: The written plan names each session, what it adds to the example file, which component it targets and the rate in AED. For a Higher Level student it maps the challenge preparation backwards from the school's dates. Nothing recurring begins before you have agreed it.

process.title: Weekly slot, and a file that grows
process.description: Sessions hold the same hour on Gulf Standard Time and move around mock weeks, examination periods and Ramadan timings. Each one adds documented entries and leaves one marked short analysis, so by the spring the student has a revision resource that no published guide could have supplied.

process.title: Review on coverage and on marks
process.description: Every four to six weeks the tutor reviews two things with you: whether marked analyses are improving, and whether the example file now covers the content areas and contexts evenly. Gaps in the second are the better predictor of an examination problem, and they are fixable in a fortnight once named.

whyPoints.title: Built for a subject with no revision shelf
whyPoints.description: Digital Society was first examined in 2024, so the usual apparatus of workbooks and circulating exemplars is thin. The work here is building the student's own documented evidence and drilling an answer structure, which is what the absence of published resources actually requires.

whyPoints.title: An example file with a fixed format
whyPoints.description: Development, date, source, content area, concept, context, contested claim. Seven fields, two or three new entries a week, reviewed for coverage rather than volume. It is the highest-return habit in the subject and it only exists if somebody insists on it every session.

whyPoints.title: A sequence that works on any question
whyPoints.description: Content area, concept, context, dated example, trade-off. Drilled until automatic, it removes the dependence on which topic appears, and it converts the strong instincts students already have about technology into answers a mark scheme recognises.

whyPoints.title: The Higher Level challenge treated as research
whyPoints.description: Pre-released material means this component can be prepared almost completely, which makes it the best return on preparation time available. We map stakeholders, interventions, costs and conflicts with sources attached, then write to time on several framings.

whyPoints.title: A straight answer on generative tools
whyPoints.description: Submitted work must be the student's own, with any tool use acknowledged as the school and the IB require. In this subject the honesty rule and the mark scheme agree, because generated prose lacks exactly what is graded: specific, dated, attributed evidence.

whyPoints.title: Sourced facts and no borrowed authority
whyPoints.description: Permit rules come from u.ae and mohre.gov.ae, the ADEK ethics position is flagged as press-reported until verified, and no IB examination date is published here because the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically. We claim no regulator or board approval.

faqs.question: What is IB Digital Society and how is it different from Computer Science?
faqs.answer: Digital Society replaced Information Technology in a Global Society and was first examined in 2024. It assesses analysis of digital developments in society, using concepts such as change, identity, power and systems, across content areas from data and algorithms to artificial intelligence, in contexts such as political, economic and health. Computer Science assesses programming and computational thinking. A student who wants to build systems should take Computer Science; a student who wants to analyse what systems do to people should take Digital Society. Families choosing options confuse the two routinely.

faqs.question: Why are there so few revision resources for Digital Society?
faqs.answer: Because the subject is new: 2024 was its first examination session, so the shelf of workbooks and the circulating pool of marked exemplars that surround an established course have not accumulated yet. That is not a reason to avoid the subject; it changes what support is for. The useful purchase is not explanation of how technology works, which most students have, but a method for building their own documented evidence and external marked feedback that shows where their work sits against the bands.

faqs.question: What should go in a Digital Society example file?
faqs.answer: Seven fields per entry: the development stated accurately in one sentence, the date, the named source, the content area it belongs to, the concept it illustrates, the context in which the impact lands, and the claim that is genuinely contested about it. That last field is the one students omit and the one that makes an entry usable, because an example without an argument attached is a fact rather than evidence. Two or three properly documented entries a week is enough, provided coverage across content areas is reviewed periodically.

faqs.question: How do we stop the example file being all about artificial intelligence?
faqs.answer: By reviewing it against the framework rather than the calendar. Every few weeks, read the file by content area and by context and list what is missing: networks, media, computers, the environmental and health contexts are the usual gaps, because artificial intelligence dominates what students encounter day to day. Then choose the next fortnight's entries deliberately to fill them. A file with fourteen artificial intelligence entries and nothing on media will underperform on half the paper regardless of how good those entries are.

faqs.question: How long is the Digital Society inquiry project?
faqs.answer: The report runs to a tight limit in the region of 1,200 words, supported by selected material. Confirm the exact current figure and criteria with your child's teacher, because this subject is new enough that documentation is still settling and a stale number would misdirect weeks of work. The practical implication is that description has to be minimal: students who spend their count explaining how a technology works arrive at the analysis with a few hundred words left, and the marks are in the analysis.

faqs.question: What makes a good inquiry project question in Digital Society?
faqs.answer: Specificity about three things: the technology, the setting, and the group affected. Asking whether artificial intelligence is good for employment cannot be answered in a short report, so the result is a summary of other people's opinions. Asking about a named technology's effect on a particular kind of work in a particular place can be answered if sources exist. The decisive step is testing the question against evidence the student already holds before committing to it, rather than discovering mid-investigation that the material is not there.

faqs.question: How should a Higher Level student prepare for the pre-released challenge material?
faqs.answer: As research, not revision. Because the material is known in advance, this component can be prepared almost completely, which makes it the best use of preparation time in the subject. Map the stakeholders and what each wants, the available interventions and who proposes them, the cost of each and who bears it, the evidence that any of them work, and where they conflict. Attach sources throughout. Then write to time on several possible framings, three timed attempts being about right, weeks before the session.

faqs.question: My child understands the technology but scores poorly. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly the middle of the answer sequence. Strong technical understanding produces a confident description, an assertion that something raises concerns, and then a stop. The marks require a concept doing analytical work, a named context in which consequences land, a dated and sourced example, and a trade-off that identifies who gains and who bears the cost. The same knowledge routed through that sequence reaches a different band. It is a structural fix, usually visible within three or four marked short analyses.

faqs.question: Can my child use generative AI tools while studying Digital Society?
faqs.answer: Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own, and any use of a generative tool must be acknowledged in the way the school and the IB require. The distinction that matters is where the tool sits in the process: using one to find material that is then checked against a primary source is research; using one to generate text for a submission is not acceptable. In this subject it is also counterproductive, because the assessed quality is specific, dated, attributed evidence, which generated prose characteristically lacks. Check your school's own policy.

faqs.question: What local Abu Dhabi examples work for Digital Society?
faqs.answer: Documented ones. The UAE appointed a minister of state for artificial intelligence in 2017, a verifiable fact about technology governance. The emirate hosts a university dedicated to artificial intelligence research in Masdar City. Government services run through a unified digital platform accessed with a national digital identity, which is the clearest available case for the identity concept in a political context, including the question of inclusion for those who cannot or will not enrol. Name the source, record the date, and state what is contested.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Digital Society tutor to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. There are no home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In this subject that is close to ideal, because the material under discussion is on a screen anyway: a policy document, a dataset, a platform interface, a dated report. Tutor and student annotate the same artefact, and the annotated version goes straight into the example file instead of into a notebook.

faqs.question: Is it a problem that my child is in the school's first Digital Society cohort?
faqs.answer: It is a specific, manageable disadvantage. A first cohort has no predecessors' marked work inside the school, so neither students nor, sometimes, the department has a settled sense of what each band looks like in practice. The teaching may be excellent and the calibration still absent. External marked feedback is the direct remedy, and it is more valuable here than in a long-established subject. Ask the department how many cohorts have sat the subject; the answer tells you how much internal exemplar material exists.

faqs.question: Does a Digital Society tutor in Abu Dhabi need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, as for any private tutoring in the country. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee.

faqs.question: How many Digital Society sessions does a DP1 student usually start with?
faqs.answer: A weekly slot from early in DP1 is the pattern that works best in this subject, precisely because the example file has to accumulate rather than being assembled late. Each session adds documented entries and produces one marked short analysis. Inquiry project supervision folds in when the question is due, and Higher Level challenge preparation runs for several weeks once the material is released. We prefer a fixed block with a stated end point, and will say so if marked work stops moving.

faqs.question: Can Digital Society lessons shift around Ramadan and school deadlines?
faqs.answer: Yes. Slots are held rather than fixed, so they move to post-Iftar timings during Ramadan and around mock weeks and internal deadlines without the booking lapsing. One scheduling point is specific to this subject: sessions are more useful immediately before an inquiry project checkpoint than after it, because the decisions that determine the mark, question scope and source selection, are made early. We try to place sessions ahead of those checkpoints rather than in the recovery period.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-digital-society-tutor.closingHeading: Send whatever examples your child already has
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-digital-society-tutor.closingBody: The most useful thing to bring to a first Digital Society conversation is not a marked paper. It is whatever collection of real-world examples your child has gathered, in whatever state it is in, plus the level and the stage of the inquiry project. The tutor will show what a properly documented entry looks like, write one short analysis from it, and name the gaps in coverage. That is what the free 50-minute online lesson is built around, in one subject, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. Lessons run online from any community in the emirate, held on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Five things you should be able to look at, rather than a report on how it is going
paragraphs: Economics is the Diploma subject where parents have the least ability to judge the teaching. In mathematics an answer is right or wrong; in economics a confident paragraph about inflation sounds like competence whether or not it would score. That is why so many Abu Dhabi families pay for a term, receive encouraging messages throughout, and discover from a mock that nothing shifted. The problem is not dishonesty. It is that nothing concrete was ever produced for anyone to inspect.

So this page is organised around artefacts. There are five, and each one proves something different: a scored Paper 3 attempt with the reasoning shown, a folder of hand-drawn diagrams with the labelling corrected, part (b) answers scored against the published level descriptors, three dated commentary drafts, and a short written record naming what changed each week. None of them predicts a grade. All of them can be examined by a parent who has never studied economics, which is the entire point.

The component structure explains why those five and not others. At Higher Level, Paper 1 carries 20 per cent through extended response, Paper 2 carries 30 per cent through data response, Paper 3 carries 30 per cent as the policy paper with quantitative work, and the portfolio of three commentaries carries 20 per cent. Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level, which makes it the component where Higher Level students most often lose the grade they were predicted, and the one least likely to be covered thoroughly in a crowded class.

The portfolio deserves its own attention because it behaves differently from everything else. Three commentaries of up to 800 words each, based on published news articles the student finds, each drawing on a different unit and a different key concept, marked by the school against lettered criteria and moderated externally. It is 20 per cent of the grade with no clock on it, which means it is the part of the course most responsive to calm work in term time and the part most often left until it cannot be rescued.

Teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time slots. For economics that matters practically: diagrams are drawn on a shared screen and saved, answers are scored against descriptors with the wording visible, and the commentary drafts sit in a dated folder rather than in a notebook. Where AED figures appear they are published market bands with the source and year named, describing what Abu Dhabi families are charged rather than advertising a fee. If your child is in DP2 and missing a predicted grade, start with the Paper 3 section; if they are in DP1 with commentary deadlines ahead, start with the portfolio section, because that is the component you can still protect cheaply.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-economics-hl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Economics is usually a new subject in DP1, which makes the starting point unusually variable. These are the routes Abu Dhabi students arrive from.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Economics at Higher Level is examined through three written papers and a portfolio of three commentaries. The course runs across four units, from basic concepts through microeconomics and macroeconomics to the global economy, and is tied together by nine key concepts that the commentaries must engage with explicitly. Higher Level adds both depth and the quantitative policy paper, which has no Standard Level equivalent.
programmes.countryNote: Economics is one of the larger Higher Level entries in Abu Dhabi, chosen by students heading to business, finance and policy routes in the UAE and abroad. Because most students meet the subject for the first time in DP1, the gap between the confident talkers and the accurate writers opens early and is rarely visible on a first report.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and societies in the MYP builds research, source handling and structured writing, assessed against criteria that reward investigation and communication. It does not build diagram work or quantitative handling of markets, so students arriving from this route usually write fluently and lose marks on technical accuracy rather than on expression.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi IB continuum students often arrive at Higher Level Economics with strong essay habits from humanities subjects. That is a mixed inheritance: part (b) answers written as history essays, with narrative where evaluation was wanted, are the most common early loss and respond well to a few weeks of scored practice.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel upper secondary
programmes.description: Students may arrive from IGCSE Economics or Business Studies, or from neither. Those with IGCSE Economics have met supply and demand diagrams and basic macroeconomic indicators, usually with short directive questions. Those without have met none of it, and the diagram work in particular has to be built from the beginning rather than refined.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi's large British-curriculum sector feeds both types into the same Higher Level class. Students who studied Edexcel Economics A at IGCSE tend to be strongest on definitions and weakest on evaluation; students with no economics background are often better at evaluation and slower on diagrams. Knowing which your child is saves a term of mismatched teaching.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-economics-hl-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Higher Level Economics sits inside a package, and the notes below say what each companion subject actually demands in writing or in calculation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three papers and a portfolio. Paper 1 is extended response with a 10-mark explain part and a 15-mark evaluate part; Paper 2 is data response; Paper 3 is the quantitative policy paper unique to Higher Level. Marks are lost most often in part (b) evaluation, in diagram labelling and in Paper 3 calculation set out without interpretation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The same four units without the policy paper, with Paper 1 at 30 per cent, Paper 2 at 40 per cent and the portfolio at 30 per cent. Students considering a move down should note that the portfolio weight rises, so commentary quality matters more rather than less.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside economics by Abu Dhabi students. It rewards applied case analysis and a different evaluation style, and students who mix the two conventions tend to write business answers in economics papers, where the diagram and terminology marks then go uncollected.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The common pairing with Higher Level Economics. Its handling of functions, rates of change and statistics maps directly onto Paper 3 quantitative work, particularly elasticity, tax incidence and national income calculations.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Strong algebra, which helps with Paper 3 arithmetic, though it provides little practice in interpreting a number economically. A student can compute a correct elasticity figure and collect nothing for failing to say what it implies for the firm.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Shares development, trade and sustainability material with the global economy unit. Students taking both can reuse case evidence, provided they keep the two subjects' evaluation conventions distinct in their writing.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Overlaps with the global economy unit on trade, integration and development. Its essay style rewards contested argument, which transfers well to economics part (b) answers if the student also brings the required diagram and terminology.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The written load here collides directly with commentary deadlines in most Abu Dhabi schools. Families planning economics hours should check the English coursework calendar before committing to a schedule in those weeks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and essay land in the same terms as the economics portfolio. Students who treat both as writing tasks to be done in the same fortnight produce weaker versions of each, and the portfolio is the one that carries 20 per cent of a subject grade.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Often written in economics by Higher Level students. Supervision belongs to the school; a tutor teaches research method and gives feedback on the student's own drafts, and the submitted text stays the student's work throughout.

sections.heading: The five artefacts, and what each one actually proves
paragraphs: A parent who has not studied economics can still audit economics tuition, provided the right things are produced. The five below were chosen because each is concrete, each is cheap to generate inside a session, and each proves something the others do not. Between them they cover the three papers and the portfolio, which is the whole of the assessment, and none of them requires you to judge whether an argument about monetary policy is sound.

The honest limits matter as much as the uses. A scored Paper 3 attempt shows whether quantitative work is being interpreted rather than merely computed; it does not show that the student will perform under exam pressure. A folder of diagrams shows technical accuracy improving; it says nothing about evaluation. Dated commentary drafts show whose thinking moved; they cannot tell you what the school will award. Anyone claiming a single artefact predicts a grade is overselling a useful thing.

Used together over eight weeks, though, they answer the question families actually have, which is whether to continue. If the diagram folder is cleaner, the part (b) scores are rising on the same question types, the Paper 3 attempts now carry interpretation after each figure, and the commentary drafts are improving in the student's own voice, the work is landing. If none of that is true, more sessions of the same kind will not change it, and that conclusion is available weeks before the next school report.

sections.heading: Paper 3 is where Higher Level Economics is actually decided
paragraphs: Paper 3 carries 30 per cent of the Higher Level grade and exists only at Higher Level. It asks for calculation and then for policy: work out the figure, say what it means, recommend a response and justify the recommendation against the data supplied. Students who are strong essay writers frequently treat it as an arithmetic exercise, produce correct numbers and collect a fraction of the available marks because nothing was interpreted.

The failure is visible on any scored attempt. An elasticity value appears with no statement of what it implies for revenue or incidence. A national income figure is computed and left to speak for itself. A policy is recommended with a generic justification that could have been written without reading the data at all. None of this is a mathematics problem, which is why asking a mathematics tutor to help with Paper 3 usually produces better arithmetic and the same mark.

The repair is mechanical and it works. Every figure is followed, in writing, by a sentence saying what it implies in this context. Every recommendation cites a number from the stimulus. Every attempt is scored with the reasoning shown rather than ticked. In a crowded Abu Dhabi class, Paper 3 is often the component taught last and practised least, which is precisely why a short block on it is the highest-yield purchase available to a Higher Level student with a predicted grade they are not hitting. Six focused sessions here can reach a component worth almost a third of the grade.

sections.heading: Diagram marks are drawn, not described
paragraphs: Economics is unusual among the essay subjects in awarding marks for drawing. A diagram that is correctly titled, with both axes labelled with the right variables and units, the original and new curves distinguished, the shift direction correct and the relevant areas identified, earns marks that a flawless paragraph cannot recover. Students lose these marks constantly, and they lose them in ways that are trivial to fix once someone sits and looks at the drawing rather than the prose.

The recurring losses are consistent across Abu Dhabi cohorts. Axes labelled price and quantity with no units or market named. Curves shifted but not relabelled, so the examiner cannot tell which is which. Equilibrium points unmarked. Areas shaded for welfare loss without being identified in the text. A diagram drawn to illustrate a point the answer never makes. Each of these is a few marks, and together across a paper they routinely account for the gap between two grades.

This is why the diagram folder exists as a separate artefact. Diagrams are drawn by hand in the session, corrected label by label, and kept. A parent can flick through ten of them in two minutes and see whether the labelling has become habitual, which is a faster and more reliable signal than any verbal report. It is also the artefact students resist least, because the improvement is obvious to them as well, and a student who can see one kind of mark being recovered usually becomes more willing to work on the harder kind.

sections.heading: Part (a) and part (b): two different jobs on one question
paragraphs: Paper 1 presents extended-response questions in two parts: a 10-mark part asking the student to explain, and a 15-mark part asking them to evaluate or discuss. They reward different things and most students write the same kind of answer twice. The explain part wants definition, theory, a correct diagram and application, delivered cleanly. The evaluate part wants a judgement that is argued, qualified and supported, and a student who simply explains more thoroughly reaches a ceiling well below the available marks.

In Abu Dhabi the pattern is sharpest among students who come from humanities-heavy MYP backgrounds. They write fluent, well-organised prose that narrates economic theory and never commits to a position. The marks for evaluation are awarded for things like weighing short run against long run, naming the assumptions a model depends on, considering who bears a cost, and reaching a conclusion that follows from what was argued rather than from a general sentiment about markets.

The practical method is to score the student's own answers against the published level descriptors with the wording in front of them, then ask them to place the answer themselves and justify the placement. Done eight or ten times, this changes how they write because they stop producing everything they know and start producing what the descriptor rewards. It is slower than being told the rule and it is the only approach that reliably survives into an exam, because under pressure a student falls back on the habit rather than on the advice.

sections.heading: The portfolio: three commentaries, dated drafts and the line that does not move
paragraphs: The portfolio is 20 per cent of the Higher Level grade: three commentaries of up to 800 words each, based on published news articles the student selects, each drawing on a different unit of the course and a different key concept, marked by the school against lettered criteria covering diagrams, terminology, application and analysis, the chosen key concept, and evaluation. The current mark allocation per criterion is set out in the subject guide your school holds, and your teacher is the authority on how it is applied.

Most of the available mark is decided by the article and the plan rather than by the writing. An article that reports an outcome without describing a mechanism gives the student nothing to analyse. An article that covers three units at once makes the key concept choice incoherent. Planning all three commentaries together, so that units and concepts do not collide and no single article is asked to carry too much, is an hour of work that protects a fifth of the subject grade.

The boundary is simple and it is stated here deliberately. A tutor teaches the criteria, the article selection, the diagram choice and the 800-word discipline, reads the student's draft, and responds with questions: which key concept is this actually engaging, what does your diagram show that your paragraph does not claim, where is the evaluation as opposed to the description? Drafts are kept dated so the progression is visible in the student's own voice. Finished commentaries are sold in this market; submitting one is a malpractice matter handled by the IB, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than on the seller.

sections.heading: What movement from a 4 to a 6 looks like on paper
paragraphs: Families want to know what progress looks like before the next report, and in economics it has a recognisable sequence. Technical marks move first because they are mechanical: diagram labelling, terminology used precisely rather than loosely, definitions given where the question asks for them. Paper 3 interpretation moves next, within a few weeks, because it is a habit of following a number with a sentence. Evaluation moves last and most slowly, because it requires a student to hold two positions and choose between them in writing.

That sequence is why a family looking only at the total grade concludes in week five that nothing is happening. The artefacts tell a different story: the diagram folder is cleaner, the part (a) answers are collecting their definition and diagram marks reliably, and the part (b) scores have not budged. That is progress in the right order, and the part (b) scores typically follow four to six weeks later once the technical work stops consuming the student's attention.

The table below sets out what each grade band tends to look like on a script, what changes first, and the evidence to look for. It is a guide to reading your own child's work rather than a promise about outcomes. Where none of the described changes appear over eight weeks, the approach is wrong and should be changed rather than extended, which is a conclusion the artefacts make available long before an examination does.

sections.heading: An in-home economics tutor in Abu Dhabi against online, on the artefacts each leaves
paragraphs: In-home economics tuition in Abu Dhabi is a real market and the honest comparison starts with its price. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-350 an hour, with home tutors reported up to AED 500 where the subject is scarce or the journey long. Economics at Higher Level is a scarce subject in this emirate, particularly for Paper 3, so families in peripheral communities are quoted at the top of that range when they are quoted at all.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Higher Level Economics teaching for Abu Dhabi families is delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time slots. The trade is explicit: you give up a person in the room, and the shortlist stops being people willing to drive to Al Samha at 17:30 and becomes economists who mark Paper 3 regularly.

For this subject the format also decides whether the artefacts exist. Diagrams drawn on a shared screen are saved automatically; diagrams drawn in a notebook stay in the notebook. Scored answers with descriptor wording quoted beside them are a file; the same conversation at a kitchen table is a memory. The comparison below is on those practical differences rather than on atmosphere, which is a genuine advantage of being in the room and not one that shows up in a mark.
