sections.heading: What to ask your economics teacher, and what ADEK does not tell you
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. That tells you about a school. It will not tell you whether your child's part (b) answers are reaching the top descriptor band, and no inspection rating has ever answered that question for anybody.

The questions that help are the ones your school can answer in a short meeting. Which components is my child losing marks on, rather than which grade did they receive? Has the class completed Paper 3 teaching, and when will it be practised under time? What are the internal deadlines for each of the three commentaries, and which units and key concepts has my child chosen for them? Those four answers let a tutor plan around the school rather than across it.

There is also a rule specific to this emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics expectations for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and a teacher tutoring privately is required to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. Confirm the current wording with the school or on ADEK's own policy pages. The practical point is that the apparently convenient arrangement carries a risk that falls on the teacher.

sections.heading: A schedule that survives Ramadan, mocks and the commentary season
paragraphs: Three things disrupt economics support in Abu Dhabi every year, and all three are predictable. Ramadan compresses school days and moves family routines later, so sessions shift to post-Iftar evenings or weekend mornings. School mock periods remove a fortnight of capacity for written work. Commentary deadlines cluster with Theory of Knowledge and English coursework in the same weeks, which is a problem of total writing capacity rather than of economics.

Because sessions are online there is no travel to renegotiate, so a slot change is a calendar edit. The thing that needs planning is the sequence rather than the timing. Portfolio work belongs in the quieter weeks before the cluster arrives, not inside it. Paper 3 blocks suit the period immediately after mocks, when the student has a scored attempt to react to and the diary has opened again. Scored writing practice continues through everything because it is the slow component.

A practical pattern that works for many Abu Dhabi families: plan all three commentaries early in DP1 so units and key concepts do not collide, write the first one well before its deadline, use the post-mock window in DP2 for Paper 3, and keep one timed written answer a week running throughout. That schedule costs no more than an ad hoc one and avoids the situation that ends most Diploma years badly, which is three deadlines and a weak paper arriving in the same fortnight. Families who set that sequence in writing at the start of DP1 rarely need to buy emergency hours later, and emergency hours are the most expensive kind.

process.title: Send one answer, not a description
process.description: The most useful first message carries one of your child's own part (b) answers, or one Paper 3 attempt, with the mark it received. A message saying economics is not going well cannot be acted on. One mid-band answer tells a tutor which of the five artefacts needs building first and roughly how long it will take.

process.title: A free 45-minute trial that produces something
process.description: The trial is a working session with no card details required, and it ends with an artefact: a scored answer with reasons, or a corrected diagram set, or a judgement on an article's suitability for a commentary. If it produces only a conversation about potential, you have learned something useful about how the sessions would run.

process.title: Choose the block by component
process.description: Paper 3 work, scored writing and portfolio sessions are different purchases. A DP2 student missing a predicted grade usually needs Paper 3 first. A DP1 student with commentary deadlines ahead needs the portfolio planning session, which protects 20 per cent of the grade for an hour or two of work.

process.title: Fix the slot and keep the folder
process.description: A fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, chosen around the school run and adjusted for Ramadan without a charge. Every session adds to the diagram folder, the scored answers or the dated drafts. The folder is the deliverable, and it should be somewhere a parent can open it without asking.

process.title: Audit at week eight against the artefacts
process.description: At eight weeks the questions are specific. Is the diagram folder cleaner? Are part (b) scores rising on comparable questions? Do the Paper 3 attempts carry interpretation after every figure? Are the commentary drafts improving in the student's own voice? If the answers are no, the approach changes or the arrangement ends.

whyPoints.title: Artefacts a non-economist can audit
whyPoints.description: Five concrete outputs, each inspectable by a parent who has never studied the subject. Economics is the Diploma subject where confident talk most resembles competence, which is exactly why the work should be produced in a form you can look at rather than reported on.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as the Higher Level component it is
whyPoints.description: Thirty per cent of the grade, unique to Higher Level, and usually the last thing a crowded class practises. Sessions treat it as economics rather than arithmetic, with every figure followed by what it implies and every recommendation tied to the data supplied.

whyPoints.title: Descriptors put in front of the student
whyPoints.description: Part (b) answers are scored against the published level descriptors with the wording visible, and the student places their own answer and justifies it. That is how evaluation writing changes, as opposed to being told that evaluation is important.

whyPoints.title: Portfolio planned, not rescued
whyPoints.description: All three commentaries are planned together so units and key concepts do not collide and no article is asked to carry more than it can. An hour of planning early protects a fifth of the subject grade, which is the best-value hour in the course.

whyPoints.title: A coursework line stated in advance
whyPoints.description: Commentary feedback arrives as questions on dated drafts and the text stays the student's own. Finished commentaries are openly sold in this market and the malpractice consequence lands on the candidate, so the version trail is protection as much as evidence.

whyPoints.title: Market figures with sources, none about us
whyPoints.description: AED bands on this page name the survey or provider that published them and the year. No success rate, grade-improvement figure or star rating appears anywhere, because none of those could be published here with the number of students, the dates and the method attached.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level Economics artefacts should we be collecting as proof of progress?
faqs.answer: Five, and each proves something different. A scored Paper 3 attempt with the reasoning written out shows whether figures are being interpreted. A folder of hand-drawn diagrams shows technical accuracy. Part (b) answers scored against the published descriptors show whether evaluation is being written rather than described. Three dated commentary drafts show whose thinking moved. A weekly written record shows the sessions have a plan. None predicts a grade; together they tell you within eight weeks whether to continue.

faqs.question: What makes Paper 3 different from the other two economics papers?
faqs.answer: It exists only at Higher Level, carries 30 per cent of the grade, and asks for calculation followed by policy: produce the figure, say what it implies, recommend a response and justify it against the data supplied. Strong essay writers often treat it as arithmetic, produce correct numbers and collect a fraction of the marks because nothing was interpreted. That is why asking a mathematics tutor for help with Paper 3 usually improves the arithmetic and leaves the mark unchanged.

faqs.question: How much do diagrams matter in Higher Level Economics answers?
faqs.answer: Enough that they decide grades. Marks are awarded for a correctly titled diagram with both axes labelled with the right variables, original and new curves distinguished, shifts in the correct direction, equilibria marked and relevant areas identified and referred to in the text. The usual losses are trivial to fix once someone looks at the drawing rather than the prose: unlabelled axes, unrelabelled curves, unmarked equilibria, shaded areas never mentioned in the answer. Across a whole paper these routinely account for a grade.

faqs.question: Our daughter's part (b) answers score lower than her part (a). Why?
faqs.answer: Because the two parts want different things and she is probably writing the same kind of answer twice. The 10-mark part asks her to explain: definition, theory, correct diagram, application. The 15-mark part asks her to evaluate, which means weighing short run against long run, naming the assumptions a model rests on, considering who bears a cost, and reaching a conclusion that follows from the argument. Explaining more thoroughly reaches a ceiling. Scoring her own answers against the published descriptors is what changes it.

faqs.question: How long should each economics commentary be, and how many are there?
faqs.answer: Three commentaries, each up to 800 words, based on published news articles the student finds. Each should draw on a different unit of the course and a different key concept, and the school marks them against lettered criteria covering diagrams, terminology, application and analysis, the key concept and evaluation. Together they carry 20 per cent of the Higher Level grade. The word ceiling is strict and is part of the skill: a commentary that needs 1,200 words to make its point has usually chosen an article with too much in it.

faqs.question: Which commentary criterion do Abu Dhabi students lose marks on first?
faqs.answer: The key concept criterion, more often than any other, because students choose a concept after writing rather than before and then assert the connection in a closing sentence. Diagrams are the next most common loss, usually a correct diagram that the text never actually uses. Evaluation is the third: describing a limitation is not evaluating it. All three are decided at the planning stage, which is why an hour spent on article choice and concept allocation protects more marks than an hour spent editing prose.

faqs.question: Who decides the news article a commentary is based on?
faqs.answer: The student, and that is not a technicality. The selection is part of the assessed work, so a tutor's role is teaching the criteria an article has to satisfy: recent enough, published by a credible outlet, describing a mechanism rather than only an outcome, narrow enough for one unit and one key concept. The student then applies those criteria and brings candidates to be discussed. If a tutor hands over an article, the first and most important decision in the commentary was not the student's.

faqs.question: What evidence shows a Higher Level Economics grade is moving before the next report?
faqs.answer: The sequence is predictable, so look for it in order. Technical marks move first: cleaner diagram labelling and precise terminology, visible within two or three weeks. Paper 3 interpretation follows, with a sentence of implication after each figure. Evaluation moves last, usually four to six weeks later, once technical work stops absorbing attention. A family looking only at the total will conclude in week five that nothing is happening, while the artefacts show progress in exactly the right order.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram offer an in-home economics tutor in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Higher Level Economics teaching for Abu Dhabi families runs one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time slots. The local in-home market is genuine, with published bands of roughly AED 180-350 an hour and more for scarce subjects, and Higher Level Economics is scarce here. Online delivery replaces a travel radius with a shortlist of economists, including tutors who mark Paper 3 regularly.

faqs.question: How do the quantitative questions in Paper 3 differ from mathematics questions?
faqs.answer: The arithmetic is the easy half. A mathematics question ends when the figure is correct; a Paper 3 question begins there. An elasticity value has to be followed by what it implies for revenue or for who bears a tax. A national income calculation has to be read as a statement about an economy. A policy recommendation has to cite a number from the stimulus rather than a general principle. Students with strong mathematics often compute flawlessly and score mid-band, which is a reading and writing failure rather than a numerical one.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level Economics tuition cost in Abu Dhabi per hour?
faqs.answer: Published bands put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and IB specialists at AED 200-450 and above, with in-home one-to-one at about AED 180-350 in Bestimate's 2026 table. Unitors advertises IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase publishes AED 270 for its specialist tier; those are their figures, quoted as market context rather than as our price. Ask specifically whether scoring written answers and reading commentary drafts sit inside the hour, because for this subject that is most of the value.

faqs.question: Can economics sessions run after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most Abu Dhabi families move them there. School days compress during Ramadan and routines shift later, so post-Iftar evenings and weekend mornings become the practical slots. Because sessions are online there is no travel to rearrange, so the change is a calendar edit rather than a renegotiation, and there is no rescheduling charge for it. The useful planning point is sequence rather than timing: portfolio work belongs in the quieter weeks, and timed written practice continues throughout because it is the slow component.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Economics worth taking for a business degree in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, and the only reliable confirmation is each university's own admissions page. Many business and finance programmes in the UAE and abroad list economics as preferred rather than required, and some specify a mathematics route instead. Check before DP1 choices are confirmed, because moving level later is disruptive. Note also that no tutor should tell you tuition is required for admission or for Ministry of Education equivalency; that is a claim about a regulatory process rather than about teaching.

faqs.question: Our son writes strong essays and loses marks on data response. What fixes that?
faqs.answer: Making him use the stimulus. Data response rewards claims anchored in the material provided: a figure quoted, a trend named in the units given, a change described with reference to the table rather than to general theory. Students with essay confidence write around the data instead of from it, and the marks for using it go uncollected. The fix is mechanical and quick: every claim in a Paper 2 answer has to point at something in the stimulus, practised under time until it becomes the default.

faqs.question: What if the tutor and our school disagree about an economics answer?
faqs.answer: Your school wins on anything procedural, and that should be said plainly at the start. The teacher sets the internal deadlines, approves the commentary plan and applies the criteria your child is marked against. Where there is a genuine difference of interpretation on an answer, the useful response is to ask the teacher which descriptor their mark reflects, which turns a disagreement into information. A tutor who encourages a student to override a supervisor's guidance on coursework is creating a problem that the student, not the tutor, will carry.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-economics-hl-home-tutor.closingHeading: Ask for an artefact before you book a term
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-economics-hl-home-tutor.closingBody: The fastest way to judge economics support is to make it produce something. Send one of your child's own part (b) answers or a Paper 3 attempt with the mark it received. The free 45-minute session returns a score against the published descriptors with the reason stated, or a corrected diagram set, or a judgement on whether a chosen article can carry a commentary. No card details are required. If what comes back is a conversation about potential rather than a marked piece of work, you have your answer about how the rest of the term would have gone.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Higher Level Economics to Abu Dhabi Diploma students: the diagram discipline Paper 1 rewards, the data-response technique Paper 2 demands, the quantitative policy work that is unique to Paper 3, and the portfolio commentaries that carry 20% of the Higher Level grade.

intro.heading: What Higher Level Economics support costs in Abu Dhabi, component by component
paragraphs: Nobody buys Economics tutoring in general. Families buy it because something specific has gone wrong, and in Higher Level Economics there are exactly four things it can be: Paper 1, Paper 2, Paper 3 or the portfolio. Each is a different repair job, consumes a different number of hours, and therefore produces a different total on the invoice at the same hourly rate. Pricing the subject without naming the component is how a family ends up spending a term's budget on the part that was already working.

The hourly rate itself is the least variable part. Market rates for IB specialist tutoring in the UAE run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour, a band published in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. TutorChase publishes AED 270. Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. BartyED publishes AED 650 for an examiner tier. Entry tiers advertised from AED 33 to AED 65 by Tutopiya and EdFlik are university-student and group formats, which is a different product from Higher Level Economics and should not be compared on price alone.

Paper 3 is the component that makes Higher Level Economics cost more than Standard Level, and it is the reason the two pages on this site are not interchangeable. Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level, carries 30% of the grade on its own, and asks for calculation and policy recommendation rather than essay writing. Students who are fluent at Paper 1 essays frequently arrive at Paper 3 having never been taught to work a numerical question under time pressure, and that gap takes a block of dedicated sessions rather than general revision.

The portfolio is the component families most often underestimate. It is 20% of the Higher Level grade, three commentaries of no more than 800 words each, assessed against lettered criteria for a combined 45 marks. Almost all of the marks lost in a first draft are lost in two places: the diagram and the key concept. Both are repairable in a small number of hours, which makes the portfolio the cheapest marks on the course to move, and the ones a family should price first.

The fourth cost input is local. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of Abu Dhabi private schools, and its professional-ethics rules, as reported by Gulf News, bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. The MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years and carries a code of conduct saying the same. The lawful Abu Dhabi pool is therefore smaller than the number of Economics teachers in the emirate, and a smaller lawful pool prices higher. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India, and every Abu Dhabi lesson runs online over live video.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Higher Level Economics sits in Group 3 of the Diploma. The routes below decide how much groundwork an Abu Dhabi student arrives with, which is the first thing that changes a cost estimate.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Economics is organised around four units and nine key concepts, and at Higher Level it is examined over three papers plus the portfolio. The nine concepts are not decoration: one of them has to be explicitly applied in each commentary and carries its own criterion marks.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level Economics groups in Abu Dhabi are frequently small, sometimes fewer than ten students, because the subject competes with Business Management for the same choosers. A small group means a student sees very few worked Paper 3 answers and very few marked commentaries before their own are due, which is precisely the gap that drives families to buy outside hours.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and Societies in MYP assesses knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. The last of those transfers directly into the evaluation criterion of an Economics commentary. What MYP does not supply is diagram technique, which is the single most mechanical skill in the Diploma course and the one most Abu Dhabi students arrive without.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Abu Dhabi school runs MYP to Year 11 rather than entering an IGCSE cohort, students reach DP1 Economics with strong written argument and no prior exposure to supply and demand diagrams. A short, mechanical diagram block in the first term is a cheaper purchase than essay coaching in DP2.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Combines a small number of DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. A CP student taking Economics sits the same papers and submits the same portfolio. Higher Level Economics inside a CP is unusual, and it removes the Theory of Knowledge load that otherwise competes with portfolio deadlines in the second year.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi a CP Economics student is often the only one in their year taking the course, which means no classroom comparison for a commentary draft. That is the scenario where the cost of one-to-one hours is not a premium over classroom teaching but a substitute for it.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: The Diploma core runs alongside Economics and competes for the same weeks. An Extended Essay in Economics is a separate 4,000-word piece supervised at school, distinct from the portfolio, with its own authenticity record. Families budgeting for Higher Level Economics support should decide early whether they are also buying essay research-method teaching, because the two needs peak in the same term.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools typically set internal Extended Essay and portfolio deadlines earlier than the IB's own windows. Two deadlines in one term is the commonest reason a family's monthly tutoring spend doubles without anybody planning it.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Higher Level Economics is the subject in question. The ones after it are what Abu Dhabi students pair it with, each annotated for what the pairing does to the number of hours a family ends up buying.

subjects.name: Economics (Higher Level)
subjects.description: Three papers plus a portfolio. Paper 1 is extended response at 20%, Paper 2 data response at 30%, Paper 3 a quantitative policy paper at 30% and Higher Level only, and the portfolio 20%. The quantitative load in Paper 3 is what distinguishes the Higher Level course and the Higher Level tutoring bill.

subjects.name: Economics (Standard Level)
subjects.description: Two papers and the portfolio, with no Paper 3. Paper 1 carries 30%, Paper 2 40% and the portfolio 30%. Because the portfolio is weighted higher at Standard Level, a family moving a student down after DP1 should rebalance spending towards commentary work rather than papers.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The usual alternative choice rather than a companion, though some Abu Dhabi students take both. Shared ground is limited to market structures and some stakeholder analysis; the assessment styles differ sharply. Two separate tutors is normally the honest answer, which doubles the hourly spend.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Supplies most of what Paper 3 needs: percentage change, index numbers, elasticity calculation and interpretation of real data. A student taking Applications usually needs transfer coaching rather than new teaching, which is a cheaper purchase.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Produces students who are algebraically confident and unpractised at applied economic calculation under time pressure. The Paper 3 gap for these students is presentation and interpretation rather than arithmetic, and it closes in a small number of sessions once named.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Shares development economics, trade and sustainability content. Students taking both can be taught the shared material once, and an Abu Dhabi family booking separate tutors for the two often pays twice for the same explanation of global interdependence.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Overlaps on trade blocs, development and intervention. The evaluation habits it teaches transfer usefully into Economics Paper 1 part (b) answers, which is where most Abu Dhabi students lose essay marks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Not an Economics subject, but the commentary and essay components are written assessments and weak written structure shows up in both. Where a student is losing marks for disorganisation rather than economics, that is an English problem being paid for as an Economics problem.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Economics
subjects.description: A separate piece from the portfolio, supervised at school. A tutor can teach question framing, data sourcing and economic method, and comment on drafts the student has written. The words must be the student's own and the supervisor records authenticity as part of the assessment.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Shares nothing in content and everything in calendar. The exhibition and essay deadlines land in the same weeks as portfolio commentaries at most Abu Dhabi schools, and any honest costing has to account for the weeks when a weekly Economics hour is unaffordable in time.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi families pay different totals partly because of where they live: school choice follows community, and school choice determines whether Economics is offered at Higher Level at all, how large the group is, and when a session can realistically start.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Several established Diploma cohorts within minutes of each other. Higher Level Economics is offered at most of them, groups are reasonable in size, and sessions can start at 16:30, so an hour costs an hour rather than an hour plus a drive.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Towers with a growing Diploma population and a bridge commute. Economics groups at nearby schools are small. Families here commonly buy a Paper 3 block rather than a full-year plan, because the classroom covers content adequately and quantitative work is where it stops.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa communities feeding the Khalifa City and Al Raha school corridor. The afternoon run towards Dubai makes a fixed 17:30 online slot far more reliable than any arrangement involving travel, which protects the weekly cadence through the DP2 spring.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Short school runs and a high proportion of students taking two Group 3 subjects. The cost question here is usually whether one tutor can cover Economics and Geography, and the answer is often yes for the shared development content.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: Newer schools with young Diploma cohorts, where Higher Level Economics may run with very few students. Fewer classmates means fewer marked commentaries to learn from, which is a direct driver of outside spend here.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Older island neighbourhoods with larger, long-running Diploma groups. More internal mock papers circulate, so families tend to buy targeted component blocks rather than continuous support.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Mainland communities with longer commutes and a wide curriculum spread. A specialist within a short drive is unlikely; online delivery removes the travel premium that an in-home rate carries in this part of the emirate.

regions.note: Fast-growing mainland districts where a Higher Level Economics student may be one of two or three in their year. The realistic comparison here is not online against in-home but one-to-one against no specialist at all.

sections.heading: Pricing Higher Level Economics by the component that is broken
paragraphs: The useful question is not what an Economics tutor charges in Abu Dhabi. It is how many hours this particular problem takes, because the rate is roughly fixed and the hours are not. Four components, four different repair jobs, four very different totals.

Diagram technique is the cheapest thing on the course to fix and the most commonly broken. A student who cannot draw and label a correctly shifted curve under time pressure loses marks in Paper 1, in Paper 2 and in every commentary, which means one mechanical block of two or three sessions pays back across three components at once. Families who buy content revision instead will spend a term and see the same diagram errors.

Paper 3 is the expensive one, and it is specific to Higher Level. It carries 30% of the grade, it is quantitative, and most students have had far less practice at it than at essays because schools reach it late in DP2. Six to eight focused sessions is a realistic block, and buying it in March rather than November costs the same per hour while delivering considerably less.

Essay structure for Paper 1 is the slowest to move, because it is a writing problem rather than an economics problem. Evaluation in part (b) is where Abu Dhabi students lose most of their Paper 1 marks: the analysis is competent and the judgement is absent. That takes a run of marked essays over a term, not a weekend intensive, and a provider promising otherwise is selling you optimism.

sections.heading: The 45-mark portfolio, criterion letter by criterion letter
paragraphs: No competitor page measured in this research set names a single Economics internal assessment criterion, which is remarkable, because the criteria are published, lettered and worth 45 marks between them. A parent who knows the letters can read a returned commentary and see exactly where the marks went.

The portfolio is three commentaries. Each must be no more than 800 words, each must draw on a different unit of the syllabus, each must use a different source published no earlier than one year before the commentary was written, and each must apply one of the nine key concepts explicitly. Each commentary is assessed against five lettered criteria. A further criterion covers whether the portfolio as a whole meets those presentation requirements, which is three marks most students should collect in full and some lose through a word count or a date.

The marks are not spread evenly across skills, and that is the practical point. Diagram and application carry three marks each per commentary. Terminology carries two. Key concept carries three. Evaluation carries three. So the diagram, the key concept and the evaluation between them hold nine of the fourteen marks available in each commentary, and all three are mechanical enough to teach directly.

What a tutor does here has a hard boundary that is worth putting in writing. A tutor can teach diagram technique, explain what applying a key concept actually looks like as opposed to naming one, show what the top evaluation band contains, and comment criterion by criterion on a commentary the student has written. A tutor cannot supply text, cannot choose and summarise the article for the student, and cannot revise a draft into a submission. The school supervisor keeps the authenticity record, and the IB treats a breach as malpractice by the candidate.

sections.heading: Paper 3, and why Higher Level costs more than Standard Level
paragraphs: Paper 3 is the single clearest reason a Higher Level Economics plan costs more than a Standard Level one in this emirate. It exists only at Higher Level, it carries 30% of the subject grade, and it does something none of the other components does: it asks for calculation, and then asks for a policy recommendation built on the result.

The arithmetic involved is not difficult. Percentage change, index numbers, elasticity, tax incidence, calculations around market equilibrium, and the derivation of figures from a given data set are all within reach of any Diploma student. The problem is almost never capability. It is practice, presentation and the habit of showing working in the form the mark scheme credits. A student who writes the right number with no working loses marks that a student with the wrong number and clear method sometimes keeps.

The second half of the paper is where Higher Level Economics students in Abu Dhabi most often come unstuck. A policy recommendation is not an essay and it is not a list. It asks for a specific, justified choice, with the trade-offs named and the constraints acknowledged, in a tight word budget under time pressure. Students who write beautiful Paper 1 essays frequently write unusable Paper 3 recommendations, because the two components reward opposite instincts.

Timing matters for cost here more than anywhere else on the course. Most schools reach Paper 3 material late, which means the families who buy support for it do so in the DP2 spring, at the moment when evening slots across the emirate are scarcest. Six to eight sessions bought in the autumn of DP2 and six to eight bought in March cost the same and are not the same purchase.

sections.heading: Where Abu Dhabi Economics students lose Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks
paragraphs: The two essay-and-data components hold half the Higher Level grade between them, and the losses on both are predictable enough to diagnose from a single marked paper. They are also the losses least likely to be fixed by reading the textbook again.

Paper 1 is extended response in two parts. Part (a) asks for explanation and part (b) for discussion or evaluation, and the mark distribution punishes students who treat both the same way. The dominant failure is a part (b) that analyses competently and then stops, with no judgement, no weighing of the alternatives and no acknowledgement of context. A student can know the economics completely and lose a third of the available marks there.

Paper 2 is data response, and the dominant failure is describing the data rather than using it. A question asking the student to use the extract expects specific figures, specific quotations and specific links to theory. Answers that paraphrase the extract and then set out textbook theory beside it read fluently and score poorly. The fix is mechanical: every claim tied to a named piece of evidence from the material in front of them.

Both components also reward diagram use inside written answers, which is why diagram technique is the highest-return purchase on the whole course. A correctly labelled diagram with a stated shift, an identified new equilibrium and a sentence in the text that actually refers to it earns marks in Paper 1, in Paper 2 and in criterion A of every commentary. Students who draw diagrams as decoration earn none of them.

sections.heading: What Economics tuition costs beside everything else a family pays
paragraphs: Tutoring is usually assessed against the hourly rate of another tutor, which is the least informative comparison available. The more useful frame is what it costs beside the other items in an Abu Dhabi education budget, because that is what determines whether a plan is affordable across two years rather than one term.

Context on fees: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package Dubai valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Abu Dhabi fees run through ADEK's own approval process. Tutoring carries no fee freeze and no cap, which is the strongest argument available for buying fewer hours earlier.

Monthly package rates circulating in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour are AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Read the top band as the realistic exam-year number for Higher Level Economics, since the final term usually means two hours a week rather than one.

One item families forget entirely: examination entry. A candidate retaking a subject, or sitting as a private candidate, pays entry fees through the school or an approved centre, and those are separate from tuition and set by the board and centre rather than by any tutor. Build them into the two-year picture before committing a monthly tutoring budget that leaves no room for them.

sections.heading: ADEK, the permit, and the tutor you are not allowed to hire
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain private schools are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK publishes inspection outcomes and runs the fee-increase approval process for the emirate. It is named by none of the competitor pages measured in this cluster, which is a strange omission on pages aimed at Abu Dhabi parents.

The rule that affects a family's choice most directly concerns teachers. Gulf News reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Confirm the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it.

The federal position is clearer still. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount quoted to you is unverified.

What a parent should do with all of this is short. Ask whether the tutor holds a current MoHRE private tuition work permit. Ask whether they teach at your child's school. A provider who cannot answer both questions plainly is selling a risk alongside the hour, and the risk does not sit with them. MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, so there is no reason for a permit to be a mystery.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for Economics in this emirate
paragraphs: A good proportion of Abu Dhabi families searching for an Economics tutor start by looking for one who can drive over, and that deserves a straight comparison rather than a dismissal. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so what follows is the comparison rather than a sales argument.

On rate the two overlap. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and UAE home tutors generally at AED 200 to AED 500 with travel included, against AED 200 to AED 450 for an online IB specialist. The difference is not price. It is which tutors exist for you. Higher Level Economics with real Paper 3 experience and portfolio supervision behind them is a narrow brief, and the subset of that group living within a workable evening drive of Al Shamkha or Baniyas is very small.

The second difference is operational. Economics sessions live on diagrams, data extracts and mark schemes. A shared screen puts all three in front of both people simultaneously, a diagram can be drawn, corrected and annotated live, and the annotated version is saved rather than folded into a bag. A commentary draft can be read, commented on and returned inside the hour.

The third is scheduling, and in this emirate it is decisive. A tutor crossing the mainland at 17:00 holds one slot that evening. Online, a student can take a 30-minute diagram clinic the night before a mock, which nobody would drive for. The honest limitation is unchanged: a student who will not engage without a person in the room is a poor fit, and the free first session exists so a family establishes that before spending anything.

sections.heading: Availability, and what happens when no Higher Level specialist is free
paragraphs: Availability is the thing nobody in this market publishes, and for Higher Level Economics in Abu Dhabi it is a real constraint rather than a sales device. The brief is narrow: current syllabus, comfortable with Paper 3 quantitative work, experienced at portfolio supervision, and lawfully permitted to tutor in the UAE. The ADEK ethics position and the MoHRE permit regime both narrow the resident pool further.

For a weekday evening slot in DP1 a match is usually straightforward. For a 17:00 slot in the February or March of DP2, when every Diploma family in the emirate wants the same hour, it is not. At that point there are three honest answers and a provider who always says yes is not giving you any of them.

A different time is the cheapest concession and the most effective: moving to 20:00 or a weekend morning widens the available pool substantially in exam term. A different tutor profile is the second: a Business Management or Geography specialist who also teaches Economics can handle Paper 1 and Paper 2 work competently even if Paper 3 is not their strongest ground, and that trade-off should be named rather than hidden. The third is waiting with a date attached rather than being matched to whoever is free.

Where no UAE-resident specialist is available, a matched tutor may be based elsewhere and teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed before any commitment. Two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to contact numbers outside the UAE without stating where delivery happens, which is the sort of thing a family discovers at the least convenient moment.

process.title: Name the component, not the subject
process.description: Tell us which of Paper 1, Paper 2, Paper 3 or the portfolio is the problem, and what the last mark on it was. That single sentence narrows the plan and the cost more than any general description of how Economics is going. If you are not sure, the first session establishes it.

process.title: Send one marked piece of work
process.description: A returned Paper 1 part (b), a marked data-response question or a commentary with the school's criterion comments on it. Any one of those tells a specialist in five minutes whether the loss is diagram technique, evaluation, evidence use or quantitative method.

process.title: Take the first session at no charge
process.description: A full session online with the matched tutor, with no payment and no card held. It should end with a written component-by-component view: what is costing marks, how many sessions that specific repair takes, and in what order to buy them if the budget is finite.

process.title: Buy the blocks in cost-effective order
process.description: Diagram technique first, because it returns marks in three components at once. Then the portfolio, which holds 45 marks and is the most teachable. Then Paper 3 if the student is at Higher Level. Paper 1 evaluation last, because it is the slowest to move and needs a term rather than a block.

process.title: Review on marked work every six weeks
process.description: Compare marks by component against the starting position rather than against a target. If the component bought has not moved in six weeks, change the diagnosis, the mode or the tutor. Continuing to buy the same hours because the sessions feel productive is the commonest way a budget disappears.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as its own block
whyPoints.description: The Higher Level only paper carries 30% of the grade and asks for calculation and policy judgement rather than essay writing. It gets a dedicated block with timed practice, rather than being folded into general revision in the final weeks.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty boundary is written down

Supplying text, choosing and summarising the article, or revising a draft into a submission is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequences fall on the candidate. Providers in this market sell completed coursework; that practice is refused here.

faqs.question: What does an hour of Higher Level Economics tuition cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates for IB specialist tutoring in the UAE run roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table is the source for that band, TutorChase publishes AED 270, Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for an examiner tier. Rates advertised from AED 33 to AED 65 by Tutopiya and EdFlik are university-student or group formats rather than Higher Level specialists. The more useful question is how many hours your specific component needs, because the rate barely varies and the hours vary enormously.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 3 push the cost of Higher Level Economics support up?
faqs.answer: Because it is an extra component that exists only at Higher Level, carries 30% of the subject grade, and asks for something the other papers never ask for: calculation, shown working, and a policy recommendation built on the result. Most schools reach the material late in DP2, so students arrive at it with far less practice than they have at essays. A realistic block is six to eight sessions, which at market rates of AED 200 to AED 450 an hour is the largest single line in a Higher Level plan.

faqs.question: How many of the 45 portfolio marks can tutoring realistically move?
faqs.answer: A useful amount, because the losses concentrate in teachable places. Each commentary carries three marks for diagrams, three for application and analysis, three for the key concept, three for evaluation and two for terminology, with a further three marks for whether the portfolio meets its presentation requirements. Diagram technique and explicit key-concept application together hold six marks per commentary and are the two most mechanical things on the course to teach. Evaluation inside 800 words is harder but still trainable. The marks are moved by the student's own revision of their own draft.

faqs.question: Which portfolio criterion letter is worth the most per session spent?
faqs.answer: The key concept criterion, in most first drafts. It carries three marks per commentary and is the one students most often lose almost entirely, because they name a concept in the introduction and then write a commentary that never uses it again. Applying a concept means the analysis is organised around it throughout. That is a single session of teaching with an immediate effect on all three commentaries. Diagrams are a close second: three marks each, and a labelled diagram the text actually refers to is mechanical to produce once shown.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package cheaper than hourly booking for Higher Level Economics?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the comparison needs care. Packages circulating in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Check three things before comparing them with an hourly rate: the actual length of a session, whether unused sessions carry over, and whether the package tutor is a Higher Level specialist or a generalist. A package of eight generalist sessions is not cheaper than four specialist hours if the component you need repaired is Paper 3.

faqs.question: Can my child use UAE news articles for the portfolio commentaries?
faqs.answer: Yes, and local or regional material often works well because it gives the analysis something concrete to attach to. The requirements are about structure rather than geography: each commentary must use a different source, each source must be published no earlier than one year before the commentary is written, each commentary must draw on a different unit of the syllabus, and each must stay within 800 words. UAE policy stories on subsidies, housing, labour markets or trade can serve any of those units. Confirm the current rules in the subject guide your child's coordinator holds.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to fix diagram marks in Higher Level Economics?
faqs.answer: Less than almost anything else on the course, which is why it should be bought first. Two or three sessions at market rates of AED 200 to AED 450 an hour covers the mechanical work: drawing the curve correctly, labelling both axes, showing the shift rather than describing it, identifying the new equilibrium, and writing a sentence in the text that refers to the diagram. The return is unusual because diagram marks appear in Paper 1, in Paper 2 and in criterion A of every commentary, so one block pays back across three components.

faqs.question: Does ADEK publish anything that tells me about a school's Economics teaching?
faqs.answer: ADEK publishes inspection outcomes for private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, and those reports describe teaching and learning quality at a whole-school and sometimes a phase level. What they will not tell you is how a particular Higher Level Economics group is doing, because an inspection band is not a subject-level measurement. For the Economics-specific picture, ask the school directly how many students are taking it at Higher Level, who teaches it, and what the internal portfolio deadlines are.

faqs.question: What should we budget for Higher Level Economics across two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Work from Bestimate's monthly estimates rather than from an hourly rate. A single weekly hour runs AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month in the mid market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, and the final term usually means two hours a week rather than one. A component-led plan is cheaper: a diagram block, a portfolio block and a Paper 3 block bought in that order will cost considerably less across two years than continuous weekly support, if the student's content base is sound.

faqs.question: Is group Economics tuition in Abu Dhabi worth the saving?
faqs.answer: For shared content revision it can be, because explaining monetary policy to four students costs the same as explaining it to one. For the work that actually moves a Higher Level grade it is poor value. The repairs that matter are individual: your child's part (b) evaluation habit, your child's unused diagrams, your child's missing working in a Paper 3 calculation, your child's commentary draft. None of those survives a shared hour, and a group format cannot give criterion-referenced feedback on four different drafts at once.

faqs.question: Do you come to our villa in Saadiyat Island for Economics lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every Abu Dhabi lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For Economics the format is a genuine advantage: a shared screen holds the data extract, the mark scheme and a diagram being drawn and corrected live, and the annotated version is saved at the end of the session rather than disappearing into a folder.

faqs.question: How much of Higher Level Economics is actually quantitative?
faqs.answer: Enough to matter and not enough to be a barrier. Paper 3 is built around calculation, and Paper 2 includes calculation items within the data response, so a meaningful share of the Higher Level grade depends on arithmetic competence under time pressure. The arithmetic itself is accessible to any Diploma student. What separates marks is practice, and whether working is written in the form the mark scheme credits. Students taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation usually need transfer coaching rather than new teaching, which costs fewer hours.

faqs.question: Does a private Economics tutor in Abu Dhabi need a permit, and is there a fee?
faqs.answer: Yes to the permit and no to the fee. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without the permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so distrust any specific figure. MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service lists a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: We are starting eight weeks before the May papers. What is realistic and what does it cost?
faqs.answer: At eight weeks the portfolio is submitted and those marks are fixed, so the money goes entirely into the three written papers. Expect two sessions a week rather than one, which at market rates of AED 200 to AED 450 an hour is the upper monthly band of AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above that Bestimate describes for specialist exam-year support. The highest-return work in that window is diagram technique and shown working in Paper 3 calculations, because both are mechanical. Paper 1 evaluation habits rarely change in eight weeks.

faqs.question: Do we pay extra if my son retakes Economics in a later session?
faqs.answer: Tuition and examination entry are separate costs and it is worth separating them in your planning. Entry for a retake, or for a candidate sitting outside their school, is arranged through the school or an approved examination centre and priced by the board and centre, not by any tutor. Tuition for a retake is usually a short, component-specific block rather than a repeat of the course, because the student already holds the content. Ask the school's Diploma coordinator about entry arrangements and deadlines before committing a tuition budget.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.closingBody: Higher Level Economics is four assessed components, and what a family spends in Abu Dhabi follows almost entirely from which of the four is broken. Diagram technique is the cheapest and returns marks in three places. The portfolio holds 45 marks and is the most teachable. Paper 3 is the Higher Level premium and deserves its own block, bought early rather than in March. Send one marked piece of work and the component it came from, take the first session at no charge, and buy the blocks in the order the diagnosis gives you.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-economics-sl-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Economics at Standard Level to Diploma students in Abu Dhabi. Profiles say which components they are asked for, whether commentary draft reading is inside their hour, and their Gulf Standard Time availability. Ask what the first session will produce before you compare any two quotes.

intro.heading: Spend by component, because the components are not equally expensive to fix
paragraphs: Economics at Standard Level is examined through two written papers and a portfolio of three commentaries. Paper 1 carries 30 per cent, Paper 2 carries 40 per cent and the portfolio carries 30 per cent, which is higher than the Higher Level equivalent. Those three numbers should decide a budget, and they almost never do. Most Abu Dhabi families buy weekly sessions in whatever the class is currently teaching, which spreads the money evenly across components that respond to paid time very unevenly.

The portfolio is the clearest example. It is 30 per cent of the grade, it has no clock on it, and most of its mark is settled by decisions taken before any writing: which article, which unit, which key concept, which diagram. Four or five hours spread across the deadline term addresses a third of the subject grade. Compare that with broad content revision, which can absorb twenty hours and mostly repeats what the school is already delivering across 150 taught hours.

The second decision that moves a number is format. One-to-one is the most expensive per hour and the only format that can mark one student's essay properly. A pair at the same school and level halves the rate per student and works well for content and for timed practice. A group class is cheaper again and cannot do the one thing most Standard Level economics students need, which is somebody reading their own writing and saying where the marks were available.

The third is scarcity rather than distance. Economics specialists are thinner on the ground in this emirate than science tutors, especially people who mark data response and commentaries regularly. That shows up in quotes as a premium that has nothing to do with travel and does not disappear because you live centrally. Families in Al Shamkha and families in Al Bateen are quoted differently for in-home work because of the journey; both are quoted more for economics than for mathematics because of the subject.

Every AED figure on this page is a published band with the provider or survey and the year named. None of them is our price: tuition is quoted on enquiry after a free 45-minute trial session, with no card details required to book it. Teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time slots, which means no travel sits inside the rate and the same figure applies wherever in Abu Dhabi you live. Read the component table first if you are deciding what to buy, the calendar section if you are deciding when, and the format table if you are weighing one-to-one against a pair or a group class. The three answers together usually come to a smaller total than the weekly arrangement most families are quoted at the outset.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-economics-sl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: What a family needs to buy depends on where the student met the subject, since economics is new to most Diploma students and entirely new to some.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Economics at Standard Level covers four units, from basic concepts through microeconomics and macroeconomics to the global economy, tied together by nine key concepts. Assessment is Paper 1 extended response, Paper 2 data response and a portfolio of three commentaries. There is no Paper 3, which is the Higher Level policy paper, so Standard Level students carry a higher portfolio weighting instead.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, Standard Level Economics is often taken as a sixth subject alongside a heavier package, which affects the budget more than the content does. A student with two Higher Level sciences has little writing capacity left for commentary season, and that collision is the thing most worth planning spending around.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and societies builds source handling, research and structured writing against criteria that reward investigation and communication. It does not build diagram work or quantitative market analysis, so students from this route generally write well and lose technical marks. Content hours are rarely what they need; diagram and terminology hours are.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi continuum students often arrive able to argue and unable to draw. That is cheap to fix, because diagram accuracy is mechanical: a few hours of hand-drawn correction recovers marks across both papers and the portfolio at once, which makes it the best value early purchase for this group.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel upper secondary
programmes.description: Some students arrive from IGCSE Economics or Business Studies and some from neither. Those with a background know supply and demand and the main macroeconomic indicators from short directive questions. Those without start from nothing, and in a Standard Level class moving at pace the gap opens in the first term rather than the second.
programmes.countryNote: Because Abu Dhabi's British-curriculum sector is large, Standard Level groups routinely mix both types. For a family budgeting, the question to ask the school is whether the class is being taught as though everyone has prior economics. If it is, a student without that background needs a short catch-up block early, which is far cheaper than a rescue in DP2.

subjects.name: Economics

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Adds the quantitative policy paper at 30 per cent and reduces the portfolio weighting to 20 per cent. Students considering moving up should know the added component is where Higher Level grades most often slip, and that supporting it costs more because fewer tutors mark it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A frequent companion. Its evaluation style differs from economics, and students who blend the two write business answers in economics papers. Buying command-term work once for both subjects is efficient; buying content twice is not.

subjects.description: Covers the statistical and graphical handling that economics data response rewards. Students on this route rarely need separate quantitative support for Standard Level economics, which removes a category of spend.

subjects.description: Its coursework deadlines collide with commentary deadlines in most Abu Dhabi schools. Check the English calendar before booking economics hours into those weeks, because the constraint will be writing capacity rather than understanding.

subjects.description: Another subject with heavy written demands and a different evaluation convention. Students carrying economics, psychology and English together should expect their bottleneck to be time in term two rather than any single subject's difficulty.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Lands in the same weeks as the commentary deadlines. Budgeting economics sessions into that fortnight is the most common planning mistake, and the portfolio is the component that suffers because it has no external deadline to force it.

sections.heading: The portfolio is 30 per cent at Standard Level and the cheapest third to protect
paragraphs: Standard Level Economics has no Paper 3, so the portfolio carries more weight here than at Higher Level: 30 per cent of the grade for three commentaries of up to 800 words each, based on articles the student finds, each engaging a different unit and a different key concept. It is marked by the school against lettered criteria covering diagrams, terminology, application and analysis, the key concept and evaluation, with the current mark allocation set out in the subject guide the school holds.

What makes it cheap to protect is that most of the mark is decided before the writing. An article reporting only an outcome gives nothing to analyse. An article spanning three units makes the key concept choice incoherent. A diagram chosen after the paragraphs are written usually illustrates nothing the text claims. Planning all three commentaries together takes an hour or two and removes the most common causes of a low mark across a third of the subject grade.

The table below prices the components against the hours families typically buy for each, using the published market bands set out later on this page. The last column is the uncomfortable one: it asks what share of the grade each purchase can reach. Broad content revision scores badly there not because content does not matter, but because the school is already delivering 150 taught hours of it and a second delivery rarely adds marks. Read the last column before the price column, because a cheap hour aimed at nothing is still a wasted hour.

paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, which is why families buy support reactively and pay more for it. The sequence below counts backwards from the examination session UAE schools sit in May, using the milestones your own school sets rather than published dates. IB session and results dates are not restated here: they should be confirmed with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org, because a date quoted from a tutoring website is not a source.

Read it as a spending plan rather than a revision plan. Each row names what is worth buying in that window and what it costs at published market bands. The pattern it produces is front-loaded and cheap: planning and diagram work early, when hours are inexpensive and nothing is urgent, and a short marked-writing block late, when the student has mock results to react to. Emergency purchases in the final six weeks are the most expensive hours in the whole course and buy the least.

One further point about timing. Commentary deadlines in most Abu Dhabi schools fall in the same weeks as Theory of Knowledge and English coursework, so the constraint in that fortnight is total writing capacity rather than economics understanding. Buying economics hours into that collision tends to produce a stressed student and a rushed commentary. Buying them four weeks earlier costs the same and works. Ask your Diploma coordinator for the internal deadline calendar in September rather than discovering it in February, since the whole plan hangs off those dates.

sections.heading: One-to-one, a pair or a group: what each costs per student
paragraphs: Format changes the per-student cost more than tutor seniority does, and the three formats are not interchangeable. One-to-one is the only arrangement in which a tutor reads one student's commentary draft and says where the marks were available. A pair at the same school and level roughly halves what each family pays and handles content, diagrams and timed practice perfectly well. A group class is cheaper again and is a content delivery mechanism.

The mistake families make in both directions is predictable. Some pay one-to-one rates for content a group session could deliver, which is buying the most expensive format for the least demanding job. Others buy a group class for a student whose problem is that nobody has ever marked their writing, and then conclude after a term that tutoring does not work. The question to ask is not which format is better but which one can do the specific job the component needs.

The table compares them on that basis. Note the last column: what each format cannot do. A group class cannot mark thirty individual commentary drafts, however good the teacher is, which is the same constraint your school's economics teacher is working under. That constraint is the actual reason to pay for one-to-one hours, and it is worth paying for precisely and sparingly rather than weekly for two years. A pair arrangement only works where both students are genuinely at the same level, so agree the pace between the two families before the first session rather than after it.
