sections.heading: The Higher Level essay, and whether it is worth the extra Higher Level
paragraphs: Higher Level adds a written essay on a work or text studied in class, developed from the student's own line of inquiry. It is the component that rewards the students who were already enjoying the subject and punishes the ones who took Higher Level for the points. The reason is that it has no question to lean on: the student generates the inquiry, and a weak inquiry produces a weak essay however well it is written.

A workable line of inquiry is narrow, arguable from the text, and answerable in the word count. Students begin with something enormous, usually a theme across a whole novel, and then write a tour. The useful session is spent shrinking the inquiry until it is small enough to be answered properly, which students experience as being told their idea is too interesting and later recognise as the thing that made the essay possible.

Families in this emirate also ask the prior question, which is whether to take English A at Higher Level at all. The honest answer depends on the rest of the Diploma. A student aiming at humanities, law or communications benefits from the extra component and the reading. A student aiming at engineering, with two science Higher Levels already, is adding a long independent written task to the heaviest possible workload. Check the Higher Level requirements on each university's own admissions pages, because they vary and they change, and treat any tutoring page's summary of them, including this one, as a prompt to verify.
bullets: The Higher Level essay has no set question; the student generates the inquiry
A broad inquiry produces a tour of the text rather than an argument

sections.heading: Grade movement: what moves between terms, and roughly how fast
paragraphs: This is the question every family actually wants answered, and most providers answer it with a promise. The honest version is a table, because the four criteria move at genuinely different speeds and knowing which is which decides where a term's money goes.

Focus and organisation is the fast one. It is a planning habit, it responds within three or four weeks, and it often produces the first visible mark change, which is useful because it buys a student's belief that the subject is learnable. Analysis and evaluation takes a term, because the student is replacing a reflex, assertion, with a different reflex, mechanism. Knowledge of the set texts moves exactly as fast as the student reads and annotates them, which is to say it is entirely within their control and nothing to do with tutoring. Language moves slowest, and attempts to accelerate it generally produce a more ornate version of the same imprecision.

What follows from that is a sequencing rule rather than a promise. Early in a block, work on structure and on question and extract choice, because those move. Across a term, work on the mechanism of analysis. Leave language as a steady background correction rather than a target. And if a family arrives six weeks before the papers, say plainly which columns are out of reach rather than selling a term's work compressed into a fortnight. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone quoting a specific improvement should be read with real scepticism.

sections.heading: What to ask for after four weeks of support
paragraphs: A block in this subject should be auditable by a parent who has never read the set texts. Four weeks is long enough for the diagnosis to have happened and for one fast criterion to have moved, and short enough that stopping is still cheap. There are three things to ask for, and all three are documents rather than opinions.

The first is a written statement of which criteria were weak across the scripts the tutor read, and which one the block is targeting first. If this does not exist in writing, the diagnosis has not been made. The second is a fresh timed piece produced after the first three or four sessions, marked against the same criteria, so there is a before and an after rather than a feeling. The third is the student's own account of what they now do differently when they plan an essay, which is the most revealing of the three and takes thirty seconds to obtain.

If the answer to all three is vague, the sessions have become company rather than teaching, and that happens in this subject more than in any other because English tutoring can feel productive while changing nothing. Stopping at four weeks and trying a different diagnosis costs less than a term of pleasant conversations. That test applies to any provider, including this one, and it is worth running on every arrangement a family pays for. Four weeks is also short enough that a student has not yet decided the sessions are simply part of their week.
bullets: A written statement of the weak criteria, produced in week one
A fresh timed piece marked against the same criteria by week four

sections.heading: Mixed cohorts, Arabic alongside, and the English A or English B question
paragraphs: An English A class in this emirate often contains students with radically different English histories. One joined an English-medium school in Year 1, another in Year 9, a third arrived last September from a system taught in another language entirely. They sit in the same room with the same set texts and the same deadlines. For the teacher this is a real constraint rather than an oversight: four criteria, two profiles, one lesson.

That mix produces a specific question families sometimes need to ask, and it is better asked early. A student losing most marks on language rather than on analysis, and finding the reading load genuinely unmanageable rather than merely heavy, may be in the wrong course. English B is a language-acquisition course with its own reading, listening, writing and oral components, and moving between courses is a decision for the Diploma coordinator in the first part of DP1, not later and not by a tutor. Saying so sometimes costs a booking; it is still the right advice.

The surrounding timetable matters too. Arabic, Islamic education and social studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools, with Arabic placement driven by a student's background. For a Diploma student carrying six subjects plus the core plus those, the evening is genuinely full, and the realistic support pattern is often fortnightly sessions with reading in between rather than weekly sessions with nothing done between them. Families who book weekly out of anxiety often get less movement than families who book fortnightly and protect the reading time.
bullets: English A cohorts in this emirate are frequently very mixed

sections.heading: Proofreading, feedback and the academic-honesty line in English
paragraphs: English is the subject where the honesty line is easiest to cross by accident, because helping with words looks so much like helping with ideas. The rule a family can rely on is that the student's own expression is part of what is being assessed. Marking-style feedback that identifies a weak paragraph, questions whether a claim has been evidenced, or points out a repeated structural habit is teaching. Rewriting a paragraph so it reads better is doing the student's assessed work for them.

That line applies to parents as much as to tutors, and it is worth a conversation at home. A parent who improves the sentences in a piece of assessed work has removed the evidence the teacher needs and changed what is being marked. A parent who reads a draft and says they lost the thread in the middle has given genuinely useful feedback without touching anything. The second is more helpful than the first, which surprises people.

Two further boundaries hold for every page on this site. Official syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked rather than reproduced, because reproducing them is a copyright matter. And no component is supplied, completed or edited to a finish by a tutor. One page ranking for these searches sells completed assessments outright; the risk of that arrangement is carried entirely by the student, which is reason enough to refuse it. A family who is offered a finished piece of work by any provider has learned something important about that provider at no cost.
bullets: A student's own expression is part of what is assessed
Feedback names a problem; it does not fix the sentence
Lost the thread here is more useful than a rewritten paragraph
Official papers and mark schemes are linked, never reproduced

sections.heading: What this costs in Abu Dhabi, and who published the figures
paragraphs: Market rates for this subject sit in the same bands as any other Diploma specialism, and the published figures are worth stating because most competitor pages in this search publish none at all. Bestimate's 2026 tutoring cost table puts one-to-one visits at roughly AED 180-350 and specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level work at AED 200-450 and above. Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase publishes AED 270. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33-52 at the university-student end, and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. Those are other providers' figures as published in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

English is also the subject where the cheap hour is most tempting and most often wasted, because a general graduate can plausibly discuss a novel. What a mid-band script needs is someone who can name which of four criteria is costing the marks and run the drill that fixes it. A pleasant hour of discussion about a text produces no measurable change, and families usually discover this after a term rather than after a month, which is the real argument for auditing a block at four weeks.

Private tutoring in the UAE also runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules also describes a prohibition on Abu Dhabi school staff tutoring their own enrolled students for payment, which is worth verifying against ADEK's own policy document.

process.title: Send three marked scripts, not a description
process.description: Before the free trial lesson, send three or four of your child's own returned pieces with the teacher's marks and comments on them. One script shows an incident; three show a pattern. The trial is then spent on a real diagnosis instead of introductions. One free trial lesson per student, booked without card details.

process.title: Get the weak criteria named in writing
process.description: The first session ends with a written statement of which criteria are losing the marks across those scripts and which one the block will target first. If that statement does not exist, the diagnosis has not happened, and everything after it is general essay practice at a specialist rate.

process.title: Work the fast criteria first
process.description: Structure, planning habit, question choice and extract pairing all move within a few weeks. Starting there produces an early visible change, which matters for a student who has decided they are bad at English. The slower work on analysis then happens with the student's cooperation rather than against their resignation.

process.title: Re-measure with a fresh timed piece
process.description: After three or four sessions, a new piece is written under time and marked against the same criteria. That gives a before and an after rather than an impression. It also exposes an unproductive block at four weeks instead of at the end of a term, which is the point at which stopping is still cheap.

process.title: Keep the set texts the student's job
process.description: Reading and annotating the works studied is the one part of this subject nobody can do for a student, and it is the part that moves fastest when they do it. Sessions are not spent reading the texts aloud. Where a student has not read them, that is the honest first conversation.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis by criterion, not by impression
whyPoints.description: Blocks start by reading the student's own marked scripts against the four criteria and naming which are weak. Most English tutoring treats every weakness as a need for more essay practice, which is why a term can pass with no measurable change in a subject that is actually quite diagnosable.

whyPoints.title: Honest timescales for each kind of improvement
whyPoints.description: Structure moves in weeks, analysis in a term, language slowly and unevenly. Those differences are published on this page so a family can decide where a term's budget goes, rather than being promised an undifferentiated improvement that no provider can deliver.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted as the market's, with sources named
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: A published boundary on feedback
whyPoints.description: Feedback names a weak paragraph, questions an unevidenced claim, and identifies a structural habit. It does not rewrite a sentence. The student's expression is part of what is assessed, so improving it for them removes the evidence the teacher needs and changes what is marked.

whyPoints.title: Willing to say the course is wrong
whyPoints.description: A student losing most marks on language rather than analysis, with an unmanageable reading load, may belong in English B. That is the Diploma coordinator's decision and the conversation belongs with the school. Raising it costs a booking and is the correct advice.

whyPoints.title: No accreditation claimed that we do not hold
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no office in the UAE. It holds no approval, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and it does not supply or complete any assessed component.

faqs.question: My child keeps getting 12 out of 20 with a comment about needing more depth. What does that actually mean?
faqs.answer: It means nothing useful on its own, which is the problem. Depth could mean the interpretation is thin, the analysis asserts an effect without showing the mechanism, the structure has buried the argument, or the expression is imprecise. Those are four different problems with four different fixes. Reading three or four of your child's scripts side by side against the four criteria reveals which one recurs, and that pattern is the diagnosis. A single script shows an incident; three show a habit, and habits are what a block of sessions can realistically change.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an English A tutor to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Support here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with marked scripts and annotated drafts opened on a shared screen. For this subject the format is genuinely well suited: the work is reading a script together line by line, marking it up, and comparing it with the criteria, all of which is easier on a shared screen than over a table. It also removes the drive across the emirate from the hour you are paying for.

faqs.question: Which part of this course improves fastest if we only have one term?
faqs.answer: Focus and organisation, followed by Paper 1 timing. Both are planning habits rather than knowledge, and both tend to move within three or four weeks. Question choice for Paper 2 and extract pairing for the oral move faster still, sometimes within a session or two, because they are decisions rather than skills. Analysis and evaluation takes a term because the student is replacing one reflex with another. Language control moves slowest. A term spent on the fast items produces visible change; a term spread evenly across all four usually does not.

faqs.question: My child writes beautifully but the marks are average. How is that possible?
faqs.answer: Because fluency and analysis are different skills, and fluency can actively hide the gap. A confident writer reads a text, forms an impression, and writes an elegant essay defending that impression. The criteria reward showing how the text's construction produces its effect, which is a narrower and less comfortable kind of writing. These students usually score well on understanding and in the middle band on analysis and evaluation. The fix is a drill: for each technique named, write the sentence explaining the mechanism between the choice and the effect before moving on.

faqs.question: Why does my child struggle with the unseen texts in Paper 1 but not with the novels?
faqs.answer: Because novels have been taught and the unseen material has not, and because non-literary text types each carry their own conventions. A student can analyse an opinion column and then meet a public-information poster, a satirical cartoon or an infographic and analyse only the words in it, ignoring layout, framing, the implied audience and what has been left out. Half the available analysis sits in what the text is for and who it addresses. Practising across varied text types, with a few minutes of planning each time, closes that gap faster than more essays on the set works.

faqs.question: What is the single most common structural mistake in Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Writing two essays instead of one. The student covers the first work in four paragraphs, the second work in four, then adds a closing paragraph observing that both deal with the theme. That caps the mark however good the individual observations are, because comparison is the assessed act rather than an afterthought. A comparative essay compares inside every paragraph: one aspect of the question at a time, examined across both works, with attention to where they diverge. Students find this hard for about three attempts and easier than their old method afterwards.

faqs.question: How do we choose a global issue for the individual oral that will actually work?
faqs.answer: Choose a claim, not a noun. Migration, gender and climate are topics, and a topic produces ten minutes of commentary on two extracts that both mention it. An issue is contested and arguable, so each extract can do different work: how the language of borders turns people into numbers, or how urgency is manufactured in environmental appeals. Then pick extracts that pull against each other rather than agreeing, because agreement leaves nothing to examine. Both decisions are made before any rehearsal, and they matter more than delivery does.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level English A worth it alongside two science Higher Levels?
faqs.answer: Consider it carefully. Higher Level adds an independent written essay with no set question, which means the student generates their own line of inquiry and a weak inquiry produces a weak essay however well written. For a student heading towards humanities, law or communications, the extra component and the reading are genuinely valuable. For a student with two science Higher Levels and an engineering ambition, it adds a long independent task to the heaviest workload available. Check the Higher Level requirements on each university's own admissions pages, since they vary and change.

faqs.question: How would I know after a month whether the tutoring is worth continuing?
faqs.answer: Ask for three documents. A written statement of which criteria were weak across the scripts the tutor read and which one is being targeted first. A fresh timed piece written after three or four sessions and marked against the same criteria, so there is a before and an after. And your child's own account of what they now do differently when planning an essay. If all three answers are vague, the sessions have become company rather than teaching, and changing the diagnosis costs far less than a term of pleasant conversations.

faqs.question: Should I correct the English in my child's draft before they hand it in?
faqs.answer: Better not to. Your child's own expression is part of what the criteria assess, so improving the sentences removes the evidence the teacher needs and changes what is being marked. There is a more useful kind of help that touches nothing: read the draft and say where you lost the thread, which claim you did not believe, or which paragraph repeated the one before it. That is real feedback and it leaves the writing entirely theirs. The same boundary applies to a paid tutor, who names a problem rather than fixing a sentence.

faqs.question: My child joined an English-medium school in Year 9 and is drowning in English A. Are they in the wrong course?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it is worth asking early rather than hoping. The signal is where the marks are being lost. A student losing them mainly on analysis and structure is in the right course and needs teaching. A student losing them mainly on language, with a reading load that is genuinely unmanageable rather than merely heavy, may belong in English B, which is a language-acquisition course with its own components. That decision sits with the Diploma coordinator and belongs in a conversation with the school in the first part of DP1, not with a tutor and not in DP2.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Abu Dhabi English A families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One, and often one a fortnight rather than one a week. The limiting factor in this subject is reading and drafting done between sessions, not time spent in them, and a Diploma student here is also carrying Arabic, Islamic education and social studies alongside six subjects and the core. A fortnightly slot with a piece of work produced in between usually moves faster than a weekly slot with nothing done between. The exception is a final-term consolidation block, where short, frequent sessions on timing and question choice genuinely help.

faqs.question: What does English A support cost per hour for a family in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Published market bands put specialist IB tutoring at roughly AED 200-450 an hour and above. Unitors lists IB from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 table puts one-to-one visits at AED 180-350 with specialist work at AED 200-450 and higher. Budget online options run from around AED 33-65. Those are other providers' published figures as at October 2026. English is the subject where a cheap hour is most tempting, because any graduate can discuss a novel, and least effective, because a mid-band script needs criterion-level diagnosis rather than discussion.

faqs.question: Can a tutor rewrite a paragraph to show my child what good looks like?
faqs.answer: Not inside their assessed work, no. A tutor can write an example on a different text entirely, model the thinking out loud, or annotate the student's paragraph with questions about what is missing. What they cannot do is improve the sentences in a piece that will be submitted, because expression is part of what is assessed and the work has to be the student's own. That boundary is stated here because this is a search in which completed coursework is openly sold, and the student carries the entire risk of that arrangement.

faqs.question: Do English A tutors working with Abu Dhabi students need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tutoring in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here. The permit is free, so its absence is worth asking about.

faqs.question: It is six weeks to the papers and my child is at a 4. What is honestly achievable?
faqs.answer: Some things and not others, and a provider who will not separate them is not worth hiring. Reachable in six weeks: a planning habit that gets the whole Paper 1 text addressed in the time, a comparative paragraph structure for Paper 2, better question choice, and a rehearsed oral structure. Not reachable: unread set texts, and meaningful change in language control. The useful block is short, frequent, and targeted only at the first list. No grade can be promised and nobody should offer one, whatever the fee or the timescale.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-l.closingHeading: Send the marked scripts and let them say what is wrong
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-l.closingBody: An IB DP English A Language and Literature home tutor in Abu Dhabi is worth paying for once the diagnosis is specific. Send three or four of your child's own returned pieces with the teacher's comments on them, say which component worries you most, and the free trial lesson will name which of the four criteria is costing the marks and what the first fortnight should change. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, every word submitted stays your child's own, and nothing on this page promises a grade or a number of marks.

intro.heading: What a parent can actually inspect in this subject, week by week
paragraphs: English A Language and Literature is the Diploma subject where parents are least able to tell whether progress is happening. In Maths a wrong answer is wrong. Here a parent reads an essay that sounds articulate, sees a 4 on the report, and has no way to connect the two. The gap is not in the writing. It is that the mark was awarded against four named criteria, and nobody outside the classroom has been shown which of those four was weak.

Abu Dhabi families feel this more acutely than most, because the cohort is unusually mixed. In a single Diploma class on Al Reem Island there will be students who have been in English-medium schools since Foundation Stage sitting next to students who arrived in Year 10 from a different system, and both are taking the same paper against the same criteria. A report grade of 4 means something different in each case, and a tutor who cannot say which criterion produced it is guessing.

This page is therefore built around evidence rather than reassurance. Each component is set out with its duration, its weighting at both levels, and the criterion letters it is marked against, with the mark allocation for each. There is a worked description of what an examiner's comment on a Paper 1 actually means in practice. There is a week-by-week account of what improvement looks like when it is real, and what it looks like when a student is simply writing longer essays. And there is a plain explanation of the one component that can legitimately be drafted and redrafted under supervision, the Higher Level Essay, and the boundary a tutor must not cross on it.

The evidence standard cuts both ways, which is the point. If four sessions produce a marked Paper 1 where criterion B has moved from 2 to 4 out of 5, that is visible and checkable. If four sessions produce a student who writes more fluently and scores the same, that is visible too, and a parent is entitled to ask what the next four hours will do differently. Our session notes exist so that question can be asked with the documents open.

ADEK licenses and inspects the private schools these students attend, and publishes its own inspection outcomes, so a school report sits inside a wider framework a parent can read. What ADEK does not do is explain why one child's comparative essay scored 17 out of 30 and another's scored 24. That explanation lives in the criteria, and the criteria are public. Most of the work on this page is making them usable. One further local point shapes the evidence a family can gather: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff in the emirate from taking paid private tutoring work with students enrolled at their own school, so the obvious shortcut of asking your child's own English teacher for paid sessions is closed here. That makes the marked script, released by the school and read by someone independent, the central document rather than an optional extra.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-l.programmesIntro: The evidence a parent can inspect changes shape at each stage of the IB continuum. These are the three stages Abu Dhabi families most often buy English support against, and what counts as proof of progress in each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme English A: Language and Literature
programmes.description: Three areas of exploration organise the course: readers, writers and texts; time and space; and intertextuality. Assessment is a guided textual analysis paper, a comparative essay paper, an individual oral, and at Higher Level an essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words. Marks come from criterion-referenced judgements, not from a mark scheme of right answers, which is why evidence of progress has to be read criterion by criterion.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts frequently include students who joined an English-medium school partway through secondary. The course does not adjust for that, and neither do the criteria, so the useful first piece of evidence for one of these students is a marked unseen analysis rather than a teacher's general impression.

programmes.name: MYP Language and Literature
programmes.description: Four criteria run through MYP Language and Literature: analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. The letters change meaning at Diploma level but the habit does not, and a student who has learned to read a criterion descriptor and locate their own work inside it arrives in DP1 able to use feedback. That skill is worth more than any amount of extra reading.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi continuum schools report MYP achievement on a 1 to 8 scale per criterion, which gives a parent in Khalifa City or Al Raha Gardens a far more legible baseline than a single overall letter. Keeping those criterion scores from MYP 5 makes the first Diploma report much easier to interpret.

programmes.name: IGCSE First Language English into DP1
programmes.description: Many Abu Dhabi students arrive in DP1 from Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE English rather than from MYP. IGCSE rewards accurate, well-organised directed writing and close reading against a mark scheme. Diploma Language and Literature rewards argument about how a text constructs meaning for a reader. The gap between those two is the most common cause of a disappointing first Diploma essay from a student who scored a 9 or an A star.
programmes.countryNote: This transition is a measurable one. A student who scored highly at IGCSE and lands a 4 on a first Diploma unseen paper has a specific, diagnosable gap, usually in criterion B, and it closes in a small number of sessions once named. Families often book a short block in the first term of DP1 for exactly this reason.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-l.subjectsIntro: The components and skills an Abu Dhabi family buys hours against, with the criterion each is actually judged on and what a weak performance looks like on paper.

subjects.name: Paper 1: guided textual analysis
subjects.description: Unseen non-literary text with a guiding question. Standard Level candidates analyse one passage; Higher Level candidates analyse two. Marked against criteria A to D at five marks each. The usual failure is feature-spotting: naming a metaphor and a rhetorical question without saying what either does to a reader.

subjects.name: Paper 2: comparative essay
subjects.description: An unseen general question answered through two literary works studied in class. Criterion A carries ten marks here and criterion B another ten, so knowledge and analysis dominate. Essays fail by running two separate summaries in parallel instead of building one comparative argument.

subjects.name: Individual Oral
subjects.description: A fifteen-minute oral examining a global issue through one non-literary extract and one literary extract, followed by examiner questions. Forty marks across four criteria. The commonest weakness is a global issue so broad that neither extract illuminates it specifically.

subjects.name: Higher Level Essay
subjects.description: An essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words developing a line of inquiry about one literary work or one non-literary body of work studied in the course. The only component that can be drafted, supervised and improved over weeks, which makes it the most legible evidence of progress in the subject.

subjects.name: Non-literary bodies of work
subjects.description: Advertising, political speech, journalism, photography, graphic novels and digital media are studied as bodies of work, not as single texts. Standard Level covers two bodies of work and Higher Level three. Students who treat these as warm-up material for the literature arrive at Paper 1 underprepared.

subjects.name: Literary works and the works requirement
subjects.description: Standard Level studies four literary works, Higher Level six, chosen to meet requirements on period, place and form. A student should know which of their works are available for Paper 2 and which are reserved for the oral or the essay, and surprisingly many do not.

subjects.name: Areas of exploration
subjects.description: Readers, writers and texts; time and space; intertextuality. These frame how texts are taught and are the vocabulary examiners use. A student who can place a question inside the right area of exploration writes a more focused answer than one working from memory of a class discussion.

subjects.name: The learner portfolio
subjects.description: A mandatory record of the student's own work across the course, not directly assessed but the source material for the oral and the Higher Level Essay. A thin portfolio in DP1 becomes a scramble in DP2, and a full one makes both the essay and the oral substantially cheaper to prepare.

subjects.name: Criterion-referenced self-marking
subjects.description: Reading a descriptor and locating one's own paragraph inside it. This is the skill that converts a tutor's feedback into independent improvement, and it is the fastest route from a 4 to a 5 for a student whose writing is already fluent.

subjects.name: Timed writing under examination conditions
subjects.description: Paper 1 and Paper 2 are written by hand under time pressure. A student who produces excellent untimed essays and weak timed ones has a planning problem rather than a knowledge problem, and that is diagnosable from a single marked script.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-l.regionsTitle: Where Abu Dhabi Language and Literature students study, and what the evidence looks like locally
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-l.regionsIntro: Reporting conventions differ between Abu Dhabi schools, and so does the amount of marked work a family ever sees. The notes below describe what parents in each area most often bring to a first session.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Mixed-intake Diploma cohorts where a single class can span first-language and recently arrived English users. Parents here usually arrive with a report grade and no marked script, and the first useful step is obtaining one.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Established international schools with detailed criterion-level reporting. Families here often have the evidence already and want help reading it, which is a shorter and cheaper engagement than a full diagnosis.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Large villa communities feeding several curricula. Many students here transferred from IGCSE into DP1 and carry a strong IGCSE grade alongside a weak first Diploma essay, which is a specific and fixable pattern.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Continuum intake with MYP criterion histories available. Where a family kept MYP criterion scores, the Diploma baseline is far easier to establish and the first session can go straight to the writing.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Older island neighbourhoods with long-standing schools. Afternoon traffic on the Corniche approach makes a 4pm start unrealistic for most households, so evening slots dominate.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Central districts with a high proportion of bilingual households where Arabic is the home language and English the school language. Criterion D, language, is the most common specific weakness and responds quickly to targeted work.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: Newer housing with long commutes to island schools. Students here often do their best written work at weekends, which makes a Saturday morning session more productive than a weekday evening one.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Mainland communities where families compare one-to-one against group options closely. For essay subjects the comparison usually favours one-to-one, because the feedback has to be on this student's paragraph.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Saadiyat Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: These schools carry much of the emirate's established Diploma provision and generally report in criterion detail. Students we support attend schools across this cluster; the work is additional to their school course and never a substitute for the class teacher's marking.

sections.heading: The four components, their weightings and the criterion letters behind every mark
paragraphs: Standard Level candidates sit three components; Higher Level candidates sit four. Each is marked against criteria identified by letter, and the mark allocation differs by component, which is why a 5 on one paper and a 5 on another do not describe the same performance. A parent who knows which criterion carries ten marks and which carries five can read a report in a way that a general grade conversation does not permit.

On Paper 1 all four criteria carry five marks each, out of twenty. On Paper 2 the first two criteria carry ten marks each out of thirty, which means knowledge of the studied works and the quality of comparative analysis dominate and tidy organisation cannot rescue a thin argument. The Individual Oral is marked out of forty with ten marks on each criterion, so organisation and language carry proportionally more weight there than anywhere else. The Higher Level Essay is marked out of twenty across the same four criteria.

The weightings matter for where hours should go. At Standard Level the two written papers together carry the large majority of the grade and the oral the remainder. At Higher Level the load spreads across four components, with Paper 1 the single largest and the oral and essay each carrying a meaningful share. A Higher Level student weak on unseen analysis and strong on studied texts is losing marks in the biggest component, and that is an argument for spending the hours on Paper 1 rather than on more reading.

Published figures are revised between subject guide editions, so treat the table below as the shape of the assessment rather than as the final authority, and confirm current weightings and limits with your child's Diploma coordinator. The criterion letters and what each rewards are the stable part, and they are the part most useful to a parent.

sections.heading: Reading a marked Paper 1 the way an examiner read it
paragraphs: A marked Paper 1 is the single most useful document a parent in Abu Dhabi can obtain, and most never ask for one. It converts a report grade into four numbers, and the pattern of those four numbers tells you what kind of problem you have. The first session in almost every engagement begins here, which is why the diagnostic session exists as a format of its own.

A script with strong criterion A and weak criterion B is the most common pattern in this subject and the most reassuring. It means the student understood the passage and could not analyse it: they identified what the text says and stopped short of how it makes a reader think that. This moves quickly, because the understanding is already present and what is missing is a habit of asking a second question of every observation. Two or three sessions of working through the student's own sentences generally produces a visible shift.

Weak criterion A with respectable criterion B is rarer and slower. It usually means the student is applying a template of analytical moves without having read the passage carefully, which produces fluent paragraphs about a text they have partly misread. The remedy is unglamorous and effective: slow annotated reading before any writing, with the student required to state the passage's argument in one sentence before analysing anything. Weak criterion C indicates planning, and weak criterion D is usually either sentence control or register, each of which has its own short set of drills.

The important thing about this reading is that it is checkable by the person paying. If a tutor says criterion B is the problem, the next marked script either shows movement in B or it does not. There is no need to take a view on teaching style. Four sessions and two marked scripts are enough evidence for a parent to decide whether to continue, and that is a far better basis for a decision than a feeling that lessons seem to be going well.
bullets: Ask the school for a marked script with criterion marks, not just a grade
Strong A and weak B: understanding present, analysis missing, moves fast
Weak A and stronger B: template applied to a partly misread text, moves slowly
Weak C: a planning problem, visible in the essay's shape rather than its sentences
Weak D: register or sentence control, both drillable

sections.heading: The Higher Level Essay, and why it is the clearest evidence of progress available
paragraphs: The Higher Level Essay is 1,200 to 1,500 words developing a line of inquiry about one literary work or one non-literary body of work from the course. It is written over weeks, under the school's supervision, with drafts. That makes it unique in this subject: every other mark is produced in a room under time pressure, where a parent sees only the outcome, while the essay leaves a trail of dated documents.

Used properly, that trail is the best progress record a family will get. A line of inquiry submitted in week one, a first draft in week three, a marked draft in week four and a final version in week six are five documents a parent can read in order. Progress in criterion B shows up as observations gaining consequences. Progress in criterion C shows up as the essay stopping its tour of the work and committing to one argument. None of this requires a parent to be an English specialist; it requires the documents to exist and be dated.

The supervision boundary is strict and is worth saying aloud at the start of a block. A tutor may teach what each criterion rewards, discuss the line of inquiry and say whether it is answerable in 1,500 words, read a draft and identify where the argument stalls or where the word count is being spent badly, and teach the student to cut their own text. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, choose the line of inquiry, or provide a previous candidate's essay as a model to work from. Authorship has to stay with the student throughout, and schools increasingly ask for drafts precisely so that it can be shown to have done so.

Standard Level candidates do not sit this component, which changes the evidence picture for them. Without an essay, the legible proof of progress is a sequence of marked unseen papers and a recorded practice oral, which is why Standard Level engagements usually generate more timed writing than Higher Level ones do.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of real progress looks like, and what it does not
paragraphs: Parents are usually told that English takes time, and that is true in the sense that reading maturity accumulates slowly. It is misleading as a description of criterion-level improvement, which often moves in weeks once the right criterion has been identified. The distinction is worth holding onto, because it is what separates a block of tutoring that is working from one that has become a habit.

A working engagement looks like this. Week one produces a cold timed paper and four criterion marks. Week two targets the weakest single criterion and nothing else. Week three applies it to a second timed paper and the marks are compared, not described. Weeks four and five extend the same change to Paper 2, where the mark allocation is different and therefore the technique shifts. Weeks six to eight either move to the oral and the essay, or return to the first criterion if it has not held. At every point there is a document and a number.

An engagement that has stopped working looks different, and the signs are specific. Sessions discuss texts rather than the student's writing. No new timed work has been produced for three weeks. Feedback has become encouragement. The student can describe what the tutor says but cannot apply it without the tutor present. Any of those is a reason to change the plan, and a tutor who cannot name the criterion they are currently working on should be asked to.

Grade movement itself is a lagging and lumpy signal. A student can improve two criterion marks and stay on the same overall grade for a term, which is normal and not a failure. For that reason the record we keep is criterion-level rather than grade-level, and the honest answer to how fast a grade moves is that it depends on how far through a boundary the student already was, which the school can tell you and we cannot.

sections.heading: The Individual Oral: the mark families almost never see
paragraphs: The Individual Oral is examined inside the school, recorded, and marked out of forty across four criteria at ten marks each. Most parents in Abu Dhabi never hear it. It is the component where a student can lose a large number of marks for reasons that have nothing to do with their English, and where preparation pays back most predictably.

The structure is specific. A candidate selects a global issue, then one extract from a non-literary body of work and one from a literary work studied in the course, and argues how the issue is presented in and through both. Fifteen minutes, with examiner questions at the end. The most common structural failure is a global issue chosen so broadly that it floats above both extracts: identity, or inequality, stated at a level of generality where no particular line of either text is required. A sharper issue produces a sharper oral almost automatically, because the extracts then have work to do.

The second failure is balance. Candidates who know their literary work well and their non-literary body of work vaguely spend eleven minutes on one and three on the other, which damages criteria A and C simultaneously. The fix is mechanical: time the practice, out loud, with a clock visible, and record it. Students almost always discover that their internal sense of balance is wrong by several minutes.

Because the oral is internally examined and recorded, a practice recording made at home is the closest available proxy and a genuinely useful piece of evidence. A student who has recorded themselves twice, listened back, and cut their own opening is in a different position from one who has rehearsed in their head. This is also work a tutor can support without any authorship question arising, since the words are spoken by the candidate in the examination itself.

sections.heading: Reading an Abu Dhabi school report alongside what ADEK publishes
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. That gives a parent two different documents about their child's education: a school report about the student, and an inspection report about the school. They answer different questions and are often confused for each other.

An inspection outcome describes provision: teaching quality, leadership, outcomes across the school. It tells you something real about the environment, and nothing about whether your child's criterion B is weak. A strong inspection outcome does not mean a particular Diploma class is being marked generously or harshly, and a parent reading a disappointing English grade should not look to the inspection report for an explanation. The explanation is in the marked script.

Predicted grades are the other document families misread. A predicted grade is the school's professional estimate for the IB, based on performance so far, and it is used in university applications. It is not a mark and it is not a promise. When a predicted grade sits below what a family expected, the productive question to the school is which components produced it and what would have to change, rather than whether the prediction can be revised. Schools answer the first question willingly and the second rarely.

One local rule is worth knowing. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the federal private tuition permit carries a code of conduct with the same restriction. So the natural instinct of asking your child's English teacher for paid sessions is not available in this emirate, and that is a regulatory position rather than a school preference.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, the learner portfolio, and what a tutor must not touch
paragraphs: Two components in this subject involve work produced outside an examination room, and both are covered by the IB's academic honesty requirements. The Higher Level Essay is submitted as the candidate's own, and the learner portfolio is a record of the candidate's own work across the course. A breach of authenticity is a matter for the student's Diploma, not merely an embarrassment for the tutor, which is why the boundary belongs on a page about evidence.

What a tutor may do is substantial, and it is where the value sits. Teach the criteria and what each rewards. Discuss a line of inquiry and say whether it is answerable at the required length. Read the student's draft and name where an observation lacks a consequence, where the structure tours rather than argues, where the register slips. Teach cutting and planning as transferable techniques. Mark a timed paper honestly against the criteria. Model analytical reading on a text the student is not submitting, which is a particularly efficient way to teach criterion B without touching assessed material.

What a tutor may not do is supply any part of the submitted text. No sentences for insertion, no paragraph rewritten into its final form, no line of inquiry chosen on the student's behalf, no previous candidate's essay offered as a template, and no editing pass that leaves the prose better than the student could produce unaided. The test is simple: could the student have written this version themselves, and do they understand why it is better? If the answer to either is no, the line has been crossed.

This matters in the UAE search results specifically, because operations selling completed Internal Assessments and essays advertise openly in this market, one of them with a published price. A family comparing providers should treat any offer to hand over finished assessed material as a risk to their child's Diploma rather than as a convenience, and should expect a legitimate tutor to refuse it plainly and in writing.

sections.heading: Getting started, including what happens when the evidence says do nothing
paragraphs: The honest version of starting is that the first step costs nothing and the second step should be a diagnostic rather than a package. Ask the school for a marked script with criterion marks. Take the free trial lesson, one per family, with no card details taken, and bring that script to it. If no marked script is available, the trial can be built around a cold timed paper instead, which produces the same four numbers.

What follows is a stated weakest criterion and an hours estimate. Sometimes the estimate is zero. A fluent Higher Level student scoring 4s whose marked scripts show balanced criterion marks across the board usually needs more reading and more timed practice rather than a tutor, and we say so. A student whose criterion D is weak because English is their third language needs something different again, and a short targeted block beats an open-ended weekly commitment.

Supply in this emirate is worth being candid about. Experienced Diploma English teachers are not rare, which makes this a better-covered subject than Theatre or Arabic A. Even so, if nobody suitable is free for the level and component you need, you are told that with a realistic date rather than being matched to a generalist. Lessons are delivered one to one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India, and that keeps the choice of tutor open rather than limited by driving distance.

On permits, the position is simple and checkable. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with eligible categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted at you. IB Gram holds no regulator licence or accreditation of any kind and operates no office in the UAE.

faqs.question: How do I know whether an English A Language and Literature tutor is actually working?
faqs.answer: Ask for two things: the criterion the tutor is currently working on, and the document that will test whether it moved. In this subject every mark is awarded against criteria identified by letter, so improvement is visible as a change in one of those marks on a comparable piece of timed writing. A marked script from week one and another from week four, read side by side, settle the question without anyone needing to take a view on teaching style. If no new timed work has been produced for three weeks, that is the signal to change the plan.

faqs.question: What is the difference between criterion A and criterion B on Paper 1?
faqs.answer: Criterion A is understanding and interpretation: has the candidate grasped what the passage is doing and read it accurately. Criterion B is analysis and evaluation: does the candidate explain how the text produces that effect on a reader, and judge how well it works. The commonest pattern in Abu Dhabi scripts is a strong A with a weak B, which means the student understood the passage and stopped at identifying features. That gap closes relatively quickly, because the understanding is already in place and what is missing is the habit of asking what each observation does.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Higher Level Essay, and where is the line?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a firm boundary. A tutor may teach what each criterion rewards, discuss whether a line of inquiry is answerable within 1,200 to 1,500 words, read the student's dated draft and name where the argument stalls or where words are being spent badly, and teach cutting as a technique. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a paragraph into final form, choose the line of inquiry, or provide another candidate's essay as a model. The test is whether the student could have produced that version unaided and understands why it is stronger.

faqs.question: My son scored a 9 at IGCSE English and a 4 on his first Diploma essay. What happened?
faqs.answer: This is one of the most common patterns in Abu Dhabi, and it is usually diagnosable rather than mysterious. IGCSE rewards accurate close reading and well-organised directed writing against a mark scheme. Diploma Language and Literature rewards an argument about how a text constructs meaning for a reader, judged against criteria rather than against expected points. A student with excellent IGCSE technique frequently writes a fluent, well-organised answer that never evaluates, which lands squarely in the middle of criterion B. It typically takes a small number of sessions once named.

faqs.question: How many literary works does my daughter have to study at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Higher Level candidates study six literary works and non-literary texts from three bodies of work; Standard Level candidates study four literary works and two bodies of work. The selections have to satisfy requirements on period, place and literary form, which the school manages. The practical point for a student is knowing which of their works are reserved for which component, because a work used in the Individual Oral is not then available for the Paper 2 comparative essay. Confirm the current requirements and your child's specific allocation with their Diploma coordinator.

faqs.question: How narrow should my son's global issue be for the Language and Literature oral?
faqs.answer: Narrower than most candidates choose. The oral asks a candidate to show how a global issue is presented in and through one non-literary extract and one literary extract, and a broad issue such as identity or inequality floats above both texts, which damages the knowledge and focus criteria at once. A sharper formulation forces specific lines to do work: how a particular publication frames migrant labour, for instance, rather than migration in general. Narrowing the issue is often the single change that moves an oral from the middle band to the upper one, and it costs one session.

faqs.question: Does the Individual Oral really need to be timed in practice?
faqs.answer: Yes, out loud and with a visible clock. The oral runs to a fixed length with examiner questions at the end, and candidates almost always misjudge balance between their two extracts when rehearsing internally, typically giving the literary work far more time than the non-literary body of work. Recording a practice run and listening back is uncomfortable and extremely efficient: most students cut their own opening after hearing it once. Because the words are the candidate's own and spoken in the examination, this is work a tutor can support with no authorship question arising.

faqs.question: How long before a tutor can tell us what is actually wrong with my child's essays?
faqs.answer: One marked script is usually enough to name the weakest criterion, and the free trial lesson can produce that from a cold timed paper if the school has not released one. What takes longer is establishing whether the pattern is stable: a single weak script can reflect a bad day, a misread passage or a timing failure rather than a persistent gap. Two comparable pieces of timed writing across three or four weeks give a reliable answer. A tutor who offers a diagnosis after a conversation and no document is guessing.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting in the second term of DP2?
faqs.answer: It depends on the component. Paper 1 technique responds to focused work in a matter of weeks, so late starts aimed at unseen analysis are often worthwhile. The Higher Level Essay is a different matter: if the internal deadline has passed, that mark is fixed and no amount of hours will reach it. The Individual Oral may also already be examined. The useful first step late in the course is to establish which marks are still open, because hours spent on closed components are the most common way families waste money in this subject.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 2 need a different approach from Paper 1?
faqs.answer: Because the mark allocation is different. On Paper 1 all four criteria carry equal marks, so organisation and language matter proportionally more. On Paper 2 knowledge of the studied works and comparative analysis carry ten marks each out of thirty, so a tidy, well-written essay that compares two works superficially scores poorly while a slightly rough essay with a genuine comparative argument does better. Students who prepare for Paper 2 by revising plot summaries are preparing for the wrong criterion, and that is visible in a marked script within one paragraph.

faqs.question: Will the tutor follow my child's school reading list or teach different texts?
faqs.answer: The school's works are the ones that count, so the comparative essay and the oral work from your child's own set texts rather than from a tutor's preferred list. The exception is deliberate: teaching analytical technique on a text the student is not submitting is often the most efficient way to build criterion B, because there is no assessment pressure on the passage and no authorship question at all. For Paper 1 the passages are unseen anyway, so practice material is drawn from a wide range of non-literary sources.

faqs.question: Does my daughter's English grade affect UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is assessed against the certificate rather than one subject, and the requirements differ by curriculum track. On the sourced British track, candidates must show five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels. The American track sets English proficiency through IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing. We do not publish an IB threshold because we have not read one on an official Ministry page. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around Ramadan and the Abu Dhabi school timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and essay subjects adapt better than most. School days shorten across the UAE during Ramadan and family evenings reorganise around Iftar, so the usable window for most Abu Dhabi households moves later. Reading a marked paragraph and rewriting it is productive in a 60 or 75-minute post-Iftar slot in a way that long timed practice is not, so the content of sessions shifts rather than the frequency. Internal deadlines falling during or just after Ramadan are worth mapping in advance, because the available working hours in those weeks are genuinely fewer.

faqs.question: What do the session notes actually contain?
faqs.answer: Four things: which criterion the session targeted, what was worked on in the student's own writing, what the student is doing before the next session, and which document will show whether it worked. They go out the same day and they are deliberately specific enough to be argued with. A note saying a student is making good progress is useless to a parent; a note saying criterion B was targeted through three of her own paragraphs and a second timed paper is due next Tuesday can be checked against the paper when it arrives.

That record is the whole offer: not a promise about a grade, but evidence you can inspect while it happens.

intro.heading: A literature-only Diploma is a reading problem before it is a writing problem
paragraphs: English A: Literature is the narrower of the two English A courses and the more demanding in one specific way: there is nowhere to hide from the works. Standard Level students study nine, Higher Level thirteen, drawn from a prescribed reading list and from the school's own choices, and spread across three areas of exploration with minimum requirements for works in translation, literary forms, periods and regions. Confirm those counts with your child's teacher and against the current subject guide, because they are the backbone of the course and no figure in this project has been verified against ibo.org.

That structure has a direct consequence for tutoring. In a course where the assessment is drawn from works the student is supposed to have read, a student who has not read them cannot be rescued by technique. Paper 2 is written without the texts in the room. The individual oral draws on two of the works studied. The Higher Level essay develops a line of inquiry from one of them. A tutor who pretends otherwise ends up delivering plot summaries at a specialist hourly rate, which is a poor use of a family's money and a worse use of a term.

Where outside help genuinely earns its fee is narrower and quite specific. The unseen passage in Paper 1 is a skill, and it is teachable. Writing comparatively from memory is a technique, and it is drillable. Building a usable store of short quotations rather than a vague recollection of a novel is a method, and most students have never been shown one. Turning a loose impression of a poem into a statement about how its construction produces its effect is a habit, and it transfers across every work on the list.

The failure pattern in Abu Dhabi cohorts has a recognisable shape. Students arrive from First Language English and English Literature at IGCSE, where an accurate, well-expressed personal response to a set text earns good marks. The Diploma asks for an argument about construction, and asks for it about an unseen passage the student has no context for and about two works held only in memory. The adjustment is real, it is not a matter of effort, and it accounts for most of the gap between a confident Year 11 and a middling DP1 report.

ADEK licenses and inspects the private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection ratings, and the schools here run a wide spread of curricula, so works lists differ considerably between campuses in the same community. Arabic, Islamic education and social studies run alongside the licensed curriculum as well, which puts a real squeeze on reading time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Support here is one-to-one over live video, with passages and drafts annotated on a shared screen.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-a-literature-hom.programmesIntro: The three routes below feed English A: Literature in Abu Dhabi schools, and each leaves a student fluent in one thing and unprepared for another. Knowing which route a student took predicts the first fortnight's work.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Language and Literature
programmes.description: MYP assesses analysing, organising, producing text and using language, with tasks produced over days rather than under exam conditions. Students arriving this way usually grasp that analysis means explaining how a choice creates an effect. What they have rarely done is sustain an argument about two works at once, from memory, in ninety minutes.
programmes.countryNote: Only a minority of Diploma students in this emirate come through MYP, mostly from the schools running the full continuum. For them the first block tends to be timed-conditions practice rather than skill teaching, which is a shorter and cheaper intervention than families anticipate.

programmes.name: IGCSE English Literature
programmes.description: IGCSE Literature teaches close reading of set texts and rewards a well-organised personal response supported by quotation. It builds genuine confidence. It also rewards a register the Diploma marks down: assured summary, appreciation of the writer's skill, and an argument about meaning rather than about construction.
programmes.countryNote: This is the dominant route into English A: Literature in Abu Dhabi, given the size of the British-curriculum cohort here. The signature first Diploma script from these students reads well, covers the text accurately, and sits in the middle band because it never explains a mechanism.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme English A: Literature
programmes.description: A literature-only course. Paper 1 is a guided analysis of previously unseen literary material, with Higher Level students analysing two passages where Standard Level analyse one. Paper 2 is a comparative essay on works studied, written without the texts. The individual oral examines a global issue through two of the works. Higher Level adds a written essay developed from the student's own line of inquiry.
programmes.countryNote: Works lists differ sharply between Abu Dhabi schools, even neighbouring ones, so the first thing any session establishes is which works this student is actually studying. Generic preparation on commonly taught novels is a waste of a specialist hour if the school chose differently.

programmes.name: Extended Essay in English
programmes.description: A 4,000-word research essay on a literary question, supervised in school and marked externally. The reliable failure is a question wide enough to invite a tour of a novel. Support is process coaching and feedback on drafts the student has produced, with the essay staying entirely their own work.
programmes.countryNote: Literature students in this emirate often choose a work from their own cultural background for the Extended Essay, which is a strong instinct provided there is published criticism they can reach and cite. Checking that before the question is fixed saves a term.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-a-literature-hom.subjectsIntro: Literature students usually book it alongside something else. The subjects below are the common pairings in Abu Dhabi requests, with what each assesses and where the Literature student typically needs support.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis of unseen literary passages, a comparative essay written from memory, an individual oral across two works, and at Higher Level an essay from the student's own line of inquiry. Marks leak to summary, to appreciation in place of argument, and to quotations recalled approximately.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The same literary skills applied alongside non-literary texts, with Paper 1 set on unseen non-literary material. Students sometimes move between the two courses early in DP1, and that decision belongs with the Diploma coordinator rather than with a tutor.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language-acquisition course with reading, listening, writing and oral components. A student whose marks are lost on language rather than on literary argument, and whose reading load is genuinely unmanageable, may belong here instead.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Papers plus a historical investigation with a source-evaluation section. Literature students take it often, and the two reinforce each other: period context sharpens reading of a nineteenth-century novel, and close reading sharpens source evaluation.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with commentaries and a prescribed-title essay. Literature students write confidently and often loosely, reaching for interpretation as a knowledge question. The repair is a claim, a counterclaim and a real example in every paragraph.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in UAE private schools alongside the licensed international curriculum, with placement set by a student's background. For a Literature student it is the subject whose own reading load competes most directly with the works list.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Papers across approaches and options plus an internal investigation. A frequent pairing with Literature in this emirate, and the write-up of the investigation is where those students usually want structural rather than content help.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Comparative study, process portfolio and exhibition, all submitted. Students pairing it with Literature carry a heavy documentation load alongside a heavy reading load, which makes the term calendar the first thing to plan.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Two papers with technology permitted, plus an exploration. The usual maths route for a humanities-weighted Diploma, and the exploration is where a tutor's involvement stays strictly feedback on the student's own draft.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-a-literature-hom.regionsIntro: What changes between parts of Abu Dhabi in this subject is the works list, the size of the cohort and how much of the evening is left for reading. The notes below cover each.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Long-established island schools with experienced English departments and works lists that tend to be ambitious. Students here usually get good teaching on the works and want help with unseen passages and with writing Paper 2 from memory.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Largely English-first intakes and settled cohorts, so classes are less mixed than elsewhere in the emirate. The commonest request from here is for a confident writer stuck in the middle band because the essays appreciate rather than argue.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: A mobile international population feeding several schools, with students joining Diploma cohorts mid-course more often than anywhere else in the city. Those students arrive having missed works the rest of the class read a term ago.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Falah
regions.note: Outer residential communities with long school runs in both directions. Reading time is the scarce resource here rather than tuition time, so the useful support pattern is fortnightly, with works read between sessions.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Large villa communities with big year groups nearby. Cohorts are sizeable, which means fewer individually annotated essays per student, so families often arrive with several marked pieces and no clear diagnosis.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: Newer campuses whose works lists vary a great deal and change as departments settle. Establishing which works are actually being studied is the first thing a session does, because preparation on the wrong novel is worse than none.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Central, residential and close to most island schools. The constraint is the number of subjects stacked into an evening alongside the mandatory UAE subjects, which is why the reading plan matters more than the session count.

regions.name: Mussafah and Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Mainland communities with the widest spread of prior schooling in any Literature class in the emirate. The question of whether a student is in the right English course comes up most often from these postcodes, and it belongs with the coordinator.

schoolClusters.city: Schools with long-settled Diploma English departments
schoolClusters.note: These are the campuses where the works list has been stable for several years, teaching on the works is strong, and the tutoring request is nearly always about unseen passages or about writing comparatively from memory rather than about the texts themselves.

schoolClusters.city: Schools where the Diploma sits beside a large British-curriculum cohort
schoolClusters.note: Students here come into English A: Literature straight from IGCSE Literature in the same building, which produces a very consistent first-term problem: strong, readable essays that explain meaning rather than construction.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving the mainland and outer communities
schoolClusters.note: A broad spread of curricula, fee levels and prior schooling, and the most mixed English classes in the emirate. Requests from this cluster are more likely to involve a works list the student has not finished and a genuine question about course fit.

It is the most self-contained purchase in this course because it needs no knowledge of the school's works list, and it is the component that moves fastest. Higher Level students drill both passages rather than one.

sections.heading: Literature or Language and Literature: what the choice actually changes
paragraphs: Families in this emirate regularly arrive unsure which of the two English A courses their child is on, and occasionally the student is not certain either. The distinction matters because it changes what Paper 1 contains and what the oral draws on, and therefore what any support should consist of.

Literature studies literary works only. Its Paper 1 sets unseen literary material, poetry or prose, and its individual oral examines a global issue through two of the literary works studied. Language and Literature studies literary works alongside non-literary texts, sets unseen non-literary material in Paper 1, and pairs a literary extract with a non-literary one in the oral. Both run at Standard and Higher Level, and both add a written essay at Higher Level.

Neither course is easier, and the common belief that Literature is the harder one is only half right. Literature demands more sustained reading and offers no escape from the works. Language and Literature demands familiarity with text types a student may never have been taught to read, and the unseen material can be genuinely alien. The table sets out the comparison properly, which is useful both for a family choosing in Year 11 and for one working out why a student is struggling in DP1. Moving between the two courses is possible early in DP1 and becomes impractical after that, so the question is worth asking in the first term rather than in the second. The decision belongs with the Diploma coordinator, who knows the timetable, the class sizes and what the student's writing actually looks like.
