abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-b-home-tutor.programmesIntro: English B sits in a sequence of language-acquisition courses, and which one a student came from decides whether they need language teaching, exam technique, or a conversation with the coordinator about the wrong course.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Language Acquisition
programmes.description: MYP language acquisition runs across phases rather than year groups, assessing listening, reading, speaking and writing against four criteria. Students who reach the upper phases arrive in English B comfortable with the skill categories and used to being assessed on all four. What they usually lack is any experience of a timed receptive paper, because MYP assessment is rarely run that way.
programmes.countryNote: A minority of Abu Dhabi Diploma students come through MYP. Where they do, the English B diagnosis is usually straightforward: the language is in place and the purchase needed is a short block of timed-paper practice rather than a term of teaching.

programmes.name: IGCSE English as a Second Language
programmes.description: Cambridge offers English as a Second Language in a form with a speaking component and one without, and the syllabus codes differ accordingly. It builds exactly the right foundations for English B: reading for gist and detail, directed writing, and a graded speaking test. Students arrive able to handle the task types and often underestimate the step up in text length and abstraction.
programmes.countryNote: This is the dominant route into English B in Abu Dhabi, and it produces the most predictable first-term problem: a student who scored well at IGCSE and finds the Diploma's longer reading texts and five themes considerably more demanding than expected.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme English B
programmes.description: English B is a language-acquisition course at Standard or Higher Level, organised around five prescribed themes: identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organisation and sharing the planet. Assessment covers a productive writing task, receptive papers in listening and reading, and an individual oral. Higher Level students additionally study two literary works, and the Higher Level oral is based on an extract from one of them.
programmes.countryNote: English B classes in this emirate are unusually mixed, because intakes are. The practical consequence is that a single class contains students who need vocabulary work and students who need examination technique, and the teacher cannot run both courses at once inside one timetable.

programmes.name: Extended Essay and the bilingual diploma
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word research project supervised in school, and an English B student writing it in English is doing so in their second language, which is a workload question as much as a language one. Separately, the award of a bilingual diploma depends on the combination of language courses a student takes, and the conditions should be confirmed with the Diploma coordinator.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Abu Dhabi often ask whether English B blocks a bilingual diploma. The conditions are set by the IB and administered by the school, so the coordinator is the only reliable source. No external tutor can confirm a student's eligibility, and none should claim to.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-b-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: English B seldom appears alone in a request from this emirate. The subjects below are the common pairings, with what each assesses and where an English B student usually needs the help.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A writing task from a choice of prompts and text types, a listening paper, a reading paper, and an individual oral, with two literary works added at Higher Level. Marks leak to the wrong text type, to listening practised only passively, and to orals that describe a stimulus instead of developing an argument from it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The first-language course, with unseen non-literary analysis in Paper 1 and a comparative literary essay in Paper 2. Some English B students are capable of this course and placed below it, and some English A students would be better served here. Either way the decision is the coordinator's.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in UAE private schools alongside the licensed international curriculum, with placement determined by a student's background rather than preference. A student taking both Arabic and English B is carrying two language courses, which is a real timetable load.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with commentaries and a prescribed-title essay. For a second-language student, TOK is often harder than any subject, because the essay rewards abstraction and precision at once. Structural teaching helps more here than vocabulary work.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Papers plus a research project at Higher Level. A frequent pairing with English B in this emirate. The case-study reading in Business is dense, and a student struggling with English B reading speed will feel it in this subject too.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Papers with data response and essays, plus a portfolio of commentaries. Command-term precision matters enormously, and second-language students lose marks for answering a different command term rather than for not knowing the content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Two papers with technology permitted, plus an exploration. Often the lowest-friction subject for an English B student, because the language load is lightest, though the exploration write-up is an exception that catches people out.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Papers plus a scientific investigation. The terminology volume in Biology is larger than in any other science, which makes it the science where an English B student most often needs vocabulary support alongside content teaching.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Papers across approaches and options plus an internal investigation. Studies have to be recalled in precise terms, and a second-language student's marks often turn on the accuracy of a few dozen phrases rather than on understanding.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-b-home-tutor.regionsIntro: In English B the local variable is the intake of the school and the length of the evening. Both affect how many paid hours a family actually needs and when they can be scheduled.

regions.name: Mussafah and Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Mainland communities feeding schools with the widest intake spread in the emirate, which means the largest English B cohorts and the most mixed ones. Requests from here are more often for genuine language support than for examination technique.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Villa communities with long evening drives to the island, where the travel premium on a visiting tutor is most obvious. For a course that benefits from short, frequent sessions, the online format changes the arithmetic substantially here.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: A mobile international population with students joining cohorts mid-course. Those students are the ones most likely to have been placed into English B on arrival without a proper assessment, which is worth revisiting with the coordinator.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Falah
regions.note: Outer residential communities where the school run consumes the late afternoon. Sessions realistically start after 18:00, and three short sessions a week work better for language practice than one long one.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Largely English-first intakes, so English B cohorts here are small and often contain students who could manage English A. For those families the honest first question is whether the course is right rather than how many hours to buy.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Older island neighbourhoods near long-established schools with experienced language departments. Requests from this cluster lean towards the listening paper and the individual oral rather than towards vocabulary.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: Newer campuses with commuting intakes and varying provision. Higher Level English B, with its two literary works, is not offered everywhere, and families here sometimes need help with works the school covers lightly.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah

sections.heading: What English B support costs in Abu Dhabi, and when cheap is correct
paragraphs: This is the one Diploma subject where the budget end of the tutoring market is not a trap. Language acquisition responds to frequency and exposure, which a capable graduate speaker can provide perfectly well at AED 50 to AED 100 an hour. Examination technique responds to someone who has read the subject guide and knows what the papers reward, which is a different person and a different price. A family that buys both appropriately spends considerably less than a family that buys either exclusively.

The arithmetic is worth doing explicitly. Three short conversation and listening sessions a week at the budget band costs roughly the same per month as two specialist hours. The budget sessions move fluency and comprehension; the specialist hours move technique and will not move fluency. A student failing on vocabulary range needs the first. A student with good English losing marks for writing a blog post when the prompt required a formal letter needs the second. Buying four specialist hours a month for a vocabulary problem is the commonest overspend in this subject.

The table sets out the market as providers publish it, with what each band can honestly deliver for English B. Every figure is attributed and dated October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price list: our own model is hourly at the specialist end for technique work, with a free trial lesson before anything is booked. The column to read is the last one, because it is the one no competitor page in this search attempts.

sections.heading: Four components, and which ones are worth paying for
paragraphs: English B assesses a productive writing task, receptive skills in listening and reading, and an individual oral, with Higher Level adding two literary works that the Higher Level oral is built on. Receptive skills carry half the grade between them, which surprises families who have assumed that speaking and writing are the course.

The value of paid help differs sharply by component, and the reason is how much of each one is knowledge rather than fluency. The writing task is heavily technique-dependent, because the marks turn on choosing and executing the right text type: a formal letter, a blog entry, a set of instructions, an article, each with its own conventions. A student with good English can lose a substantial share of the available marks by writing fluently in the wrong register. That is teachable in a few hours and almost never taught at home.

Listening is the opposite. It improves with exposure, slowly, and no amount of specialist explanation accelerates it much. Reading sits between the two: speed and stamina come from reading volume, while the question-type techniques are teachable quickly. The oral is mostly technique at Standard Level, where the stimulus has to be used rather than described, and more knowledge-dependent at Higher Level, where the extract comes from a studied literary work. Confirm all weightings and formats with your child's teacher and the current subject guide; nothing here has been verified against ibo.org. The practical use of the table is to stop a family buying a comprehensive package across all four skills when two of the four are better served by a habit than by an invoice.

sections.heading: The listening paper, and why money cannot buy it quickly
paragraphs: Listening is the component families underestimate and the one that most resists a cheque. It carries a substantial share of the receptive marks, it is sat under timed conditions with recordings played a set number of times, and it is the skill that improves most slowly because it depends on accumulated hours of exposure rather than on explanation.

The specific problem for students in this emirate is accent range rather than comprehension as such. A student in an English-medium Abu Dhabi school hears English all day, mostly from teachers who are experienced at being understood by second-language students and who moderate their speech accordingly. The recordings in a listening paper do not. Natural pace, regional accents, overlapping speech and idiom all appear, and a student whose exposure has been entirely classroom-shaped meets them for the first time in an examination.

The cheap fix is also the effective one, which is unusual. Thirty minutes a day of unmoderated English audio, chosen for range rather than clarity, does more over a term than four specialist hours a month. News broadcasts, documentary audio, interview podcasts with several speakers, and anything where people talk over each other. What a paid session genuinely adds is a weekly timed paper with the answers discussed afterwards, so the student learns how the questions distribute marks and where they are losing them. One short block plus daily exposure beats a term of expensive sessions. Parents often find this suggestion disappointing, because it transfers the work from a provider back to the household, and it remains the only thing that reliably moves this component.

sections.heading: Standard or Higher Level English B: what the choice costs
paragraphs: Higher Level English B adds two literary works and bases the individual oral on an extract from one of them, which changes both the workload and the support bill. Families usually ask the question as though it were purely about ability. It is also about time and money, and the honest comparison is useful before DP1 rather than during it.

The case for Higher Level is real. It is a more substantial qualification, it suits a student whose English is strong enough that Standard Level would be unchallenging, and for some university routes a Higher Level language is useful. It also forces the kind of extended reading that improves everything else a second-language student does. The case against is equally real: two literary works in a second language, on top of six subjects and the core and the mandatory UAE subjects, is a genuine load, and a student who is in English B because their English is still developing is not the student for whom extra literary reading is the best use of the year.

The support cost difference is concrete rather than vague. A Standard Level student usually needs a short technique block and daily exposure. A Higher Level student often needs the same plus help with the two works, especially where a thin department has covered them lightly, which adds materially to the hours. The table sets out the comparison on the dimensions that actually decide it, and the Higher Level requirements of any university should be checked on that university's own admissions pages.

sections.heading: Five reasons two English B quotes differ by AED 200 an hour
paragraphs: Two providers can quote AED 80 and AED 280 for what a parent describes identically as English B help. Neither is necessarily wrong. They are selling different things, and the gap is explained by five variables that are worth knowing before any conversation about price.

The first is whether the tutor works from the subject guide. A tutor who can name the five prescribed themes, say what distinguishes a blog entry from an article in the writing task, and explain what the oral is assessed on is in a different market from a fluent speaker who will chat about current affairs. The second is whether the tutor marks written work to a standard rather than correcting it, which is a skill and a time cost. The third is Higher Level literary works, which narrow the pool sharply.

The remaining two are in the family's control. Format is the obvious one: a visiting tutor prices a drive across the emirate into the fee, and in a subject that wants three short sessions a week rather than one long one, that premium applies three times a week. Timing is the quieter one. Insisting on a 17:00 weekday slot narrows the pool to whoever is free in that hour, which in a language subject usually means paying more for less specialism. The table ranks all five by how much they actually move a quote, and the first three are the ones worth paying for while the last two are the ones worth giving up.

sections.heading: What the grade is actually for: equivalency, universities and the bilingual diploma
paragraphs: Parents in this emirate ask three separate questions about English B and they tend to arrive as one. Does it count for Ministry of Education equivalency. Does it satisfy a university's English requirement. Does it prevent a bilingual diploma. The answers are different and two of them are not ours to give.

Equivalency is a Ministry process administered through the emirate's attestation channel, not something a tutoring provider performs, influences or guarantees. For the British curriculum, published reporting sets out five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no lower than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the American track, English proficiency is specified as IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 in reading and writing, with SAT Math 450 for mathematics. No IB points threshold is published here, because none has been read on the Ministry's own pages.

University English requirements are set by each university and are usually satisfied through a recognised test rather than through a school qualification, so an English B grade may or may not substitute. Check it on the admissions page of the actual course. The bilingual diploma is awarded by the IB under its own conditions and administered by the school, which makes the Diploma coordinator the only reliable source for a specific student. Anyone telling you that tutoring secures equivalency, admission or a bilingual diploma is describing something they cannot deliver.

sections.heading: If you can only afford one block, buy this one
paragraphs: Plenty of families in this emirate are deciding between one tutoring block and none, across six subjects, and English B is competing with Mathematics and the sciences for the same money. The honest ranking inside this subject is clear enough to state.

Buy the writing-task technique block. Six to ten specialist hours spent on text types and their conventions changes a mark in a way nothing else in this subject does for the money, because the loss it fixes is pure knowledge: a student writing a fluent blog entry when the prompt required a formal proposal is losing marks they could keep tomorrow. Nothing else in English B has that property. Listening needs a term of exposure. Reading speed needs volume. The oral needs rehearsal. Only the writing task has a short, teachable, high-value gap.

If there is money for a second block, buy oral structure rather than more language practice, because most students describe the stimulus instead of using it to build an argument and that is a thirty-minute realisation rather than a term's work. Everything else in this subject is better bought with time than with money: thirty minutes a day of unmoderated audio, a book read for pleasure in English every few weeks, and a weekly timed paper the student marks against the answers themselves. That advice loses us sessions and it is still the right advice. A family with one block of money to spend across six subjects should also weigh whether English B is where it belongs at all, because a Mathematics or Chemistry gap is often costing more points.

sections.heading: Checking a language tutor's claims, and the permit position
paragraphs: English B attracts a wider range of providers than any other Diploma subject, because the barrier to entry looks low: a fluent English speaker can plausibly offer English help. That makes verification more useful here than elsewhere, and there are three checks a parent can run in a single conversation without any subject knowledge.

Ask which five themes the course is organised around. Ask what distinguishes the text types available in the writing task. Ask what the individual oral is assessed on at the level your child is taking, which differs between Standard and Higher Level. A tutor working at examination level answers all three immediately. A fluent speaker without the guide answers none of them, which does not make them useless for conversation practice at the budget rate; it makes them the wrong purchase at the specialist rate.

Then there is the permit, which is a factual matter rather than a judgement. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, issued free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, public and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's private tutor licensing service lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule of amounts, so none is quoted here. Separately, press reporting describes ADEK rules barring Abu Dhabi school staff from paid tutoring of their own enrolled students; verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document.
bullets: Ask for the five themes, the text types and what the oral assesses

sections.heading: Correction, feedback and what nobody may do with a written task
paragraphs: In a second-language course the honesty line is unusually easy to cross with good intentions, because improving a sentence looks like teaching. The principle to hold is that the student's own language is what is being assessed. A corrected piece of work tells the teacher what the tutor can do, not what the student can do, and it removes the information the teacher needs in order to help.

Useful feedback in this subject is specific and leaves the words alone. Naming a recurring error pattern, three tense slips in a paragraph, is teaching. Pointing out that the register does not match the text type required is teaching. Marking a task against the criteria and explaining which band it sits in is teaching. Rewriting the paragraph so it reads better is not, and it is what a great many cheap providers do because it is quick, visible and satisfying for everyone except the student.

The same holds for any assessed component anywhere on this site. Nothing is supplied, completed or edited to a finish by a tutor, official syllabus documents and past papers are linked rather than reproduced, and no page here promises a grade, a band or a number of marks. A predicted grade is the subject teacher's professional judgement from the work in front of them, and no external provider produces or validates one. One page ranking for these searches sells completed assessments outright, and the risk of that arrangement sits entirely with the student.

process.description: Tell us whether the problem looks like language, with limited vocabulary and listening difficulty, or technique, with good English losing marks on the paper. process.title: Send one marked writing task
process.description: A single returned writing task with the teacher's marks shows more than any description. The text type, the register and the error pattern are all visible in it. One free trial lesson per student, booked without card details, and it is spent on that task rather than on introductions.

process.title: Buy the technique block, not a term
process.description: Where the diagnosis is technique, the purchase is six to ten specialist hours with a defined end: text types learned, receptive paper techniques practised, oral structure rehearsed. Open-ended weekly arrangements in this subject drift for a year because nothing in them can be marked finished.

process.title: Set up the free half of the plan
process.description: Thirty minutes a day of unmoderated English audio chosen for accent range, a book read for pleasure every few weeks, and a weekly timed paper the student marks themselves. None of this costs anything, and it does more for listening and reading than any paid hour can.

process.title: Re-check the course fit if nothing moves
process.description: A student losing marks on everything, with a reading load that is genuinely unmanageable, may be in a course that does not fit either upwards or downwards. That is a conversation with the Diploma coordinator in the first part of DP1. Raising it costs us a booking and is the correct advice.

whyPoints.title: Two different purchases, named and priced separately
whyPoints.description: This page says plainly that language practice and examination technique are different products at different rates, and that buying one at the other's price is the commonest overspend in the subject. Most providers in this search sell a single undifferentiated hour at one price.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted as the market's, with the source named

whyPoints.title: Advice that reduces what we sell

whyPoints.title: Component-level honesty about value
whyPoints.description: The writing task has a short, teachable, high-value gap. Listening does not. That difference decides where a limited budget should go, and it is published in a table rather than hidden behind an offer of comprehensive support across all four skills.

faqs.question: How much should we expect to pay for English B help in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It depends which of two things you are buying. Conversation and listening practice is available at the budget end, with Tutopiya advertising from around AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, and at that price it does a real job. Examination technique sits at the specialist band: Unitors lists IB from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 table puts specialist work at AED 200-450 and above. Those are published figures from October 2026. Buying technique at the budget price, or practice at the specialist price, is where families lose money.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an English B tutor to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Support here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In this subject the saving matters more than in most, because language work rewards three short sessions a week rather than one long one, and a visiting fee prices a drive across the emirate into every single one of them. Removing the travel buys frequency, which is the thing language acquisition actually responds to.

faqs.question: Which single component gives the best return if we can only buy one block?
faqs.answer: The writing task. Six to ten specialist hours spent on text types and their conventions changes a mark in a way nothing else in English B does for the money, because the loss being fixed is knowledge rather than skill. A student writing a fluent blog entry when the prompt required a formal proposal is throwing away marks that could be kept immediately. Listening needs a term of exposure, reading speed needs volume, and the oral needs rehearsal. Only the writing task has a short, teachable, high-value gap in it.

faqs.question: Why is my child's English fine in class but weak in the listening paper?
faqs.answer: Because classroom English is moderated and examination audio is not. Teachers in English-medium Abu Dhabi schools are practised at being understood by second-language students, so they slow down, choose plainer words and avoid idiom without thinking about it. The recordings do none of that: natural pace, regional accents, overlapping speakers and colloquial phrasing all appear. A student whose entire exposure has been classroom-shaped meets all of it for the first time under exam conditions. Thirty minutes a day of unmoderated audio over a term closes more of that gap than paid hours will.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying a specialist rate for conversation practice?
faqs.answer: Generally no, and saying so costs us work. Speaking at length improves with frequency and with a patient partner who keeps the conversation going rather than correcting every sentence, and a capable graduate speaker at AED 50 to AED 100 an hour does that perfectly well. What a specialist adds is understanding of what the oral is assessed on, which is a short, one-off intervention rather than a weekly one. The efficient pattern is frequent cheap practice plus two to four specialist hours on structure, rather than weekly specialist conversation.

faqs.question: What does the individual oral actually assess at each level?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level it is built on a visual stimulus connected to one of the five prescribed themes, and the assessment rewards using the stimulus to develop and sustain an argument rather than describing what is in it. At Higher Level it is based on an extract from one of the two literary works studied, so it depends on the works having been read properly. Confirm the current format with your child's teacher, because the details matter and nothing in this project has been verified against ibo.org. Most students describe when they should be arguing.

faqs.question: Should my child take English B at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Only if their English is already strong enough that Standard Level would be unchallenging, and if the timetable has room. Higher Level adds two literary works in a second language on top of six subjects, the core, and the mandatory UAE subjects, and it bases the oral on an extract from one of them. The support bill roughly doubles, concentrated on the works and the oral. For a student still consolidating the language, extra literary reading is not the best use of the year, and Standard Level done well is a better outcome than Higher Level done partially.

faqs.question: My child was put into English B when they joined. Was that assessed properly?
faqs.answer: Worth asking, particularly for students who joined an Abu Dhabi school mid-course. Placement on arrival is sometimes made quickly from a short conversation, and a student with strong English can end up in a course that will not stretch them while a student who needs it can be placed in English A. The signal is where the marks go: strong scores across all four skills with no real difficulty suggests the wrong course. Moving between English A and English B is practical early in DP1 and awkward later, and the decision is the coordinator's.

faqs.question: Does an English B grade satisfy a university's English language requirement?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it has to be checked course by course rather than assumed. Many universities meet the requirement through a recognised test, with IELTS and TOEFL the common routes, and some accept a school qualification in place of one. The only reliable source is the admissions page of the specific course your child is applying to, since requirements vary between institutions and change between cycles. Treat any tutoring page's summary of them, including this one, as a prompt to verify rather than as an answer.

faqs.question: Do you offer any outcome-linked refund or grade promise?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone offering one. A grade depends on two years of a student's own work, on reading and listening done outside sessions, and on components marked by the school and by the IB, none of which a tutoring provider controls. An outcome-linked refund is either unenforceable or a sign that the published terms matter more than the teaching. What is offered here instead is a free trial lesson per student, a bounded block with a defined end, and an honest statement of what cannot be fixed.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor actually knows the English B course?
faqs.answer: Three questions in one conversation, and no subject knowledge needed on your side. Which five themes is the course organised around. What distinguishes the text types available in the writing task. What is the individual oral assessed on at the level my child is taking. Somebody working at examination level answers all three without hesitating. A fluent speaker who has not read the guide answers none, which is fine for conversation practice at the budget rate and poor value at AED 250 an hour. Ask before booking a block rather than after.

faqs.question: Can a tutor correct my child's writing task before it is handed in?
faqs.answer: They should not, and nor should a parent. In a language-acquisition course the student's own English is precisely what is being assessed, so a corrected piece tells the teacher what the tutor can write, not what the student can. It also removes the error pattern the teacher needs in order to teach. Useful feedback names the pattern instead: three tense slips in one paragraph, or a register that does not match the text type required. That leaves the words entirely the student's own and is far more useful to them.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an English B student in this emirate usually need?
faqs.answer: More frequent and shorter than families expect for the language half, and far fewer in total for the technique half. Two or three sessions of thirty to forty minutes a week beat one ninety-minute session for speaking and listening, because frequency is what language acquisition responds to. Technique is the opposite: six to ten hours in total, concentrated, with a defined end. The common mistake is one weekly hour forever, which is too infrequent to build fluency and too unfocused to fix technique, at the specialist price.

faqs.question: Does taking English B affect the bilingual diploma?
faqs.answer: The bilingual diploma is awarded by the IB under its own conditions and administered by your child's school, which makes the Diploma coordinator the only reliable source for a specific student. The conditions turn on the combination of language courses taken and, in some cases, on the language of other subjects, so the answer genuinely depends on the whole timetable rather than on English B alone. No external tutor can confirm eligibility and none should claim to. Ask the coordinator early, because the timetable decisions that affect it are made in DP1.

faqs.question: Do English B tutors in Abu Dhabi need a MoHRE permit, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: They do, and it is free. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, issued free of charge and valid for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, public and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's private tutor licensing service lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no schedule of amounts is published, none is quoted here.

faqs.question: What happens if no English B specialist is free at the time we want?
faqs.answer: You are told before anything is booked. Where no UAE-resident specialist covers the slot requested, the match comes from the wider pool of Diploma English B tutors working to Gulf Standard Time, most often from India, in the same online format and on the same hourly basis, with the tutor's location stated upfront rather than discovered afterwards. Several providers in this search route UAE families to non-UAE numbers without saying so. In this subject flexibility helps a great deal, because frequent short sessions need slots outside the weekday evening crush.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-b-home-tutor.closingHeading: Decide which half you are buying before you compare rates
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-b-home-tutor.closingBody: An IB DP English B home tutor in Abu Dhabi costs anywhere from AED 33 to AED 650 an hour on published figures, and the right number depends entirely on whether you need language practice or examination technique. Send one marked writing task, say which looks like the problem, and the free trial lesson will tell you which block to buy and what to do for free instead. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, every word submitted stays your child's own English, and nothing on this page promises a grade.

intro.heading: Where the money goes in English B, and where it should go
paragraphs: English B is a language acquisition course, and that single fact changes the economics of tutoring it. A Diploma Literature or Chemistry tutor is selling subject expertise, and the market prices expertise. An English B tutor is largely selling structured practice, feedback on register, and exposure to spoken English at examination pace. Those are real and valuable, and they do not require the top of the market. A family paying specialist rates for listening practice is paying for the wrong thing competently delivered.

The grade is split in a way most Abu Dhabi families never see written down. One paper covers productive skills, a single piece of writing in a chosen text type. The other covers receptive skills, listening and reading, and between them those two halves make up a quarter and a half of the grade respectively, with the individual oral assessment carrying the remaining quarter. So half the marks are in comprehension, which responds to volume and consistency, and a quarter is in writing, which responds to targeted feedback on a small number of pieces. Spending evenly across all three is a defensible plan. Spending evenly without knowing the split is an accident.

The expensive mistake in this subject happens before any tutor is hired. Students are placed in English A or English B at the start of DP1, and a placement that is wrong in either direction costs two years of friction. A strong English user parked in English B spends the Diploma under-challenged and may hit a ceiling in university applications. A student placed in English A who needed English B spends the same two years producing essays against literary criteria they cannot reach, and the tutoring bill climbs accordingly. Reviewing that placement in the first term is the single highest-value conversation available, and it is free: it happens with the school.

Abu Dhabi has a specific version of this problem. Diploma cohorts here commonly include students who speak English fluently in conversation and have never written formal English, students who arrived in Year 10 from a national-curriculum school, and students for whom English is a third language after Arabic and a home language. All three profiles can look identical in a classroom discussion and perform completely differently on a reading paper. A cold timed paper settles it in ninety minutes and costs one session.

This page is built around the money. It sets out the published market bands in AED and who publishes each figure, the arithmetic of a two-year commitment at those rates, which component gives the most marks per hour, the text-type conventions that make writing feedback efficient, and the proficiency requirements the Ministry of Education publishes for equivalency, so a family does not end up paying twice for the same English. Every figure is attributed, and none of them is an IB Gram price list.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-b-tutor.programmesIntro: Three language-acquisition routes feed Abu Dhabi Diploma classes, and each carries a different likely spend. The decision between them is made by the school, usually in the first weeks of DP1, and it is worth a parent's attention before any tutor is engaged.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme English B
programmes.description: A Group 2 language acquisition course at Standard or Higher Level, organised around five prescribed themes and a set of conceptual understandings covering audience, context, purpose, meaning and variation. Assessment is one writing task, one receptive-skills paper covering listening and reading, and an individual oral assessment. Higher Level adds two literary works studied in English.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the English B cohort is frequently the most mixed class in the school, spanning students who need genuine language support and students who are there because English A felt risky. Those two groups need opposite plans, and a single marked reading paper separates them faster than a term of observation.

programmes.name: English A, and when English B is the better route
programmes.description: English A is a Group 1 course for students working in their best language, marked against literary and analytical criteria. English B is a Group 2 course marked against language acquisition criteria. A student can hold a strong Diploma with either, and the choice should reflect current written proficiency rather than ambition or family preference.
programmes.countryNote: The placement conversation is free and happens with the Diploma coordinator. Families in Khalifa City and on Al Reem Island frequently reach us in the second term of DP1 having spent on English A tutoring for a student whose own school had suggested English B, which is the most expensive avoidable pattern in this subject.

programmes.name: MYP Language Acquisition into English B
programmes.description: MYP Language Acquisition runs in phases rather than year groups, which means two students in the same class can be working at different phases. A student finishing MYP 5 in a higher phase is a candidate for English A; one in a lower phase is better served by English B. The phase record is the most useful placement evidence a family can hold.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Abu Dhabi continuum school has recorded phases, ask for them before DP subject choices are confirmed. It converts a judgement call into a documented starting point and often removes the need for any paid assessment at all.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-b-tutor.subjectsIntro: What an English B family actually buys hours against, with the share of the grade each carries and the honest view on how expensive it is to improve.

subjects.name: Paper 2: listening
subjects.description: Recorded audio with comprehension questions, sat under timed conditions. Half of the receptive paper and therefore a substantial share of the grade. It improves with volume rather than with expertise, which makes it the cheapest marks in the course to recover and the ones most often left alone.

subjects.name: Paper 2: reading
subjects.description: Authentic written texts with comprehension questions. Marks are lost to unfamiliar text conventions and to time, not usually to vocabulary. Practice on the specific question formats produces faster gains than general reading, and it can be done independently once the format is understood.

subjects.name: Paper 1: productive writing
subjects.description: One task chosen from three, written in a specified text type and within a word range that differs by level. Register and text-type conventions carry real marks, so feedback on three well-chosen pieces beats twelve unmarked ones. This is where tutoring hours are most clearly worth their rate.

subjects.name: Text types and their conventions
subjects.description: Blog, article, brochure, email, essay, interview, proposal, report, review, speech, set of instructions. Each has conventions of layout, address and register that an examiner expects. Learning five of them properly is more valuable than recognising all of them vaguely.

subjects.name: Individual oral assessment at Standard Level
subjects.description: Built on a visual stimulus linked to one of the prescribed themes, with a short presentation followed by discussion. Students who describe the image and never connect it to the theme lose marks that a single structured practice run usually recovers.

subjects.name: Individual oral assessment at Higher Level
subjects.description: Built on an extract from one of the two literary works studied, followed by discussion of the course themes. This is the one place where Higher Level English B resembles a literature course, and it is the component Higher Level candidates most often underestimate.

subjects.name: The two literary works at Higher Level
subjects.description: Higher Level candidates study two works written in English. They are not assessed as literature in their own right, but they supply the oral extract and feed the themes, so a student who has read them attentively has a materially easier oral.

subjects.name: The five prescribed themes
subjects.description: Identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organisation and sharing the planet. Every task and every oral connects to one of them. A student who can speak for two minutes on each theme with concrete examples is prepared for most of what the course asks.

subjects.name: Register and audience control
subjects.description: Writing a formal proposal in the voice of a blog post is one of the commonest ways to lose marks with otherwise accurate English. It is quick to fix once named, and it is invisible to a student working alone, which is precisely what makes feedback worth paying for.

subjects.name: Timing and handwriting under pressure
subjects.description: Both papers are sat under time, and the word range on the writing task is binding at both ends. Students who routinely overshoot or undershoot have a planning problem that costs marks independently of their English, and it is diagnosable from one timed piece.

sections.heading: What an English B tutor costs in Abu Dhabi, and why language subjects sit lower in the band
paragraphs: Published rates for Diploma tutoring in this market span a wide range, and the spread reflects who is teaching rather than which subject. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45, both at the entry end for online or group work. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and subject specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, while BartyED publishes AED 650 for its premium tier. Each of those is the provider's own published figure, read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price.

For English B the useful observation is that the top of that range buys something this course does not need. Premium rates are priced for scarce subject expertise: a Higher Level Physics specialist, an examiner-badged mathematician. English B asks for a competent, experienced language teacher who knows the five themes, the text types and the paper formats. That person sits in the AED 150 to AED 300 band, and paying above it rarely changes an outcome in this subject.

There is one exception worth naming. Higher Level English B includes two literary works and an oral built on an extract from one of them, and that part of the course does reward a teacher with literature experience. A family whose Higher Level candidate is strong on comprehension and nervous about the oral is reasonably buying a narrower, more specialised two or three sessions, and paying a higher rate for those specific hours is a defensible choice.

The format premium is separate from the expertise premium and larger than families expect. In-home delivery prices travel into the hour: Bestimate's in-home band sits above comparable online rates, and independent home tutors in this market quote up to AED 500. For an Abu Dhabi address off the island, that premium is substantially a drive. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; tutoring here is delivered one to one over live video, and visiting tutors are a service we run only in India, which takes the travel component out of the price entirely.

sections.heading: The placement decision that costs more than any tutor
paragraphs: Before a family spends anything on English tutoring, the question worth settling is which English course the student should be in. Group 1 English A is marked against literary and analytical criteria for students working in their best language. Group 2 English B is marked against language acquisition criteria. Both can sit inside a strong Diploma, and the right answer depends on current written proficiency rather than on how fluently a student speaks at the dinner table.

Both directions of error are expensive. A student placed in English A who needed English B spends two years producing essays judged against criteria they cannot yet reach, and the tutoring bill rises as the family tries to close a gap that the course design will not allow them to close. A strong English user placed in English B may find the course comfortable and then discover that a university programme wanted evidence the Group 2 course does not provide. Neither error is a school's fault; placements are made on limited early evidence.

The honest arithmetic is worth laying out, because it is what makes this a money question rather than an academic one. One session a week across two Diploma years at the published band of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour is roughly sixty to seventy sessions, which is AED 9,000 to AED 21,000 depending on the tutor. Families who fight a placement rather than fix it often land at the upper end of that calculation. Families who settle the placement in the first term and then buy a targeted writing block plus oral preparation typically spend a small fraction of it.

Settling it costs nothing. The Diploma coordinator holds the MYP Language Acquisition phase record where there is one, the first term's marked work, and the professional judgement. A cold timed reading paper adds a hard number if the school's view and a parent's instinct disagree, and that can be done inside a free trial lesson. What a family should not do is treat the placement as fixed and buy hours against it.

sections.heading: Where the marks are, and which of them are cheap
paragraphs: English B splits across three assessed elements and they are not equally expensive to improve. The receptive-skills paper, covering listening and reading, carries half the grade. The productive writing task carries a quarter. The individual oral assessment carries the remaining quarter. That distribution is the most useful planning fact in the subject, and most families reach a tutor without having seen it.

Listening and reading improve with volume and format familiarity. A student who sits four past listening sections under timed conditions, checks them, and identifies the question types they miss will gain more than one who talks about listening strategy for four hours at AED 250. This is unusual among Diploma subjects and it is a genuine opportunity: half the grade responds to disciplined independent work, supported by a monthly review rather than weekly contact.

Writing is the opposite. A student cannot see their own register, and nobody improves a proposal they believe is already appropriate. Marked feedback on a small number of pieces, each in a different text type, each rewritten after comment, is where paid hours buy the most in this subject. Three or four well-marked pieces generally change a student's writing more than a term of practice without feedback, and that makes a short block better value than an open-ended commitment.

The oral sits in between. It needs a small number of recorded practice runs rather than ongoing teaching, because what students get wrong is structural: describing the stimulus without connecting it to a theme at Standard Level, or treating the literary extract as a comprehension exercise at Higher Level. Two or three sessions usually exhausts the available improvement, and a tutor proposing ten has misread the component.

sections.heading: Text types: the five worth learning properly
paragraphs: The writing paper asks for one task from a choice of three, each specifying a text type and an audience. A blog post, a formal proposal, a report, a review, a speech and a set of instructions all have different conventions of layout, address and register, and examiners expect the conventions as well as the language. Students lose marks writing accurate, fluent English in the wrong voice, which is maddening precisely because the English was fine.

The efficient approach is not to study every text type. Candidates choose their task, so a student who knows five text types confidently will almost always find one they can write well. Learning five properly, with a model structure and a register checklist for each, is a two or three session investment with a return across both papers and the oral. Learning all twelve superficially produces a student who recognises the label and still writes a letter when asked for a proposal.

Register is the part no student can self-diagnose. A seventeen-year-old who writes naturally in a conversational register will produce a proposal that opens with a greeting and a rhetorical question, and will not see anything wrong with it. A marked piece with the register problems circled is worth more than any explanation given in advance, which is the practical argument for feedback-shaped tutoring in this course rather than instruction-shaped tutoring.

Word ranges differ by level and are binding at both ends, so a Higher Level candidate who writes a Standard Level length piece has a problem independent of quality. Students should know their range as a number and should have written to it under time at least three times before the examination. Confirm the current ranges and timings with the school's Diploma coordinator, since published figures are revised between guide editions.

sections.heading: The individual oral, and why it differs at the two levels
paragraphs: The individual oral assessment is examined inside the school and carries a quarter of the grade. At Standard Level it is built on a visual stimulus connected to one of the five prescribed themes: the candidate presents on the image for a few minutes and then discusses the theme more widely. At Higher Level it is built on an extract from one of the two literary works studied, followed by discussion of the course themes. Those are different tasks and they fail differently.

Standard Level candidates lose marks by describing. A photograph of a crowded market can be described accurately for three minutes without ever connecting to identities, social organisation or sharing the planet, and a candidate who does that has answered a question nobody asked. The fix is a one-sentence habit: name the theme in the first fifteen seconds and return to it. Practised twice, it changes the shape of the whole presentation.

Higher Level candidates lose marks by treating the extract as a comprehension passage. The task is not to explain what happens in the passage but to use it as a way into the themes, which requires having read the work and being willing to move outward from it. This is the one component in English B where a tutor with literature teaching experience is materially better than a general language teacher, and where paying a higher rate for two or three sessions is justified.

Both versions benefit from recording. A candidate who has recorded a full timed run and listened back will have discovered their own padding, their habit of restarting sentences, and whether they can actually fill the time. That is cheap, uncomfortable and effective, and because the words are the candidate's own and spoken in the examination, no authorship question arises at any point.

sections.heading: Do not pay twice: English B and the Ministry's proficiency routes
paragraphs: Families in Abu Dhabi frequently run two English projects at once without noticing. There is the Diploma course, and there is whatever English evidence a university or the Ministry of Education wants for equivalency and admission. Paying separately for both, with two tutors and two sets of hours, is common and often avoidable.

The Ministry's published equivalency requirements differ by curriculum track, and the figures that are sourced are worth knowing precisely. On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. On the British track, candidates must show five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. No IB points threshold is published here, because we have not read one on an official Ministry page and an unsourced figure would be worse than none.

The practical consequence is a question to ask early rather than late. If your child will need an IELTS or TOEFL score anyway, the skills overlap with English B substantially: timed reading, timed listening, structured writing to a brief. A plan that treats them as one project, with the same practice serving both, costs considerably less than two separate engagements. Whether a specific university accepts English B Higher Level in place of a test is a question for that university's admissions office, and the answer varies, so ask them directly rather than assuming either way.

Equivalency itself is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring platform performs or guarantees, and tutoring is not required for it. Verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae or through your emirate's attestation channel before making any plan that depends on them.

sections.heading: Honest arithmetic for two Diploma years
paragraphs: Most families want a number before they start, and the market mostly declines to give one. Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, a currency UAE parents do not transact in. The arithmetic below uses the published AED bands and states its own assumptions, so a parent can adjust it rather than trust it.

A standing weekly hour across both Diploma years is roughly sixty to seventy sessions once holidays are deducted. At the qualified-teacher band of AED 150 to AED 300 that is about AED 9,000 to AED 21,000. Monthly packages circulating in this market, around AED 799 for eight online sessions, work out lower per hour and lock in a volume the subject may not need. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle band, which is consistent with those figures.

The targeted alternative looks very different on a spreadsheet. A placement review with the school costs nothing. One diagnostic session establishes the weak component. A writing block of four sessions, an oral block of three, and a monthly review session through the receptive-skills work across eighteen months comes to roughly fifteen to twenty paid hours, or about AED 2,250 to AED 6,000 at the same published bands. Half the grade in that plan is carried by independent practice, which is the correct answer for a comprehension paper.

Neither plan is right for every student. A candidate who will not do independent work needs the structure a weekly slot provides, and paying for accountability is a legitimate purchase rather than a waste. The point is that the choice should be made deliberately, with the split of the grade and the published rates visible, rather than by defaulting to a weekly hour because that is what tutoring normally looks like.

sections.heading: Permits, availability and what a tutor may not do
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the rules are straightforward enough to check. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted at you is unverified.

Two further points apply in this emirate specifically. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct reflects the same restriction. And a tutoring business with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: in Dubai that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit issued to training institutes. IB Gram holds no regulator licence or accreditation of any kind, operates no office or centre in the UAE, and names regulators here only to explain what they do.

Availability in English B is better than in most Diploma subjects, because experienced language teachers are not scarce. Even so, Higher Level oral support built on a literary extract narrows the pool, and if nobody suitable is free for the level and component you need, you are told with a realistic date rather than matched to a generalist. You see what the matched tutor has actually taught before the trial lesson rather than after it.

On coursework, the boundary is the same as in every Diploma subject and is worth saying plainly. A tutor marks the student's own writing, names the register and convention problems, teaches the text types, and rehearses the oral. A tutor does not supply replacement sentences, rewrite a piece into its final form, or hand over model answers to adapt. Operations in this market sell completed assessed work outright, one of them with a published price, and a family should treat that as a risk to their child's Diploma rather than a service.

faqs.question: What does an IB English B tutor charge per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates relevant to this course run from about AED 33 to AED 45 an hour at the entry level, through AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified and experienced language teacher, up to AED 500 or more at the premium end. Those are named providers' own figures read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33, EdFlik from AED 45, Unitors IB from AED 200, TutorChase AED 270, Bestimate 200 to 450 and above, BartyED AED 650. For English B the mid band is usually the right purchase, because the course needs an experienced language teacher rather than scarce subject expertise.

faqs.question: Is English B cheaper to support than English A?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, for two reasons. The band is lower, because a strong language teacher rather than a Diploma literature specialist can do most of the work. And half the grade sits in a listening and reading paper that improves with independent timed practice rather than with contact hours, so a well-planned engagement buys fewer paid sessions than an English A engagement typically does. The exception is Higher Level oral preparation on a literary extract, which narrows the pool of suitable tutors and reasonably attracts a higher rate for two or three sessions.

faqs.question: My son speaks English fluently but writes badly. Is English B the right course?
faqs.answer: It often is, and the mismatch you describe is extremely common in Abu Dhabi. Conversational fluency and formal written control are separate skills, and Group 1 English A is marked against literary and analytical criteria that assume the written side is already secure. The decision belongs with the Diploma coordinator, who holds the first term's marked work and any MYP Language Acquisition phase record. A cold timed reading and writing paper adds a hard number if the school's view and your instinct differ, and that can be done inside a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Which part of English B gives the most marks per dirham spent?
faqs.answer: Marked feedback on written pieces, and it is not close. A student cannot see their own register, so three or four pieces in different text types, each marked for convention and rewritten, change their writing more than a term of unmarked practice. By contrast the listening and reading paper, which carries half the grade, responds mainly to volume of timed practice and format familiarity, so paying by the hour for it is poor value. The oral needs two or three recorded runs and then stops improving, which makes it cheap in total.

faqs.question: Can my daughter improve her listening score without a tutor?
faqs.answer: To a large extent, yes, and saying otherwise would not be honest. Listening improves with the volume of timed practice and with identifying which question types she consistently misses, both of which she can do alone once the format has been explained. What a tutor adds is the initial explanation, accountability, and a monthly review that checks whether the practice is actually happening and what the error pattern is. One taught session plus a schedule plus monthly review is the structure we would normally propose for this component.

faqs.question: How long is the writing task, and does the length matter?
faqs.answer: The writing task specifies a word range that differs between Standard and Higher Level, and it is binding at both ends. A candidate who writes substantially short has not met the task; one who overshoots loses control of structure and often of time for checking. Students should know their range as a number and should have written to it under timed conditions at least three times before the examination. Confirm the current range and paper timing with your child's Diploma coordinator, because published figures are revised between subject guide editions.

faqs.question: Which text types should my child actually learn properly?
faqs.answer: Five, not twelve. The paper offers a choice of tasks, so a candidate who knows five text types confidently will nearly always find one they can write well. A sensible five are the formal proposal, the report, the blog post, the review and the speech, because they span the register range and their conventions are distinct. Learning each with a model structure and a register checklist takes two or three sessions in total and pays back across the writing paper and the oral. Recognising all twelve labels vaguely helps nobody.

faqs.question: What happens in the Higher Level oral, and why does it cost more to prepare?
faqs.answer: At Higher Level the individual oral assessment is built on an extract from one of the two literary works studied in the course, followed by discussion of the prescribed themes. Candidates commonly treat the extract as a comprehension passage and explain what happens in it, rather than using it as a route into the themes. Preparing that well benefits from a tutor with literature teaching experience as well as language teaching, which narrows the available pool and reasonably attracts a higher rate for the two or three sessions involved.

faqs.question: Do we need separate IELTS tutoring as well as English B?
faqs.answer: Often not, and running both separately is one of the more expensive mistakes families make. The skills overlap substantially: timed reading, timed listening, and structured writing to a brief. The Ministry's American-track proficiency routes are a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, all of which draw on the same abilities English B develops. Whether a particular university accepts English B Higher Level instead of a test varies, so ask that university's admissions office directly rather than assuming.

faqs.question: Should we buy an English B monthly package or pay for single sessions?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether you will use the sessions. Packages circulating in this market at around AED 799 for eight online sessions work out below the per-hour mid band, which is genuine value if all eight are needed. The risk in English B specifically is that the course does not need steady monthly volume: writing feedback comes in short blocks, oral preparation saturates after a few runs, and the receptive paper is independent work. A package can quietly commit you to hours that the subject's shape does not call for.

faqs.question: Do rates in Abu Dhabi rise closer to the examination session?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens more than rates do. Published bands stay broadly stable through the year, but the tutors a family would actually want are booked earlier in the spring term, and the remaining choice narrows. The effect on a household budget is indirect: a late start often means accepting a higher-band tutor because the mid-band ones are full. For English B this matters most for Higher Level oral support, where the suitable pool is smallest, so that block is worth booking before the internal assessment window approaches.

faqs.question: Is there VAT on private tuition fees in the UAE?
faqs.answer: The VAT treatment of education services in the UAE depends on the provider and the service, and we will not state it as fact here without a Federal Tax Authority citation, because getting it wrong in either direction misleads a parent making a financial decision. What a family should do is ask any provider directly whether a quoted AED figure includes VAT and request a tax registration number if one is claimed. Verify the underlying treatment with the Federal Tax Authority or a tax adviser rather than relying on any tutoring website.

faqs.question: Can sessions fit around Ramadan and shortened Abu Dhabi school days?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this course adapts better than most. School days shorten across the UAE during Ramadan and household evenings reorganise around Iftar, so the usable window moves later. Short listening practice and a 60-minute writing feedback session both work well after the meal, while long timed papers do not. The sensible adjustment is to move timed practice before or after those weeks and keep feedback sessions running through them, and to identify any internal oral assessment dates that fall in or just after Ramadan well in advance.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson cover, and what is the condition?
faqs.answer: One trial lesson per family, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. It is a working session rather than a sales call: your child either writes a short timed piece or sits a reading section, and the tutor marks it and says what the weakest element actually is. It ends with an hours estimate, which is sometimes zero, and an honest view on whether the English A or English B placement looks right. The only condition is that it is one lesson per family, not one per subject or tutor.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-b-tutor.closingHeading: Check the placement, then buy the narrow thing
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-english-b-tutor.closingBody: English B rewards a family that spends deliberately. Settle the English A or English B question with the school, which costs nothing. Take a free trial lesson, one per family with no card details taken, and find out which of the three assessed elements is actually weak. Then buy the narrow thing: marked writing feedback where a student cannot self-correct, two or three recorded oral runs, and a schedule rather than contact hours for the paper that carries half the grade. Lessons run one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and every AED figure on this page belongs to the provider who published it.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-environmental-systems-an.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Environmental Systems and Societies: systems and models, the ecology and biodiversity material, water, soil, atmosphere and energy, human population and resource use, and the practical and investigative work. intro.heading: The subject families choose as the easy science, marked like a science
paragraphs: Environmental Systems and Societies has a reputation on Abu Dhabi option sheets that the course itself does not support. It can satisfy either the individuals and societies group or the sciences group, which is why so many students pick it, and the content looks approachable next to Chemistry. Then the first proper assessment arrives and the marks come back in the fours. The reason is almost always the same: the student has written a well-informed general essay about the environment, and the examiner was looking for a systems argument with data, units, named examples and a stated perspective.

This page is built on evidence rather than encouragement, because ESS is a subject where a parent genuinely cannot tell from a report card what is going wrong. A 4 can mean weak content knowledge, or excellent content with no command-term discipline, or a student who writes beautifully and never draws a systems diagram correctly. Those three problems need completely different work, and the only way to tell them apart is to read marked writing. Our arrangements all produce it: criterion-level marks, in writing, before the lesson, kept where you can read them.

There is a second complication specific to this subject right now. The ESS guide was substantially revised, with the new specification first examined in 2026, and the revision changed emphasis as well as content. Older revision material circulating online refers to the previous structure, and a tutor working from it will teach the wrong weighting of effort. Before any plan is written, confirm with your child's IB coordinator which version of the course the cohort is registered for and whether the school offers it at standard or higher level, because that single answer determines what the tutoring should cover.

Abu Dhabi has an advantage in ESS that few students use. The course is assessed through real systems and named examples, and the emirate contains unusually clean ones: planted and natural mangrove stands in the Eastern Mangroves and at Jubail, a wetland reserve at Al Wathba with a resident flamingo population, a marine biosphere reserve in the western region, oryx reintroduction on Sir Bani Yas, large-scale desalination, a solar plant in Al Dhafra and a nuclear station at Barakah in the same energy mix. A student who can discuss water security using their own emirate's figures writes with a specificity that general essays never reach.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no accreditation or endorsement from the IB, from ADEK or from any school named on this page. We match the student with a tutor who has taught the course, run the lessons live online, and keep the marked work legible to a parent. Parents get the marked work, the named target and an honest answer about what tutoring can and cannot change in the time left before the examinations.

Ask which group your child is in before buying any plan.

programmes.description: The preparation route in an IB continuum school. programmes.description: The British-track route into ESS. The gap is scale: IGCSE answers are short and recall-weighted, while ESS answers need a systems argument with evidence.

sections.heading: Why a well-written ESS answer can still score a 4
paragraphs: The commonest marked script we see from Abu Dhabi ESS students is fluent, informed and clearly the work of somebody who cares about the environment. It scores a 4. The reason is that it answers a question the paper did not ask. ESS questions carry command terms, and those terms are instructions about structure: outline, describe, explain, compare, discuss, evaluate and justify all demand different shapes of answer, and the marks are allocated against the shape.

The second pattern is the missing apparatus. ESS is a systems course, so an answer about a lake, a fishery or a city asks to be handled as a system with inputs, outputs, stores and flows. Students who write about causes and effects in prose, without ever using that framework, lose the marks reserved for systems thinking even when every factual statement is correct. Drawing the diagram, even roughly, before writing is usually worth more than an extra paragraph of content.

The third pattern is perspective. ESS asks students to recognise that two people can look at the same environmental problem and disagree because they hold different value positions. An answer that argues for one position without naming the value systems in play caps its own evaluation marks. Students find this strange at first because no other science asks it of them, and it is the single most teachable thing in the course.

All three are diagnosable from one marked piece of writing, which is why the first session with a new ESS student is a marking session rather than a syllabus tour. Send a timed answer and a class essay, and the tutor can usually say within the hour which of the three is costing the grade, and what the first fortnight should target.

sections.heading: Command terms and where the band actually changes
paragraphs: This is the working tool for the first month with most ESS students. The command terms are published, they are used consistently, and almost every mid-band answer we mark has treated a higher-order term as if it were a lower-order one. Describing when asked to evaluate is a ceiling, not a style choice.

The table below sets out the terms that cost Abu Dhabi students the most marks, what a weak answer typically does, and what moves it up. It is deliberately practical: a student should be able to read the term in the question and know the shape of the paragraph they are about to write before they write it. That decision, made in ten seconds, is worth more than any amount of extra reading.

Two details inside the table deserve emphasis. Data questions are where the fastest gains sit, because the losses are mechanical: no units, no reference to the figures provided, a trend stated without a magnitude, or a calculation shown without the working. Those are habits, and habits change inside two or three marked pieces. Extended responses take longer to move because they need judgement about what to include.

The other detail is the named example. ESS rewards specificity, and a student with six well-prepared named examples covering ecosystems, water, energy, soil, pollution and population will outperform a student with general knowledge of all six. Building that reference sheet, in the student's own words, is a standing piece of work in every plan we write.
