sections.heading: Abu Dhabi as the case study: six named examples on the doorstep
paragraphs: ESS answers live or die on named examples, and Abu Dhabi students routinely reach for distant ones they have read about rather than local ones they have seen. That is a straightforward loss. An examiner reading about a specific mangrove stand with its own planting history, visitor pressure and ecosystem services gets evidence; an examiner reading about rainforests in general gets atmosphere.

The emirate supplies examples across most of the specification. Mangrove systems in the Eastern Mangroves and at Jubail cover ecosystem services, zonation, carbon storage and conservation management. The wetland reserve at Al Wathba covers protected-area management and the effect of water supply on an artificial habitat. The western marine biosphere reserve covers seagrass, dugong populations and designation. Sir Bani Yas covers reintroduction of a species that was hunted out. Large-scale desalination covers water security, brine discharge and energy intensity, which is one of the most examinable trade-offs in the whole course. And the emirate's energy mix, with a solar plant in Al Dhafra and a nuclear station at Barakah, covers energy choice, emissions and the arguments people make about both.

Using them well has a method. Each example needs a figure or two the student can actually recall, a stated management intervention, named stakeholders, and one honest limitation. Students who prepare examples that way can deploy the same case across several different questions; students who memorise a paragraph can deploy it only when the question happens to match.

The reference sheet has to be written by the student, in their own words, from sources they can cite. That is partly academic honesty and mostly memory: material a student has summarised themselves is recalled under pressure, and material handed to them is not. A tutor's job is to tell them which examples are worth the effort and to check that the figures are right.

sections.heading: The investigation: where help stops being help
paragraphs: The investigative component is where families most often want support and where the boundary matters most. What a tutor may do is teach the research methods, discuss candidate questions, challenge a question that cannot be answered with the data available, explain what the assessment criteria reward, and give written feedback on drafts the student has produced. What a tutor may not do is design the study, supply the analysis, rewrite sections into their own prose, or hand over a structure with the content filled in.

This is not a cautious reading of the rules. Academic honesty findings fall on the student, not on the adult who overstepped, and the penalty reaches the whole Diploma rather than the single subject. Our competitor research in this market found a provider openly selling completed internal assessments at a fixed price. What is being sold there is a malpractice case with an invoice attached, and any family weighing it should see it in those terms.

The practical consequence is that timing decides how much a tutor can usefully contribute. Most of the available value sits in the research question and the method, which means the useful window opens when the work is being planned and narrows sharply once data has been collected. A student who arrives with a completed study built on an unanswerable question cannot be rescued by feedback; they can only be helped to write up honestly what they found.

Our record-keeping is deliberate here. The tutor notes what they reviewed and what they advised, so if the school ever asks how the work was supported there is a factual answer. Several Abu Dhabi schools now ask students to log external support, and a student who can show exactly what help was given is in a far stronger position than one relying on memory.

sections.heading: What ESS support costs in Abu Dhabi, and what you get for it
paragraphs: Published market rates for private tuition in the UAE run from roughly AED 45 to 65 an hour at the budget online end, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, to AED 200 to 450 and above for IB and IGCSE specialists; one premium provider publishes AED 650, and a Dubai rate survey puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500. Those figures belong to the providers who published them. IB Gram does not publish a tariff on this page and then quote something else on the phone.

What is more useful than a single hourly number is the shape of the spend across a Diploma year, because ESS support is rarely needed continuously. The table converts the specialist market band into the blocks families actually buy. It is arithmetic on published bands rather than a price list, and the point is to let you recognise a reasonable quote and plan the commitment before you start.

Two Abu Dhabi specifics are worth noting. School fees in the emirate are regulated by ADEK rather than by Dubai's authority, and fee schedules are published per school, so compare any tutoring commitment against your own school's published fees rather than against a Dubai figure quoted in the press. And marking is the variable that makes quotes incomparable: an hour of lesson plus a properly marked timed answer is around ninety minutes of tutor work, so ask explicitly whether written marking is included before comparing two numbers.

For the most common pattern we see in ESS, a block of six to eight sessions around the investigation in Year 12 plus a ten-week run-in before the papers in Year 13 does most of the work. That is a planned, bounded spend with a target attached, which is a better arrangement than an open-ended weekly session that nobody ever reviews.

sections.heading: Does ESS count? Group placement, universities and equivalency
paragraphs: This is the question that worries Abu Dhabi parents most once the grade stabilises, and it deserves a precise answer rather than reassurance. Inside the Diploma, ESS can satisfy either the individuals and societies group or the sciences group, which gives students flexibility in building a timetable. Outside the Diploma, what matters is what each university says about it, and that varies by course and country.

The rule of thumb is that competitive science and engineering courses usually name the laboratory sciences they want, and ESS is not always accepted as one of them. Courses in geography, environmental policy, sustainability, business, law and the social sciences generally treat it as a strong subject. The only reliable method is to read the published entry requirements for the specific courses on the student's list, including the UAE universities, and to do that in Year 12 while subject changes are still possible rather than in Year 13 when they are not.

On Ministry of Education equivalency, the sourced position is narrower than most pages claim. For the British track, the requirement includes five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency can be shown by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with at least 450 in SAT Mathematics. No verified IB points threshold is published that we can cite, so treat any figure you see as unconfirmed and check the Ministry's own channel.

IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee equivalency or attestation, and nobody should imply tutoring is required for it. Equivalency is a documentary process run by the authorities; we describe it and point you at the official route.

sections.heading: Permits, ethics and the questions to ask any Abu Dhabi tutor
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and the detail is checkable. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount quoted to you is unverified.

Abu Dhabi adds a rule that changes what families should ask for. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct points the same way. The arrangement that occurs to every parent first — paying your child's own ESS teacher for weekend sessions — is therefore the one to avoid. It is also weaker on its own terms, because the value of an external marker is that they did not set the predicted grade.

Two further questions separate a serious tutor from a confident one. Ask which version of the subject guide they teach from, since the revised specification was first examined in 2026 and plenty of circulating material predates it. Then ask for an example of marked student work with the student's details removed, so you can see whether the marking is criterion-level or a tidy paragraph of encouragement.

Finally, be wary of material offered as a download. Subject guides, past papers and mark schemes belong to the IB, and a tutor should cite and link them rather than circulate copies. A provider handing out bundles of restricted material is telling you something about how they treat rules generally, which matters a great deal in a subject with an internally assessed component.

faqs.question: Is ESS a soft option compared with Biology or Chemistry?
faqs.answer: It is broader and less mathematical, but it is not softer in the way option sheets imply. The content spans ecology, water, soil, atmosphere, energy and population, and the papers test systems thinking, data interpretation with units, named examples and the ability to identify the value positions behind an argument. Students who pick it expecting a lighter science usually lose marks on exactly those features rather than on content. The honest summary is that ESS is easier to understand and harder to write well, which is why so many capable Abu Dhabi students sit in the fours for a term before anything changes.

faqs.question: My daughter's ESS essays read well and still score 4s. What is missing?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three things, and marked work tells you which. First, command-term discipline: describing when the question says evaluate caps the mark regardless of quality. Second, systems apparatus: writing about causes and effects in prose without ever treating the situation as a system with inputs, outputs, stores and flows forfeits the marks reserved for that. Third, perspective: arguing a position without naming the environmental value systems in play limits evaluation marks. All three are teachable, and a single marked timed answer is normally enough to identify which one is live.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi examples are worth preparing for the papers?
faqs.answer: Six cover most of the specification. The mangrove systems at Jubail and the Eastern Mangroves give ecosystem services, zonation and conservation management. Al Wathba wetland gives protected-area management in an artificial habitat. The western marine biosphere reserve gives seagrass and dugong conservation. Sir Bani Yas gives species reintroduction. Desalination gives water security against brine and energy cost. The emirate's solar and nuclear capacity gives energy choice and emissions. Each needs a couple of recallable figures, a named management intervention, stakeholders and one honest limitation, written in the student's own words.

faqs.question: The ESS course changed recently. Does that affect which tutor we need?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the first question to ask. The subject guide was substantially revised with first examinations in 2026, and much of the revision material circulating online describes the previous structure. A tutor working from old material will misallocate effort, which is worse than no tutor because it feels productive. Ask any candidate which version they teach from and how many cohorts they have taken through the current one. Also confirm with your child's IB coordinator which version the school is registered for and at which level, because schools were not all on the same timetable for the change.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with practical and investigative work?
faqs.answer: With everything except the physical data collection, which is the student's job anyway. The parts that decide the mark are the research question, the method, the handling and presentation of data, and the evaluation, and all four are worked on through screen sharing and written feedback. What the tutor must not do is design the study, supply the analysis or rewrite sections into their own prose; the student produces the work. In practice the most valuable sessions happen before data is collected, because a question that cannot be answered with the data available cannot be fixed afterwards.

faqs.question: Does ESS satisfy a science requirement for university applications?
faqs.answer: Inside the Diploma it can count in either the sciences group or the individuals and societies group. Outside it, acceptance varies by course. Competitive science, medicine and engineering programmes usually name the laboratory sciences they require and may not accept ESS as one of them, while geography, environmental policy, sustainability, business, law and social science courses generally welcome it. Read the published entry requirements for the specific courses on your child's list, including UAE universities, and do it in Year 12 while a subject change is still possible rather than in Year 13 when it is not.

faqs.question: How many sessions does an Abu Dhabi ESS student typically need?
faqs.answer: The pattern that works most often is a diagnostic start of two or three sessions, a block of six to eight around the investigation in Year 12, and a ten-week run-in of two sessions a week before the papers. That is bounded and reviewable, which matters more than the total. Open-ended weekly tutoring with no target is how families spend a great deal and cannot say what changed. Every plan we write has a review point at week six where marked scores either moved or did not, and if they did not, the plan or the tutor changes.

faqs.question: Where exactly does a tutor have to stop on the ESS investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach research methods, discuss candidate questions, challenge one that cannot be answered with available data, explain what the criteria reward, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not design the study, supply the analysis, rewrite passages in their own words or hand over a filled-in structure. The student produces the work. We keep a record of what the tutor reviewed and advised, which helps where a school asks students to log external support. Services selling finished coursework exist in this market and what they are selling is a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: Are Abu Dhabi school fees and tutoring costs regulated the same way as Dubai's?
faqs.answer: No, and the distinction matters when you read press coverage. Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are licensed and inspected by ADEK, which also handles fee regulation in the emirate, while Dubai's schools sit under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. A Dubai fee announcement therefore tells you nothing directly about your own school. For tutoring there is no regulated price at all: published market rates for the UAE run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 at the premium end, and the sensible comparison is against your own school's published fee schedule.

faqs.question: My son is in Year 13 with eight weeks to go. Is ESS support still useful?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the target is the papers rather than the coursework. Eight weeks is enough to fix command-term discipline, data-question mechanics and the systems apparatus, because those are rules a student can learn to apply, and each is worth marks across every paper. It is also enough to build and test a set of named examples. What it is not enough for is a content rebuild from scratch, and it is far too late for the investigation. We would run two marked timed papers a week with one named target per fortnight.

faqs.question: Can ESS sessions move during Ramadan without losing momentum?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the change is agreed before the month starts. Abu Dhabi school hours shorten and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so a 5pm slot becomes unusable. Sessions normally move to post-Iftar times from about 8.30pm, or to weekend mornings when a two-hour stretch is needed for a full timed paper. Ramadan currently falls inside the revision term for the May session, so this is the most valuable block of weeks in the course. Families who plan the shift in advance keep their rhythm, and those who improvise commonly lose three or four weeks.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover ESS and Biology for the same student?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the overlap in the ecology material makes it efficient. The warning is that the two subjects reward different writing. Biology marks terminology precision and expects answers tightly keyed to the specification; ESS marks systems thinking, perspective and named examples, and tolerates breadth. A tutor who teaches both needs to keep the registers separate, because the commonest casualty is an ESS answer written in Biology register, which reads accurately and misses the marks for value systems. Ask a candidate how they would mark the same ecology answer differently for each subject.

faqs.question: What should the first ESS session with a new tutor actually produce?
faqs.answer: A written diagnosis. Send two pieces of work in advance, ideally including one timed answer, and the tutor should mark them cold against the command terms before the lesson. The session then explains which of the three common failure modes is costing marks, what the first fortnight targets, and what the student will write between sessions. What it should not be is a tour of the specification: you already know what the course covers, and what you are buying is an explanation of why a capable student is a band below expectation.

faqs.question: Why online rather than somebody who can come to our villa in Al Reef?
faqs.answer: Because ESS specialists are scarce and geography does not improve teaching. Searching within a short drive of Al Reef narrows the pool to whoever lives nearby, usually a Biology or Geography tutor willing to cover ESS, which is exactly the mismatch that produces answers in the wrong register. Online matching keeps the subject specialism and removes travel from both the price and the timetable, which is what makes a 6.30pm weekday slot workable. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; every lesson here runs live over video, one-to-one.

The fastest way to find out which one applies is to have an ESS specialist mark a timed answer and a class essay against the published command terms and set out, in writing, what is costing the marks. That is what the free trial lesson is for, and it happens before any payment. Tell us the predicted grade, the level the school offers and which version of the subject guide the cohort follows, and we will match your child with a tutor for live one-to-one online lessons in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: What an ESS tutor costs in Abu Dhabi, before anyone sells you a package
paragraphs: Environmental Systems and Societies is the only Diploma subject that can be counted in two groups at once, and that single administrative fact shapes its tutoring market. An Abu Dhabi family looking for Biology help finds a crowded field within an afternoon. The same family looking for ESS finds two or three names, both already booked for the term. Scarcity, not difficulty, is what sets the price here. An IB DP Environmental Systems and Societies tutor in Abu Dhabi is commonly quoted between AED 180 and AED 400 an hour, and the quote usually arrives with no breakdown of what is inside it.

This page is built around that number rather than around adjectives. It sets out what providers in this market publish, which parts of the course push a quote upwards, what a block of individual-investigation review realistically costs, and what two years of weekly support adds to a school bill that ADEK has already approved. Every figure is attributed to the provider or the rate survey that published it. None of it is an IB Gram price list: our sessions begin with a free trial lesson, and the rate per 60 minutes is agreed with you before anything is booked.

Delivery changes the arithmetic as much as experience does. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visits are a service we run only in India. We say that in the first hundred words because a family paying a premium hourly rate for a tutor's travel deserves to know that part of the fee is paying for the car, not the teaching.

The subject itself explains where the hours go. ESS asks a student to handle systems language, environmental value systems, named case studies and real data in the same answer, then to design and report an individual investigation worth a quarter of the final grade. Under the current subject guide the course is available at Higher Level as well as Standard Level, which is a change from the previous guide. Confirm with your school's IB coordinator which level your child is entered for and which guide the cohort is following, because schools in the emirate moved at different speeds.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The years in which the group choice is actually made. Individuals and Societies and Sciences both feed ESS, and a student who has written a good MYP science investigation has already met half the skills the Diploma investigation needs: a research question, a controlled variable, a graph that answers something. Support at this stage is cheaper per hour than Diploma work and often removes the need for crisis hours later.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run Middle Years eAssessment and several do not, and the difference changes what a Year 11 student arrives with. Families on the island and in the Al Raha corridor frequently move between British and IB schools mid-stage, so we check which assessment model the child has actually sat before pricing a block of work.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Primary work has no bearing on an ESS grade, but it is where the habit of evidence starts. A Year 5 child who can explain why a measurement was repeated is doing the thing the Diploma investigation marks years later. Primary support in Abu Dhabi is quoted well below Diploma rates, and parents usually book it for English and mathematics rather than for environmental topics.
programmes.countryNote: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools as a federal requirement, so a Primary timetable in Abu Dhabi is fuller than the same school's timetable abroad. We factor that into session length rather than pretending a tired child learns the same at 7pm.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller route in this emirate, combining Diploma courses with a career-related study. Students taking ESS as one of their Diploma courses within a Career-related Programme are assessed on the same subject guide, with the same investigation weighting, so the tutoring work is identical even though the overall certificate differs.
programmes.countryNote: Because the Career-related Programme is rarer in Abu Dhabi than the full Diploma, families often cannot find anyone locally who has taught a student on this route. Online matching removes that problem; it is the clearest case in this emirate where geography was the only thing limiting the choice of tutor.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-environmental-systems-an.subjectsIntro: Most families who book ESS support book a second subject within the year, usually because the two share a skill rather than a topic. These are the Diploma courses our Abu Dhabi tutors cover alongside Environmental Systems and Societies, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.levels: SL and HL under the current guide
subjects.description: Systems thinking, environmental value systems, named case studies and the individual investigation. Marks are lost on vague terminology, case studies used without data, and investigations whose research question is far wider than the evidence collected. Sessions usually split between paper technique and investigation structure.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The subject families most often compare ESS against. Content volume is far higher and the command terms are stricter. Students who switch from ESS to Biology usually underestimate the recall load; students who switch the other way underestimate how much writing ESS demands.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Shares case-study discipline and the habit of naming a place, a date and a figure in every answer. An Abu Dhabi student taking both can reuse one well-researched regional case study across subjects, provided the framing is rewritten for each syllabus.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Where ESS students taking it alongside often lose time. Energy, equilibrium and organic chemistry carry the highest failure rate in our Abu Dhabi caseload. Tutoring tends to focus on multi-step calculation layout, because marks are lost in presentation as often as in understanding.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistical content here overlaps directly with what an ESS investigation needs: correlation, significance, sampling. A student weak in this course usually produces an investigation whose data analysis stops at a bar chart.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most Abu Dhabi engineering and medicine applicants are pushed towards. It is not the better fit for an ESS student by default, and the choice should be made against the specific university requirement rather than reputation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Energy flow, efficiency and thermodynamics appear in ESS in simplified form. Students taking both find the ESS treatment frustratingly qualitative; the fix is learning which command terms expect a number and which expect an argument.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: The other group 4 subject with a smaller cohort in Abu Dhabi. Like ESS, it carries an investigation involving data from real participants, and the same scarcity of specialist teachers pushes its market rate upwards in this emirate.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Externalities, market failure and sustainability sit in both syllabuses with different vocabulary. Students taking both can be marked down for importing economic terms into an ESS answer where the examiner expects systems language.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Shares the ESS habit of weighing competing value positions. The engagement activity and the ESS investigation both reward a narrow, researchable question, so students taking both often benefit from planning the two in the same session.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The ESS idea of an environmental value system maps neatly onto knowledge questions about perspective and bias. Students who understand one tend to write better in the other, and a single tutor can keep the two consistent.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A popular choice in ESS and a common place for an Abu Dhabi student to stall. Support is process coaching: narrowing the question, checking the research is feasible in this climate and this city, and reading what the student has already written.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-environmental-systems-an.regionsTitle: Where in Abu Dhabi our ESS students live, and what that does to the price
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-environmental-systems-an.regionsIntro: Location changes a tutoring quote in this emirate more than most parents expect, because an in-home rate includes the drive and an online rate does not. These are the communities our Abu Dhabi ESS families come from, with the scheduling reality of each.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Island villa families often have the earliest realistic start time, because school runs are short. An in-home tutor crossing from the mainland at 5pm adds a traffic premium to the hourly rate; an online session at 5pm does not.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living and a single causeway. Several families here tell us an in-home tutor cancelled twice over parking before they moved the subject online. ESS needs no equipment beyond a laptop, which makes it a straightforward subject to move.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The densest cluster of our Abu Dhabi Diploma caseload. Villa compounds here sit a long drive from the island, so in-home quotes run at the upper end of the market band while the online rate stays flat.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: A corridor of international-school families with heavy after-school commitments. Sessions here are most often booked at 6.30pm or later, and a fixed weekly slot matters more than a cheap hourly rate.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer housing with long internal distances and event traffic on race and concert weekends. Families here plan around unpredictable Fridays, so we schedule ESS investigation reviews mid-week rather than at the weekend.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Older island neighbourhood close to several long-established schools. Short commutes mean a 4.30pm start is realistic, which is the one slot where in-home and online pricing come closest together.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Central, well served by schools, and a community where multiple siblings in one household is common. Two children in the same subject block does not halve the rate, but it does remove a second set of travel costs from an in-home quote.

regions.name: Masdar City and Khalifa Industrial Zone
regions.note: A small but relevant cluster: students here live beside the sustainability infrastructure their ESS syllabus describes. Several investigations in our caseload have used local energy and water data rather than a textbook case study.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Mainland communities where in-home tutoring is genuinely cheaper than on the island, because tutors live closer. The trade-off is a much smaller pool of people who have taught the Diploma, let alone ESS.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Falah
regions.note: Outer communities where an in-home visit often means a 40-minute drive each way. This is where the online rate wins on arithmetic alone, before any argument about subject specialism is made.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat Island and the Corniche
schoolClusters.note: Island schools with established Diploma cohorts. Group 3 and group 4 option blocks vary year to year, so confirm directly with the school whether ESS is running for your child's cohort and at which level before planning tutoring around it.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City and the Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: The corridor that generates most of our Abu Dhabi Diploma enquiries. Students here commonly combine an IB school timetable with academy sport or music, which is why evening slots fill first in this cluster.

schoolClusters.city: Al Reem Island, Yas Island and the newer communities
schoolClusters.note: Newer schools and newer cohorts, where a subject can appear on the option sheet one year and not the next. Families moving in mid-Diploma are the group most likely to need a tutor who has taught the current guide rather than the previous one.
schools: Nord Anglia International School Abu Dhabi

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across the term
modes.description: A fixed 60-minute slot each week through the term, alternating between paper technique and whatever the school has just taught. This is the cheapest route per unit of progress because nothing has to be re-explained from scratch, and it is the only mode in which a tutor can see a pattern in the mistakes rather than a single bad paper.
bullets: One hour a week, same slot, Gulf Standard Time
Written note after each session naming what was practised and what was set
Marked work returned before the next session rather than at the end of the block
Pausable for school examination weeks and travel

modes.title: Individual investigation review block
modes.description: A six to eight hour block bought as a unit, spread across the weeks a student is working on the investigation. The tutor questions the research question, checks the method can actually produce data, reads what the student has written and marks a practice version against the published criteria. The writing is the student's throughout.
bullets: Stage-by-stage review rather than one read of a finished document
Feasibility check on data collection in this climate and this city
Marking of a practice version against the criteria the school will apply
A written list of what the student must change, in their own words

modes.title: Pre-examination intensive
modes.description: A short, dense run of sessions in the weeks before the May session, built on marked past questions rather than fresh content. It is the most expensive way to buy improvement per dirham, because the hours are compressed and specialist availability is tightest exactly then, but it is the right purchase when term-time support was not booked.
bullets: Two or three sessions a week for four to six weeks
Timed questions marked and returned within 24 hours
Focus on command terms and data questions, not on new content
Booked early, because specialist slots in April disappear first

sections.heading: What the Abu Dhabi market charges for Diploma ESS help
paragraphs: A Diploma-level ESS tutor working with Abu Dhabi students is quoted at roughly AED 180 to AED 400 an hour. Below that band you are usually buying a university student with no experience of the subject guide; above it you are usually buying a reputation. The band itself is assembled from figures providers in this market have published, not from an average we invented, and the table below names who charges what.

Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. That silence is why parents ring four agencies and get four unexplained numbers. The useful comparison is not tutor against tutor but model against model: an agency, a marketplace, an independent tutor and a tuition centre are selling genuinely different things at genuinely different costs.

Read the table as a map of what the money buys rather than as a price list. The right-hand column matters more than the rate: a lower hourly figure with no marking and no written feedback is often more expensive per unit of progress than a higher one that returns a marked paper every week. Rates quoted here are the published figures of the providers named, as read in October 2026, and any of them may change without notice. One more thing worth knowing before you ring round: nobody in this market prices ESS separately from the other Diploma sciences on their public page, so the figure you are quoted on the phone for this subject is frequently higher than the figure advertised, and the reason given is availability rather than difficulty.
bullets: Ask every quote the same four questions: who teaches, is marking included, is feedback written, what is the cancellation rule
A rate quoted per lesson rather than per hour hides a 45-minute session surprisingly often
Monthly packages look cheaper and usually assume a session count you will not always use
No provider in this market can price an ESS specialist as if they were a Biology tutor and still find one

sections.heading: Six things that move the number on an Abu Dhabi ESS quote
paragraphs: The same tutor will quote two Abu Dhabi families different numbers for the same subject, and the reasons are mundane. Time of year is the largest single factor: a slot in October is a scheduling decision, a slot in April is an auction. Specialist scarcity is the second, and it bites harder in ESS than in any other group 4 subject because the cohorts are small and the teaching pool is smaller.

Level is a smaller factor than parents assume. The jump from Standard to Higher Level in this subject adds content and depth, but it does not double the hourly rate; what changes is the number of hours needed, not the price of each one. The component being supported matters far more. An hour of paper technique is ordinary teaching. An hour spent on an investigation that is already three weeks late involves reading, marking and a conversation about what cannot be fixed, which is why review blocks are priced as blocks.

Then there is what the rate includes, which is where most of the real variation hides. Marking takes a tutor roughly as long as teaching. A provider who returns a marked paper every week and a written session note has built that time into the figure; one who quotes AED 150 and sends nothing has not. Finally, delivery: an in-home rate in this emirate carries the drive, and from Khalifa City to the island at 5pm that is a real cost someone is paying.
bullets: Timing: October planning versus April scarcity is the single biggest swing
Scarcity: an ESS specialist is rarer in this emirate than a Biology specialist, and priced accordingly
Component: paper practice is cheaper per hour than investigation review, which is bought as a block
Inclusions: marking and written feedback cost the tutor time and sit inside any honest rate
Delivery: an in-home figure includes travel; an online figure does not, which is most of the difference
Continuity: a weekly slot costs less per unit of progress than the same hours bought in a panic

sections.heading: The individual investigation is where most of the money goes
paragraphs: The individual investigation carries a quarter of the ESS grade and consumes more tutoring hours than the written papers combined. The reason is sequencing. A student who chooses a research question too wide in week one will produce data that cannot answer it in week six, and no amount of late help repairs a question that was wrong at the start. The cheapest version of this subject is the one where someone sensible looks at the question before any data is collected.

What a tutor may do here is tightly bounded, and the boundary is not a policy preference but an IB academic-honesty rule. The student designs, collects, analyses and writes. A tutor asks questions, checks a method is safe and repeatable, points at a criterion the student has not addressed, and marks a practice version so the student can see the gap. A tutor who hands back a rewritten document has put the student's whole Diploma at risk, and we will not do it.

The table below is the version of this we give Abu Dhabi families on the phone: the stages, what the student owns, what a tutor can legitimately contribute, and roughly how many hours each stage absorbs. Hours are what we observe across our own caseload rather than a published standard, and a student who starts in DP1 uses fewer of them than one who starts in February of DP2. The pattern we see in Abu Dhabi is that the first two stages are the ones families skip and the last two are the ones they pay most for, which is the wrong way round: an hour spent narrowing a question in November removes several hours of repair work in March.

sections.heading: Why an ESS specialist is harder to find in Abu Dhabi than a Biology tutor
paragraphs: Three things make this subject scarce in the emirate at once. The cohorts are small: an Abu Dhabi school may run one ESS class in a year group of a hundred and twenty, and a school that drops the option for a year produces no experienced teachers at all. The subject is often taught by a Geography or Biology specialist covering it rather than by someone who chose it, which is perfectly workable in a classroom and less so when a parent wants an hour of focused investigation review.

The third reason is regulatory, and it is specific to Abu Dhabi. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes teachers being barred from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with teachers working outside school hours expected to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical effect on a parent is simple: the one person who knows your child's course best is not available to you privately.

That is the honest case for online matching, and it is an arithmetic case rather than a marketing one. A family that insists on someone who can drive to Khalifa City is choosing from the people who live near Khalifa City and are free at 6pm. A family that accepts a live video session is choosing from everyone who has taught the current ESS guide. In a subject this thinly staffed, that is the difference between a specialist and whoever is nearest.
bullets: Small cohorts mean few experienced ESS teachers in any one emirate
Option blocks change year to year, so a school's ESS experience can lapse
ADEK ethics rules, as reported, close off your child's own school teacher
Online delivery widens the pool from one neighbourhood to the whole subject

sections.heading: Online or in-home in Abu Dhabi: what the extra AED buys
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real and legitimate market in this emirate, and parents who want it should understand what they are paying for. Published market rates for an in-home visit run from around AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The premium is not teaching quality. It is forty minutes of driving, fuel, and the fact that the tutor can teach one fewer student that evening.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and we would rather say that plainly than let a family discover it after a deposit. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. For UAE families every session is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own work shared on screen and marked copies returned afterwards. For a subject with no laboratory requirement and no equipment beyond a laptop, there is very little that a physical presence adds.

The comparison below is the one we would want as parents. It covers what each option is, what the market charges, what Abu Dhabi logistics do to it in practice, and who each option genuinely suits. A family with a child who will not work without an adult in the room should read the third row carefully; that is a real reason to choose a different model, and it is not a reason we would argue with.

sections.heading: Is the tutor you are paying permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in this country is regulated by permit, and a parent can check the position without any specialist knowledge. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through its smart app, website and e-services system. Anyone quoting you a permit fee has invented it.

The eligible categories are broader than most parents assume: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of fine amounts has been published, so any specific figure circulating online should be treated as unverified, and this page will not repeat one.

Two further points matter in Abu Dhabi specifically. First, a tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs its own permit from the emirate authority; an individual working online from their own home does not become a training institute. Second, IB Gram is not approved, endorsed or certified by ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or any examination board, and any provider telling you otherwise about themselves is making a claim you should ask them to evidence with a permit number.

sections.heading: Two years of ESS support, set against the rest of the school bill
paragraphs: Tutoring is a line in a much larger education budget, and it is worth sizing against the others before deciding how much is sensible. In Abu Dhabi, private school fees are set within a framework the emirate authority approves, and the school publishes its own band; a parent comparing tutoring cost to fees should read the school's current published fee schedule, approved at emirate level, rather than any figure an agency quotes. Across the border in Dubai, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, which gives some sense of the direction of travel in the market generally.

Against a fee of that scale, the choice is rarely whether to buy any support at all but when. A single weekly hour from DP1 term two to the May session of DP2 is a large number of hours at a moderate rate. A six-hour investigation block plus a four-week pre-examination intensive is a small number of hours at a high rate. Both are defensible. What is not defensible is paying specialist rates in April for content that should have been fixed in October.

The table sets out the components of a realistic two-year ESS budget using published market figures, with each row attributed. Treat the monthly package rows as what the market advertises rather than what IB Gram charges: our own rate is quoted per 60 minutes, after a free trial lesson, and no package is required to start.

sections.heading: Where ESS marks go missing, and what an hour can actually fix
paragraphs: The most common pattern in our Abu Dhabi ESS caseload is a student who understands the content and writes answers that score two marks below what they deserve. Four causes account for nearly all of it. The first is terminology: using sink, store and flow loosely in a subject where each word has a defined meaning. The second is the environmental value system, which students treat as an opinion to be stated rather than a position to be identified, applied and compared.

The third is the case study used without evidence. A named location with no figures, no date and no mechanism earns credit for recall and nothing for application. Abu Dhabi students have an advantage here that most of them ignore: desalination, district cooling, mangrove restoration and groundwater depletion are visible from the car window and documented by local authorities. A case study a student can actually describe in detail beats a textbook example they half remember.

The fourth is command terms. Evaluate, justify, outline and discuss each demand a different shape of answer, and a student who writes a good essay to the wrong instruction loses marks they never see. This is the cheapest thing to fix and the most reliably fixable: it is technique, not content, and a term of marked practice generally moves it. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child. What an hour a week can honestly offer is a marked paper, a named weakness and a specific thing to practise before the next one.
bullets: Systems vocabulary used loosely is the single most common avoidable loss
An environmental value system must be identified and applied, not merely asserted
Case studies need a figure, a date and a mechanism to score beyond recall
Command terms decide the shape of the answer and are learned by marked practice
Local UAE examples are usually stronger than half-remembered textbook ones

process.title: Tell us the subject, level and the deadline that worries you
process.description: A short message naming the school, the level and what has actually gone wrong is enough to start. For ESS we also ask whether the individual investigation has been chosen, because that single answer changes the shape and the cost of everything that follows.

process.title: We quote a rate per 60 minutes in writing
process.description: No package, no joining fee, no rate that changes after the first month. The quote states what is included: teaching, marking, a written session note and the cancellation rule. If a specialist is not free at the hour you need, we say so instead of offering a generalist at a specialist rate.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach
process.description: Not a sales call with a coordinator. The student works on their own material for the hour, and afterwards you get a written view of where the marks are going and how many hours a realistic plan needs. If the match is wrong, we change the tutor rather than argue about it.

process.title: A fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: The same hour each week, set around school, academy training and family travel. Slots can be moved during school examination weeks, and during Ramadan sessions commonly shift to after Iftar, which we plan for rather than treat as an exception.

process.title: Written evidence after every session
process.description: A note naming what was practised, what was set and what the marked work showed. Over a term those notes are the record a parent can actually read, and they are how a vague worry about ESS turns into a specific list of components and command terms.

whyPoints.title: The rate is quoted before you commit
whyPoints.description: A number per 60 minutes, in writing, with inclusions listed. Three of the six most visible pages in this search publish no price at all and the two that do quote in dollars. A parent should not have to book a call to find out what an hour costs.

whyPoints.title: Market figures are attributed, not invented
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is traceable to the provider or rate survey that published it, read in October 2026. Where a figure cannot be verified, including any fine for tutoring without a permit, this page says so and leaves the number out.

whyPoints.title: Specialists rather than whoever is nearest
whyPoints.description: ESS cohorts in this emirate are small and the local teaching pool is smaller. Online delivery means the choice is among tutors who have taught the current subject guide, not among the people free to drive to your community before dinner.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is stated, not blurred
whyPoints.description: The student designs, collects, analyses and writes. A tutor teaches, questions, marks practice work and names criteria that have not been met. We will not hand back a rewritten document, because that is a malpractice risk carried entirely by your child.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is described honestly
whyPoints.description: Every UAE session is one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and we say so on the page rather than after a deposit. No UAE office, no local branch, no claim to approval by ADEK or any examination board.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for this city
whyPoints.description: Island and mainland commutes, academy training, race weekends on Yas Island and post-Iftar slots during Ramadan all change when a session can realistically run. We plan the year around them instead of defaulting to a 4pm slot nobody can make.

faqs.question: What does an hour of Diploma ESS support cost in Abu Dhabi right now?
faqs.answer: Published market rates for Diploma-level Environmental Systems and Societies support in this emirate run from roughly AED 180 to AED 400 an hour, read in October 2026. Below about AED 150 you are usually buying a non-specialist, often a university student teaching from a textbook rather than the subject guide. Above AED 500 you are paying a reputation premium, which may be justified and should be evidenced. IB Gram quotes a rate per 60 minutes in writing after a free trial lesson, with marking and a written session note included, so the figure you agree is the figure you pay.

faqs.question: Why do two Abu Dhabi tutors quote AED 200 and AED 450 for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Usually because they are selling different things. The lower quote tends to cover teaching only, with no marking, no written feedback and no investigation review. The higher one typically includes a marked paper each week, a session note, and a tutor who has taught the current ESS guide rather than a related science. Timing matters too: the same tutor charges differently for an October slot and an April one, because specialist availability collapses before the May session. Ask both providers the same four questions about marking, feedback, cover and cancellation, and the gap usually explains itself.

faqs.question: Is a monthly ESS package better value than paying by the hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether you use the sessions. Advertised UAE packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Divide by the session count and compare against the hourly rate: a package is only cheaper if you actually sit every session, and families travelling over half-term or sitting school examinations frequently do not. IB Gram does not require a package. The rate is per 60 minutes, agreed in advance, and unused weeks are simply not charged.

faqs.question: Does the rate rise in the weeks before the May examinations?
faqs.answer: Rates for an existing weekly slot should not change mid-term, and ours do not. What changes is availability, which has the same effect on your wallet. By March and April the specialists who have taught the current ESS guide are largely booked, so the remaining options are either less experienced or priced at the top of the band. A family that wants pre-examination intensive support at a sensible rate should book the slot in the autumn term and scale the hours up later, rather than trying to buy specialist time in the final six weeks.

faqs.question: Can we buy support for the individual investigation alone?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most common single purchase Abu Dhabi families make in this subject. A review block of six to eight hours is spread across the weeks the student is working, rather than spent on one read of a finished document. At specialist rates of AED 250 to AED 400 an hour that is roughly AED 1,500 to AED 3,200. The hours cover questioning the research question, checking the method can produce usable data, teaching the statistics and marking a practice version against the published criteria. The student designs, collects, analyses and writes every part of it.

faqs.question: Is ESS cheaper to tutor than Biology or Chemistry at Diploma level?
faqs.answer: No, and often the opposite. Hourly rates for Diploma sciences sit in a similar band, but supply differs sharply. Biology and Chemistry specialists are plentiful in the UAE market, which keeps rates competitive; ESS cohorts are small, option blocks change year to year, and few teachers have taught the current guide. Scarcity pushes the quote towards the upper end of the band. The offsetting factor is hours: an ESS student often needs fewer total hours than a Chemistry student, because the content load is lighter and more of the grade sits in one piece of coursework.

faqs.question: Why can my son's own ESS teacher at his Abu Dhabi school not tutor him privately?
faqs.answer: Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes teachers being prohibited from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. The practical consequence for a parent is that the person who knows the course best is unavailable privately, which is one of the clearest reasons Abu Dhabi families look beyond their own neighbourhood for a specialist.

faqs.question: What does an in-home ESS tutor in Abu Dhabi charge, and what is the money buying?
faqs.answer: Published in-home rates in this market run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The premium covers travel, fuel and the student the tutor cannot teach while driving. For a subject needing only a laptop, a shared screen and marked work, that premium buys presence rather than teaching. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visits are a service we provide only in India, and every UAE session runs one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: How many hours of ESS support does an Abu Dhabi Diploma student usually book?
faqs.answer: Across our own caseload the common shapes are a weekly hour through DP1 term two and DP2, which is roughly fifty to sixty hours over two years, or a compressed plan of a six to eight hour investigation block plus fifteen to twenty hours before the May session. Students starting in February of DP2 use more hours per mark gained, because content gaps and coursework pressure arrive together. These are observations from our own students rather than a published standard, and your child's number depends on where the marks are currently going.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with my child from outside the UAE still need a permit?
faqs.answer: The permit question depends on where the tutor is working from, and it is a fair thing to ask any provider. A tutor resident in the UAE who gives private lessons, including online lessons, needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; it is free and valid for two years. A tutor resident and working abroad is governed by their own jurisdiction's rules. What matters for you is that the provider answers the question clearly and can evidence the position rather than deflecting it.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi schools enter students for ESS at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Option blocks change year to year, so the only reliable answer comes from the school. Ask your IB coordinator two things: whether Environmental Systems and Societies is running for your child's cohort, and at which level. Under the current subject guide the course is offered at Higher Level as well as Standard Level, which is a change from the previous guide, and schools in the emirate adopted it at different speeds. We do not publish a list of which school teaches what, because such a list is out of date within a year and a parent who relies on it plans around a subject their child cannot take.

faqs.question: Will an ESS grade help with UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process and not something a tutoring provider performs or influences. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. No IB points threshold has been verified for this project, so we publish none. Check the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly before planning subject choices around it.

faqs.question: Can a single tutor cover ESS and Geography on one invoice?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it can be efficient rather than merely cheaper. The two subjects share case-study discipline, the habit of naming a place and a figure, and overlapping content on resources and population. One tutor keeps the framing consistent and can stop a student importing geography vocabulary into an ESS answer where the examiner expects systems language. The rate is per hour rather than per subject, so two subjects in one hour means less time on each. For a DP2 student with an investigation deadline we usually recommend separate hours.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if we pause sessions during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Nothing is charged for a session that does not run. Many Abu Dhabi families move to post-Iftar slots rather than pausing, and we schedule for that in advance instead of cancelling week by week. Others pause entirely and resume afterwards, which is a reasonable choice in DP1 and a harder one in DP2 if a coursework deadline sits in the same window. We plan the term around Ramadan, school examination weeks and family travel at the start, so the slot is held rather than lost.

faqs.question: How do I compare two ESS tutoring quotes from Abu Dhabi agencies fairly?
faqs.answer: Put both on the same four questions. Is the rate per 60 minutes or per lesson, and how long is a lesson? Is marking of set work included, and is feedback written or verbal? What happens in May if the tutor becomes unavailable? And who is actually teaching, with what experience of the current ESS guide? Then ask for the cancellation rule in writing. Most of the apparent price gap in this market closes once both quotes are expressed as cost per marked, documented hour with cover arrangements stated.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-environmental-systems-an.closingHeading: Start with the number, then with a trial lesson
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-environmental-systems-an.closingBody: If you are weighing an IB DP Environmental Systems and Societies tutor in Abu Dhabi against a quote you already hold, the useful next step is a free trial lesson with the tutor who would actually teach. Your child works on their own material for the hour; afterwards you get a written view of where the marks are going, how many hours a realistic plan needs, and a rate per 60 minutes with inclusions stated. Sessions run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time around school and training. If no ESS specialist is free in the hour you need, we will tell you rather than offer a generalist at a specialist rate.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-extended-essay-home-tuto.tutorsIntro: The mentors listed here have supervised or marked Extended Essays in a named subject, which is the thing worth paying for. A general academic tutor will improve a paragraph; a subject mentor will tell you that the research question cannot be answered in 4,000 words, which is the intervention that changes the grade.

intro.heading: What paid Extended Essay help is worth, and what you already have for free
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is an independent 4,000-word research piece in a registered subject, written across the two Diploma years, with a school supervisor assigned to it. That supervisor is free. The IB sets a recommended allocation of supervision time — commonly three to five hours in total, including the concluding viva voce — and three mandatory reflection sessions recorded on the Reflections on Planning and Progress Form. Confirm the current figures with your DP coordinator, because they are set in the IB's own guide.

That is the context any paid quote should be read against. A family in Abu Dhabi is not buying supervision; it exists already. They are buying cover for the gaps between those few hours: a research question that will not work, a subject the supervisor does not read, a student who has written 5,800 words and cannot cut, a term where nothing happened and the deadline is six weeks out.

Market rates are published by comparison sites rather than by tutors, so here they are. Rate comparisons compiled in October 2026 put qualified subject tutors working online at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 once travel is inside the fee, and IB specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with premium named tutors advertised as high as AED 650. Monthly packages appear from about AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are market figures, not IB Gram prices.

The Extended Essay is unusual in that the useful spend is concentrated in a few short windows rather than spread evenly. Two hours at the research-question stage are worth more than ten hours of drafting support, because a question that cannot be answered in the word limit cannot be rescued by better writing. Most families discover this in reverse order, which is why the bill ends up where it does.

There is also a hard ceiling on what money can legitimately buy. The essay must be the student's own work, the reflections must be their own, and the viva voce is a conversation they have unaided. Criterion E, engagement, carries marks of its own and is assessed through those reflections. A mentor who offers to supply text is selling a risk that lands on the candidate rather than on themselves.

Delivery in the UAE is online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi and sends no tutor to an address in this emirate; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For a research project that is a convenience rather than a compromise: the work is documents, and documents are better shared on a screen than carried to a villa.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-extended-essay-home-tuto.programmesIntro: Extended Essay costs vary with where the student is in the Diploma and with what their school has already provided. These notes describe the three positions Abu Dhabi families actually ring from.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is a core requirement alongside Theory of Knowledge and CAS, registered in one subject, capped at 4,000 words, and graded A to E. It combines with TOK to contribute points to the Diploma total and carries a failing condition of its own at the lowest grade. Confirm the current award conditions with your DP coordinator rather than from any third party.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools set internal Extended Essay deadlines well before the IB submission date, often with a first full draft due in the first term of DP2. Those internal dates are what a spend plan should be built around, because they are the ones that actually constrain the work. Ask the coordinator for the school's written timeline in DP1; families who have it spend materially less than those who improvise.

programmes.name: Students already in difficulty
programmes.description: The most common paid enquiry: a student with a research question that does not work, or a draft that is too long, too descriptive, or in a subject nobody at home can read. Here the money buys triage, and triage is cheap compared with drafting support. One or two hours of honest diagnosis usually replaces a month of expensive flailing.
programmes.countryNote: In this emirate the DP2 crunch is sharpened by internal assessment deadlines landing in the same weeks across several subjects. The practical consequence is that the hours bought in that window cost more in attention than in dirhams, and that the cheapest version of this project is the one planned in DP1 and merely supported in DP2.

programmes.name: Students arriving mid-Diploma
programmes.description: A student joining an Abu Dhabi school mid-course may arrive with an essay registered in a subject the new school teaches differently, or with no registration at all. The first paid hour should go on establishing what the new school requires and by when, not on content, because the requirements decide everything that follows.
programmes.countryNote: Mid-course arrivals are routine in Abu Dhabi, where employment postings run to two and three years. Transfers are also the group most likely to be quoted for a large block of hours they do not need, because the apparent crisis is administrative. Get the school's written timeline first and the quote will usually shrink.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-extended-essay-home-tuto.subjectsIntro: What an Extended Essay costs to support depends heavily on the subject it is registered in, because some essays need data the student cannot easily obtain. The subjects below are the ones Abu Dhabi families most often register in, with the cost consequence named.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.levels: Core · 4,000 words · graded A to E
subjects.description: An independent research piece in a registered subject with a school supervisor, three reflection sessions on the RPPF, and a concluding viva voce. Marks are lost on research questions too broad to answer, description where critical analysis was required, and presentation errors in referencing that cost cheap marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Among the most expensive essays to support, because a strong one usually wants primary data and school laboratory time is finite. Where the school cannot provide access, a well-designed secondary-data essay is cheaper and often scores better than a thin experiment.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same constraint as Biology with tighter safety limits on what a school will allow. The costly failure here is a question that requires equipment nobody has, discovered two months in. One hour spent checking feasibility against the school's actual kit is the best-value hour in the project.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Popular in this emirate and relatively cheap to support, because the data is public. The common and expensive error is a question about the whole UAE economy rather than a narrow, answerable one, which no amount of drafting help can repair later.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Attractive because local company material feels accessible, and risky because primary interviews often require permissions that take weeks. Where interviews are in Arabic, translation and transcription add real hours that nobody budgets for at the start.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Human participants mean ethical approval, consent and school permission, and in a school setting that paperwork alone can run to weeks. Most cost overruns in Psychology essays are administrative rather than intellectual, which is why the feasibility check matters more here than elsewhere.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Cheap to support when the sources are accessible and expensive when they are not. Essays on regional history can require Arabic-language sources, and a student without the language either narrows the question or budgets for translation; both are decisions to take in DP1.

subjects.name: English A
subjects.description: Usually the least expensive essay to support, because the text is the data. The spend concentrates entirely at the research-question stage, where a question about a theme rather than about a specific argument produces 4,000 words of description.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Low in materials cost and high in supervisor scarcity, since few school supervisors are comfortable with the subject at this level. This is the clearest case for paid subject-specific mentoring, because the gap is expertise rather than effort.

sections.heading: Who provides what, and which of it is already paid for
paragraphs: The first step in controlling Extended Essay cost is a map of what exists for free. The school assigns a supervisor, with a recommended allocation of supervision hours including the concluding viva voce, and runs three mandatory reflection sessions recorded on the Reflections on Planning and Progress Form. The school library provides database access. The DP coordinator provides the internal deadlines. None of that is billed.

What the free provision reliably covers is process: registration, deadlines, the reflection conversations, approval of the research question, and a final interview. What it covers unevenly is subject expertise, because a supervisor is assigned from available staff and may not read the subject the student has chosen at the level the essay needs. That unevenness is the honest reason to buy anything.

The second honest reason is capacity. A supervisor with several essays and a full teaching timetable gives each student a few hours across two years. A student who needs more contact than that is not being short-changed; they are using more than the system allocates. Paid hours top that up, and they are only worth their price where they do something the supervisor is not able to do.

The third is diagnosis under time pressure. A supervisor who sees a draft three weeks before an internal deadline is working inside the same constraint as everyone else. An outside reader with a clear hour and the published criteria open can produce a written diagnosis quickly, and that single document is often the whole of what a family actually needed to buy.

sections.heading: The spend calendar: which weeks repay paid hours
paragraphs: Extended Essay money is badly distributed in most families, with little spent early and a great deal spent late. The project rewards the opposite pattern, because early errors compound and late help can only tidy. A spend calendar built in DP1 typically costs less than half of one assembled in a panic during DP2.

The early windows are cheap and decisive. Choosing the subject to register in, testing the research question for answerability, and checking feasibility against the school's actual resources are two or three hours of work that determine the next twelve months. At the qualified band of AED 150 to AED 300 that is a few hundred dirhams, and it is the only spend that reliably prevents other spend.

The middle of the project generally does not repay paid hours at all. Reading, note-taking, data collection and first drafting are the student's own work and the supervisor's territory, and a weekly paid session through this period mostly buys company. Families on standing arrangements usually discover they paid most in the months where least was happening.

The late windows repay a specific kind of help: one diagnosis on a complete draft, and one session on cutting to the word limit. Both are discrete, both produce a document, and both are better bought as single blocks than as a monthly commitment. sections.heading: What makes an Abu Dhabi Extended Essay cost more than the same essay elsewhere
paragraphs: Some of the cost drivers in this project are local, and they are the ones nobody warns families about. The first is primary data. An essay that needs human participants requires consent and school permission, and in an Abu Dhabi school that paperwork can run to weeks rather than days. The delay is not the school being obstructive; it is a reasonable process meeting a student timetable that did not allow for it.

The second is language. Essays on regional subjects frequently rest on Arabic-language sources, interviews or documents. A student without the language either narrows the question or pays for translation and transcription, and the second option is real money and real time. The decision belongs in DP1, where it costs a conversation, rather than in DP2, where it costs the schedule.

The third is laboratory access. School laboratory time is finite everywhere, and a science essay requiring repeated trials competes with teaching. Where access is limited, the cheaper and often better-scoring route is a well-designed secondary-data essay, which is also the one most students resist because an experiment sounds more impressive.

The fourth is calendar compression. Abu Dhabi schools set internal draft deadlines earlier than the IB submission date, and those deadlines land in the same weeks as internal assessments in other subjects. Paid hours in that window cost more in attention than in money, and the way to avoid them is to put the question and feasibility work a year earlier.
