sections.heading: The research question is the cheapest thing to fix and the dearest to get wrong
paragraphs: Nearly every expensive Extended Essay began with a question that could not be answered in 4,000 words. A question about a whole national economy, a whole author, a whole historical period or a whole biological process does not fail because the student wrote badly. It fails because no 4,000-word answer exists, so the essay becomes a survey and the criteria reward analysis.

Diagnosing that takes about twenty minutes with someone who reads the subject, and the test is mechanical: state the question, then state what the conclusion would look like. If the conclusion is a summary of what is known rather than a judgement the student has reached, the question is too broad. Narrow it until the conclusion is contestable and the whole project becomes cheaper.

The cost of getting this wrong rises sharply with time. In DP1, a rethink is one session. After three months of reading, it costs the reading. After a first full draft, it costs the draft, and at that point families start buying hours at specialist rates in the worst week of DP2 to rescue something structurally unsound. This is the single clearest place where a few hundred dirhams early replaces a few thousand late.

A supervisor approves the question, and approval is not the same as endurance. A question can be approved, perfectly respectable, and still prove unanswerable once the student is inside it. That is a normal research experience rather than a failure by anyone, and it is exactly the moment an outside subject reader earns their fee, because changing course early is cheaper than persevering.

sections.heading: Three pricing models, and the trap in each
paragraphs: Extended Essay help is sold three ways in this market and the model matters more than the rate. By the hour, by the draft, or by the project. Each suits a different problem and each has a predictable failure, and a family that picks the model deliberately usually pays considerably less than one that accepts whatever is offered first.

By the hour is the most flexible and the easiest to overspend on, because hours accumulate in the months when nothing needs an adult. It suits the feasibility and question stage, where two focused hours do the work, and it suits specialist mentoring in a subject the school cannot cover. It does not suit the long middle of the project.

By the draft is the model most families should use for the late stages: one fixed fee for a complete read and a written diagnosis against the criteria. The trap is scope. Agree in advance whether that includes a second read after revision, and what happens if the draft arrives at twice the word limit, because both change the work substantially.

By the project — a single fee for support from question to submission — looks tidy and carries the most risk. It bundles the months that need nothing with the hours that need someone, and it creates an incentive to be involved in the writing itself, which is exactly where the honesty line sits. Where a project fee is quoted, ask what it excludes and how the hours are distributed across the calendar.

sections.heading: The cheap marks: reflections, referencing and the word limit
paragraphs: Some Extended Essay marks cost nothing and are routinely left on the table. The three reflection sessions are recorded on the Reflections on Planning and Progress Form, and engagement is assessed through them as a criterion in its own right. Students treat the form as administration, write it in fifteen minutes the night before, and lose marks that required only honesty and a little detail about what actually changed in their thinking.

Referencing and presentation are the same story. A consistent citation style, a properly formatted bibliography, correct use of appendices and a title page that follows the school's instructions are worth marks under presentation, and they are the only marks in the project that can be secured with no intellectual effort whatsoever. Students lose them while paying for help with analysis.

The word limit is the third. Examiners are not required to read beyond 4,000 words, so anything past that point is work the student did for nothing, and a conclusion sitting at 4,300 words may simply not count. Cutting is a skill and it is worth one paid session if a draft is badly over, but the cheaper route is to plan section word budgets before drafting.

The useful habit for a family is to audit these three things before buying anything else. Read the RPPF entries; if they contain no specific change of direction, they are costing marks. Check the bibliography for consistency. Check the word count including whatever the current guide says counts towards it. Those three checks take an evening and cost nothing, and they frequently recover more than the first paid session would.

sections.heading: What no fee can buy, at any price
paragraphs: There is a firm limit to what paid help can legitimately do here, and it is worth stating in commercial terms as well as ethical ones. The essay must be the student's own work. The reflections must record the student's own thinking. The viva voce is a conversation they hold unaided with their supervisor, and a candidate who did not do the work tends to reveal it there within a few minutes.

A mentor may test a research question, check feasibility, explain a criterion, recommend where to look, read a draft and name what is not working, explain why a paragraph describes rather than analyses, and teach the student to cut. A mentor may not supply text, restructure a draft into a different essay, rewrite prose to a level the student cannot reach, or produce the reflections. We decline those requests, including from families who ask kindly and close to a deadline.

Text generated by an AI tool belongs in the same category for submitted work. In an Extended Essay it is also unusually easy to detect, because the references are plausible and frequently wrong, and a fabricated citation in a bibliography is a conspicuous problem in a project marked partly on the handling of sources. A mentor's realistic contribution here is teaching a student to verify every reference they cite.

One further caution, since this is a page about money: there are services in this market selling completed assessed work, with prices advertised openly. Buying one is an academic-integrity breach that puts the candidate's diploma at risk, not the seller's business. No part of this page should be read as an offer of that kind, and a provider who implies they can take the project off your hands is quoting for something nobody can legitimately sell.

sections.heading: Online mentoring against an in-home tutor for a research project
paragraphs: In-home tutoring exists here and families often assume it is the premium option. Published market comparisons put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour with travel inside the fee, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online and AED 200 to AED 450 or more for an IB specialist. Those are market figures from published rate tables rather than IB Gram prices.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE. We do not send a tutor to an Abu Dhabi address and we run no home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tuition is a service we offer only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one online, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and for this project that is a practical advantage rather than a concession.

The Extended Essay is a documents project. The work is a research question on a shared document, a draft annotated in front of both people with the criteria open alongside, a bibliography checked line by line, and a cut list built live. A tutor sitting in your living room reads the same screen you would have shared, having charged for the drive and taken a 90-minute minimum booking to justify it.

Supervisor scarcity is the other half of the argument. The whole reason to buy mentoring is usually that nobody at the school reads the subject at this level, and the in-home pool within reach of your community is smaller than the school's staff room. For an essay registered in Mathematics or Psychology, the local option may not exist at any price while the online one does.

process.title: Get the school's timeline before spending anything
process.description: Ask the DP coordinator for the internal Extended Essay deadlines, the supervisor's name and subject, and the dates of the three reflection sessions. Half the quotes families receive shrink once that document exists, because the apparent crisis is usually a calendar problem.

process.title: Free trial lesson used as a feasibility check
process.description: The trial is free, needs no card and carries no obligation. It tests the research question against the word limit, the available data and the school's actual resources, and you leave with the question rewritten and a written note on feasibility whether or not you continue.

process.title: Choose the pricing model deliberately
process.description: Hourly for question and feasibility work, per draft for diagnosis, specialist mentoring where the school has no subject cover. Agree in writing what a draft read includes, whether a second read is covered and the maximum word count. Decline project fees unless the exclusions are written down.

process.title: Buy against a named deliverable
process.description: Every block has an output: a rewritten question, a feasibility note, an annotated draft with the criteria named, a cut list by section. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the document lands in a shared folder you keep.

process.title: Stop when the deliverable is done
process.description: There is no standing arrangement to cancel. The months of reading and drafting do not need paid hours, and we will say so rather than filling them. Families who follow the spend calendar on this page typically buy four to six sessions across the whole project.

whyPoints.title: We tell you what the school already gives you free
whyPoints.description: A supervisor with an allocated number of hours, three reflection sessions, library access and the internal deadlines. Paid help is only worth its rate where it does something that provision cannot, and naming that boundary costs us hours we could otherwise bill.

whyPoints.description: Two hours at the research-question stage outperform ten at drafting, because a question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words cannot be rescued by better writing. The spend calendar on this page is the plan we actually recommend.

whyPoints.title: Priced per deliverable, not per month
whyPoints.description: Each block produces a document: a rewritten question, a feasibility note, an annotated draft, a cut list. There is no standing weekly arrangement, because the long middle of this project genuinely does not need one.

faqs.question: If the school already provides a supervisor, what am I paying an Extended Essay mentor for?
faqs.answer: For the gaps the free provision does not cover. A supervisor has an allocated number of hours across two years, including the concluding viva voce, and is assigned from available staff, so they may not read your child's registered subject at the level the essay needs. Paid hours are worth their rate for three things: testing whether a research question is answerable, subject expertise the school cannot supply, and a written diagnosis of a complete draft. For everything else the supervisor is the right person and is already paid for.

faqs.question: What does Extended Essay help cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published rate comparisons compiled in October 2026 put qualified subject tutors working online at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 with travel inside the fee, and IB specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 or more, with premium named tutors advertised up to AED 650. Monthly online packages appear from about AED 799 for eight sessions. Those are market bands from published tables rather than IB Gram prices, and they are the benchmark any quote you receive should be read against.

faqs.question: Which stage of the Extended Essay is actually worth paying for?
faqs.answer: The research-question stage, by a wide margin. Two hours spent testing whether a question can be answered in 4,000 words with the data and resources actually available will often save a month of expensive rescue work later. After that, one session diagnosing a complete draft and, if needed, one on cutting to the word limit. The long middle — reading, note-taking, data collection, first drafting — is the student's own work and rarely repays a standing paid arrangement.

faqs.question: Our son's draft is 5,900 words. How much does cutting cost?
faqs.answer: Usually one session, because cutting is a skill rather than a labour: the work is identifying which sections are description that the criteria do not reward, which quotations can be summarised, and what belongs in an appendix under the current guide's rules. At market bands that is AED 150 to AED 450. Worth knowing before you pay: examiners are not required to read beyond 4,000 words, so a conclusion sitting past the limit may simply not count, which makes this a high-return single session.

faqs.question: Is a project fee from question to submission good value?
faqs.answer: Rarely, for two reasons. It bundles months that genuinely need nobody with the few hours that need someone, so you pay through the idle period. And a fixed fee tied to a finished essay creates pressure towards involvement in the writing itself, which is where the academic-honesty line sits and where the risk falls on your child rather than the provider. If a project fee is quoted, ask in writing what it excludes and how the hours are distributed across the calendar.

faqs.question: Does registering the essay in a science cost more to support in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the reason is access rather than difficulty. School laboratory time is finite and competes with teaching, safety limits what a student may attempt, and an experimental design needing repeated trials may not fit the slots available. Where that is the position, a well-designed secondary-data essay using published datasets is cheaper and frequently scores better than a thin experiment. The feasibility check against the school's actual equipment is one hour and prevents the most expensive failure in this project.

faqs.question: My daughter wants to interview a local company. What does that add?
faqs.answer: Time, permissions and possibly translation. Company access requires someone's agreement and often several weeks of waiting, and interviews conducted in Arabic need transcription and translation, which is real money and real hours that nobody budgets at the start. For most Business Management questions, published reports and filings are a stronger evidence base than one interview, because they can be analysed rather than merely quoted. Make that decision in the first Diploma year, where it costs a conversation.

faqs.question: Do the reflection sessions and the RPPF really carry marks?
faqs.answer: Yes. Engagement is assessed through the three mandatory reflection sessions recorded on the Reflections on Planning and Progress Form, and it is a criterion in its own right within the total. Students treat the form as administration and write it the night before, losing marks that needed only honesty and some specific detail about what changed in their thinking and why. Confirm the current mark allocation with your DP coordinator. Reading your child's RPPF entries is free and frequently recovers more than a paid session would.

faqs.question: Can a mentor fix a research question that the supervisor already approved?
faqs.answer: Yes, and approval is not the same thing as durability. A question can be entirely respectable, approved in good faith, and still prove unanswerable in 4,000 words once the student is inside the reading. That is an ordinary research experience, not a failure by the supervisor. The test is mechanical: state the question, then state what the conclusion would look like. If the conclusion is a summary of existing knowledge rather than a judgement the student reached, narrow the question before another month is spent.

faqs.question: Does the Extended Essay affect the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process?
faqs.answer: Equivalency requirements are set by the Ministry and differ by curriculum, and for the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels. For the IB no points threshold should be taken from any third-party page; verify on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency, and no tutoring is required for it.

faqs.question: Does a mentor need a MoHRE permit to charge for Extended Essay help in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents and university students. Those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. Ask any mentor whether they hold it before money changes hands.

faqs.question: Can we pay someone to proofread the essay before submission?
faqs.answer: Advice on grammar, consistency and formatting is legitimate; making the changes is not. The practical line is that errors may be pointed out and corrections must be the student's own, because prose rewritten to a level the candidate could not produce is no longer their work. In a project assessed partly on presentation and the handling of sources, the useful version of this service is a consistency check on the bibliography and citation style, which costs little and secures marks that need no intellectual effort.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an Extended Essay tutor to our home in Abu Dhabi, and would that cost more?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE, and no tutor is sent to an address here; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Published market comparisons put in-home visits at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online tutor, with the gap largely travel. For this project the bigger issue is subject match: the local pool for a Mathematics or Psychology essay may contain nobody who reads it at this level.

faqs.question: How many sessions do Abu Dhabi families usually end up buying for the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Families who follow a spend calendar typically buy four to six sessions across the whole project: two on the research question, one on feasibility, one or two diagnosing drafts, and one on cutting to the word limit. Families who start in the second term of the final year and buy weekly hours spend several times that and get less, because the decisive errors were made a year earlier. The cheapest version of this project is the one planned early and merely supported late.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for help to move an Extended Essay grade by one letter?
faqs.answer: That arithmetic is yours, and nobody can honestly promise a letter. What can be said is where the effect is clearest: a question that was unanswerable becoming answerable, a draft that described becoming a draft that argues, and free presentation and reflection marks being collected rather than left. Those are structural changes rather than polish. Expect a reasoned view on what the draft is currently missing against the published criteria, and treat any specific grade promise as a reason to look elsewhere.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-extended-essay-home-tuto.closingHeading: Get the school's timeline, then buy only the hours that work
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-extended-essay-home-tuto.closingBody: If you are pricing an IB DP Extended Essay home tutor in Abu Dhabi, start with two free things: the school's written Extended Essay timeline, and your child's own RPPF entries. Then take the free trial lesson, which costs nothing, needs no card and carries no obligation, and use it as a feasibility check rather than an introduction — you leave with the research question rewritten and a written note on whether it can be answered in 4,000 words. From there, buy against named deliverables: a diagnosis, a cut list, a subject reality check. Lessons run online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below mentor Extended Essay projects by subject: research question shaping, source discipline, the structure that criterion C rewards, and reflection writing that is not an afterthought. Each works to a stated number of hours rather than an open arrangement.

intro.heading: The Extended Essay is a project, so price it like one
paragraphs: Families in Abu Dhabi buy Extended Essay help in one of two shapes, and only one of them is good value. The first is a block: a defined number of hours attached to defined stages, starting with the research question and ending before the final submission, with a number agreed at the outset. The second is a monthly arrangement that starts in DP1 and quietly continues until the deadline, which is how an AED 300 hourly rate becomes a four-figure total that nobody reviewed.

Market rates give you the arithmetic to choose. One-to-one tutoring in the UAE, surveyed in October 2026, runs from roughly AED 45 an hour at the university-student end to AED 650 and above for a premium named tutor. Agency start rates are around AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts the subject-specialist band at AED 200 to 450 plus and in-home visits at AED 180 to 350. Those are market figures with their sources, not our price list.

Applied to an Extended Essay, a realistic block is somewhere between eight and sixteen hours spread across a year, heavily loaded at the front. At specialist rates that is a sum a family can plan around and compare. What it is not is a monthly line item, and a provider who cannot tell you how many hours they expect to need has not scoped the work.

There is a prior question that costs nothing and changes the answer. Every Extended Essay has a school supervisor whose time is already inside your fees, allocated around three reflection sessions and a concluding discussion. In Abu Dhabi the amount of that time a student actually receives varies between schools and between departments inside the same school, depending on how many candidates a supervisor is carrying. Ask the coordinator before buying anything, because where supervision is genuinely strong the right block is short or nothing at all.

Where the hours go matters as much as how many there are. The essay is marked against five criteria worth 34 marks in total, and they are not equally weighted. Criterion C, critical thinking, carries by far the largest share on its own. Criterion D, presentation, carries the smallest. Yet the hours families buy most readily are formatting, proofreading and bibliography tidying, which sit in the smallest criterion. That mismatch is the single most expensive habit in Extended Essay spending.

IB Gram mentors Extended Essays as one-to-one online sessions over live video for families across Abu Dhabi. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. Every word of the essay and of the reflections is the student's own: we ask whether a claim is supported, whether the research question is answerable in 4,000 words, and whether the method matches the question. We do not supply text, rewrite sections, or comment on a draft about to be submitted as final.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.programmesIntro: Only the Diploma Programme requires an Extended Essay, but the research habits it assesses are built earlier and the cost of not building them lands here. This is how the spend typically falls across the continuum in Abu Dhabi.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: One independent research essay of up to 4,000 words in a chosen subject, supervised by a school supervisor, with three reflections recorded on the reflections on planning and progress form and a concluding discussion. Graded A to E and combined with Theory of Knowledge to produce the diploma core points.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools vary widely in how much supervision time they actually deliver against the IB's recommended allocation. Where a supervisor is carrying eight students alongside a full teaching timetable, the gap families fill externally is real. Where supervision is strong, buying external mentoring on top is paying twice, and asking the coordinator how many supervision hours are scheduled is a free way to find out which you are in.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Personal Project is the Extended Essay's direct ancestor: an independent piece of work with a process journal, a product and a report, assessed on planning, action and reflection. A student who kept a real process journal in the MYP finds the reflections requirement familiar rather than baffling.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest preparation available anywhere in the continuum and almost nobody pays for it, which is correct. Reopening a completed Personal Project's process journal at the start of DP1 costs nothing and removes two of the three places Extended Essay projects stall in Abu Dhabi: vague questions and reflections written in a panic the night before a deadline.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP Exhibition is a collaborative inquiry with a presentation rather than an essay, but it introduces the idea that a question is chosen, narrowed and defended. No external support is normally bought at this stage and none is needed.
programmes.countryNote: Worth naming only because families arriving in Abu Dhabi from examination-driven systems sometimes treat the PYP Exhibition as a soft year. A child who has never had to narrow their own question tends to produce an unanswerable Extended Essay research question six years later, and that is the problem that costs the most to fix in DP1.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students do not write an Extended Essay. The CP core includes a reflective project instead, assessed against its own criteria, with a different length and a different structure. Preparation for one does not transfer cleanly to the other.
programmes.countryNote: The commonest overpayment in the Abu Dhabi core is a CP student being charged for Extended Essay mentoring, or a DP student being coached against reflective project criteria. Both happen. Confirm with the coordinator which core component your child is registered for before paying anyone for support against it.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.subjectsIntro: Subject choice changes the research question, the data problem and therefore the hours required. These are the Extended Essay subjects Abu Dhabi students pick most often, with the cost logic attached to each.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Popular and expensive to support when the student plans primary experimental work, because a method that cannot be run in a school laboratory has to be redesigned. Secondary-data essays using published datasets cost less to mentor and often score better, since criterion C rewards analysis rather than apparatus.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same pattern as Biology with a sharper safety constraint. The commonest rescue job is a question requiring equipment or reagents the school will not sanction, discovered in week six. One early session on feasibility saves several later.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Attracts ambitious questions with no measurable outcome. Mentoring hours here go almost entirely into narrowing: turning a question about a phenomenon into a question about a measurable relationship that 4,000 words can actually settle.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Comparatively cheap to support because the data problem disappears, but demanding on criterion C: the essay must argue, not merely derive. Under-chosen in Abu Dhabi cohorts, and distinctive when done with discipline.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Needs a genuine dataset and a theoretical frame that fits it. Regional data on trade, energy, tourism and labour markets is accessible, which keeps the hours down, but questions about the whole economy are unanswerable and get rewritten late at cost.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Attractive because local case material is plentiful, risky because the question frequently becomes a consultancy report rather than an analysis. Mentoring time goes into holding an analytical frame instead of a recommendation.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Strong value per mentoring hour when the student has access to a bounded body of sources. The expensive failure is a topic requiring archives nobody here can reach; the cheap success is a narrower question on sources available in English and Arabic online.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Primary research with human participants raises ethics requirements that schools must approve, and an ethics refusal in week eight is an expensive restart. Essays built on published studies avoid that entirely and are frequently stronger on critical thinking.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Low data cost, high analytical demand. The text is available, so hours go into the argument rather than into logistics. The commonest problem is a question that invites summary of the work instead of an argument about it.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Requires specific works the student can examine properly, which the emirate's galleries and collections make more feasible than in many places. Mentoring is about resisting biography and description in favour of analysis.

subjects.name: World Studies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary route built around a global issue examined through two subjects. Genuinely harder to mentor, because the essay must integrate rather than alternate between the two lenses, and that usually means more hours than a single-subject essay.

sections.heading: What Extended Essay support costs in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: A sensible Extended Essay block in this market is eight to sixteen hours spread across the year, bought at the subject-specialist rate. Market rates surveyed in October 2026 put that band at AED 200 to 450 and above per hour, with the wider UAE one-to-one range running from about AED 45 at the university-student end to AED 650 and above for a premium named tutor. Agency start rates begin around AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table gives AED 200 to 450 plus for specialists and AED 180 to 350 for in-home visits.

Those are market figures with sources attached, published because a parent cannot judge a quote without them and because most pages competing for this search publish none at all. They are not IB Gram's prices. We scope the hours against the stage the project is at and discuss the plan on a consultation, with one free trial consultation per project and no card details taken beforehand.

The table below distributes a block across the five stages of the work. Read the hours column rather than the money column: it shows how front-loaded this project is. More than half the useful mentoring time sits before a single section of the essay has been drafted, and the stage families most readily pay for, final tidying, is the one with the least available marks behind it.

A quote that names a total for the essay rather than a number of hours should be refused. It is either an unscoped guess or an offer to produce the work, and the second is a malpractice problem rather than a service. Ask for the hours, the stages, the hourly figure and the point at which the block ends.

sections.heading: Where the 34 marks sit, and where the money should follow them
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is marked out of 34 across five criteria, and the distribution is lopsided in a way that should reshape any spending decision. Criterion C, critical thinking, carries twelve of those marks on its own, more than a third of the total. Criterion A, focus and method, and criterion B, knowledge and understanding, carry six each. Criterion E, engagement, assessed through the reflections, also carries six. Criterion D, presentation, carries four.

Now compare that with how families spend. Presentation is tangible: a title page, consistent referencing, a tidy contents list. It is easy to buy help with and easy to verify. It is also the smallest criterion on the sheet. Critical thinking is the opposite: hard to see, hard to buy, impossible to add at the end, and worth three times as much.

Criterion E is the quietest opportunity in the project. Engagement is assessed through 500 words of reflection written across three points in the process, and it carries the same marks as knowledge and understanding of an entire subject. Students routinely reconstruct all three reflections the week before submission, producing a bland account of a project that actually involved real decisions and real dead ends. Those dead ends are the material criterion E rewards.

The practical rule that follows is to spend early on A and C and almost nothing on D. A research question that is answerable and a method that fits it will carry criterion A for free. A student who has been asked, repeatedly, what their evidence does not show will produce criterion C writing without being taught a formula. Nothing bought in the final fortnight touches either.

sections.heading: Why the Extended Essay is bought as a block, and the two ways that goes wrong
paragraphs: Unlike a subject tutor, an Extended Essay mentor is not maintaining a weekly skill. They are helping a student through a sequence of decisions, each of which takes an hour or two and then releases weeks of independent work. The correct shape is therefore bursts with gaps, and the gaps are where the essay actually gets written.

The first way this goes wrong is the open arrangement. A weekly slot booked in September of DP1 and left running produces thirty sessions, most of which have nothing specific to do, and a total that nobody would have agreed to in advance. The tell is a session that begins with how is it going rather than with a document on screen.

The second is the compressed block. A family starts in February of DP2 with the deadline in sight and buys ten hours in three weeks. By then the research question is fixed, the reading is done, the method cannot change and criterion C cannot be rebuilt. Those ten hours are spent on presentation and panic, which is the smallest criterion and the highest hourly cost in the year, because exam-season availability is tight across this market.

The version that works is dull and cheap by comparison. Two or three hours in DP1 on the question. One or two on method. Three to five in DP2 autumn on the argument. One or two on the reflections. One at the end on checks. A family that books in that order typically spends less than a family that books a weekly slot for a term, and arrives with a stronger essay.

sections.heading: What the school supervisor already provides, and why you may be paying twice
paragraphs: Every Extended Essay has a school supervisor, and their time is already inside your school fees. The IB expects a limited, specified amount of supervision across the project, built around the three reflection sessions and a concluding discussion. That is not a lot of hours, but it is the authoritative guidance on the project, from someone who knows the subject, the school's internal deadlines and the student.

Before buying anything externally, ask the coordinator two questions: how many supervision hours are scheduled for this project, and how many students is the supervisor carrying. In Abu Dhabi the answers vary enormously between schools and sometimes between departments in the same school. A supervisor with two students and a free period is a different proposition from one with nine students and a full timetable.

Where supervision is strong, external mentoring should be narrow and short: a second analytical voice on criterion C, or help with a research question in a subject the supervisor does not teach. Where it is thin, the gap is real and worth filling, but it should still be filled in the stages where marks live rather than spread across the year.

What external mentoring must never do is substitute for the supervisor's role in the IB's process. The three reflections and the concluding discussion are between the student and the school. The school authenticates the work. An external mentor who positions themselves as the real supervisor is creating a documentation problem for the candidate, and the candidate is the one the IB's procedures apply to.

sections.heading: Subject choice is the cheapest decision in the project
paragraphs: The subject a student chooses decides the data problem, and the data problem decides the hours. An essay built on published sources costs a fraction of one built on primary research that has to be redesigned twice. This is a decision made in a single conversation in DP1 and it determines most of what follows.

The expensive pattern is familiar. A student picks a science subject out of enthusiasm, designs an experiment that requires equipment the school does not have or ethics approval it will not grant, discovers this in week six, and starts again with less time and more panic. Every hour of mentoring after that point is rescue work bought at the same rate as planning work would have been.

Abu Dhabi offers some genuine advantages that are worth using rather than ignoring. Regional economic and energy data is accessible for an Economics essay. Specific exhibited works are available for a Visual Arts or History question. A multilingual school population makes certain language and human-science questions answerable with primary material collected properly, provided the school approves the ethics in advance.

The table below sets out the commonest choices with the data problem and the cost implication attached. It is not a ranking: the right subject is the one the student can sustain for a year. It is a map of where the hours tend to go, so a family can see the bill before it arrives rather than after.

sections.heading: The line between mentoring and producing, and the market that crosses it
paragraphs: Extended Essay support is the part of the diploma where the market is least honest. Operations advertising in this space offer finished assessed coursework outright, with a price attached and a turnaround time. That is not an expensive tutoring service. It is an academic-integrity breach that triggers the IB's malpractice procedures, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the seller.

A parent can draw the line without knowing the IB regulations in detail, because it reduces to one question: who is writing the words? A mentor may help shape a research question, test whether a method fits it, interrogate the strength of a source, ask what the evidence fails to show, point out that a paragraph asserts rather than argues, and explain what criterion C rewards. A mentor may not supply sentences, rewrite a section, build an outline for the student to fill, or edit a near-final draft.

Generated text belongs in the same category. An essay produced in part by a language model is not the student's own work, and in a 4,000-word research piece it is identifiable: generic examples, symmetrical argument, confident claims with no source behind them. Students sometimes intend to use a tool for a first pass and keep more of it than they meant to. The safe rule is that nothing enters the document the student did not write.

We also do not supply IB material. Exemplar essays, assessment instruments, subject guides and mark schemes belong to the IB and to your child's school, and reproducing them would be a copyright problem as well as poor practice. If a provider offers you a bank of past Extended Essays to work from, that tells you what kind of operation it is.

sections.heading: Cost in context, and what a legitimate quote looks like
paragraphs: Set against the rest of a diploma budget, a properly scoped Extended Essay block is small. Monthly tutoring packages advertised in the UAE run at AED 799 a month for eight online sessions at the budget end and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. An eight to sixteen hour block, bought once, sits comfortably below a year of any of those.

School fees give the wider frame. Fees are regulated at emirate level: in Dubai, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27 under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. In Abu Dhabi, fee applications go through ADEK, which licenses and inspects the emirate's private schools and publishes its own inspection ratings. We publish no Abu Dhabi fee figure because we have not read one on ADEK's own pages.

A legitimate quote for Extended Essay mentoring states the hourly figure, the session length in minutes, the number of hours proposed, the stages those hours cover, and the point at which the block ends. It does not quote a price for an essay. It does not require payment for a term in advance. It does not include a charge for a tutor permit, because the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 is granted free of charge for two years.

On tax, keep the question narrow: ask whether the figure quoted to you includes VAT. The wider treatment of tuition fees under UAE VAT rules is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring page, and anyone asserting a position on it without citing the authority is guessing on your behalf.

sections.heading: The February Extended Essay, and what it costs
paragraphs: The most expensive Extended Essay in Abu Dhabi is the one that starts in February of DP2. It is expensive in three separate ways, and families rarely see the third until the bill arrives.

The first is availability. Demand across this market concentrates in the weeks before the May session, when internal assessments in six subjects land alongside the essay deadline. Specialists booked in October are bought at October availability; the same request in February is filled from whoever is free, often at the top of the band.

The second is that the hours can no longer reach the marks. By February the research question is registered, the reading is done, the method is fixed and the reflections are overdue. Criterion C, twelve of the 34 marks, is built into the structure of a draft that already exists. What ten hours can still change is presentation, worth four marks, and a little of criterion E if the reflections have not yet been written.

The third is the opportunity cost inside the diploma. Ten hours bought in February are ten hours not spent on examined subjects in the final run-up, and the Extended Essay's contribution to the core points is smaller than the difference a grade boundary makes in an examined subject. A family in that position is often better advised to cap the essay work, hand the student a presentation checklist, and spend the money where marks are still movable. We will say so when that is the honest answer.

process.title: Tell us the stage, not the subject
process.description: Research question not yet approved, or draft written and criterion C thin, or reflections untouched three weeks out. The stage determines the hours. A request for Extended Essay help without a stage attached cannot be scoped and should not be quoted on.

process.title: Ask your coordinator first, and tell us the answer
process.description: How many supervision hours are scheduled, and how many students the supervisor carries. Where supervision is strong we will recommend a shorter block or none, and that is a cheaper conversation than any session we could sell you.

process.title: Scope the block in hours, with an end point
process.description: We state the number of hours, the stages they cover and the point at which the block closes before anything is booked. If a stage turns out to need less, the block shortens. If it needs more, we say why before adding anything.

process.title: Spend the first hours on the question
process.description: Candidate research questions tested against the 4,000-word ceiling and against the resources actually available, including the school laboratory and the ethics process. The output is a written question the supervisor can approve, which carries criterion A.

process.title: Interrogate the argument, never the prose
process.description: In DP2 autumn the sessions are about claims, evidence, counter-evidence and limitations, because that is criterion C and twelve of the 34 marks. The student drafts every word. We question reasoning and do not comment on a draft about to be submitted.

process.title: Close the block and hand over a checklist
process.description: Presentation is four marks and a student can secure it from a checklist without paying anyone by the hour. When the analytical work is done we end the block, say so in writing, and leave the final tidying with the student and the supervisor.

whyPoints.title: Priced in hours and stages, never per essay
whyPoints.description: A quote names the hourly figure, the session length, the hours proposed and the stages they cover. Anyone quoting a price for an Extended Essay is either guessing or offering to produce it, and the second puts the candidate at risk rather than the seller.

whyPoints.title: Hours follow the marks
whyPoints.description: Criterion C carries twelve of the 34 marks and presentation carries four, so the block is weighted accordingly. Most Extended Essay money in this market is spent the other way round, on the things that are easiest to see and worth least.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you not to buy
whyPoints.description: Where the school's supervision is strong, or where February leaves nothing movable, the honest recommendation is a shorter block or none. A family that hears that once tends to trust the scoping on everything else.

whyPoints.title: AED market bands published with sources
whyPoints.description: The figures on this page carry their survey date and origin, including Bestimate's 2026 rate table. Three of the six most visible pages serving UAE families publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on authorship
whyPoints.description: The student writes every word of the essay and of the reflections. We do not supply text, build outlines to be filled in, review final drafts, or distribute IB exemplars, subject guides or mark schemes.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled to the Abu Dhabi diploma calendar
whyPoints.description: Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time around school bus arrivals from the island and the mainland corridor, with later slots for Al Reef and Mohammed Bin Zayed City, and rescheduling to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan when families ask.

faqs.question: How much should Extended Essay support cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Think in hours, not in totals. A properly scoped block is eight to sixteen hours across the year at the subject-specialist rate, which market figures surveyed in October 2026 put at AED 200 to 450 and above per hour. The wider UAE one-to-one range runs from about AED 45 at the university-student end to AED 650 and above at the premium end, with agency start rates around AED 200 for IB. Those are market figures with sources, not our prices. A quote for an essay rather than for hours should be refused.

faqs.question: Why is Extended Essay help sold as a block rather than a term?
faqs.answer: Because the work is a sequence of decisions, not a weekly skill. Each decision takes an hour or two and then releases weeks of independent writing, so the right shape is bursts with gaps. An open weekly slot booked in DP1 produces thirty sessions, most with nothing specific to do, and a total nobody agreed in advance. The signal to watch for is a session that opens with how is it going rather than with a document on screen.

faqs.question: How many hours of supervision does the school already provide for free?
faqs.answer: A limited and specified amount, already inside your fees, structured around the three reflection sessions and a concluding discussion. The exact allocation and how thinly it is spread vary a great deal between Abu Dhabi schools. Ask the coordinator two things: how many supervision hours are scheduled, and how many students the supervisor is carrying. A supervisor with two students and a free period is a different proposition from one with nine and a full timetable, and the answer should decide whether you buy anything externally.

faqs.question: Where do the 34 Extended Essay marks sit across criteria A to E?
faqs.answer: Criterion A, focus and method, carries six. Criterion B, knowledge and understanding, six. Criterion C, critical thinking, twelve, which is more than a third of the total on its own. Criterion D, presentation, four. Criterion E, engagement, assessed through the reflections, six. The distribution should reshape how a family spends: the hours most readily bought are proofreading and formatting, which sit in the four-mark criterion, while the twelve-mark criterion is under-bought because it is harder to see.

faqs.question: Does the subject my child chooses change what the support costs?
faqs.answer: Substantially, because the subject decides the data problem. An essay built on published sources needs far fewer mentoring hours than one requiring primary experimental work that may have to be redesigned. The expensive pattern is a science question needing equipment the school lacks or ethics approval it will not grant, discovered in week six. Psychology and World Studies are typically the heaviest to mentor; English A, Mathematics and a well-scoped History question are among the lightest.

faqs.question: What is the RPPF and how long are the three reflections?
faqs.answer: The reflections on planning and progress form records the student's three reflections across the project, totalling 500 words, and it feeds criterion E, which carries six marks. The reflections should be written as the work happens, capturing real decisions, setbacks and changes of direction. Students routinely reconstruct all three the week before submission, producing a bland account of a project that actually involved dead ends. Those dead ends are exactly what the criterion rewards, and they cannot be recalled convincingly months later.

faqs.question: What is the viva voce and does it need preparation?
faqs.answer: It is the concluding discussion between the student and the supervisor at the end of the project, and it feeds the supervisor's view of the student's engagement. It is a conversation about what the student did, what they would change and what they learned, not an examination of the subject content. Light preparation helps: knowing the decisions taken and being able to explain why. Scripting it does not, because a rehearsed answer about a research process reads as exactly that.

faqs.question: Is 4,000 words a target or a ceiling?
faqs.answer: A ceiling. Going over it is self-harming, since material beyond the limit is not assessed and the presentation criterion notices. Going well under it is usually worse, because the analysis that criterion C rewards never gets room to develop. The practical approach is to draft long and cut deliberately: a student who writes 4,800 words and cuts to 3,900 generally produces a stronger essay than one who stops at 3,200, provided the cutting removes description rather than argument.

faqs.question: Can a tutor legitimately read an Extended Essay draft?
faqs.answer: A mentor can discuss an in-progress draft's reasoning, ask whether a claim is supported, point out that a paragraph asserts rather than argues, and question how limitations are handled. What a mentor must not do is supply sentences, rewrite a section, provide an outline to be filled in, or comment on a draft about to be submitted as final. The dividing line is who holds the pen. The three reflections and the concluding discussion belong to the student and the school supervisor, not to an external tutor.

faqs.question: What should I do if an agency offers a finished Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Walk away, and treat the offer as information about the provider. Selling completed assessed coursework is an academic-integrity breach that triggers the IB's malpractice procedures, and the consequence falls on your child rather than on the seller, potentially reaching the whole diploma. The same applies to an essay generated by a language model and passed off as the student's work. If a provider also offers you a bank of past Extended Essays to work from, that tells you what kind of operation you are dealing with.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start paying for Extended Essay help?
faqs.answer: By February of DP2 the hours can no longer reach most of the marks. The research question is registered, the reading is done, the method is fixed and the draft's structure already determines criterion C, which is twelve of the 34 marks. What ten hours can still change is presentation, worth four, and some of criterion E if the reflections are unwritten. Availability is also tightest then across this market. In that position, capping the essay work and spending the money on examined subjects is frequently the better call.

faqs.question: Is a World Studies Extended Essay more expensive to support?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. The interdisciplinary route requires a global issue examined through two subjects in a way that genuinely integrates them, rather than alternating between two lenses in successive sections. That integration is the hardest thing in the project to get right and it takes more mentoring hours than a single-subject essay. It also rewards well when it works, because the field of competent World Studies essays is thinner. Decide early, with the coordinator, whether the student has the appetite for it.

faqs.question: Can my child do an Extended Essay in a subject they do not study?
faqs.answer: The school decides what it will supervise, and that is a conversation with the coordinator rather than with a tutor. In practice a student choosing a subject outside their six carries a knowledge and understanding burden that criterion B tests directly, with no classroom teaching behind it. Sometimes it works, where the interest is genuine and long-standing. More often it adds mentoring hours in DP1 that a subject the student already studies would not have needed at all.

faqs.question: Does a primary-research Extended Essay cost more to support in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Noticeably, in two ways. Experimental work has to fit the school laboratory's equipment and safety limits, and research with human participants needs ethics approval the school must grant. An approval refused in week eight is an expensive restart at the same hourly rate. Essays built on published datasets avoid both and frequently score better on criterion C, because the hours go into analysis instead of into logistics. If primary research is the point of the project, settle feasibility in the first two sessions.

faqs.question: What does an Extended Essay mentoring invoice look like in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It names the hourly figure, the session length in minutes, the number of hours proposed, the stages those hours cover, and the point at which the block ends. It should not quote a price for an essay, require a term's payment in advance, or include any charge for a tutor permit, because the MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 is granted free of charge for two years. On tax, ask only whether the quoted figure includes VAT; the wider treatment is a Federal Tax Authority matter.

faqs.question: Should we pay for proofreading of the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and never at a specialist hourly rate. Presentation is four of the 34 marks and consists of things a student can secure from a checklist: a consistent referencing style, a contents page, numbered sections, the word count observed. Paying by the hour for it converts the smallest criterion into the largest invoice line. There is also a boundary question: editing to completion is not proofreading, and a third party rewriting sentences in a submitted essay is a malpractice exposure for the candidate.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.closingHeading: Scope the hours before you buy them
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.closingBody: Ask your child's coordinator how many supervision hours are scheduled and how many students the supervisor carries. Then decide what, if anything, to buy on top, and buy it in stages: two or three hours on the research question in DP1, three to five on the argument in DP2 autumn, one or two on the reflections, one at the end on checks. That block sits well below a year of weekly tutoring at any of the market rates on this page, and it puts the hours where twelve of the 34 marks actually live. Tell us the stage the project is at and we will match an IB DP Extended Essay tutor in Abu Dhabi to it, with a stated hour count and an end point.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-film-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work on Diploma Film at Standard and Higher Level for students in Abu Dhabi schools: the textual analysis, the comparative study, the film portfolio and its reel, and the Higher Level collaborative project. Camera operation stays practical and school-based. Sessions run live online, timed to Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Film is marked on evidence, and most of the evidence is written
paragraphs: Diploma Film looks like the one Diploma subject where a student is assessed on something they make. That is half true, and the half that is false is where almost every mark is lost. The examiner sees a recorded oral, a recorded multimedia study, a set of portfolio pages, a short reel, and at Higher Level a project report. The examiner does not see the rehearsals, the reshoots, the group arguments, the equipment failures, or the fact that the lead actor withdrew two days before the shoot. If a decision is not evidenced in the submitted material, it did not happen as far as the grade is concerned.

That single fact reorders what outside help is worth buying. A student who can operate a camera and cut a sequence is not thereby a student who scores well, because the camera work is assessed through the argument the student makes about it. The textual analysis is an argument about a four- to five-minute extract from a prescribed film. The comparative study is a research argument about two films from different cultural contexts, supported by a list of sources. The film portfolio is an argument about the student's own practice in three distinct film roles. Argument, sourcing and documentation are the grade.

Abu Dhabi adds its own pressures. Diploma Film is not offered in every school in the emirate, and where it is, the cohort is often small enough that a student has no classmate ahead of them to copy a workflow from. ADEK licenses and inspects the private schools here and publishes its own inspection ratings, and enrolment is spread between the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and the newer mainland communities. A student in Al Shamkha with a school that runs Film thinly has the same deadline as a student on Saadiyat with a staffed media department and a kit cupboard.

There is also a practical constraint peculiar to this subject in this city. Filming needs locations, and locations in Abu Dhabi are mostly owned, managed and gated: malls, corniche promenades, residential compounds, school grounds. A student planning a shoot on the assumption that they can simply turn up and record is planning a problem. Scoping a project around what can actually be filmed, with permission, in the weeks available is a sizeable share of what a Film session is for, and it is the work that prevents a reel from being abandoned halfway through.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Diploma Film support here is one-to-one over live video, which for this subject is the better format rather than the compromise. A tutor needs to see the timeline, scrub through a cut, pause on a frame and read a portfolio page beside it. That is screen work. The published market band for IB specialist tutoring runs at AED 200-450 an hour, and removing the drive across the emirate means the hour is spent on the edit rather than on the ring road.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-film-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Film arrives in the Diploma from several directions, and the route a student took predicts their first problem. The three programmes below are the feeders that matter in Abu Dhabi schools, with what each one leaves a student ready and unready for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Arts and Design
programmes.description: MYP arts and design units assess knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding, with a process journal running alongside the practical work. Students who have kept that journal honestly arrive in Diploma Film with the one habit the portfolio needs: recording a decision while it is being taken rather than reconstructing it later. Students who treated the journal as a tidy-up exercise arrive without it.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a smaller MYP cohort than British-curriculum cohort, so in most schools here only a minority of Diploma Film students come through MYP. Where they do, the first paid block is usually short, because the documentation habit transfers and only the Film-specific vocabulary has to be added.

programmes.name: IGCSE Media Studies and Drama routes
programmes.description: Media and drama courses at IGCSE build useful technical fluency: shot types, editing software, basic sound. What they do not build is the comparative research habit the Diploma expects, because an IGCSE media task is usually a production brief with given parameters rather than a question the student has to frame and then answer from sources.
programmes.countryNote: Because the British-curriculum cohort in this emirate is large, most Diploma Film students in Abu Dhabi arrive by this route. Their first paid block is almost always the comparative study, where framing a researchable question about two films from different cultural contexts is the gap.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Film
programmes.description: Diploma Film is taken at Standard or Higher Level. Both levels submit a recorded textual analysis of an extract from a prescribed film, a recorded multimedia comparative study of two films from different cultural contexts with a list of sources, and a film portfolio documenting work in three film roles with a completed reel. Higher Level adds a collaborative project: a short film made as a group, with each student submitting an individual project report.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi school offering the Diploma runs Film, and those that do often run it with a single class and one specialist teacher. A cohort of four or five is normal. That means no precedent, no older student's portfolio to look at, and no departmental habit about when the reel should be locked.

programmes.name: Extended Essay in Film
programmes.description: A 4,000-word research essay on a film question, supervised in school and marked externally. The recurring failure is a question that invites description of a favourite director rather than an argument that evidence can settle. Support here is process coaching and feedback on drafts the student has produced, never supplied text.
programmes.countryNote: Film is a popular Extended Essay choice among Abu Dhabi students who do not take the subject, which creates a specific problem: an essay in a discipline whose analytical vocabulary the student has never been taught. Those students need the vocabulary first and the question second.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-film-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Film is rarely the only request in a household. The subjects below are the ones that most often sit alongside it in an Abu Dhabi Diploma, with what each assesses and the point at which a Film student usually needs help with it.

subjects.name: Film
subjects.description: Textual analysis, comparative study and film portfolio at both levels, plus the collaborative project at Higher Level. Marks leak to unsourced claims, analysis that describes a scene instead of arguing about it, portfolio pages that assert a role rather than evidence it, and submissions that overrun their stated limit.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 analyses unseen non-literary texts, Paper 2 compares literary works, plus an individual oral. The overlap with Film is direct: both reward a student who can move from a specific textual detail to a claim about effect, in a sentence that does both jobs at once.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Comparative study, process portfolio and exhibition, all submitted. Students taking Film and Visual Arts together carry two documentation-heavy courses whose internal deadlines usually fall in the same weeks, so sequencing the submissions matters more than extra teaching in either.

subjects.name: Theatre
subjects.description: Director's notebook, research presentation, collaborative project and, at Higher Level, a solo piece. The shared skill with Film is writing about an artistic decision against a tradition or a theorist, which is the move both courses mark and neither teaches quickly.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: Papers plus an inquiry project on a real-world digital challenge. Film students often pick it as a pairing and then find the inquiry project competing for the same documentation energy as the portfolio. The fix is calendar work, not subject teaching.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in UAE private schools alongside the licensed international curriculum, with placement driven by a student's background. For a Film student it is typically the subject occupying the evening slots either side of a shoot weekend.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Papers plus a historical investigation with a source-evaluation section. That section is the nearest relative in the Diploma to the comparative study's sourcing requirement, and a student who does one properly usually finds the other easier.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with commentaries and a prescribed-title essay. Film students tend to write TOK essays about representation and reach for opinion. The repair is structural: a claim, a counterclaim and a real example in every paragraph.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Two papers with technology permitted, plus an exploration. Arts-heavy Diploma students most often take this route and most often need help with the statistics content and with keeping the exploration their own work.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-film-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Film is the Diploma subject where geography changes the work itself rather than just the commute. The notes below cover what each part of Abu Dhabi offers a student who has to shoot something, and what it costs them in access.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: The cultural district and open public frontage make this the easiest part of the emirate for a student to find a usable location, although the institutions here are managed sites and permission is a conversation, not an assumption. Schools in the cluster tend to have media kit and a staffed department.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Tower living, which rules out most of the obvious interiors and makes building management the gatekeeper for anything shot in a lobby, corridor or podium. Students here usually film on school grounds or inside their own apartment, so lighting becomes the first technical problem.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa compounds with gated access and quiet streets. Outdoor shooting is practical here in a way it is not on the island, provided neighbours and compound management are asked first. The trade-off is a long evening drive to any school media facility outside the community.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Managed waterfront and residential districts with several schools inside the corridor. The locations look excellent on camera and are almost all owned by someone, which makes this the area where students most often need to plan a permission request two weeks ahead.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Older island neighbourhoods with varied streetscapes and a genuinely different visual texture from the newer districts, which is useful for a student looking for something other than glass towers. Several long-established schools sit nearby.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: Newer campuses and large managed attractions. Almost nothing here can be filmed without asking, so students from this cluster tend to build projects around interiors and controlled spaces, and they benefit most from early scope-testing.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Central, residential and close to most of the island's schools. Access is easier than on the newer islands and the constraint is usually time rather than permission, with mandatory and optional subjects already filling most evenings.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Mainland communities where the local specialist pool is thinnest on arts subjects. Students here are the most likely in the emirate to be the only Film candidate in their year, and the ones for whom an online specialist replaces a conversation that is not otherwise available.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Saadiyat schools
schoolClusters.note: The longest-established international schools in the emirate. Those running Film generally have camera and editing provision and a teacher who has taken a cohort through all four tasks before, so requests from this cluster are usually about one task rather than the whole course.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas
schoolClusters.note: Newer campuses with large year groups and long evening commutes. Film runs in some and not others across this corridor, and students whose own school does not offer it sometimes take it elsewhere or carry it as an Extended Essay subject instead.
schools: The International School of Choueifat Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Mainland and Mussafah
schoolClusters.note: Schools serving the inland communities across a wide spread of curricula. Media and arts specialists are the hardest staffing category to fill in this cluster, which is why Film requests from these postcodes more often cover the whole course rather than a single task.

sections.heading: The four assessed tasks, and the evidence each one actually demands
paragraphs: A Diploma Film grade is built from submitted artefacts, and each artefact has a form, a limit and a thing it is really testing. Students and parents tend to picture the subject as a filmmaking course with some writing attached. The assessment reads the other way round: it is an analysis and documentation course in which films get made, and the films exist mainly as material the student then has to argue about.

The textual analysis is a recorded oral built on a short extract from a film on the prescribed list, and it is marked on the quality of the argument about film language rather than on delivery. The comparative study is a recorded multimedia piece comparing two films from different cultural contexts, submitted with a list of sources which is itself assessed. The film portfolio documents the student's own practice in three distinct film roles and arrives with a completed reel. At Higher Level, the collaborative film project adds a group film and an individual report.

The table below sets out the shape of each task. Treat the weightings and limits as a structure for a conversation with your child's teacher rather than as the authority: the IB revises components, and no figure in this project has been confirmed against ibo.org, which returns an error to automated requests. The column worth reading twice is the last one, because it names the thing that most often costs marks even when the film itself is good.

sections.heading: Reading a four-minute extract: what the textual analysis is really testing
paragraphs: The textual analysis defeats more Abu Dhabi Film students than any other task, and almost never for the reason they expect. Students arrive able to name shot types and film language confidently. What the task asks for is a sustained argument about how a specific sequence produces a specific effect, supported by evidence from the sequence itself, inside a tight running time. Naming techniques is the easy part and earns very little on its own.

The pattern in weak recordings is consistent. The student moves through the extract in chronological order, describing each shot, attaching a correct label to it, and asserting a mood. There is no claim being tested, so there is nothing for the evidence to support. A strong recording inverts that: it opens with a claim about what the sequence is doing, then returns to three or four moments that earn the claim, which means the student has to leave most of the extract unmentioned and say so.

A session on this task is mechanical in the best sense. The tutor and student scrub the extract on a shared screen, timecode the handful of moments that matter, and build the argument from those moments outward. Then they cut. Almost every first attempt runs long, and the thing students instinctively cut is the analysis rather than the description, which makes the recording worse while making it shorter. Learning to cut the right half is a skill that takes one or two sessions and then holds for the rest of the course.
bullets: The argument comes first; the extract is evidence, not a running order
Three or four timecoded moments beat a walk through every shot
Overrun is normally fixed by cutting description, never analysis

sections.heading: The comparative study is a research task wearing a film costume
paragraphs: The comparative study asks a student to frame a question about film, answer it by comparing two films from different cultural contexts, and submit the sources they used. The last part is the part students treat as administrative and examiners treat as evidence. A study with a thin source list is a study that has asserted rather than researched, whatever the voiceover says.

Question framing is where the hours go. A workable question has a narrow focus, a reason the two chosen films can answer it, and an answer that could have come out differently. An unworkable question is a theme stretched across two films a student happens to like. The table below sorts real question shapes into the two categories, because reading the difference is faster than being told it. Students in this emirate often reach for a Gulf or Arab film as one of the pair, which is a genuinely strong instinct provided the film is reachable and something has been written about it that the student can cite.

Sourcing is the other half, and it is where Abu Dhabi students have a specific practical problem: access. Academic film writing sits behind paywalls, school library provision for film criticism is usually thin, and a student working from video essays alone ends up citing material they cannot evaluate. Part of a session is spent finding citable writing the student can actually reach, and part is spent teaching them to distinguish a source that supports an argument from one that simply agrees with it.

sections.heading: The film portfolio: three roles, and the paper trail behind each
paragraphs: The portfolio is the task where good students lose the most marks, because the work it assesses is work they did months earlier and documented badly or not at all. A student has to evidence their own practice in three distinct film roles, and the word doing the damage is evidence. A page saying the student was the cinematographer and found the lighting challenging is an assertion. A page showing a lighting plan, the problem it was built to solve, the two set-ups tried, and why the second was kept is evidence.

Role choice matters more than students realise. Picking three roles that all happen in the edit suite is comfortable and thin. Picking roles that genuinely sit at different points of the pipeline, one in planning, one on set and one in post, produces a portfolio with three different kinds of evidence in it and reads as a student who has understood what the task is for. Those decisions are cheap to make early and expensive to repair once the shoot has happened.

The reel is the easier half, and it carries one standing trap: length. Students cut the reel to fit the limit at the last minute by trimming whichever sequence is longest, rather than the one that demonstrates least. The table below sets out, role by role, what evidence actually counts and what students most often hand in instead. A portfolio session is usually spent turning reconstruction back into documentation, which is only possible while the production is still running.
