sections.heading: Academic honesty when a parent at home speaks German
paragraphs: German B raises an honesty question that does not arise in most subjects, because a meaningful share of these candidates have a parent or grandparent who speaks German fluently. A family member who corrects a draft is acting generously and may also be producing a script the candidate could not have written, which under IB academic honesty rules is a problem for the candidate rather than for the relative.

The boundary is the same for a relative as for a paid tutor. Explaining a rule, pointing out that a paragraph contains an error without rewriting it, testing whether a correction has been learned, and discussing ideas for content are all legitimate. Supplying sentences, rewriting a paragraph into better German, or translating an English draft are not. The test is whether the student could reproduce the language unaided afterwards.

Machine translation sits on the wrong side of that line and is worth naming directly, because it is the live issue in language courses. Output from a translation tool in a Paper 1 response is visible to an experienced examiner precisely because it is better than the rest of the script, and the mismatch invites scrutiny of the whole piece. Where translation tools are genuinely useful is as material: comparing the tool's version with the student's own and explaining the differences is a strong session.

What a tutor working with us will do is mark the student's own work against criterion letters and explain the logic of the mark scheme. What a tutor will not do is produce the work, in any subject, at any level of urgency. That refusal is published here because a page that implies otherwise is selling the student a risk, not a service.

sections.heading: A German B session, minute by minute, and what it can repair
paragraphs: A session that improves a German B grade is more boring than families expect and leaves more behind. The first ten minutes are a cold test of the previous session's target — not a review, a test, with a score written down. If the score is poor, the session changes plan immediately, because teaching something new on top of something unlearned is the most common way paid hours are wasted.

The middle thirty minutes take one thing. A single error class with its triggers and a drill of six to ten instances, or one text type with its conventions and a short timed piece, or one literary extract placed and discussed. Two topics in an hour feels productive and retains worse than one, particularly at the end of a long Abu Dhabi school day with a bus commute in it.

The last fifteen minutes produce the artefacts. The student writes the summary rather than receiving it: the rule in their own words, three example sentences, the task set for the week. Then the session note goes to the shared folder with the cold-test score, what was taught, and what will be tested next time. A parent who cannot read German can still read that sequence and see whether anything is moving.

What this cannot repair is worth saying. One session does not move a grade. One session can fix a named class of error, establish a text type, or rescue an oral strategy. Three to six, aimed at the two or three classes a marked script actually shows, is what moves a 4 to a 5 or a 5 to a 6. Anyone promising more than that from an hour is selling optimism, and the IB does not mark optimism.

process.description: The output is a written list of error classes ranked by how many marks they are costing, the text types not yet mastered, and the recommended order of work. If two blocks of three sessions would do it, that is the recommendation rather than a year of weekly hours.

process.description: At the end of a block the target is tested cold and the result is compared with the baseline. Continuing, changing target or stopping is decided on that number. A tutor who cannot show the number is asking you to re-book on a feeling.

whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, model, mark and test. They do not write, rewrite or translate work that will be submitted, and they decline when asked, including when a deadline is close. Under IB rules the consequence of the alternative lands on the student.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability
whyPoints.description: German B at Higher Level is a narrow specialism and availability is finite. If nobody suitable is free at your hour we say so, rather than seating a general German speaker in front of an HL candidate and letting the gap appear in a mock.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between German B at Standard and Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Both levels sit the same four assessment types, but Higher Level adds the study of two literary works, requires a longer written response in Paper 1, and builds the individual oral on an extract from one of those works instead of a visual stimulus. The reading and listening texts are also more demanding. Confirm word ranges and timings with your DP coordinator against the current Language B guide. The practical question for a family is not difficulty but fit: HL rewards a student who can discuss ideas in German, not simply one with good grammar.

faqs.question: Why does my son write accurate German and still lose marks in Paper 1?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the response is in the wrong form. Paper 1 names a text type, and register, audience, layout and the conventions of that form are assessed alongside the language. A beautifully written essay submitted where an interview or a report was asked for loses marks that extra vocabulary cannot recover. Ask to see a marked script with the text-type marks separated from the language marks. If nobody has ever separated them, that is the gap, and six sessions of text-type work usually closes it.

faqs.question: How long does it take to fix case and adjective ending errors?
faqs.answer: A named class of error typically takes a block of three to six sessions to drill, plus a cold retest two or three weeks later to show whether it held. Case errors come in classes rather than individually: prepositions that always take the dative, two-way prepositions, verbs with a dative object, then adjective endings on top. Fixing scripts sentence by sentence does not work because the student learns the sentence rather than the rule. Expect the error log to show falling instance counts per hundred words rather than a dramatic jump.

faqs.question: My daughter understands German films but scores badly in the listening paper. Why?
faqs.answer: Films give context, repetition and visual support, and the listening paper gives none of those. Marks go missing in three predictable places: two-digit numbers, which German speaks units-first; negation, where one short word flips an answer; and the later passages, where attention has degraded. All three are trainable. Short weekly number dictation, cold passages where every answer depends on negation, and full-length practice rather than single passages. Take a raw score first and date it, so the comparison after a month is like for like.

faqs.question: Which two literary works will my child study for Higher Level German B?
faqs.answer: The school chooses them, within the IB's requirements, so the answer comes from your child's teacher or DP coordinator rather than from a tutor. Ask in DP1 rather than DP2, and ask whether the choice is settled, because a late substitution leaves a candidate preparing one work well and meeting the second shortly before the oral. Once you know the titles, HL oral preparation can use unseen extracts from them under timed conditions, which is the only rehearsal that resembles the real task.

faqs.question: Is German B worth taking if my child has only had two periods a week since Year 7?
faqs.answer: Usually yes at Standard Level, and the MYP phase descriptor is the document that settles it. Two periods a week for several years produces students who speak with confidence and write loosely, which is a cheap profile to improve because the lost marks are concentrated in written accuracy and text type. Higher Level is a different question, since it adds two literary works and extended discussion. Bring a cold timed writing sample to the placement conversation; a dated script carries more weight than anyone's estimate.

faqs.question: Can a German-speaking parent help with Paper 1 practice at home?
faqs.answer: With real care. Explaining a rule, saying that a paragraph contains an error without rewriting it, testing whether a correction has stuck and discussing content ideas are all fine and genuinely useful. Rewriting the German, supplying sentences or translating an English draft are not, because the submitted work must be the student's own under IB academic honesty rules and the consequence falls on the candidate. The honest test is whether your child could produce the same language again unaided a week later.

faqs.question: Does using a translation tool for German homework cause a problem?
faqs.answer: For assessed work, yes. Translation output sits above the rest of a candidate's script and the mismatch is visible to an experienced examiner, which invites scrutiny of the whole piece. For practice, the tools are genuinely useful in one specific way: comparing what the tool produced with what the student wrote, and explaining each difference, teaches more grammar in twenty minutes than a worksheet does. The rule we work to is that nothing goes into submitted work that the student could not have written and cannot defend.

faqs.question: How many German B sessions does an Abu Dhabi student usually need to move a grade?
faqs.answer: Grades generally move on two or three error-class blocks of three to six sessions each, not on open-ended weekly tuition. The number depends on what a marked script shows: a candidate losing marks on text type and on dative prepositions needs roughly two blocks and a timed paper, while one whose issue is listening stamina needs a different and cheaper intervention. Be suspicious of any plan written before a marked script has been read, and of any promise about a specific grade, which nobody can honestly make.

faqs.question: Our family relocates mid-DP. Can German B support continue across countries?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where online delivery earns its place. Sessions run over live video and follow the family rather than the address, so a posting to another country, a long summer away or a term of travel does not interrupt the error log. Times are rebased to the new local time zone and the shared folder stays intact, which matters because German accuracy decays quickly during gaps. Tell us the new time zone a week ahead and the slot is moved rather than paused.

faqs.question: Does ADEK regulate what a private German tutor in Abu Dhabi may charge?
faqs.answer: No. ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; it does not set private tutoring rates. Separately, individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years. Ask any tutor whether they hold it. Market rates are set by the market, and published comparisons put qualified online tutors in this emirate at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a German tutor to a villa in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE, and no tutor is sent to a villa, apartment or compound here; in-home tutoring is offered only in India. German B lessons for Abu Dhabi families are one-to-one online, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. For a narrow specialism this is the stronger arrangement: the tutor is chosen from everyone qualified who is free at your hour, rather than from the few who could drive to Khalifa City by 16:30.

faqs.question: Can German sessions move during Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes. School days shorten, afternoons are harder, and speaking practice at 16:00 while fasting produces less than the same work after Iftar. Sessions move to post-Iftar slots for the month, and the content moves with them: reading-paper technique and written accuracy in any shorter afternoon slot, oral rehearsal later in the evening. What is worth avoiding is a complete month off, because the error classes that were falling tend to reappear and the first two sessions afterwards go on recovery.

faqs.question: What should a German B tutor send us after each session?
faqs.answer: A short note with four things in it: the cold-test score on the previous target, what was taught, the task set, and what will be tested next time. Plus any marked work with criterion letters written on it and the error class named. A parent who reads no German can still audit that sequence, because the question is whether the cold-test scores are rising. If the only output is a cheerful message that the session went well, there is nothing to audit.

faqs.question: Is it realistic to start German B tutoring eight weeks before the May papers?
faqs.answer: Realistic, but the plan has to change. Eight weeks is not long enough to clear several error classes, so the work becomes triage: one timed Paper 1 and one full listening paper marked in the first week, the two highest-cost error classes named, and the remaining sessions split between those and text-type conventions, which pay back fastest. New grammar is not introduced at this stage. Expect honest framing rather than a promise, because nobody can commit to a grade in eight weeks or in eighty.

intro.heading: German B is a systems problem, and systems can be taught
paragraphs: German rewards a particular kind of student and punishes a particular kind of teaching. It rewards anyone willing to learn a handful of systems properly, because once the systems hold they generate correct output indefinitely. It punishes the approach most students default to, which is treating each new ending as a fact to memorise. A child who has filled three exercise books with correct answers and still cannot write a paragraph has usually been taught German as a list rather than as a structure.

There are four of these systems and they interlock. The case system, which decides the form of articles, pronouns and adjectives according to the grammatical job a noun is doing. Adjective endings, which depend on the case, the gender, the number and crucially on what kind of word came before the adjective. Word order, where the main verb sits second in a statement and goes to the end in a subordinate clause, creating the bracket that German sentences are built around. And separable verbs, whose prefixes detach and travel to the end of the clause.

The useful consequence for tutoring is that German B marks move in steps rather than smoothly. A student who finally understands that the preceding word selects the adjective-ending pattern does not improve by two per cent; they stop making an entire class of error. That is why marked work in this subject should be annotated by error type as well as by criterion, and why three tasks are usually enough to see which system is missing rather than which words are.

Assessment is the same shape as the other language B courses, which is worth stating so nobody is surprised. Paper 1 is written production and carries a quarter of the grade. Paper 2 combines listening and reading and carries half. The individual oral carries the remaining quarter, is conducted and marked inside your child's school, and is moderated by the IB. Higher Level adds two literary works written in German and replaces the visual-stimulus oral with one built on an extract from one of them. Families moving into the emirate mid-Diploma should check which level their new school actually runs, because German B at Higher Level is not offered everywhere and a mid-course level change is awkward to arrange.

Lessons are delivered one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared document so the writing is watched as it happens. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. German B is a small specialism in this emirate and the honest position is that geography should not decide access to it: a family in Al Reem should be able to work with someone who has taught the HL extract oral, rather than with whoever happens to speak German nearby.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-german-b-tutor.subjectsIntro: In German the useful breakdown is by grammatical system rather than by topic, because that is where the marks are won and lost. Each entry below is a structure, with what it governs and how long it takes to secure.

subjects.name: The four cases
subjects.description: Nominative, accusative, dative and genitive, selected by the job a noun does and by the preposition or verb governing it. The foundation of everything else, and the structure most often half-known. Secure in roughly a term of deliberate work.

subjects.name: Adjective endings
subjects.description: Three patterns chosen by what precedes the adjective: a definite article, an indefinite one, or nothing at all. Students taught these as three unrelated tables rarely use any of them correctly under time. Taught as one decision, they become quick.

subjects.name: Word order and the verbal bracket
subjects.description: The conjugated verb sits second in a statement; other verb parts go to the end, creating a bracket around the clause. In a subordinate clause the whole verb moves to the end. This is what makes German sound German and what students abandon under pressure.

subjects.name: Separable and inseparable verbs
subjects.description: Prefixes that detach and travel to the end of the clause, against those that never move. The error is rarely about meaning and almost always about position, which makes it quick to fix once a student notices the pattern.

subjects.name: The perfect tense with haben and sein
subjects.description: Choosing the right auxiliary and placing the past participle correctly at the end. The most common narrative structure in the written paper, and the one where word order and verb formation fail together.

subjects.name: Modal verbs
subjects.description: High-frequency, irregular in the present, and they push the infinitive to the end of the clause. Excellent value in a session because they appear constantly and they teach the bracket structure at the same time.

subjects.name: Gender and plural formation
subjects.description: Gender has to be learned with the noun rather than deduced, and plural formation follows several patterns. Not glamorous and quietly expensive: a wrong gender propagates into the article and then into the adjective ending.

subjects.name: Subordinate clauses and the passive
subjects.description: Range that lifts a written task out of the simple register, provided the verb-final rule holds. Worth attempting only once word order is stable, because a collapsed complex sentence scores lower than a correct simple one.

subjects.name: Konjunktiv II for politeness and hypotheticals
subjects.description: A small set of forms that make a candidate sound markedly more competent in both the oral and the written task. Cheap to learn, disproportionately visible, and routinely left out of a crowded syllabus.

sections.heading: What makes German B different from the other language B courses
paragraphs: Every language B course assesses the same three components and uses the same criteria, so on paper German, French and Spanish B are the same subject in different words. In a tutoring room they are not. French B difficulty is weighted towards listening and towards text-type conventions. Spanish B difficulty is weighted towards the verb system and the subjunctive. German B difficulty is weighted towards morphology and word order, and that concentration changes what a session should contain.

The practical effect is visible in marked work. A French B student's written task tends to be fluent with the wrong register or the wrong task response. A German B student's task tends to answer the question well and bleed marks through endings - a wrong case after a preposition, an adjective ending drawn from the wrong pattern, a participle left in the middle of the clause. The message is intact and the language criterion absorbs the damage steadily.

That is good news, because morphological error is systematic. It repeats, which means it can be counted, and it comes from a missing rule rather than from missing vocabulary. A student who stops making one whole class of ending error has not improved incrementally; they have closed a leak. This is why German B rewards annotating marked work by error type as well as by criterion letter, and why three tasks are usually enough to identify which system is absent rather than guessing at it.

sections.heading: The case system: where German B marks actually go
paragraphs: German has four cases and they are not a decorative feature of the grammar; they are how the language marks who is doing what to whom. The case is selected by the job the noun does in the clause, by the preposition in front of it, or by the verb governing it. Articles, pronouns and adjective endings all change accordingly, so a single wrong case decision propagates into three visible errors in one phrase.

Most students arrive half-knowing this. They have the nominative and accusative reasonably secure, have met the dative as a list of prepositions to memorise, and treat the genitive as optional. The predictable results are a dative preposition followed by an accusative article, a two-way preposition used without thinking about whether movement or position is meant, and a verb that takes the dative being given a direct object instead.

Teaching this well means teaching the triggers rather than the tables. A student who can ask one question - what is selecting this case here - reaches the right answer far more reliably than one reciting a chart. The two-way prepositions get their own treatment, because the movement-or-position decision is the single most common case error in Abu Dhabi marked work we see, and it is also the fastest to fix once a student knows the question to ask. The genitive deserves one deliberate block of its own as well. Students avoid it, avoidance caps the language mark, and a handful of set phrases bring it back into use within a fortnight.

sections.heading: Word order: the bracket, and the verb that goes last
paragraphs: German word order is rule-governed and unforgiving. In a statement the conjugated verb sits second, whatever comes first. Any other verb parts - an infinitive after a modal, a past participle in the perfect tense, a separable prefix - go to the end of the clause, forming a bracket that encloses everything in between. In a subordinate clause the whole verb assembly moves to the end. Once a student sees these as one pattern rather than three rules, their writing changes quickly.

What breaks under pressure is the bracket. A student writing at speed produces an English word order with German words, which is intelligible and scores poorly, because range and accuracy are both judged. The repair is to practise the bracket deliberately in short sentences until it is the default, then extend. Attempting complex subordinate structures before the bracket is automatic produces collapsed sentences that score below correct simple ones.

Separable verbs are the same problem wearing a different hat. The prefix detaches and travels to the end, and students who know this perfectly well in an exercise forget it the moment they are concentrating on content. The fix is volume at low complexity: many short sentences with separable verbs, written fast, until the prefix lands at the end without thought. Ten minutes of that beats an hour of explanation, which is true of most of German. It also transfers directly to the oral, where word order is the first casualty of nerves and the easiest thing for an examiner to hear.

sections.heading: Adjective endings, taught as one decision rather than three tables
paragraphs: Adjective endings are where German B students lose confidence, and almost always because of how they were taught. Presented as three separate tables - after a definite article, after an indefinite article, after nothing - they look like a hundred and twenty facts. Presented as one decision, they are a question with three branches: what kind of word came before this adjective, and has it already shown the case and gender clearly?

That single reframing does most of the work. If the preceding word has already marked case and gender unambiguously, the adjective takes the minimal ending. If it has not, the adjective carries the heavier ending that does the marking instead. The pattern after an indefinite article sits between the two precisely because the indefinite article is ambiguous in some slots and not others. Students who hold that logic stop guessing.

Practice then has to be in free writing rather than in tables, because the test is whether the decision is made while attention is elsewhere. We mark these errors by type, count them across three tasks, and show the student the count rather than describing the problem. A student who sees that eleven of fourteen language annotations in a task were adjective endings understands the priority immediately, and that is a more efficient conversation than any amount of encouragement. It also tells a parent where the next six weeks should go, in one line, without anybody needing to read German.

sections.heading: The three components, and the German difficulty each exposes
paragraphs: Paper 1 is written production and carries a quarter of the grade, 250 to 400 words at Standard Level and 450 to 600 at Higher Level. It is where morphology is most exposed, because sustained writing gives the case system and the adjective endings many chances to fail. Paper 2 holds listening and reading and carries half the grade, and in German the specific listening difficulty is the bracket: the word that completes the meaning often arrives at the end of a long clause.

The individual oral carries the final quarter, is conducted and marked inside your child's school, and is moderated by the IB. At Standard Level it runs from a visual stimulus linked to a prescribed theme; at Higher Level from an extract of one of the two literary works studied. For a German B candidate in a cohort of three or four, the scarce resource is unscripted conversation with someone who is not their teacher, and that shortage shows up directly in the interaction marks.

Current timings, task counts and criterion wording are set out in the IB subject guide held by your child's school. We work from it and do not reproduce or supply IB documents, past papers or mark schemes - those are the school's to provide and the IB's to publish. Ask the DP coordinator for the component breakdown and the internal oral deadline in writing at the start of DP1; both take one email and both change how the two years are planned.

sections.heading: Online or an in-home tutor in Abu Dhabi: the honest comparison
paragraphs: Parents searching for a German tutor in this emirate usually start by looking for someone local, and it is worth being straightforward about what that gets you and what it costs. The in-home market is real, it is priced higher because travel is priced in, and its availability is limited by who lives within a reasonable drive of your address. For a widely taught subject that is a mild constraint. For German B in Abu Dhabi, where candidates number in the handfuls, it is a severe one.

IB Gram does not provide in-person tutoring in Abu Dhabi, and we would rather say so on this page than after a booking. Lessons here are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared document so written work is watched as it is produced. That is not a compromise dressed up as a feature: for a grammar-led subject, the screen is where the marked task, the annotation and the error count actually live, and nothing has to survive a school bag.

The table below compares the options on the things that differ, with rates as published by the sources named rather than as our own price list. Two points deserve emphasis. Travel time in Abu Dhabi is not symmetrical - an island address and a mainland address face very different constraints - and a tutor's willingness to travel narrows the pool of subject specialists far more than it narrows the pool of general language teachers.

sections.heading: Is your tutor permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is a permitted activity with a specific route, not an unregulated one, and this is a fair question for any parent to ask. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. According to the federal government's own service information, the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

MoHRE's service page for the permit is listed as the issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, states no fees, gives a two-working-day completion time, and directs applicants to the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. That is the official route, and it is the one to check against rather than any tutoring company's description of itself. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears here.

There is a further point specific to Abu Dhabi. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct to similar effect. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document. The practical upshot for a parent is simple: your child's own subject teacher is not the right person to engage privately.

sections.heading: What six weeks of German fixes, and what needs a year
paragraphs: German rewards honesty about timescales because its systems do not negotiate. In six weeks of one hour a week with written homework, a student can make the verbal bracket automatic in short sentences, learn the adjective-ending decision as a single question, stop the most common two-way preposition error, and acquire Konjunktiv II for politeness - which is a disproportionate gain in both the oral and the written task for very little effort.

What needs a year is the full case system working unprompted in extended writing, the genitive moving from avoided to used, reading speed through subordinate clauses and compound nouns, and the range of structures that lifts a written task above the simple register. Those improve in steps rather than smoothly, with visible plateaus between them, and no tutor can promise a particular grade in this subject or any other. No outcome statistics appear anywhere on this site, because we could not show you the data behind them.

If your child is in DP2 with limited time, the order inverts and narrows. Count the error types in a recent marked task, fix the two most frequent, make the bracket automatic, and put the remaining hours into the oral block because it carries a quarter of the grade against a fixed internal school deadline. That is a smaller claim than a transformation and it is the one we would rather be judged on. Tell us the internal deadline in the first message and the hours get allocated against it rather than against a syllabus list.

faqs.question: Does my child need the German cases secure before starting German B?
faqs.answer: Not secure, but not absent either. German B assumes previous experience, and most students arrive with the nominative and accusative reasonably reliable, the dative half-learned as a list of prepositions, and the genitive avoided. That is a workable starting point. What matters is that the case system is taught by its triggers rather than by charts during DP1, because a wrong case decision propagates into the article and then into the adjective ending, costing three visible marks in one phrase.

faqs.question: Why does my child keep getting adjective endings wrong when they know the tables?
faqs.answer: Because tables are recalled deliberately and endings have to be produced while attention is on content. Presented as three separate tables the endings look like well over a hundred facts; presented as one decision they are a single question - what has the preceding word already marked, case and gender clearly or not? Students who hold that logic stop guessing. The practice then has to be in free writing rather than in gap-fill exercises, since an exercise prompts the very thing being tested.

faqs.question: What is the verbal bracket, and why does it matter so much in German?
faqs.answer: In a German statement the conjugated verb sits second, whatever comes first, and any other verb parts - an infinitive after a modal, a past participle, a separable prefix - travel to the end of the clause. Together they form a bracket enclosing everything between. In a subordinate clause the whole verb assembly goes to the end. It matters because it is the first thing to collapse under time pressure, producing English word order with German words, which is intelligible and scores poorly.

faqs.question: How is IB German B assessed at Standard and Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Three components. Paper 1 is written production, a quarter of the grade, 250 to 400 words at Standard Level and 450 to 600 at Higher. Paper 2 holds listening and reading and carries half. The individual oral carries the final quarter, is conducted and marked inside the school and then moderated by the IB. Higher Level adds two literary works written in German and replaces the visual-stimulus oral with one built on an extract from one of them. There is no coursework essay.

faqs.question: Which German varieties will my child hear in the listening paper?
faqs.answer: Material is drawn from the German-speaking world, so Austrian and Swiss voices appear alongside standard German, and regional colouring is normal in authentic recordings. The bigger German-specific listening difficulty is structural rather than accentual: the word that completes the meaning often arrives at the end of a long clause, so a student decoding left to right has committed to an interpretation before the verb lands. Training a student to hold the clause is worth more than accent drills.

faqs.question: Is German B harder than French or Spanish B?
faqs.answer: It is differently hard. All three use the same assessment shape and the same criteria, so the difference is where the difficulty concentrates. German loads it onto morphology and word order, which are systematic and therefore teachable in blocks. Spanish loads it onto the verb system and the subjunctive. French loads it onto listening and onto register and text-type conventions. German suits a student willing to learn structures properly and frustrates one who prefers to absorb a language by exposure.

faqs.question: My child was at a German-curriculum school. Should they take German B or German A?
faqs.answer: That depends on their written German rather than on their speaking, and the school decides. A student educated in German is usually a German A candidate, where the subject is literature and language analysis rather than language acquisition. A student from a German-speaking household but schooled in English often speaks fluently and has never written assessed German, which is a German B profile with a conventions gap. A timed written task settles it quickly, and taking that evidence to the DP coordinator is more productive than arguing from fluency.

faqs.question: Do schools in Abu Dhabi actually offer German B?
faqs.answer: A minority do, usually to very small numbers, and some run it only when enough students request it. Where it runs, teaching is close and practice volume is inevitably low, which is a different problem from poor teaching and needs a different answer. Ask the school two questions before DP1: whether German B will run in your child's cohort, and whether Higher Level is available. The answers determine whether outside support is a convenience or a necessity.

faqs.question: Can my child take German B if their school does not offer it?
faqs.answer: Some schools permit a student to take a language as a self-taught or externally supported subject and some do not, and the arrangement has registration implications with the IB. This must be confirmed in writing by the school before DP1 rather than assumed, because a late discovery is very difficult to resolve. Where it is permitted, outside support carries far more of the load than usual, and the oral and the literary works at Higher Level are the parts that need the most structure.

faqs.question: What does a German tutor charge per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates, mostly quoted for Dubai, give the range. Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end. Unitors lists IGCSE tutoring from around AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase quotes about AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts specialist exam-year support at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above. Visiting tutors run from about AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in. Those are their figures, not our price list.

faqs.question: Is a visiting tutor better than online lessons for German in this emirate?
faqs.answer: For German specifically the answer tilts strongly towards online, because the pool of local specialists is tiny. A visiting arrangement limits you to tutors who live within a reasonable drive, which for a widely taught subject is a mild constraint and for German B at Diploma level is a severe one. IB Gram does not provide in-person tutoring in Abu Dhabi in any case, and for a grammar-led subject the shared screen is where the marked task, the annotations and the error counts actually live.

faqs.question: How do I check that a private tutor in Abu Dhabi holds the right permit?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, and expect a straight answer. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and, according to the federal service information, is granted free of charge for two years to categories including registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents and students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: What may a German tutor do with work my child submits to school?
faqs.answer: Teach, question, model and give feedback - nothing beyond that. A tutor may mark practice tasks against the published criteria, count errors by type, rehearse the oral with unfamiliar stimuli or extracts and review recordings with the criteria open. A tutor has no part in the assessed recording, supplies no content for it, and sees no assessed written work before the school does. At Higher Level the literary works are read and discussed with the student, never summarised for them to reproduce.

faqs.question: How quickly can German grammar errors actually be fixed?
faqs.answer: In steps rather than smoothly, and the steps are predictable. Six weeks of one hour a week with written homework can make the verbal bracket automatic in short sentences, convert adjective endings into a single decision, remove the most common two-way preposition error, and add Konjunktiv II for politeness. A year is the honest figure for the full case system working unprompted in extended writing, for the genitive moving from avoided to used, and for reading speed through subordinate clauses and compound nouns.

faqs.question: Will German help with a university application from the UAE?
faqs.answer: A language acquisition grade contributes to the Diploma total universities read, and German specifically matters for applications to German-speaking countries, where public universities may require a recognised language qualification for German-taught programmes - check the individual institution rather than relying on a general answer. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, the British-track rules are published but no IB points threshold has been read on an official Ministry source for this page, so verify that on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-german-b-tutor.closingHeading: Send one marked task and we will count the errors
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-german-b-tutor.closingBody: German is the language where a single marked page tells you most. Send a recent piece of your child's written German and we will count the errors by type - case, adjective ending, verb position, word order - which usually identifies the missing system immediately. The trial lesson is free, takes no card details and carries no obligation, and your child keeps the annotated task whatever you decide. Add the level, the school and the internal oral deadline if you know it, and the plan is built around that date.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-global-politics-home-tut.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma Global Politics at Standard and Higher Level. Each profile names the guide version and the units they have taught, and whether they supervise the engagement project and the Higher Level orals, because those are separate skills from classroom teaching and the match has to be made on both.

intro.heading: Four documents that show whether anything is changing
paragraphs: Global Politics is the Diploma subject where tutoring is hardest to evaluate and easiest to fake. Sessions are interesting. Students enjoy them. The conversation ranges across current events and everybody leaves feeling well informed. Three months later the grade has not moved, and nobody can point at what was supposed to change. That is a structural problem with how the support was bought rather than a failure of effort.

The fix is to insist on artefacts. Four documents, each carrying a mark or a criterion judgement, make this subject as auditable as any other. A marked source-paper answer with the marks shown question by question. A timed extended response marked against the published markbands with the band named. The engagement project proposal with its research question and its planned activity assessed for viability. And, at Higher Level, a recorded practice presentation with the criteria applied to it. A parent who asks for those four will know within a month whether the arrangement is doing anything.

The reason the grade does not move without them is specific to this subject. Global Politics does not reward being informed. It rewards structure: a key concept applied accurately, a case used as evidence rather than as illustration, a counter-position stated at its strongest and then answered, and a judgement that could have gone the other way. A student who knows a great deal about a conflict and writes a narrative of it is doing the thing the subject explicitly does not want, and no amount of further reading will fix that, because reading is not what is missing.

Two local details matter. Cohorts in this emirate are frequently very small, sometimes three or four students, because the subject is newer than History or Geography in many departments. That means little past student work to calibrate against and often a teacher who is carrying the subject alongside another. And more than one version of the course has been in circulation, so material written for one guide can mislead a student sitting the other; confirm which applies with your school's Diploma coordinator before buying anything. Lessons themselves run online, one to one, over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, because home visits are a service we provide only in India.

What follows is organised around the four artefacts, then the engagement project, then the orals, then what the emirate makes possible for engagement, and finally the regulator, the honesty boundary and the cost. The rate is at the end because it is meaningless until you know what the hour has to hand back. One thing worth saying before any of it: the student described above is not behind. A child who argues well about international affairs has the hardest part already, and what remains is a set of mechanical habits that can be taught in a term.

Artefact two: a timed extended response marked against the markbands, band named
Artefact three: the engagement proposal, with question and activity assessed for viability
Artefact four: at Higher Level, a recorded practice presentation with criteria applied

programmes.description: Two years covering the course's core political content and key concepts, assessed through a source-based paper, extended-response essays, and an internally assessed report arising from a political engagement the student undertakes. programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and Societies in the middle years assesses investigation, communication and critical thinking against criteria that already separate description from argument. abu-dhabi/ib-dp-global-politics-home-tut.subjectsIntro: Global Politics is chosen alongside a recognisable set of subjects here, and the pairings matter because several of them share content with it directly. These are the combinations seen most often.

subjects.description: Core political content and key concepts assessed through a source-based paper, extended responses, an engagement report and, at Higher Level, oral case studies. Marks are lost to narrative, to cases used as illustration rather than evidence, and to judgements never actually made.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A source paper of twenty-four marks, essay papers at fifteen marks per essay and a 2,200-word historical investigation. The source technique transfers directly between the two subjects, and students taking both should be practising it once rather than twice.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Three core units, optional themes and a fieldwork report. The Higher Level global interactions content on power, networks, development and global risks overlaps with Global Politics closely enough that a case prepared for one serves the other with its framing adjusted.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Micro, macro and the global economy with a portfolio of commentaries. The development and trade content runs alongside the Global Politics material on development and interdependence, and the evaluation move at the end of a long answer is identical.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Three approaches to behaviour, option topics and an experimental report. Shares Global Politics' dependence on command terms, and students who learn the verb ladder in one subject apply it in the other without being taught twice.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Non-literary and literary texts, unseen analysis, an individual oral and a Higher Level essay. Directly useful here, because the source paper is an exercise in reading a text for purpose, audience and bias.

subjects.name: Philosophy
subjects.description: Core themes, a prescribed text and an internally assessed analysis. The conceptual precision Philosophy demands is exactly what separates an accurate use of legitimacy or sovereignty from a loose one in a politics essay.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Offered at several levels across the emirate's schools and mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum for the groups the regulations specify. A real constraint on a politics student's week, since both subjects demand sustained written work.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Five content units, two written papers and a research project worth a quarter of the grade. Often the third humanities choice, and the lightest for reading volume in a block that already contains Global Politics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and financial mathematics. Quietly useful to a politics student, because development and inequality are measured with indicators whose construction a student should be able to criticise rather than quote.

sections.heading: The four artefacts, and what each one proves
paragraphs: This is the audit a parent can run without knowing anything about international relations. Each artefact carries a judgement against published criteria, which means it can be compared with the next one, which means progress is observable rather than reported. Publishing this is worth doing because no competitor page in the researched set offers any mechanism at all for checking whether tutoring is working.

The first artefact is a marked source-paper answer with the marks shown question by question. It localises the problem immediately: a student losing the short comprehension marks is reading carelessly, a student losing the comparative question has never been taught to write across two sources, and a student losing the extended evaluative question is failing to combine source material with their own knowledge. Those are three different repairs with three different hour counts.

The second is a timed extended response marked against the published markbands with the band named and one move to the next band written out. Over a sequence of these, two things should be visible. The band should move. And the same feedback should not appear three times, because feedback repeated is feedback that was received rather than acted on, which means the approach needs changing rather than repeating.

The third is the engagement proposal, assessed for viability before anything is undertaken, and the fourth is a recorded practice presentation for Higher Level students with the criteria applied to the recording. Both are things a parent can look at. A proposal that names an activity, a research question, the people involved and the dates is viable. One that names a topic is not, and discovering that in DP1 costs nothing while discovering it in DP2 costs the component.

sections.heading: Informed is not the same as assessed: what the mark scheme rewards
paragraphs: The most common profile on this page is a student who follows international news, holds considered views, performs well in debate and writes mid-band essays. The instinct is to treat this as a knowledge problem and to read more. It is not a knowledge problem, and reading more makes the essays longer without making them better.

What the subject rewards is a specific structure. A key concept named and used accurately, not as a label but as an analytical tool. A case deployed as evidence for a claim, with enough specific detail that it could not be swapped for a different case. A counter-position stated at its strongest, because an objection presented weakly earns nothing. And a judgement that answers the question asked, with the conditions under which it would be different.

Concept precision is where the quickest gains sit. Legitimacy, sovereignty, power, interdependence, development, human rights, justice, equality and the rest are technical terms in this course with specifiable meanings, and students use them interchangeably with their ordinary-language cousins. A student who can distinguish legitimacy from legality, or power from influence, and can show the distinction doing work in an argument, is writing in a different band from one who uses the words as decoration.

The failure that persists longest is narrative. A student asked to evaluate a claim about intervention writes the history of an intervention. Everything in it may be accurate. None of it answers the question, because the question asked for a judgement and received a chronology. The fix is a forced plan in which each paragraph opens with a claim about the question and closes with a weighing, and it is uncomfortable for two essays before it becomes the student's natural shape.
bullets: A concept named and doing analytical work, not used as a label
A case specific enough that it could not be swapped for another
The counter-position stated at its strongest, then answered
A judgement with the conditions under which it would differ

sections.heading: The source paper: reading for purpose rather than content
paragraphs: The source-based paper presents a small booklet of material on one topic and asks a series of questions of increasing demand. The early questions test whether the student has read accurately. A middle question asks for comparison across sources. The final and most heavily weighted question asks for an evaluation that combines the sources with the student's own knowledge of the course content.

The skill that runs through all of it is reading a source for what it is trying to do rather than for what it says. Who produced this, for whom, and to what end. A government statement, an advocacy organisation's report, an academic analysis and a journalist's account are four different kinds of evidence, and a student who treats them as four descriptions of the same facts is missing the point of the exercise and the marks attached to it.

The comparative question is the one most often mishandled, and the error is identical to the one History students make: writing a paragraph about each source and leaving the comparison for the reader to infer. The marks require explicit statements across sources on shared points of comparison. A grid drawn before writing, with the point down one side and each source across the top, fixes it in a couple of sessions.

The final question is where the band is decided, and the reliable diagnostic is whether the answer contains anything the booklet does not. An answer built only from the sources sits in the middle. An answer that brings a concept from the course, a case the sources do not mention, and a judgement the sources do not reach, is doing what was asked. Evidence of progress is concrete: the student's answers start containing named cases and concepts that appear nowhere in the material provided.
bullets: Origin, purpose and intended audience read before content
A comparison grid drawn before the comparative answer is written
The final answer must contain concepts and cases absent from the booklet
Time control early in the paper protects the heavily weighted question

sections.heading: The engagement project: an activity first, a report second
paragraphs: The internally assessed component arises from a political engagement the student undertakes and is submitted as a written report within a stated word limit. Confirm the current limit, the required structure and the weighting with your school's Diploma coordinator, because more than one version of this course has been in circulation and the requirements differ between them.

The structural point that families miss is the order of operations. This is not an essay with an activity attached as justification. The activity comes first, it has to be real, it has to be sustained enough to produce something worth analysing, and the research question has to arise from it rather than being imposed on it afterwards. A student who picks a topic, writes an essay and then describes a loosely related activity has produced a report that will read exactly like what it is.

The second point is that the report is analytical rather than descriptive. It must connect what the student experienced to the course's concepts and to wider political theory and practice, and it must do so with the same discipline the essays demand: concept, evidence, counter-position, judgement. A report that narrates an experience and then observes that politics is complicated has missed the criteria entirely.

The third is scheduling, and it is the commonest practical failure. An engagement that depends on other people's time has to be arranged around the school calendar, and in this emirate the long weekends and the Eid breaks absorb a significant part of the available window. A project approved in DP1 with the activity under way by the end of that year is comfortable. A project approved late in DP2 produces a report about something the student barely did, and no amount of writing skill will disguise it.

sections.heading: Higher Level: the oral case studies and the rehearsal nobody does
paragraphs: Higher Level students complete an extension assessed through oral presentations on global political challenges, each on a separate case and each delivered to time against published criteria. This is a distinct assessment with its own demands, and it is the component most often attempted unrehearsed, because talking is the thing these students are already good at and so it feels like the part that needs no work.

That instinct is wrong for a measurable reason. Fluent speakers run long. A student who can talk about a political challenge for twenty minutes and is required to present for a fraction of that will either be cut off mid-argument or will race the conclusion, and the criteria that reward analysis and judgement are precisely the ones at the end. Time control is a technical skill and it is learned by recording, timing and redrafting rather than by intending to be brief.

The content requirement is the same discipline as everywhere else in the course. A challenge identified precisely rather than gestured at. Specific cases examined with evidence. The course concepts used accurately as analytical tools. Multiple perspectives presented fairly, including the one the student disagrees with. And a judgement reached rather than a survey delivered. A presentation that explains an issue thoroughly and never evaluates anything sits in the middle bands regardless of delivery.

The practical support here is unglamorous and effective: the student records a practice run, the recording is watched with the criteria in hand, and the specific failures are named. Over-running. A concept used loosely in the second minute. A perspective presented as obviously wrong. A conclusion that summarises rather than decides. Three rehearsal cycles usually produce a different performance, and the recording is an artefact a parent can watch rather than a report they have to trust.
bullets: Two separate cases, each delivered to time against published criteria

sections.heading: Political engagement an Abu Dhabi student can genuinely undertake
paragraphs: Students and parents often assume the engagement requirement means activism, and then conclude that it is impractical. Neither is right. The course requires a political engagement, which is broader than campaigning, and the mark rewards the analysis arising from it rather than the nature of the activity. A well-chosen, modest, properly documented engagement outscores an ambitious one that produced nothing to analyse.

What works well for students here falls into a few shapes. Sustained volunteering through a school-sanctioned placement, where the student sees how an organisation makes decisions and allocates resources. A Model United Nations commitment taken seriously enough to involve real preparation and reflection rather than attendance. A sequence of interviews with practitioners, which is often the strongest option because it produces primary material nobody else has. Attendance at public lectures and forums, which Abu Dhabi hosts in some number, followed up with correspondence. Or a school or community project the student actually helps run.

The emirate offers specific research and engagement context worth knowing about. The International Renewable Energy Agency is headquartered here, which makes energy governance an unusually accessible topic for a student in this city. The Emirates Red Crescent operates nationally and humanitarian action is a core-course theme. These are institutions a student can research and, where appropriate and with the school's involvement, approach; they are not placements that any tutoring provider arranges, and nobody should imply otherwise.

Two constraints to respect. The engagement must stay inside what the school sanctions and within UAE law, and the course does not require anything that would strain either. And where other people are involved, consent and data minimisation apply: collect only what the project needs, keep identifying information separate, and have a plan for deleting it. The UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs personal data generally, and a student who has thought about it looks like a researcher rather than a candidate.
bullets: Engagement is broader than activism and the mark rewards the analysis
Interview sequences often produce the strongest primary material
Keep the activity inside what the school sanctions and within UAE law
Consent and data minimisation apply wherever other people are involved

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi cohorts, and what a class of four actually means
paragraphs: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in this emirate and publishes inspection ratings. Those ratings are awarded to schools rather than to departments, which is particularly limiting for a subject as new as this one in many Abu Dhabi schools. A highly rated school may be running Global Politics for the first time with four students and a teacher who also teaches History.

A very small cohort has real consequences, and they are not all bad. The teaching is close to individual, which is an advantage. What is lost is calibration: no spread of past student work at different mark bands, nobody in the room producing a better essay for the student to compare against, no second internal reader for a borderline engagement report, and no audience for oral rehearsal beyond the teacher. Those are exactly the gaps external support fills, and framing it that way is more honest than suggesting the school is failing.

The questions to ask the department are narrow. Which guide version applies. Which units have been taught and which remain. How many students sit the subject and at which levels. Whether the engagement activities have been approved and what has been approved before. At Higher Level, when the orals are scheduled and whether rehearsals are built into class time. And whether anonymised past reports can be shown at different mark bands.

On mandatory subjects and the national picture: Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies run alongside the licensed curriculum for the groups the regulations specify, which consumes hours a politics student also needs for written work. Dubai's regulator sets this out in detail for its own schools; the federal position is that private schools must follow Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their own curriculum. Dubai sits with KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain with ADEK, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of them, nor from the IB, and claims none.

sections.heading: Sourcing and academic honesty in a politics subject
paragraphs: This subject has an honesty dimension the others do not, because its material is contested and because the internet supplies unlimited confident commentary on every topic on the syllabus. Two distinct problems follow. The first is attribution: a student who has absorbed an argument from a commentator and presents it as their own analysis has a referencing failure even where no text was copied. The second is evidence quality: an advocacy organisation's claim and an academic finding are different kinds of thing and a report that treats them identically is weaker for it.

Teaching the distinction is part of the subject rather than an administrative addition. A student who can say what kind of source a claim came from, what that source was trying to achieve, and why the claim is still usable with that noted, is demonstrating the analytical skill the source paper assesses directly. The habit transfers from the engagement report to the examinations without further teaching.

The tutor boundary is the same as in every Diploma subject and worth stating in full. A tutor may teach concepts, explain what each criterion asks for, question an engagement proposal before it is approved, read a student's own draft and say where a claim is unsupported or where description has replaced argument, point out a referencing failure, rehearse an oral and apply the criteria to the recording, and ask the questions that prompt a revision. A tutor may not supply text, script a presentation, restructure a section into its final form, or produce any part of the assessed work.

Scripting the orals deserves a specific mention because it is the particular temptation here, and because a scripted presentation is both detectable and a malpractice problem. A student reading someone else's argument aloud cannot answer a question about it, which is exactly what a teacher will do. One site in the competitor research sells completed internal assessments outright; the consequence of buying any such thing falls on the student rather than the seller. Ask any provider for a written statement of what they refuse to do before booking hours.

sections.heading: What Global Politics support costs here, and how the lessons run
paragraphs: What the market charges is worth stating before anything else, with the sources named. A qualified subject tutor working online across the UAE is quoted at roughly AED 150-300 an hour. IB specialists go from about AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards. In-home visits sit at roughly AED 180-500, higher because the drive is billed inside the hour. Those bands are drawn from published provider pages and from Bestimate’s Dubai rate table, read in October 2026, and they describe the market rather than an IB Gram price list.

In this subject the question that separates quotes is whether anything is marked. Global Politics support is unusually pleasant to deliver badly: an hour of well-informed discussion satisfies everyone and changes nothing. An hour that returns a timed extended response marked against the published markbands with the band named is a different product, and the two are frequently quoted at the same figure. Ask explicitly, and ask what the first three sessions will hand back.

On delivery, stated plainly: every UAE lesson is one-to-one and online, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Abu Dhabi and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For this subject the format carries a specific benefit, because oral rehearsal is recorded and reviewed on screen anyway, and a recording is a better rehearsal tool than a listener in the room.

On availability, honestly. The Diploma Global Politics teaching population inside the UAE is small, because the subject is newer and the cohorts are tiny. For essay technique and source work a match usually takes a few days; for the Higher Level orals or engagement supervision near an internal deadline it can take longer. Where nobody is free we say so and offer a tutor based elsewhere teaching the same specification at the same rate, or give a date rather than a maybe. No competitor in the researched set discloses a coverage limit at all.
