process.title: Confirm the guide version and the units taught
process.description: More than one version of this course has been in circulation, and material written for one misleads a student sitting the other. One email to the Diploma coordinator settles the version, which units have been covered, and whether the engagement activity has been approved. Send the answers with your enquiry.

process.title: Send one marked response
process.description: A marked source-paper answer with the marks shown per question, or a marked extended response, distinguishes a reading problem from a comparison problem from a judgement problem. Those three need different work and different numbers of hours, and twenty minutes with the script separates them.

process.title: Free trial with the markbands open
process.description: Held by the tutor who would take the weekly slot, with your child's own marked work on the shared screen. It ends by naming the band the writing sits in and the single move that reaches the next band. A closing statement about enjoying the subject is a reason not to book.

process.title: Agree the artefact each session returns
process.description: Hours rather than terms, with the marked document each session hands back written down in advance. In a subject where discussion feels productive, specifying the artefact is the only way to tell teaching from conversation, and a provider who will not specify has answered the question.

process.title: Audit at six weeks against the marked work
process.description: Lay the marked responses out in order. If the band moved on the component being worked, continue. If the same feedback appears three times, the approach is wrong rather than the student, and the recommendation should be a different approach, a different tutor, or stopping.

whyPoints.title: Every session returns a marked artefact
whyPoints.description: A marked response with the band named, a proposal assessed for viability, or a rehearsal recording with the criteria applied. In a subject where an hour of interesting discussion satisfies everybody and changes nothing, the returned document is the only honest evidence of teaching.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the guide version and the units
whyPoints.description: More than one version of this course is in circulation and cohorts are tiny. We state which version and which units the tutor has taught and for how many cohorts, because a politics graduate who has not taught the current guide is a well-read stranger to the mark scheme.

whyPoints.title: Feedback that is not allowed to repeat
whyPoints.description: If the same comment lands on three consecutive responses, the sessions are describing a habit rather than repairing it. We treat repetition as a failure of the teaching and change the approach, which is the opposite of what an open-ended weekly arrangement rewards.

whyPoints.title: Orals rehearsed on camera, not discussed
whyPoints.description: The Higher Level extension is the component most often attempted unrehearsed, because these students are confident speakers. Recording, timing and reviewing against the criteria is unglamorous and it is what fixes over-running and missing judgements. The recording is an artefact a parent can watch.

whyPoints.title: A published boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches concepts, questions a proposal, comments on a student's own draft and applies criteria to a rehearsal. A tutor does not script a presentation, supply text or produce assessed work. The boundary is published because a market in completed coursework operates alongside this one.

whyPoints.title: No regulator used as a credential
whyPoints.description: ADEK licenses and inspects private schools in this emirate; other emirates sit with KHDA, SPEA, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge or the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of them, nor from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether Global Politics tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: By insisting on marked artefacts rather than progress reports, because this is the subject where enjoyable sessions most easily substitute for teaching. Ask for four things: a marked source-paper answer with the marks shown question by question in the first fortnight, timed extended responses marked against the published markbands with the band named, the engagement proposal assessed for viability, and at Higher Level a recorded practice presentation with the criteria applied. Over six weeks the band should move and the same feedback should not appear three times.

faqs.question: What should a marked Global Politics essay tell me?
faqs.answer: A band, the reason for it, and one named move to the band above. The markbands reward a concept used accurately as an analytical tool, cases deployed as evidence rather than illustration, a counter-position stated at its strongest and answered, and a judgement that addresses the question asked. A useful marked essay says which of those is missing. If the comment is about how interesting the argument was, or lists further reading, it is not feedback and nothing in the next essay will change.

faqs.question: Which version of the Global Politics course is my child's school teaching?
faqs.answer: Ask the Diploma coordinator, because more than one version of this course has been in circulation and material written for one misleads a student sitting the other. While you are asking, get which units have been taught and which remain, whether the engagement activity has been approved, and at Higher Level when the orals are scheduled. Those four answers determine what a tutor should work on first. A provider who books you in without asking any of them has told you how closely they intend to match.

faqs.question: What are the key concepts in the Global Politics course and why do they matter?
faqs.answer: They are the technical vocabulary the whole course is built on: power, sovereignty, legitimacy, interdependence, human rights, justice, equality, development, globalisation, inequality, sustainability, peace, conflict, violence and non-violence among them. The exact set depends on the guide version, so confirm it with the school. They matter because precision with them is the cheapest mark gain available here. A student who can distinguish legitimacy from legality, or power from influence, and show the distinction doing work in an argument, writes in a different band from one using them as decoration.

faqs.question: How does the source paper differ from the essay paper in this subject?
faqs.answer: The source paper gives a small booklet of material on one topic and asks questions of increasing demand: accurate reading first, then comparison across sources, then an evaluative question that must combine the sources with the student's own knowledge. The essay paper supplies nothing and requires the student to bring everything. The diagnostic for the source paper's final question is simple: does the answer contain concepts and cases that appear nowhere in the booklet? If not, it will sit in the middle bands however well written.

faqs.question: What counts as political engagement for a student living in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Far more than activism, which is the usual misconception. Sustained volunteering through a school-sanctioned placement, a Model United Nations commitment taken seriously enough to involve real preparation, a sequence of interviews with practitioners, attendance at public lectures and forums followed up properly, or a school or community project the student genuinely helps run. Interview sequences are often the strongest because they produce primary material nobody else has. Keep the activity inside what the school sanctions and within UAE law; the course requires nothing that would strain either.

faqs.question: How long is the engagement report and what has to be in it?
faqs.answer: It sits within a stated word limit and has a required structure, both of which depend on the guide version your child is sitting, so confirm them with the Diploma coordinator rather than relying on a figure from any tutoring page. What matters more than the number is the order of operations: the activity comes first, it has to be real and sustained, and the research question has to arise from it. A report where a topic was chosen, an essay written and an activity attached afterwards reads exactly like what it is.

faqs.question: What do Higher Level students have to present orally?
faqs.answer: The Higher Level extension is assessed through oral presentations on global political challenges, each on a separate case and each delivered to time against published criteria. The content demand is the same as everywhere in the course: a challenge identified precisely, specific cases examined with evidence, concepts used accurately, multiple perspectives presented fairly including the one the student rejects, and a judgement reached. The practical difficulty is time. Fluent speakers over-run and lose the analysis marks at the end, which is why rehearsal on camera matters more than further reading.

faqs.question: How many case studies does my child actually need for the essays?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most students try to collect, held to a higher standard. Three or four cases per unit, each known well enough to supply specific detail that could not be swapped for another case, covers the essay papers. What makes a case usable is not breadth of knowledge but precision: the actors, the dates, the measurable outcome, and the concept it illustrates doing analytical work. Twenty cases held as general awareness is worse than four held properly, because general awareness cannot function as evidence for a claim.

faqs.question: Why does my child describe a conflict instead of analysing it?
faqs.answer: Because narrative is the default shape for anyone who knows a lot about an event, and because it feels like demonstrating knowledge. Asked to evaluate a claim about intervention, the student writes the history of an intervention: accurate, detailed, and not an answer, since the question wanted a judgement and received a chronology. The repair is a forced plan in which every paragraph opens with a claim about the question and closes with a weighing. It is uncomfortable for two essays and then becomes the student's natural shape.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the engagement project without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the most valuable help comes before anything is done. A tutor may interrogate a proposed activity and research question for viability, explain what each criterion asks for, ask what the student will actually be able to analyse afterwards, read the student's own draft and point out where description has replaced argument, and identify a referencing failure. What a tutor may not do is supply text, restructure a section into final form or produce any part of the assessed work. The same applies to the orals: rehearsal is permitted, scripting is not.

faqs.question: Is Global Politics accepted by universities as a humanities subject?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, but requirements are set course by course and vary within the same institution, so read the entry profile for every destination on your child's list rather than relying on a general answer. Some politics and international relations courses name specific preferred subjects and some do not. Certificate equivalency through the Ministry of Education is a separate process from admission: the British-track rules are published and specific, while no IB points figure appears in the source we verified, so check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly.

faqs.question: Does a very small Global Politics cohort put my child at a disadvantage?
faqs.answer: Not in the teaching, which becomes close to individual, but in calibration, which is a real loss. A class of four has no spread of student work at different mark bands to compare against, nobody else in the room producing a stronger essay, no second internal reader for a borderline engagement report, and no audience for oral rehearsal beyond the teacher. Those four gaps are exactly what external support fills. Ask the department whether anonymised past reports at different bands can be shown, because that single document closes the largest of them.

faqs.question: What does Diploma Global Politics support cost in the Abu Dhabi market?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor working online across the UAE is quoted roughly AED 150-300 an hour, IB specialists from about AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards, and in-home visits roughly AED 180-500 because travel sits inside the hour. Those figures come from published provider pages and Bestimate's Dubai rate table, read in October 2026, and describe the market rather than our prices. The question that separates quotes here is whether anything is marked, because an hour of well-informed discussion satisfies everybody and moves no band.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around Abu Dhabi school timings and the Ramadan calendar?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the online format is what makes it straightforward. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the productive study window shifts late, so a standing slot normally moves to after Iftar for that period; the long weekends and the Eid breaks need planning around rather than through, because internal coursework deadlines tend to cluster against them. Because there is no travel to rearrange, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation. For a subject whose progress depends on written work produced between sessions, protecting a workable hour matters more than which hour it is.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-global-politics-home-tut.closingHeading: Ask for the artefact, not the update
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-global-politics-home-tut.closingBody: Send one marked response and the guide version your child's department is teaching, and we will say what the first block should work on and roughly how many hours it should take. Then ask for the same four documents from anybody you are considering: a marked source answer, a marked timed response with the band named, the engagement proposal assessed for viability, and at Higher Level a rehearsal recording with the criteria applied. The trial is free and held by the tutor who would take the slot. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one online over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not make home visits in the UAE.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-global-politics-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Global Politics at Standard and Higher Level to Abu Dhabi students over live video. Each profile names the thematic studies they cover, whether they supervise the engagement component, and whether they coach the Higher Level presentations.

intro.heading: The subject is marked on concepts, and students answer with news
paragraphs: Global Politics attracts the students who read. That is the problem. A student who follows international affairs closely arrives in DP1 able to describe a dozen situations in detail and gets a surprising mark on the first essay, because the course is not assessed on how much is known about events. It is assessed on whether events are used to argue something about power, sovereignty, legitimacy, interdependence, development, human rights, peace and conflict. Those are analytical tools, and the marks are for using them.

You can see the pattern in a single paragraph. Asked to evaluate the effectiveness of an international institution, a well-read student narrates what that institution has done, in order, with accurate detail. The band descriptors want a criterion for effectiveness, stated explicitly, then evidence weighed against it, then a counterargument taken seriously enough to change the judgement or survive it. The first version is journalism. The second is Global Politics. The gap between them is a few weeks of structured work, not a year of extra reading.

The course is assessed through a source-based paper, an essay paper, an internally assessed engagement component in which the student engages with a political issue and writes about it, and, at Higher Level, two recorded oral presentations on global political challenges. The exact weightings and the name of the engagement component depend on which guide your child's cohort is examined under, because the IB revised this subject's guide for recent first assessment. Confirm both with the Diploma coordinator rather than trusting any tutoring page, including this one.

Abu Dhabi offers this subject something unusual. The capital holds the diplomatic missions, the headquarters of the International Renewable Energy Agency in Masdar City, and the Barakah nuclear plant in the Al Dhafra region, and the country hosted COP28 in Dubai in 2023. For a student studying interdependence, environmental governance or the politics of energy, that is reachable case-study material rather than borrowed examples. Used carefully, it produces more original answers than a recycled study of a well-known crisis.

Used carelessly, it produces something worse. Global Politics requires balanced analysis of contested issues, and a student writing about their own region needs academic sources, multiple perspectives and no advocacy. A section further down this page deals with that directly, because it is the one aspect of this subject where a tutor's judgement matters as much as their subject knowledge. Lessons for UAE families run live online, one to one, with a shared screen; there are no home visits in Abu Dhabi, as in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

One practical note before the detail. This subject is taught in fewer schools in the emirate than History or Economics, and where it runs the class is often three or four students. That changes what a family should look for. In a large cohort a student calibrates against classmates' marked work; in a class of four there is almost nothing to calibrate against, and a competent essay can sit two bands below where the student believes it sits. External marking is the cheapest correction available, and it is the reason most of our Global Politics enquiries from this emirate arrive after a first set of DP2 mocks rather than before them.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-global-politics-tutor.programmesIntro: Global Politics is a Group 3 Diploma course, and students reach it from three main routes in this emirate. Each route produces a different first-term weakness.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Assessed by a source-based paper, an essay paper, an internally assessed engagement component, and at Higher Level two recorded presentations on global political challenges. The course content is organised around key concepts and thematic studies, which means the same concept recurs across different topics and a student who has learned it once can use it everywhere.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi school offers Global Politics, so students sometimes take it in small classes of three or four, or as a self-taught option supported by a teacher of another subject. Those students need a specialist more than most, because small classes rarely generate the range of marked exemplars that calibrate a student's sense of what a band-five answer looks like.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP individuals and societies teaches investigation, perspective-taking and structured communication, all of which transfer. What does not transfer is the requirement to define a concept and then apply it as a measuring tool, which is the central move of every Global Politics answer and is rarely practised before DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Students arriving from an Abu Dhabi MYP cohort tend to write fluently and evaluate loosely. The early fix is a definitions discipline: a concept used in an essay has to be defined in the terms the course uses, not in general terms, and then applied consistently to the end of the answer rather than abandoned after the introduction.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students may take Global Politics as a Diploma course alongside their career-related study and reflective project, sitting identical components. The engagement component suits CP students well, because many are already involved in community or workplace activity that connects to a political issue.
programmes.countryNote: CP cohorts in Abu Dhabi are small, so a CP student taking Global Politics may be the only one in the school doing so. That makes external calibration valuable: without classmates' marked work to compare against, a student has no reference point for how far an evaluation has to go before it reaches the upper bands.

programmes.name: Extended Essay in Global Politics
programmes.description: A 4,000-word research essay on a focused political question, supervised in school. The subject-specific trap is choosing a question about a situation still unfolding, where the literature is journalism rather than scholarship and no settled analysis exists to engage with.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi students have good access to multilateral and policy material through institutions based in the emirate and through university libraries on Saadiyat Island. A question about environmental governance or energy transition politics can be answered from published policy literature, which marks better than a question about last month's events.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-global-politics-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the components and neighbouring courses Abu Dhabi families raise alongside Global Politics, with the specific demand each one makes.

subjects.name: Key concepts
subjects.levels: HL and SL, throughout the course
subjects.description: Power, sovereignty, legitimacy, interdependence, human rights, development, peace and conflict, and related ideas, used as analytical instruments. Every essay question is answerable through at least one of them, and an answer that never names one cannot reach the upper bands however accurate its detail.

subjects.name: Source-based paper
subjects.description: A short stimulus booklet with questions rising in demand: a definition or outline, an explanation drawn from a source, a comparison across sources, and a final evaluation requiring the sources together with the student's own knowledge. The last question carries the most credit and is the least practised.

subjects.name: Essay paper
subjects.description: Extended responses across the thematic studies, marked on a sustained argument supported by relevant examples and genuine engagement with alternative views. Higher Level candidates write more essays in a longer paper, so timing discipline becomes a separate skill from argument quality.

subjects.name: Engagement component
subjects.description: The student engages with a political issue in practice and writes a report connecting that experience to research and to the course concepts. The report has a word limit that is strictly applied, and the commonest loss is a long description of the activity with the analysis compressed into the final page.

subjects.name: Higher Level extension
subjects.description: Two presentations on two different global political challenges, each with a time ceiling of about ten minutes. Students who treat them as a talk rather than as a structured analysis run over, drift into description, and lose the marks that are available for conceptual framing and evidence.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The strongest companion subject, because it supplies the depth of example that Global Politics essays need. The caution runs the other way: a History-trained student may give chronology where the question wanted a conceptual judgement about the present.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Reinforces the development and interdependence material directly, particularly on trade, aid and inequality. Students taking both tend to write the most confident answers on globalisation, provided economic diagrams stay in the Economics examination.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Overlaps on resources, climate governance and global risks, and Higher Level Geography's global interactions material is close kin to several Global Politics themes. The shared risk is spatial description where political analysis of power and legitimacy was required.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Trains close reading of a text for purpose, audience and bias, which is precisely the skill the source-based paper asks for. Students strong here usually improve fastest on the source questions once the transfer is pointed out.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Global Politics supplies TOK material on perspective, bias and the limits of political knowledge. The two can be prepared together, and a student who has thought carefully about perspective in TOK writes better counterarguments in Global Politics.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-global-politics-tutor.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi communities, institutions and the case material each one puts in reach
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-global-politics-tutor.regionsIntro: For this subject the geography of the emirate is useful in a particular way: it holds institutions a student can study from published material. These notes cover both where students live and what is analytically available nearby.

regions.name: Masdar City
regions.note: Home to the headquarters of the International Renewable Energy Agency, which publishes extensive policy material. For students working on environmental governance or the politics of energy transition, the primary documents are public and the institution is in the same city.

regions.name: Al Bateen and the diplomatic area
regions.note: Where the capital's diplomatic missions concentrate. Students here sometimes have family connections to foreign-service or international-organisation work, which can support the engagement component if handled with care about confidentiality and balance.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: University campuses and cultural institutions on the island give access to academic libraries, public lectures and scholarly literature. That matters for an Extended Essay, where the difference between policy journalism and peer-reviewed sources shows up in the mark.

regions.name: Al Dhafra region
regions.note: The Barakah nuclear plant sits in this part of the emirate, and the international safeguards framework around civil nuclear power is published and analysable. A rich case for sovereignty, interdependence and regulation, used analytically rather than promotionally.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: The corridor with the largest Diploma population in the emirate, and the one where Global Politics is most often taught in small classes. Students here benefit most from external calibration, because a class of four produces few exemplars to compare against.

regions.name: Al Reem Island and Al Maryah
regions.note: Dense apartment communities with long school runs and tight evenings. Fixed online slots in the early evening are what actually hold here, and a Higher Level presentation rehearsal needs a predictable hour rather than a flexible one.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer schools and younger cohorts, with Global Politics often newly introduced. Where a subject is new in a school, the first cohort has no prior students' work to learn from, which is exactly the gap one-to-one work fills.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Inside the same emirate, with a smaller international-school market and very limited local coverage of this subject. Most Al Ain students who take Global Politics need a specialist who is not within driving distance, which is the straightforward case for online delivery.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Corniche schools
schoolClusters.note: Students we support on the island attend established schools, not all of which offer Global Politics. Where it is offered, class sizes are often small. Ask the individual and societies department whether the subject runs this year and which thematic studies it covers.

sections.heading: How Global Politics is assessed, and what each component rewards
paragraphs: Standard Level students complete three assessed components: a source-based paper, an essay paper, and the internally assessed engagement component. Higher Level students complete those three plus an extension consisting of two recorded presentations on global political challenges. The weightings differ between levels, and the precise figures depend on which version of the subject guide your child's cohort is examined under, because the IB revised this course's guide for recent first assessment. We publish no weighting percentages here for that reason; the Diploma coordinator holds the authoritative version.

What does not change between guide versions is what each component rewards, and that is where tutoring effort belongs. The source paper rewards reading a document for what it argues and for the interests behind it. The essay paper rewards a sustained conceptual argument. The engagement component rewards connecting lived engagement to research and to concepts. The Higher Level extension rewards the ability to frame a contested global challenge and reach a defensible judgement about it inside ten minutes.

The table below sets out those demands component by component, with the failure mode each one attracts. It is deliberately written without percentages so that it remains accurate whichever guide applies. Take it to your child's teacher and ask which components are weakest; that single question produces a better tutoring plan than any amount of discussion about predicted grades, because each of these components fails for its own reason and needs its own remedy.

sections.heading: Answering with a concept instead of with the news
paragraphs: This is the central skill of the subject, and almost all retrievable marks sit in it. A question asks whether an institution has been effective, or whether an intervention was legitimate, or how far interdependence constrains sovereignty. A well-read student answers by describing what happened. The band descriptors reward something structurally different: the concept defined in the terms the course uses, a criterion made explicit, evidence weighed against that criterion, and an alternative reading taken seriously.

Take legitimacy as an example. A student can define it loosely as being accepted, and then write three paragraphs of description. Or they can define it as the course does, distinguish the sources from which legitimacy is claimed, state which of those they will use as the test, and then assess the evidence against that test, noting where it points the other way. The second answer may contain less information than the first and will score higher, which is the single most counterintuitive fact about this subject for a student who prides themselves on reading widely.

The teaching move is narrow and repeatable. Write the concept at the top of the plan. Write the criterion under it. Write three claims that test the criterion. Write the counterargument that most threatens the judgement. Then write the essay. Five minutes of that, practised until it is automatic, is worth more than any amount of additional case-study reading, because the case studies the student already knows become usable. The table below maps the recurring concepts to the question stems they tend to appear in.

sections.heading: The source-based paper, question by question
paragraphs: The source paper gives a short stimulus booklet and a series of questions that rise in demand. The opening question asks for a definition or an outline and is worth few marks, so a student who writes a paragraph there has already lost time. The next requires an explanation drawn from a named source, which means quoting or referring to it rather than writing from memory. Then comes a comparison across sources, which fails unless the comparison is made in linked statements rather than in two separate summaries.

The final question is where the paper is won or lost. It requires the sources and the student's own knowledge in a single evaluative answer, and students lose roughly half the available credit by using one and not the other. Some write a source-only answer that reads like a comprehension exercise. Others write an essay that ignores the booklet entirely, which is the more common error among the well-read students this subject attracts. Both are avoidable with practice on this one question type.

We practise the paper in reverse order. The final question comes first, every week, until the structure is automatic: claim, source evidence, own-knowledge evidence, alternative reading, judgement. Then the earlier questions are drilled for brevity, because the only thing they require is accuracy and speed. Four sessions of that typically moves this component more than a term of content work, for the simple reason that nothing in it depends on knowing more politics.

sections.heading: The engagement component: experience, research and a word limit that bites
paragraphs: The internally assessed component asks the student to engage with a political issue in practice and then write about it, connecting that engagement to research and to the course concepts. Its current name and exact word limit depend on the guide in force for the cohort, so confirm both with your child's teacher; what follows is about the structure, which has been stable in substance.

Two failures account for most lost marks. The first is choosing an issue with no analytical traction: a worthy activity that generates goodwill and no political question. Volunteering is engagement; it becomes assessable when there is a contested political issue behind it that research can illuminate, such as how a service is funded, who is excluded from it, or which authority is responsible. The choice of issue is therefore an academic decision made at the start, not a description written at the end.

The second failure is the word budget. Students write a long narrative of what they did, because it is the easy part and they remember it, and then compress the analysis into a final page. The report is marked on the connection between engagement, research and concepts, and that connection lives in the part that gets squeezed. Setting the budget before drafting, and keeping a dated record of the engagement as it happens rather than reconstructing it afterwards, prevents both problems. A tutor comments on drafts the student has written, naming the component; no portion of the submitted text comes from anybody else.

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi case material, used analytically
paragraphs: Most Global Politics answers worldwide draw on the same handful of well-known cases, which makes them harder to distinguish. Students in this emirate have alternatives that are both reachable and documented. The International Renewable Energy Agency is headquartered in Masdar City and publishes policy material in volume. The Barakah nuclear plant in the Al Dhafra region sits inside an international safeguards framework whose rules are public. The country hosted COP28 in Dubai in 2023, generating a documented record of multilateral negotiation. Academic libraries and public lectures on Saadiyat Island give access to scholarship rather than commentary.

The analytical value is specific. Energy transition governance tests interdependence and sovereignty at once, because the institutions involved have authority that states grant and can withhold. Civil nuclear regulation is a clean case for the difference between legal obligation and practical capacity. Multilateral climate negotiation is where legitimacy arguments are made explicitly by the participants themselves, which gives a student primary material instead of secondary characterisation.

The discipline required is the same discipline the subject always requires. A local case must be analysed, not promoted: the question is what it shows about a concept, and the answer has to acknowledge readings that cut against the preferred one. Sources should be published policy documents and academic literature, with the organisation named, rather than news summaries. Handled that way, proximity is an advantage. Handled as advocacy, it reads as uncritical and the evaluation marks disappear.

There is also a sensible limit on how far to lean on local material. An examiner marks what the question asked, and a prepared case does not always fit. Students who build an entire revision plan around two local anchors sometimes force them into questions where a better-known case would serve the argument more cleanly. The workable balance is two or three local cases known deeply enough to be used flexibly, alongside the standard cases the course teaches, with a clear sense of which concept each one demonstrates best.

sections.heading: The Higher Level extension: two challenges, ten minutes each
paragraphs: Higher Level candidates present on two different global political challenges, each recorded and each held inside a time ceiling of around ten minutes. Confirm the current timing and format with your child's teacher. What makes this component distinctive is that it is assessed as analysis rather than as presentation skill: fluency helps, but the marks are for framing the challenge, applying concepts, weighing evidence and reaching a judgement that acknowledges other readings.

Three things go wrong, predictably. Students overrun, because they have prepared material rather than an argument, and the final judgement is delivered in a rush or not at all. Students choose two challenges that are really one, which halves the range of concepts they can demonstrate. And students describe the challenge for seven minutes before analysing it for three, which inverts the mark distribution.

Rehearsal to the clock is the whole remedy, and it has to be recorded. A student who is told they ran over does not quite believe it; a student who watches themselves spend four minutes on background does. We rehearse each presentation at least twice, review the recording against a structure the marks reward, and cut material rather than adding it. Choosing two genuinely different challenges is settled at the start, because discovering the overlap during rehearsal means starting one of them again.

Timing of the rehearsals themselves matters more than families expect. Rehearse too early and the student has nothing finished to rehearse; rehearse the night before recording and there is no time to act on what the review shows. The pattern that works is a first run roughly two weeks before the school's recording deadline, a cut-and-restructure session after it, and a final timed run a few days out. Scheduling that sequence is straightforward online and awkward in any arrangement that depends on somebody driving across the emirate at a fixed hour.

sections.heading: Contested material, academic balance and what a tutor will not do
paragraphs: Global Politics requires students to examine contested issues, and that requires care. The course is assessed on balanced analysis supported by evidence, which means a student is credited for understanding perspectives they do not hold and penalised for advocacy that ignores them. That standard is also the practical answer to a question Abu Dhabi parents sometimes ask: whether this subject requires their child to take positions in public. It does not. It requires them to analyse positions, which is a different activity and a more marketable skill.

Our tutors work to three rules in this subject. Keep to the course's concepts and the thematic studies the school teaches. Use published academic and policy sources, named, rather than commentary. Present perspectives rather than conclusions on contested political questions, and make the student argue their own case against a counterargument rather than inheriting the tutor's view. A tutor's job here is to strengthen the reasoning, not to supply the opinion.

The coursework boundary is the same as in every Diploma subject and worth stating plainly. A tutor may teach concepts, explain what the descriptors reward, challenge a weak criterion, discuss research, and comment on drafts the student has written. A tutor may not author any part of a submitted report, supply sentences to insert, script a presentation, or hand over finished work. Providers selling completed coursework are selling a malpractice risk that lands on the candidate. Official subject guides and papers are referenced and linked at source, never redistributed as downloads.
bullets: The course rewards balanced analysis, not advocacy

sections.heading: Permits, ADEK and the practical questions before you book
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs under a permit regime. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. u.ae states that it is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page describes application through its smart app, website and e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time and no fee listed.

u.ae also states that individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, so no figure appears on this page. Since the permit is free and processed in days, asking a prospective tutor whether they hold it is a reasonable question, and a reluctance to answer it is itself informative.

The emirate's school regulator is ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Gulf News has reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tuition of students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also prohibits serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school; verify the current wording on adek.gov.ae. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, operates no office in the UAE, and claims none of those things. Market rates for a Diploma subject specialist in this emirate, read from providers' own published pages in October 2026, run roughly AED 150 to AED 450 an hour online; our own terms are quoted after the free first lesson rather than published as a tariff.

faqs.question: Why does my well-read child score in the middle bands in Global Politics?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answers describe events instead of using concepts. The course is assessed on whether power, sovereignty, legitimacy, interdependence, human rights and development are used as analytical tools, so an accurate narrative with no concept named cannot reach the upper bands. The fix is structural rather than informational: define the concept in course terms, state the criterion being applied, weigh evidence against it, and take one counterargument seriously. Students who already read widely usually move fastest, because the examples they need are already in their heads.

faqs.question: What are the assessed components of IB Global Politics at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Higher Level candidates complete a source-based paper, an essay paper, the internally assessed engagement component, and an extension consisting of two recorded presentations on two different global political challenges. Standard Level candidates complete the first three. We do not publish weighting percentages on this page, because the IB has revised this subject's guide and the figures depend on which version your child's cohort is examined under. The Diploma coordinator holds the authoritative weightings, and asking which components are weakest is the more useful question anyway.

faqs.question: How do we choose an issue for the Global Politics engagement component?
faqs.answer: Choose one with a contested political question behind it, not merely a worthwhile activity. Volunteering at a food bank is engagement; it becomes assessable when the report examines how the service is funded, who is excluded from it, or which authority bears responsibility. That choice is an academic decision taken at the start, because research has to be able to speak to it. Students who pick the activity first and look for the politics afterwards usually end up describing what they did and compressing the analysis into the final page.

faqs.question: What is the Higher Level extension in Global Politics and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: Two recorded presentations on two different global political challenges, each inside a time ceiling of roughly ten minutes; confirm the current format with your child's teacher. The marks are for analysis rather than for presentation skill: framing the challenge, applying concepts, weighing evidence and reaching a judgement that acknowledges other readings. The three common losses are overrunning, choosing two challenges that are effectively one, and spending seven minutes on description before three on analysis. Recorded rehearsal to the clock fixes all three.

faqs.question: How should an Abu Dhabi student use local examples in Global Politics?
faqs.answer: Analytically, with named published sources. The emirate holds genuinely useful material: the International Renewable Energy Agency is headquartered in Masdar City and publishes policy documents, the Barakah plant sits inside a public international safeguards framework, and the country hosted COP28 in Dubai in 2023. Each illuminates a concept. The discipline is to examine what the case shows and to acknowledge readings that cut against the preferred one. A local case treated as advocacy loses the evaluation marks that make it worth using at all.

faqs.question: Does Global Politics require my child to take political positions publicly?
faqs.answer: No. The course requires students to analyse contested issues using evidence and to understand perspectives they do not hold. Credit is given for balanced analysis and withheld for advocacy that ignores alternatives, so the academic incentive points away from position-taking. Our tutors keep to the course's concepts and the school's thematic studies, use published academic and policy sources, and present perspectives rather than conclusions. The student argues their own case against a counterargument; a tutor strengthens the reasoning rather than supplying the view.

faqs.question: What does the last question on the Global Politics source paper require?
faqs.answer: The sources and the student's own knowledge, in one evaluative answer. Students lose about half the available credit by supplying only one of the two. Some write a comprehension exercise that never leaves the booklet; others, usually the well-read ones, write an essay that ignores it entirely. The structure that works is claim, evidence from a named source, evidence from own knowledge, an alternative reading, then a judgement. We practise that question first every week until it is automatic, and drill the earlier questions for brevity afterwards.

faqs.question: Is Global Politics taught in many Abu Dhabi schools?
faqs.answer: Fewer than offer History or Economics, and where it runs the classes are often small, sometimes three or four students. That has a specific consequence: a small class generates few marked exemplars, so students have no reference for how far an evaluation must go to reach the upper bands. External calibration matters more here than in a large cohort. Ask the individuals and societies department whether the subject runs this year and which thematic studies it covers, since both can change with staffing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Global Politics Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the boundary we state to the student in the first session. A tutor may challenge the research question, discuss the scholarship, explain what the criteria reward, and comment on drafts the student has written. A tutor may not author any portion of the text, supply sentences to insert, or hand over finished work; the school supervisor remains the formal supervisor. The subject-specific advice worth having early is to avoid questions about unfolding events, where the available literature is journalism and no settled analysis exists to engage with.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Global Politics tutor to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. There are no home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the format has two practical benefits: source booklets and student essays are annotated on a shared screen and saved, and Higher Level presentation rehearsals can be recorded and reviewed immediately, which is awkward to arrange in a living room and central to how that component improves.

faqs.question: What does a Global Politics tutor cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates read from providers' own published pages in October 2026 put a Diploma subject specialist at roughly AED 150 to AED 450 an hour online, with published in-home rates in the emirate running higher because they include travel. Those are other providers' figures, attributed and dated, not ours. Because this subject is taught in relatively few schools here, the constraint is more often availability of a genuine specialist than price. IB Gram quotes its own terms after the free first lesson rather than publishing a tariff.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Abu Dhabi need a MoHRE permit to teach Global Politics?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the permit covers private tuition generally rather than any particular subject. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a DP2 Global Politics student usually need?
faqs.answer: A common pattern is four sessions on the source paper's final question, weekly essay coaching through the mock period, engagement component supervision when the school's internal deadline approaches, and for Higher Level two or three recorded rehearsals per presentation. We prefer a fixed block with a stated end point to an open weekly booking. If marked work stops moving after a fair run, the right recommendation may be a different tutor or a different format, and we will make it.

faqs.question: Can presentation rehearsals and lessons shift around Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes. Slots are held rather than fixed, so they move to post-Iftar timings during Ramadan and around mock weeks and examination periods without the booking lapsing. For the Higher Level extension there is a scheduling point worth planning: rehearsal value decays if it happens too far ahead of the recording deadline, so we deliberately place the final rehearsal close to it, which is easier to arrange online than with any travelling arrangement.

faqs.question: Which subjects pair best with Global Politics for an Abu Dhabi student?
faqs.answer: History supplies the depth of example that essays need, Economics reinforces the development and interdependence material, and Geography overlaps on climate governance and global risks. English A trains the close reading the source paper rewards. The risks run in predictable directions: History-trained students give chronology where a conceptual judgement was wanted, Economics students reach for diagrams, and Geography students describe spatial patterns instead of analysing power. Naming the habit is usually enough to stop it.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-global-politics-tutor.closingBody: The quickest diagnosis in this subject comes from two short pieces of work: one paragraph of a recent essay and one attempt at the final question on a source paper. Together they show whether the loss is conceptual, evaluative or structural, and those three problems need different remedies. That is what the free 50-minute online lesson is built around, in one subject, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. You will leave with a written diagnosis, a plan naming the component each session targets, and the rate in AED. Lessons run online from any community in the emirate, held on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The Hindi B problem is a register problem with a paperwork solution
paragraphs: Hindi B sits in Group 2 of the Diploma as a language acquisition course, available at Standard and Higher Level, assessed by a written paper, a listening paper, a reading paper and an individual oral. Four assessments, no internal assessment, no coursework. Everything is produced in a handful of hours at the end of two years, which is why a family can feel confident all the way to a mock and then be surprised.

In Abu Dhabi the typical candidate is a student from an Indian-heritage family who speaks Hindi at home, switched to an English-medium curriculum years ago, and chose Hindi B as a sensible sixth subject. That student arrives with enormous spoken fluency and a narrow slice of the written language, and the gap between the two is not obvious to anyone until a marked script appears.

The reason is that Hindi exists on the page in a register the household rarely uses. Formal written Hindi draws heavily on Sanskritised vocabulary; everyday spoken Hindi in the Gulf is mixed with English and with Urdu-derived words and pronounced with regional habits. Both are legitimate Hindi. Only one of them is being marked. A student writing a report in the language they use with their grandmother has produced good communication and the wrong register.

The second cost is reading speed. The reading paper uses authentic texts, which in Hindi means newspaper prose, formal letters and public-information writing — exactly the varieties a student who speaks Hindi daily may never have read. Decoding Devanagari at speed is a trained skill, and a student decoding slowly runs out of time on questions they could have answered.

So this page is organised around evidence rather than reassurance, because in a language a parent may speak fluently and read rarely, instinct is unreliable in both directions. Each term produces a file: raw scores on a cold reading and listening paper, a marked written script with the criterion letter on it, a recorded oral, and the school's predicted grade. Three such files across the Diploma make a trend that nobody has to interpret generously.

Delivery in the UAE is online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi and does not send a tutor to an address in this emirate; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Handwritten Devanagari is still marked, by photograph and screen share, and the section on that below explains the mechanics rather than asserting it works.

Market rates are worth knowing before any quote arrives. Published comparisons put a qualified subject tutor working online in this market at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, in-home visits at around AED 180 to AED 350, and monthly online packages from about AED 799 for eight sessions. Hindi speakers are plentiful in Abu Dhabi, so quotes at the lower end are common; people who have marked IB Hindi B against its own criteria are considerably rarer, and that is the skill the hour is actually for.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-hindi-b-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Hindi B candidates in Abu Dhabi arrive from three distinct schooling histories, and each one produces a different shaped gap. These notes describe what each route leaves a student holding at the start of DP1.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects over two years with Hindi B available in Group 2 at Standard or Higher Level. Both levels sit a written paper, a listening paper, a reading paper and an individual oral; Higher Level adds two literary works, a longer written response and an oral built on a literary extract. The Group 2 grade counts towards the Diploma total like any other subject.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Hindi B groups are often small and sometimes combine levels, and in a few schools the course runs with a teacher whose main subject is something else. None of that is a scandal — it is what small cohorts produce — but it changes what outside support should do. Ask the DP coordinator whether SL and HL are taught separately and whether the HL works have been selected.

programmes.name: Transfers from CBSE or ICSE schooling
programmes.description: A student who studied Hindi as a second or third language to Class 10 under an Indian board brings real written foundations: Devanagari fluency, grammar taught explicitly, and exposure to formal registers. What they often lack is the IB's assessment logic — text types, prescribed themes, and an oral that rewards discussion rather than recitation.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a substantial Indian-curriculum school population alongside its IB and British schools, and transfers into DP1 from Indian boards are routine in this emirate. Those students are usually the strongest Hindi B candidates in the room and the ones most likely to underperform in the first term, because they are being assessed on a structure nobody has explained to them yet.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language Acquisition runs in phases, and Hindi is offered in some but not all Abu Dhabi continuum schools. A student finishing in Phase 4 or above moves into Hindi B comfortably. The characteristic MYP gap is accuracy under timed conditions, since MYP tasks reward communication and Hindi B rewards control inside a form.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Abu Dhabi school does not offer Hindi in MYP, students arrive in DP1 having had no formal Hindi instruction since primary school while speaking it daily at home. That profile needs written and reading work almost exclusively, and spending the first term on conversation practice with it is the most common way a year of tuition produces no grade movement.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-hindi-b-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Hindi B is usually one line on a longer tutoring request. Below are the subjects Abu Dhabi families most often pair with it and what each pairing actually asks for.

subjects.name: Hindi B
subjects.description: Written paper, listening paper, reading paper and individual oral, each a quarter of the grade. Marks leave through register slips into spoken Hindi, slow Devanagari decoding in the reading paper, missing text-type conventions, and at HL through summarising a literary extract instead of discussing it.

subjects.name: Hindi A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A Group 1 course for a student whose Hindi is a first language in the full sense: literary analysis, comparative study, examinations in Hindi. Rarely offered in Abu Dhabi, and the wrong destination for most household speakers, who read far less than they speak.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The usual Group 1 pairing here. The analytical structures transfer well to the Hindi B oral at HL, where the task is to argue rather than retell, and the register discipline transfers in the opposite direction more usefully than families expect.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Common in Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts. Its internal assessment lands in the same window as Hindi oral preparation in most schools, so the two need to be sequenced on a calendar in DP1 rather than negotiated in a panic in DP2.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The frequent Group 5 choice alongside a language. Students comfortable with AI often have strong procedural habits, which transfer directly to reading-paper technique: scan, locate, manipulate, move on rather than translate from the beginning.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Taken widely by Abu Dhabi students aiming at medicine and engineering. Chemistry rewards precise definition, which helps with Hindi vocabulary discipline and hurts in the oral, where a candidate waits to be certain before speaking and loses interaction marks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Bilingual students carry ready-made TOK examples: what is lost in translation, how a claim behaves differently in two languages, why a proverb resists rendering. Planting two such examples in DP1 saves a scramble for material before the exhibition.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: UAE private schools must teach Arabic alongside their licensed curriculum, so a Hindi B student in Abu Dhabi is formally studying two additional languages. Two non-Latin scripts in the same week is a real load, and separating the revision by a day improves retention in both.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: May be registered in Hindi B and written in Hindi. It suits a confident HL candidate and punishes a borderline one, since the essay consumes exactly the hours the language itself needed. An essay in English about Hindi literature is a different, and usually safer, proposition.

regions.name: Al Reef

regions.name: Mussafah and Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Mainland communities with a large Indian-curriculum school population nearby, so many students here arrive with CBSE Hindi behind them. That group needs assessment-structure work first and language work second.

modes.description: Two short sessions a week built around timed authentic texts: a news report, a public notice, a formal letter. sections.heading: Which quarter of the Hindi B grade is actually leaking
paragraphs: Hindi B produces four marks and no coursework: a written response, a listening score, a reading score and an oral. Each is a quarter of the total. The first job with any new family is not teaching — it is finding out which of the four is costing the grade, because the four respond to completely different work and the wrong diagnosis wastes a term.

Most schools can supply the component breakdown from a mock if asked directly, and most parents have never asked. A single percentage for Hindi hides the shape of the problem entirely. A candidate on 70 in writing and 38 in reading has a reading problem that looks like a Hindi problem, and no amount of grammar work will shift it.

The household-speaker profile has a signature. Oral marks are usually the strongest, listening is adequate, writing is middling, and reading is the lowest of the four, often by a wide margin. The CBSE-transfer profile is almost the inverse: strong writing and reading, weaker oral interaction, and listening that drops on unfamiliar accents. Those two profiles need opposite plans, and they are frequently sitting next to each other in the same Abu Dhabi classroom.

Once the leak is located, the first fix is nearly always narrower than families expect. Reading responds to timed practice on authentic texts and to explicit unknown-word tolerance. Writing responds to register work and text-type conventions. Oral interaction responds to recorded conversation on unseen material. Listening responds to volume of exposure. Each has a measurable before-and-after, which is what makes the plan auditable.

sections.heading: Two Hindis in one household: the register the examiner is reading
paragraphs: The single most useful thing an Abu Dhabi family can understand about this course is that the Hindi spoken in the car and the Hindi printed in a newspaper are different registers with different vocabularies. Formal written Hindi leans on Sanskrit-derived words; conversational Gulf Hindi mixes in English freely and uses a great many Urdu-derived words that are entirely natural in speech and out of place in a formal report.

This is not a judgement about correctness. Both registers are real Hindi and the spoken one is more widely used. It is a statement about what is being assessed. A candidate who writes a formal letter using the vocabulary of family conversation has communicated successfully and has not demonstrated the range the mark scheme is looking for, and will be marked accordingly.

The work is therefore additive rather than corrective. Nobody needs to stop speaking the Hindi they speak. The student builds a formal-register bank — the written forms, the compound verbs, the connectives that signal formal argument — and learns to switch into it deliberately for Paper 1 and out of it for the oral, where a natural spoken register is appropriate. Switching is the skill; purity is not the goal.

There is one more layer that catches students out: Devanagari conventions that never arise in speech. Nasalisation marks, the correct forms of borrowed sounds, and the matra errors that a fluent speaker makes precisely because they are writing what they hear. These are quick to fix once counted, and counting them per hundred words is how a parent sees the trend rather than taking it on trust.

sections.heading: The reading paper is where household speakers lose most
paragraphs: The reading component uses authentic Hindi texts, which means they were written for Hindi readers and not for learners. Newspaper prose, public-information writing, formal correspondence. They contain words the candidate has never met and sentence structures the spoken language does not use, and the task is not to understand everything but to locate and manipulate specific information under time.

A student who speaks Hindi daily and reads it rarely approaches this paper the only way they know: start at the beginning, understand each sentence, then answer. Under timed conditions that strategy fails twice over. It consumes the clock on the first text and it leaves the easy marks on the last text unattempted. The student concludes that their Hindi is weak when their procedure is wrong.

The replacement procedure is explicit and takes about four sessions to install. Read the questions first. Scan for the locating words. Accept that a proportion of the vocabulary will be unknown and answer around it. Answer in the order of difficulty rather than the order on the paper. Then, and only then, go back for the harder inference questions with whatever time remains.

Measurement here is unusually clean, which makes it ideal for a progress file. Take a cold paper, record the raw score and the seconds per question. Install the procedure. Take a comparable paper four weeks later under identical conditions. The two numbers either moved or they did not, and nobody has to form an opinion about whether the sessions felt productive.

sections.heading: The progress file: what a term of Hindi B evidence looks like
paragraphs: A progress file is four pieces of paper per term, and it exists because a parent cannot judge a Hindi script by looking at it, even a parent who speaks Hindi fluently. Reading formal Devanagari prose for register and accuracy is a trained activity, and most households do not contain someone who does it professionally. The file substitutes documentation for instinct.

What goes in it: the raw score and timing from a cold reading paper, the raw score from a full listening paper, one marked written script with the criterion letter and the error classes named, and a recorded oral attempt on unseen material. Plus the school's current predicted grade, written down with the date, because predictions move and nobody remembers what they were in October.

The comparison is the point. The same four measurements, under the same conditions, three times across the Diploma: early DP1, end of DP1, and midway through DP2 before the oral window. Three data points make a line. One data point makes an argument, and two make a coincidence. A tutor recommending a second year of weekly sessions should be able to show you the line.

The file also exposes the uncomfortable cases honestly. A student whose reading score has climbed twenty raw marks while their predicted grade has not moved is telling you something useful: either the prediction lags the evidence, which is a conversation with the school, or the gains are in a component the school weights differently. Both are better than a shrug, and neither is visible without the paperwork.

sections.heading: Handwritten Devanagari in an online lesson: how it is actually marked
paragraphs: The fair objection to online delivery in this subject is specific and worth answering properly: Hindi B written work is handwritten in Devanagari, and a tutor on a screen cannot look over a student's shoulder at a page. Families raise it constantly and the dismissive answer — that technology solves everything — deserves the scepticism it gets.

What actually happens is unglamorous and works. The student writes on paper under time, exactly as in the examination, then photographs the page and drops it into the shared folder. The tutor marks the image, writes the criterion letter and the error class on it, and returns it. In the next session the marked page is on screen for both of them, scrolled and annotated live. The artefact is better than what a kitchen-table lesson produces, because it is dated, stored and comparable.

For the mechanical side of handwriting — matra placement, letter formation, spacing — a phone propped above the page gives a live view of the hand while writing, which is the one thing a screen share cannot do on its own. That is a five-dirham piece of equipment and a two-minute setup, and it is used in the sessions where formation genuinely matters rather than in every session.

The honest limitation is speed under pressure. A tutor cannot feel a student's writing slow down in real time the way a teacher walking the room can. The substitute is measurement: timed pieces inside the examination word range, with the time taken recorded, so the trend in writing speed is visible even though the sensation of it is not. Most families find they trade an impression for a number, which in this subject is a good trade.

sections.heading: Home tutoring in Abu Dhabi, and what the online comparison really buys
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a large and busy market in this emirate, and for Hindi it is unusually well supplied, because Abu Dhabi has a substantial Hindi-speaking population. A tutor arrives at a villa in Khalifa City or an apartment in Al Nahyan and teaches for an hour. Published market comparisons put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, and online qualified subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to AED 300. Those are market figures from published rate tables rather than IB Gram prices.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE. We do not send a tutor to an Abu Dhabi address and we do not run home visits in Abu Dhabi; that is a service we offer only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one online, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. Stating it directly is more useful than letting a family assume otherwise through a first phone call.

The distinction that matters for Hindi B is not availability of Hindi speakers, which is plentiful, but availability of people who have marked IB Hindi B against its criteria. Speaking Hindi fluently and knowing where a Paper 1 response loses a register mark are unrelated skills, and the second is rare in any single emirate. Online, the pool is everyone with that skill who is free at your hour.

The second thing it buys is the file. Marked images, recorded orals, logged raw scores, all in one folder that both sides can open two years later. An in-home arrangement leaves a notebook and goodwill. For a subject where the parent often cannot assess the work directly, documentation is not bureaucracy; it is the only way to know whether the money is doing anything.

sections.heading: Hindi, Arabic and the UAE's mandatory subjects in one school week
paragraphs: A Hindi B candidate in Abu Dhabi is rarely studying one additional language. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, which means Arabic sits on the timetable alongside the licensed international curriculum. For most Hindi B students that is two non-Latin scripts and two sets of unfamiliar vocabulary in the same week.

ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and is the authority whose published listings should be read on any school question. What ADEK does not do is relieve the timetable pressure, and the pressure is real: a student revising Arabic vocabulary and Hindi vocabulary in the same evening retains measurably less of both than one who separates them by a day.

The practical sequencing advice is dull and effective. Put the two languages on different days. Keep Hindi reading practice short and frequent rather than long and occasional, because decoding speed responds to frequency. Where Arabic assessments cluster, drop Hindi to maintenance for that fortnight rather than running both at full intensity and doing neither well.

One misconception worth closing: a Hindi B grade does not substitute for the Arabic requirement, and Arabic study does not help the Hindi grade. They are separate obligations with separate assessments. Families occasionally hope that a strong Hindi result will offset a weak Arabic report, and schools do not treat them that way, because they answer to different requirements.

sections.heading: What the numbers cannot show, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: A page built on evidence should be honest about the limits of its own evidence. Raw scores on a cold paper are reliable; predicted grades are not, because they are produced by a teacher balancing a dozen considerations and they move for reasons that have nothing to do with a student's Hindi. A progress file tells you about skills. It does not forecast a May result, and nobody who claims otherwise is reading their own data.

Mock papers are also imperfect instruments. Different schools in this emirate use different past papers, mark them with different leniency, and sit them under different conditions. A mock score that rises after a school changes paper source has not necessarily measured anything. That is why the file uses the same paper format under the same conditions rather than whatever the school happened to set.

We make no claim about grade outcomes, no guarantee of improvement, and no promise about a specific score. What we will say is what the work consists of, what it is measured by, and what the measurements have done so far for the student in front of us. Any tutor offering a particular grade for a particular number of hours is selling something the IB does not sell.

The same honesty applies to assessed work. A tutor may teach register, model formal Hindi on a different topic, mark a student's own draft against criterion letters and test whether a correction held. A tutor may not write, rewrite or translate a piece that will be submitted. Under IB academic honesty rules the consequence of crossing that line falls on the candidate, which is exactly why the line is published here rather than left to be negotiated at a deadline.
