process.title: Ask the school for the component breakdown
process.description: Before booking anything, request the four component scores from the most recent mock rather than the overall Hindi grade. That single document decides whether the work is reading, register, listening or interaction, and families who skip it usually buy a term of the wrong thing.

process.title: Free trial lesson that produces numbers
process.description: The trial runs a cold timed reading text and a short written piece rather than a conversation in Hindi, which a household speaker will always pass. It is free, needs no card, carries no obligation, and you keep the raw scores and the marked script either way.

process.title: A written plan with a measurement date in it
process.description: You receive the ranked leak, the recommended session pattern, and the date of the next measurement, in writing. If the honest answer is four reading sessions rather than two years of weekly hours, the plan says four reading sessions.

process.title: Sessions that leave artefacts
process.description: Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Written work is photographed, marked with criterion letters and stored dated in a shared folder; orals are recorded. Each session note records the cold-test result and the task set.

process.title: Termly file, then a decision
process.description: At the end of each term the four measurements are retaken under the same conditions and compared with the baseline. Continuing, changing approach or stopping is decided from those numbers, and the file belongs to you whether or not the sessions continue.

whyPoints.title: Register taught as an addition, not a correction
whyPoints.description: Nobody is told their household Hindi is wrong. The student builds the formal written register alongside it and learns to switch deliberately, because switching is the assessed skill and purity is not the goal in any component.

whyPoints.title: Reading treated as the main event
whyPoints.description: For household speakers the reading paper is usually the lowest of the four scores and the cheapest to move. Timed authentic texts, an explicit procedure, and seconds-per-question logged, instead of general comprehension practice that never gets timed.

whyPoints.title: Devanagari marked, not waved at
whyPoints.description: Written work is handwritten under time, photographed and returned annotated with criterion letters and error classes. Where letter formation matters, a phone above the page gives a live view of the hand. The mechanics are described because they are the fair objection to online delivery.

whyPoints.title: A file you can audit without reading Hindi
whyPoints.description: Raw scores, timings, error counts per hundred words and dated recordings. Three measurement points across the Diploma produce a line rather than an impression, which is the only basis on which a second year of hours should be bought.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, stated before booking
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson runs over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an Abu Dhabi address and does not run home visits in this emirate; in-home tuition is an India-only service.

whyPoints.title: Claims kept to what the data supports
whyPoints.description: No promised grades, no pledged improvement, no statistics without a method behind them. We will tell you what moved, by how much, under what conditions, and where the measurement is unreliable.

faqs.question: My child speaks Hindi at home. Why is the Hindi B reading score the lowest of the four?
faqs.answer: Because speaking and reading Hindi are different skills, and the reading paper uses authentic texts written for Hindi readers: newspaper prose, notices, formal correspondence. A student who speaks daily and reads rarely decodes Devanagari slowly, starts at the first sentence, tries to understand everything and runs out of time. Ask the school for the raw reading score rather than the overall grade. The fix is procedural and takes about four sessions: questions first, scan for locating words, answer around unknown vocabulary, easiest questions first.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hindi we speak and the Hindi in the exam?
faqs.answer: Register. Formal written Hindi draws on Sanskrit-derived vocabulary and sentence structures that spoken Hindi rarely uses, while everyday Gulf Hindi mixes in English and Urdu-derived words naturally. Both are real Hindi; only the formal register is expected in the written paper. The work is additive rather than corrective: the student builds a formal word bank from authentic texts and learns to switch into it for writing and out of it for the oral, where a natural spoken register is entirely appropriate.

faqs.question: How can handwritten Devanagari be marked in an online lesson?
faqs.answer: The student writes on paper under timed conditions exactly as in the examination, photographs the page and uploads it to a shared folder. The tutor annotates the image with the criterion letter and the error class and returns it, and the marked page is on screen for both of them in the next session. Where letter formation or matra placement matters, a phone propped above the page gives a live view of the hand. The result is a dated, comparable artefact rather than a correction in a notebook.

faqs.question: Which component breakdown should I ask my child's school for?
faqs.answer: The four separate component results from the most recent mock: written response, listening, reading and individual oral, as raw scores rather than percentages. One overall Hindi grade hides the shape of the problem completely. A candidate scoring well in writing and poorly in reading needs a different term of work from one with the opposite profile, and the two profiles often sit in the same classroom. Most schools provide the breakdown when asked directly in writing after a parents' evening.

faqs.question: My son studied Hindi under CBSE until Class 10. Where does that leave him in Hindi B?
faqs.answer: Usually in a strong position with one specific gap. Indian-board Hindi gives real written foundations: Devanagari fluency, explicit grammar, exposure to formal registers. What it does not give is the IB's assessment logic — named text types, five prescribed themes, and an oral that rewards sustained discussion rather than prepared recitation. Those students often underperform in the first DP1 term for structural reasons and then move quickly. Bring a marked Indian-board script to the first session; it saves a diagnostic hour.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Hindi B worth taking for a household speaker?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the decision should be made on a timed script rather than on spoken fluency. Higher Level adds two literary works, a longer written response, and an oral built on a literary extract instead of an image, which means reading demand rises sharply. A student whose reading score is the weakest of their four components will find HL expensive in hours. Take a cold reading paper and a timed written piece at the end of DP1, then decide with the DP coordinator on that evidence.

faqs.question: Does a Hindi B grade satisfy the Arabic requirement in a UAE school?
faqs.answer: No. They are separate obligations. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum and must follow the Ministry's general regulations, and a Group 2 Diploma subject does not substitute for that. Schools do not trade one against the other because they answer to different requirements. The practical consequence is timetable load: two non-Latin scripts in one week, which is why we suggest separating Hindi and Arabic revision by a day rather than stacking them.

faqs.question: How quickly should we expect a Hindi B reading score to move?
faqs.answer: Decoding speed and raw score typically respond within four to six weeks of twice-weekly timed practice, provided the practice is timed and cold rather than comfortable. The honest way to know is to take a paper under fixed conditions, record the raw score and the seconds per question, install the procedure, and retake a comparable paper a month later. If the two numbers have not moved, the method changes rather than the hours increasing. Nobody should promise a particular grade from a particular number of sessions.

faqs.question: Can a Hindi B tutor help with an oral that is recorded at school?
faqs.answer: With preparation, yes; with the assessment itself, no. Sessions rehearse on unseen material — a visual stimulus at Standard Level, a literary extract at Higher Level — with the conversation half drilled before the presentation half, because that is the order in which marks are lost. Rehearsals are recorded so hesitation and accuracy drops can be counted rather than described. What a tutor cannot do is coach during the assessed oral or supply a script to be delivered, which would make the performance not the candidate's own.

faqs.question: What does Hindi tuition cost in the Abu Dhabi market?
faqs.answer: Published comparisons put qualified subject tutors working online at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour in this market and in-home visits at around AED 180 to AED 350, with monthly online packages advertised from about AED 799 for eight sessions. Those are market figures from published rate tables, not IB Gram prices. Hindi speakers are plentiful here, so rates at the lower end are common; people who have marked IB Hindi B against its criteria are much rarer, and that is the skill worth paying for.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Hindi tutor to our apartment in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE, and no tutor is sent to an apartment, villa or compound here; in-home tutoring is offered only in India. Hindi B lessons for Abu Dhabi families are one-to-one online, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain is that written work is marked as a stored, dated artefact and orals are recorded, which an in-home lesson at the kitchen table does not produce.

faqs.question: We travel to India for six weeks each summer. Does that break the plan?
faqs.answer: Only if the sessions stop. Lessons run over live video, so the schedule is rebased to Indian Standard Time and continues, and a summer in a Hindi-reading environment is genuinely useful if it is used: newspapers, signage, public notices, with a timed text twice a week. What does damage is a six-week silence, which shows up immediately in the next reading timing. Tell us the dates a week ahead and the slot moves rather than pausing.

faqs.question: Will an outside Hindi tutor annoy my child's school?
faqs.answer: In our experience, rarely, provided the tutor stays in their lane. Teachers object to outside help that contradicts their teaching, supplies work, or arrives with claims about the school. They generally welcome a tutor who marks the student's own practice against criterion letters and sends nothing to the school at all. If you want to tell the teacher, the useful framing is the component you are working on and the measurement you are using, which is information rather than a complaint.

faqs.question: Can the tutor write the formal letter for Paper 1 practice if my daughter is stuck?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may model a formal letter on a completely different topic, teach the conventions, mark your daughter's own attempt against criterion letters, explain why a phrase costs a register mark and test whether the correction held weeks later. Supplying the text, rewriting her paragraphs into better Hindi or translating from English is producing work that is not hers, and under IB academic honesty rules the consequence lands on the candidate. We decline those requests, including close to a deadline.

faqs.question: How many Hindi B sessions a week do Abu Dhabi families usually book?
faqs.answer: Two short contacts rather than one long session, for reading at least, because Devanagari decoding speed responds to frequency more than to duration. A common pattern is two 45-minute slots in DP1 — one reading sprint and one register and writing session — moving to a single 60-minute oral-focused session in DP2 once written accuracy is stable. Families in the mainland communities with long bus commutes often prefer one weekday contact plus a weekend block for full timed papers.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-hindi-b-home-tutor.closingHeading: Get the component scores first, then decide what to buy
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-hindi-b-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking at an IB DP Hindi B home tutor in Abu Dhabi, ask the school for the four component results from the last mock before you book anything. With those numbers in hand, the free trial lesson takes forty minutes, needs no card, carries no obligation, and produces the rest of the baseline: a cold reading score with timings, a marked written piece with criterion letters, and a recorded oral on unseen material. You keep the file either way. From there the work is narrow, measured and auditable, and lessons run online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-hindi-b-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Hindi as an IB Diploma language B subject: prescribed themes, text types, the listening and reading papers, and the individual oral at both levels. Each works in Hindi during the lesson and switches to English only to explain a marking criterion.

intro.heading: Hindi B is a language exam, not a language test
paragraphs: Most Abu Dhabi families who look for Hindi B help are not worried about whether their child can speak Hindi. They are worried about a 4 or a 5 appearing on a report for a subject the child uses at the dinner table every evening. That gap is the whole subject in miniature. Hindi B does not measure how well a student converses. It measures whether they can produce a specified text type, on a prescribed theme, in a register the task demands, and whether they can show conceptual understanding of audience, context, purpose and meaning while doing it.

The four assessed components pull in different directions. Paper 1 asks for one piece of writing chosen from three options, each tied to a named text type: a blog entry, a formal letter, a speech, a set of guidelines, a report, a diary extract. A student who writes beautifully fluent Hindi and ignores the conventions of the chosen text type loses marks under the message criterion no matter how natural the language sounds. Paper 2 splits into listening and reading, both answered in Hindi, both sitting at the same weighting as the writing paper combined. The individual oral is recorded at school and marked internally before moderation.

Script is the second recurring surprise. Spoken Hindi at home is frequently a mixed register, and many students in Abu Dhabi read Devanagari slowly because their day runs in English at school and in English or Arabic outside it. Paper 1 is handwritten. Paper 2 reading passages are set in Devanagari with no transliteration. A student who decodes the script at half speed runs out of time on a paper that is not actually hard, and the mark drop reads like a comprehension problem when it is a fluency-of-reading problem.

At HL the course adds two literary works read in Hindi, and the individual oral changes shape completely: instead of responding to a visual stimulus tied to one of the five themes, the student analyses an extract from one of those works. That is a different skill, closer to literary comment than to description, and it is the single component where HL students most often underperform relative to their classwork. Schools in Abu Dhabi that run Hindi B usually have one teacher covering SL and HL together, which leaves the HL extract work thin.

What a tutor can realistically change in a term is narrow and specific: text-type conventions committed to memory, a bank of theme-linked vocabulary that is actually deployed rather than recognised, timed reading under Devanagari pressure, and an oral that is structured instead of improvised. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because the pool of people who can mark a Hindi B oral against the criteria is tiny and scattering it by postcode would not help an Abu Dhabi family at all.

The individual oral carries the remaining 25% and is marked by the school, then moderated

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-hindi-b-tutor.programmesIntro: Hindi appears at more than one point in the IB continuum, and Abu Dhabi schools place it differently depending on when a family arrived in the emirate. These are the programmes a Hindi-speaking student passes through and what each one actually does with the language.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two years where Hindi becomes an examined subject with a published assessment model. Students take it as language B at SL or HL in Group 2, or as language A: language and literature in Group 1 if the school supports that route. The Group 2 choice is normally locked in during the Year 11 options process, and changing it after the first term of DP1 is difficult because the themes are taught in sequence.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi DP cohorts are small by Dubai standards, so a school may run Hindi B for a handful of students across both levels in one timetabled block. Families in Khalifa City and Mohammed Bin Zayed City often find the subject is offered but thinly staffed, which is why online one-to-one support for the HL extract work and the oral is the most common request we see from this emirate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Hindi sits in the MYP language acquisition strand, taught in phases rather than levels. Phase placement, not year group, decides what a student is assessed on, and the four MYP criteria are listening, reading, speaking and writing in equal weight. The phase a student exits MYP in is the best single predictor of whether Hindi B SL or HL is the right DP entry point.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi IB continuum schools assess MYP Hindi internally without an eAssessment entry, so there is no external mark to compare against. That makes the DP1 diagnostic the first honest measurement a family gets, and it frequently arrives a year later than it should. A phase 4 exit with weak writing is a warning for HL, not a recommendation.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Hindi in the PYP is an additional-language strand with no external assessment and considerable variation between schools. Some run it as a daily lesson with reading in Devanagari from Year 2; others treat it as a weekly cultural session with transliterated text. The difference compounds for a decade and shows up in DP1 as a reading-speed gap rather than a vocabulary gap.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi primary provision for Hindi is uneven across the emirate, and a family moving from an Indian-curriculum school in Mussafah to an IB continuum school on Saadiyat Island will usually find the script expectation drops rather than rises. Keeping Devanagari reading alive through the PYP years is the cheapest intervention available to a Hindi-speaking household here.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines DP courses with a career-related study and a language development component. A student on the CP may study Hindi as part of language development without sitting the Language B examinations, which changes the assessment picture entirely: there is a portfolio rather than a paper, and the grade descriptors are not the Language B criteria.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in Abu Dhabi is limited to a small number of licensed schools, and the language development strand is the part families understand least. If your child is on the CP and someone has offered you Hindi B exam coaching, check with the DP coordinator first which assessment route is actually registered, because the two require different preparation.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-hindi-b-tutor.subjectsIntro: A Hindi-speaking student in an Abu Dhabi DP cohort has more Group 1 and Group 2 options than the options booklet usually makes clear. These are the routes that come up in the conversation, with what each one assesses.

subjects.name: Hindi B
subjects.description: Language acquisition for students with prior experience of Hindi. Four components: Paper 1 productive writing, Paper 2 listening, Paper 2 reading, and the individual oral. HL adds two literary works and shifts the oral to an extract-based analysis. The commonest mark loss sits in text-type convention, not grammar.

subjects.name: Hindi A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A Group 1 course for students operating in Hindi at near-native written level. Assessment moves to Paper 1 guided textual analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral on a global issue, and at HL a separate HL essay. Far more reading, and no credit for simply being a fluent speaker.

subjects.name: Hindi A: Literature, school-supported self-taught
subjects.description: Where a school cannot staff Hindi A, a student may take literature at SL as a self-taught candidate with a supervising coordinator. It demands independent reading of the prescribed works and a learner portfolio. Abu Dhabi schools use this route occasionally and it needs disciplined external support to work.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Some Hindi-speaking students take Arabic as their Group 2 language instead, usually because the school teaches it well and Hindi thinly. The assessment model mirrors Hindi B exactly, so the component skills transfer even though the vocabulary does not.

subjects.name: Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: A beginners' Group 2 course with its own narrower syllabus and a lower ceiling in terms of expected range. Not a soft option: the prescribed themes are the same five, and the writing task still demands text-type accuracy within a restricted lexicon.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Group 1 subject almost every Abu Dhabi DP student takes alongside Hindi B. Paper 1 is unseen non-literary analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works. Students who handle English A Paper 1 well usually have the analytical habit the Hindi B HL oral needs.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: The other widely staffed Group 2 option in the emirate. Same four-component model as Hindi B. Families sometimes switch here when the school's Hindi provision is a single shared block, trading cultural familiarity for a better-resourced classroom.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: Growing in Abu Dhabi DP timetables. The assessment structure is identical to Hindi B, which makes it a useful comparison when a family is weighing whether their child's problem is Hindi specifically or the Language B model generally.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Included here because the Group 2 decision is rarely made in isolation. A student carrying Maths AA HL has limited revision capacity for a second HL, which is often the strongest practical argument for taking Hindi B at SL rather than HL.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK overlaps with Hindi B more than students expect: the optional theme knowledge and language asks exactly the questions a bilingual Abu Dhabi student lives with. Material developed for the Hindi B conceptual understanding criterion often doubles as TOK exhibition thinking.

sections.heading: What a Hindi B search in Abu Dhabi is usually trying to fix
paragraphs: Parents searching for an IB DP Hindi B tutor in Abu Dhabi almost never describe a language problem. They describe a mark that does not match the child. The report says 4; the child negotiates in Hindi with grandparents on video calls every Sunday. Both are accurate, because the examination is not testing the thing the family can see.

Three specific mismatches account for most of it. The first is register: a student who speaks a comfortable mixed Hindi-English register at home writes it into a formal letter, and the message criterion drops. The second is text type: the Paper 1 options each name a text type and the conventions are assessable, so a speech without a salutation or a blog without a reader address loses marks that have nothing to do with linguistic range. The third is reading speed in Devanagari, which decides whether Paper 2 reading is a comprehension exercise or a race.

The fourth, less common but more damaging, is a wrong level. A fluent speaker is pushed into HL on the strength of conversation, then meets two literary works and an extract-based oral with no literary training. HL Hindi B is a reading course as much as a speaking one, and that is not obvious from the course title.

A useful first session therefore does not teach anything. It diagnoses: one timed Paper 1 under handwriting conditions, one reading passage against the clock, and five minutes of unprepared oral against a stimulus. Those three measurements tell you which of the four problems you actually have, and they stop a family paying for the wrong intervention for a term.

sections.heading: Hindi B at SL and HL: the four components and what each is worth
paragraphs: The Language B assessment model is identical in structure at SL and HL, and different in scale. The same four components, the same weightings, longer texts and an extra literary requirement at the higher level. Knowing the weightings changes how a family spends tutoring money: the listening and reading papers together are half the grade, and they are the two components schools timetable least.

Paper 1 gives three tasks and the student picks one. Each task names its audience, its purpose and its text type. The word count rises from 250-400 at SL to 450-600 at HL, which sounds modest until you remember it is handwritten in Devanagari under time pressure. Paper 2 is sat as one examination in two parts: a listening section with recorded passages played twice, and a reading section with written passages, both answered in Hindi.

The individual oral is recorded at school, marked by the teacher and sent for moderation. At SL the student speaks about a visual stimulus connected to one of the prescribed themes, then holds a discussion. At HL the stimulus is replaced by an extract from one of the two literary works studied, and the expectation shifts towards analysis of what the writer does rather than description of what is shown.

Durations and timings below follow the current Language B model. Confirm the exact figures for your child's session with the school's DP coordinator, since the IB publishes the authoritative detail in the subject guide and the examination instructions rather than on any third-party page.

sections.heading: Where Hindi B marks are actually lost
paragraphs: The Language B criteria are the diagnostic tool, not the grade descriptors. Written and oral work is judged on language, on message, and on conceptual understanding. Most Abu Dhabi students who underperform are strong on the first and weak on the other two, which is the opposite of what a parent expects when the child is a confident speaker.

Message losses are structural. The task asked for a report and received an essay. The task named a school magazine readership and the response addressed nobody. The task required two points of view and the student gave one at length. None of those are language errors, and no amount of vocabulary work fixes them. They are fixed by memorising text-type conventions and by planning for ninety seconds before writing.

Conceptual understanding is the criterion students have never had explained to them. It rewards a response that visibly understands its audience, context, purpose, meaning and variation in register. A formal letter that opens with a casual greeting signals a failure of conceptual understanding even if every word is spelled correctly. In the oral it shows up as a student describing a photograph instead of connecting it to the theme it was chosen to illustrate.

On the receptive side, the losses are mechanical. Listening answers written in English score nothing. Reading answers lifted verbatim as a whole paragraph when the question wanted a phrase score nothing. Running out of time on the last reading passage costs more than any single grammatical weakness, and timing is the easiest thing on this list to fix in four sessions.

sections.heading: Hindi B, Hindi A or a different Group 2 language?
paragraphs: The level and route decision is worth more than a term of tutoring and is usually made in twenty minutes during a Year 11 options evening. In Abu Dhabi it is complicated by provision: a school may offer Hindi B but not Hindi A, or offer Hindi A only through the school-supported self-taught literature route, which is a serious undertaking for a teenager.

The honest test for Hindi A is written, not spoken. Can the student read a page of unseen literary Hindi prose and say something about how it is constructed? If not, Hindi A will be an uphill two years regardless of how fluent their speech is. The honest test for Hindi B HL rather than SL is similar: can they tolerate reading two full literary works in Hindi and comment on an extract without the book in front of them?

There is also the diploma-level question of total HL load. A student taking Maths AA HL, Chemistry HL and Hindi B HL has three content-heavy higher levels and an Extended Essay to write, which in practice means the Hindi HL literary reading gets dropped first. Taking Hindi B at SL and spending the recovered hours on the sciences is frequently the better diploma decision even when the child could pass HL.

Switching Group 2 language entirely is the least-discussed option. A student with weak Devanagari reading but strong analytical habits sometimes does better in a well-staffed French or Spanish B class than in a thinly staffed Hindi block, because the assessment model is identical and the teaching time is not.

sections.heading: The five prescribed themes and what Abu Dhabi students bring to them
paragraphs: Every Language B course covers five prescribed themes: identity, experiences, human ingenuity, social organisation, and sharing the planet. The themes are not topics to be memorised. They are the frames the Paper 1 tasks and the SL oral stimuli are built on, so a student who has a bank of theme-linked vocabulary and two concrete examples per theme walks into the examination with half the thinking already done.

Abu Dhabi students arrive with an unusually strong hand on some of these and an unusually weak one on others. Identity and experiences are rich: migration between India and the Gulf, multilingual households, schooling in a third language, summers in one country and winters in another. Students write well on these because they have something to say, and the vocabulary follows the content.

Social organisation and sharing the planet are where the vocabulary gap bites. A student can discuss water scarcity, desalination, construction labour, public transport or waste in English and in Arabic classroom terms, but has never had to do it in Hindi. The content knowledge is there and the lexicon is missing, which is a fast problem to fix with targeted vocabulary work and slow to fix by general conversation practice.

Human ingenuity is the theme most often left until last and most often examined. It covers technology, communication, innovation, entertainment and the arts, and it is the theme where a student with a strong Design or Computer Science background can do something genuinely interesting if they have the Hindi to carry it. Building two prepared examples per theme, in Hindi, with the vocabulary written down, is the single most efficient piece of homework in this subject.
bullets: Identity: family, language, migration, belonging, self-image
Experiences: travel, education, rites of passage, life stories
Human ingenuity: technology, communication, innovation, the arts

Sharing the planet: environment, resources, equality, shared challenges

sections.heading: What language tutoring costs in Abu Dhabi, and why online changes the maths
paragraphs: Published tutoring rates in the UAE sit in wide bands, and almost no competing page puts an AED figure on the record at all. The table below collects what agencies, platforms and independent tutors serving this market advertise, surveyed in October 2026, alongside the rate bands published in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimate. These are market rates. They are not IB Gram's price list, and any figure quoted to you should come with the session length it refers to.

A minority language changes the economics. For Maths or Physics, an Abu Dhabi family choosing between online and an in-home tutor is choosing between a wide pool and a narrower local one. For Hindi B, the local pool of people who can mark an oral against the Language B criteria and explain the conceptual understanding descriptor is small enough that geography stops being a sensible filter. The in-home premium in the table buys travel, not expertise.

There is a second, quieter cost. An in-home language tutor who is a fluent Hindi speaker but not a Language B teacher will deliver pleasant conversation lessons that improve nothing measurable, because the marks are not lost in conversation. That is the most expensive outcome available in this subject: a year of lessons at a reasonable hourly rate that moves the grade not at all.

IB Gram delivers Hindi B as one-to-one online tuition over live video to families across Abu Dhabi. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Rather than quote a figure here, we match the subject and level first and discuss the plan on a consultation, with one free trial lesson per subject and no card details taken beforehand.

sections.heading: Hindi B alongside Arabic: the subject load nobody budgets for
paragraphs: A Hindi-speaking student in an Abu Dhabi private school is rarely studying one additional language. Federal rules require private schools to teach Arabic, Islamic education and social studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to deliver, and the emirate regulators enforce that requirement alongside the school's own programme. For a DP student that means Hindi B in Group 2 and Arabic as a mandatory subject sitting outside the diploma.

The Dubai regulator's published guidance on mandatory subjects, which is the most detailed public document on how this works in the UAE, is explicit on two points worth knowing even outside Dubai: separate classes must be organised for Arabic first-language and non-Arab groups, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit with a recommendation that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes.

In Abu Dhabi, ADEK licenses and inspects the emirate's private schools and publishes its own inspection ratings, and the federal baseline on Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies applies here as it does across the country. The practical effect on a DP timetable is that a student may be carrying two non-examined language commitments plus an examined Group 2 subject, and the examined one is the one that appears on the diploma.

This matters for how a family schedules tutoring. Loading a second weekly Hindi session onto a week that already contains mandatory Arabic, two HL sciences and an Extended Essay deadline tends to produce attendance problems rather than progress. One well-used weekly session with marked written work between lessons outperforms two sessions that get cancelled.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a language subject: what a Hindi B tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: Language subjects attract a particular kind of malpractice, because the assessed products look like things an adult could simply supply. A tutor can draft a flawless Paper 1 response. A tutor can script an oral so tightly that the student recites it. Both breach IB academic-honesty rules, and the consequence lands on the student, not on the tutor.

The boundary is clear in practice. A tutor may teach text-type conventions, model a response that is then discarded, mark the student's own writing against the criteria, explain why a sentence misses the register, drill vocabulary, run timed practice, and rehearse the oral by asking unprepared discussion questions. A tutor may not supply sentences to be reproduced in an assessed task, may not prepare a script for the individual oral, and may not correct a draft that is about to be submitted as an assessed piece.

The oral deserves specific mention because it is recorded at school and marked internally. The IB expects an unrehearsed response to the stimulus or extract. A student who delivers a memorised monologue is usually identifiable from the recording, and the tell is that the discussion that follows collapses. Rehearsing structure and anticipating question types is legitimate preparation. Memorising a text is not.

IB Gram does not supply completed coursework of any kind, in any subject, and will not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes. Those are the school's to provide and the IB's to publish. Several pages ranking for searches like this one sell finished assessed work, and a parent should treat that as the warning sign it is rather than a service.

sections.heading: What Hindi B counts for at UAE Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: Families in Abu Dhabi who expect their child to apply to a UAE university, or to need an attested secondary certificate for any purpose here, run into equivalency. The Ministry of Education sets out what each curriculum must show, and the rules differ by track. For the British route, published guidance requires five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details catch people out. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects on that British-track count, which means a student who assumed their mandatory Arabic grade filled a slot may be a subject short. And at least one widely ranking tutoring page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published five-subject rule. Check the figure against the Ministry's own guidance rather than against a tutoring site.

For the IB specifically, we publish no points threshold on this page. The equivalency requirements we can source cover the British and American tracks; no IB points figure has been read on the Ministry's own pages during the preparation of this page, so stating one would be guesswork on a regulatory matter. Verify any IB requirement directly with the Ministry of Education or the attestation authority before relying on it.

What this means for Hindi B is simple and often reassuring. A Group 2 language taken as part of a completed IB Diploma is a subject on the transcript like any other. Equivalency is a process the family and the school handle with the authority, not something a tutoring platform performs or can speed up, and no tutoring is required for it.

faqs.question: What does IB DP Hindi B actually assess at SL and HL?
faqs.answer: Four components, identical in structure at both levels. Paper 1 is productive writing: one task from three, in a named text type, worth 25%. Paper 2 is sat as one examination in two parts, listening and reading, each worth 25%, both answered in Hindi. The individual oral carries the final 25%, recorded at school and moderated. SL writing is 250-400 words, HL 450-600. HL also requires two literary works, and the HL oral is built on an extract from one of them rather than a visual stimulus. Confirm exact durations with your school's DP coordinator.

faqs.question: My child speaks Hindi at home but keeps losing marks in Paper 1. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always register and text type rather than language. Paper 1 names an audience, a purpose and a text type, and the message criterion rewards following those conventions. A student who writes comfortable spoken-register Hindi into a formal letter, or produces an essay when a report was asked for, loses marks while sounding entirely fluent. The conceptual understanding criterion compounds it: it looks for visible awareness of audience, context and purpose. The fix is memorising text-type conventions and planning for ninety seconds before writing, not more vocabulary.

faqs.question: Is Hindi B easier than Hindi A: Language and Literature?
faqs.answer: Different rather than easier, though Hindi B is the lighter reading load. Hindi B is a language acquisition course with four components and five prescribed themes. Hindi A is a Group 1 literature-based course with guided textual analysis, a comparative essay and, at HL, an additional essay. The honest test is written: if your child cannot read unseen literary Hindi prose and comment on how it is built, Hindi A will be a difficult two years however fluent their speech. Fluency in conversation earns no credit in Hindi A.

faqs.question: How much does a Hindi B tutor in Abu Dhabi charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates surveyed in October 2026 run from AED 45-150 an hour for budget online tutors to AED 150-300 for a qualified subject teacher online, AED 180-500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB specialist. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home at AED 180-350 and specialists at AED 200-450 plus. Those are market figures, not ours. For a minority language the in-home premium buys travel rather than Language B expertise, which is the distinction worth paying for.

faqs.question: Can my child take Hindi B if the school in Abu Dhabi does not teach it?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the school, and it is a conversation with the DP coordinator rather than with a tutor. Schools register candidates for subjects they can support, and some will accommodate a language outside their timetable through a self-taught or externally supported arrangement while others will not. What a tutoring platform cannot do is register a candidate or create a school's provision. Ask the coordinator early in Year 11, because the answer shapes the whole Group 2 decision and is difficult to revisit in DP1.

faqs.question: What is the individual oral in Hindi B and how is it different at HL?
faqs.answer: It is a recorded one-to-one assessment carried the school marks before moderation, worth 25% at both levels. At SL the student responds to a visual stimulus linked to one of the five prescribed themes, then holds a discussion. At HL the stimulus is replaced by an extract from one of the two literary works studied, and the expectation moves from describing to analysing what the writer does. That shift is the main reason HL students underperform relative to their classwork, because extract analysis is rarely rehearsed enough at school.

faqs.question: How many literary works does Hindi B HL require?
faqs.answer: Two, read in Hindi across the two years. They are not examined by a separate paper. They feed the HL individual oral, where the student analyses an extract from one of them. Students and families frequently discover this late, because the works sit outside the prescribed-theme teaching sequence and are easy to postpone. In a timetable with three higher levels and an Extended Essay, the literary reading is the first thing dropped, and the consequence lands on a component worth a quarter of the grade.

faqs.question: Does Hindi B count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: A Group 2 language inside a completed IB Diploma appears on the transcript like any other subject. The published equivalency rules we can source cover the British and American tracks: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels. No IB points threshold has been read on the Ministry's own pages, so this page publishes none. Verify any IB requirement with the Ministry or the attestation authority directly.

faqs.question: How much Devanagari handwriting practice does Paper 1 need?
faqs.answer: More than most students get, because Paper 1 is handwritten and nothing else in their week is. A student who types Hindi occasionally and handwrites it almost never will produce 450-600 HL words slowly and untidily, and legibility is the examiner's problem turned into the student's mark. We set handwritten practice from the first session and keep every Paper 1 attempt on paper rather than on screen. Four or five timed handwritten attempts usually brings pace and legibility to where the examination needs them.

faqs.question: Which of the five prescribed themes causes Abu Dhabi students the most trouble?
faqs.answer: Social organisation and sharing the planet, consistently. Students here can discuss water scarcity, public transport, construction labour or waste in English and often in classroom Arabic, but have never had to do it in Hindi. The content knowledge exists and the lexicon does not, which is a fast problem to fix with targeted vocabulary and a slow one to fix through general conversation. Identity and experiences are usually their strongest themes, because migration between India and the Gulf gives them genuine material to write about.

faqs.question: Can a tutor coach the individual oral without breaking IB academic-honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may rehearse structure, run mock orals to the real timing, anticipate discussion questions, build theme vocabulary and give feedback on recordings. A tutor may not prepare a script for the student to memorise, supply sentences for the assessed recording, or edit an assessed draft to completion. The IB expects an unrehearsed response, and a memorised monologue usually shows itself when the discussion that follows collapses. We state that boundary to the student in the first session.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Hindi B HL usually need in the exam year?
faqs.answer: One well-used weekly session with marked written work in between is the normal starting point, rising to two or three in the weeks before the oral recording window or the May session. Loading a second weekly slot onto a timetable that already carries mandatory Arabic, two content-heavy higher levels and an Extended Essay deadline tends to produce cancellations rather than progress. The better lever is usually the quality of the work done between lessons, which is why written work is set and returned marked every week.

faqs.question: Does my child still have to study Arabic alongside Hindi B in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly yes. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic, Islamic education and social studies alongside whichever international curriculum they are licensed to deliver, and the emirate authorities enforce that. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK licenses and inspects the emirate's private schools and publishes its inspection ratings. So a DP student may carry mandatory Arabic outside the diploma while taking Hindi B inside it. Only the Group 2 subject appears on the diploma, but both consume timetable hours, which matters when planning tutoring.

faqs.question: Are Hindi B lessons taught in Hindi or in English?
faqs.answer: The lesson runs in Hindi, because the examination runs in Hindi and listening answers written in English score nothing. Tutors switch to English only to explain a marking criterion or a text-type convention, where precision about what the examiner is rewarding matters more than immersion. Students who are used to a mixed home register find the first two sessions tiring and then adjust quickly. Parents who want to follow the feedback get the written marking in English, keyed to the criterion that lost the marks.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. School hours shorten during Ramadan, energy in the late afternoon drops and the useful study window moves to after Iftar. We reschedule the fixed weekly slot for the month rather than pausing, since Ramadan frequently falls close to internal oral recording windows and mock examinations. Timed paper practice generally works better in the morning during that month, so some families move their Paper 1 practice to a weekend slot and keep the evening session for oral rehearsal.

faqs.question: What happens if no Hindi B specialist is free when we enquire?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a timeframe, rather than matching you to a general Hindi speaker and hoping. Diploma-level Language B teaching in Hindi is a narrow specialism, and availability is tighter in the weeks before oral recording windows and the May session. Where the wait is real, we will say how long it is likely to be and what the student can usefully do in the meantime, including which component to work on alone. A match that cannot mark against the criteria is worse than a short wait.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-hindi-b-tutor.closingHeading: Start with a diagnosis, not a package
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-hindi-b-tutor.closingBody: If your child is fluent in Hindi and the Hindi B grade does not show it, the useful next step is a measurement rather than a booking. One timed Paper 1 under handwriting conditions, one reading passage against the clock and five minutes of unprepared oral will tell you which of the four components is actually losing the marks, and whether the problem is register, text type, reading speed or a level that was chosen on the strength of conversation. Tell us the level, the weakest component and the school's internal deadline, and we will match an IB DP Hindi B tutor in Abu Dhabi accordingly, with one free trial lesson and the diagnosis shared either way.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-history-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma History at Standard and Higher Level. Each profile names the prescribed subject for the source paper, the world history topics and, at Higher Level, the regional option they have taught, because those three choices are made by the school and they decide whether a tutor is a specialist for your child or a stranger to the content.

intro.heading: What you should be able to read after four weeks
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements in this subject cannot be assessed. Sessions happen, the student says they were useful, a report arrives at the end of term with the same grade on it, and nobody can say what changed. History is unusually easy to audit, because every component produces a document with a number on it. A parent who asks for marked work rather than for progress updates will know within a month whether the money is working.

Here is the standard worth holding anyone to. By the end of week two there should be a marked source-paper answer with the mark split shown question by question, so you can see whether the student is losing the four-mark value-and-limitations question, the six-mark comparison, or the nine-mark mini-essay. By week four there should be at least two timed essays marked against the published markbands with the band stated and the specific move to the next band written out. By week eight those bands should have moved on the component being worked on, or there should be a stated reason why not. By week twelve the investigation should exist in draft with its three sections identifiable.

That standard matters because History grades move in a particular pattern. They do not creep upwards evenly. A student stuck at 9 out of 15 on essays is usually making one repeatable mistake, and when it is corrected the mark jumps. A student losing the comparison question on the source paper is losing the same six marks every time, and a drill fixes it in two sessions. The things that look like gradual improvement are usually three discrete repairs, each visible in a marked script, each with its own fix. Which is why the marked script is the unit of evidence and the session note is not.

Abu Dhabi adds its own detail. Cohorts here are small, the prescribed subject and the world history topics are chosen by the department, and at Higher Level the regional option is frequently History of Africa and the Middle East, which is both appropriate for the region and taught by relatively few tutors anywhere. A tutor matched on the words Diploma History and not on those three choices will spend the first fortnight reading the content rather than teaching it. Lessons themselves run online, one to one, over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, because home visits are a service we provide only in India.

The sections that follow take the components in the order the marks arrive, and each one ends with what the evidence of progress on it looks like. The cost section is at the end rather than the beginning, because a rate is only meaningful once you know what the hour is supposed to produce.
bullets: Week two: a marked source answer with the mark split shown per question
Week four: two timed essays marked against the markbands with the band named
Week eight: a band moved on the component being worked, or a stated reason
Week twelve: an investigation draft with its three sections identifiable
Ask the department for the prescribed subject, the world history topics and the regional option

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-history-home-tutor.programmesIntro: History is examined at Diploma level, but the writing discipline it rewards is built earlier and the investigation sits in the core alongside everything else. These are the stages that matter to an Abu Dhabi family, with what evidence of progress looks like at each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, a source-based paper worth twenty-four marks, two essay papers at fifteen marks each per essay, and a historical investigation worth twenty-five marks inside a 2,200-word ceiling. Higher Level adds a third paper of three essays on a regional option. Every component produces a markable document, which makes this the easiest Diploma subject in which to prove tutoring is working.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi History groups are frequently small and taught by one teacher across both levels. Ask which prescribed subject the source paper covers, which two world history topics the essays will come from, and at Higher Level which regional option is being taught. Those three answers determine tutor fit entirely and they cost one email to obtain.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and Societies in the middle years assesses knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and critical thinking, which is recognisably the Diploma paper in miniature. A student who learned to support a claim with specific evidence arrives in DP1 writing bands higher than one who learned to narrate.
programmes.countryNote: Students entering Diploma History in this emirate often arrive from a British middle school where source work meant describing a document. The Diploma wants origin, purpose and content used to assess value and limitation, which is a different skill. A short block before DP1 on that single move is the cheapest intervention available in the subject.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: IA, EE and TOK
programmes.description: The historical investigation, an Extended Essay that History students frequently choose to write in the subject, and Theory of Knowledge all draw on the same analytical habit. The investigation is the one with a hard word ceiling and a three-part structure, and it is where supervision rather than teaching produces the marks.
programmes.countryNote: Internal deadlines in Abu Dhabi schools cluster before the long weekends and the Eid breaks, and the investigation needs source access settled well before the first draft. Plan the supervision cycles against the school's internal date rather than anything external, since the internal date usually sits months earlier.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-history-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: History is chosen alongside a recognisable set of subjects in this emirate, and the pairings affect how heavy the written workload actually is. These are the ones seen most often, with what each is assessed on.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A source paper of twenty-four marks, essay papers at fifteen marks per essay, a Higher Level regional option, and a 2,200-word investigation worth twenty-five marks. Marks are lost to narrative where analysis was required, and to claims made without specific evidence attached.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Political concepts examined through a source booklet and extended responses, plus an engagement project with a written report. The closest subject to History in the way it is marked, and students taking both find the source technique transfers directly between them.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Core units on population, climate vulnerability and resource security, optional themes, and a fieldwork report with a word ceiling. Shares History's reliance on named case material: a general answer about a general place scores in the lowest band available.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Micro, macro and the global economy, with a portfolio of commentaries on published articles. Pairs usefully with History because the evaluation move is identical, and students often find the diagram work the only genuinely new skill.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: Studied works, unseen literary analysis, an individual oral and a Higher Level essay. The paragraph discipline is the same as History's: claim, evidence, weighing. Students strong in one are usually one technique away from being strong in the other.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Offered at several levels across the emirate's schools and mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum for the groups the regulations specify. A real timetable constraint for a History student, since both subjects demand sustained written work in the same evenings.

subjects.name: Philosophy
subjects.description: Core themes, a prescribed text and an internally assessed analysis of non-philosophical material. Chosen by History students who enjoy the argumentative side, and the two reinforce each other because neither rewards unsupported assertion.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Five content units, two written papers and a research project carrying a quarter of the grade. A common third humanities choice, and the lightest of them for reading volume, which matters in a block that already contains History.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Three approaches to behaviour, option topics and an experimental report on four criteria. Shares History's dependence on command terms, so a student who has learned to read the verb in one subject carries the gain across.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: A comparative study, a process portfolio and an exhibition. Taken alongside History by students who want a practical subject, and the comparative study rewards exactly the contextual analysis History teaches.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-history-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is online, so the community a family lives in does not change which tutor is available. It does change the evening, and in a subject built on written work produced between sessions the timing of the slot matters. These are the areas the enquiries come from.

regions.name: Corniche and Al Markaziyah
regions.note: Central island living with short school runs, which makes an early evening slot genuinely workable. Families here often arrive with a specific marked paper in hand, which is the fastest possible start for a subject diagnosed from documents.

regions.name: Al Manaseer
regions.note: Established residential district close to several long-running Diploma cohorts. The common request here is investigation supervision rather than weekly teaching, because the content is covered in class and the coursework is where students are unsupervised.

regions.name: Al Rawdah
regions.note: Quieter island neighbourhood where households frequently have a Diploma student and a younger sibling on a different curriculum. Scheduling is the practical constraint, and a fixed weekly slot that survives the term is worth more than a flexible one.

regions.name: Al Muroor
regions.note: Dense central area with a mix of school catchments, so the study window opens at different times across the same street. Online delivery means the awkward hour costs the same as the convenient one, which is not true of any visiting arrangement here.

regions.name: Al Bandar
regions.note: Waterfront community along the Al Raha stretch, with a long approach road that makes visiting tutors expensive. For a subject where the useful work happens on paper between sessions, the drive buys nothing a video call does not.

regions.name: Al Ghadeer
regions.note: Community on the emirate boundary with a commute in both directions and a late-opening study window. Students here are among the clearest beneficiaries of online delivery, because the local pool of Diploma History specialists is effectively empty.

regions.name: Al Maqtaa and the area between the bridges
regions.note: A corridor position between the island and the mainland, with families drawing on schools in both directions. Prescribed subjects differ between those schools, which is exactly why the match has to be made on the content rather than the postcode.

schoolClusters.city: Island Diploma History cohorts
schoolClusters.note: History is long established across this cluster, which means past student investigations exist at a range of mark bands. Students we support attend schools here; no affiliation or endorsement is implied. Ask whether anonymised past investigations can be shown, because one marked exemplar at 14 out of 25 and one at 22 teaches the criteria faster than any explanation.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Reem and the newer campuses
schoolClusters.note: Departments making their first History submissions have no internal bank of past work to calibrate against, and the regional option at Higher Level may be newly chosen. External supervision here functions as a second opinion on borderline work rather than as replacement teaching.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi
Nord Anglia International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and the eastern corridor
schoolClusters.note: Where Diploma demand concentrates in this emirate, and where a number of students transfer in from British-track schools at sixteen. Those students usually need the source technique rebuilt rather than revised, which is a scoped piece of work with a visible end point.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-history-home-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of support, each defined by what it hands back. The thing they have in common is that every session produces a marked document, because in this subject that is the only honest evidence that anything has changed.

modes.title: Marked essay cycles against one component
modes.description: The student writes a timed essay before the session, the tutor marks it against the published markbands and names the band, and the session is spent on the single move that reaches the band above. Four or five cycles is usually enough to shift a student stuck in the middle bands, because the thing holding them there is normally one repeatable habit.
bullets: Written to time before the session, not during it
Marked against the published markbands with the band stated
One named move per cycle, not a general critique

modes.title: Source-paper drill block
modes.description: A short block aimed only at the first paper: the three-mark and two-mark opening questions, the four-mark assessment of value and limitations using origin, purpose and content, the six-mark comparison, and the nine-mark answer that has to use sources and own knowledge together. Highly mechanical, and the fastest mark movement in the subject.
bullets: Each question type drilled separately to its own mark allocation
Origin, purpose and content applied every time, without exception
Full papers sat to the hour at least twice

modes.title: Investigation supervision cycles
modes.description: Fortnightly supervision across the investigation, taken in the order the marks are awarded: the question and the sources first, then the body of the investigation, then the reflection. The tutor questions rather than corrects, so the work remains the student's own and the reflection has something genuine to reflect on.
bullets: Source access and question viability settled before any drafting
Each section returned with the criterion it is marked against named
Word ceiling managed from the start rather than cut at the end

sections.heading: A twelve-week evidence trail, and what each stage should produce
paragraphs: This is the audit a parent can run without knowing any history. It depends only on documents, each of which carries a number, and it will tell you within a month whether the arrangement is working. The point of publishing it is that no competitor page in the researched set offers any way at all to check whether tutoring is doing anything, and families are left assessing a service by how the sessions felt.

The first two weeks are diagnostic and should produce a marked source-paper answer with the marks shown question by question. That single document localises the problem. A student losing the four-mark value-and-limitations question has a technique gap that takes one session. A student losing the nine-mark answer is failing to integrate sources with own knowledge, which takes three or four. A student losing marks evenly across all four has not been taught the paper's structure at all.

Weeks three to eight are the repair, and the evidence is timed essays with bands named. Two things should be visible in that sequence: the same specific feedback should not appear twice, because feedback repeated is feedback not acted on, and the band should move on the component being worked rather than on the subject generally. A student whose essays all improve slightly has had encouragement; a student whose Paper 2 band moved from the middle to the upper range has had teaching.

Weeks nine to twelve belong to the investigation, and the evidence is a draft with three identifiable sections rather than a continuous essay. The most common failure at this stage is a student who has written 2,200 words of narrative with no identification and evaluation of sources at the front and no reflection at the back. That is a structural problem, it is worth a large share of the twenty-five marks, and it is visible to a parent who has simply been told what the three sections are called.

sections.heading: Where the marks live across the four assessed components
paragraphs: Before any audit is useful, a parent needs to know what the components are and what each is worth, because a tutor working hard on the wrong one can produce a lot of marked work and no grade movement. Diploma History is assessed through a source-based paper, two essay papers, and an internally assessed historical investigation, with the third paper sat only by Higher Level students.

The source paper carries twenty-four marks and is sat in one hour on a single prescribed subject chosen by the school. It has four questions with different allocations, and because the allocations differ the technique for each is different too. The essay papers work in fifteen-mark units: two essays on the second paper drawn from the world history topics the department teaches, and three essays at Higher Level on the regional option. The investigation carries twenty-five marks inside a 2,200-word ceiling and is divided into three sections with their own mark allocations.

The arithmetic that follows matters for planning. A student who improves their essay writing by one band improves several components at once, because the fifteen-mark markbands are shared across the essay papers. A student who fixes the six-mark comparison question on the source paper gains in one place only. Both are worth doing; the order should depend on how many marks each is currently losing, which is exactly what the diagnostic document in week two establishes.

The weighting of the investigation differs between the levels, and the current figures should be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator rather than taken from any tutoring page. What does not vary is the structure of its twenty-five marks, and that structure is the most useful single thing a family can be told about the component, because almost every weak investigation is weak structurally rather than historically.

sections.heading: Reading a marked source paper: what the four questions each demand
paragraphs: The first paper is mechanical in a way the essays are not, and that makes it the best place to start with a student who needs an early win. Four questions, twenty-four marks, one hour. The opening questions are short comprehension items worth three marks and two marks, and they are lost mainly to students who write too much and run out of time later in the paper.

The four-mark question asks the student to assess the value and limitations of a source with reference to its origin, its purpose and its content. That phrasing is the entire technique. Students lose marks by writing about the content alone, or by describing the origin without saying what the origin does to the source's value. The fix is a required structure applied every single time: this is where it came from, this is why it was made, this is what is in it, and therefore it is strong for this and weak for that.

The six-mark question asks for comparison and contrast between two sources, and this is the single most commonly botched question on the paper. Students write a paragraph on each source and leave the comparison implicit. The marks require explicit linked statements across both sources on shared points, and the quickest route is a grid drawn before writing: point, what source one says, what source two says, similar or different. Two sessions of that normally recovers most of the six marks.

The nine-mark question requires sources and own knowledge used together, and it is where a strong student separates from an average one. Answers that are all source and no knowledge, or all knowledge with sources mentioned, sit in the middle. The structure that works treats each paragraph as an argument supported by both a source reference and a piece of contextual knowledge the sources do not contain. Evidence of progress on this question is specific: the student's answers should start containing dates, names and events that appear nowhere in the source booklet.
bullets: Origin, purpose and content applied every time on the four-mark question

sections.heading: Why an essay stalls at nine out of fifteen, and what moves it
paragraphs: A student who writes fluently, knows the period and keeps scoring nine out of fifteen is the most common case in this subject, and the cause is almost always the same. The essay narrates. It tells the examiner what happened, in order, accurately, and it never turns the material into an argument about the question that was asked. Length is not the problem; a shorter essay that argues outscores a longer one that recounts.

The second cause is evidence used generically. A student writes that economic conditions worsened, that opposition grew, that the government responded harshly. Each statement may be true and none of it is evidence, because evidence in this subject is specific: a named measure, a date, a figure, a named person, an identifiable event. The markbands reward precise supporting detail, and the difference between a middle band and an upper band is frequently nothing more than the replacement of general statements with specific ones.

The third is the absent counter-argument. Upper bands require awareness that the question could be answered differently and a reason for preferring the answer given. Students avoid this because it feels like weakening their case. In practice an essay that states the strongest objection and then explains why it does not overturn the argument reads as considerably more confident than one that pretends the objection does not exist.

Each of those three is a single repair, and each is visible in a marked script. That is why the evidence standard set out earlier insists that feedback should not repeat: if the same comment about narrative appears on three consecutive essays, the sessions are describing the problem rather than fixing it. The fix for narrative is a forced plan in which every paragraph begins with a claim about the question. It is uncomfortable for two essays and then it becomes how the student writes.
bullets: Narrative scores in the middle bands however well it is written
Evidence means a named measure, a date, a figure or an identifiable event
The strongest objection stated and answered reads as confidence, not weakness

sections.heading: Higher Level: the regional option and the three-essay paper
paragraphs: Higher Level students sit an additional paper of three essays on a regional option chosen by the school, across two and a half hours. The step up is less about difficulty than about stamina and breadth: three fifteen-mark essays in one sitting, drawn from a wide regional syllabus, with no source booklet to lean on. Students who have revised intensively on a narrow set of topics find themselves with nothing to write on the third question.

In this emirate the regional option is frequently History of Africa and the Middle East, which is appropriate and has one practical consequence worth knowing: the pool of tutors anywhere who have taught that option through several cohorts is smaller than for the European or American options. A tutor who has taught History of Europe is not a specialist for a student sitting Africa and the Middle East, and the honest ones will say so. Ask the question before booking and expect a direct answer.

The revision strategy that works for this paper is breadth-first rather than depth-first, which is the opposite of what students instinctively do. The aim is to be able to write a competent fifteen-mark essay on every section of the option rather than an outstanding one on three sections. That means a planned sequence of essay outlines across the whole syllabus, with full essays written only on the areas the outlines reveal as weak.

Evidence of progress here is unusual and specific: the number of syllabus sections on which the student can produce a credible plan in ten minutes. That number should rise week by week, it is easy for a parent to check by asking, and it predicts the paper outcome better than the mark on any single essay does.

sections.heading: The historical investigation: three sections, twenty-five marks, 2,200 words
paragraphs: The investigation is the component where supervision earns its fee, because most of its failures are structural and all of them are preventable. It carries twenty-five marks inside a 2,200-word ceiling and is written in three sections: an identification and evaluation of sources, the investigation itself, and a reflection on what the process revealed about the methods of the historian. Each section has its own mark allocation and its own criterion.

The first section is short and dense. It states the question, identifies the sources to be used, and evaluates two of them for value and limitations with reference to origin, purpose and content, which is the same technique the source paper demands. Students treat it as an introduction and write background instead, losing marks that were available for a mechanical task they already know how to do.

The second section is the body of the work and carries the largest share of the marks. It has to be an argument answering the stated question, using specific evidence, referencing the sources properly, and reaching a conclusion that follows from what preceded it. The commonest failure is a narrative of the period with the question answered in the final paragraph, which is the same error that caps essays at nine out of fifteen and should have been repaired before the investigation began.

The third section is a reflection on method and it is the most mishandled part of the component. It is not a reflection on how the student found the process, nor a summary of conclusions. It asks what the investigation revealed about how historians work and what they are limited by: the nature of the surviving evidence, the problem of selection, the difficulty of establishing causation. A student who has genuinely struggled with a source has something to say here; a student who read three secondary accounts has nothing, and the reflection reads as invented because it is.

sections.heading: Source access for an investigation written in this emirate
paragraphs: A question a student cannot source is a question that will produce a weak investigation, and this is decided in the first supervision conversation rather than discovered in the third draft. The practical constraint for a student in Abu Dhabi is not that sources are unavailable but that the student has not been taught where to look, and so defaults to whatever a general web search returns.

What is genuinely accessible is wider than students assume. School library subscriptions frequently include academic databases that nobody has shown the cohort how to use. Published collections of documents in translation exist for most periods on the Diploma syllabus. Digitised newspaper archives cover the twentieth century in depth. National and institutional archives in several countries publish scanned material openly. A student who spends one supervised hour learning to search properly saves a fortnight later.

What is not accessible needs saying too, because a question requiring untranslated material in a language the student does not read, or physical archives that cannot be visited, is a question to change rather than to struggle with. The supervisor's job at this stage is to be unhelpful in a specific way: to keep asking what the student will actually read, until the answer is a list of documents rather than a topic.

On a legal point that matters, published syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes should not be reproduced or circulated. Reference them, cite the official source and ask the school for its licensed copies. We link to official pages rather than hosting any of that material, and any provider offering a downloadable library of it is offering something they are not entitled to distribute.
bullets: Settle what the student will actually read before the question is fixed
School database subscriptions are usually under-used rather than absent
