sections.heading: What "IB DP home tutor in Abu Dhabi" costs, and what the money buys
paragraphs: A visiting Diploma tutor in Abu Dhabi costs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour. The lower end of that is Bestimate's published in-home band of AED 180 to 350; the upper end reflects specialist home tutors advertising to AED 500. The same specialist teaching the same subject over live video sits in the AED 200 to 450 band for IB specialists, per Bestimate's rate table, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. The difference between the two is not teaching quality. It is a car.

That matters because the thing a parent is buying is teaching minutes with the right specialist, and a visiting arrangement spends part of the budget on moving a person across Abu Dhabi. It also shrinks the pool of people you may choose from to those willing to make the trip at the hour you need. For a common subject that is a mild constraint. For Visual Arts HL or Film HL in Khalifa City it is usually a complete one.

IB Gram's own answer is to remove the travel and keep the specialist. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. We do not publish our own hourly figures on this page, because the number depends on the subject, the level and how rare the specialism is, and a single advertised rate would be either misleading or useless. The free first lesson comes before any quote.

The comparison table below is the one to take into any conversation with any provider in this emirate. It compares the same purchase across the formats actually available in Abu Dhabi, including what is inside the rate and what is not. The column that decides most decisions is the last one: how many specialists you can actually choose from.

sections.heading: The travel hour nobody invoices, priced across Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi is a spread-out emirate and that has a price. A tutor who drives from Al Bateen to Khalifa City for a 5pm session, teaches for sixty minutes and drives back has given up well over two hours for one paid hour. Nobody does that at the same rate they would charge for an hour at a desk, and nobody should. The question for a parent is not whether travel is in the rate, because it always is. The question is how much of your budget is buying transport rather than teaching.

The arithmetic is simple and uncomfortable. If a tutor's working evening is three and a half hours and travel eats ninety minutes of it, they can teach two sessions instead of three. To earn the same amount they must charge about half again per session. That is the whole explanation for why in-home bands sit above online bands in every published rate table in this market, including Bestimate's, and it is why the gap widens the further you live from the school clusters.

There is a second cost that never appears in a quote: the sessions that do not happen. A visiting arrangement is fragile in a way an online one is not. Traffic on the Sheikh Zayed bridge, a sandstorm, a tutor's own school commitments, a family's travel, and the session is cancelled or shortened. Over a thirty-week Diploma year, a handful of lost sessions is a meaningful share of what you paid for, and it tends to be lost in exactly the weeks that matter.

None of this means in-home tutoring is a bad product. It means it is a different product with a travel surcharge and a smaller choice of teacher, and it should be compared honestly against the alternative rather than treated as the default. For Diploma subjects specifically, where the match is to one subject at one level, the trade is usually unfavourable: you pay more and choose from fewer specialists.

sections.heading: Nine things that move a Diploma quote in this emirate
paragraphs: Two families in the same Abu Dhabi community can be quoted rates that differ by a factor of three for what sounds like the same thing. Usually nothing dishonest is happening. They are buying different products, and the variables below are the ones doing the work. Reading them in order is also the fastest way to get a quote down without giving anything up.

The biggest single lever is subject rarity, and it is the one parents least expect. A Mathematics HL hour in Abu Dhabi is competitively priced because many people can teach it. A Film HL or Visual Arts HL hour is expensive because almost nobody locally has marked those components, and in a small-cohort emirate that scarcity is sharper than it is in Dubai. If your quote looks high, the first question is whether it is high for the subject or high for the market.

The second lever is the component. Teaching content is faster work than supervising an internally assessed component, where a tutor reads a student's draft, maps it against each criterion and writes feedback that the student then acts on. That is slow and it is usually priced above routine teaching. Families who budget for subject teaching and then discover that Internal Assessment supervision is quoted separately are encountering this, not being overcharged.

The third is timing, and it is entirely within your control. Rates in this market are not formally seasonal, but availability is, and availability is what sets the price you can actually get. Specialists in thin subjects are bookable in September and gone by March. A family that identifies a problem in DP1 is buying from a full market; the same family in the spring of DP2 is buying whatever is left. That is the real cost of waiting, and it is larger than any rate negotiation.

sections.heading: Packages, sessions and the arithmetic of a Diploma year
paragraphs: The hourly rate is the number families negotiate and the session count is the number that decides the bill. A Diploma year of roughly thirty teaching weeks at one weekly hour is thirty hours per subject. At the middle of the IB specialist band that is a meaningful annual figure for one subject, and families supporting two subjects through both Diploma years are making a two-year commitment considerably larger than they usually model at the outset.

Monthly packages change the per-hour maths and are worth asking about. Published market packages in this region include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Those are the numbers to hold up against any quote you receive.

Three questions separate a good package from a bad one. What is the session length, not just the count? What happens to unused sessions at the end of the month? And is marking of work between sessions inside the price? A package of eight sessions that turns out to mean eight forty-five-minute slots with no marking is a different product from eight marked hours, and the difference is not visible in the headline figure.

The pattern that wastes the most money in Abu Dhabi is buying a block before a diagnosis. A family worried in October commits to three months of weekly hours in a subject, and in week five discovers the weakness was in a different subject, or was a timing problem fixable in two sessions. The sequence that does not waste money is: free diagnostic lesson, written diagnosis, then a block sized to the diagnosis. The order is the saving.

sections.heading: Tuition inside a whole Diploma budget
paragraphs: Tutoring is rarely the only education cost in an Abu Dhabi household, and pricing it in isolation is how families end up surprised. School fees, examination registration where a student is a private candidate, university application costs and the Diploma's own incidental expenses all compete for the same money, and they arrive on a predictable schedule that can be planned around.

The useful framing is a two-year total rather than an hourly rate. Decide how many subjects you will genuinely support, for how many terms, and at what weekly frequency. One subject at one hour a week through both Diploma years is a different commitment from two subjects through DP2 only, and the second is often the better value because it concentrates spending where the grades count and the components fall due.

It is also worth knowing what is not a tutoring cost. The examination registration a school handles for its own candidates is inside the school's fees; a private candidate pays separately and should ask the examination centre directly. Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are published by the boards and should be reached through the official sites rather than bought from anyone, because those are copyright works and a tutor distributing copies is a sign to walk away.

On value-added tax, we deliberately say less than other pages do. The treatment of tuition fees under UAE VAT is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority, and we do not state it as fact here. What you should do is ask any provider, including us, whether a quoted dirham figure is inclusive or exclusive of VAT, and ask whether they hold a tax registration number. A provider who cannot answer either question has told you something worth knowing.

sections.heading: The permit question, and what it costs you to skip it
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work rather than informal work, and this belongs in a pricing section because it changes who may legitimately quote you a rate. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Two things follow for a parent comparing quotes. The permit is free, so a tutor who adds a licensing cost to your rate is adding something that does not exist. And individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no fine schedule published anywhere. If a provider quotes you a specific fine figure to create urgency, that figure is not verifiable and the urgency is manufactured.

There is an Abu Dhabi-specific layer. Gulf News has reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is press reporting rather than the policy text, so verify the current wording with ADEK. The cost implication is direct: the cheapest apparent option, your child's own subject teacher, is the one route that is closed.

An operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal again. A tuition centre in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation of any kind and claims none; we are a matching platform delivering lessons over live video, and we would rather say that plainly than let a logo imply otherwise.

sections.heading: Why the cheapest hour is usually the most expensive
paragraphs: The budget end of the Abu Dhabi market is real and sometimes right. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. For homework supervision, for keeping a DP1 student on top of reading, or for a Standard Level subject where the issue is organisation rather than content, that is a sensible purchase and the premium band would be waste.

It stops being sensible the moment the problem is component-specific. A tutor at AED 50 an hour who has never marked an Internal Assessment against its criteria cannot tell your child which criterion is costing the marks, because that knowledge is the entire product. Twenty sessions at AED 50 is a thousand dirhams of pleasant company and no grade movement. Four sessions at AED 300 with someone who has marked forty of those components is twelve hundred dirhams and a different outcome. The arithmetic favours the expensive hour more often than families expect.

The way to tell which you need is to ask for a diagnosis before buying hours, and to insist that the diagnosis names a component. 'He needs to work harder' is not a diagnosis. 'His Paper 2 essays are answering a question he prepared rather than the one asked, and that is costing roughly a grade' is. The second one tells you both what to buy and how much of it, and a tutor who cannot produce that sentence after reading marked work is not the specialist you are paying for.

The other hidden cost is substitution. A cheap arrangement that produces no movement does not just waste the money spent; it consumes the term in which the problem was cheap to fix. Finding out in February that the autumn was wasted is the single most expensive outcome available in Diploma tutoring, and it is almost always the consequence of buying hours before a diagnosis rather than of buying the wrong rate.
bullets: Budget tutoring is right for supervision and organisation, not for components
Insist any diagnosis names a component and a criterion, not an attitude
Four expensive specialist sessions often beat twenty cheap generalist ones
The real cost of a wasted term is the cheap window it consumed

sections.heading: What money cannot buy in a Diploma, at any rate
paragraphs: This section is here because the top of this market includes people selling things that should not be for sale, and an Abu Dhabi parent under pressure in the spring of DP2 is the exact customer for them. One page competing for these searches advertises completed Internal Assessments at a published price. The transaction is straightforward and the consequence falls entirely on the candidate.

The IB's academic-honesty rules require assessed work to be the student's own. A paid tutor may teach the content, explain each criterion, model the technique on a different example, read a draft and say precisely where it does not meet the criterion, and set the student the revision to make. A paid tutor may not supply text that appears in the submission, select the data, restructure a draft into its final form, or hand over a finished component. No rate changes that boundary, and a provider who offers to cross it for a higher fee is pricing your child's candidacy.

The test we use is simple and a parent can apply it without any subject knowledge. Ask your child to explain, unprompted, why a particular paragraph is in the Internal Assessment and what it is doing for the argument. If they cannot, that paragraph is not theirs, however it arrived. The same test works on an Extended Essay and on a Theory of Knowledge submission, and it is a better safeguard than any assurance a provider gives you.

The related thing you cannot legitimately buy is material. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright works published by the boards. A tutor should cite and link them, and work from the official versions. A provider advertising a private library of unreleased material is selling a risk, and it is your child's risk rather than theirs.
bullets: Tutors teach, mark and give feedback; assessed work stays the student's own
Apply the authorship test to any paragraph in a draft, unprompted
Official syllabus and paper material belongs on the boards' own sites
No rate makes the academic-honesty boundary movable

process.title: Say which subject and which component
process.description: A rate cannot be quoted usefully against 'Diploma help'. It can be quoted against 'Chemistry HL, the exploration is three weeks late and the mock was a 4'. That sentence also tells you whether you are buying content teaching or component supervision, which are priced differently everywhere in this market.

process.title: Take the free first lesson before any package
process.description: The first lesson costs nothing and no payment details are taken to book it. Its purpose is a written diagnosis naming the leaking component and roughly what it will take. Buying a block before this step is the commonest way to waste money on Diploma tutoring in Abu Dhabi.

process.title: Size the commitment to the diagnosis
process.description: A technique error is three to six sessions. A content gap is eight to twelve with a revisit. A process problem is a calendar, not a tutor. Once you know which one you have, choose between paying per session and a monthly block, and ask what happens to unused sessions.

process.title: Compare quotes on the same basis
process.description: Per hour of teaching actually received, with marking included, at the session length you will actually use. Ask whether Internal Assessment supervision is quoted separately and whether the figure is inclusive of VAT. Two quotes that look different often turn out to be the same price for different products.

process.title: Review on evidence at six weeks
process.description: Set the review date when you start, not when you are worried. At it, look at marked work: per-question marks, criterion comments, paper completion times. If none of those have moved, change something. Renewing because the sessions feel pleasant is how a Diploma budget disappears.

whyPoints.title: The travel surcharge is removed, not disguised
whyPoints.description: An in-home rate in Abu Dhabi carries a drive inside it. Lessons here run one-to-one over live video, so the whole rate buys teaching. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India, and we say so rather than implying otherwise.

whyPoints.title: Every figure on this page has a source
whyPoints.description: The AED bands come from Bestimate's rate table and from the published prices of EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase and BartyED, read in October 2026. Three of the best-ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars.

whyPoints.title: A diagnosis before a package
whyPoints.description: The free first lesson produces a written note naming the leaking component. That is what sizes the commitment, and it is the step that stops a family buying three months of the wrong subject. It also sometimes concludes that no tutoring is needed.

whyPoints.title: Subject rarity does not become your problem
whyPoints.description: In a small-cohort emirate, a thin Higher Level subject locally means a high price or nobody at all. Matching online removes the scarcity premium, because the pool is every specialist free at that hour rather than those willing to drive to your community.

whyPoints.title: We do not quote what we cannot stand behind
whyPoints.description: No price list on this page, because a Diploma rate depends on subject, level and scarcity. No VAT position stated as fact, because that belongs to the Federal Tax Authority. No fine figures for unpermitted tutoring, because none are published.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is not a price point
whyPoints.description: Tutors review and give feedback on the student's own work and nothing more, at any rate. One page competing for this search sells finished Internal Assessments; the consequence of that purchase lands on the candidate, not on the seller.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP home tutor in Abu Dhabi charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Market in-home one-to-one rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate table publishes AED 180 to 350 for in-home visits, and specialist home tutors advertise up to AED 500. The same specialist teaching online sits in the AED 200 to 450 band for IB specialists, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. The gap between the two is travel, not teaching. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices; ours follow a free first lesson and depend on the subject, the level and how scarce the specialism is.

faqs.question: Why does a visiting tutor cost more than the same tutor online?
faqs.answer: Because a visiting tutor is selling you a slice of their evening, not just an hour of teaching. A round trip from the island to Khalifa City at five in the afternoon can exceed an hour, which means two sessions in an evening instead of three. To earn the same amount the rate has to rise by roughly half. There is also a fragility cost: traffic, weather and scheduling clashes cancel visiting sessions in a way they do not cancel a video call, and those lost sessions are part of what you paid for.

faqs.question: Should I pay for ninety-minute sessions or sixty?
faqs.answer: Sixty for content teaching, ninety for internally assessed component work. A content session has a natural length: diagnose, teach, practise, set work. Ninety minutes of that is usually twenty minutes of diminishing returns. Component supervision is different, because reading a draft, mapping it against criteria and agreeing the next revision does not compress well. Ninety-minute blocks also usually carry a lower effective hourly rate, so ask for both figures. For a student under sixteen, sixty minutes is the practical ceiling regardless of the subject.

faqs.question: Does the rate include marking between sessions?
faqs.answer: Ask, because it is the single largest difference between two quotes that look identical. A rate without marking is roughly a third cheaper and substantially less useful, since the whole mechanism of a weekly hour is that work is set, attempted, marked and then revisited. A tutor who sets nothing between sessions is running a conversation rather than a course. Our sessions set work and mark it before the next one, and we would rather you asked every provider the question than assumed it of any of them.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package cheaper than paying per session in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Usually yes per hour, and it commits you. Published market packages in this region include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Before buying one, establish three things: the session length rather than just the count, what happens to unused sessions at month end, and whether marking is inside the price. A block bought after a diagnosis is good value. A block bought before one is the commonest way families in this emirate waste a term's budget.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a DP2 student actually need?
faqs.answer: For one subject with a technique problem, one hour a week for six weeks and then stop. For one Higher Level subject with a genuine content gap, one hour a week through the year with a revisit cycle. For two subjects, two separate specialists at one hour each rather than one tutor stretched across both. More than three tutored hours a week in DP2 usually competes with the student's own revision and starts producing less, not more, which is a point no provider has an incentive to tell you.

faqs.question: Do rates go up before the May session?
faqs.answer: Rates do not formally move, but availability does, and availability is what sets the price you can actually get. Specialists in thin Higher Level subjects are bookable in September and largely gone by March. A family identifying a weakness in DP1 chooses from a full market at the standard band; the same family in the spring of DP2 chooses from what is left, at whatever that costs. The practical effect is a premium for waiting, and it is bigger than anything you could negotiate off an hourly rate.

faqs.question: What does Internal Assessment supervision cost compared with subject teaching?
faqs.answer: Generally above the teaching rate, because the work is slower. A tutor reads the student's draft, maps it against each published criterion, writes feedback and then sets the revision for the student to make. That cannot be done at the pace of a content lesson. Many providers in this market quote it separately, and families who budget only for teaching are then surprised. Ask for both figures at the start. The hours are also concentrated between the summer of DP1 and the autumn of DP2 rather than spread across the year.

faqs.question: Is there VAT on private tuition in the UAE?
faqs.answer: The treatment of tuition fees under UAE value-added tax is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority, and we will not state it as fact on a tutoring page. What you should do is practical: ask any provider, including us, whether a quoted dirham figure is inclusive or exclusive of VAT, and whether they hold a tax registration number. Get the answer in writing alongside the rate. A provider who cannot answer either question clearly has told you something useful about how the rest of the arrangement will be handled.

faqs.question: Can two of my children share one paid session?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is whether they are working on the same thing. Two siblings in the same Diploma subject at the same level with the same weakness can share an hour at a per-student rate well below one-to-one. Two siblings in different subjects or different years cannot, and an hour split between them delivers less than half an hour each. At primary and lower middle school the arithmetic is friendlier because the content overlaps more. For Diploma subjects it rarely works, because the match is to one subject at one level.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to support a Diploma student in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Start with the school. Subject teachers hold clinics, departments publish revision materials, and the Diploma coordinator can often explain a predicted grade in a way that changes what you need to buy. Then take a free diagnostic lesson to establish whether the problem is knowledge, technique or process. A technique problem is three to six sessions with a specialist and nothing more. Buying thirty sessions of generalist support because it has a low hourly rate is the most expensive cheap option available in this market.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who lives in Abu Dhabi cost more than one based elsewhere?
faqs.answer: For in-home work, where the tutor lives decides both the rate and whether they will take the booking at all. For online work it is largely irrelevant, which is the point: the match is made on subject and level rather than on postcode, and the rate reflects the specialism rather than the commute. Where no suitable specialist is available in the UAE at your hours, a tutor based elsewhere teaching on Gulf Standard Time over the same video link is the alternative, and we tell you that before you commit rather than after.

faqs.question: How do I compare two quotes that are not quoting the same thing?
faqs.answer: Reduce both to one number: dirhams per hour of teaching actually received, with marking included, at the session length you will really use. Then check four things on each. Is travel inside the rate? Is Internal Assessment supervision separate? Is the figure inclusive of VAT? And is the named tutor actually teaching that subject at that level this year? Most apparent price gaps in the Abu Dhabi market close once those four are equalised, and the ones that remain usually reflect subject scarcity rather than quality.

faqs.question: Is the free trial lesson genuinely free, and what is the condition?
faqs.answer: It is one free first lesson per student, booked through a consultation, and no payment details are taken to arrange it. The condition worth stating is what it is for: it is a diagnostic, not a sample lesson, so it involves marked work being looked at and the student attempting something under time. It ends with a written note naming the leaking component. If the honest conclusion is that the problem belongs with the school rather than with a tutor, the note says that and nothing is sold.

faqs.question: What should I budget for the whole two years of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Model it as subjects multiplied by weeks rather than as an hourly rate. One subject at one weekly hour across roughly thirty teaching weeks is thirty hours a year, and Bestimate's monthly estimates put a weekly specialist hour at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more in an examination year. Decide how many subjects you will genuinely support and in which year. Concentrating two subjects into DP2, when grades count and components fall due, is usually better value than spreading thin support across both years.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-home-tutor.closingHeading: Get the diagnosis, then the number
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-home-tutor.closingBody: The right sequence saves more than any rate negotiation. Find out which component is losing the marks, size the commitment to that answer, and only then compare quotes on the same basis: dirhams per teaching hour, marking included, at the session length you will actually use. Tell us the subject, the level and what the last marked piece said. The first lesson is free, no payment details are taken to book it, and it ends with a written note you can use even if you hire somebody else. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and if no specialist in that subject is free at your hours we will say so before you commit.

intro.heading: What an Abu Dhabi parent can verify about IA work, and what they cannot
paragraphs: A Diploma candidate hands in six internal components over about eighteen months. Nobody outside the school sees them marked. Your child's teacher assigns a mark against published criteria, the school moderates internally, and the IB samples and adjusts at the end. The parent sits outside that loop entirely. So when a family in Abu Dhabi searches for an IB DP Internal Assessment home tutor, the real anxiety underneath the search is not usually about teaching. It is about visibility. There is money going out, a deadline coming, and no instrument for telling whether the work is actually improving.

That is the problem this page is built around. Not what an internal assessment is, which any school handbook explains, but what a parent can hold in their hand as evidence. The answer is narrower than most providers admit and more useful than a progress report. You can see a dated draft. You can see annotation that names a criterion letter and says which descriptor band the paragraph currently sits in. You can see a change log: what the student rewrote between Tuesday and the following Tuesday, and whether that change addressed the comment or avoided it. You can see whether the research question has stopped moving, which is usually the single best predictor of whether the piece will land.

What you cannot see, and should be suspicious of anyone offering, is a predicted mark presented as a number with a decimal point. Internal marks are moderated. A tutor who tells you the exploration is "a 17 out of 20" is describing their own opinion of a descriptor band, not a result. The honest version is a range with a reason attached: criterion B is sitting in the middle band because the mathematics is correct but unextended, and here is the one paragraph that would move it. That sentence is checkable. A number is not.

The second thing a parent cannot see is authorship, and that is the part that matters most. The IB treats an internal component as the student's own work, supported by a supervisor, with one formal round of written teacher feedback on a draft. A tutor who sits outside that relationship has to be scrupulous about where their hands go. Annotation, questioning, modelling on a different example, teaching the statistics the student never covered: all legitimate. Supplying sentences that end up in the document: not. Our sessions are run so that the record shows the student's revisions, and so that a coordinator reviewing the version history would see nothing surprising.

Internal assessment work in Abu Dhabi carries one local wrinkle worth knowing before you pay anyone. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. Press reporting of those rules is clear enough that families should treat the offer of your child's own subject teacher, privately, as a problem rather than an advantage. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before acting on it.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-internal-assessment-home.programmesIntro: Internal assessment is a Diploma Programme phrase, but the habit of being marked against published criteria starts years earlier in an IB school. Where your child sits in that sequence changes what a tutoring hour should be doing, so the programmes below are described by the assessment they produce rather than by age alone.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each carrying an internally assessed component alongside the examination papers. The Theory of Knowledge exhibition and essay and the Extended Essay sit on top as core requirements. The internal components run on school-set deadlines that cluster in the second half of DP1 and the first half of DP2, which is why three of them regularly land in the same fortnight.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts are concentrated in a handful of schools licensed by ADEK on the island, along the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and on Yas Island. That concentration means a subject can be taught by one teacher across the whole year group, so a student who does not click with that teacher's explanation of uncertainty analysis has nowhere else in the building to go.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each scored one to eight, with no percentages anywhere. The Personal Project in the final year is the first piece of long-form independent work most IB students meet, and it rehearses the habits an internal assessment demands: a researchable question, a process record, and a judgement about what the evidence will actually support.
programmes.countryNote: Many Abu Dhabi families arrive mid-MYP from a British or American system and meet criterion marking for the first time. The practical consequence for internal assessment work two years later is a student who has never had to justify a method in writing, which is the skill the DP investigation criteria are built to test.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with the Year 6 exhibition as its culminating piece of collaborative research. Nothing here is externally assessed, and no criterion letters appear. What it does establish is whether a child is comfortable being asked why they chose a method, which is the question that governs criterion marks for the next decade.
programmes.countryNote: PYP provision in Abu Dhabi is spread widely across community schools in Khalifa City, Al Reef and the newer mainland developments. Parents at this stage rarely need subject tutoring; where support helps is English and mathematics fluency, since a Year 6 reading gap is visible in an MYP science criterion C response four years later.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Combines DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and a language portfolio. The reflective project is assessed against published criteria and functions much as an internal assessment does, with a supervisor, an ethical dimension and a word limit.
programmes.countryNote: CP cohorts in the UAE are small and concentrated in a few schools, so a CP student needing support on the reflective project is often the only candidate in the building taking that pathway. Online matching is the practical answer to a cohort of one; a locally resident tutor pool rarely contains the right person.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-internal-assessment-home.subjectsIntro: Every subject's internal component is marked against its own criteria, with its own raw total and its own failure modes. The grid below names the component rather than the subject in general, because "IA help" is not a service — supervision of a Chemistry scientific investigation is. Confirm the current mark totals with your child's coordinator; subject guides are revised.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.levels: HL and SL — the mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Twenty marks across five criteria, worth a fifth of the subject grade at both levels. Most marks are lost on criterion C, personal engagement, and criterion E, use of mathematics: a correct but textbook treatment of a standard result sits in the middle band however neatly it is presented.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.levels: HL and SL — the mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Same twenty marks, same five criteria, a different flavour of risk. AI explorations usually have real data and under-used mathematics. A regression line with no residual analysis and no discussion of why the model is appropriate scores poorly on criterion E even when the dataset is interesting.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: HL and SL — the scientific investigation
subjects.description: One investigation, marked against research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, worth a fifth of the subject grade. The commonest defect is a research question that names neither a measurable dependent variable nor a controlled range, which caps the design criterion before any data exist.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: HL and SL — the scientific investigation
subjects.description: Same criteria as the other sciences, with uncertainty and error propagation doing most of the damage. Students who recorded a burette reading to two decimal places and then quoted a concentration to five significant figures lose analysis marks they could have kept with ten minutes of teaching.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: HL and SL — the scientific investigation
subjects.description: Graphical analysis is where this one is won. A linearised plot with sensible error bars, a gradient used to extract a physical constant, and a comparison against an accepted value will carry the analysis and conclusion criteria. A bar chart of three repeats will not.

subjects.name: History
subjects.levels: HL and SL — the historical investigation
subjects.description: Twenty-five marks in three sections, including an explicit evaluation of two sources by origin, purpose and content. Students write history essays instead and lose the section one marks entirely. The word limit is tight and the reflection section is routinely treated as an afterthought.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.levels: HL and SL — the portfolio of commentaries
subjects.description: Three commentaries on three different units of the syllabus, each on a news article published within a set window, each under a strict word limit. The repeated error is a commentary that summarises the article instead of applying a diagram and analysing it, and three articles that all belong to the same unit.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.levels: HL and SL — the business research or project
subjects.description: Assessed on a real organisation and a real problem, with marks for the quality of the research question and the use of supporting documents. Students pick a global company with no accessible data and then cannot evidence anything, which costs them across several criteria at once.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.levels: HL and SL — individual oral and HL essay
subjects.description: The individual oral turns on a global issue genuinely visible in both extracts, not asserted over them. The HL essay needs a line of inquiry narrow enough to sustain argument. Both are internally assessed and both reward a student who can say what they are arguing in one sentence.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.levels: HL and SL — the experimental study
subjects.description: A replication of a published study, written up with the statistics actually applied rather than described. Marks go missing on the exploration of the original study and on a results section that reports a test without stating why that test suits the design and the data.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.levels: HL and SL — the fieldwork write-up
subjects.description: Built on primary data a student collected themselves, so the method section has to survive scrutiny. The frequent problem in the Gulf is fieldwork designed around a question the local environment cannot answer, which then forces a conclusion the data do not support.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.levels: HL and SL — comparative study and process portfolio
subjects.description: Two internal components rather than one, each with its own page limits and its own criteria. The process portfolio is judged on evidence of experimentation over time, which means a portfolio assembled in the last fortnight reads as exactly that to an examiner.

Buying the wrong shape is the commonest way families waste money on this component: a weekly hour is pointless three days before upload, and an intensive is wasted on a student with no research question.

modes.description: The pattern that produces the clearest evidence. A session every two weeks across the drafting period, each one ending with an annotated version and a short written note. Between sessions the student revises alone, which is what the component is testing. This shape makes grade movement visible because there is a dated sequence of drafts to compare rather than one before-and-after.

sections.heading: What an internal assessment evidence file looks like, and when it should exist
paragraphs: An internal assessment evidence file is not a formal thing the IB requires. It is the set of artefacts a paying parent should be able to see, and it exists whether or not anyone collects it deliberately. If you cannot assemble it after a month of sessions, the sessions are producing conversation rather than progress. The point of naming the artefacts is that each one is binary: it exists or it does not, and its absence tells you something specific rather than leaving you to read a tutor's tone of voice.

The most informative artefact is the dated draft sequence. Three versions a fortnight apart, each with annotation that names a criterion letter, lets you see whether the student is responding to feedback or working around it. A student who receives a comment on criterion D and returns a draft with a longer introduction is avoiding the comment. That is visible in the sequence and invisible in a verbal report. The second most informative artefact is the research question history, because a question that is still moving in week six is the single clearest warning sign in this whole component.

The table below is the file we aim to have in place after four weeks. Where an artefact is missing, the right conversation is about why, not about whether the tutor is nice. A missing change log usually means the student is rewriting from scratch each time instead of revising, which is slower and scores worse. A missing statement of what cannot be fixed usually means nobody has looked honestly at the deadline. Both are fixable in one session if named.

sections.heading: Reading a marked draft when you are not the subject teacher
paragraphs: Most parents in this position are competent, educated adults who cannot judge a Chemistry investigation, and that is entirely reasonable. The useful move is not to learn Chemistry. It is to learn to read the shape of the annotation, which is subject-independent. Good annotation on a draft points at a criterion, quotes the descriptor the paragraph currently satisfies, and says what a higher band would contain. You can check all three of those without knowing anything about titration.

Three tests work on any subject. First, does each comment name a criterion letter? A margin note reading "expand this" is not feedback against anything. Second, does the comment distinguish between a defect of content and a defect of presentation? Those have different costs: a missing uncertainty analysis loses marks, an untidy graph title usually does not. Third, does the comment say what the student should do, or does it say what should be there? The second phrasing is the one that quietly turns into dictation, and it is the form to watch for.

The fourth test is about you rather than the document. After reading the annotation, can you say in one sentence what the next piece of work is? If yes, the supervision is doing its job. If you finish the page knowing only that things are being worked on, ask for the change log and the criterion mapping explicitly. Nobody minds the question, and a tutor who cannot produce either is not keeping records a coordinator would recognise.
bullets: Every comment should name a criterion letter from the subject guide
Content defects and presentation defects cost different amounts; the annotation should distinguish them
"Do this next" is coaching; "this should say that" drifts towards dictation
You should be able to state the next task in one sentence after reading the draft

sections.heading: Criterion letters, raw marks and what each internal component is worth
paragraphs: The single most useful fact about internal assessment is that the marks are not distributed the way students assume. Across the sciences and mathematics, the criteria that reward judgement — evaluation, personal engagement, reflection — carry more weight than students give them, while the criteria that reward neatness carry almost none. A student who spends an extra week formatting and skips the evaluation section has traded marks for comfort. Naming the raw totals makes that trade visible, and it is the gap that nothing in the competing pages on this search fills.

The share of the subject grade also varies more than families expect. A fifth is the common figure, but History is a quarter at Standard Level and a fifth at Higher Level, and the Economics portfolio is close to a third at Standard Level. That matters for how you allocate a limited tutoring budget across six subjects. If one of your child's subjects puts thirty per cent of the grade in a document, that document is the highest-leverage thing a tutoring hour can touch anywhere in the Diploma.

The figures below are drawn from the published IB subject guides. Subject guides are revised, and a school may be teaching a cohort under an older version, so treat the table as the shape of the thing and confirm the exact totals with your child's Diploma coordinator before you plan around them. What will not change is the ranking: judgement criteria outweigh presentation criteria in every single subject.

sections.heading: The authenticity record: versions, dates and one formal round of feedback
paragraphs: The IB's position on internal assessment support is not ambiguous, and it is worth stating plainly because the search results for this query include at least one operation selling finished documents. An internal component must be the student's own work. The supervising teacher may give one round of formal written feedback on a draft, and the student declares the work authentic on submission. Everything a tutor does has to sit comfortably inside that structure, which in practice means the record should look ordinary to anyone who inspects it.

What makes a record look ordinary is a visible history of the student's own revisions. If a document's version history shows gradual change in one voice, with dates spread across weeks, it tells a consistent story. If it shows a thin outline followed by a polished submission appearing in a single sitting, it raises a question the student has to answer. So the practical rule for our sessions is that the student holds the keyboard. A tutor annotates, asks, teaches the missing method, models the same technique on a different example, and then stops. Nothing a tutor says arrives in the document as a sentence.

This is also the honest answer to the question families ask most nervously: will the school know a tutor was involved? Possibly, and it does not matter. There is nothing to hide in paying for teaching. What would matter is a document whose voice does not match the student's class work, or a methodology section describing statistics the student cannot explain when asked. Both are detectable in a five-minute conversation with a supervisor, which is exactly why the only safe form of help is the kind that leaves the student able to defend every line.
bullets: The student holds the keyboard in every session; a tutor annotates and questions
Method teaching happens on a worked example that is not the student's own task
Version history should show gradual change in a single voice across weeks
If a student cannot explain a paragraph aloud, it should not be in the document

sections.heading: An IA term counted backwards from your school's upload deadline
paragraphs: Nobody ranking for this search counts the term backwards, and it is the most useful planning tool available. The date that governs everything is not the examination session. It is your school's internal upload deadline, which sits weeks earlier and is set by your coordinator, not by the IB. Ask for it in writing at the start of the year. Every milestone below is counted from that date, and the arithmetic is what tells you whether a plan is realistic or wishful.

The common failure is arithmetic rather than effort. A student who starts an investigation six weeks before upload has not left room for data collection to fail once, which it usually does. A student who settles a research question in week two has bought themselves the ability to lose a fortnight and recover. This is the single thing a parent can control, and it costs nothing: insist on a research question in writing early, and treat its continued movement as the warning sign it is.

Note that IB session and results dates are deliberately absent from this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project is confirmed from the IB itself. Abu Dhabi schools predominantly enter candidates for the May session, and your coordinator holds the authoritative calendar. Where Cambridge or Pearson dates matter to a sibling sitting IGCSE, those boards publish live timetables and should be read directly rather than restated here.

sections.heading: ADEK, your school's internal calendar, and the teacher you may not pay
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, ADEK, which the UAE government's own portal describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. That is worth knowing for two reasons. The first is that ADEK publishes an inspection record for your child's school, and an inspection report is a far better guide to how well a Diploma programme is run than any marketing page. The second is the ethics rule, which has direct consequences for internal assessment support.

Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, with teachers tutoring outside school hours required to hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document before relying on the exact wording. The direction of travel is unambiguous enough that an offer of your own child's supervisor, privately and for money, should be declined.

The permit itself is worth understanding, because it is the one compliance question a parent can actually check. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which introduced private tuition work permits. The UAE government portal states the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', is the official application route.

The MoHRE private tuition permit is free of charge and granted for two years
No published fine schedule exists, so treat any quoted figure as unverified
Your child's own subject teacher is the wrong person to pay for internal assessment help

sections.heading: What internal assessment supervision costs around Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for this family of searches publish no price at all, and two of the remaining ones quote United States dollars, a currency no Abu Dhabi family transacts in. So here is the market in dirhams, with every figure attributed to whoever published it. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list. Our own model runs on a free first lesson and a consultation that quotes against the subject, level and component, because an hour of Mathematics exploration supervision and an hour of general revision are not the same product.

Document supervision usually sits at the upper end of whatever band a provider quotes, for a straightforward reason: it requires someone who has marked against those criteria, and it consumes preparation time outside the session reading a draft. An hour of supervision that includes a read of eight pages and written annotation is not an hour of the tutor's time. Any provider quoting a single flat rate for all tutoring is either absorbing that or not doing it.

The other number worth knowing is how little of this component you may actually need to buy. A diagnostic read plus a pre-upload check is two or three hours and is sufficient for a competent student whose research question is sound. Fortnightly supervision across a term is the right purchase when the student has stalled or the method teaching is genuinely missing. Buying a weekly hour from October to April for a student who needed three hours in total is the commonest waste in this market.

sections.heading: Online document work against a visiting tutor, on the same draft
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and every one of our country pages says so. That is a constraint worth defending rather than apologising for, and internal assessment work is the component where the case is strongest. A document is already a shared object. Two people reading the same screen, with a cursor and a comment thread, is not a degraded version of sitting side by side at a kitchen table. For annotation work it is better, because everything said leaves a record.

The second argument is about who you get. Abu Dhabi has a finite number of people who have marked a Physics scientific investigation against the current criteria, and the subset of those who will drive to Al Falah on a Tuesday evening is smaller still. Matching online removes the driving radius from the selection criteria entirely. A family in Khalifa City gets a specialist in their child's actual component rather than the best available person within a twenty-minute commute.

The third argument is the one families discover for themselves after a term. A visiting tutor's hour includes travel the family pays for in money and in schedule rigidity: the slot cannot move, because the tutor has a route. An online slot moves. During Ramadan it moves to after Iftar. In the fortnight before an upload deadline it can become two short sessions instead of one long one, which is what document work actually wants. None of that is available when someone is driving across the emirate to reach you.

sections.heading: When the evidence says the sessions are not working
paragraphs: A page that sells supervision should also say when to stop buying it, because the evidence file makes that judgement possible and almost nobody publishes the criteria. Four weeks is a fair window. By then there should be a dated draft sequence, annotation mapped to criteria, and a change log. If all three exist and the drafts are still not moving, the problem is not the supervision and more supervision will not fix it.

There are three usual diagnoses. The first is that the subject knowledge underneath is missing, so the student cannot act on feedback about analysis because they do not understand the analysis. The fix is subject teaching, not document supervision, and it is a different purchase. The second is that the research question was never viable, in which case the honest move is to change it if the deadline allows and to optimise within a capped mark if it does not. The third is motivational: the student does not want to work on this and is performing compliance in sessions. Nothing bought by the hour fixes that, and saying so is more useful than selling another block.

Coverage is the last honest disclosure. Abu Dhabi does not contain a resident specialist for every Higher Level component, and the thinner pathways — Visual Arts process portfolios, the Career-related Programme reflective project, less common language A combinations — sometimes have no local match at all. When that happens we say so before you commit, name the match time, and where the right specialist is based outside the UAE, we tell you that too. No competitor page in this cluster discloses a coverage limit. It is the easiest trust signal available and it costs only candour.

Missing subject knowledge needs teaching, not more document review
A non-viable research question should be changed early or optimised within its ceiling
Coverage gaps and match times are disclosed before you commit, not after

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Not "IB help" but "Chemistry HL scientific investigation, draft due in five weeks". That sentence is what makes a match possible. If you also know your school's internal upload deadline, send it; everything in the plan is counted backwards from that date rather than from the examination session.

process.title: A free first lesson that returns a diagnosis
process.description: The first session is a read of whatever exists, against the published criteria, ending in a written note: what band each criterion currently sits in, what would move it, and what cannot be fixed in the time available. If the answer is that you do not need ongoing supervision, you will be told that.

process.title: Agree the shape, not just the hours
process.description: Fortnightly supervision, a one-off diagnostic, method teaching or a pre-upload check are different products with different prices. Picking the wrong shape is how families overspend on this component. The shape is agreed in writing along with a review point, usually four weeks out.

process.title: Check the file at the review point
process.description: At four weeks, look at the artefacts rather than at how the sessions felt. Dated drafts, criterion annotation, a change log, and a statement of what is out of reach. If any of the four is missing, that is the conversation to have, and it is a fair one to raise with us directly.

process.title: Change the plan when the evidence says to
process.description: Supervision that is not moving a draft should be swapped for subject teaching, reduced to a pre-upload check, or stopped. A tutor who proposes more hours in response to no movement is not reading the file. Rematching is normal and carries no penalty.

whyPoints.description: Every session produces a dated draft, criterion-letter annotation and a two-line change log. That is the deliverable, not a feeling that things are going well. It also means a disagreement about whether the work is improving can be settled by looking rather than by arguing.

whyPoints.description: A Mathematics exploration, a historical investigation and a Visual Arts process portfolio need three different people. Matching online instead of by driving distance means the selection is made on who has marked that component, which is the only criterion that predicts useful supervision.

whyPoints.description: Some Higher Level components have no resident specialist in Abu Dhabi. When that is true for your child's subject, you hear it before you commit, along with the match time and where the right person is based. No page in this search result does that, which is why it is worth doing.

faqs.question: What should I have in my hand after four weeks of internal assessment sessions?
faqs.answer: Four things, all of them documents. A dated sequence of at least three drafts. Annotation on each one that names a criterion letter and says which descriptor band the passage currently satisfies. A change log of two lines per session saying what moved between versions. And a written statement of what cannot be fixed in the time remaining. If you have all four and the drafts are visibly different from each other, the supervision is working. If you have reassurance and no documents, that is the conversation to have at the four-week mark rather than in the week before upload.

faqs.question: How many marks is each internal component worth across my son's six Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: It varies more than families expect, which is why it is worth checking subject by subject. Around a fifth of the subject grade is the common figure for the sciences and for both mathematics courses. History is a quarter at Standard Level and a fifth at Higher Level. The Economics portfolio of three commentaries is closer to a third at Standard Level. Raw totals differ too: twenty marks for a mathematical exploration, twenty-four for a scientific investigation, twenty-five for a historical investigation. Confirm the current figures with your Diploma coordinator, since subject guides are revised and a cohort may be taught under an older version.

faqs.question: My daughter's supervisor has already given the one formal round of written feedback. Is a tutor still allowed to look at the draft?
faqs.answer: Yes. The one-formal-round rule governs what the supervising teacher provides, not what other teaching a student may receive. A tutor can read the draft, annotate it against the criteria, explain what the supervisor's comments mean in practice, and teach a method the student never covered. What a tutor cannot do is supply sentences that end up in the document, or rework a passage so the voice stops being the student's. The practical test is whether your daughter can explain every line aloud afterwards. If she can, the help was teaching.

faqs.question: How does a tutor annotate a draft without crossing the IB's authenticity line?
faqs.answer: By pointing rather than supplying. An annotation that reads "criterion D asks you to evaluate the method; this paragraph describes it instead" tells the student what is wrong and leaves the work to them. An annotation that supplies the replacement sentence does not. In practice the student holds the keyboard throughout, methods are taught on a worked example that is not their own task, and nothing said in a session arrives in the document verbatim. The version history should show gradual change in one voice across weeks, which is what an ordinary, honest record looks like.

faqs.question: What does a comment about criterion B on a Chemistry investigation actually mean?
faqs.answer: Criterion letters refer to the published descriptors in the subject guide, and each one rewards a different kind of thinking rather than a different section of the document. In the sciences the criteria cover research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A comment on the design criterion is usually about whether the research question fixes a measurable range and controls the obvious confounders. A comment on evaluation is about whether weaknesses are identified with a specific effect on the result, rather than listed as generic apologies. Ask the tutor to quote the descriptor; a comment that cannot be traced to one is not feedback against anything.

faqs.question: Can I see the version history of my child's exploration?
faqs.answer: You can, and it is the most informative five minutes available to a parent on this component. Any document platform keeps a revision record. What you are looking for is a gradual pattern: edits spread over weeks, in one voice, with the volume of change tapering as the deadline approaches. What should prompt a question is a thin outline followed by a finished document appearing in one sitting. You are not auditing your child. You are checking that the record tells a story they could explain to a coordinator, which protects them far more than it inconveniences them.

faqs.question: Three internal deadlines fall in the same fortnight at my son's Abu Dhabi school. What gets priority?
faqs.answer: Rank them by three things in order: the share of the subject grade, how far each document already is, and whether the remaining work needs data or only writing. A component carrying a third of a subject grade beats one carrying a fifth. A document missing its data collection cannot be rescued by a late weekend, while one needing a rewritten evaluation can. Then speak to the coordinator. Internal deadlines are set by the school, not the IB, and a compressed cluster is often an artefact of calendar-building rather than a fixed requirement. Coordinators move them more often than families expect.

faqs.question: What does internal assessment supervision cost per hour around Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 or more; Bestimate's 2026 rate work puts visiting tutors at AED 180-350 and some home tutors as high as AED 500, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Document supervision tends to sit at the upper end of whichever band applies, because reading and annotating eight pages consumes preparation time outside the session. Those are market figures from the providers named, not IB Gram's prices. Ours are quoted after a free first lesson.

faqs.question: Why is there no in-home option in Abu Dhabi when other providers advertise one?
faqs.answer: Because IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and our country pages have said so consistently. For internal assessment work specifically that is an advantage rather than a compromise. A document is a shared object already, so two people reading the same screen with a comment thread lose nothing and gain a permanent record. More importantly, matching without a driving radius means your child gets someone who has marked their exact component, not the best available person who will travel to your area on a Tuesday.

faqs.question: Is my child's own subject teacher at an Abu Dhabi school allowed to take paid sessions on his investigation?
faqs.answer: Treat that offer as a problem. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers giving paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. Beyond compliance there is a straightforward conflict: the person who marks the document should not also be paid to improve it.

faqs.question: The data are collected but no analysis has started and there are five weeks to upload. Is that recoverable?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, and more comfortably than families fear. Five weeks with data in hand is a better position than ten weeks with a vague question. The work now is sequential: process the data, decide and justify the analysis, write the conclusion against the actual numbers, then evaluate honestly. Three or four focused sessions across those five weeks is a realistic plan, with the student working between them. What is not recoverable in five weeks is a research question that cannot be answered by the data collected. That is why the first session is a read rather than a lesson.

faqs.question: How do I tell the difference between a tutor who is coaching and one who is quietly taking over?
faqs.answer: Read the annotation and listen to your child. Coaching language names a criterion and asks a question: what does this paragraph claim, and where is the evidence for it? Taking-over language supplies the answer in finished prose. The second signal is comprehension. Ask your child to explain one paragraph of the current draft aloud, without the document in front of them. If they can, the work is theirs. If they cannot explain a method or a statistical choice that appears in their own document, something has gone in that should not have, and it needs removing before submission rather than after.

faqs.question: Which permit must a private tutor in the UAE hold, and can a parent verify it?
faqs.answer: The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The UAE government portal states it is granted free of charge for two years and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure quoted to you. Ask your tutor directly, and read MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', for the official route.

faqs.question: Can supervision sessions move to post-Iftar times during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Diploma candidates it often has to, because a stretch of the drafting period can fall inside Ramadan in any given year. Online delivery is what makes that straightforward: a slot that shifts to nine or ten in the evening costs nobody a drive across the emirate after a long fast. Many families also use the month differently, trading a weekly hour for shorter, more frequent reviews at a quieter time of night. Tell us before the month starts rather than during it, so the slot is rebooked rather than cancelled.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist for my child's Higher Level component is free this term?
faqs.answer: You are told before you commit, with a match time and an honest description of the alternative. Abu Dhabi has no resident specialist for every Higher Level component, and the thinner pathways — Visual Arts process portfolios, the Career-related Programme reflective project, less common language A combinations — are the ones most likely to come up empty locally. Where the right person is based outside the UAE, we say so and you decide. What we will not do is hand a Visual Arts portfolio to a generalist and call it a match, which is the failure mode this disclosure exists to prevent.

faqs.question: Should we buy supervision for all six of my daughter's internal components?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not. Rank the six by how much of the subject grade each one carries and by how shaky the draft is, then buy for the top one or two. A competent student with a sound research question often needs nothing more than a diagnostic read and a pre-upload check, which is two or three hours in total. Fortnightly supervision across a term is the right purchase when a student has genuinely stalled or when the underlying method was never taught. Spreading a budget thinly across six documents produces six lightly reviewed drafts and no movement anywhere.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-internal-assessment-home.closingHeading: Start with the draft, not with a package
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-internal-assessment-home.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB DP internal assessment home tutor in Abu Dhabi, the fastest useful step is to send the component, the level and the school's internal upload deadline, and let the first lesson be a read of whatever exists. It is free, it ends in a written note against each criterion, and it sometimes concludes that you do not need ongoing supervision at all. Lessons are one-to-one and online, on Gulf Standard Time, for families across Saadiyat Island, Al Reem Island, Khalifa City, Al Raha and the mainland communities. Nothing in the document will be written by anyone but your child.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tuto.tutorsIntro: The tutors below coach internal assessments by criterion in their own subject: research design in the sciences, use of mathematics in an exploration, source evaluation in History. Each works from the student's draft and the published descriptors, and each marks rather than edits.

intro.heading: IA marks are lost in specific places, not spread thinly
paragraphs: A disappointing internal assessment mark almost never means the work was bad everywhere. It means two criteria out of four or five scored near the bottom while the rest scored respectably, and the total came out middling. That is why generic help on an IA rarely moves anything: a tutor who improves the writing in a piece whose research design was flawed has polished the part that was already fine.

The criteria are public and the school marks against them. A science investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each, twenty-four in total. A mathematics exploration is marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, twenty marks in total with use of mathematics carrying the largest single share. History runs three sections with the investigation itself carrying most of the weight. Each scheme has its own vulnerable spots and they are consistent from cohort to cohort.

Across all of them, five failure modes recur. A topic too broad to produce a controlled, answerable question. Raw data presented without processing. A conclusion that restates the hypothesis rather than interpreting the evidence. An evaluation that lists generic weaknesses, human error being the worst of them, instead of examining the method that was actually used. And reflection or engagement written in the final hour, after the marks for it were already available during the work.

The diagnostic consequence is practical. Before buying hours, find out which criteria the school's feedback actually marked down. Most Abu Dhabi schools return a criterion-level breakdown on a first draft, and that sheet tells you whether you are buying research design, data processing or evaluation. A family that arrives with that breakdown gets a useful first session; a family that arrives with my child needs IA help gets a session spent finding the sheet.

Timing changes the answer as much as the criterion does. An investigation still at the question stage has every mark in play, because the design can be narrowed and the apparatus checked. The same investigation three days before the school's internal deadline has perhaps a third of its marks still movable: the evaluation can be made specific, the conclusion can be made to interpret rather than restate, and the presentation can be tidied, but the design, the data and the mathematics chosen are fixed. Families almost always buy at the second point and almost never at the first, which is the inverse of where the value sits.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with the draft and the descriptors on a shared screen. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because IA coaching is screen work by nature: the document, the spreadsheet, the graph and the criterion sit side by side, and nothing about that improves by being in the same room. What matters far more is that the tutor teaches the subject the IA belongs to.

Mathematics exploration: five criteria totalling twenty marks, use of mathematics the largest
Most IA marks are lost in two criteria, not across the whole piece
