Sequencing by marks at risk rather than by the nearest date is the single most useful planning decision a family makes in that term.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP is entirely criterion-marked, with four criteria per subject and published descriptors, so a student arriving in DP1 from the MYP already understands that marks come from a descriptor rather than from a percentage. The sciences criterion on inquiring and designing is a direct ancestor of IA research design.
programmes.countryNote: This is the clearest advantage an Abu Dhabi continuum student has over a transferring student, and it is routinely wasted. A student who has written MYP criterion C reflections for five years can read an IA descriptor fluently. A student arriving from an examination-only system in DP1 often cannot, and that gap shows up in the first IA draft rather than in a test.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No formal assessment of this kind, but the PYP's inquiry cycle teaches the habit an IA depends on: asking a question narrow enough to investigate, planning how to find out, and saying what the finding did and did not show. Those three steps are the structure of every internal assessment in the diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving into an Abu Dhabi continuum school part-way through primary sometimes see the inquiry approach as unstructured compared with what they left. The payoff arrives much later, in whether a sixteen-year-old can narrow their own question without being handed one, which is where IA marks begin.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students take DP courses and therefore sit the internally assessed components belonging to those courses, but the CP core replaces Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay with a reflective project and other components assessed on their own criteria.
programmes.countryNote: The practical point in Abu Dhabi is that a CP student's workload shape is different: fewer internally assessed subject components, plus a reflective project with its own deadline. Support bought against the wrong set of criteria is wasted, so confirm with the coordinator which components your child is actually registered for.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tuto.subjectsIntro: Each subject's internal assessment is a different piece of work with its own criteria. These are the ones Abu Dhabi diploma students most often need help with, and the criterion that usually costs them.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A scientific investigation marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The habitual loss is research design: a question with uncontrolled variables, often because the organism or the environment refused to cooperate and the method was not adjusted in the write-up.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same four criteria as the other sciences. Loss concentrates in data analysis, where uncertainties and propagation are handled loosely, and in evaluation, where a weakness is named without being connected to the data it actually distorted.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The investigation most likely to produce a clean relationship and the least likely to interrogate it. Conclusion is the vulnerable criterion: a gradient is calculated, matched to theory, and never situated in the wider physics that would make it meaningful.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the most marks and is where HL students lose by using mathematics comfortably below the level of their course.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same five criteria. The characteristic loss is reflection: a student models a real situation competently, produces an answer, and never asks whether the model was appropriate or what its limits were, which is the criterion in plain sight.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A historical investigation in three sections, with the investigation itself carrying the bulk of the marks. Source evaluation is where it is won: value and limitation handled by origin, purpose and content rather than by labelling a source primary or secondary.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Commentaries on published news extracts, each inside a tight word limit. The recurring failure is explaining the theory and forgetting to apply it to the specific article, or choosing an extract too thin to carry a diagram and an evaluation.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: A report on an experimental study with human participants, which means school ethics approval sits on the critical path. The commonest cost is a design approved late, compressing the analysis and the discussion into a weekend.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral, recorded at school on a global issue through two texts, with an additional HL essay at higher level. Marks go on whether the global issue is genuinely traced through both extracts rather than announced and abandoned.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: A fieldwork report built on data the student collected, which makes site choice decisive. Abu Dhabi offers workable urban and coastal fieldwork, but a site chosen for convenience rather than for the question costs marks in the written analysis.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: Internally assessed components alongside the exhibition, with limits set in the current subject guide. The habitual loss is description of works rather than comparison and analysis, which is the same discipline problem that affects arts essays generally.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tuto.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi areas our IA students come from
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tuto.regionsIntro: IA enquiries from this emirate arrive in waves tied to school internal deadlines rather than to geography. These are the areas they come from, and what local scheduling does to a session.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The largest volume of IA enquiries in the emirate, across several schools with different internal deadline calendars. Buses home between 3:30pm and 4:15pm make a 5pm or 6pm session workable on school nights.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Short commutes and dense diploma numbers. Requests here skew towards science investigations, and often arrive with the school's criterion-level feedback already in hand, which makes the first session twice as useful.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Mature diploma cohorts with experienced IA practice. Enquiries tend to be students chasing the top band on one criterion rather than students in difficulty, and the work is usually evaluation or reflection.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Mainland corridor families running several timetables at once. A fixed slot through the IA fortnight beats flexibility, because an investigation left for a week loses its thread and the student restarts the analysis.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Established island neighbourhoods near long-running schools. Traffic on and off the island at 3pm to 4pm makes a fixed afternoon arrangement unreliable, which online delivery removes as a factor.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Long bus routes and later arrivals home, so sessions run after 6pm. Weekend mornings work well for data-processing work, which needs an uninterrupted stretch rather than a tired hour.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Substantial diploma population with a heavy science bias in IA requests. Feasibility is the recurring theme: whether the planned investigation can actually run with the apparatus the school has available.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer campuses with IA practice still settling, which shows up as inconsistent draft feedback between departments. Students here benefit most from being taught to read the descriptor themselves.

schoolClusters.city: Mainland corridor diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: The biggest IA cohorts in the emirate and the widest spread of internal deadline calendars. This is where deadline collisions are most acute, and where sequencing by marks at risk matters most.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Corniche diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Long-established practice and detailed criterion-level draft feedback in most departments. Students from this cluster usually arrive knowing which criterion scored low, which makes targeted work possible from the first session.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Yas and Al Reem campuses
schoolClusters.note: Newer schools with growing diploma numbers and laboratory provision that varies by campus. Investigation feasibility is a live question here, and it is cheaper to settle before a method is written than after.

modes.title: Criterion diagnostic, one session
modes.description: A single session that reads the draft against the published descriptors and reports which criteria are scoring low and why. The output is a written note naming the criterion, the evidence in the draft and the specific change required. Many families need nothing beyond this.

modes.title: Design and feasibility block, before the work begins
modes.description: Two or three sessions in the planning phase: narrowing the question, controlling the variables, confirming the method can run with the apparatus the school actually has, and checking that the data the design produces can be processed meaningfully.

modes.title: Analysis and evaluation block, after data collection
modes.description: Two to four sessions on the half of the mark scheme that students neglect: processing raw data correctly, handling uncertainty, writing a conclusion that interprets rather than restates, and an evaluation grounded in the method actually used.

sections.heading: The five ways an internal assessment loses marks, ranked
paragraphs: Across subjects and across cohorts, the same five failures account for the large majority of lost IA marks. They are worth ranking because the ranking tells a family where to spend attention, and because four of the five can be prevented at a stage when prevention is nearly free.

First and most expensive is a topic too broad to control. A question that cannot name its independent variable, or that covers a decade of history, or that models an entire market, fails at the design criterion and then poisons everything downstream: the data cannot be processed cleanly, so the conclusion cannot interpret it, so the evaluation has nothing specific to evaluate. One flawed decision in week one costs marks in three criteria.

Second is raw data presented as analysis. A table of measurements and a scatter plot are not data analysis; processing is. Means with uncertainties, gradients with their meaning, appropriate graph types, and a clear line from the numbers to the claim. Students who collect carefully and process lightly lose a whole criterion while believing the work was thorough.

Third is the conclusion that restates the hypothesis. The temperature increased the rate, as predicted, is not a conclusion in the sense the criterion means. The criterion wants interpretation, a link to accepted subject knowledge, and an honest statement of what the data supports and how strongly.

Fourth is the generic evaluation. Human error, more time, better equipment: these phrases appear in thousands of IAs and earn nothing, because they are not about this investigation. Fifth is reflection and engagement written in the final hour, which is the cheapest criterion in the diploma to score and the most commonly thrown away.

The table below maps each failure to the criteria it damages and to the point at which it can still be fixed. Read the last column before buying hours: two of these are fully recoverable in a week and two are not.

sections.heading: The science investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The scientific investigation in Biology, Chemistry and Physics is marked on four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Twenty-four marks in total, and the balance is the thing to notice. Half the available marks sit after the data has been collected, which is the half most students treat as writing up.

Research design asks for a focused question, identified and controlled variables, and a method with enough detail that someone else could repeat it. The commonest loss here is a method lifted from a class practical sheet and lightly adapted, which signals that the student did not design anything. The second is a question whose variables cannot actually be held constant, discovered during collection and never acknowledged in the write-up.

Data analysis rewards processing: calculations shown, uncertainties handled consistently, graphs chosen because they reveal the relationship rather than because the software offered them, and enough repetition to say something about reliability. A student who records three trials and averages them without reference to spread has processed arithmetically and not scientifically.

Conclusion wants interpretation set against accepted subject knowledge, with the strength of the claim matched to the quality of the evidence. Evaluation wants the weaknesses of this method, their specific effect on these results, and improvements that are realistic and targeted. The difference between a low and a high evaluation is almost always specificity: not the measurements were imprecise, but the thermometer's resolution was the limiting factor on the smaller temperature intervals, which compressed the differences the question depended on.

Word limits apply to these investigations and are set in the current subject guide, with the sciences working to a limit in the region of three thousand words. Confirm the figure and what it includes with your child's teacher, since appendices, tables and captions are treated differently between subjects and guides are revised.

sections.heading: The mathematics exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The exploration is a different animal from a science investigation and students frequently approach it as though it were an essay about maths. It is marked on five criteria totalling twenty marks, and the largest single allocation is use of mathematics. That is the criterion that decides whether the piece reads as a diploma-level exploration or as a well-presented project.

Use of mathematics rewards mathematics at the level of the course, used correctly, with understanding demonstrated rather than asserted. The characteristic HL failure is a student exploring something genuinely interesting with mathematics drawn from two years earlier. The characteristic SL failure is the reverse: a reach into unfamiliar mathematics copied without understanding, which the criterion penalises harder than modest mathematics handled well.

Mathematical communication is where tidy students lose marks they did not know were available. Symbols must be defined, notation must be consistent, calculator and software syntax must not leak into the formal mathematics, and graphs need labels and scales that mean something. None of this is difficult and all of it is mechanical, which makes it the best value on the sheet.

Personal engagement and reflection together carry a meaningful share of the twenty marks and are the two criteria most often abandoned. Engagement is not enthusiasm in an introduction; it is evidence of the student's own thinking in the choices made. Reflection is not a paragraph at the end; it is a thread through the work, asking at each stage whether the mathematics did what was wanted and what its limits were. The table sets out all five with what each rewards.

On length, the guidance is expressed in pages rather than words and sits in the region of twelve to twenty for a typical exploration. Treat it as guidance on scale rather than a target to hit, and confirm the current figure through your coordinator.

sections.heading: Topic choice decides the mark before any work is done
paragraphs: If a family can influence only one thing about an internal assessment, it should be the topic, and the window for that is short. A question narrow enough to be controlled, with data the student can actually obtain and mathematics or theory at the level of the course, sets a ceiling on the whole piece. A broad question sets a low one that no amount of later effort raises.

The practical test is whether the student can state the question in one sentence with its variables named. In the sciences that means an independent variable, a dependent variable and the things being held constant. In History it means a question about a bounded body of sources. In Economics it means one article, one diagram, one piece of theory. In mathematics it means a specific mathematical object or relationship rather than an area of interest.

The second test is feasibility, and in Abu Dhabi it is usually about apparatus and approval. A method requiring equipment the school laboratory does not hold, reagents it will not sanction, or ethics approval for human participants that has not been requested, is a design that will be discovered in week six. Settling this before a method is written is nearly free. Settling it afterwards is a restart.

The third is whether the student cares. Personal engagement is an explicit criterion in the mathematics exploration and an implicit advantage everywhere else, because a student working on something they chose produces better reflection and more honest evaluation. A topic selected from a departmental list to save a decision tends to produce a competent, forgettable piece in the middle band.

Pick something the student will still care about in eight weeks

sections.heading: Why human error is the worst sentence in an IA
paragraphs: Every evaluation criterion in the diploma rewards the same thing: a specific account of how the method used affected the results obtained, and improvements that address that specific effect. Every weak evaluation does the same thing instead: names a universal limitation that would apply to any investigation ever conducted.

Human error is the worst offender because it explains nothing and implies that the student does not know which part of their own procedure was unreliable. More time and better equipment are close behind. A marker reading those phrases cannot award the criterion, not out of strictness, but because there is nothing there to credit.

What earns the criterion is unglamorous and specific. The instrument's resolution relative to the differences being measured. The time between preparing a solution and using it. The fact that the room temperature drifted by several degrees across the afternoon because the measurements ran from one to five. A variable that was supposed to be controlled and demonstrably was not, with the evidence in the data to show it.

That means evaluation depends on a record kept during the work, not reconstructed after it. A student who notes what went wrong as it happens writes a strong evaluation in an hour. A student who finishes collecting and then tries to remember writes human error, because that is all that is left. The cheapest intervention available in any IA is a running log of problems, dated, kept while the work is live.

sections.heading: What the school sends, what the IB checks, and what that means for a mark
paragraphs: Internal assessment means marked by the school, not marked loosely. The teacher applies the published criteria, the school submits marks and a sample of the work, and the IB checks the school's application of the standard. Where a school has applied the descriptors generously or harshly across its cohort, the IB can adjust that school's marks for the component.

Two consequences follow for a family. The first is that a draft mark from a teacher is an indication rather than a promise, and a student should not plan their overall grade around an optimistic internal figure. The second is that arguing with a teacher about a mark is rarely productive, because the teacher is applying a standard they are also accountable to.

The useful response is to work on the criterion rather than the number. If data analysis scored in the middle band, the question is what the descriptor for the band above actually asks for and whether the draft can show it. That is a concrete conversation with a concrete answer, and it is the whole content of a productive IA session.

The school also keeps control of what is submitted and when. Internal deadlines are set by the school inside the IB's submission window and are usually earlier than students assume, sometimes by weeks. We publish no IB submission or results dates on this page: the IB's own site is the authority and it does not permit automated checking, so any date printed here would be second-hand. Ask the coordinator.

sections.heading: Collision weeks in the Abu Dhabi diploma calendar
paragraphs: A full diploma candidate completes six internal assessments plus the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge components. Schools in Abu Dhabi set their internal deadlines independently by department, and the predictable result is that three criterion-marked drafts land in the same fortnight, usually alongside mock examinations.

Sequencing matters more than effort in that fortnight, and the right rule is marks at risk rather than nearest deadline. An IA worth thirty per cent of a subject grade with two criteria scoring low has more recoverable marks than one worth twenty per cent that is already solid. Students default to the nearest date, which is how a strong piece gets polished while a weak one is submitted unimproved.

Ramadan adds a specific local layer. School hours shorten, afternoon energy drops and the productive working window moves to after Iftar. Where Ramadan falls across an IA deadline cluster, the families who plan for it keep their sessions and move them later in the evening rather than pausing for the month. Data processing and writing go better in the morning during that period, so weekend slots earn their place.

The practical sequence we recommend is simple. Ask each department for the internal deadline in writing. List the IAs with their weighting and the criteria currently scoring low. Work on the two with the most recoverable marks. Hand the solid one a checklist and submit it. That ordering is unglamorous and it reliably outperforms working on whichever deadline is closest.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with an internal assessment, and what nobody may do
paragraphs: Internal assessment is where the IB's academic-honesty rules bite hardest, because the work is produced over weeks away from supervision and the school has to authenticate it as the student's own. A candidate found to have submitted work that is not theirs faces an IB malpractice process whose consequences can reach the whole diploma rather than the single subject.

The legitimate scope of a tutor is wide and specific. Teaching the subject content the investigation needs. Explaining what a descriptor band actually asks for. Marking the student's own draft against the criteria and saying which band it sits in and why. Asking whether a conclusion is supported by the data. Pointing out that an evaluation is generic. Teaching how to process data, propagate an uncertainty or structure a reflection, using a different example.

Outside that scope: supplying text, rewriting a section, providing the data, performing the calculations, building an outline for the student to fill, and editing a draft to completion. The test is whether the student could explain and reproduce every part of what is submitted. IB Gram does not supply completed coursework in any subject and does not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, assessment instruments, mark schemes or exemplar work.

This is also the part of the market a parent should examine most carefully. Operations advertising against searches like this one sell finished internally assessed work outright, at a price, with a turnaround. That is not premium tutoring. It is a malpractice exposure transferred onto the student, and the student is the one the IB's procedures apply to.

sections.heading: What one session can move, and what it cannot
paragraphs: Families usually ask how many sessions an IA needs. The better question is what stage the work is at, because the stage determines which criteria are still in play. An investigation at the design stage has every mark available. The same investigation three days before submission has perhaps a third of them.

Before data collection, everything is movable: the question can be narrowed, the variables controlled, the apparatus checked, the processing route planned. This is where two or three hours buy more than ten hours later, and it is the stage families least often buy, because nothing looks wrong yet.

After collection and before the draft, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation are fully available, which in the sciences is three of four criteria and eighteen of twenty-four marks. Research design is fixed, but an honest account of its limitations feeds the evaluation, so even a flawed design is not wasted if it is reported accurately.

In the final week, what remains is presentation, communication, the conclusion's wording and the evaluation's specificity. Those are real marks and they are worth a session. What is gone is the design, the data and the mathematics chosen. A provider who promises substantial improvement at that stage is either misunderstanding the criteria or offering to do the work, and the table below is the honest version.

There is one more case worth naming, because it comes up every year in Abu Dhabi. A student with a genuinely unusable design, discovered with weeks rather than days remaining, sometimes has the option of a reduced but salvageable version: a narrower question using the data already collected, agreed with the teacher. That is a conversation with the department, not with a tutor, and it is almost always better than submitting an investigation whose design the student cannot defend.

Where the recoverable marks no longer justify the hours, we say so. A family in the last week of a solid IA is usually better served by a presentation checklist and an hour on evaluation wording than by a block of sessions, and the time saved is better spent on examined papers where a grade boundary is still in reach.

process.title: Bring the school's criterion feedback
process.description: Most Abu Dhabi departments return a criterion-level breakdown on a first draft. That sheet names which criteria scored low, which is the whole starting point. A family that arrives with it gets a working first session; without it, the first session is spent reconstructing what the teacher already said.

process.title: Say what stage the work is at
process.description: Question not approved, data collected but unprocessed, or draft returned with a mark. The stage determines which criteria are still available and therefore how many hours are worth buying. We will tell you when the answer is one session rather than six.

process.title: Match on the subject, not on IA in general
process.description: A science investigation needs a scientist who has marked research design. A mathematics exploration needs someone who can judge whether the mathematics is at course level. There is no general internal assessment tutor, and treating it as one subject is the commonest matching error.

process.title: Score the draft against the descriptors
process.description: The first working session reads the student's draft against the published criteria, states which band each criterion sits in, and explains what the band above asks for. The output is written, ranked by marks recoverable per hour, and usable without us.

process.title: Work the criteria that are still open
process.description: Design work before collection, processing and conclusion after it, evaluation and specificity at the end. We will not sell design hours on a finished investigation, and we will say plainly when the recoverable marks no longer justify the sessions.

process.title: Hand back a checklist and close
process.description: Presentation and communication marks can be secured by the student from a checklist. When the analytical work is done we end the block and say so in writing, rather than continuing through the deadline on an open arrangement.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis by criterion, in writing
whyPoints.description: Every engagement starts by scoring the student's own draft against the published descriptors and naming the band each criterion sits in. A parent gets a written note of which criteria are losing marks and what the band above requires, which is checkable rather than impressionistic.

whyPoints.title: Subject specialists, not IA generalists
whyPoints.description: Research design in Biology, uncertainty propagation in Physics, source evaluation in History and use of mathematics in an exploration are four different judgements. We match on the subject because the criteria can only be applied by someone who teaches it.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what each stage can still change
whyPoints.description: In the final week, presentation and evaluation wording are available and the design is not. We say that rather than selling hours against criteria that have closed, and we publish the stage-by-stage version of it on this page.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on authorship
whyPoints.description: We teach, explain descriptors, mark drafts and question reasoning. We do not supply text, provide data, perform calculations, build outlines to be filled in or edit to completion, and we do not distribute IB guides, instruments or exemplar work.

whyPoints.title: Sequencing advice for the collision fortnight
whyPoints.description: When three criterion-marked drafts land together, we help rank them by marks at risk rather than by nearest deadline, which is the ordering that recovers the most and the one students least often choose on their own.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled to the Abu Dhabi school week
whyPoints.description: Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time after bus arrivals from the island and the mainland corridor, with later slots for Al Reef and Mohammed Bin Zayed City, weekend mornings for data processing, and post-Iftar timing during Ramadan.

faqs.question: What does Internal Assessment mean across the six IB Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: It means the component your child's own school marks against published criteria, with the IB then checking how the school applied the standard. The format differs completely by subject: a scientific investigation, a mathematical exploration, a historical investigation in three sections, commentaries on news extracts in Economics, a recorded oral in the languages, portfolio work in the arts. What they share is criterion marking, a length limit and an internal deadline set by the school rather than by the IB.

faqs.question: How much of the final grade does an IA carry in each subject?
faqs.answer: Typically between a fifth and a third of the subject grade, varying by subject and by level. The sciences and mathematics sit around a fifth; several written subjects carry more at standard level than at higher level, because the external papers take up more of the higher-level grade. Those proportions change when the IB revises a subject guide, so confirm the current weighting for each of your child's six subjects with the DP coordinator rather than relying on any third-party page.

faqs.question: What are the four criteria on the science investigation worth?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, at six marks each, twenty-four in total. The balance is the thing worth noticing: half the available marks sit after the data has been collected, in the half of the work students treat as writing up. Research design is the only criterion that closes early. Analysis, conclusion and evaluation remain fully available right up to the draft, which is why a student who has already collected data is far from out of options.

faqs.question: Which criterion do maths explorations lose marks on most often?
faqs.answer: Use of mathematics, which carries the largest single allocation of the twenty marks. The usual higher-level failure is exploring an interesting idea with mathematics drawn from two years earlier, which reads as comfortable rather than as diploma level. The opposite failure is reaching into unfamiliar mathematics copied without understanding, which the criterion penalises more heavily than modest mathematics handled properly. Both are decided at topic choice, which is why that conversation is worth more than any later session.

faqs.question: Does the school's IA mark always reach the IB unchanged?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The school marks against the published criteria, submits its marks and a sample of work, and the IB checks how consistently the school applied the standard. Where a school has been generous or harsh across its cohort, the component marks for that school can be adjusted. The practical implications: treat a draft mark as an indication rather than a promise, do not plan a predicted grade around an optimistic internal figure, and work on the criterion rather than arguing about the number.

faqs.question: Is there a page limit on the mathematics exploration?
faqs.answer: The guidance for the exploration is expressed as a page range rather than a word count and sits in the region of twelve to twenty pages for a typical piece. Treat it as an indication of scale rather than a target: a short exploration that handles course-level mathematics correctly scores better than a padded one that does not. Appendices and how graphs are counted vary, so confirm the current figure and what it includes with your child's teacher before planning the structure.

faqs.question: What is the 3,000 word limit on the science investigation measured against?
faqs.answer: The investigation works to a word limit set in the current subject guide, in the region of three thousand words, and what counts towards it is the part families get wrong. Treatment of tables, captions, calculations, data in appendices and references differs between subjects and between guide revisions. Ask the teacher directly what is included, because a student who assumes appendices are free and then has to cut two thousand words in the final week loses marks in presentation and in analysis simultaneously.

faqs.question: Why do strong students lose marks on the evaluation criterion?
faqs.answer: Because strong students write confident general statements, and the criterion rewards specific ones. It wants the weaknesses of this method, their measurable effect on these results, and improvements that address that effect. A capable student writes that precision could be improved; the criterion wants to know that the thermometer's resolution was the limiting factor on the smaller intervals, which compressed the very differences the question depended on. Specificity requires a record kept during the work rather than reconstructed afterwards.

faqs.question: Why is "human error" the worst thing to write in an IA evaluation?
faqs.answer: Because it credits nothing and signals that the student does not know which part of their own procedure was unreliable. It would apply to any investigation ever conducted, which is precisely why it earns no marks. More time and better equipment sit in the same category. What does earn the criterion is unglamorous: an instrument's resolution against the differences measured, a delay between preparing and using a solution, a room temperature that drifted across the afternoon, a control variable that demonstrably was not held constant.

faqs.question: When should an Abu Dhabi DP1 student start their first IA?
faqs.answer: At the question, as early as the department allows, because that is the only stage where every criterion is still fully available. Two or three hours spent narrowing a question, naming the variables and confirming that the apparatus and any ethics approval actually exist will do more than ten hours spent later. Students and families delay because nothing looks wrong yet, which is exactly why it is the cheapest point to intervene and the stage almost nobody buys support for.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark an IA draft against the criteria?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most useful thing a tutor does. Reading the student's own draft against the published descriptors, stating which band each criterion sits in, explaining what the band above asks for and ranking the fixes by marks recoverable is legitimate teaching. What is not legitimate is supplying text, rewriting sections, providing data, performing the calculations, handing over an outline to be filled in, or editing a draft to completion. The student must be able to explain and reproduce everything submitted.

faqs.question: What happens if two IAs are due in the same week?
faqs.answer: Sequence by marks at risk rather than by the nearest deadline, which is the opposite of what most students do. An internal assessment carrying a larger share of its subject grade with two criteria scoring low has more recoverable marks than a solid one carrying less. Work the two with the most available marks, hand the solid one a presentation checklist and submit it. Ask each department for its internal deadline in writing first, because those dates are usually earlier than students assume.

faqs.question: Does personal engagement really carry marks in the maths exploration?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a named criterion, alongside reflection. Together they are a meaningful share of the twenty marks and they are the two most commonly abandoned. Engagement is not enthusiasm declared in an introduction; it is visible evidence of the student's own thinking in the choices they made and the directions they took. Reflection is not a closing paragraph; it is a thread asking at each stage whether the mathematics did what was wanted and what its limits were. Both are far easier to earn during the work.

faqs.question: How many IA commentaries does Economics require and how long are they?
faqs.answer: The Economics internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news extracts, each inside a tight word limit in the region of eight hundred words, with the number and the exact limit set in the current subject guide. The two recurring failures are explaining a theory at length without applying it to the specific article, and choosing an extract too thin to support a diagram and a genuine evaluation. Extract selection is the decision that determines the mark, and it takes minutes to get right.

faqs.question: Can my child change the IA topic after the school has approved it?
faqs.answer: That is the department's decision, not a tutor's, and the answer depends on how far the work has gone and how close the internal deadline is. Where a design is genuinely uncontrollable, raising it early with the teacher is far better than collecting unusable data and hoping the write-up disguises it. Where data has already been collected, an honest account of the design's limitations can feed the evaluation criterion well, so a flawed design is not automatically a lost investigation.

faqs.question: Is an IA mark the same as the final subject grade?
faqs.answer: No. The internal assessment is one component contributing its published share of the subject grade, with the external papers carrying the rest. A strong IA raises the total and does not rescue weak papers, and a weak IA is not fatal to a good grade. It is worth knowing the arithmetic for each of your child's six subjects, because it tells you where revision time is actually worth spending in the final term rather than where it feels most urgent.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tuto.closingHeading: Find the criterion, then decide the hours
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-internal-assessment-tuto.closingBody: Ask your child's department for the criterion-level feedback on the draft, and look at which two criteria scored low. That sheet, plus the stage the work is at, tells you almost everything about what is worth buying: design hours before data collection, processing and conclusion work after it, evaluation specificity at the end, and nothing at all against criteria that have already closed. Tell us the subject, the stage and which criteria the school marked down, and we will match an IB DP Internal Assessment tutor in Abu Dhabi who teaches that subject, with one free trial session and a written criterion diagnosis either way.

intro.heading: Why two Mandarin quotes in the same emirate differ by AED 400 an hour
paragraphs: Ask around Abu Dhabi for Mandarin B help and the numbers that come back will range from under AED 60 an hour to over AED 600. Both ends are real. The low end is a fluent speaker, often a university student, teaching conversation. The high end is someone who has marked this course against its criteria and can tell you which of four assessments is costing the grade. Those are different products wearing the same job title.

Published rate comparisons compiled in October 2026 put the bands roughly as follows: budget online tutoring from AED 33 to AED 65 an hour on platform rate cards, qualified subject tutors working online at AED 150 to AED 300, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 once travel is priced in, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium named tutors advertised as high as AED 650. Monthly packages appear at about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours. Those are market figures from published tables, not IB Gram prices.

Mandarin then sits at the upper end of whatever band it lands in, for three reasons that are specific rather than mysterious. The specialist pool in any single emirate is small. The useful tutors are frequently in East Asian time zones, where your child's 17:00 is their 21:00. And the subject carries a workload no European language has: a character set that must be produced, not merely recognised, which means more hours of a different kind.

The last point is where families most often buy the wrong thing. Character production is expensive to teach and cheap to practise. Paying a specialist rate for an hour of character drilling that a student could do alone with a spaced-repetition routine is the most common waste in this subject, and it is why a plan should separate what needs a tutor from what needs discipline.

There is also a question of what the rate includes. Two quotes at AED 220 can mean entirely different things once you ask whether marking of written work is inside the hour, whether a session note is produced, whether orals are recorded, what the cancellation terms are, and whether the figure includes any applicable tax. We publish those questions because the answers are where the real price difference sits.

Delivery in the UAE is online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi and does not send a tutor to an address in this emirate; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For Mandarin that is the arrangement that makes the specialist rate worth paying, because the specialist is rarely within driving distance of Khalifa City at 16:30.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-mandarin-b-home-tutor.programmesIntro: What a Mandarin plan costs depends mostly on where the student is starting, and in Abu Dhabi they start from three recognisably different places. These notes put each route against the hours it tends to need.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Mandarin B sits in Group 2 at Standard or Higher Level, assessed by a written paper, a listening paper, a reading paper and an individual oral, with no internal assessment. Higher Level adds two literary works and builds the oral on a literary extract. The cost consequence is direct: Higher Level needs a tutor who has read those works, which narrows the pool again and moves the quote upward.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Mandarin B cohorts are small, and in some Diploma schools the class is a handful of students covering both levels. Families here often discover in DP2 that the hours they needed were in DP1, when character production could still be built gradually. Front-loading is cheaper than rescuing, and in this subject the difference between the two is measured in hundreds of dirhams a month.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language Acquisition places Mandarin learners in phases. A student arriving in DP1 from Phase 4 has usually met enough characters to begin Mandarin B without emergency support, and their spend goes on assessment technique rather than on the language. A Phase 2 or 3 arrival needs a character programme first, and that is a two-year cost rather than a term's.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi IB school offers Mandarin through MYP, and where it runs with two periods a week the character load accumulated by Year 11 is modest. Asking the school how many characters students are expected to produce by the end of MYP is a blunt question that produces a very useful number for budgeting.

programmes.name: Heritage and partial speakers
programmes.ageRange: Ages 15-18 · Entering or inside the DP
programmes.description: A student who speaks Mandarin at home but reads and writes little is the most common misplacement in this subject. Spoken fluency makes the oral comfortable and leaves the reading and writing components exposed. The plan is cheap in conversation hours and expensive in character hours, which is the opposite of what the family usually expects to buy.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi's professional population includes families on medium-term postings from East Asia whose children have been in English-medium schooling for years. For them the placement conversation between Mandarin B and the ab initio course matters more than any tutoring decision, and it should happen before DP1 options close rather than after the first report.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Common among students aiming at technical degrees, including in Chinese-medium institutions. The AA internal assessment lands in the same term as Mandarin oral preparation in most Abu Dhabi schools, so hours bought in that window cost more in attention than in money.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Frequently chosen alongside Mandarin by students with an eye on regional business routes. Its internal assessment deadlines are the ones most likely to collide with a character programme, and the collision is predictable enough to plan around in DP1.

subjects.description: Taken widely in the emirate's Diploma cohorts. Physics students tend to be systematic, which suits spaced character practice unusually well, and that matters to the budget because systematic students can do more of this work without paying for it.

subjects.description: Mandarin learners have sharp TOK material available, since writing systems make the relationship between language and knowledge concrete. Preparing two examples during DP1 avoids paying for TOK support later to find material the student already had.

subjects.description: UAE private schools teach Arabic alongside their licensed curriculum, so a Mandarin B student here is building two unfamiliar writing systems at once. That is the strongest argument in this subject for separating practice across days rather than funding more hours.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: May be registered in Mandarin B and written in Mandarin, which is a demanding choice that suits a strong Higher Level candidate. The budget point is blunt: an essay in Mandarin consumes the exact hours the language itself needed, so it is rarely the economical route.

sections.heading: What Mandarin B support actually costs in Abu Dhabi, in AED
paragraphs: A Mandarin B tutor in this market will quote somewhere between about AED 60 and AED 650 an hour, and the number tells you which product is being sold rather than how good it is. Published rate comparisons compiled in October 2026 give the bands, and publishing them is the whole point of this section: three of six competitor pages reviewed for this market quote no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a family here transacts in.

The bands break down by what the tutor is. Platform rate cards advertise from AED 33 to AED 65 an hour for budget online tutoring, generally university students teaching conversation. Qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150 to AED 300. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180 to AED 350 because travel time is inside the fee. IB and IGCSE specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium named tutors have been advertised at AED 650.

Monthly structures matter more than hourly ones for budgeting. Online monthly packages appear from about AED 799 for eight sessions; in-home monthly packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. A published market estimate for weekly one-hour sessions runs AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

All of these are market figures taken from published rate tables and competitor pages, not IB Gram prices, and they are reproduced here so a family can read a quote against something. sections.heading: Five things that move a Mandarin quote in this emirate
paragraphs: The spread between AED 150 and AED 450 for apparently the same hour is not arbitrary, and a family that understands the drivers can usually place itself in the band deliberately rather than accidentally. Five things do most of the work, and four of them are negotiable.

Supply is the first and the least negotiable. Mandarin B is a minority Diploma subject in Abu Dhabi, so the number of people who have taught and marked it here is small; at Higher Level, where two literary works must be discussed, it is smaller again. Scarcity sets the floor, and no amount of comparison shopping within one emirate changes it.

Time zone is the second and is directly negotiable. Many of the strongest Mandarin B tutors are in East Asian time zones, four or more hours ahead of Gulf Standard Time, which turns your child's convenient 17:00 slot into their 21:00. Slots that are comfortable at both ends are priced lower than slots that require someone to work late, and a family willing to take an early morning weekend slot often buys the same tutor for less.

Then there is level, format and what the rate includes. Higher Level costs more than Standard because the pool shrinks. A pair or small group lowers the per-student rate and raises the risk if the two students are not at the same point. And a rate that includes marking of timed written work, a session note and recorded orals is a different product from one that does not, which is why the comparison should be made on inclusions rather than on the headline figure.

sections.heading: The character workload is the line item nobody prices
paragraphs: Mandarin B differs from every European language option in one expensive respect: the writing system must be produced, not merely recognised. A student can read a character they cannot write, and the written paper requires writing. That asymmetry is the real workload, it accumulates over terms rather than weeks, and it is where a two-year budget is decided.

The common and costly mistake is to pay a specialist rate to supervise it. Character production is built by frequent, short, spaced practice with handwritten output, which a disciplined sixteen-year-old can run alone once the routine is set. Buying that hour weekly at AED 250 is paying a consultant to watch someone do press-ups.

What does need the specialist is everything the student cannot judge for themselves: whether a written response meets the text-type conventions, why a reading answer lost its mark, whether an oral response is developing or circling, and which of the four components is actually costing the grade. That is the hour worth the band, and it is roughly one hour a week, not three.

Timing matters as much as rate. Character work started in DP1 is cheap because it rides on time the student already has; the same work attempted in the second term of DP2 competes with internal assessments in five other subjects and usually has to be bought in intensive blocks at the worst moment. Front-loading a minority language is not enthusiasm — it is cost control.

sections.heading: What a quoted hourly rate usually leaves out
paragraphs: Two tutors quoting AED 220 can be offering products that differ by half their value, and the difference is almost never in the teaching. It is in what happens around the hour. Families who ask five questions in writing before booking generally end up paying less for more, which is why the questions are listed here rather than left as a negotiating advantage.

First, marking. Is written work marked outside the session, with criterion letters, or is session time used to read it? The second is a quiet way of charging teaching time for administration. Second, session notes: is there a written record of what was tested, what was taught and what was set, or does the arrangement depend on everybody remembering?

Third, recordings for oral work, which in a language course are not a luxury: a student cannot hear their own hesitation. Fourth, cancellation terms, which matter in a city with school trips, Ramadan timing changes and family travel. Fifth, tax treatment — ask plainly whether the quoted figure includes any applicable tax, and get the answer in writing. We make no statement here about how tuition is treated for UAE VAT, because that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance rather than for a tutoring page.

One further question is worth asking anybody, at any rate: whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. A tutor who does not know what you are asking about is telling you something useful.

sections.heading: A tutoring dirham in context: what a term and a two-year plan come to
paragraphs: Hourly rates are hard to think about and term totals are easy, so the arithmetic is worth doing once. The figures below are built from the published market bands rather than from an IB Gram price list, and they assume a thirteen-week term, which is roughly what Abu Dhabi school terms run to.

One session a week at the qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to AED 300 comes to roughly AED 1,950 to AED 3,900 a term. Two sessions a week doubles it. A four-session diagnostic block before mocks is AED 600 to AED 1,200 at the same band. A Higher Level oral block of six sessions at specialist rates of AED 200 to AED 450 lands between AED 1,200 and AED 2,700.

Across the full Diploma, a family running one weekly session in DP1 and two in DP2 with two intensive blocks is looking at a four-figure commitment per term and a five-figure one across two years at the specialist end. That is a real number and it deserves to be seen before the first booking rather than assembled invoice by invoice.

Set against that, the cheapest intervention in this subject costs nothing: a character routine the student runs daily from the start of DP1. Families who do that consistently buy roughly half the hours of families who do not, which is the only genuine saving available here. Everything else is a choice about which band to buy from.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for Mandarin, and what travel costs you
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a genuine market here and for most subjects it is well supplied. For Mandarin B it often is not, particularly outside the island and the central districts, and particularly at Higher Level. The published in-home band of AED 180 to AED 350 an hour exists because travel time is inside the fee, and in a city with long mainland commutes that loading is substantial.

IB Gram does not sell that service in the UAE. We do not send a tutor to an Abu Dhabi address and we do not run home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tuition is a service we offer only in India. Every lesson here is one-to-one online, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. Publishing that plainly saves a family the first phone call.

For this subject the comparison is not close. Online, the pool is every Mandarin B specialist free at your hour, including those who have read the Higher Level works. In-home, the pool is whoever can reach your community by the time your child is home, which in Mohammed Bin Zayed City or Al Falah may be nobody with Diploma experience at all. The rate difference is the smaller part of the gap.

There is one honest point in the other direction, and families raise it fairly: handwriting. Characters are written by hand and a tutor on a screen cannot watch a pen. The practical answer is a phone propped above the page for a live view of the hand during the sessions where formation matters, plus photographed scripts marked and returned dated. That is better evidence than a correction in a notebook, though it is a workaround rather than a denial of the problem.

sections.heading: Where Mandarin money gets wasted, in order of frequency
paragraphs: The most frequent waste is buying conversation for a student whose problem is the page. A heritage speaker with fluent spoken Mandarin and a weak reading score will have a pleasant hour discussing topics in Mandarin and no change in their grade, because three of the four assessments involve the written language. The hour felt productive and bought nothing.

The second is paying specialist rates for repetition. Character production and vocabulary recognition are self-run work. A tutor should set the routine, check it periodically and spend the paid hour on things requiring judgement. A plan where most of the session is drilling is a plan where most of the fee is unnecessary.

The third is timing: buying in DP2 what was needed in DP1. Nothing in this subject can be compressed safely, because character production depends on spacing rather than intensity. Families who start in the second term of DP2 end up buying intensive blocks at the worst possible moment, competing with internal assessment deadlines in five other subjects.

The fourth is the simplest to avoid: hiring a fluent speaker who has never seen the course. Native fluency is widely available at the bottom of the rate card and is not the scarce commodity. What is scarce is somebody who can look at a written response and say which criterion lost the mark. That is what the premium is for, and it is the only part of the quote worth paying a premium for.

sections.heading: The permit question, and the rule about your child's own teacher
paragraphs: Before money changes hands it is worth knowing who may legally take it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's own service, listed as private tutor licensing, with no fee.

Those who offer private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone, including us. The useful question for a parent is simply whether the person holds the permit, and the useful follow-up is whether they can say which resolution it comes under.

There is a second rule specific to this emirate. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff indicates that teachers are prohibited from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, but the direction is clear enough: arranging paid tuition from your child's own class teacher is not the shortcut it appears to be.

None of this makes IB Gram a licensed or approved anything. We hold no accreditation from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or any examination board, we operate no office or centre in the UAE, and we would not claim otherwise. What we can do is name the rules, point to the official channel, and tell you what questions to ask whoever you hire.

process.title: Say what the school examines and at what level
process.description: Two facts change the search before any money is discussed: whether the school examines in simplified or traditional characters, and whether your child is Standard or Higher Level. If Higher Level, the two literary works matter, because the tutor needs to have read them.

process.description: The trial is free with no card required and no obligation. It produces a short timed writing sample, a cold reading score and a view of character production, from which you get a written estimate of how many hours are specialist work and how many are self-run.

process.title: Split the plan into paid and unpaid work
process.description: The plan names explicitly which work needs a tutor and which the student runs alone, with a daily character target. Families who follow the split buy roughly half the hours of those who do not, and that is the main saving available in this subject.

process.title: Agree the inclusions, not just the rate
process.description: Before booking, confirm in writing what is inside the fee: marking of timed work with criterion letters, a written session note, recorded orals, and the cancellation terms. Ask whether any applicable tax is included. These are where two identical rates diverge.

process.title: Book in blocks and review at the end of each
process.description: Work runs in short blocks against named targets with a cold retest at the end. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Continuing is a decision made on the retest result rather than a standing arrangement nobody reviews.

whyPoints.description: No accreditation from any regulator or board, no UAE office, no examiner status asserted without evidence, no promised grades, and no statistics without a stated method. In a market full of unsourced numbers, that is the differentiator worth having.

faqs.question: Why do Mandarin tutors in Abu Dhabi quote so much more than French or Spanish tutors?
faqs.answer: Three reasons, all structural. The pool of people who have taught and marked IB Mandarin B in one emirate is small, and smaller again at Higher Level where two literary works must be discussed. Many of the strongest tutors sit in East Asian time zones, so a Gulf evening slot means late-evening work for them, which carries a premium. And the subject needs more contact hours overall because characters must be produced rather than recognised. Published market bands put qualified online tutors at AED 150 to AED 300 and specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 or more.

faqs.question: What should a Mandarin B hour include for the rate to be fair?
faqs.answer: Marking of timed written work outside the session with criterion letters on it, a written session note recording what was tested and set, recorded oral rehearsals, and stated cancellation terms. Ask whether any applicable tax is included and get the answer in writing. Two quotes at AED 220 can differ by half their value on those four items alone. If written work is read during the session, you are paying teaching rates for administration, which is the most common hidden cost in this market.

faqs.question: Can we lower the cost by taking a slot that suits the tutor's time zone?
faqs.answer: Often substantially, and it is the most reliable discount available in this subject. Gulf Standard Time runs about four hours behind Beijing, so a weekday 17:00 slot in Abu Dhabi is 21:00 for a tutor in East Asia and is priced accordingly. An early weekend morning in Abu Dhabi, or a slot before school, lands in a tutor's comfortable afternoon. Families who offer that flexibility frequently get a more experienced tutor at a lower rate than those who insist on the convenient hour.

faqs.question: How many Mandarin B hours should we budget across the two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: At published market bands, one weekly session in DP1 and two in DP2 plus two intensive blocks is a four-figure commitment per term and a five-figure one across the Diploma at the specialist end. A thirteen-week term at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour is roughly AED 1,950 to AED 3,900 for one session a week. The honest variable is character debt: a student who runs daily production practice from the start of DP1 typically needs about half the paid hours of one who does not.

faqs.question: Is a small group cheaper than one-to-one for Mandarin B?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, and published market tables show group rates well below one-to-one. The condition is that the students are at the same point in the character workload, which in Mandarin is unusually unforgiving. Two candidates who can produce different numbers of characters cannot do the same written task productively, and the group ends up pitched to one of them. A pair works when both are at the same level and the same stage; beyond that it saves money by delivering less.

faqs.question: Does my child need to know whether the school examines simplified or traditional characters?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the first question to settle, because it decides which tutors are usable at all. The school sets this, so the answer comes from the Mandarin teacher or DP coordinator. A tutor trained in one system teaching a student examined in the other wastes both the hour and the practice between sessions. Ask before paying for anything. It is also worth asking whether any classmates are being examined in the other system, because that affects how the class is taught.

faqs.question: Should we pay a tutor to supervise character practice?
faqs.answer: No. Character production is built by short, frequent, spaced practice with handwritten output, and a disciplined sixteen-year-old runs that alone once the routine is set. Paying AED 250 an hour to watch it happen is the single largest waste in this subject. What needs the specialist is judgement: whether a written response meets its text-type conventions, why a reading answer lost a mark, whether an oral is developing. Set the routine, check it every few weeks inside an existing session, and spend the paid hour on the rest.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start Mandarin support in DP1 or wait until DP2?
faqs.answer: DP1 is cheaper, and by a wide margin. Character production depends on spacing rather than intensity, so it cannot be compressed safely into a short period. Families who start in the second term of DP2 end up buying intensive blocks at the worst moment, competing with internal assessment deadlines in several other subjects, and paying specialist rates for work that would have ridden on spare time a year earlier. Front-loading a minority language is cost control rather than enthusiasm.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a licence to charge for Mandarin lessons in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so nobody should quote you an amount. Ask any tutor whether they hold it.

faqs.question: Can we hire my daughter's own Mandarin teacher privately?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi that is the wrong route. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff indicates teachers are prohibited from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy before relying on it. Beyond the rules, it is a poor idea in practice, because the person marking your child's class work should not also be paid to improve it.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Mandarin tutor to our home in Abu Dhabi, and what would that add to the cost?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE, and no tutor is sent to an address here; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. For reference, published market comparisons put in-home visits at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online tutor, with the gap largely travel time. In Mandarin the bigger issue is not the premium but whether anyone with Diploma experience can reach your community at all.

faqs.question: Before we commit to Mandarin hours, what does the free trial lesson cover?
faqs.answer: It is one session at no charge, with no card required and no obligation to continue. It runs as a working diagnostic rather than a sales call: a short timed writing sample, a cold reading score, and a look at character production. Afterwards you receive a written estimate of how many hours are specialist work and how many the student should run alone. You keep that estimate whether or not you book. The only condition is one trial per student, which we state because a free offer with unstated conditions is not free.

faqs.question: Are Mandarin rates higher during the exam term?
faqs.answer: In this market, generally yes at the specialist end, because demand concentrates in the months before the May session while supply does not change. Published market estimates for specialist exam-year support run AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more a month against AED 600 to AED 1,200 for mid-range support. The implication for budgeting is to book the exam-term block early rather than shopping for it in the same fortnight as everyone else, and to use the cheaper earlier terms for the work that needs spacing anyway.

faqs.question: Is paying for a Higher Level Mandarin tutor worth it for one extra point?
faqs.answer: That arithmetic is yours to do, and the honest answer is that nobody can promise a point. What can be said is where the money has the clearest effect: the Higher Level oral, built on an extract from one of the two literary works, is the component where an unprepared candidate loses most and where self-study helps least, because it needs a conversation partner who knows the works. If the budget covers one block in the Diploma, that is usually the block. Expect a reasoned recommendation rather than a prediction.

faqs.question: How do we compare two Mandarin quotes properly?
faqs.answer: Put them side by side on seven items rather than on the hourly figure: the rate, whether marking happens outside the session with criterion letters, whether a written session note is produced, whether orals are recorded, the cancellation terms, whether any applicable tax is included, and whether the tutor holds the MoHRE permit. Then ask each one which of the four Mandarin B components they would work on first and why. The answer to that last question separates people who have taught the course from people who speak the language.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-mandarin-b-tutor.tutorsIntro: Mandarin B at diploma level is a scarce specialism in the Gulf. The tutors below teach it as an IB Language B subject with the assessment criteria in front of them, and each quotes by session length rather than by package, so a family can compare a number against the market table on this page.

intro.heading: The price question deserves a number, not a form
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring pages serving UAE families publish no price at all, and one of those asks the price in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it. The two that do quote use US dollars, a currency nobody in Abu Dhabi pays school fees in. For a parent trying to budget a diploma year, that is useless, so this page starts with AED figures and says where each one came from.

Market rates for one-to-one tutoring in the UAE, surveyed in October 2026, run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the university-student end to AED 650 and above for a premium named tutor. Agency start rates for IGCSE support begin around AED 150 and for IB around AED 200. In-home visits are advertised at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table putting the in-home band at AED 180-350 and the subject-specialist band at AED 200-450 plus. Monthly packages exist too: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions at the budget end, AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Mandarin sits high inside those bands, and the reason is worth understanding before you negotiate. Nothing about Language B assessment is harder in Mandarin than in French. What differs is how many people in this market can teach it to the criteria. A tutor who speaks Mandarin natively is easy to find in the Gulf. A tutor who speaks Mandarin natively, has taught the IB Diploma Language B course, can mark a Paper 1 response against the message and conceptual understanding criteria, and is free at 6pm Gulf Standard Time on a Tuesday is not. Scarcity, not difficulty, is what you are paying for.

The second thing that moves a quote is which component the hours are aimed at. Character recognition speed for Paper 2 reading is slow, patient work that rewards weekly repetition over months. Individual oral rehearsal is the opposite: a concentrated three or four week block before the school's recording window, at two or three sessions a week, after which the rate stops. A family that understands the shape of the spend can buy the second without committing to the first, and that single distinction is usually worth more than any discount they could negotiate.

IB Gram delivers Mandarin B as one-to-one online tuition over live video to families anywhere in Abu Dhabi. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. For a subject this thinly supplied, that is not a compromise: it is the only way an Al Reef or Saadiyat family gets a diploma Mandarin specialist rather than the nearest available Mandarin speaker, and the in-home premium in the table below is paying for travel in any case.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-mandarin-b-tutor.programmesIntro: What Mandarin costs a family changes with the programme, because the amount of external support each one needs is different. Here is how the spend typically falls across the continuum in Abu Dhabi.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, four assessed components, and the only point at which Mandarin produces a grade that follows the student to university. This is where almost all paid Mandarin support is bought, and where the rate sits at the top of the band because the tutor needs the assessment model as well as the language.
programmes.countryNote: An Abu Dhabi DP cohort taking Mandarin B is usually small, and a small cohort means a shared SL and HL teaching block. Families here therefore buy external support to cover the level-specific work the shared block cannot reach: the HL literary extracts, and timed Paper 2 reading. Budget for a concentrated block rather than two uninterrupted years.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Mandarin in the MYP language acquisition strand is taught by phase, with listening, reading, speaking and writing weighted equally. Support bought here is cheaper per hour because no external assessment model is involved, and it is the best-value money in the whole continuum because character recognition compounds.
programmes.countryNote: Spending on MYP Mandarin in Abu Dhabi is unusual and tends to be reactive, after a phase placement surprises a family. The cheaper decision is a modest weekly commitment in Years 9 and 10 that keeps character recognition moving, which removes the most expensive single problem from DP1: a student reading characters at half examination pace.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An additional-language strand with no external assessment, delivered very differently from school to school. Some teach characters from Year 2, others run a weekly session in pinyin only. Paid support at this stage is rare and inexpensive, and its value is almost entirely about keeping character writing alive.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi primary provision for Mandarin varies sharply between campuses, and a family moving within the emirate can find the character expectation drops without warning. Where that happens, a short weekly arrangement costs a fraction of DP2 remediation and is the clearest example on this page of spending early to spend less later.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs DP courses with a career-related study and a language development component. A CP student may study Mandarin through language development without sitting the Language B examinations, which is a portfolio rather than a paper, and the preparation required is different and generally cheaper.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision across Abu Dhabi is limited to a small number of licensed schools, and this is the commonest place families overpay. If someone has quoted you for Mandarin B examination coaching, confirm with the DP coordinator which route your child is actually registered for before paying for an assessment model that does not apply.
