subjects.name: Mandarin B
subjects.description: Language acquisition for students with prior Mandarin. Four components: Paper 1 writing, Paper 2 reading, Paper 2 listening, individual oral. HL adds two literary works. Sits at the top of the specialist rate band in the UAE because qualified diploma-level teachers are scarce here rather than because the course is unusually hard.

subjects.name: Mandarin ab initio
subjects.description: A beginners' course with a narrower prescribed vocabulary and its own assessment model. Supported at a lower rate than Mandarin B because the lexicon is bounded, but not a soft option: the same five themes apply and character writing is still examined under time.

subjects.name: Mandarin A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A Group 1 course for students operating in written Mandarin at near-native level, with guided textual analysis and a comparative essay. The scarcest teaching of all in this market, and priced accordingly. Rarely offered on an Abu Dhabi timetable without a self-taught arrangement.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Better staffed in Abu Dhabi than Mandarin and therefore cheaper to support per hour. Families occasionally compare the two for a child with neither as a home language, where the deciding factor is which the school teaches properly rather than which looks better on a transcript.

subjects.name: French B
subjects.description: The reference point for pricing. Identical assessment model to Mandarin B, a far deeper local tutor pool, and a rate that usually lands one band lower. Comparing a French B and a Mandarin B quote side by side is the clearest demonstration that the premium is a supply premium.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: Expanding on Abu Dhabi timetables and priced similarly to French. Useful as a second comparison when a family is testing whether a Mandarin quote is high because of the language or because of the particular tutor.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Included because the Group 1 and Group 2 spend compete for the same budget. A student weak in English A Paper 1 analysis will struggle with the Mandarin B HL extract work too, and fixing the analytical habit once is cheaper than paying two tutors to fix it twice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The commonest subject a family is already paying for when the Mandarin question arrives. Worth naming because the honest advice is sometimes to keep the Maths support and take Mandarin B at SL rather than fund two higher levels at specialist rates.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK is unpaid for most families and overlaps with Mandarin B usefully through the knowledge and language optional theme. Material a student develops for the Mandarin conceptual understanding criterion frequently serves a TOK exhibition object, which is free value rather than a billable hour.

sections.heading: What a Mandarin B tutor costs in Abu Dhabi, answered first
paragraphs: Market rates for diploma-level Mandarin B support in Abu Dhabi, surveyed in October 2026, sit mostly in the AED 200 to 450 per hour specialist band, with online delivery at the lower end and in-home visits carrying a travel premium on top. Entry-level online tutoring in the UAE advertises from around AED 45 an hour, and a premium named tutor at the top of the published market reaches AED 650 and above. Mandarin rarely appears at the bottom of that range for diploma work, because the tutors who can mark against the Language B criteria are few.

Those are market figures with sources, not IB Gram's price list. We match the subject, level and component first and quote on a consultation, with one free trial lesson per subject and no card details taken before it. The reason for publishing the market table at all is that a parent cannot judge a quote without it, and the pages competing for this search mostly decline to provide one.

Read the table by format rather than by prestige. The in-home column is not buying better teaching than the online column; it is buying the same teaching plus the tutor's drive to Saadiyat or Al Reef. For a widely taught subject that premium sometimes makes sense. For diploma Mandarin in this emirate it narrows the pool to whoever is nearby, which is the opposite of what a scarce specialism needs.

One practical note on session length. Quotes in this market are given per hour but lessons are frequently sold in 90-minute blocks, which is the right length for timed writing plus marked feedback. Ask for the per-session figure and the length together, because a low hourly rate attached to a 45-minute lesson is a higher number than it looks.

sections.heading: The six variables that move a Mandarin B quote in this emirate
paragraphs: Two families in the same Khalifa City compound can be quoted rates 200 dirhams apart for what sounds like the same lesson. The gap is almost always explained by six things, and five of them are inside a family's control.

Level is the first. HL carries two literary works and an extract-based oral on top of the SL model, so an HL tutor is pricing a wider job. The month is the second: demand concentrates before the school's oral recording window and again before the May session, and a block booked in October costs what October costs. Session length is the third, and the one most often glossed over in a quote.

The fourth is the component. Reading-speed work is long and patient; oral rehearsal is short and intensive. A family that asks for help with Paper 2 reading and the oral, separately, buys a smaller total than a family that asks for help with Mandarin. The fifth is format, where in-home adds travel rather than teaching, and the sixth is scarcity, which is the one variable nobody controls: when a specialist is not free, the alternative is a higher rate, a wait, or a less specialist tutor.

What does not move the number nearly as much as parents expect is the tutor's nationality or whether Mandarin is their first language. A native speaker with no Language B teaching behind them will deliver conversation lessons at a specialist price, which is the most expensive outcome available in this subject: a full year of pleasant sessions that moves no criterion at all.

sections.heading: Why Mandarin is priced above most diploma subjects here
paragraphs: Nothing in the Language B assessment model treats Mandarin differently from French or Spanish. The components are the same, the weightings are the same, the five prescribed themes are the same and the criteria are the same. A page that tells you Mandarin B is intrinsically harder and therefore dearer is selling you a story. The price difference is a labour-market fact.

Abu Dhabi has a substantial Mandarin-speaking population and very few people in it who have taught the IB Diploma Language B course. The intersection a family actually needs is narrower still: native or near-native Mandarin, diploma teaching experience, the ability to explain the conceptual understanding criterion in English to a parent, and availability at 6pm Gulf Standard Time on a school night. Each additional condition cuts the pool, and the rate rises as it does.

This is why the online decision is not a cost-saving compromise for this subject. Removing geography as a filter widens the pool more for Mandarin than for any other Group 2 language on an Abu Dhabi timetable. A family insisting on an in-home Mandarin tutor in Al Reef is choosing from the people who live within a reasonable drive of Al Reef and can teach the diploma, which in practice may be nobody.

There is a corollary worth stating plainly. If a quote for in-home diploma Mandarin in this emirate comes in at the low end of the market, something in the specification is probably missing, and nine times out of ten it is the diploma experience rather than the language. Ask which components the tutor has taught and which criteria they mark against before you ask the rate.

sections.heading: Where the hours go: Mandarin B components priced by preparation time
paragraphs: Budgeting by subject produces a bigger number than budgeting by component. The four assessed parts of Mandarin B demand very different amounts of tutoring, and two of them respond to a short block rather than a term.

Paper 2 is where the hours concentrate, because it is half the grade and because character recognition speed is the slowest thing on the list to shift. A student who reads characters at below examination pace is not failing comprehension; they are running out of time on the final passage. That is weekly work over months, and it is the part of the plan a family should start early and cheaply rather than late and intensively.

The individual oral is the opposite shape. Six to ten concentrated hours in the three or four weeks before the school's recording window moves a component worth a quarter of the grade, and then the spend stops. Paper 1 sits between the two: text-type conventions can be memorised quickly, but handwriting characters accurately at speed under time cannot.

The hour figures below are what a typical exam-year block spends, not a rule. They are useful mainly for comparing a quoted package against what it claims to cover, and for spotting a plan that has allocated nothing to Paper 2 reading. If a package of thirty hours proposes to cover the subject and the breakdown puts twenty of them into speaking, the money is aimed at a quarter of the grade.

There is one more allocation worth protecting at HL. The two literary works feed the extract-based oral and nothing else, so they generate no paper of their own and are easy to defer indefinitely. Ten to sixteen hours spread across the two years keeps them alive. Compressed into the fortnight before the recording window, the same reading produces an oral that describes the extract rather than analysing it, which is exactly where HL candidates lose ground against their own classwork.

sections.heading: Characters, tones and the HSK confusion
paragraphs: Families frequently arrive having bought the wrong product, and the commonest version is HSK preparation sold as Mandarin B support. The HSK is a proficiency qualification with its own graded vocabulary lists and its own examination format. It is a reasonable thing to hold. It is not what the IB assesses, and hours spent working through HSK levels do not map onto the Language B criteria.

What the diploma actually asks for is production against a brief. The student must write a named text type for a named audience on a prescribed theme, handwriting characters accurately under time, and must read unseen passages at pace. A learner with a strong HSK level and no text-type training will write grammatically clean Mandarin that misses the message criterion entirely, and the mark will look inexplicable to everyone involved.

Tones are the second place money goes astray. Tone accuracy matters in the oral, where a mispronunciation that changes a word costs clarity under the language criterion, and it matters not at all in the two written components. A tutor who spends an exam-year block drilling tones is spending it on 25% of the grade while Paper 2's 50% goes untouched.

The honest advice on characters is less comfortable. There is no cheap way to buy character recognition speed late. It is built by frequency over months, which is why the lowest-cost version of this subject is a modest weekly commitment from MYP onwards and the highest-cost version is a panic block in DP2. Families who ask us in Year 9 pay far less in total than families who ask us in February of DP2.

For wider context, school fees in the UAE are regulated at emirate level rather than set freely. In Dubai, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Abu Dhabi fee applications are handled by ADEK, which licenses and inspects the emirate's private schools and publishes its own inspection ratings. We do not publish an Abu Dhabi fee figure here because we have not read one on ADEK's own pages.

What that regulation means for a tutoring budget is that the fee line is comparatively predictable and the tutoring line is not. A family can hold tutoring at AED 240 to 600 a month on Bestimate's budget estimate for weekly one-hour sessions, or find themselves at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above in a specialist exam year. The variable is almost entirely how late the decision gets made.

sections.heading: Permits, invoices and what a legitimate quote looks like
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a parent paying AED 300 an hour is entitled to know the position. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's own service for it is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears on this page; figures circulating online could not be verified.

Two things follow for a family in Abu Dhabi. The first is that nobody should charge you for a permit application, because the permit itself costs nothing. The second is that a tutor who is a teacher at your own child's school is a problem rather than a shortcut: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported and confirm the current ADEK policy wording if it matters to your situation.

On the paperwork itself, a legitimate quote states the rate, the session length, what happens to a cancelled session, and who to contact if the match is wrong. It does not require payment for a term before the first lesson. A tutoring operation running premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific thing issued to institutions with a physical centre; no online tutor or matching platform should imply they hold one.

sections.heading: Paying for a level decision instead of a term of lessons
paragraphs: The cheapest useful thing a family can buy in this subject is often a single diagnostic session, because the most expensive mistake is a level chosen on the strength of conversation. A student who speaks Mandarin at home and reads characters slowly will survive SL and struggle visibly at HL, where two literary works and an extract-based oral sit on top of everything else.

A diagnostic is cheap because it measures rather than teaches: one timed writing task handwritten, one unseen reading passage against the clock, and a few minutes of unprepared speaking. The output is a written statement of which criterion is losing marks and whether the level is right. Families who do this in Year 11 sometimes conclude they need no tutoring at all, which is a result we are happy to report.

The second-cheapest useful purchase is a component block rather than a subject commitment. Buying oral rehearsal before the recording window, or six weeks of timed reading, produces a measurable change against a specific criterion for a bounded sum. Buying Mandarin support indefinitely produces a monthly line item that nobody reviews.

Where the diagnosis points to a level change, the saving dwarfs any hourly negotiation. Dropping from Mandarin B HL to SL in time removes the literary reading, lightens the oral, and frees hours for whichever higher level actually matters to the university application. That conversation belongs with the DP coordinator, and the earlier in DP1 it happens, the more of it is still available.

process.description: Any quote you receive, including ours, should name the session length alongside the rate. Compare it against the market table on this page. An hourly figure attached to a 45-minute lesson is a higher price than it appears, and packages quoted monthly hide both.

process.description: One timed handwritten task, one unseen reading passage against the clock, a short unprepared oral. The output is a written note of which criterion loses the marks and whether the level is right, shared with you whether or not you continue afterwards.

process.title: Match on diploma experience, then on language
process.description: The filter is whether the tutor has taught Language B and marks against its criteria. Native fluency is necessary and nowhere near sufficient, and in this subject the gap between the two is where most family budgets in the Gulf disappear.

process.title: Buy the block the diagnosis names
process.description: Oral rehearsal before the recording window. Timed reading over a term. Paper 1 conventions in four sessions. Bounded purchases with an end date beat an open monthly commitment, and we will tell you when a block is finished rather than extending it.

process.title: Review the spend against the marked work
process.description: Every few weeks, look at the marked scripts rather than at how the lessons feel. If the criterion the plan targeted has not moved, the plan changes or stops. That review is the only real protection a family has against paying a specialist rate for conversation practice.

faqs.question: What does a Mandarin B tutor cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Diploma-level Mandarin B support in this market sits mostly in the AED 200-450 per hour specialist band, surveyed October 2026, with online delivery at the lower end and in-home visits adding a travel premium. The wider UAE range runs from about AED 45 an hour at the university-student end to AED 650 and above for a premium named tutor. Agency start rates are around AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. Those are market figures with sources, not our price list; we quote on a consultation after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Why is Mandarin tutoring priced above Maths or Physics in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Supply, not difficulty. The Language B assessment model treats Mandarin exactly as it treats French: same four components, same weightings, same five themes, same criteria. What differs is how many people in this market can teach the diploma course and mark against its criteria. Native Mandarin speakers are plentiful in the Gulf; diploma-experienced Language B teachers in Mandarin who are free at 6pm Gulf Standard Time are not. Each condition narrows the pool and lifts the rate, which is why removing geography as a filter matters more here than in any other Group 2 language.

faqs.question: Is a native Mandarin speaker worth the higher rate?
faqs.answer: Only alongside diploma teaching experience. A native speaker with no Language B background will deliver fluent, pleasant conversation lessons at a specialist price and move no criterion, because the marks are not lost in conversation. They are lost in text-type convention, in the conceptual understanding criterion, and in reading speed under time. Ask which components a tutor has taught and which criteria they mark against before asking the rate. Fluency is necessary; it is nowhere close to sufficient, and this is the commonest way a Gulf tutoring budget is wasted.

faqs.question: Does my child need HSK preparation as well as Mandarin B?
faqs.answer: Not for the diploma. The HSK is a separate proficiency qualification with its own vocabulary lists and examination format, and hours spent on HSK levels do not map onto the Language B criteria. A learner with a strong HSK level and no text-type training writes grammatically clean Mandarin that misses the message criterion. If your family wants the HSK for its own sake, hold it as a separate goal with a separate budget, and do not let it be sold to you as examination preparation for Mandarin B.

faqs.question: How many hours of Mandarin B support does an exam year realistically take?
faqs.answer: A typical exam-year block spends roughly 8-12 hours on Paper 1, 10-14 on Paper 2 reading, 6-10 on listening and 6-10 concentrated in a three or four week oral rehearsal block, with another 10-16 across two years on the HL literary works. Those are observations rather than a rule. The useful point is the shape: reading is long and weekly, the oral is short and intensive, and a plan that allocates nothing to Paper 2 reading is ignoring half the grade.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to put two siblings in the same Mandarin session?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, and it is usually the wrong economy for this subject. Group rates in the UAE are advertised well below one-to-one, but Mandarin B marks are lost in individually diagnosed places: one child's reading speed, another's text-type conventions. A shared session drifts towards whatever both can do together, which is conversation. Where siblings sit at genuinely similar levels on the same component, a shared block can work for a few weeks. As a default for an exam year it tends to cost less and achieve less.

faqs.question: Should we pay for character writing practice or do it ourselves?
faqs.answer: Mostly do it yourselves, with the tutor setting and checking it. Character recognition speed is built by frequency over months, and paying a specialist rate to watch a student practise is poor value. What the tutor should supply is the right practice, timed, and a weekly measurement of whether reading pace is moving. The expensive version of this subject is a panic block in DP2 after years without character practice; the cheap version is twenty minutes most days from MYP onwards, checked rather than supervised.

faqs.question: What should a legitimate tutoring invoice in Abu Dhabi show?
faqs.answer: The rate, the session length in minutes, the number of sessions covered, what happens to a cancelled or rescheduled session, and a named contact if the match is wrong. It should not require a term's payment before the first lesson, and it should not include any charge for a tutor permit, because the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. On tax, limit the question to whether the quoted figure includes VAT; the wider tax treatment of tuition is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority, not for a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Does a Mandarin B tutor need a MoHRE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private lessons in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time on MoHRE's own service listing. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Is Mandarin B HL worth the extra cost over SL?
faqs.answer: Only if the student reads Mandarin willingly and the rest of the timetable has room. HL adds two literary works and rebuilds the oral around a printed extract, which prices wider and demands reading hours that a student carrying two content-heavy higher levels and an Extended Essay rarely finds. In practice the literary reading is the first thing dropped, and it feeds a component worth a quarter of the grade. Where the university target does not require Mandarin at HL, SL plus the recovered hours is frequently the better diploma decision.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi rise closer to the May session?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens and effective prices firm up, which amounts to the same thing for a family. Demand concentrates twice: before schools' internal oral recording windows, and in the weeks before the May examinations. A specialist booked in October is bought at October availability; the same request in March is bought from whoever is left. For a scarce subject like diploma Mandarin the effect is sharper than for Maths or Biology, because there is far less slack in the pool to absorb the surge.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to keep Mandarin B ticking over in DP1?
faqs.answer: A modest weekly commitment aimed squarely at Paper 2 reading, with character practice set as homework and measured rather than supervised. That is the one skill that cannot be bought back quickly later, and it is half the grade across the two reading and listening sections. Leave the oral alone until DP2 and buy it as a block. Families who run this pattern through DP1 spend less in total than families who do nothing until February of DP2 and then buy an intensive sprint at exam-season availability.

faqs.question: Can we pay for a short block instead of a term of Mandarin lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for two of the four components it is the better purchase. Oral rehearsal is six to ten hours concentrated into three or four weeks before the school records, after which the spend stops. Paper 1 text-type conventions can be covered in four sessions. Reading speed is the component that genuinely needs a term. We will scope a block with a stated end date and tell you when it is finished rather than rolling it into an open monthly arrangement nobody reviews.

faqs.question: Do Abu Dhabi school fees and tutoring costs rise together?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, because fees are regulated at emirate level and tutoring is not. In Dubai, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not increase for 2026-27, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Abu Dhabi fee applications go through ADEK, which licenses and inspects the emirate's private schools. We publish no Abu Dhabi fee figure because we have not read one on ADEK's own pages. The practical point: the fee line is comparatively predictable and the tutoring line depends on how late you decide.

faqs.question: How much does the Mandarin B individual oral rehearsal usually cost?
faqs.answer: Applying the specialist band of AED 200-450 or more per hour to a typical six to ten hour block gives a bounded figure a family can plan around, bought once in the three or four weeks before the school's recording window. It is the single most efficient spend in this subject, because the oral carries a quarter of the grade and responds to structure and rehearsal rather than to months of accumulation. What it must not include is a prepared script: the IB requires an unrehearsed response, and a memorised monologue tends to collapse in the discussion that follows.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Mandarin B and Mandarin ab initio in cost terms?
faqs.answer: Ab initio usually supports at one band lower, around the AED 150-300 qualified-tutor range rather than the AED 200-450 specialist band, because the prescribed vocabulary is bounded and the teaching pool is a little wider. It is not a soft option: the same five prescribed themes apply and characters are still written under time. The level decision belongs with the DP coordinator and should be made on what the student can read, not on what the hour costs, because a misplaced student is the most expensive outcome of all.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-mandarin-b-tutor.closingHeading: Get the number, then get the diagnosis
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-mandarin-b-tutor.closingBody: Compare any Mandarin quote you are given against the market table on this page, with its session length stated in minutes, and ask which components the tutor has taught before asking anything else. Then buy the smallest useful thing: a diagnostic session that measures handwriting speed, reading pace and unprepared speaking, and tells you in writing which criterion is losing the marks and whether the level is right. Tell us the level, the weakest component and the school's internal deadline, and we will match an IB DP Mandarin B tutor in Abu Dhabi to that brief, with one free trial lesson and the diagnostic note shared either way.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach one course at one level: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. They know the five topic areas by their published hours, they mark against the exploration criteria letter by letter, and they prepare Paper 3 as a separate discipline rather than as more of Paper 2.

intro.heading: Why the course matters more than the postcode
paragraphs: A search for a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches tutor in Abu Dhabi almost always starts with a specific document: a mock script, a predicted grade sheet, or an exploration draft that came back with a comment about reflection. The course is the most algebraically demanding of the four Diploma mathematics routes, and the gap between understanding a topic and converting it into marks is wider here than anywhere else on the timetable. Students arrive at a session able to explain implicit differentiation perfectly and still unable to earn more than half the marks on a related-rates question, because the question is testing the setting-up, not the differentiating.

That gap is diagnosable. The IB allocates 240 teaching hours to this course against 150 for Standard Level, and the ninety-hour difference is not spread evenly. It sits in proof by induction, complex numbers in polar and Euler form, vector geometry in three dimensions, integration by substitution and by parts, differential equations, and Maclaurin series. A Higher Level candidate who is struggling is usually struggling inside that extra ninety hours, and the first job of a tutor is to establish which part of it, because the remedy for a topic gap, a technique error and a timing problem are three completely different plans.

The second job is to separate the papers. Paper 1 is two hours with no calculator and rewards exact values, clean algebraic manipulation and visible method. Paper 2 is two hours with a graphic display calculator and rewards knowing which function answers the question while still writing enough to earn the method marks. Paper 3 is one hour, 55 marks, two long problem-solving questions, and it rewards a skill the other two never test: following an unfamiliar line of reasoning for twenty-five minutes without abandoning it. A student can be secure in the content and lose a grade entirely on that third paper.

Delivery is where this page has to be plain. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in the UAE: home visits in Abu Dhabi are not something we sell, and that service exists only in India. For Higher Level Analysis specifically, that constraint turns out to be an advantage. An in-home maths tutor in Abu Dhabi is selected from the people willing to drive to your community on a Tuesday at five, and the number of those people who can teach de Moivre's theorem and mark a Paper 3 script is small. Online, your child is matched from the whole available pool of Higher Level Analysis teachers, and the thirty minutes a tutor would have spent on Khalifa City traffic is spent on maths instead.

Everything below is written to be used. It sets out what the in-home market charges in Abu Dhabi and who publishes those figures, how the 240 hours are distributed across the five topic areas, what each of the four components is worth and what it rewards, the places Higher Level candidates predictably leak marks, how the twenty exploration marks are allocated across five criterion letters, and what ADEK's position means for who may legally tutor your child. Where a number belongs to a source, the source is named. Where a date belongs to the IB, the page tells you to confirm it with your child's Diploma coordinator rather than trust a figure on a tutoring site.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Abu Dhabi schools run the IB continuum, and Higher Level Analysis sits at the end of it. These are the programmes that decide whether a student is ready for this course, and what each one changes about how support is organised.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL is one of the heaviest Higher Level choices available, with 240 teaching hours, three examination papers and an internally assessed exploration. Grades are a conversion of component marks, so a candidate's problem is always located in a component rather than in the subject as a whole.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts are often small by international standards, and a Higher Level Analysis set of four or five students is common at schools on the island and in the Khalifa City corridor. A small set means the teacher cannot slow down for one student without stalling the others, which is precisely the situation one-to-one support is for. ADEK licenses and inspects these schools and publishes its own inspection outcomes.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups marked against four criteria each on a 1-8 scale, with no external papers before the optional MYP 5 eAssessment. MYP mathematics is where the Analysis and Approaches decision is really made: a student who has been placed in extended mathematics and is comfortable with algebraic proof has the profile this course expects, and one who has not usually does better on the Applications route.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the option form for DP1 often lands before the MYP 5 results do, which means the Higher Level Analysis decision is taken on a teacher recommendation rather than on a mark. Families on Al Reem Island and in Al Raha Gardens frequently ask for a short block of sessions in MYP 5 purely to find out whether the Higher Level route is realistic before the form is signed.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses taken alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. A student on this programme still sits the same Diploma mathematics papers for any mathematics course they take, so the assessment detail on this page applies unchanged.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families usually meet this programme when a student is strong in two subjects and sinking in six. Any move from the full Diploma to courses, or from Higher to Standard Level mathematics, belongs with the school's Diploma coordinator first. A tutor's useful contribution is an honest view of whether the Higher Level mathematics grade is recoverable in the weeks that remain.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Higher Level Analysis rarely travels alone. These are the Diploma subjects Abu Dhabi students most often take alongside it, described by the mathematics each one actually demands, because a weak Higher Level maths grade usually shows up in two subjects at once.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry and vectors, statistics and calculus, assessed across two long papers, a one-hour extended-response paper and a 20-mark exploration. Marks leak on exact values in the non-calculator paper, on method that is thought but not written, and on explorations that compute accurately and never explain the choice of mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The same five topic areas over 150 hours, two 90-minute papers of 80 marks each at 40 per cent apiece, and no Paper 3. Students who step down from Higher Level in DP1 keep the exploration and lose the hardest calculus and the complex-number work, which is why the timing of that decision matters more than the decision itself.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields, circular motion and induction all assume calculus fluency the physics course does not teach. Abu Dhabi students taking Physics HL with Analysis HL frequently find that a single weakness in differentiation shows up as two sinking grades, and fixing it in the maths session repairs both.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Equilibrium, kinetics and energetics lean on logarithms, rates of change and graphical gradients. The marks are rarely lost on chemistry; they are lost on rearranging an expression under time pressure, which is a mathematics habit rather than a chemistry one.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level Economics adds calculation-heavy questions on elasticity, revenue and market outcomes. Analysis HL students are usually comfortable here, but the discipline of writing an interpretation after the number is a different skill from getting the number, and it is where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Abstract data structures, recursion and complexity reasoning reward the same formal thinking as proof by induction. Students who find induction uncomfortable in mathematics usually find recursion uncomfortable here, and the two respond to the same kind of practice.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Investment appraisal, break-even and ratio analysis are arithmetic rather than Higher Level mathematics, but the internal assessment asks for a defensible quantitative argument. Analysis HL students often overcomplicate it; the mark scheme rewards clarity.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Mathematics is one of the areas of knowledge, and Higher Level Analysis students have unusually good material for it: proof, axioms and the question of whether mathematical truth is discovered or constructed. A maths tutor can supply the examples; the essay itself must be the student's own.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Mathematics
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent investigation that a small number of Analysis HL students choose. It is a different task from the exploration, with a different supervisor and a different set of criteria, and the common failure is a research question that is too broad to resolve mathematically.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The other route, built on modelling, statistics and technology rather than proof. It is not an easier course; it is a different one, and a student who moves across in DP1 trades algebraic manipulation for matrices, graph theory and statistical testing.

sections.heading: What a home tutor search for Higher Level Analysis actually buys in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: A home tutor for Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL in Abu Dhabi is, in the local market, a tutor who travels to your community and teaches at your table. Published rates for that service run roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour according to Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate table, and listings for in-home one-to-one work in the UAE reach AED 500 at the specialist end. The travel is inside the hour you are paying for, whether or not it is itemised, and in Abu Dhabi the distance between a tutor living on the island and a student in Al Shamkha is a real constraint on who will take the booking at all.

IB Gram does not operate that way. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address: home visits in Abu Dhabi are not part of what we sell, and that service exists only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video, with the same tutor in the same slot each week and the work marked between sessions. The honest case for it is not that video is nicer than a kitchen table. It is that the binding constraint on in-home tutoring is geography, and the binding constraint on a Higher Level Analysis grade is whether the person teaching it has marked Paper 3 scripts before.

Those two constraints pull against each other. The pool of people in Abu Dhabi who will drive to Mohammed Bin Zayed City on a Tuesday evening is one set; the pool who can teach complex numbers in Euler form, Maclaurin series and vector geometry in three dimensions is another; and the overlap is thin. Online, the second pool is the only one that matters. The table below puts the options side by side with the figures their own publishers quote, so the comparison is on evidence rather than on assertion.

One option that often appears in these conversations should be ruled out early. Abu Dhabi families sometimes ask whether their child's own school mathematics teacher can tutor privately. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff says that paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school is prohibited, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, but do not build a plan around that route.

sections.heading: Where the 240 hours go, and what Standard Level never sees
paragraphs: The IB subject guide allocates 150 teaching hours to Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level and 240 at Higher Level, with roughly thirty of those hours in both courses given to the toolkit and the exploration. The ninety-hour difference is the whole of the Higher Level problem, and it is distributed unevenly: calculus and geometry absorb most of it, while statistics grows by only a few hours. A parent who knows that distribution can read a report differently, because a student who is behind in calculus is behind in the largest block of the course.

The content in that extra ninety hours is not harder versions of Standard Level topics. Much of it is new mathematics with no Standard Level ancestor at all. Proof by induction is a form of argument rather than a calculation. Complex numbers in polar and Euler form, and de Moivre's theorem with them, require a student to hold a geometric picture and an algebraic one at the same time. Vector equations of lines and planes move the geometry into three dimensions, where a sketch stops helping. Differential equations, Euler's method and Maclaurin series arrive late, in DP2, when the exploration deadline is also live.

This is why a diagnosis beats a package. Two Higher Level students on the same predicted grade can have entirely different problems: one has never understood what an induction proof is supposed to establish, the other understands all of it and cannot finish a paper. The first needs teaching, the second needs timed practice and a different habit, and buying ten hours without knowing which is which wastes most of them. The table sets out the published hours by topic area alongside the Higher Level content and the failure that usually shows up first.

Confirm the hour allocations and topic lists against your child's own copy of the current subject guide, which the school issues. The IB revises its guides, and a tutoring page is not the right place to take a syllabus from. What is stable enough to plan around is the shape: a Higher Level course with most of its extra weight in calculus and three-dimensional geometry, a non-calculator paper that punishes weak algebra, and an extended-response paper that nobody at Standard Level sits.

sections.heading: Four components, and what each one is actually rewarding
paragraphs: Higher Level Analysis is assessed across four components, and each rewards a different behaviour. Paper 1 runs for two hours over 110 marks with no calculator and carries 30 per cent. It rewards exact values, surds and logarithms handled by hand, and method written down line by line. Students who revise by checking answers on a calculator tend to discover in Paper 1 that they have been rehearsing the wrong skill for a year.

Paper 2 is the same length and the same mark total at the same weighting, with a graphic display calculator allowed throughout. The error here is the mirror image: a student solves the problem entirely on the calculator, writes the answer, and collects none of the method marks. A well-prepared candidate uses the technology to get the result and still writes the steps that earn the marks, which is a habit a tutor can install in a handful of sessions.

Paper 3 is one hour, 55 marks, 20 per cent, and two long problem-solving questions that develop an unfamiliar idea in stages. It is sat only by Higher Level candidates, and it is the component Abu Dhabi students most often tell us they ran out of time on. The skill it tests is persistence with structure: reading part (a) properly because part (f) depends on it, and recovering when an early idea fails rather than starting again. That is trainable, and it is trained with timed papers and a mark scheme, not with more content.

The fourth component is the mathematical exploration, 20 marks and 20 per cent, written over several weeks against internal school deadlines. It is the only component where the student chooses the mathematics, and the only one where a tutor's role has a hard boundary. Taken together, the four mean something practical: a student can be fluent in the course and still lose a grade to Paper 3 timing, or secure in the papers and lose it to an exploration that reflects on nothing.

sections.heading: Where Higher Level candidates leak marks, in the order it costs them
paragraphs: The most expensive leak is Paper 1 algebra. A student who reaches for a calculator during revision and then faces two hours without one loses marks on surds, exact trigonometric values, logarithm manipulation and anything requiring an answer in a specified form. The marks do not vanish on hard questions; they vanish in ones and twos across easy ones, which is why the mock score looks inexplicable to a parent who knows the child understands the topic.

The second is method marks on Paper 2. Mark schemes award for stated approach, substitution and intermediate results. A candidate who types the integral into the calculator and writes one line has forfeited most of the available credit even with a correct answer. This is the single cheapest thing to fix in a Higher Level plan, because it is a writing habit rather than a mathematical gap, and it usually takes three or four marked scripts before it sticks.

The third is Paper 3 structure. Candidates abandon a question when part (c) fails, when the mark scheme would have given them parts (d) and (e) from a stated assumption. Others spend thirty-five of their sixty minutes on the first question and never read the second. Both are fixable with timed practice against the published scheme, and both are nearly impossible to fix in the last fortnight.

After those come the predictable topic failures. Induction proofs that assert rather than argue. Vector problems in three dimensions solved as if the objects were flat. Conditional probability read as joint probability. Integration by a method chosen out of habit. Explorations that calculate correctly and never say why that mathematics was the right tool. Every one of these is diagnosable from a marked script, which is why the first session asks for the last piece of marked work rather than for a description of the problem.

sections.heading: What one session changes, and what needs a term
paragraphs: Some Higher Level problems are genuinely one-session problems. A student who does not know that method marks exist, or who has never seen how a Paper 3 question is structured, or who is rounding during a calculation rather than at the end, can be corrected in an hour and will hold the correction. These are process errors, and they are over-represented among students whose teachers describe them as careless. Careless is almost never the diagnosis; an unexamined habit usually is.

Others are four- to six-session problems. A topic that was taught in a week the student was away, or covered at speed because the set had to move on, needs teaching and then testing: explanation, worked examples, independent practice, a marked attempt, and a second marked attempt a fortnight later to check it held. Calculus technique, vector geometry and complex numbers all sit in this band for a student who has the rest of the course.

A smaller group are term-length problems, and the honest thing is to say so before taking the booking. A DP2 student who has not secured the Standard Level algebra underneath the Higher Level course is not going to acquire it and the Higher Level extension in six weeks, and a plan that pretends otherwise wastes a family's money and the student's remaining time. In that situation the useful conversation is often with the school's Diploma coordinator about level, not with a tutor about hours.

The free first lesson exists to put a booking into one of those three bands. The tutor reads the most recent marked work, asks the student to attempt something under time, and sends a written note naming the leaking component and the realistic shape of the fix. If the note says this belongs with the school rather than with us, it says that plainly. A diagnosis that costs nothing and redirects you correctly is worth more than ten hours aimed at the wrong component.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks, five letters, and the line a tutor will not cross
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is internally assessed, moderated by the IB and worth 20 per cent of the Higher Level grade. It is marked out of 20 across five criteria identified by letter, and the allocation surprises most families: presentation and communication carry four marks each, personal engagement and reflection three each, and the mathematics itself six. A Higher Level student who writes twelve pages of impressive analysis and never reflects on it has capped the grade in a way no amount of extra mathematics can lift.

That allocation changes what support should look like. The most valuable session happens before any mathematics is attempted, when the research question is still negotiable, because almost every low-scoring exploration can be traced to a question that was too broad, too standard, or impossible to engage with personally. A tutor who reads a finished draft can improve the presentation marks. A tutor who is in the conversation at week one can change which criteria are reachable at all.

The boundary is firm and it is in the student's interest, not ours. A tutor explains what a criterion is asking, points at the place in the draft where the marks are being lost, teaches the mathematics the student has chosen to use, and sets the next revision for the student to carry out. Nothing in the submitted document originates with the tutor, and no tutor rewrites a passage into its final form. One page competing for this search sells finished Internal Assessments outright; the consequences of that land on the candidate, as malpractice, not on the seller.

Practically, that means keeping a record. Students should be able to show their supervisor what feedback they received and what they then changed, and schools increasingly ask. Session notes from a tutor are useful evidence that the work is the student's own, which is a reason to prefer feedback in writing over feedback given verbally and forgotten.

sections.heading: ADEK, option blocks and the four-student Higher Level set
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge. The u.ae government portal states that ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and ADEK publishes its own inspection outcomes, which is the place to read a school's rating rather than a tutoring site. What ADEK does not do is decide which Diploma mathematics courses an individual school offers; that is a timetabling and staffing decision made by the school.

The practical consequence for Higher Level Analysis is set size. Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts are small compared with the large British-curriculum rolls in the same city, and it is common for a school to run one Higher Level Analysis set of four or five students, timetabled against another Higher Level subject. That has two effects. The set cannot slow down for one student without stalling the others, and a student who needs to move between mathematics routes may find the timetable, rather than the mathematics, is what prevents it.

It also means the option form matters more here than families expect. The decision between Analysis and Applications, and between Higher and Standard Level, is frequently taken in MYP 5 or Year 11 before any Diploma marking has happened, on a teacher recommendation. Where a school runs only one of the two routes at Higher Level, the choice has effectively been made for the student by the timetable. Asking the Diploma coordinator which sets will actually run, and how many students are in each, is a better use of a meeting than asking about results.

For families weighing a private tutor against the school's own staff, note the regulatory position. Private tuition in the UAE is permitted by a MoHRE work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with suspicion.

sections.heading: If no Higher Level Analysis specialist is free at your hour
paragraphs: Higher Level Analysis is a narrow specialism, and the hours Abu Dhabi families want are narrow too: most requests land between 5pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time on weekdays. Those two facts collide, particularly in the weeks around mocks when every Diploma family in the Gulf is looking for the same slot. No competitor in this market publishes what happens then, which is why families discover the answer in week five rather than week one.

Our position is to say it before you commit. If no Higher Level Analysis teacher is available at the hour you need, we tell you at the point of enquiry and give you the real options: a different hour with the specialist you want, the same hour with a tutor who covers the Standard Level content while a Higher Level slot opens, a weekend block instead of a weekday hour, or a recommendation to wait. What we do not do is put a general maths tutor into a Higher Level booking and let you find out in a month.

There is a version of this that works well, and Abu Dhabi families use it often. A weekend morning in Gulf Standard Time is lightly booked and suits a Paper 3 block better than a weekday evening does, because sixty minutes of unfamiliar problem-solving after a full school day and a commute from the island is not where a student's best work lives. Several families deliberately move their Higher Level hour to a Saturday morning in DP2 for exactly that reason.

Session timing also moves with the calendar. Through Ramadan many Abu Dhabi households shift academic work to a later evening slot after Iftar, and because lessons run over video rather than requiring anyone to travel, moving a weekly hour by two or three hours is a scheduling change rather than a logistics problem. Mock weeks, school trips and travel between terms are handled the same way: the slot moves, the tutor does not.

process.title: Say the course, the level and the component
process.description: Not 'maths help' but 'Analysis and Approaches HL, Paper 1 came back at 42 per cent and the exploration has no research question yet'. That sentence decides which specialist you are matched with. Attach the most recent marked script if you have one; it is worth more than any description of the problem.

process.title: Take the free first lesson as a diagnosis
process.description: The tutor reads the marked work, asks your child to attempt something under time, and establishes whether the issue is content, technique or process. You receive a written note naming the leaking component and the realistic shape of the fix, including the case where the answer is that this belongs with the school.

process.title: Fix the rhythm and set a review date
process.description: A fixed weekly hour in Gulf Standard Time, work set at the end of each session and marked before the next, and an agreed point four to six weeks out at which you look at evidence. Setting that review date at the start matters more than negotiating the rate.

process.title: Read the marked scripts, not the atmosphere
process.description: At the review, ask for the marked work rather than for an impression. Per-question marks, method marks earned on Paper 2 questions, and the time taken to complete a timed section are the signals that move first. A tutor who cannot show you a changed mark after six weeks has not given you anything checkable.

process.title: Change the plan when the evidence says to
process.description: Sometimes the scripts say the mathematics is fine and a different subject is the problem. Sometimes they say Higher Level is not realistic and the conversation belongs with the Diploma coordinator. Both are useful findings, and both beat renewing a plan because it has become routine.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the course, not on driving distance
whyPoints.description: An in-home tutor in Abu Dhabi is chosen from the people willing to travel to your community at the hour you need. Online, the pool is every available Higher Level Analysis teacher. For a course with Paper 3 in it, that difference in expertise is larger than any difference the room makes.

whyPoints.title: The delivery model is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not visit UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. Pages ranking for this search route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without ever saying where the tutor sits.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure belongs to its source
whyPoints.description: Market bands on this page are attributed to the rate table or company that published them, with the month they were read. We do not present a market band as our own price list, and we do not publish a number we cannot point at a source for.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty boundary is written down
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, mark and give feedback on the student's own work, and nothing in a submitted exploration originates with a tutor. That line is on the page because a competing site sells completed Internal Assessments, and the malpractice consequence falls on the candidate rather than the seller.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are disclosed up front
whyPoints.description: If no Higher Level Analysis specialist is free at the hours you need, we say so at enquiry and name the alternatives. Nobody else in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is why families usually meet one after they have already paid.

whyPoints.title: Regulatory facts are cited rather than asserted
whyPoints.description: ADEK licenses Abu Dhabi private schools; the MoHRE private tuition permit is free of charge for two years under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation and claims none, and the official sources are linked so you can read them yourself.

faqs.question: We are in Al Raha Gardens — is in-home Higher Level maths tuition available from IB Gram?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any UAE address, and home visits in Abu Dhabi are not a service we sell; that option exists only in India. Higher Level Analysis lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week and work marked between sessions. For this course that is the stronger arrangement, because an in-home booking in Al Raha Gardens is filled from the people willing to drive there at five o'clock, and very few of them have marked a Paper 3 script. Online, your child is matched from every available Higher Level Analysis teacher.

faqs.question: What does the Abu Dhabi market charge for Higher Level Analysis, and why is it dearer than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Published UAE market rates put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, IB and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450, and in-home one-to-one work at AED 180 to 350, reaching about 500 at the specialist end. TutorChase publishes AED 270. Higher Level Analysis sits at the upper end of those bands for two reasons: the course carries 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and Paper 3 narrows the pool of people who can teach it credibly. Those figures are the market's, not our price list. Ask about the free first lesson before discussing hours.

faqs.question: What is in Paper 3, and can it be prepared for on its own?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is a one-hour, 55-mark paper worth 20 per cent of the Higher Level grade, sat only by Higher Level candidates. It contains two long problem-solving questions that develop an unfamiliar idea in stages, so part (f) usually depends on having read part (a) properly. It can absolutely be prepared for separately, and it often should be, because the skill it tests is persistence with structure rather than additional content. A short block of timed papers marked against the published scheme moves it faster than more topic teaching does, provided the content is broadly in place first.

faqs.question: My son understands the calculus but keeps underperforming on Paper 1. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always the revision method. If a student practises with a graphic display calculator to hand, they rehearse recognising answers rather than producing them, and then meet two hours with no calculator in Paper 1. The marks are lost in ones and twos across straightforward questions: surds left unsimplified, exact trigonometric values half-remembered, logarithm rules applied in the wrong order, answers not given in the required form. The fix is unglamorous and quick: timed non-calculator sections every week, marked, with the recurring error named rather than corrected silently. Three or four marked scripts usually change the pattern.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level Analysis topics have no Standard Level equivalent at all?
faqs.answer: Several, which is why stepping between levels is not simply a change of difficulty. Proof by induction is Higher Level only and is a form of argument rather than a calculation. Complex numbers in Cartesian, polar and Euler form, with de Moivre's theorem, appear only at Higher Level. So do vector equations of lines and planes with scalar and vector products, Maclaurin series, L'Hopital's rule, integration by substitution and by parts, volumes of revolution, differential equations with Euler's method, and Bayes' theorem. Confirm the current lists against your child's own copy of the subject guide, which the school issues and the IB periodically revises.

faqs.question: How many teaching hours does the IB give to this course, and why does that number matter to us?
faqs.answer: The subject guide allocates 240 hours to Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and 150 at Standard Level, with around thirty hours in both courses for the toolkit and the exploration. The number matters because the extra ninety hours are not spread evenly. Calculus grows from roughly 28 hours to 55 and geometry and trigonometry from 25 to 51, while statistics grows by only a handful. So a report saying your child is behind in calculus is a report about the largest block of the course, and a report about statistics is a much smaller problem than it sounds.

faqs.question: Our Abu Dhabi school runs one Higher Level Analysis set of five students. Is that a disadvantage?
faqs.answer: It cuts both ways. A set of five gives more teacher attention per student than a class of twenty-five, which is genuinely valuable. The difficulty is that a small set cannot slow down for one student without stalling the rest, and it is usually timetabled against another Higher Level subject, so moving between mathematics routes may be blocked by the timetable rather than by the mathematics. Ask the Diploma coordinator which sets will actually run next year and how many students are in each. That answer shapes the option form more than any results table will.

faqs.question: How is the exploration marked, and what may a tutor legitimately do with it?
faqs.answer: It is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation and mathematical communication at four marks each, personal engagement and reflection at three each, and use of mathematics at six. A tutor may explain what a criterion asks, teach the mathematics the student has chosen, read a draft and say where marks are being lost, and set a revision for the student to carry out. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a passage into its final form, or contribute any part of the submitted document. Keep the written feedback: it evidences that the work is the student's own.

faqs.question: Can my daughter move from Higher Level Analysis to Standard Level during DP2, and what does she lose?
faqs.answer: Schools do allow it, but the window is real and it narrows fast, because the school has to timetable her into a Standard Level set that may already be full and the IB registration has to be amended. The content she loses is the Higher Level extension: induction, complex numbers, three-dimensional vectors, the harder calculus and Paper 3. The exploration carries across. The decision belongs with the Diploma coordinator rather than with a tutor, and the useful contribution a tutor can make is an honest view of whether the Higher Level grade is still reachable in the time left.

faqs.question: Does Abu Dhabi's school regulator decide which mathematics courses a school can offer?
faqs.answer: No. The Department of Education and Knowledge licenses and inspects private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes its own inspection outcomes, and the u.ae government portal describes ADEK as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Which Diploma mathematics courses are timetabled at which level is a staffing and timetabling decision taken by the individual school. That is why two ADEK-inspected schools a few kilometres apart in Khalifa City can offer entirely different mathematics options, and why the question belongs to the Diploma coordinator.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school mathematics teacher tutor them privately in the evenings?
faqs.answer: Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff says that paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school is prohibited, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's published policy before acting on it. Either way, it is not a route to build a plan around, and a teacher who offers it is taking a risk that ultimately sits with your child's school.

faqs.question: Does a private mathematics tutor working with an Abu Dhabi family need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE is regulated through a MoHRE work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so be sceptical of any specific amount you are quoted as fact.

faqs.question: There are ten weeks until the papers and my child is sitting on a 4 at Higher Level. Is it worth starting?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the 4 is made of, which is why the first lesson is a diagnosis rather than a sales call. If the content is broadly in place and the marks are going on unwritten method, non-calculator algebra and Paper 3 timing, ten weeks is enough to change the picture, because those are habits. If the Standard Level algebra underneath the course was never secure, ten weeks will not deliver both that and the Higher Level extension, and we will say so. An honest no is cheaper than ten hours aimed at the wrong component.

faqs.question: Will a weekly Higher Level maths slot survive Ramadan and the Abu Dhabi school calendar?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a timing change. Many Abu Dhabi households move academic work to a later evening slot after Iftar during Ramadan, and because lessons run over live video rather than requiring anyone to travel, shifting a weekly hour by two or three hours is a calendar adjustment rather than a logistical one. The same applies to mock weeks, school trips and travel between terms: the slot moves and the tutor stays the same, which matters for a course where the tutor's picture of how your child works is part of what you are paying for.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level Analysis specialist is free at 6pm Gulf Standard Time?
faqs.answer: We tell you at the enquiry rather than after you have paid. Most Abu Dhabi families want a slot between 5pm and 8pm on weekdays, and around mock season those hours fill. The options we put in front of you are a different hour with the specialist you want, a weekend morning block, or waiting for a slot to open. A weekend morning often suits Paper 3 better anyway, because an hour of unfamiliar problem-solving after a school day and a commute off the island is not where a student's best work happens.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the script, not with a package of hours
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-home-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step is not deciding how many Higher Level hours to buy. It is finding out which of the four components is losing the marks, because the answer changes everything: a method-mark habit is three sessions, a missed calculus topic is six, and a missing Standard Level foundation under a Higher Level course is a conversation about level rather than about tutoring. Send us the course, the level and the last marked script, and attach the exploration draft if there is one. The first lesson is free and ends with a written note naming the leak and the realistic shape of the fix. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and if no Higher Level Analysis specialist is free at your hours, we will tell you before you commit rather than after.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors work on IB Diploma Programme Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and the HL sciences that sit alongside it. They read scripts before they teach topics, because at this level the grade is usually decided by where the working breaks rather than by what the student has not met.

intro.heading: Three different failures, one grade, and only one of them is about mathematics
paragraphs: Parents looking for an IB DP Math AA HL tutor in Abu Dhabi almost always describe a confusing picture. The student was strong at IGCSE or MYP mathematics, understands the lessons, can do the exercises when the topic is named at the top of the page, and then produces a 4 or a 5 in a DP1 assessment. The report says things like needs to show more working or should check answers, which is accurate and not actionable. The underlying picture is nearly always a mixture of three separate failures that happen to arrive as one number.

The first is genuine mathematical gap: an HL-only topic such as proof by induction, complex numbers, three-dimensional vectors or differential equations that was taught quickly and never consolidated. The second is method selection, where the student knows every technique and cannot tell which one a question is asking for, which is what makes an unseen Paper 2 question feel impossible and a textbook exercise feel easy. The third is communication: method marks lost because the working does not show what was done, accuracy marks lost to premature rounding, reasoning marks lost because a justification was thought rather than written.

Those three have different costs. Communication is repairable in a handful of sessions and typically returns the most marks per hour of tuition. Method selection takes a term of mixed, unlabelled practice. Content gaps take as long as the content takes. A tutor who starts by teaching topics without reading a script is guessing which of the three you are paying for, and in Abu Dhabi, where HL maths cohorts are frequently small and move fast, that guess is expensive.

Tuition for Abu Dhabi families is delivered one to one and online, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visits are a service we run only in India. For HL mathematics that is a straightforward advantage. The pool of tutors who have taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, including Paper 3, is small anywhere in the world, and the probability that one of them lives a twenty-minute drive from Khalifa City on a Tuesday evening is lower still. A shared screen with a graphics tool and the student's own script does everything a kitchen table does.

Abu Dhabi adds its own context. ADEK licenses and inspects private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection ratings, and the Diploma cohort is spread across the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor and the newer mainland communities. Many schools run a single HL maths class, which means the pace is set by the strongest students in it and a child who falls two weeks behind has nowhere inside school to catch up. That structural fact, rather than any individual weakness, is why so many Abu Dhabi families buy HL maths support in DP1.
