abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: AA HL sits inside a system of four DP mathematics courses and two years of internal deadlines. These are the parts of that system that change what tutoring has to do.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
programmes.description: A 240-hour Higher Level course covering number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, with an explicit emphasis on proof and on algebraic technique. Assessment is three written papers plus the mathematical exploration, which is marked out of twenty against five criteria. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and Paper 3 is an extended problem-solving paper unique to Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, AA HL is normally one class per year group in an IB school, sometimes shared between DP1 and DP2 in smaller cohorts. ADEK licenses and inspects these schools and publishes inspection ratings. The practical consequence of a single class is that there is no second set to move into, so a student who slips does so without an internal safety net, which is the most common reason families here start tutoring in the first term of DP1.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
programmes.description: The 150-hour Standard Level version of the same course, examined by two papers plus the exploration and without Paper 3. It shares most of the core content and omits the Higher Level extensions, including the heavier proof, complex number and differential equation material. The grade ceiling is the same 7.
programmes.countryNote: The realistic question for an Abu Dhabi DP1 family is not whether Standard Level is easier but when the switch is still possible. School timetables and option blocks decide that, and in a small cohort it may turn on whether a Standard Level class runs in the same slot. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the deadline and the mechanics before the decision becomes urgent rather than after.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
programmes.description: The other Higher Level route, also 240 hours, weighted towards modelling, statistics and technology use rather than algebraic proof. It is not a softer course; it is a different one, and it suits a student whose strength is interpretation and whose patience for algebraic manipulation is limited.
programmes.countryNote: Degree requirements, not difficulty, should settle this choice. Some engineering, mathematics and physics programmes name Analysis and Approaches specifically, and others accept either at Higher Level. Check each programme's own admissions page rather than trusting a summary, including for universities inside the UAE, because requirements differ between institutions and between faculties.

programmes.name: Arriving from MYP or IGCSE mathematics
programmes.description: The two common entry routes. MYP mathematics builds inquiry and conceptual understanding and assesses against criteria; IGCSE builds procedural fluency against tightly structured questions. Neither trains the algebraic stamina or the unlabelled problem selection that AA HL assumes from week one.
programmes.countryNote: The step into AA HL catches strong IGCSE students in Abu Dhabi more often than weak ones, because a grade 8 or 9 earned on structured questions does not predict performance on an unstructured HL problem. A student arriving from either route usually needs six to eight weeks on algebraic fluency and on reading unlabelled questions, before any HL-only content is introduced.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the parts of AA HL where Abu Dhabi students most often lose marks, with what each one actually demands. The last entries are skills rather than topics, and they apply across every paper.

subjects.name: Proof, including induction
subjects.description: A structured argument with a fixed shape: base case, inductive assumption, inductive step, conclusion. Marks are awarded for the structure as much as for the algebra, so a student who performs the algebra and omits the assumption statement loses reasoning marks on work that is mathematically correct.

subjects.name: Complex numbers
subjects.description: Modulus-argument form, products and quotients, powers and roots, and the geometry of the Argand diagram. Students lose marks by leaving arguments outside the required range and by treating roots of unity as an algebra exercise rather than as a set of points with a geometric pattern.

subjects.name: Vectors, lines and planes in three dimensions
subjects.description: Scalar and vector products, equations of lines and planes, and the intersection and angle problems built on them. The usual failure is spatial rather than algebraic: a student who cannot sketch the configuration picks the wrong technique and executes it perfectly.

subjects.name: Differential equations
subjects.description: Separation of variables, the integrating factor, homogeneous substitutions and Euler's method. This topic is often taught late in DP2, which means it reaches students at their most tired and least willing to ask, and it appears in Paper 3 contexts where the equation has to be built before it can be solved.

subjects.name: Maclaurin series and further calculus
subjects.description: Series expansions, limits and improper integrals, and the manipulation that connects them. Marks are lost on the bookkeeping rather than the concept, which makes this a topic where neat working is worth real marks rather than being a matter of presentation.

subjects.name: Functions and transformations
subjects.description: Composite and inverse functions, rational functions, and the behaviour of graphs including asymptotes and symmetry. HL questions frequently combine a transformation with a calculus demand, so students who learn each separately cannot answer the combined question.

subjects.name: Calculus: differentiation and integration
subjects.description: Implicit differentiation, related rates, integration by substitution and by parts, and volumes of revolution. The largest single source of avoidable loss across HL papers is the missing constant, the unchanged limits after substitution, and the chain rule applied to the outer function only.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, discrete and continuous random variables and expectation. Abu Dhabi students often arrive strong on distribution calculations and weak on conditional reasoning, which is where the HL questions sit.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Marked against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The commonest loss at HL is mathematics that sits below the level of the course, not mathematics that is wrong. A tutor may teach, question and give feedback; the work submitted is the student's own.

subjects.name: Paper 3 problem solving
subjects.description: Extended, scaffolded investigations where each part depends on the last and the question supplies unfamiliar definitions. It tests whether a student can read mathematics they have never seen and follow it, which is a trainable habit distinct from knowing the syllabus.

subjects.name: Command terms and mark types
subjects.description: Hence, show that, deduce, verify, justify and determine are instructions with marks attached, and IB mark schemes award method, accuracy and reasoning separately. Students who treat these as stylistic lose marks on questions they answered correctly.

subjects.name: Graphical calculator technique
subjects.description: Solving numerically, finding intersections and turning points, defining functions and storing values, and knowing when the calculator is faster than algebra. Equally important is knowing when a calculator answer earns nothing because the question demanded exact form.

sections.heading: The three kinds of AA HL mistake, and how to tell them apart in one script
paragraphs: Read a marked HL paper with a pen and sort every lost mark into one of three piles. Pile one: the student did not know the mathematics. Pile two: the student knew the mathematics and chose the wrong route, or could not see which route the question wanted. Pile three: the student did the right mathematics and did not get paid for it, because the working did not show the method, because a value was rounded too early, or because a justification existed in their head and not on the page.

The proportions matter more than the total. A script dominated by pile three looks like carelessness and is not: it is a systematic failure to write for an examiner who awards method, accuracy and reasoning marks separately. That pile is the cheapest to fix and the most frequently misdiagnosed, because the word careless invites a student to try harder rather than to change what they write down. Pile two is a term of mixed, unlabelled practice, because the skill is selection and selection cannot be practised on a page headed Integration by Parts.

Pile one is the only pile that requires teaching content, and in Abu Dhabi it is usually smaller than parents expect and concentrated in the HL-only topics: induction, complex numbers, three-dimensional vectors, differential equations, Maclaurin series. Those get taught at pace in a single-class cohort, and a student who was absent or lost for two lessons has no second set to fall back on. The table below is the sorting instrument, and a parent can apply it to their child's last paper without any mathematics.

sections.heading: Command terms are instructions with marks attached
paragraphs: In an IB mathematics paper the command term is not a style preference. Show that tells the student the answer is given and that the marks are entirely in the steps, so a correct final line with nothing above it earns very little. Hence tells the student to use the previous result, and an independent method that reaches the same answer can forfeit marks. Hence or otherwise removes that constraint. Verify asks the student to substitute and confirm rather than to derive. Deduce asks for a conclusion drawn from something already established.

Justify and determine both ask for reasoning on the page. A student who knows why a stationary point is a maximum and writes only maximum has answered the question in their head and not on the script. This is the single most common reason a strong Abu Dhabi student's marks sit below their understanding, and it is also the fastest thing to repair, because it requires no new mathematics at all. We drill it by taking questions the student has already solved and rewriting only the sentence the command term demanded.

The underlying structure is the mark scheme. IB schemes award method marks for a recognisably correct approach, accuracy marks for the correct value, and reasoning marks for the stated argument, and they tell examiners when a mark is lost and when it follows through. Students who have seen a few of these schemes write differently afterwards, because the abstraction becomes concrete: there is a mark on this line, and it is awarded for writing something I was leaving out.

sections.heading: Where accuracy marks go, and the three-significant-figure habit
paragraphs: Unless a question states otherwise, a final answer in IB mathematics is expected to three significant figures, and exact form is required when the question asks for it. Those two rules between them account for a steady drip of lost marks on Paper 2 across every cohort we see. The student solves correctly, rounds an intermediate value to three figures, carries it forward, and arrives at a final answer that is wrong in the third figure. The method marks survive; the accuracy mark does not.

The habit that fixes it is mechanical. Keep full precision in the calculator, store intermediate values rather than retyping them, and round once at the end. Students resist storing values because retyping feels faster, and it is faster until the third time a long decimal is mistyped. We make the cost visible by having the student solve the same question twice, once rounding as they go and once storing, and comparing the final figures. The argument ends there.

Exact form is the mirror image. A question asking for an exact value is asking for a surd, a fraction or a logarithm, and a decimal answer from the calculator earns nothing however correct. Conversely, a Paper 1 question sat without a calculator cannot be answered by a decimal approximation at all. Students who have been taught to read for the words exact and give your answer to before starting lose far fewer of these, and that reading habit takes about one session to establish and a month to make automatic.
bullets: Read the question for exact, to three significant figures, or to the nearest
Store intermediate values; never retype a rounded decimal
Round once, at the end, and only then
Check whether the paper permits a calculator before choosing a method
A decimal where exact form was demanded earns nothing

sections.heading: Paper 3 is a reading skill before it is a mathematics skill
paragraphs: Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level and it unsettles strong students more than weak ones. It presents extended, scaffolded investigations, often defining an object the student has never met, and then asks them to work with that definition across several dependent parts. Nothing in it is off-syllabus, but very little of it looks like anything in the textbook, and students who have succeeded by recognising question types find there is nothing to recognise.

The trainable skill is reading mathematics you have not seen and taking it seriously. We practise in a fixed sequence: read the definition twice, write out one small example of it by hand, check the example against anything the question has already told you, and only then start part (a). Students who skip the worked example almost always misread the definition and then execute flawless mathematics on the wrong object, which costs the entire question rather than one mark.

The second skill is partial credit under dependency. In an investigation where part (c) uses the answer to part (b), a student stuck on (b) can often still earn marks in (c) by stating an assumption and proceeding. Abandoning the question is the expensive response and is also the instinctive one at the forty-minute mark of a long paper. Rehearsing the move, out loud, in a session, changes behaviour in the exam more reliably than being told to keep going.

The third is stamina, which is why this work has to be timed. A student who can handle an unfamiliar definition at the start of a session often cannot at the end of one, and the paper arrives after other papers in an exam period. We run complete investigations under the clock rather than in pieces, because the mathematics is rarely what fails at minute thirty-five.
bullets: Read any supplied definition twice, then write a small example by hand
Expect unfamiliar notation; it is explained in the question
When a part is stuck, state an assumption and continue for method marks
Budget time per part rather than per paper
Practise under the clock; the difficulty is stamina as much as content

sections.heading: The DP1 to DP2 handover: what should be secure before the summer
paragraphs: Most of the HL maths trouble we see in Abu Dhabi in DP2 was created in DP1 and went unnoticed because DP1 assessments were topic-labelled. The useful question at the end of DP1 is therefore not what grade did the report say, but which techniques can the student still execute cold, without the topic being named, after a holiday. That is a different and much more informative test, and it can be run in an afternoon.

The table below is the audit we run in June. It is deliberately specific: each row names a technique, the symptom that shows it is not secure, and roughly how long it takes to repair before DP2 starts. Families who do this in June arrive in DP2 with a short, known list. Families who do not usually discover the same list in February, when the class is teaching differential equations and there is no room to go back for implicit differentiation.

A word on holidays, because Abu Dhabi families travel. Two weeks of nothing is fine and arguably useful. Eight weeks of nothing, in a subject whose currency is algebraic fluency, is not, and the cost is paid in September at exactly the moment the HL-only content accelerates. Twenty minutes of mixed practice three times a week through the break preserves more than a fortnight of intensive catch-up recovers.

The audit is also the right moment to revisit the level decision honestly. A student who clears every row cold is in the right course. A student who clears none of them, after a year of teaching and a term of support, is being told something by the evidence, and the conversation to have is with the Diploma coordinator about whether Standard Level is still available in the timetable. That conversation is much easier in June than in the following February.

sections.heading: Single-class HL cohorts, ADEK and the Abu Dhabi structural problem
paragraphs: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, inspects them and publishes its own ratings, and the Diploma population is distributed across the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor and the newer mainland communities. What that distribution produces, in practice, is a lot of schools running one Higher Level mathematics class per year group. An inspection rating tells you about the school; it tells you nothing about what a single-class cohort does to an individual student.

A single class has two consequences. The pace is set by the students who are coping, because a teacher with one class cannot differentiate into a second set, and there is no lower group to move into if the pace is wrong. So a student who loses two weeks to illness, travel or a difficult topic has no internal mechanism for recovery, and the gap compounds through a course where almost everything depends on algebraic fluency established earlier.

This is the honest reason HL maths tutoring is common in Abu Dhabi, and it is a structural reason rather than a reflection on schools or students. It also shapes what good tutoring looks like here. The job is usually not to teach the course again but to re-teach two or three specific HL-only topics at a different pace, and to supply the mixed unlabelled practice a class working topic-by-topic through a syllabus does not have time to set.

It follows that the first conversation should be with the school rather than with a tutor. Ask the Diploma coordinator which HL-only topics have been taught and in what order, whether a Standard Level class runs in the same timetable slot, and when the internal exploration deadlines fall. Those three answers shape a tutoring plan more than anything a provider can tell you, and they cost one email.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks, five criteria, and the line a tutor will not cross
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is marked out of twenty against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. At Higher Level the criterion that most often costs marks is the last one, because the mathematics has to be commensurate with the level of the course. A beautifully presented exploration built on Standard Level mathematics is capped, and students discover this late because the piece feels finished and reads well.

The second common loss is reflection, which students interpret as describing how they felt about the project. The criterion rewards evaluating the mathematics: what the model fails to capture, what a different assumption would change, where the result is sensitive. That is a specific kind of writing and it can be taught by questioning, which is exactly what a tutor is for.

The boundary is firm and we state it rather than leave it implied. A tutor may teach the mathematics, test whether a chosen topic can carry HL-level work, explain what each criterion rewards, demonstrate technique on different material, and give feedback on a draft the student has already produced. A tutor may not supply content for submission or rewrite a draft on the student's behalf. Everything submitted is the student's own, and the student is the person the IB would penalise, which is why this boundary protects them rather than us.

Timing is the practical lever a tutor can pull without going near that line. The exploration is almost always worth more marks per hour of work in DP1 than in the fortnight before the internal deadline, because a topic tested early can still be changed and a topic tested late cannot. Families who book two or three sessions purely on topic choice, months ahead, routinely get more from them than families who book six on polishing a draft that cannot carry Higher Level mathematics.
bullets: Test the topic early for whether HL-level mathematics fits it
Mathematics commensurate with the course is the HL sticking point
Reflection evaluates the mathematics, not the experience of doing it
Notation and technology use are assessed, not cosmetic
Feedback on the student's own draft only; nothing supplied for submission

sections.heading: Scheduling an HL maths slot in Abu Dhabi, including Ramadan
paragraphs: HL mathematics needs a long slot rather than a frequent one, because the useful unit of work is a complete problem plus the repair that follows it, and that does not fit in forty minutes. Ninety minutes once a week, at an hour when the student is not already finished for the day, beats two short evening sessions. In practice that means fighting for an earlier slot than families expect to need, and in Abu Dhabi the school bus run is what decides how early is possible.

Build the year around the school's internal deadlines rather than around the written papers alone. Exploration drafts, mock weeks and school assessment weeks absorb all of a Diploma student's capacity, and a plan that ignores them loses a fortnight each time one lands. The pattern that survives is a fixed weekly slot plus one mixed problem set in between, with the expectation that deadline weeks are for reading the student's own marked work rather than adding new material.

Ramadan changes the rhythm of the whole UAE working day, and Diploma families routinely move sessions to post-Iftar timing for the month. That works well for mathematics provided it is agreed in advance, because the whole household's evening shifts at once. Where the month overlaps a heavy internal deadline, the sensible move is to place timed Paper 3 practice outside it and use the lighter weeks for consolidation, rather than attempting the hardest work at the most disrupted time of year.

process.description: One long recurring slot in Gulf Standard Time, agreed around the bus run, activities and prayer times, plus one unlabelled mixed set between sessions. The unlabelled part is what builds method selection; labelled practice cannot.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before teaching
whyPoints.description: The first session sorts lost marks into content, selection and communication, because those three need different work. Tutoring that starts with a topic list is answering a question nobody asked, and in a 240-hour course there is no spare time for that.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 taught as a habit
whyPoints.description: Extended investigations reward reading an unfamiliar definition carefully and continuing when a part is stuck. Both are rehearsable, and neither is addressed by revising the syllabus again, which is what most HL maths support offers.

whyPoints.title: Mark-scheme literacy
whyPoints.description: Students see how method, accuracy and reasoning marks are awarded and write differently afterwards. We reference the official documents and link the board's own sources rather than reproducing or supplying board material.

whyPoints.title: A specialist rather than a nearby graduate
whyPoints.description: The pool of tutors who have taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level including Paper 3 is small. Online delivery means you choose from that pool rather than from the people willing to drive to your community on a Tuesday.

whyPoints.title: Honest about delivery
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one to one and online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visits are an India-only service. Several providers in this market leave that unstated until after an enquiry.

whyPoints.title: Clear about limits
whyPoints.description: No promised grade, no claim of IB or regulator approval, and no statistic without a sample size, a date and a method. If no AA HL specialist is free at your hour, you are told before anything is committed.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP Math AA HL tutor in Abu Dhabi look at first?
faqs.answer: A marked script, before any topic is taught. Every lost mark gets sorted into three piles: mathematics the student did not know, mathematics they knew but could not select under unlabelled conditions, and mathematics they did correctly and were not paid for because the working, the rounding or the justification fell short. The proportions decide the plan, because those three repairs cost two sessions, a term and however long the content takes respectively. A tutor who begins with a syllabus checklist is guessing which one you are buying.

faqs.question: My son says his lost marks are just careless. Is that actually fixable?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and faster than anything else in the course, because careless is almost always a systematic failure to write for an examiner. IB mark schemes award method, accuracy and reasoning marks separately. A student who shows no intermediate working loses method marks, one who rounds mid-question loses accuracy marks, and one who thinks the justification instead of writing it loses reasoning marks. None of that is attention; all of it is habit. Two to four sessions comparing his scripts against how marks are allocated typically returns more marks per hour than new content.

faqs.question: What does the command term hence mean in an AA HL question?
faqs.answer: It means use the result you have just obtained. The method mark is attached to using that previous result, so a student who starts again with an independent approach can reach the correct answer and still lose marks. Hence or otherwise is different: it permits any valid method. The distinction is worth real marks across both calculator and non-calculator papers, and students who have never had it pointed out tend to treat both phrases as decoration. We drill it on questions the student has already solved, rewriting only the first line.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter lose accuracy marks when her method is right?
faqs.answer: Almost always premature rounding. Unless a question says otherwise, a final answer is expected to three significant figures, and a value rounded mid-calculation and carried forward produces a final answer that is wrong in the third figure. The method marks survive and the accuracy mark goes. The fix is mechanical: keep full precision, store intermediate values rather than retyping them, round once at the end. Have her solve the same question twice, rounding as she goes and then storing, and compare the answers. The habit changes after that demonstration.

faqs.question: When does an AA HL answer need exact form rather than a decimal?
faqs.answer: Whenever the question asks for an exact value, and always implicitly on the non-calculator paper, where a decimal approximation cannot be produced legitimately in the first place. Exact means a surd, a fraction, a logarithm or a multiple of pi, and a calculator decimal earns nothing in its place however correct it looks. The reverse error is equally costly: giving an exact form when the question asked for three significant figures. Training a student to read for exact, to three significant figures or to the nearest before starting takes one session and a month to automate.

faqs.question: Is a graphical calculator a help or a liability in AA HL?
faqs.answer: Both, depending on the paper and the question. On the calculator papers it is faster than algebra for intersections, turning points and numerical solutions, and a student who cannot use it fluently loses time they need elsewhere. It becomes a liability when it substitutes for understanding, because Paper 1 is sat without it and because questions demanding exact form award nothing for a decimal. The practical balance is fluency plus judgement: know the calculator well, and read every question for whether it is permitted to help.

faqs.question: What should be secure in AA HL by the end of DP1?
faqs.answer: Six things, tested cold without the topic named: manipulation of rational expressions without a calculator, the four differentiation rules chosen without prompting, integration by substitution and by parts with limits changed and the constant kept, the four-part structure of a proof by induction, complex numbers moved between forms with arguments in range, and the ability to identify the required technique in an unlabelled question within about a minute. Run that audit in June. A short known list before the summer is worth far more than the same list discovered in February of DP2.

faqs.question: How do small Higher Level maths classes in Abu Dhabi affect my child?
faqs.answer: Many Abu Dhabi IB schools run a single HL mathematics class per year group, which has two effects. The pace is set by the students who are coping, because one class cannot be differentiated into two sets, and there is no lower group to move into if the pace is wrong. So a student who loses two weeks to travel, illness or a hard topic has no internal route back, and in a course built on cumulative algebraic fluency that gap compounds. This is structural rather than a criticism of schools, and it is the honest reason tutoring is common here.

faqs.question: What is a tutor allowed to do with my child's AA HL exploration draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the mathematics, test early whether a chosen topic can carry mathematics at the level of the course, explain what each of the five criteria rewards, demonstrate technique on different material, and give feedback on a draft the student has already produced. A tutor cannot supply content for submission or rewrite the draft on the student's behalf. Everything submitted is the student's own work. The student is the person the IB would penalise, which is precisely why the boundary protects them.

faqs.question: Which exploration criterion costs Higher Level students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Use of mathematics, because at Higher Level the mathematics must be commensurate with the level of the course. A well-presented exploration built on Standard Level techniques is capped, and students find this out late because the piece reads as finished. The second most common loss is reflection, which students write as how they felt about the project rather than as an evaluation of the mathematics: what the model misses, what a different assumption would change, where the result is sensitive. Both are teachable by questioning, which is the appropriate kind of help.

faqs.question: Is one ninety-minute AA HL session a week enough?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes, provided a mixed unlabelled problem set is completed between sessions. HL mathematics rewards a long slot over a frequent one because the useful unit of work is a complete problem followed by the repair it exposes, and that does not fit into forty minutes. Two short sessions a week tend to become two interrupted ones. What does more than adding hours is making the between-session set mixed and unlabelled, because that is the only way method selection improves.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change an AA HL revision plan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The evening shifts for the whole household, and Diploma families routinely move sessions to post-Iftar timing for the month. That works well for mathematics if it is agreed in advance rather than improvised week by week. Where Ramadan overlaps a heavy internal deadline or a mock window, place timed Paper 3 practice outside it and keep the disrupted weeks for consolidation and shorter drills. Attempting the most demanding work at the most disrupted point of the year is the mistake, and it is avoidable by planning in the first week of term.

faqs.question: Which degree routes actually ask for Higher Level Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Some engineering, mathematics, physics and quantitative economics programmes name Analysis and Approaches specifically, and others accept either Higher Level mathematics course. The requirement varies between institutions and between faculties inside the same institution, including within the UAE, so the only reliable method is to read each programme's own admissions page and, where it is ambiguous, email the admissions office. Do not let a tutoring page, including this one, be your source for an entry requirement, and do not let anyone suggest that tutoring is required for admission.

faqs.question: Does a private maths tutor in Abu Dhabi need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service via its smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount quoted online.

faqs.question: What happens if no AA HL specialist is free at our hour?
faqs.answer: You are told before anything is committed. The usual options are a different hour with the specialist, a fortnightly rhythm with longer problem sets in between, or a tutor whose Higher Level experience is in the other mathematics route and who says so plainly. What we will not do is place a Standard Level or general maths tutor and describe them as an AA HL specialist, because at this level the gap appears in the first Paper 3 question and a family has by then paid for a month of approximate help.

intro.heading: Why one Standard Level hour is quoted at AED 150 and another at AED 450
paragraphs: Pricing in this market is opaque on purpose. Three of the six highest-ranking pages for Abu Dhabi tutoring queries publish no price at all, and one of those asks the price in its own list of questions and then declines to answer it. Two more quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. So a parent gathering quotes for Standard Level Analysis support ends up with a spread from roughly AED 150 to well over AED 450 an hour and no way to tell what the difference buys.

Most of the spread is explained by four things, and only one of them is teaching quality. The first is format: a group class at a tuition centre, a one-to-one video lesson and a tutor who drives to Khalifa City are three different products priced as if they were one. The second is travel, which is inside an in-home rate whether or not it appears as a line. The third is specialism: a Diploma mathematics teacher who marks against the exploration criteria commands more than a general secondary maths tutor, and reasonably so. The fourth is simply what the provider thinks you will pay, which is why identical hours are quoted hundreds of dirhams apart.

The honest market picture, from figures their own publishers put in writing, looks like this. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, starts at around AED 33 to 65 an hour at the entry rates EdFlik and Tutopiya advertise. Qualified subject tutors online sit roughly between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits run about AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's Dubai rate table and up to AED 500 in specialist home-tutor listings. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists cluster at AED 200 to 450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named or examiner-led tutoring reaches AED 650, which is BartyED's published figure.

None of those are IB Gram's prices, and this page does not pretend otherwise. What IB Gram does is match a Standard Level Analysis student to a specialist in that exact course and level and deliver the lessons one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address: home visits in Abu Dhabi are not part of what we sell, and that service exists only in India. The first lesson costs nothing, is one per student, requires no card and no block booking, and exists to produce a written diagnosis rather than a quote.

What follows is the arithmetic rather than the argument. The provider models side by side with their own published rates. The seven factors that genuinely move a Standard Level quote in Abu Dhabi, from the district you live in to the week of the academic year you ask. What a term-length plan comes to monthly rather than hourly, since that is the number a household budget actually works with. Where families in this emirate most often waste money. And the things worth trying before paying anyone at all, which is not advice a tutoring page usually offers.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: What you pay for depends on which programme your child is in, because the assessment load differs sharply. These are the programmes behind an Abu Dhabi mathematics enquiry, with what each one does to the cost of support.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level carries 150 teaching hours, two examination papers at 40 per cent each and an exploration at 20 per cent. It is the mathematics course most Abu Dhabi Diploma students take, and the one most often supported for a single term rather than two years.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma support in Abu Dhabi is usually bought in DP2 rather than DP1, which is the expensive way round. A weekly Standard Level hour started in DP1 at a mid-market rate costs less over two years than a pre-examination intensive block at specialist rates, and it produces a tutor who already knows how your child works under time pressure. The cheapest plan is almost always the early one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups marked against four criteria each on a 1-8 scale, with no external examinations before the optional MYP 5 eAssessment. Mathematics support here is cheaper per hour than Diploma support, because the content is less specialised, and far cheaper in total, because problems caught in MYP 4 do not become Standard Level foundation gaps in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families often meet the mathematics route decision in MYP 5, when the DP1 option form arrives before the MYP results do. A short block of two or three sessions purely to establish whether Analysis or Applications fits is one of the better-value purchases available in this market, and it is almost never the one families make.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. A student taking Standard Level Analysis within this programme sits the same two papers and submits the same exploration, so the cost of support is the same as for a full Diploma candidate.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi this programme is uncommon but it exists, and it occasionally becomes the sensible answer when a family is spending heavily on four subjects at once. Where support is being bought across several subjects simultaneously, the conversation worth having is with the Diploma coordinator about load, before the one with a tutor about hours.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Where Abu Dhabi families spend most, by subject. These are the Diploma subjects that attract the heaviest tutoring spend in this emirate, with a note on what drives the rate in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Two 90-minute papers of 80 marks each at 40 per cent apiece, plus a 20-mark exploration. Rates sit in the mid-band because the course is widely taught and the tutor pool is deeper than at Higher Level. Spend rises in DP2 when the exploration deadline and the mock window land in the same month.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The same five topic areas over 240 hours instead of 150, with a third paper worth 20 per cent. Quotes run above Standard Level because Paper 3 narrows the pool of people who can teach it. A Standard Level student should not be paying a Higher Level rate for content they will not be examined on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology rather than proof. Priced similarly to Analysis at the same level, with one difference: students who moved across in DP1 often need a short bridging block, and that is a defined short cost rather than an open-ended plan.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Among the highest spend in Abu Dhabi, partly because the specialist pool is small and partly because weak mathematics shows up here as a second sinking grade. Families frequently buy physics support when the actual purchase they need is calculus fluency.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: High demand around the scientific investigation and the equilibrium and energetics topics. Rates match the general IB specialist band, and the common waste is buying weekly hours all year when the problem is concentrated in two topics and one internal deadline.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Support here is usually bought for the internal assessment commentaries rather than the papers, which makes it a short defined block instead of a term-long commitment. Quotes should reflect that; a term-length plan for three commentaries is a plan sold rather than needed.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Priced at the lower end of the specialist band in the UAE because the pool is larger. The individual oral and the written tasks are where the hours concentrate, and both are feedback-intensive rather than content-intensive, which changes what an hour should contain.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A narrow specialism in Abu Dhabi, which pushes quotes towards the upper band. This is the clearest case in the Diploma where online matching changes the price you can access, because the local in-home pool is close to empty.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Charged as essay-feedback sessions rather than weekly teaching, and the hours needed are few. A plan proposing a term of weekly Theory of Knowledge lessons for one 1,600-word essay is worth questioning before it is paid for.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Normally two to five sessions spread across a year, timed to the school's internal deadlines. Supervision is the school's job; a tutor's contribution is research-question narrowing and feedback on the student's own drafts, which is a small and well-bounded cost.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-home-tutor.regionsIntro: District matters less to an online rate than families expect, and a great deal to an in-home one. These notes cover what the geography of Abu Dhabi does to the price of a visit, and what it does to the hour a session can start.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Central island streets with the shortest drives in the city, so in-home quotes here sit at the lower end of the travel premium and a 4.30pm start is realistic. These are the only Abu Dhabi districts where an in-home rate is close to a fair comparison with an online one.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A large villa area twenty to forty minutes from the island depending on the hour. In-home tutors either price that drive in or decline the booking, which is why families here gather the widest spread of quotes for an identical Standard Level hour.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Dense enough that an in-home tutor can sometimes fit two students in one evening, which is the one circumstance where a visiting rate is competitive. Ask whether the quote assumes that second booking, because it usually does.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Bridge traffic decides when a student is at a desk, and an in-home tutor crossing at 5pm is paying for it in time. Standard Level sessions from this island tend to start at 6pm or later regardless of format.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: Newer capacity with small Diploma cohorts and a thin local tutor pool, so in-home quotes carry a visible premium and group classes often are not available at all for a specific Standard Level topic.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Mainland communities with the longest commutes to the island schools. A weekday session before 5.30pm is usually unrealistic here, and weekend blocks are both cheaper in practice and more productive than a tired 7pm hour.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Further out again, where the travel component of an in-home quote is highest and the local specialist pool is smallest. Nearly every Standard Level enquiry from these districts ends up as a video arrangement for that reason alone.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Short postings and frequent relocations, which changes the spending question: families here want a plan that survives a mid-year move rather than the lowest hourly figure. An online tutor transfers between countries without being rehired.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Saadiyat schools
schoolClusters.note: Established Abu Dhabi schools and the newer Saadiyat campuses, with fees towards the top of the emirate's range. Families here are typically comparing a tutoring spend against an already substantial school bill, which is why cost in context matters more than an hourly figure.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas schools
schoolClusters.note: The corridor holding most of Abu Dhabi's newer international capacity, with a wide fee spread. Raha International School runs the full IB continuum; several neighbours run British or American routes, so mathematics tutoring demand in this cluster is split across three different assessment systems.

modes.title: Weekly Standard Level hour
modes.description: One fixed hour a week with the same tutor, work set at the end of each session and marked before the next. Spread across a term this is the lowest cost per unit of progress, because nothing is repaid later in intensive rates, and it is the only format where a tutor builds a usable picture of how your child works against the clock.

modes.description: Three to five sessions timed to the school's internal deadlines, focused on the five criterion letters carrying the twenty marks. A defined block has a defined cost, which is the point: exploration support should never be an open-ended monthly commitment, and the highest-value session is the one before any mathematics is attempted.

This is the most expensive way to buy the same progress, which is worth knowing before you choose it. It works, and it works better when it is topping up a weekly hour that started months earlier.

sections.heading: What an hour of Standard Level Analysis costs in Abu Dhabi, by provider model
paragraphs: The useful comparison is not between named companies but between models, because the model determines the cost structure. A tuition centre pays rent and fills a room; a visiting tutor pays for a car and loses an hour in traffic; an online platform pays for matching and marking; a freelance tutor prices on whatever the last family agreed to. Four cost structures, four quite different numbers for an hour that a parent experiences as the same hour.

Every figure in the table below was published by whoever is credited for it and read in October 2026. Nothing in it is IB Gram's price list, and no figure here is an average of anything. Read it as the market's own disclosure, which is more than most of this market offers: three of the six strongest ranking pages for these queries publish no price at all, and the two that do publish in dollars.

The pattern worth noticing is that the in-home premium is not a quality premium. A visiting tutor at AED 300 and an online specialist at AED 300 are not the same purchase: in the first, some of the hour is a drive from the island to Khalifa City, and the pool of tutors available is whoever will make that drive on a Tuesday. The second is the whole pool and the whole hour. That is the single most consequential line in a Standard Level budget, and no competitor page states it.

On the last row, be careful. Private tuition in the UAE requires a MoHRE work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. The permit costs nothing, so a tutor charging you a premium to cover licensing is charging for something that is free. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

sections.heading: Seven things that move a Standard Level quote in this emirate
paragraphs: A quote is not a price, it is a response to your circumstances, and in Abu Dhabi the circumstances that move it are fairly predictable. Geography is the largest for in-home work: a tutor living on the island quoting for Al Shamkha is pricing a forty-minute drive each way. Timing is the second: the 5pm to 8pm weekday window is what nearly every Diploma family in the Gulf asks for, so it carries the most competition and the least flexibility.

Then comes the week of the academic year. Enquiries cluster before mocks and again a few weeks before the May session, and a specialist with a full timetable in March has no commercial reason to discount. The same request in September meets an emptier diary. Families who plan a weekly hour in DP1 are buying in the cheap part of the market; families ringing round in the final term are buying in the expensive part, with less time for it to work.

Specialism, format and the number of subjects also move the figure, and so does what is bundled. Two quotes of AED 250 are not comparable if one includes marking a timed paper between sessions and a written note, and the other is sixty minutes of conversation with no work set. The questions that separate them are simple: who marks the work, what arrives in writing afterwards, and what happens to the fee if a session is cancelled on either side.

The last factor is the one nobody lists. A quote often reflects what the provider thinks a family in a given district will pay, which is why an identical Standard Level hour is sometimes priced differently for Saadiyat Island and for Baniyas. Asking for the rate before describing your villa is not cynicism; it is how you find out whether you are being quoted a price or a postcode.

sections.heading: Monthly rather than hourly: what a term actually comes to
paragraphs: Households do not budget in hours, they budget in months, and the hourly figure is a poor guide to the monthly one. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session put budget tutoring at roughly AED 240 to 600, mid-market at AED 600 to 1,200 and specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Packaged offers seen in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those two package shapes are worth comparing carefully, because they are not the same product. Eight shorter online sessions distribute the work across a month, which is how a mathematics habit changes; four long in-home sessions concentrate it, which suits revision better than it suits learning. For Standard Level Analysis, where most of the useful work is practice between lessons rather than inside them, the frequent shorter pattern generally does more per dirham.

The table converts the published bands into plan shapes rather than packages, because the real question is how many hours a Standard Level student needs rather than what a provider wants to sell. A DP1 student with one weak topic area does not need the same plan as a DP2 student eight weeks from the papers with an unwritten exploration, and pricing them identically is how families end up paying twice.

One warning on pre-payment. A discounted ten-lesson block looks like a saving and is also a commitment made before anyone has seen your child work. If a block is offered, ask what happens to the unused portion if the match is wrong, and prefer an arrangement where the first lesson is free and the commitment starts afterwards. A provider confident in the match has no reason to need the money first.

sections.heading: What you are buying: Standard Level Analysis, precisely
paragraphs: Before paying for anything, check that the course on the quote matches the course on the timetable. Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level is 150 teaching hours across five topic areas, assessed by two papers of 90 minutes and 80 marks each, weighted 40 per cent apiece, plus a mathematical exploration worth 20 per cent and marked out of 20. There is no Paper 3 at Standard Level. A tutor quoting for Paper 3 preparation is quoting for the wrong course, and that is a surprisingly common way for families to overpay.

The two papers differ in one respect that drives most of the useful teaching. The first is sat without a calculator and rewards exact values, surds, logarithm manipulation and visible algebraic method. The second allows a graphic display calculator and punishes students who use it to produce an answer without writing the steps that earn the method marks. A Standard Level student who practises everything with technology to hand is rehearsing for one paper and not the other, and that pattern alone explains a great many disappointing mock results.

The exploration is where the spend decision is clearest. It is 20 per cent of the grade for a document of about twelve to twenty pages, marked across five criterion letters: presentation and mathematical communication at four marks each, personal engagement and reflection at three each, and use of mathematics at six. Because presentation, engagement and reflection carry fourteen of the twenty marks between them, the cheapest useful intervention is a single session before any mathematics is attempted, while the research question can still change.

Confirm the hours, weightings and criteria against your child's own copy of the current subject guide, which the school issues. The IB revises its guides and a tutoring page is not a syllabus. What is stable enough to budget around is the shape: two papers, no third paper, an internally assessed exploration, and a course whose content is more than two-thirds shared with Higher Level but assessed over considerably less examination time.

sections.heading: Tutoring spend in context: fees, places and what the market is doing
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means little without the bill it sits beside. For scale in the region, Dubai's private school sector reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate students making up about 7 per cent of the total. That is the context in which a Diploma mathematics specialist is a narrow trade: a small share of a large market, which is exactly the shape that produces thin local supply and wide price spreads.

Fee policy is also moving. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package, and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four British and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places after enrolment rose 6 per cent in 2025-26. Those are Dubai figures from KHDA's own publications. Abu Dhabi fee policy sits with the Department of Education and Knowledge, and the current position should be read on ADEK's own pages rather than inferred from Dubai.

What this means for an Abu Dhabi household is that tutoring is a discretionary line next to a large fixed one, and the discretionary line is where the control sits. A weekly Standard Level hour at the mid-market band runs to a few hundred dirhams a month more than nothing and considerably less than a term of intensive support. The expensive outcome is not the hourly rate; it is buying two years of weekly hours when the diagnosis called for six sessions, or buying six sessions when the problem was a missing foundation.

The other context worth pricing is the examination itself. A candidate entered privately rather than through their school pays entry fees set by the board and administered by a centre, which is a separate cost from tuition and is not something a tutor can arrange on your behalf. If anyone quotes a combined figure covering tuition and examination entry, ask for the two numbers separately and ask which centre is named.

sections.heading: Where Abu Dhabi families most often waste money on maths support
paragraphs: The commonest waste is hiring a generalist for a specific Diploma problem. A capable secondary maths tutor who has not taught Analysis and Approaches can run twenty pleasant sessions and change nothing, because the marks are being lost against named criteria in named components, and recognising that requires having marked the thing before. Families usually discover this in week five, having spent four figures to find out.

The second is buying hours before a diagnosis. A plan agreed over the phone on the strength of a reported grade is a plan aimed at an unknown target. A method-mark habit is three sessions; a missed topic area is six; a missing foundation underneath the course is a term and possibly a conversation about level instead. Those are wildly different purchases, and the only way to tell them apart is for somebody to read a marked script and watch the student work under time.

The third is the group class bought for an individual weakness. Group teaching has real value for pace and coverage, and almost none for a student whose problem is that they do not write method on Paper 2. The centre's schedule covers the syllabus in syllabus order, which is not the order your child's gaps are in. Paying per student for a shared pace is only cheap if the pace happens to match.

The fourth is the pre-examination intensive bought as a first resort. It is the most expensive way to acquire progress, because it buys specialist hours in the most contested weeks of the year and leaves no time for practice between sessions to do its work. It is also sometimes exactly right. The distinction is whether it is topping up a plan that has been running, or standing in for one that never existed.

sections.heading: The travel premium, and the arithmetic nobody shows you
paragraphs: Work the in-home figure through properly. A visiting tutor who accepts a 5pm booking in Khalifa City from a base on the island is committing somewhere around eighty minutes of driving around a sixty-minute lesson. No tutor absorbs that indefinitely, so it appears in the rate, in a two-hour minimum, in a refusal to take single bookings, or in a quiet preference for students who live near each other. Those are all versions of the same cost, and only one of them is visible on a quote.

There is a second cost that is harder to see. Travel shrinks the pool of people who will take your booking at all, and for Standard Level Analysis that pool is not large to begin with. The question that matters is not whether a tutor will come to your district; it is whether the person who will come to your district is the person who should be teaching this course. In much of Abu Dhabi, away from the central island streets, those are different people.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address, and home visits in Abu Dhabi are not something we sell; that service exists only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, the same tutor each week, with work set and marked between sessions. The argument for it here is financial as much as pedagogical: you stop paying for a drive, and you start choosing from everyone who teaches the course rather than everyone who lives near you.

For completeness, one in-home route genuinely does not exist. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff says paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school is prohibited, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE permit, whose code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording on ADEK's own policy page before relying on it, and do not budget for that option.

sections.heading: What to try before paying anyone at all
paragraphs: Some of the best interventions for Standard Level Analysis are free, and a tutoring page that does not say so is not being straight with you. Start with the school. A Diploma mathematics teacher running a set of fifteen will usually give a specific answer to a specific question, and the question that gets the most useful answer is not how my child is doing but which topic area and which paper the marks are being lost in. Ask for the mark breakdown by question rather than the percentage.

Second, change the practice conditions at home before changing the teaching. Have the student do one 90-minute section without a calculator, timed, with a phone in another room, and mark it against the published scheme. A surprising share of Standard Level problems resolve into two findings from that single exercise: the student has been practising with technology they will not have in Paper 1, and they are not writing the method the scheme awards marks for.

Third, use the free material that actually exists. Boards and schools publish specimen papers, subject guides and mark schemes, and the student's own school will have them. What you should not do is pay anyone for copies of past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables or subject guides, and nobody should be reproducing them for you: those documents belong to the boards, and reference and a link is the correct form.

Only after those three, consider paying. And when you do, take the free first lesson before agreeing to anything. One lesson, one per student, no card, no block booking, and it exists to produce a written diagnosis naming the leaking component. If that note says the problem belongs with the school rather than with a tutor, it says so, and you have spent nothing to learn the most useful thing available.

process.title: Send the course, the level and the last marked script
process.description: 'Analysis and Approaches SL, Paper 1 came back at 47 per cent, exploration not started' is a sentence that determines both the match and the plan. A reported grade without a script is a figure without a cause, and it is how families end up buying hours for the wrong component.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic lesson first
process.description: One lesson, one per student, no card details and no block booking. The tutor reads the marked work, asks your child to attempt something timed, and sends a written note naming the leaking component and the realistic shape of the fix, including the case where the honest answer is that the school should handle it.

process.title: Price the plan the diagnosis calls for
process.description: Three sessions for a method-mark habit, six for a missed topic area, a defined block for the exploration, or a term if the foundation is genuinely missing. Agree the shape before the rate, because a cheap hour aimed at the wrong component is the most expensive thing in this market.

process.title: Set a review point four to six weeks out
process.description: Agree at the start when you will look at evidence rather than impressions, and what evidence it will be: per-question marks, method marks earned on calculator questions, completion time on a timed section. A review date fixed in advance is worth more than any discount negotiated at the start.

process.title: Stop, change or extend on the evidence
process.description: If the scripts have moved, continue. If they have not, change the tutor, the format or the diagnosis rather than adding hours to a plan that is not working. Renewing because a plan has become routine is how a few hundred dirhams a month becomes several thousand with nothing to show.

faqs.question: What should we expect to pay for Standard Level Analysis support in the Abu Dhabi market?
faqs.answer: Published UAE bands put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, IB and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450, in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 reaching about 500 at the specialist end, and entry-level online tutoring from AED 33 to 65. TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Standard Level Analysis usually sits in the middle of the specialist band, below Higher Level, because the course has no third paper and a deeper tutor pool. Those are market figures from their publishers, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Why would two tutors quote AED 180 and AED 400 for what sounds like the same Standard Level hour?
faqs.answer: Four reasons, and only one is teaching quality. Format: a group class, a video lesson and a visit to your district are different products. Travel: an in-home rate contains the drive whether or not it is itemised. Specialism: someone who marks against the exploration criteria and teaches this course costs more than a general maths tutor. And what is bundled: marking a timed paper between sessions and sending a written note is worth considerably more than sixty minutes of conversation. Ask who marks the work and what arrives in writing, and the two quotes stop looking comparable.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class cheaper than one-to-one for this course?
faqs.answer: Per hour, usually yes: entry rates published in this market start around AED 33 to 65 per student. Per unit of progress, it depends entirely on the problem. A group covers the syllabus in syllabus order at the centre's pace, which is excellent for coverage and nearly useless for a student whose specific issue is that they produce answers on a calculator without writing method. If the weakness is broad and the student is behind across topics, a group is good value. If it is one named habit in one paper, you are paying for a pace that does not fit.

faqs.question: Does a visiting maths tutor in Abu Dhabi charge for travel time?
faqs.answer: Almost always, though rarely as a separate line. A tutor accepting a 5pm booking in Khalifa City from a base on the island is committing roughly eighty minutes of driving around a sixty-minute lesson, and that appears as a higher hourly rate, a two-hour minimum, a refusal to take single bookings, or a preference for students living close together. The second cost is less visible: travel shrinks the pool willing to take the booking, and for Standard Level Analysis that pool is already thin outside the central island districts.

faqs.question: Are tutoring fees in Abu Dhabi quoted with VAT included or added?
faqs.answer: Ask, in writing, before you agree anything, because practice varies between providers and the answer changes the number. We do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees on this page, because that is a Federal Tax Authority matter and any claim about it should carry an FTA citation rather than a tutoring company's opinion. What a family can reasonably insist on is clarity about the specific quote in front of them: is this figure the total payable, and does the provider hold a tax registration number if they are charging tax on it.

faqs.question: How many Standard Level sessions does a term usually come to, and what is the monthly figure?
faqs.answer: A weekly hour is four sessions a month, which Bestimate's monthly estimates place at roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Packaged offers in this market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. For Standard Level Analysis, frequent shorter sessions generally outperform fewer long ones, because most of the useful work happens between lessons rather than inside them.

faqs.question: Do maths tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi climb before the May session?
faqs.answer: Effective rates do, even where published ones do not. Enquiries cluster before mocks and again in the weeks before the May examinations, and a specialist with a full timetable in March has no commercial reason to discount or to offer a convenient slot. The same request in September meets an emptier diary and more flexibility on both price and timing. Families who start a weekly hour in DP1 are buying in the cheap part of the market; families ringing round in the final term are buying in the expensive part, with less time left for it to work.

faqs.question: Should we pay for a discounted block of ten lessons up front?
faqs.answer: Only after a free diagnostic lesson, and only if you know what happens to the unused portion. A pre-paid block looks like a saving and is also a commitment made before anyone has watched your child work, which is the wrong order. Ask three questions: what is refunded if the match is wrong, does the block expire, and who marks the work between sessions. A provider confident in the match has no particular reason to need the money first, and the first lesson being free should not depend on a block being bought.

faqs.question: Is exploration support billed separately from the weekly Standard Level lessons?
faqs.answer: It should be visible either way, because it is a defined piece of work rather than an open-ended one. The exploration is 20 per cent of the grade and 20 marks across five criterion letters, and most students need three to five focused sessions timed to the school's internal deadlines. Priced as a block, that cost has an end date. Priced as an extension of a monthly plan, it tends not to. The highest-value session is the first one, before any mathematics is attempted, while the research question can still be changed.

faqs.question: Our budget is around AED 150 an hour. Is Standard Level support still worth starting?
faqs.answer: Yes, with realistic expectations about what that band buys. At AED 150 you are at the lower edge of the qualified-subject-tutor range rather than in the IB specialist band, so ask directly whether the tutor has taught Analysis and Approaches and marked an exploration against its criteria. Then concentrate the budget: fortnightly sessions on one named weakness, with marked work in between, beat weekly general lessons at the same monthly spend. Take the free first lesson before committing, because the diagnosis may show the fix is three sessions rather than a term.

faqs.question: Does one tutor covering two Diploma subjects cost less than hiring two?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but check what you are trading. A tutor who genuinely teaches both Analysis and Approaches and Physics at the level your child sits them is a real saving in money and in coordination. A tutor who teaches one well and the other approximately is a false economy, because the weaker subject quietly absorbs hours without moving. In Abu Dhabi the common pairing is maths with physics, and the honest version of the answer is that it depends on the individual tutor rather than on the policy.

faqs.question: What should an hourly rate actually include besides the lesson itself?
faqs.answer: At the specialist end of this market, a reasonable expectation is work set at the end of each session, that work marked before the next, a short written note saying what moved, and a named recurring error being tracked rather than silently corrected. Messages between sessions vary by provider and should be asked about rather than assumed. Two quotes at the same figure are not the same purchase if one contains all of that and the other is sixty minutes of conversation, and the difference is invisible until the first month has been paid for.

faqs.question: What exactly does the free first lesson include, and what is the catch?
faqs.answer: One lesson, one per student, with no card details taken and no block booking required. The tutor reads the most recent marked work, asks your child to attempt something under time, and sends you a written note naming which component is losing marks and the realistic shape of the fix. The condition is simply that it is a single lesson rather than a trial period, and that it is diagnostic rather than a free hour of teaching. If the note concludes the problem belongs with the school, it says so and nothing further is sold.

faqs.question: How does a tutoring spend compare with what Abu Dhabi families already pay in school fees?
faqs.answer: It is a small discretionary line beside a large fixed one, which is exactly why it is worth controlling rather than guessing at. For regional scale, Dubai reported 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, with IB students about 7 per cent of the total, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai fees would not rise for 2026-27. Abu Dhabi fee policy sits with ADEK and should be read on its own pages. The expensive error is never the hourly rate; it is buying two years of hours when the diagnosis called for six sessions.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest thing to try before hiring anyone for Standard Level maths?
faqs.answer: Three things, all free. Ask the school's mathematics teacher for the mark breakdown by question rather than the percentage, and ask which topic area and which paper the marks are going in. Then have your child sit one timed 90-minute non-calculator section at home, phone in another room, marked against the published scheme. Then look at what that exercise reveals, which is often that the practice conditions were wrong rather than the teaching. Do not pay anyone for copies of past papers, mark schemes or subject guides; the school has them and the boards own them.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-home-tutor.closingHeading: Get the diagnosis first, then price the plan
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-home-tutor.closingBody: The number that decides what Standard Level Analysis support costs your household is not the hourly rate. It is how many hours the actual problem needs, and that is knowable in one free lesson rather than guessable over the phone. Send the course, the level and the most recent marked script, and say which paper the marks are going in if you know. You will get a written note naming the leaking component and the realistic shape of the fix, priced as a block where a block is what is needed. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, every AED figure on this page belongs to the source named beside it, and if the honest answer is that you should not be buying hours at all, the note will say that too.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Diploma Programme Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level. The relevant question for a family comparing quotes is not how senior a tutor sounds but whether an hour with them returns marks, and that is decided by what the hour contains.

intro.heading: The number nobody publishes, and the six things that move it
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranked tutoring pages for UAE searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. One of them even asks the price question in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it. That is the state of the market a family in Abu Dhabi is trying to compare, which is why this page leads with figures rather than with description. Everything quoted below was published by a provider or a rate tracker and read in October 2026, and every band is the market rather than an IB Gram price list.

The headline picture is this. Budget online provision, usually a university student or a generalist, advertises from roughly AED 33 to 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300. In-home one-to-one work, with travel inside the rate, runs about AED 180 to 500. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level provision is published around AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium named or examiner-branded provision has been advertised as high as AED 650. Monthly figures published for weekly one-hour sessions run from about AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

Those bands are wide because the product inside them varies enormously, and a parent comparing two quotes at AED 220 is often comparing two completely different hours. So the second half of this page is about what the hour has to contain for Standard Level Analysis and Approaches specifically: a marked script read for method and accuracy losses, unlabelled mixed practice rather than topic drills, and exploration work timed early enough to still change the topic. An hour that contains none of those is not cheap at AED 150.

Abu Dhabi changes the arithmetic in two ways. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection ratings, and the Diploma population is spread across the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor and the newer mainland communities, so the in-home market here prices distance heavily. And many schools run one Standard Level maths class per year group, which means a student who slips has no second set inside school and the external hour carries more weight than it would in a larger cohort.

IB Gram delivers to Abu Dhabi families one to one and online, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visits are a service we run only in India. We also do not publish our own hourly figure here and present it as the market rate, because a provider quoting itself is not research. The commercial answer is a first session at no charge, one per student, which produces a written diagnosis you can take to any provider you like.
