abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.programmesIntro: Which course your child sits, and when in the two years you start, change the quote more than any other factor. Here is how each route prices.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
programmes.description: A 150-hour Standard Level course covering number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, assessed by two written papers plus the mathematical exploration. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and Paper 2 with a graphical calculator. Confirm the current mark allocations and weightings against the subject guide through your school's IB coordinator.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, Standard Level support generally prices in the middle of the published bands rather than at the specialist end, because the pool of tutors who can teach it competently is larger than the Higher Level pool. The quote hardens from January, when DP2 families across the emirate start at the same time and the better evening slots fill first.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
programmes.description: The 240-hour Higher Level version, with three written papers including the extended problem-solving Paper 3, plus substantial additional content such as proof by induction, complex numbers and differential equations. The tutor pool is materially smaller, which is what pushes Higher Level quotes towards the specialist band.
programmes.countryNote: Relevant to a Standard Level family for one reason: if a move up or down the levels is under discussion, the cost of support changes with it. Ask the Diploma coordinator about the timetable mechanics before pricing anything, because in a small Abu Dhabi cohort the decision can turn on whether both classes run in the same slot.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
programmes.description: The other Standard Level route, weighted towards modelling, statistics and technology rather than algebraic proof. It is priced the same as Analysis and Approaches SL across the published bands, but the tutor has to have taught it, because the two courses diverge enough that generic maths support fits neither well.
programmes.countryNote: Families sometimes hope a course switch will remove the need to pay for tuition. It usually does not, because the gap being addressed is rarely course-specific: unlabelled question selection and accurate written working carry marks in both. Choose the course on degree requirements and on the student, not on an expected saving.

programmes.name: Arriving from MYP or IGCSE mathematics
programmes.description: The two routes in. IGCSE builds procedural fluency on structured questions; MYP builds conceptual understanding against criteria. Standard Level assumes algebraic reliability from the first term, so a student arriving from either route may need six weeks on fluency before any Diploma content is worth teaching.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest moment in the whole two years to buy support, and almost nobody does. Four to six sessions in the summer before DP1, spent on algebraic fluency and unlabelled practice, cost a fraction of the same work bought in the February of DP2, when rates are at their firmest and the available improvement is smaller.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the parts of AA SL that generate most tutoring requests in Abu Dhabi, described by what an hour on each realistically returns.

subjects.name: Algebraic fluency
subjects.description: Manipulating expressions, solving equations and rearranging without a calculator. The cheapest possible investment, because every other topic depends on it and because it improves with short daily practice rather than with paid hours.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Composite and inverse functions, transformations, quadratics and exponentials. High return per hour, since SL questions frequently combine a transformation with a small calculus demand and students who learn each separately cannot answer the combination.

subjects.name: Differentiation
subjects.description: Rules of differentiation, tangents and normals, stationary points and optimisation. The usual loss is the chain rule applied to the outer function only, and the second is a stationary point found and never classified when the question asked for a justification.

subjects.name: Integration
subjects.description: Definite and indefinite integration, areas, and basic substitution. Reliably worth paid hours because the errors are systematic: the missing constant, the limits left unchanged, and the area taken as the integral when part of the curve is below the axis.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Identities, equations, the unit circle and triangle rules. Marks go missing on solution ranges rather than on method, which makes this a topic where one session on reading the domain can return several marks on a paper.

subjects.name: Sequences, series and exponentials
subjects.description: Arithmetic and geometric progressions, sums, compound growth and logarithms. Mostly procedural, so it responds well to drilling, and it is a sensible candidate for self-study with a problem set rather than for paid teaching time.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Descriptive statistics, correlation and regression, probability and the normal distribution. Students often have the calculator technique and not the interpretation, which is where the marks sit, and interpretation is quick to teach.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique without a calculator
subjects.description: Exact values, surds, fractions and logarithms, with no decimal escape route. Worth separating from Paper 2 practice entirely, because the habits are different and a student who only practises with a calculator is unprepared for half the written assessment.

subjects.name: Paper 2 technique with a graphical calculator
subjects.description: Numerical solving, intersections, turning points and distributions, plus the judgement to know when the calculator is faster. Also where accuracy marks are lost to premature rounding, which is a one-session repair followed by a month of habit.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Marked against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The hours are worth most when spent early on topic choice, because a topic that cannot carry Standard Level mathematics cannot be rescued by polishing.

subjects.name: Command terms and written working
subjects.description: Show that, hence, justify and determine are instructions with marks attached, and IB mark schemes award method, accuracy and reasoning separately. The highest marks-per-hour work available in this course, and the work most tutoring skips.

subjects.name: Unlabelled mixed practice
subjects.description: Problem sets with no topic heading, which is the only way the skill of selecting a method improves. Cheap to supply and rarely supplied, because it is harder to teach from than a topic worksheet.

sections.heading: The six variables that move an AA SL quote in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: A quote is not a single number with noise around it. It is six decisions, most of which the family controls. Level is the first: Standard Level support prices below Higher Level because the tutor pool is larger. Timing in the academic year is the second and is routinely underestimated, because demand across the emirate arrives in January and the better evening slots are gone before the rates soften again. Session length is the third, with ninety-minute slots usually priced below two separate sixty-minute ones for the same total time.

The fourth is tutor tier, which is where the published bands separate most sharply, from budget generalist provision at the bottom to premium named or examiner-branded provision above AED 650. The fifth is delivery mode: in-home work carries a travel premium that in the outer Abu Dhabi communities is substantial, and small group or centre classes sit below one-to-one at the cost of individual marking attention. The sixth is commitment shape, where monthly packages are advertised at a discount to the hourly figure and also reduce your ability to stop.

Two of those six are worth optimising and four are worth understanding. Start earlier in the year and buy a longer single slot, and the same tutoring costs less and arrives in a better hour. Pay attention to tier only after establishing what the hour contains, because a specialist rate for an hour spent re-explaining topics the student already knows returns nothing. And be wary of optimising delivery mode towards in-home for a subject where the examined skill is written working that both people need to read at once.

sections.heading: Why Standard Level costs less than Higher Level, and when that is a false economy
paragraphs: The honest reason Standard Level support is cheaper is supply. A 150-hour course with two papers and no Paper 3 can be taught well by a much larger group of people than a 240-hour course with extended problem solving and substantial additional content. That is a real difference in scarcity, and it shows up in the published bands as a gap between qualified-tutor rates and specialist rates rather than as a difference in the quality of the teaching your child receives.

Where it becomes a false economy is in the exploration and in Paper 1. The exploration is marked against the same five criteria at both levels and carries the same twenty marks, and the criterion about using mathematics commensurate with the course level is judged against Standard Level rather than ignored. A cheap hour that treats the exploration as a write-up exercise rather than as a mathematics problem costs marks that are expensive to recover later, because a topic chosen badly in DP1 cannot be fixed in DP2.

Paper 1 is the other place where the cheapest hour underperforms. A tutor who teaches every topic with a calculator in hand is preparing a student for half of the written assessment. Exact values, surds and logarithmic manipulation need separate, deliberate, non-calculator practice, and a generalist maths tutor working from a textbook will often not separate them. That is worth asking about explicitly before comparing two quotes, because it is the difference between two hours that look identical on an invoice.

sections.heading: What an AA SL hour has to contain to be worth the money
paragraphs: Three things, and if an hour contains none of them the rate is irrelevant. The first is a marked script read line by line, with lost marks sorted into mathematics the student did not know, mathematics they could not select, and mathematics they did correctly and were not paid for because the working, the rounding or the justification fell short. That sorting is a fifteen-minute job for someone who has taught the course and it determines everything else.

The second is unlabelled practice. A worksheet headed Integration teaches integration; a mixed set with no headings teaches a student to recognise what a question is asking for, which is the skill that fails on an unseen paper. Almost no tutoring supplies this, because it is harder to teach from, and it is the cheapest thing a parent can insist on. Ask for the between-session set to be mixed and unlabelled, and ask the tutor what the student got wrong in last week's set before this week's session starts.

The third is specific exam-writing repair. Command terms with marks attached, method marks shown rather than implied, full precision carried and rounded once at the end, exact form supplied where the question demanded it. This is the highest marks-per-hour work in the whole course and it needs no new mathematics, which is why it belongs in the first month rather than in the fortnight before a mock. An hour spent re-explaining a topic the student already understands is the single most common way tutoring money is wasted in this market.

sections.heading: The cheapest fixes in AA SL, ranked by marks per AED
paragraphs: At the top of the list is premature rounding. Unless a question says otherwise, a final answer is expected to three significant figures, and a value rounded mid-calculation and carried forward produces a final answer wrong in the third figure, with the accuracy mark lost and the method marks intact. One session establishes the habit of storing values and rounding once; a month makes it automatic. It costs one hour and recurs on every calculator paper the student ever sits.

Second is the unclassified stationary point and its relatives: the answer found and the justification never written, where the command term asked for one. Third is the unread domain in trigonometry, where correct solutions fall outside the range the question specified. Fourth is the missing constant of integration and the unchanged limits after a substitution. All four are mechanical, all four are systematic rather than careless, and together they typically account for more lost marks on a Standard Level script than any single content topic.

Content teaching sits further down the list, not because it does not matter but because it costs more per mark. A topic takes two to four sessions to secure properly, and it returns marks only on the questions that use it. The exception is any topic the student has genuinely never met, which happens in small Abu Dhabi cohorts when a fortnight is lost to travel or illness, and which should be addressed immediately rather than revisited in the revision term.

It assumes a mid-tier qualified online tutor, one weekly session through the two years with a denser block before each exam period, plus a small number of sessions bought specifically for the exploration in DP1.

Two points of context. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, and school fee policy sits with the regulator rather than with the schools alone, so check ADEK's own published announcements for the current position rather than a tutoring page's summary. For comparison, in Dubai KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, which is the kind of statement worth looking for from your own emirate's regulator before committing to a two-year tutoring budget.

The sequencing conclusion is the useful part. Front-load. The hours bought in the summer before DP1 and in the first term are cheaper, better attended and more useful than the same hours bought in the February of DP2, when published rates are at their firmest and the available improvement is smallest. A family that spends a modest amount early and reviews on evidence almost always spends less in total than one that waits for a mock to raise the alarm.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks you cannot buy
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration carries twenty marks against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. It is the part of the course where money is most often spent badly, because families buy hours late, on polishing, when the marks were decided earlier by the choice of topic. A topic that cannot carry Standard Level mathematics cannot be rescued by a tidy write-up, and no amount of paid time changes that.

What paid time does well is test a topic early. Two or three sessions in DP1, spent asking whether a proposed idea can generate mathematics at the level of the course, whether the student can obtain or construct the data it needs, and what the reflection criterion would actually have to evaluate, is the best value available in the whole two years. Families who buy those sessions at the right moment frequently need fewer later, which is the opposite of how tutoring is usually sold.

The boundary is firm and stated rather than implied. A tutor may teach the mathematics, question the student's reasoning, explain what each criterion rewards, demonstrate a technique on different material, and give feedback on a draft the student has already produced. A tutor may not supply content for submission or rewrite a draft on the student's behalf. Everything submitted is the student's own, and in a market where at least one operator sells completed assessed work outright, that difference is worth paying attention to, because the student is the person the IB would penalise.

sections.heading: ADEK, permits, and verifying what you are paying for
paragraphs: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection ratings, which is useful for judging a school and tells you nothing about an individual tutor. No tutoring provider in Abu Dhabi holds an ADEK endorsement for tutoring, and any page claiming regulator approval is making a claim worth checking rather than trusting.

What does apply to the person teaching your child is the permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's private tutor licensing service via its smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount you see quoted.

One arrangement to avoid regardless of price. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE permit, whose code of conduct also addresses serving students affiliated with their own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document, but treat the underlying point as settled: the person marking the school assessment should not also be paid to prepare your child for it.

Ask whether the AED figure quoted is inclusive or exclusive of tax, in writing
Treat any claim of ADEK or IB approval as a reason to ask questions
Avoid any arrangement involving your child's own class teacher

sections.heading: When to start paying, when to pause, and when to stop
paragraphs: Start before the problem is urgent, because every variable moves against you later: rates harden, slots narrow, and the fixes that work in eight weeks need eight weeks to work in. The summer before DP1 and the first term of DP1 are the two cheapest, most productive windows in the two years, and they are the two windows families almost never use because nothing has gone wrong yet.

Pause during school assessment weeks, mock windows and the heaviest exploration deadline weeks. A Diploma student in those weeks has no spare capacity, and a session added to a full week produces nothing but a sense of having tried. The better use of a paid hour in such a week is reading the student's own marked assessment, which is the most informative document available and usually goes unexamined. Ramadan is handled the same way, with sessions moved to post-Iftar timing by prior agreement rather than improvised.

Stop when eight weeks of evidence shows nothing moving. The evidence is specific: marks on the last three assessments, the proportion of lost marks that are communication rather than content, and whether unlabelled problem sets are being completed. If all three are flat and the documents exist, the answer is a different tutor, a different subject for the slot, or no tutoring at all, and the last of those is sometimes correct. A provider who cannot describe the conditions under which they would recommend stopping has told you what their renewal conversation will sound like.

process.title: Send the last marked assessment
process.description: One marked Standard Level paper, with the school's mark scheme if it is available. Fifteen minutes with that script tells you what proportion of the lost marks are communication rather than content, and that proportion is what decides whether you need four sessions or a term.

process.title: Ask for the quote broken into variables
process.description: Level, session length, hour of day, tutor tier and commitment shape. Any provider who can only give one number is giving you an average. The six variables are what you control, and two of them reduce the figure without reducing the teaching.

process.title: Take the first session and keep the diagnosis
process.description: One session per student at no charge, ending in a written sorting of lost marks and a plan for the first month. Take that document to any other provider you are comparing; it makes two quotes comparable in a way that a price list cannot.

process.title: Fix the slot, the length and the between-session set
process.description: One recurring slot in Gulf Standard Time, ninety minutes where the schedule allows, plus a mixed unlabelled problem set each week. Ask for the set to be reviewed at the start of the next session rather than filed.

process.title: Review on three measures after eight weeks
process.description: Marks on recent assessments, the share of losses that are communication rather than content, and whether the practice sets are being completed. Continue, change or stop on those three rather than on how the sessions felt.

whyPoints.description: A marked script read line by line, a mixed unlabelled set every week, and explicit work on command terms and mark types. If an hour contains none of those, the rate is not the problem with it.

whyPoints.description: The cheapest and most useful hours in the two years are the ones bought before DP1 and early in DP1. Saying so reduces what a family spends in total, which is the test of whether advice is advice.

faqs.question: What is a realistic hourly budget for AA SL tuition in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with specialist IB and A Level provision quoted around AED 200 to 450 and above and budget online provision advertised from as little as AED 33 to 150. Standard Level mathematics normally prices in the middle of that picture rather than at the specialist end, because the pool of competent tutors is larger than at Higher Level. Those are market figures from providers and rate trackers, not an IB Gram price, and the top of each band is what gets quoted from January onwards.

faqs.question: Does Standard Level maths cost less to support than Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the reason is supply rather than quality. A 150-hour course with two papers can be taught well by far more people than a 240-hour course with extended problem solving, induction, complex numbers and differential equations, so Higher Level quotes drift towards the specialist band. The exceptions are the exploration, which carries the same twenty marks against the same five criteria at both levels, and the non-calculator paper, which needs the same deliberate separate practice. Pay the same attention to those two parts whichever level your child sits.

faqs.question: Why does the same tutor quote more in February than in September?
faqs.answer: Because demand across the emirate arrives at once after the winter break, when DP2 families see mock results and DP1 families see their first serious assessments. Rates harden, the better evening slots fill first, and the specialists with course experience are the first to become unavailable. The second cost is subtler: the fixes that pay best, such as rounding habits and written working, need six to eight weeks to become automatic, so a February start buys both a worse rate and a smaller available improvement.

faqs.question: Is an in-home maths tutor in Abu Dhabi worth the extra AED?
faqs.answer: Published in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor, and the gap is travel rather than teaching. For Standard Level mathematics the online format has a concrete advantage, because the student's written working has to be read line by line and a screen share shows it to both people at once. The honest case for a visit is a student who will not settle without an adult present. That is a real reason and it is not about mathematics.

faqs.question: How many AA SL sessions should we buy before judging the result?
faqs.answer: Eight weekly sessions, with a review at week four to check that documents are arriving and practice sets are being completed. Eight weeks is long enough for communication fixes to show in marks and short enough that a wrong match is cheap. Do not buy a term up front to judge at the end of it. The three measures to judge on are marks on recent assessments, the share of lost marks that are communication rather than content, and whether the unlabelled problem sets came back done.

faqs.question: Does a ninety-minute session cost more per mark than a sixty-minute one?
faqs.answer: Usually less, for this subject. Mathematics rewards a long slot because the useful unit of work is a complete problem followed by the repair it exposes, and that rarely fits in forty-five minutes of teaching time. Ninety-minute slots are also often priced below two separate sixty-minute sessions for the same total hours, because they carry fewer scheduling overheads for the tutor. The constraint is the student's concentration, which in term time means fighting for a slot before they are finished for the day rather than after.

faqs.question: What is the single cheapest thing we can fix in my child's AA SL work?
faqs.answer: Premature rounding, almost every time. Unless a question states otherwise a final answer is expected to three significant figures, and a value rounded mid-calculation and carried forward gives a final answer wrong in the third figure, losing the accuracy mark while the method marks survive. One session establishes storing values and rounding once at the end; a month makes it habit. It recurs on every calculator paper your child will ever sit, which makes it the highest return per hour available in the course.

faqs.question: Should we pay up front for a block of Abu Dhabi maths sessions?
faqs.answer: Monthly packages are advertised at a discount to the hourly figure, including online monthly packages from around AED 799 for eight sessions, so there is a genuine saving. The cost is flexibility: a block reduces your ability to stop at week four when the evidence says the match is wrong. A reasonable compromise is to pay per session for the first four, review, then take a block once you know the hour is productive. Ask what happens to unused sessions before paying for any package.

faqs.question: Can two Abu Dhabi students share an AA SL tutor to split the cost?
faqs.answer: It works when both students are at a similar point in the course and the work is content coverage. It works poorly when the marks are being lost in each student's own written working, because reading one student's script line by line is not something the other can usefully watch. Published group rates sit below one-to-one, and the saving is real. The question to ask is whose script gets read this week, and if the answer is neither, the lower rate is buying a less useful hour.

faqs.question: Are AA SL tutoring quotes in Abu Dhabi inclusive of VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get it in writing before the first invoice. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as a general rule, because that is a Federal Tax Authority matter and tutoring pages asserting it are guessing. What a parent can reasonably require is that every quoted AED figure says whether it is inclusive or exclusive, and that any provider charging tax shows a registration number. The published market bands cited on this page do not consistently state their tax treatment, which is itself worth knowing when comparing them.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for exploration support?
faqs.answer: Less than families spend, and much earlier. Three or four sessions in DP1 on topic choice, on whether the idea can generate mathematics at the level of the course, and on what the reflection criterion must evaluate, is the best value in the two years. At mid-tier published rates that is a few hundred dirhams to perhaps twelve hundred in total. Money spent late, on polishing a topic that cannot carry Standard Level mathematics, buys presentation marks and leaves the use-of-mathematics criterion where it was.

faqs.question: Is tutoring worth paying for if my child is only one grade off target?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and usually in fewer hours than expected, because a single grade is frequently carried by communication losses rather than content gaps. Sort the last marked script into mathematics not known, mathematics not selected, and mathematics not paid for, and if the third pile is the largest then four to six sessions is a realistic plan rather than a term. Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone who does should be disregarded. What can be said is which band of errors is costing the marks and roughly what it takes to repair.

faqs.question: Does ADEK regulate tutoring prices in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection ratings, and school fee policy sits with the regulator, but private tutoring is a separate market that moves with demand. What does apply to tutors is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Check ADEK's own announcements for current school fee policy rather than any tutoring page's summary, including this one.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if we pause during mock weeks?
faqs.answer: Pausing is sensible and should not be penalised. A Diploma student in an assessment week has no spare capacity, and a session added to a full week produces effort rather than marks. Where a session is kept, the best use of it is reading the student's own marked assessment, which is the most informative document available and usually goes unexamined. Ask any provider before paying what their policy is on pausing and on unused sessions in a package, because that answer tells you how a flat term will be handled.

faqs.question: Is it too late in DP2 for AA SL tuition to be worth the cost?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the arithmetic changes. Communication fixes still pay in eight weeks, because rounding habits, written method and justification sentences transfer to every question on both papers. Content gaps compress poorly, and the exploration is usually beyond useful influence once the internal deadline is close. Published specialist exam-year monthly figures run from AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above, so late support is also the most expensive. Start with the marked script, decide which pile dominates, and buy only the work that pile needs.

intro.heading: The course families underestimate, and what that costs by DP2
paragraphs: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level has a reputation problem in Abu Dhabi, and it costs students marks. It is routinely described as the softer of the two Diploma mathematics routes, chosen by families whose child found algebraic proof uncomfortable, and the first Higher Level mock usually ends that conversation. The course runs to the same 240 teaching hours as Analysis and Approaches HL. It has the same number of papers, including the one-hour Paper 3 at 20 per cent. What it swaps is the content, not the demand.

The swap is substantial. Instead of proof by induction and integration by parts, a Higher Level Applications student meets matrix algebra with determinants, inverses, eigenvalues and eigenvectors; transition matrices and steady states; graph theory with adjacency matrices, minimum spanning trees by Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms, the Chinese postman problem and travelling-salesman bounds; complex numbers used as phasors in alternating-current work; the Poisson distribution, confidence intervals, t-tests, chi-squared tests and Spearman's rank; and coupled differential equations solved numerically with Euler's method and read off phase portraits. None of that is easier than calculus. Much of it is simply unfamiliar to parents, which is why it arrives as a surprise.

The second thing families underestimate is where the marks actually sit. Statistics and probability is the largest block in the Higher Level course at roughly 52 published hours, and statistics in this course is not about computing a value. The calculator computes the value. The marks are in the sentence afterwards: what the p-value licenses you to say, in the context of the data, with the right degree of hedging. Abu Dhabi students who are strong arithmetically and weak at writing are the ones this course punishes hardest, and it punishes them quietly, two marks at a time, across a whole paper.

Delivery here is online, and the page should say so before it says anything else about tutoring. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address: home visits in Abu Dhabi are not part of what we sell, and that service exists only in India. For this course the constraint barely binds, because the limiting factor is not distance but supply. The number of tutors in any one city who are genuinely comfortable teaching eigenvalues, Chinese postman and a paired t-test is small, and it is smaller again among those willing to drive to Al Shamkha at five o'clock. Online, your child is matched from everyone who teaches the course.

What follows is the course itself. The two Higher Level routes side by side, so a family can see what was actually chosen. The published hours by topic area and exactly which content is Higher Level only. The three papers, their weightings and the technology assumption behind all of them. The places Applications candidates leak marks, which are interpretive far more often than computational. The graphic display calculator as an examined instrument. The five statistical tests and the sentence each one needs. Where this route is named in university entry requirements, and how to verify that rather than trust it. And how to check that whoever you hire is legally permitted to tutor in the UAE at all.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Matrices and eigenvalues, graph theory, statistical inference, modelling and numerical calculus across 240 hours, with three papers and an exploration. Marks leak on conclusions written without context, on hypothesis tests reported as decisions rather than as inferences, and on models fitted without any justification for the choice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same five topic areas over 150 hours, two 90-minute papers at 40 per cent each and no Paper 3. Voronoi diagrams, financial mathematics, regression and chi-squared testing all appear here, which is why a Standard Level student moving up to Higher Level has more foundation than they expect.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Investment appraisal, break-even analysis and ratio work all lean on the modelling habits this course teaches. Higher Level Applications students usually find the calculation trivial and the written justification harder, which is exactly the balance of marks in both subjects.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Elasticity, market outcomes and the quantitative Higher Level paper reward the interpretation skills Applications builds. The overlap is real: a student who can write what a coefficient means in context is being trained for both subjects at once.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Statistical literacy in the internal assessment, where a student must choose and justify an inferential test and report a result honestly. Applications HL candidates arrive with the vocabulary for this, including significance, sampling and the limits of what a test establishes.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The scientific investigation asks for data analysis and uncertainty handling, and chi-squared and correlation work recur throughout the course. Students taking Biology with Applications HL should be the strongest in their class at this, and frequently are not, because nobody connects the two.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Spatial reasoning, nearest-neighbour thinking and the use of maps and networks connect directly to Voronoi diagrams and graph theory. The internal assessment rewards a student who can analyse rather than describe, which is the same demand as this mathematics course.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Adjacency matrices, graph traversal and algorithmic complexity are shared ground with the Higher Level graph theory content. A student taking both has a genuine advantage, provided somebody points out that the two courses are describing the same objects.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Modelling, tolerance and data-driven iteration. The mathematics is lighter than in the sciences, but the habit of justifying a model rather than presenting it is identical, and it is the habit this mathematics course is actually assessing.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Applications HL students have unusually concrete material here: what a statistical test can and cannot establish, how a model relates to the world it describes, and whether a p-value is knowledge. A tutor can supply the examples; the essay must be the student's own.

sections.heading: The two Higher Level routes, side by side, as they are actually examined
paragraphs: A family searching for Higher Level Applications support in Abu Dhabi has usually already made the route choice, often on the understanding that it was the gentler option. The comparison below is the one that should have been available at the point of choosing. Both courses run to 240 teaching hours. Both have three papers and an internally assessed exploration worth 20 per cent. Both have a Paper 3 at one hour and 55 marks. The difference is what the papers contain and which skill they punish.

Analysis and Approaches builds on algebraic manipulation and proof, and its first paper is sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation builds on modelling, data and technology, and assumes a graphic display calculator in every paper. That single difference changes who finds each course hard. A student with weak algebra survives longer in Applications; a student who cannot write a conclusion in context does worse in Applications than they would have done in Analysis, because Applications asks for that sentence constantly.

In Abu Dhabi the choice is often made by the timetable rather than by the student. Where a school has limited Higher Level mathematics staffing, Analysis is usually the one offered at Higher Level and Applications at Standard Level. A student who wants Applications at Higher Level may therefore be in a set of two or three, or covering parts of the course with a textbook. That is a supply problem, not an ability problem, and it is the most common reason this page gets read.

Use the table as a decision record rather than a ranking. Neither course is the hard one. They test different things, they suit different students, and the mistake that costs the most is choosing on reputation rather than on what the student is actually good at and what the next step after school requires.

sections.heading: Where the 240 hours go, and what exists only at Higher Level
paragraphs: The subject guide allocates 150 teaching hours to Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level and 240 at Higher Level, with roughly thirty hours in both for the toolkit and the exploration. Unlike Analysis, the growth is not concentrated in calculus. Geometry and trigonometry more than doubles, largely because graph theory and vectors land there, and statistics and probability becomes the largest single block in the course.

That distribution tells you where a Higher Level Applications student is most likely to be in trouble. A student struggling with statistics is struggling with the biggest block; a student struggling with graph theory is struggling with content that has no Standard Level ancestor at all and that most parents have never seen. Minimum spanning trees, the Chinese postman problem and travelling-salesman bounds are taught nowhere else in a school mathematics curriculum, so there is no fallback intuition to lean on.

The matrix work is the other genuine cliff. Operations and determinants are approachable; eigenvalues and eigenvectors, matrix powers used to find a steady state in a transition matrix, and then coupled differential equations solved through those same eigenvalues form a chain where a weakness in the first link breaks the last three. When a Higher Level Applications student says they do not understand phase portraits, the problem is almost always three topics upstream.

Confirm every hour allocation and topic list against your child's own copy of the current subject guide, which the school issues and the IB revises periodically. What is stable enough to plan around is the shape: a statistics-heavy Higher Level course with two large bodies of unfamiliar discrete content, numerical rather than analytic calculus, and technology assumed throughout.

sections.heading: Three papers, and the technology assumption behind all of them
paragraphs: Higher Level Applications is assessed by three papers plus the exploration. Paper 1 runs two hours over 110 marks at 30 per cent and is made of shorter compulsory questions covering the whole syllabus. Paper 2 is also two hours and 110 marks at 30 per cent, built from longer extended-response questions that develop a context across several parts. Paper 3 is one hour, 55 marks, 20 per cent, and consists of two compulsory extended problem-solving investigations. The exploration carries the remaining 20 per cent across 20 marks.

The feature that distinguishes this course from its sibling is that a graphic display calculator is assumed in all three papers. That is not a convenience, it is an examined expectation. Questions are written on the understanding that the student can run a regression, obtain a test statistic and a p-value, invert a matrix, find eigenvalues and apply Euler's method on the machine. A student who is slow or uncertain on the calculator is not merely inconvenienced; they are working on a paper designed for someone who is fast on it.

This produces a very specific examination profile. The arithmetic is rarely the obstacle. The obstacles are selecting the right procedure, carrying out the right number of steps on the device, and then writing what the output means. Candidates who have practised only by hand lose time; candidates who have practised only on the device lose the written marks. Both errors are correctable and both need deliberate attention rather than more topic teaching.

Paper 3 deserves separate planning. Two long investigations in sixty minutes is a stamina and structure test, and in this course the investigations usually develop a model or a discrete structure across six or seven parts. Abu Dhabi students most often report either spending thirty-five minutes on the first investigation or abandoning the second when an early part fails. Both patterns respond to timed practice against the published scheme, and neither improves by itself.

sections.heading: Where Applications candidates lose marks: interpretation, not calculation
paragraphs: The dominant leak in this course is a correct number with nothing said about it. A student runs the regression, reports r equals 0.87, and stops. The mark scheme wanted a statement about the strength and direction of the association between the two named variables in the context given, and possibly a caution about causation. The arithmetic was never the test. This single pattern, repeated across a paper, is the difference between a 4 and a 6 for a large number of Higher Level Applications candidates.

The second leak is the hypothesis test reported as a verdict. A p-value of 0.03 does not mean the claim is true; it means there is sufficient evidence at the 5 per cent significance level to reject the null hypothesis in favour of the alternative, in the context of this sample. Candidates write 'so the two are related', and lose the mark they had already earned on the calculator. This is a sentence-level fix and it is one of the fastest improvements available in the whole Diploma.

Third is the model presented without justification. Applications asks students to choose a model and defend the choice: why a logistic rather than an exponential, what the parameters mean in context, where the model stops being reasonable. A student who fits a curve because the calculator offered it has done the computation and skipped the subject. The same habit sinks explorations, where the marks for reflection are explicitly about limitations.

After those come the predictable content failures: eigenvalue work attempted without secure matrix algebra underneath it; graph theory algorithms half-remembered, so a minimum spanning tree is built greedily but not systematically; Euler's method applied with the wrong step handling; and units and degrees of freedom lost in statistical tests. Every one of these is visible on a marked script, which is why the first session asks for the script rather than for a description.

sections.heading: The calculator as an examined instrument
paragraphs: In a course where every paper assumes a graphic display calculator, fluency on the device is part of the syllabus in practice even where it is not a topic in the guide. Higher Level Applications students need to be quick and accurate at a specific list of operations, and most of them have assembled that list by accident. Making it explicit is one of the easiest gains in the course, and it takes a session or two rather than a term.

The list is short and concrete. Linear, quadratic, exponential, logarithmic, power, sinusoidal and logistic regression, with the coefficient of determination. Solving equations and systems numerically. Matrix entry, multiplication, powers, determinants, inverses and eigenvalues. Statistical tests: chi-squared for independence and goodness of fit, one-sample and two-sample and paired t-tests, with p-values and degrees of freedom read correctly. Distributions: binomial, Poisson and normal, forwards and inverse. Numerical integration and derivatives at a point. Graphing with intersections, maxima and sign changes located rather than estimated.

Alongside the operations sits the discipline of what to write. A calculator answer with no supporting line forfeits method marks even when the value is right. A well-trained candidate records the test or model used, the values entered, the statistic obtained and the conclusion in context, which is four short lines and usually most of the available credit. Students pick this habit up fastest when a tutor marks their script against the published scheme and shows them the marks they left on the table.

There is one further practical point. Students should be examined on the machine they have practised on, with its operating system settled and its memory in the state the regulations require, and that is a matter for the school's Diploma coordinator rather than for a tutor. A borrowed calculator in an examination hall is a self-inflicted problem, and it is more common than it should be.

sections.heading: Five statistical tests, and the sentence each one needs
paragraphs: Statistics and probability is the biggest block in this course, and most of its marks are won or lost in one sentence per question. Students know how to produce the statistic. What they have usually never been taught explicitly is the form of words the mark scheme rewards, which varies by test and which is entirely learnable. Teaching it is unglamorous and it moves grades.

The structure is always the same. Name the test and the significance level. State the hypotheses in the context of the data rather than in symbols alone. Report the statistic and the p-value. Then write a conclusion that says what the evidence licenses, in the context given, and nothing stronger. A candidate who does that consistently collects marks on questions they find difficult, because the final mark is for the reasoning, not the result.

The table sets out the five tests a Higher Level Applications candidate most often meets, what each is used for, what the calculator gives, and the shape of the sentence that earns the mark. It is deliberately a reference rather than a lesson: the point is that a student should be able to produce the right form of words without thinking, in the way they can produce a quadratic formula.

One caution worth stating. These tests establish association and evidence, not cause and not truth. The mark schemes care about that distinction and so do examiners, and a candidate who writes 'this proves' has usually just thrown away a mark they earned. In the exploration the same restraint earns reflection marks, which is why the statistics block and the exploration should be taught with one voice rather than as separate things.

sections.heading: Where this route is named in university entry, and how to check
paragraphs: The anxious question behind a great many Applications enquiries in Abu Dhabi is whether this route closes a door. The honest answer has two parts. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is accepted for a very wide range of degree programmes, including many quantitative ones, and it is explicitly designed for students who will use mathematics inside another discipline. At the same time, some mathematics, physics and engineering programmes still specify Analysis and Approaches, usually at Higher Level, and a few specify it without naming an alternative.

The only reliable method is to read each programme's own admissions page, for the intake year the student will actually apply in, and to write down what it says. Requirements change, they differ between faculties inside one university, and they differ between campuses of the same institution. A tutoring page listing which universities accept which route would be out of date within a year, and several competitor pages carry exactly that kind of stale list. Ask the school's university counsellor to confirm in writing, because that is their job and they have the current information.

For UAE equivalency, be careful about what is published and what is not. The British-track rules are sourced: students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency requires an IELTS academic score of 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

No comparable IB points figure should be taken from any tutoring page, including this one. We have not read a verified IB equivalency threshold on the Ministry of Education's own site, so we do not publish one, and a competing page that publishes the wrong subject count for the British track is a useful reminder of why. Read the current requirements on moe.gov.ae or ask the emirate's attestation authority, and treat equivalency as a process the family completes rather than something a tutor performs or can speed up.

sections.heading: The exploration in Applications: real data and the modelling trap
paragraphs: The exploration is 20 marks and 20 per cent, marked across five criterion letters: presentation and mathematical communication at four marks each, personal engagement and reflection at three each, and use of mathematics at six. In Applications it almost always involves data, and that is where the trap sits. A student collects or finds a dataset, runs several regressions, picks the one with the best coefficient of determination, and writes it up. That is computation presented as investigation, and it scores poorly on exactly the criteria that carry most of the marks.

What earns marks instead is justification and limitation. Why this model rather than that one, given what the context implies about growth or saturation or periodicity. What the parameters mean in the units of the problem. Where the model stops being reasonable, and what would need to be true for it to hold. A student who writes two honest paragraphs about the limits of their own model is collecting reflection marks that a far more elaborate calculation would not have earned.

The highest-value tutoring session on the exploration is therefore the first one, before any data is gathered, while the research question can still be narrowed. A question like 'how does temperature affect energy use' produces a graph. A question about whether a logistic model describes a specific measured quantity over a specific period, with a stated reason for expecting saturation, produces an investigation. The difference is twenty minutes of conversation at the right moment.

The boundary is firm. A tutor explains what each criterion asks, teaches the mathematics the student has chosen to use, reads a draft and identifies where marks are being lost, and sets the next revision for the student to carry out. No part of the submitted document originates with a tutor, and none of it is rewritten into final form by one. Keep the written feedback: it is the clearest available evidence that the work is the student's own, and schools increasingly ask to see that trail.

sections.heading: Checking that whoever you hire is permitted to tutor in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a family hiring for a narrow specialism is the family most likely to be offered an informal arrangement. The position is clear enough to check. Private tuition work permits were introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page for it is listed as private tutor licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time.

Eligibility is wider than parents assume. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 can all apply. That breadth matters for two reasons: it means a university student offering cheap Higher Level Applications support may be perfectly legitimate, and it means there is no excuse for a professional tutor not to hold one. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so disregard any specific amount quoted as fact.

There are two limits worth knowing. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. And in Abu Dhabi, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules says school staff are prohibited from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the permit's own code of conduct barring the same thing. Verify that against ADEK's current policy document before relying on it.

IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation and claims none. We are not approved, endorsed or licensed by ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and any tutoring company telling you otherwise should be asked to produce the permit or centre number. What we do is match your child to a specialist in Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level and deliver the lessons one-to-one over live video. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and home visits in Abu Dhabi are not something we sell; that service exists only in India.

process.title: Name the course, the level and the topic block
process.description: 'Applications and Interpretation HL, the statistics unit is the problem and Paper 3 came back at 19 out of 55' is the sentence that matters. Applications and Analysis are different specialisms, and a tutor fluent in one is not automatically fluent in the other. Send the marked script if you have it.

process.title: Take the free first lesson as a diagnosis
process.description: The tutor reads the marked work, watches your child attempt something timed on the calculator, and establishes whether the issue is procedure, device fluency or the written conclusion. You get a written note naming what is leaking, including the case where the honest answer is that the school should handle it.

process.title: Start where the marks are, not where the syllabus starts
process.description: In this course that usually means statistics and inference, because it is the largest block and the one where interpretation marks go missing. Graph theory and matrices get their own treatment, because they are unfamiliar content rather than weak technique and respond to teaching rather than to practice.

process.title: Fix the rhythm and set a review point
process.description: A weekly hour in Gulf Standard Time, work set and marked between sessions, and an agreed review four to six weeks out at which you look at per-question marks rather than at impressions. Agreeing the review date at the start is worth more than negotiating the rate.

process.title: Change the plan on the evidence
process.description: If the conclusions in the scripts have started carrying context and the marks have moved, continue. If they have not, change the diagnosis rather than adding hours. Sometimes the finding is that the mathematics is fine and a paired subject is the real problem, which is a useful answer in itself.

whyPoints.title: Matched to this course, not to mathematics in general
whyPoints.description: Applications and Analysis diverge sharply at Higher Level. Eigenvalues, Chinese postman and a paired t-test are not things an Analysis specialist teaches, and a family paying specialist rates should be getting a specialist in the course their child actually sits.

whyPoints.title: The interpretation marks get taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: Most Higher Level Applications grades move when the conclusion sentence becomes automatic: test named, hypotheses in context, statistic reported, inference stated without overclaiming. That is teachable in weeks and it is the largest single pool of recoverable marks in the course.

whyPoints.title: Delivery is stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not visit UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a specialism this narrow, matching on expertise rather than on driving distance is the whole point.

whyPoints.title: Nothing is produced for the student
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria, teach the mathematics the student has chosen, read drafts and set revisions the student carries out. No part of a submitted exploration originates with a tutor. A competing site in this market sells completed Internal Assessments, and the malpractice consequence falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level the easier of the two maths routes?
faqs.answer: No, and the first Higher Level mock usually settles the argument. Both courses carry 240 teaching hours, three papers and an exploration worth 20 per cent, and both include the one-hour Paper 3. What differs is content and the skill each one punishes. Applications swaps algebraic proof and integration techniques for matrices with eigenvalues, graph theory, inferential statistics and numerical calculus, and it assumes a calculator in every paper. A student with weak algebra survives longer here; a student who cannot write a conclusion in context does worse here than they would have done in Analysis.

faqs.question: What does Applications HL contain that Analysis HL never touches at all?
faqs.answer: A surprising amount. Matrix algebra through determinants, inverses, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and matrix powers used to find the steady state of a transition matrix. Graph theory with adjacency matrices, minimum spanning trees built by Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms, the Chinese postman problem and travelling-salesman upper and lower bounds. Inferential statistics including the Poisson distribution, confidence intervals, one-sample, two-sample and paired t-tests, chi-squared tests and Spearman's rank. Coupled differential equations read through eigenvalues and phase portraits. Confirm current lists against your child's own copy of the subject guide, which the school issues.

faqs.question: Which calculator operations does my child actually need to be fluent with?
faqs.answer: A short and specific list. Linear, quadratic, exponential, logarithmic, power, sinusoidal and logistic regression with the coefficient of determination. Numerical equation and system solving. Matrix entry, multiplication, powers, determinants, inverses and eigenvalues. Chi-squared tests for independence and goodness of fit, and one-sample, two-sample and paired t-tests, reading p-values and degrees of freedom correctly. Binomial, Poisson and normal distributions forwards and inverse. Numerical integration and derivatives at a point. Graphing with intersections and maxima located rather than estimated. Most students have assembled this list by accident; making it explicit takes a session or two.

faqs.question: My daughter gets the right numbers and still loses marks. What is happening?
faqs.answer: She is almost certainly stopping at the value. This course awards the last mark for interpretation: what the statistic means for the two named variables in the context given, in units, without overclaiming. A regression coefficient reported as a number earns part of the credit; the same coefficient described as a strong positive association between the named quantities, with no claim of causation, earns the rest. It is a writing habit rather than a mathematical gap, and it is one of the fastest improvements available anywhere in the Diploma once somebody names it.

faqs.question: What is in Paper 3 for Applications, and how does it differ from the Analysis version?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is one hour, 55 marks and 20 per cent, with two compulsory extended investigations, and it is sat only at Higher Level in both courses. In Applications the investigations typically develop a model or a discrete structure across six or seven parts, with the calculator assumed throughout, where the Analysis version develops an abstract mathematical idea. The skill is the same: read the early parts properly because the later ones depend on them, and recover rather than abandon when a step fails. Timed practice against the published mark scheme moves it faster than more content teaching does.

faqs.question: How are the chi-squared and t-tests examined, and what does the scheme want written?
faqs.answer: Always in the same structure, which is what makes it learnable. Name the test and the significance level. State the hypotheses in the context of the data rather than only in symbols. Report the statistic, the degrees of freedom where relevant, and the p-value. Then conclude with what the evidence licenses: at the stated level there is or is not sufficient evidence to reject the null hypothesis, phrased in terms of the named variables. Writing 'this proves' throws away a mark the student had already earned on the calculator, because these tests establish evidence rather than truth.

faqs.question: Do engineering programmes accept Applications HL, or do they insist on Analysis?
faqs.answer: It varies by programme, by faculty and by intake year, which is why a tutoring page should not publish a list. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is accepted for a very wide range of degrees, including many quantitative ones, but some mathematics, physics and engineering programmes still specify Analysis and Approaches and a few do so without naming an alternative. Read the admissions page of each programme your child is considering, for the year they will apply, and ask the school's university counsellor to confirm it in writing. Requirements change, and stale lists on tutoring sites are a known hazard.

faqs.question: Can my son move from Applications HL to Analysis HL once DP1 has started?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the window narrows quickly. Two things have to work: the school must have an Analysis set at Higher Level with space in the timetable, and the IB registration has to be amended. The mathematical gap is substantial in both directions, because the courses are not nested; he would be picking up induction, complex numbers in Euler form, vector geometry and integration techniques while dropping matrices, graph theory and inference. The decision belongs with the Diploma coordinator. A tutor's useful contribution is an honest estimate of how many weeks of bridging the move would need.

faqs.question: What separates a strong Applications exploration from a weak one?
faqs.answer: Justification. A weak exploration collects data, runs several regressions, keeps the one with the best coefficient of determination and writes it up. That is computation dressed as investigation, and it scores badly on the criteria carrying most of the marks: presentation, communication, engagement and reflection together are fourteen of the twenty. A strong one explains why a particular model suits the context, says what the parameters mean in the units of the problem, and states honestly where the model stops holding. The most valuable session happens before any data is gathered, while the research question can still be narrowed.

faqs.question: Is graph theory genuinely part of a school mathematics course?
faqs.answer: At Higher Level in this course, yes, and it catches families out because it appears nowhere else in a school curriculum. Students meet adjacency matrices and walks, minimum spanning trees built by Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms, the Chinese postman problem for traversing every edge, and upper and lower bounds for the travelling-salesman problem. There is no earlier intuition to fall back on, so it has to be taught rather than revised. The good news is that it is self-contained: a student can be behind in graph theory without that weakness contaminating anything else in the course.

faqs.question: Our Abu Dhabi school only timetables Applications at Standard Level. What are the options?
faqs.answer: Ask the Diploma coordinator three questions in order: will a Higher Level Applications set run at all next year, how many students would be in it, and what the school's arrangement is for a student taking a course partly independently. Where a school has limited Higher Level mathematics staffing, Analysis is usually the Higher Level offer and Applications the Standard Level one, so this is a staffing constraint rather than a judgement about your child. If the set will not run, the realistic choices are Analysis at Higher Level, Applications at Standard Level, or a supported independent route.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram arrange a tutor to come to a Khalifa City address for this course?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any UAE address, and home visits in Abu Dhabi are not a service we sell; that exists only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor each week and work marked between sessions. For Higher Level Applications the trade is heavily in your favour: the number of people who can teach eigenvalues, Chinese postman and a paired t-test is small, and the number of them willing to drive to Khalifa City at five o'clock is smaller again.

faqs.question: How do I check that an Abu Dhabi tutor is legally allowed to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists private tutor licensing with a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website and e-services system. Because the permit costs nothing, a tutor charging a premium to cover licensing is charging for something free. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure as unverified.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level Applications support cost in the Abu Dhabi market?
faqs.answer: Published UAE bands put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and in-home one-to-one visits running AED 180 to 350 and up to about 500 at the specialist end. Higher Level Applications sits at the upper part of the specialist band, because the pool of people who teach it confidently is narrow. Those figures belong to the sources named, not to IB Gram, and the first lesson is free so a plan can be priced after a diagnosis.

faqs.question: How long does it take to move a Higher Level Applications grade?
faqs.answer: It depends what is broken, and the three common cases have very different timescales. An interpretation habit, where the student computes correctly and writes nothing, changes in three or four marked scripts. A block of unfamiliar content such as graph theory or eigenvalue work needs teaching and then retesting, so four to six sessions with a fortnight's gap to check it held. A student who never secured the Standard Level statistics underneath the Higher Level course is a term's work, and we will say so rather than sell a block that cannot deliver.

faqs.question: Does the UAE equivalency process care which mathematics route my child took?
faqs.answer: We do not publish an answer to that, because we have not read a verified IB equivalency rule on the Ministry of Education's own site, and an unsourced number on a tutoring page is worse than no number. What is sourced is the British track: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Read the current IB position on moe.gov.ae or ask the emirate's attestation authority directly.

Both are visible on a marked script, which is why the first lesson asks for one. Send us the course, the level and the most recent marked paper, with the exploration draft if there is one, and you will get a written note naming what is leaking and how long the realistic fix takes. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and if no Higher Level Applications specialist is free at your hours, we will tell you at the enquiry rather than after you have paid.

intro.heading: Why Abu Dhabi AI HL families end up looking for a specialist
paragraphs: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is the newest and least understood course in the Diploma. It was built for students who will use mathematics on real data — modelling, statistics, networks, optimisation — rather than for students who will prove theorems. That design decision has a consequence most Abu Dhabi families discover in the middle of DP1: AI HL is not a softer version of Analysis and Approaches HL. It is a 240-hour Higher Level course with its own hard content, and a student who chose it because the word 'applications' sounded gentler can be in genuine difficulty by the first mock.

The second thing families discover is that school feedback on AI HL is often thin, through no fault of the teachers. A Diploma cohort in an Abu Dhabi school may contain six AI HL candidates and thirty AA SL candidates. The AI HL group gets taught properly, but it rarely gets a dedicated Paper 3 clinic, because Paper 3 is a one-hour paper worth a fifth of the grade that only Higher Level students sit. Parents are then asked to judge progress from a termly report band and a sentence about effort.

This page is built around the opposite approach. Everything a tutor does with an AI HL student here produces a document you can read: a marked question with the lost marks circled and the command term named, a Paper 3 attempt with the scaffolding steps numbered, an exploration draft with letters A to E written in the margin and a mark out of twenty attached to each. You should not have to take anyone's word for whether tutoring is working. You should be able to open a folder and see it.

Abu Dhabi adds its own practical constraints. The emirate's Diploma students are spread across the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, Yas and Saadiyat, and the mainland communities, and the school day plus the drive home frequently puts the earliest realistic session at 4.30pm or 5pm. Because lessons run over live video, that geography stops mattering: the family in Al Reef and the family in Al Bateen get the same AI HL specialist in the same slot, without either of them paying for a tutor's travel time across Mussafah at rush hour.

The honest position on delivery: IB Gram does not send a tutor to a home anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India. For Abu Dhabi the model is one-to-one online tuition over live video with a shared digital whiteboard, screen sharing of the student's own script, and a recording the student can rewatch before a test. The comparison table further down this page sets out what that trades away and what it buys, in AED and in hours.

What follows is the detail: the AI HL assessment model component by component, why Paper 3 behaves differently from Papers 1 and 2, the exploration rubric by criterion letter, the specific places AI HL candidates lose marks, what the Abu Dhabi tutoring market charges, who may legally tutor here, and how the AI versus AA decision interacts with university admission. No part of it requires you to buy anything to be useful.
