abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Abu Dhabi schools licensed by ADEK run the full IB continuum, and a family searching for AI HL support is usually two years past the point where the Primary and Middle Years Programmes mattered. They still matter for diagnosis: an AI HL student who struggles with algebraic fluency is often carrying a gap that opened in MYP mathematics.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the three core elements. Mathematics is compulsory, which is why the AA or AI and HL or SL choice is the single most consequential tick on a Diploma option form. AI HL sits in Group 5 and runs for 240 teaching hours over two years, assessed by three written papers in the May session plus one internally assessed mathematical exploration.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi's Diploma cohorts are small relative to the emirate's total private-school enrolment, and AI HL groups inside those cohorts are smaller again. That is the structural reason specialist AI HL support is hard to find locally and easy to find online: a tutor pool drawn from one emirate is thin, a pool drawn from everywhere that teaches the Diploma is not.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of conceptual, criterion-referenced study. MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria rather than by paper marks, and extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5 is the route that prepares a student for a Higher Level course. Students arriving in DP1 from standard MYP mathematics often meet AI HL statistics comfortably and AI HL algebra painfully.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi IB World Schools run the continuum from PYP through to DP, so an AI HL student may have been in the same building for a decade. That continuity is useful for a tutor: the MYP criterion reports from two years earlier usually predict exactly which AI HL topic will cause trouble, and they are in the parent portal already.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary education organised around transdisciplinary themes, with mathematics taught through number, pattern, shape and data handling rather than as a separate drill subject. It builds the habit of explaining a method, which is the habit AI HL rewards and which exam technique then has to be rebuilt around command terms.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Khalifa City, Al Raha and Saadiyat frequently have one child in PYP and another sitting AI HL papers. Online delivery makes that household workable: two different tutors, two different time slots, one calendar, no second car journey.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year pre-sixteen route many Abu Dhabi students take before switching into the Diploma. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier, or Pearson's 4MA1, covers most of what AI HL assumes on day one, with the notable exception of statistical inference and matrices, which neither syllabus touches.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE to AI HL transition is the commonest diagnostic in Abu Dhabi, because a student arriving from 0580 Extended with a grade 7 has met almost no formal statistics. Hypothesis testing, correlation coefficients and transition matrices are genuinely new, not revision, and the first eight weeks of tutoring usually go there.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: AI HL support rarely stays inside one subject, because the students who choose it tend to pair it with sciences, economics or business and the same data-handling skills appear in all of them. These are the courses Abu Dhabi families most often add alongside an AI HL booking.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Five topic areas — number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, calculus — with HL adding matrices, eigenvalues, graph theory, complex numbers in modelling, and numerical solutions to differential equations. Technology is assumed throughout, so the examinable skill is interpretation rather than hand computation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-and-structure route. AA HL requires mathematical induction, complex number algebra, vector geometry and formal calculus, and its Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. Students sometimes switch from AA HL to AI HL in DP1; the switch is survivable, but the statistics content has to be built from nothing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The commonest pairing with AI HL for students heading towards engineering or architecture. The overlap is graph linearisation, uncertainty and gradient interpretation, so a tutor working on AI HL regression is usually also fixing the physics data-analysis paper without being asked.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across six organising themes, with HL extending into mechanisms, spectroscopy, energy cycles and electrode potentials. Chemistry's quantitative work rewards exactly the significant-figure and unit discipline that AI HL examiners look for in modelling answers.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change. Biology's statistical tests — chi-squared, standard deviation, t-test — are the same tests AI HL assesses formally, which makes a combined session unusually efficient.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and development, assessed by papers and three internal commentaries. HL economics calculation and AI HL optimisation share a vocabulary, and students who can read a marginal-cost diagram usually read an AI HL rate-of-change question correctly too.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business organisation, human resources, finance and accounts, marketing and operations. The finance unit uses break-even analysis, investment appraisal and forecasting, which are AI HL topics wearing different clothes, and the research project rewards the same data-presentation care the exploration does.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems fundamentals, computational thinking, programming and one option topic, plus a solution to a real client problem. Graph theory and matrix representation sit in both courses, so AI HL students taking computer science often find the networks unit the easiest content of their Diploma.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay. Students who take AI HL have unusually good TOK material available to them, because questions about modelling, correlation, prediction and the limits of data sit directly on the mathematics knowledge-question syllabus.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece in a Diploma subject. An essay supervised in mathematics and built on AI HL methods needs a genuinely researchable question; supervision here means process coaching and feedback on the student's own research, never supplying finished text.

sections.heading: What an AI HL tutor in Abu Dhabi changes in the first month
paragraphs: In the first four weeks an AI HL tutor should produce three things: a diagnosis naming the specific topics costing marks, a marked set of past-paper questions showing where the loss happens inside each answer, and a realistic read on the exploration. Nothing in that list is an opinion. All of it is a document, and all of it should be in a parent's hands before a second month is paid for.

The diagnosis is built from the student's own work rather than from a bought diagnostic test. A tutor asks for the last two school assessments, the most recent mock if there is one, and whatever exploration material exists. Those scripts are then re-marked against the IB's published command terms, because the gap between what a student knows and what a student scores is usually a command-term gap. A question that says 'find' wants a value. A question that says 'hence find' wants a value derived from the previous part. A question that says 'comment on' wants a sentence about the context, and a correct number with no sentence scores nothing on that mark.

The marked set then gets sorted into two piles, and the sort is the whole point. One pile is content the student has not learned: transition matrices, say, or Euler's method. That pile is fixable by teaching and the timeline is predictable. The other pile is content the student knows and still loses marks on: rounding before the final step, a calculator left in radians, a chi-squared conclusion stated without reference to the significance level. That pile is fixable faster and is worth more marks per hour of work, which is why it gets attacked first.

By week four a family should be able to answer a concrete question: which three topics are costing the most marks, and what is the plan for each. If a tutor cannot answer that from written evidence after four sessions, the match is wrong and should be changed rather than persisted with.

sections.heading: The AI HL assessment model, component by component
paragraphs: AI HL is assessed by three written papers in the examination session plus one internally assessed mathematical exploration. The three papers are not three versions of the same test. Paper 1 is a set of shorter questions covering the whole syllabus, Paper 2 is a set of extended-response questions, and Paper 3 is two long problem-solving questions that only Higher Level candidates sit. The exploration is marked by the school against the IB's five criteria and then moderated externally.

Technology is assumed in every AI paper, which is a structural difference from Analysis and Approaches. An AA HL candidate sits Paper 1 without a calculator; an AI HL candidate is expected to have a graphic display calculator on the desk for all three papers. That changes what the examination actually tests. Computation by hand is largely gone, replaced by model selection, interpretation and the ability to explain what a number from the calculator means in the context of the question.

The practical consequence is that calculator workflow is examinable technique rather than a convenience. Knowing which regression model to fit, how to run a hypothesis test and read the p-value, how to find an intersection numerically, and how to store and recall exact values instead of retyping rounded ones are each worth marks across all three papers. A student who is fluent with the syllabus and clumsy with the device loses marks that have nothing to do with mathematics, and those are among the cheapest marks to recover in a tutoring programme.

sections.heading: Paper 3 is the Higher Level discriminator, and it is coachable
paragraphs: Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level and carries a fifth of the grade in one hour. It presents two extended problem-solving questions, each heavily scaffolded: a context is set, a model is introduced, and the question walks the candidate through it in parts that build on one another. The mathematics inside any individual part is rarely harder than Paper 2 mathematics. The difficulty is structural, and that is exactly why it responds to practice.

The characteristic Paper 3 failure is abandonment. A student meets part (c), cannot see it, and stops — losing not only part (c) but parts (d) through (g), which depended on carrying a result forward rather than on having derived it. Examiners award marks for using a previous answer even when that answer was wrong, and students who have never been told this leave whole pages blank. Teaching a candidate to write down an assumed value, label it clearly, and continue is worth more on this paper than any additional content.

The second Paper 3 skill is reading the modelling instruction literally. These questions frequently ask a candidate to state an assumption, justify a choice of model, or comment on a limitation. Those marks are awarded for sentences, not for algebra, and students trained on Paper 1 habits write the algebra and skip the sentence. A tutor working through three or four past Paper 3 questions with a stopwatch usually finds the same two or three sentence-marks missing every time.

Because Paper 3 is HL-only, it is also the component a small school cohort is least likely to have drilled. An Abu Dhabi student in a six-strong AI HL class may have sat one timed Paper 3 before the mock. Four timed attempts with full marking is a realistic target for a tutoring block, and it is usually the single highest-yield intervention available in DP2.

sections.heading: The mathematical exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The exploration is marked out of twenty across five criteria, and the mark distribution surprises most families. Presentation and mathematical communication are worth four marks each; personal engagement and reflection are worth three each; the mathematics itself is worth six. A student who produces impressive mathematics in a badly structured document with no reflection can score eleven out of twenty, which at HL is a meaningful dent in a final grade.

Criterion E, use of mathematics, is where Higher Level candidates most often lose marks, and the reason is level rather than accuracy. The rubric asks for mathematics commensurate with the course. An AI HL exploration built on a linear regression and a correlation coefficient is accurate and insufficient. One built on a transition matrix with a steady-state interpretation, or a numerically solved differential equation with a sensitivity check, meets the level the criterion describes. Choosing the right question at the start is therefore worth more than polishing at the end.

Criterion D, reflection, is the cheapest criterion to recover and the most frequently neglected. Reflection means commenting on the significance of results, on the limitations of the model chosen, and on what a different approach would have shown — distributed through the work rather than parked in a final paragraph. Two or three substantive reflective comments at the points where a decision was made will usually move this criterion.

What a tutor may do here is bounded by IB academic honesty rules, and the boundary is not blurry. A tutor may discuss topic viability, point at a criterion and say which descriptor the current version meets, flag a notation convention, and ask the questions that make a student notice a gap. A tutor may not supply text, supply the mathematics, or hand back a rewritten version. The work must be the student's from the first question to the last page, and the school will ask the student to confirm exactly that.

sections.heading: Where AI HL marks are actually lost: a diagnostic list
paragraphs: Mark loss in AI HL is patterned rather than random, and the pattern repeats across cohorts. Statistical inference accounts for the largest single block. Candidates run a chi-squared test or a t-test on the calculator, read off a p-value, and then write a conclusion that omits the significance level, omits the context, or states that the null hypothesis is 'true' rather than not rejected. The arithmetic is done by the device; the marks are in the sentence.

Modelling questions produce the second cluster. A question gives data and asks which model is appropriate, and the candidate fits the model the lesson was about rather than the model the data suggests. Exponential, logistic, sinusoidal and piecewise behaviours each have visible signatures in a scatter plot, and recognising them is a trainable skill that takes a handful of sessions. The same cluster contains unjustified extrapolation beyond the data range, which examiners mark as a limitation to be commented on, not ignored.

The third cluster is technical hygiene, and it is the one that most annoys families when they see it: a calculator left in radian mode for a degree question, a value rounded to three significant figures and then reused in a later part, a final answer given with no units, a graph drawn with no axis labels. These are not mathematical failures. They are habits, and habits change in weeks when someone marks them strictly and consistently rather than noting them in passing.

The fourth cluster is the HL-only content that small cohorts rush at the end of DP1: matrices and eigenvalues, graph theory algorithms, complex numbers used in modelling, and numerical solutions to differential equations by Euler's method. Students often meet these topics once, under time pressure, in the same term as the exploration. A tutor can re-teach them properly in the autumn of DP2, which is late but not too late.

sections.heading: What the evidence file looks like, week by week
paragraphs: A family paying for weekly tutoring should be able to see progress without asking for a verdict. The mechanism used here is a running file, and it has four parts: a mark log by paper and topic, a set of marked scripts with the lost marks annotated, a dated version history of the exploration, and a short written note after each session naming what was worked on and what the next session will fix. None of that is elaborate. All of it is the difference between a judgement and a record.

In weeks one to four the file fills with diagnosis. Old scripts come in, get re-marked against command terms, and produce a topic list ranked by marks lost rather than by syllabus order. The mark log starts with two or three honest baseline figures from the student's own school assessments, not from a flattering entry test. A parent reading the file at the end of week four should see which topics are being attacked and why those and not others.

From roughly week five to the end of DP1 the file should show movement in the mark log on the topics that were attacked, and a first exploration question that survives scrutiny. Movement will be uneven: technical-hygiene marks come back quickly, new HL content takes longer, and statistical interpretation improves in steps rather than smoothly. A flat log across eight weeks with no explanation is the signal to change something, and it is better to see that in writing in October than to discover it from a February mock.

In DP2 the file changes character. The mark log becomes a record of timed full papers rather than topic exercises, the exploration version history closes, and the session notes shift to the three topics still costing the most. By the final term a parent should be able to point at a graph of paper marks over time and at four marked Paper 3 attempts. That is what a claim of progress looks like when it is checkable, and it is what you should ask any tutor in Abu Dhabi to produce.

sections.heading: What AI HL tutoring costs in Abu Dhabi, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Published rates in the UAE tutoring market are scarce, so the figures below are drawn from providers that publish their own prices and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey. They describe the market, not IB Gram's own fee, and they are quoted as the ranges those sources state. Rates in Abu Dhabi track Dubai closely, with in-home visits running at the upper end because the emirate's distances are longer.

Three things move the number for an AI HL booking. Level is the first: Higher Level commands more than Standard Level across every provider that publishes a split, because the tutor pool is smaller and Paper 3 competence is a narrower qualification. Format is the second: an in-home visit prices the tutor's travel into the hour, and in a city where a cross-town trip at 4.30pm can take forty minutes each way, that is a substantial share of what a family pays. Timing is the third: the final term before the May session is when demand peaks and availability is tightest.

The format comparison is where online delivery earns its place rather than being asserted. For the price of one in-home hour at the specialist rate, a family can often book two online hours with a tutor chosen for AI HL Paper 3 specifically rather than for living within a twenty-minute drive of Al Raha. That is the actual trade: a wider specialist pool and no travel premium, against the loss of a person physically in the room. For a subject where the examinable skill is interpreting output on a screen, the trade is a comfortable one.

IB Gram does not publish a price list on these pages, because the right number depends on level, frequency and how long is left before the session. A free 45-minute trial lesson with the proposed tutor comes first, with no card details taken, and the fee is confirmed in writing before any paid session is booked.

sections.heading: ADEK, MoHRE and who may legally tutor in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Private schooling in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain is overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK inspects schools and publishes ratings, and those ratings are worth reading before a school transfer. What ADEK does not do is license individual private tutors. That sits federally.

Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. According to u.ae the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists a two-working-day completion time and is the route to apply.

Two consequences matter to an Abu Dhabi parent. First, individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in u.ae's words, subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone. Second, Abu Dhabi has an additional restriction: press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. A family should verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it.

The practical reading: a tutor's own school teacher is the one person who usually cannot be hired, and a tutor who cannot discuss permit status is a tutor to ask more questions of. IB Gram holds no ADEK, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation and claims none; it matches students to independent tutors and states the delivery model plainly, which is online one-to-one video tuition for every UAE family.

sections.heading: AI or AA: what admissions actually expect
paragraphs: The AI versus AA question reaches a tutor in two different forms. In DP1 it is a live decision, and in DP2 it is a worry about whether the decision already made has closed a door. Both deserve a direct answer rather than reassurance, because the stakes are real and the information is published by universities rather than guessed at.

Engineering, mathematics, physics and most quantitative economics degrees at competitive universities state Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level, in their published entry requirements. Some will accept AI HL; many will not, and the ones that will not say so explicitly in their prospectus. Computer science varies by institution more than any other subject. Business, management, psychology, architecture, life sciences, medicine in most systems, and the social sciences broadly accept AI HL at Higher Level without comment.

The instruction that follows from this is dull and necessary: read the entry requirements for the specific course at the specific universities on the shortlist, on their own admissions pages, in the year the student will apply. That applies equally to UAE institutions and to overseas ones, and it applies before the option form is signed rather than after. A tutor can help a student read a requirement precisely, and should decline to summarise a requirement the university states for itself.

For a student already in AI HL and worried, the honest position is that AI HL is a full Higher Level mathematics course with 240 teaching hours and a demanding Paper 3, and that the overwhelming majority of degree programmes accept it. Where a specific target course requires AA, the options are a switch early in DP1, a different course choice, or a route via a foundation year. None of those is a tutoring decision, and nobody should sell tutoring as the fix for a prerequisite mismatch.

sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi school year, Ramadan and the May session counted backwards
paragraphs: Diploma students in Abu Dhabi sit the May session, which means the real calendar pressure arrives much earlier than families expect. Working backwards from the examination window rather than forwards from today is the planning habit that separates a calm DP2 from a frantic one, and it is the one thing no competitor page in this market seems to publish.

The fixed internal deadlines come first. Schools set their own exploration submission dates, typically with a first draft in DP2 autumn and a final version in the winter term, and those dates land in the same weeks as mock examinations. A student who starts thinking about an exploration question in January has lost the part of the process that Criterion C rewards, because genuine personal engagement takes time that a deadline has already consumed. The useful target is a viable question agreed before the end of DP1.

Ramadan sits inside this calendar and shifts earlier each year on the Gregorian calendar. School hours shorten, energy patterns change, and families in Abu Dhabi routinely move tutoring to post-Iftar slots for the month. Online delivery makes that trivial to arrange; an in-home arrangement often cannot absorb it at all, because a tutor's evening becomes a sequence of long drives. Planning the Ramadan schedule in advance, rather than cancelling four weeks, protects the DP2 revision run.

For the examination dates themselves, go to the source. The IB publishes its session timetables and results dates on ibo.org, and a school's Diploma coordinator will confirm the exact windows and the EUR and remark deadlines for that cohort. Cambridge and Pearson publish their own IGCSE timetables separately — Cambridge notes that every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk. No date on this page should be treated as a substitute for those sources.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP Math AI HL tutor in Abu Dhabi charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market rates give the realistic bands. Providers that publish prices put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 or more: Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase publishes AED 270. In-home visits run higher, AED 180-500 in Bestimate's 2026 survey, because travel is priced inside the hour. faqs.question: How is Paper 3 different from Paper 1 and Paper 2 in Maths AI HL?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only by Higher Level candidates, lasts one hour, carries 20% of the grade, and contains two extended problem-solving questions rather than a spread of syllabus questions. The mathematics inside each part is not usually harder than Paper 2 mathematics; the difficulty is that the parts build on each other, so a student who stops at part (c) also loses parts (d) to (g). Examiners award marks for carrying a previous answer forward even when it was wrong, which makes writing down an assumed value and continuing the single most valuable Paper 3 habit to learn.

faqs.question: How many marks does the mathematical exploration carry in AI HL?
faqs.answer: Twenty, distributed across five criteria, and it is worth 20% of the final grade. Criterion A for presentation and Criterion B for mathematical communication are four marks each. Criterion C for personal engagement and Criterion D for reflection are three each. Criterion E for use of mathematics is six. The distribution matters because strong mathematics in a poorly structured document with no reflection caps at around eleven. At Higher Level, Criterion E is lost most often on level rather than accuracy: an exploration built on a basic regression is correct but pitched below the course.

faqs.question: Can a tutor comment on an exploration draft without breaking IB academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that should be stated in writing before work starts. A tutor may discuss whether a question is viable, point at a criterion and say which descriptor the current version meets, flag notation and convention problems, and ask the questions that make a student see a gap. A tutor may not supply text, supply the mathematics, or hand back a rewritten version. The student signs an authenticity declaration for the school, and the whole document has to be theirs. Any service offering finished explorations is selling the student an IB malpractice investigation.

faqs.question: My son is at an Abu Dhabi IB school. Will a tutor work to his school's deadlines or their own?
faqs.answer: His school's. The school sets the internal exploration deadlines, the mock windows and the reporting cycle, and a tutor who ignores them creates two competing timetables. The first session should establish those dates, and the session plan is then built backwards from them. In practice that means exploration work is front-loaded into DP2 autumn, because school draft deadlines and mocks usually collide, and timed-paper work moves to the spring. Ask any tutor to tell you the school's next three deadlines after the second session; if they cannot, they are not working to a calendar.

faqs.question: How many weeks before we can judge whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Four weeks for the diagnosis and twelve for the trend. By week four a parent should be able to read a ranked list of the topics costing the most marks, a set of re-marked scripts showing where inside each answer the loss happens, and a baseline mark log drawn from the student's own school work. By week twelve the log should show movement on the topics that were attacked. Technical-hygiene marks come back fastest, new Higher Level content takes longest. A flat log across eight weeks with no explanation is a signal to change the plan or the tutor.

faqs.question: Does AI HL really need a graphic display calculator in every paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is a structural difference from Analysis and Approaches, where Higher Level Paper 1 is sat without one. Applications and Interpretation assumes technology throughout all three papers, which changes what is being tested: model selection, interpretation and explanation rather than hand computation. Calculator workflow therefore becomes examinable technique. Fitting the right regression, running a hypothesis test and reading the p-value, finding intersections numerically, and storing exact values instead of retyping rounded ones each carry marks. A student fluent in the syllabus but clumsy with the device loses marks that have nothing to do with mathematics.

faqs.question: Why do AI HL candidates lose so many marks on chi-squared and t-test questions?
faqs.answer: Because the calculator does the arithmetic and the marks live in the sentence. A candidate runs the test, reads a p-value, and then writes a conclusion that omits the significance level, omits the context of the question, or says the null hypothesis is true rather than not rejected. Marks are also lost for not stating the hypotheses at the start and for not naming the test being used. None of this is a mathematical weakness, which is why it is among the fastest mark recovery available: strict, consistent marking of the conclusion wording usually fixes it inside a few weeks.

faqs.question: Is Maths AI HL accepted for engineering degrees at UAE universities?
faqs.answer: It varies by institution and by course, and the only safe answer is to read the published entry requirements for the specific programme in the year of application. Engineering, mathematics, physics and quantitative economics courses at competitive universities frequently specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and the ones that will not accept AI say so explicitly. Business, psychology, architecture, life sciences and the social sciences generally accept AI HL without comment. A tutor can help a student read a requirement precisely but should never summarise away what a university states for itself.

faqs.question: What do matrices, networks and differential equations add to AI HL that SL never covers?
faqs.answer: They are a large part of what makes the Higher Level course Higher Level. AI HL extends into matrix algebra including eigenvalues and eigenvectors, transition matrices and steady-state behaviour, graph and network theory with its minimum-spanning-tree and route-inspection algorithms, complex numbers used in modelling, and numerical solutions to differential equations including Euler's method and coupled systems. Standard Level meets none of this. In small Abu Dhabi cohorts these topics are often taught quickly at the end of DP1, in the same term as the exploration, which is why re-teaching them properly in DP2 autumn is such a common tutoring request.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to post-Iftar times during Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning that shift in advance works far better than cancelling the month. School hours shorten during Ramadan, energy patterns change, and a late-evening slot after Iftar is often the most productive hour of the day for a DP2 student. Because lessons run over live video, moving a weekly slot by three hours for four weeks costs nothing and requires no travel rearrangement. The practical advice is to agree the Ramadan timetable a few weeks ahead, keep the weekly rhythm, and treat the month as a scheduling change rather than a pause in the revision run.

faqs.question: How quickly can an AI HL specialist be matched for a family in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Diploma subjects a match is usually possible within a few days. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is narrower, and the binding constraint is the slot rather than the subject: a 5pm Gulf Standard Time weekday request competes with every other Diploma family in the Gulf. If nothing suitable is free, the reply should say so and offer the real alternatives — a different weekday, a slightly later start, or a tutor in another time zone whose evening is the family's afternoon — rather than placing a general mathematics tutor and hoping it works.

faqs.question: What should we send when we first ask about an AI HL tutor?
faqs.answer: Six things make the first reply useful instead of generic: the course named exactly as Applications and Interpretation Higher Level, the school and year group, the specific topics causing trouble, where the exploration stands, two or three workable weekly slots in Gulf Standard Time, and the last two pieces of marked work. The marked work does most of the job. Marks matter less than the pattern of lost marks inside the answers, because that is what tells a tutor whether the problem is unlearned content or examination habit, and the two have very different timelines.

faqs.question: Does ADEK or MoHRE regulate private tutors in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: MoHRE. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, but individual private tutors are covered by the federal private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. u.ae states the permit is granted free of charge for two years and lists eligible applicants including registered school teachers, public and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our villa in Khalifa City or Al Raha?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service offered only in India. For Abu Dhabi every lesson is one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing of the student's own script, and a recording available afterwards. The trade is deliberate: a family in Al Raha gets a tutor chosen for AI HL Paper 3 experience rather than one chosen for living a short drive away, and nobody pays a travel premium inside the hourly rate for a journey across the emirate at 4.30pm.

intro.heading: The question nobody asks until month three
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements in Abu Dhabi are judged on atmosphere. The tutor is punctual and pleasant, the student does not object to the sessions, homework gets done, and everyone agrees it is going well. Three months later a mock arrives at roughly the mark it would have arrived at anyway, and a family who has spent several thousand dirhams has no way of telling what went wrong, because nothing was ever measured. The missing step was never the teaching. It was deciding, at the start, what evidence of progress would look like.

In Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level the evidence is unusually available, because almost everything in the course produces a markable artefact. Two examination papers of 80 marks each, worth 40 per cent apiece. A mathematical exploration of 20 marks across five criterion letters, written in drafts over weeks. Past papers with published mark schemes. Topic tests. A graphic display calculator whose use either appears in the written working or does not. A family that knows how to read those artefacts can tell in four weeks whether a plan is working, rather than in twelve.

What makes this course particularly readable is that its failures are specific and repetitive. A Standard Level Applications candidate who is losing marks is usually losing them in two or three identifiable ways: a correct statistic reported without any interpretation in context, a calculator answer written with no supporting line, a model fitted without justification, degrees of freedom or units dropped in a chi-squared test. Those errors recur across papers, which means they can be counted. A tutor who says the student is improving should be able to show you the count going down.

On delivery, the page should be plain before it goes further. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address: home visits in Abu Dhabi are not part of what we sell, and that service exists only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, same tutor, same slot. That matters for the evidence question in a way that is easy to miss: work set at the end of a video session is marked between sessions and returned in writing, so a parent in Al Reef or on Yas Island has a documented trail rather than a verbal report from the dining table.

The rest of this page is a method. How to read a marked Standard Level Applications script, and the four things worth looking at on it. What the two papers are actually testing and the mark totals you should be tracking. What a school report comment means when translated into a topic area. What each exploration draft should change, and which criterion is at stake in each pass. What grade movement genuinely looks like, and why a six-mark gain sometimes moves a grade and sometimes does not. And what should arrive in writing after four weeks, eight weeks and twelve.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Evidence looks different in each programme, because what gets marked differs. These are the programmes behind an Abu Dhabi mathematics enquiry and what you can actually measure inside each one.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Applications and Interpretation SL is assessed by two papers at 40 per cent each and an exploration at 20 per cent, with everything marked against published schemes and criteria. That makes it one of the most measurable courses on a Diploma timetable.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools report Diploma progress in different formats, from a 1-7 predicted grade to percentages to criterion comments, and parents comparing notes across Khalifa City and Al Raha Gardens are often comparing incompatible scales. The artefact that travels between schools is the marked script with per-question marks on it, which is why that is the thing to ask for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups marked against four criteria each on a 1-8 scale, with no external examinations before the optional MYP 5 eAssessment. Mathematics here is assessed on knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, so progress evidence is criterion scores over time rather than percentages.
programmes.countryNote: The criterion on applying mathematics in real-life contexts is the direct ancestor of Standard Level Applications, and a student who scored consistently low on it in MYP 5 will usually be losing interpretation marks in DP1. That is a useful early signal and almost no family in this emirate is told to look for it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses taken with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. A student taking Applications and Interpretation SL within this programme sits the same two papers and the same exploration, so the evidence you track is identical.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi this programme appears mainly in conversations about load, where a family is buying support in several subjects simultaneously. If evidence in three subjects is flat at once, the problem is usually the timetable rather than the teaching, and that conversation belongs with the Diploma coordinator.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Progress evidence varies by subject because the markable artefacts vary. These are the Diploma subjects Abu Dhabi families most often support alongside Standard Level Applications, with the specific thing worth measuring in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Measure per-question marks on timed 80-mark papers, the count of calculator answers written without a supporting line, and the number of statistics questions where a conclusion appears in context. All three are countable and all three move before the overall percentage does.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same five topic areas over 240 hours, with a third paper at 20 per cent and matrices, graph theory and inferential testing added. Evidence tracking is the same but with Paper 3 timing logged separately, because that paper fails on structure rather than on content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The other route, where the first paper is sat without a calculator. The marker worth watching there is exact-value work and written method, which is a different evidence set entirely. A student who moved across routes should have both tracked for a term.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across four criteria, so progress is visible criterion by criterion rather than as a score. Data analysis and evaluation are where Applications students should be strongest and often are not, because nobody connects the two courses.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Measure whether quantitative answers carry a written interpretation, exactly as in mathematics. Students who drop the conclusion sentence in one subject almost always drop it in the other, which makes a shared fix unusually efficient.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Internal assessment commentaries are marked against criteria and returned in drafts, so the evidence is draft-to-draft movement on named criteria. The Higher Level quantitative paper gives a second, separate signal worth logging alongside the maths.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The internal assessment requires a chosen and justified inferential test, which is the same skill Applications assesses. Progress here is visible in whether the student can state what a test does and does not establish, in writing, without prompting.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Fieldwork and the internal assessment produce data and a written analysis, so the measurable item is whether analysis replaces description. Applications students have the statistical vocabulary for it; the evidence shows whether they use it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Progress is slower to read because the artefacts are essays and orals rather than marked questions. Ask for criterion-level comments across two pieces rather than a single grade, because a grade hides which criterion moved.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: One essay and one exhibition, marked against published criteria. There is little to measure weekly, which is why a term-long weekly plan here is rarely justified and a small number of feedback sessions usually is.

regions.note: Large villa communities feeding Al Yasmina Academy and GEMS American Academy Abu Dhabi. Reports here often arrive as percentages from an American-style gradebook, which hides the per-question detail, so the marked script matters more than the report does.

regions.note: Raha International School runs the full IB continuum nearby, so students here usually have years of criterion comments in their record. That history is genuinely useful evidence: a criterion that has been weak since MYP 4 is a pattern, not a bad week.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Repton School Abu Dhabi and a tower population whose evenings are decided by bridge traffic. A timed 90-minute paper rarely fits a weekday here, so families schedule the full-length practice papers at the weekend and keep weekdays for marking and review.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Cranleigh Abu Dhabi and a community on short postings. Where a student has changed school mid-course, the useful baseline is a full timed paper in week one rather than any previous school's reporting, because the scales do not translate.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Central island streets with short commutes, several established schools and the most realistic weekday evening slots in the city. These are the families most able to sit a timed section on a weekday and review it the next day while it is fresh.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Samha
regions.note: Further-out communities where a long bus journey means a student is tired by five o'clock. Evidence here improves when the timed work moves to Saturday morning, because a paper sat exhausted tells you about fatigue rather than about mathematics.

regions.note: Mainland districts with long commutes to the island schools. Weekday sessions rarely start before 5.30pm, so the practical rhythm is a weekend timed paper and a midweek hour spent on what the marking showed.

sections.heading: What progress in Standard Level Applications looks like, week by week
paragraphs: A family searching for a home tutor for Applications and Interpretation SL in Abu Dhabi is buying a change in a number. The useful question, asked at the beginning rather than at the end, is which number and by when. Published market rates for in-home one-to-one work in the UAE run roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour and up to about 500 at the specialist end, and for IB specialists AED 200 to 450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. At those rates, a plan that cannot say what will be measurable in four weeks is not a plan.

IB Gram delivers this support one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and home visits in Abu Dhabi are not something we sell; that service exists only in India. The relevant consequence here is procedural rather than pedagogical: work set in a video session is marked between sessions and returned in writing, so what a parent in Al Reef gets is a documented record rather than a verbal impression relayed at dinner.

The table sets out what should be visible at each stage, and equally what should not. The most common error families make is expecting the overall percentage to move first. It does not. The first things to move are the number of questions attempted in the time, the number of calculator answers that carry a written line, and the number of statistics questions where a conclusion appears in context. Those are leading indicators. The paper percentage is a lagging one, and it typically shifts a mock or two later.

Setting the review date in advance is what makes the whole thing work. Agree, before the first paid session, that at week five you will look at two marked papers side by side and at the count of a named error. A tutor who is confident has no reason to resist that, and a family who has fixed it in advance never has to have the awkward month-three conversation about whether any of this is doing anything.

sections.heading: Reading a marked script: the four things worth looking at
paragraphs: Most parents look at a marked Applications paper and read the total. The total is the least informative thing on it. The first thing worth reading is the pattern of per-question marks: whether the losses are spread thinly across every question or concentrated in three. Thin losses across everything usually mean a technique or writing habit, because small errors recur everywhere. Concentrated losses mean a topic gap, because the student simply cannot do those questions.

The second is whether calculator answers carry a written line. In this course the device does the arithmetic, and a bare answer forfeits method marks even when it is correct. Count the questions where a value appears with nothing supporting it. That number is a direct measure of recoverable marks, it is usually larger than anyone expects, and it is the single fastest thing in the course to fix.

The third is the conclusion sentence. On any question involving data, a statistic or a model, look for a sentence that says what the result means for the named quantities in context. If it is absent, the student is leaving the final mark on most of those questions. Absence here is not carelessness; it is almost always that nobody has ever told them the sentence was the point.

The fourth is where the paper stops. A script that is complete to question 9 and blank from 10 is a timing problem, which is fixed with pacing practice rather than with teaching. A script attempted throughout with low marks everywhere is a different animal. Log the completion time as well as the mark, because a paper finished with ten minutes to spare and a paper abandoned at eighty minutes can carry the same total and need opposite remedies.
bullets: Spread losses mean a habit; concentrated losses mean a topic gap
Count the calculator answers with no supporting written line
Count the data questions with no conclusion in context
Log completion time next to the mark, every time

sections.heading: The two papers, and the numbers you are actually tracking
paragraphs: Standard Level Applications is assessed by two examination papers and the exploration. Paper 1 runs 90 minutes over 80 marks at 40 per cent and is built from shorter compulsory questions spanning the whole syllabus, so no topic area can be left uncovered. Paper 2 is also 90 minutes and 80 marks at 40 per cent, built from longer extended-response questions that develop a context across several parts. A graphic display calculator is assumed in both. The exploration carries the remaining 20 per cent across 20 marks.

For tracking purposes this structure is a gift, because both papers are on the same 80-mark scale. Two timed Paper 1 attempts six weeks apart are directly comparable in a way that a school percentage and a mock grade are not. If you record per-question marks rather than totals, you can also see whether gains came from the questions that were targeted or from somewhere else, which is the difference between a plan that worked and a lucky paper.

The papers do fail differently and should be tracked separately. Paper 1 punishes breadth gaps: a student who never learned Voronoi diagrams or the financial mathematics will meet them there, as short questions worth a few marks each, and will lose them quietly. Paper 2 punishes thread loss: the student answers part (a) and part (b), misreads what part (c) is asking in the context, and the remaining parts unravel. One is a coverage problem, the other is a reading problem.

Confirm durations, mark totals and weightings against your child's own copy of the current subject guide, which the school issues and the IB revises periodically. What is stable enough to build a tracking system on is the shape: two equal papers on the same scale, calculator assumed, plus an internally assessed exploration that is the only component where you can see progress between drafts.

sections.heading: Translating a school report comment into a topic area
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi school reports are written for the school's purposes, not for a parent planning support, and the standard phrases are vague in ways that are fixable. 'Inconsistent application' usually means the student can do the procedure and cannot decide when to use it. 'Needs to show more working' almost always means calculator answers without a supporting line. 'Struggles with problem solving' most often means multi-part questions in context, which is a Paper 2 problem rather than a knowledge problem.

Translating those phrases into topic areas is worth doing before buying hours, because the five topic areas of Standard Level Applications are very different sizes. Statistics and probability is the largest block at around 36 published hours, functions is next at around 31, then calculus at 19, geometry and trigonometry at 18, and number and algebra at 16, with about thirty further hours for the toolkit and exploration across the course. A comment about statistics is a comment about a quarter of the course. A comment about number and algebra is a much smaller problem.

The practical move is to go back to the teacher with a specific request rather than a general question. Ask which topic area the lost marks sit in, and whether the losses are concentrated or spread. A Diploma mathematics teacher running a set of fifteen will usually answer that precisely if asked precisely, and the answer is free. Families who ask how my child is doing get a sentence about effort. Families who ask which topic area and which paper get a diagnosis.

The table below maps the five topic areas against the comment language that usually accompanies them and the evidence that would show the problem had been fixed. It is deliberately written to be taken to a parents' evening.

sections.heading: The exploration, draft by draft: what each pass should change
paragraphs: The exploration is the only component where a parent can watch progress happen rather than infer it. It is 20 marks across five criterion letters, with presentation and mathematical communication at four marks each, personal engagement and reflection at three each, and use of mathematics at six. Because engagement, reflection, presentation and communication together account for fourteen of the twenty marks, the biggest gains usually come from things that are not additional mathematics.

A well-run exploration goes through a small number of named passes, each addressing a different criterion. The first, before any data is collected, settles the research question. This is where most of the eventual grade is decided and where almost nobody spends time. A question like 'how does population affect water use' produces a graph; a question about whether a particular model describes a specific measured quantity over a specific period, with a stated reason for expecting that shape, produces an investigation.

Later passes address communication, then reflection, then presentation, in that order, because each depends on the one before. Reflection written before the mathematics is settled is guesswork. Presentation polished before the structure is settled is wasted. The table sets out the sequence, what the student does at each stage and which criterion is at stake, so a family can see at any moment whether the document is moving or merely being retyped.

The boundary is strict and it protects the student. A tutor explains what a criterion asks, teaches the mathematics the student has chosen to use, reads the draft and says where marks are being lost, and sets the next revision for the student to carry out. No part of the submitted document originates with a tutor and nothing is rewritten into final form by one. Keep the dated feedback: it is the clearest available evidence that the work is the student's own, and it is the reason a documented trail is worth more than verbal advice.

sections.heading: What grade movement looks like, and what nobody can promise
paragraphs: Marks and grades move on different clocks, and conflating them causes a lot of unnecessary disappointment in DP2. Grade boundaries are set per session by the IB after the papers are marked, they move from session to session, and they are not published in advance. So a student who gains six marks on a Paper 1 has unambiguously improved and may or may not have crossed a boundary. The honest way to report progress is in marks on a stated scale, with the grade treated as a consequence rather than a target.

This is also why no tutor should be promising a grade, a points total or a specific improvement, and why a page that does is telling you something about itself. What can be committed to is process: that work is set and marked, that a named error is tracked, that you receive it in writing, and that the plan changes if the evidence does not. Anyone offering more than that is selling certainty that the assessment system does not contain.

Predicted grades are a separate thing again and they belong to the school. A predicted grade is a teacher's professional judgement submitted for university applications, and it is based on the evidence the school holds, not on what a tutor thinks. The way tutoring influences it is indirect and entirely legitimate: better marked work in the school's own assessments gives the teacher better evidence to predict from. Asking a school to revise a prediction because a tutor disagrees is not a route that works.

There is one more honest caveat. Mathematics grades in DP2 move inside a system with five other subjects, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge in it, and a student whose Applications marks climb while everything else slides has not been helped overall. A tutor who notices that pattern should say so. Several times a year the right recommendation is fewer mathematics hours and a conversation with the Diploma coordinator about load.
bullets: Track marks on a stated scale; treat the grade as a consequence
Boundaries are set per session and are not published in advance
Predicted grades belong to the school and rest on the school's evidence
Rising maths marks beside falling everything else is not a win

sections.heading: Four weeks, eight weeks, twelve weeks: what should be true by when
paragraphs: At four weeks the question is whether a habit has started to change. You should have three or four marked pieces of set work, a baseline timed section, and a written note after each session naming one tracked error. The measurable claim at this point is modest and specific: the error appears less often, and more of the paper is being attempted in the time. If none of that exists at four weeks, the problem is the arrangement rather than the student.

At eight weeks the question is whether the habit change has converted into marks under conditions. That requires a second timed paper on the same scale as the baseline, marked against the published scheme, with per-question marks recorded so the two can be laid side by side. A gain concentrated in the questions that were targeted is strong evidence. A gain spread randomly across a paper is weaker evidence and may be noise, which is worth saying out loud rather than celebrating.

At twelve weeks the question becomes whether to continue, change or stop. By then there should be two or three comparable papers, a declining count on the tracked error, and an exploration that has moved on at least two named criteria. If all three are true, the plan is working and the sensible move is to keep it and reduce intensity. If the papers are flat, adding hours to the same plan is the least promising available option, and changing the diagnosis or the tutor is more likely to help.

The whole structure depends on one decision taken at the start: agreeing in advance what will be looked at and when. It costs nothing, it takes one sentence in the first conversation, and it converts a tutoring arrangement from something a family hopes is working into something they can check. Families who do this almost never end up in a fourth month of a plan that was never going to deliver.
bullets: Week 4: marked work exists and a named error is declining
Week 8: a second timed paper on the same scale, per-question marks compared
Week 12: continue, change or stop, on the evidence rather than on feel
Agree the review points before the first paid session, not after the third

sections.heading: What should arrive in writing, and what to ask for if it does not
paragraphs: A reasonable written record for Standard Level Applications support is short and specific. After each session: what was covered, what was set, and the one error being tracked. After each marked piece: the scheme applied, the marks by question, and the error count. At the agreed review: two comparable papers and a plain statement of whether the plan is working. None of that is onerous, and a tutor working properly is generating it anyway as a by-product of marking.

If it is not arriving, ask for it directly and specifically. 'Could you send a two-line note after each session naming the error you are tracking' is a request almost any competent tutor will accommodate, and a reluctance to produce anything in writing is itself informative. The same applies to marking: a tutor who sets work but does not mark it against the published scheme is giving the student practice without feedback, which is the least efficient form of practice there is.

For exploration work the written trail serves a second purpose. Schools are increasingly careful about the provenance of internally assessed work, and a student who can show dated feedback on their own drafts, with the revisions they then made, is in a straightforwardly better position than one who cannot. That is a reason to prefer written feedback over verbal feedback even when the verbal would have been quicker.

Finally, keep the evidence in one place, because it is the thing that makes the conversation with the school useful. Walking into a meeting with two marked timed papers, a declining error count and a specific question about one topic area produces a different conversation from walking in to ask how things are going. The school has information you do not; the evidence trail is what lets you ask for the part of it that matters.
bullets: Per session: covered, set, one tracked error, in two lines
Per marked piece: scheme applied, marks by question, error count
At review: two comparable papers and a plain verdict on the plan
Keep exploration feedback dated, for the school as well as for you

sections.heading: ADEK, the school's evidence and the conversation worth having
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, and the u.ae government portal describes ADEK as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK publishes its own inspection outcomes, which is where a school's rating should be read rather than from any third-party summary. What a published inspection band does not tell you is anything about an individual Standard Level mathematics set, which is where your child's marks are actually being generated.

The school holds evidence a family cannot otherwise get: how your child's marks compare with the set, which questions the whole set lost, whether a topic was taught thinly because of timetable pressure, and what the teacher will base a predicted grade on. All of that is available on request and almost none of it arrives unprompted. The specific questions worth asking are which topic area the lost marks sit in, whether the losses are concentrated or spread, and what the student would need to show for the prediction to move.

One route to rule out. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff says paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school is prohibited, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document. Either way, your child's own teacher is a source of evidence rather than a tutoring option.

On the regulatory side for whoever you do hire, the position is checkable. Private tuition work permits were introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation and claims none.
