sections.heading: The investigation, draft by draft, at Standard Level
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is the one component where progress can be watched rather than inferred. It carries 20 per cent of the Standard Level grade, is marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each, and is capped at 3,000 words. The four criteria are research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Because they are equal, a beautifully executed experiment with a thin evaluation scores no better than a modest experiment that is evaluated properly, which is not what most students assume.

The decisive pass is the first one, before any data exists. A research question with a defined independent variable, a defined dependent variable, controlled variables that are actually controllable in a school laboratory, and a method capable of producing enough data over a wide enough range to test anything. Students who start collecting before this is settled usually end up with a dataset that cannot answer their own question, and no later analysis recovers those marks.

Later passes should each target one criterion, in an order that respects dependency. Data analysis before conclusion, because a conclusion rests on processed data with propagated uncertainties. Conclusion before evaluation, because an evaluation has to explain the gap between what was found and what was expected. Evaluation last, and specifically: quantified weaknesses with realistic improvements, not a paragraph about human error. The table sets out the sequence so a family can tell whether a draft is moving or merely being retyped.

The boundary protects the student and we state it rather than imply it. A tutor explains what each criterion asks, teaches the physics and the analysis techniques needed, reads the draft and names where marks are being lost, and sets the next revision for the student to carry out. No part of the submitted report originates with a tutor and nothing is rewritten into final form. Keep the dated feedback; where a school asks about the provenance of internally assessed work, a trail of the student's own revisions is the clearest possible answer.

sections.heading: What four, eight and twelve weeks should show in Physics
paragraphs: At four weeks the question is narrow: has a presentation or reasoning habit started to change. You should hold three or four marked pieces with the published scheme applied, a baseline timed section, and a short note after each session naming the error being tracked. The claim at this stage is modest and checkable: fewer answers missing units, and a stated principle appearing on more extended questions. If none of that exists, the problem is the arrangement rather than the student.

At eight weeks the question becomes whether the habit has converted into marks under conditions. That needs a second timed paper on the same scale as the baseline, marked question by question so the two can be laid side by side. A gain concentrated in the question types that were targeted is strong evidence. A gain scattered randomly may be noise, and saying so is more useful than celebrating it. The data-based section is usually where movement shows first, because it is the most trainable component in the course.

At twelve weeks the decision is continue, change or stop. By then there should be two or three comparable papers, a declining count on the tracked error, and an investigation that has moved on at least one named criterion. If all three hold, the plan is working and the sensible move may be to reduce intensity rather than extend it. If the papers are flat, buying more of the same is the least promising option available, and changing the diagnosis or the match is more likely to help.

The entire structure rests on one decision taken at the start, which costs nothing. Agree, before the first paid session, what will be looked at and when. Families who do that almost never spend a fourth month on a plan that was never going to deliver, and the awkward conversation about whether any of this is working simply does not arise, because the answer was already written down.

sections.heading: Marks, grades and what nobody can promise
paragraphs: Marks and grades do not move together, and conflating them causes a lot of avoidable disappointment in DP2. Grade boundaries are set per session by the IB after the papers have been marked, they shift from session to session, and they are not published in advance. A student who gains eight marks on an extended-response paper has unambiguously improved and may or may not have crossed a boundary. The honest way to report progress is in marks on a stated scale, with the grade treated as a consequence.

This is why no tutor should be offering a specific grade, a points total or a stated improvement, and why a page that does is telling you something about itself rather than about physics. What can be committed to is process: work set and marked, a named error tracked, written notes, and a plan that changes when the evidence says it should. Anything beyond that is selling a certainty the assessment system does not contain.

Predicted grades belong to the school. A prediction is a teacher's professional judgement submitted for university applications on the basis of the evidence the school holds, which is its own assessments, mocks and classwork. Tutoring influences it only indirectly, by improving the work the school sees. Asking a school to revise a prediction because a tutor disagrees does not work; asking the teacher what the student must demonstrate in the school's own assessments for the prediction to move does.

One further honest caveat. Standard Level Physics sits inside a Diploma with five other subjects, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge in it. A student whose physics marks climb while three other subjects slide has not been helped overall, and a tutor who notices that pattern should name it. Several times a year the right recommendation is fewer physics hours and a conversation with the Diploma coordinator about load.

sections.heading: Moving down from Higher Level: the evidence that should decide it
paragraphs: A meaningful share of Standard Level Physics enquiries in Abu Dhabi come from families part-way through a Higher Level course, asking whether to step down. It is a legitimate question and it should be answered with evidence rather than with sentiment. What a Standard Level student drops is the Higher Level-only material, including rigid body mechanics, relativity, thermodynamics, induction and quantum physics, along with the extensions inside shared subtopics. The investigation carries across unchanged, and so do all four of its criteria.

The evidence worth gathering before the conversation is specific. How many of the lost marks on recent papers came from Higher Level-only content as against shared material. Whether the student's data-based and reasoning habits are sound, because if they are not, the same habits will cost marks at Standard Level too. Whether the physics is the problem at all, or whether the underlying mathematics is. And what the student's other five subjects look like, because a step down taken to protect two other grades is a different decision from one taken because physics is unreachable.

The timing is a school matter and the window is real. The school has to timetable the student into a Standard Level set that may be full, and the IB registration has to be amended, so the decision belongs with the Diploma coordinator and should be raised early rather than once the mocks have confirmed what everyone suspected. A tutor's useful contribution is the evidence: a marked script annotated to show which losses were Higher Level-only, which is a twenty-minute job and genuinely helps the meeting.

The outcome is sometimes the opposite of what the family expected. Where the lost marks are concentrated in presentation habits and unstated principles rather than in Higher Level content, stepping down removes the hardest material and leaves the actual problem untouched, and the grade does not improve as much as anyone hoped. That is worth knowing before the registration is changed, and it is exactly the kind of finding a marked script delivers and a conversation does not.

sections.heading: ADEK, the school's data and the questions that get real answers
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, and the u.ae government portal describes ADEK as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK publishes its own inspection outcomes, which is where a school's rating should be read rather than from a third-party summary. An inspection band tells you nothing about one Standard Level Physics set, which is where your child's marks are actually produced.

The school holds the comparative information that makes everything else interpretable: how your child's marks sit against the set, which questions the whole set lost, whether a theme was taught thinly because of timetable pressure, when the experimental hours and the investigation deadlines fall, and what a predicted grade will rest on. Ask for those five things specifically. General questions about progress get general answers; specific questions get a diagnosis, and the school is not withholding anything, it is simply waiting to be asked.

One route to rule out before planning. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff says paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school is prohibited, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current wording on ADEK's own policy page. Either way, your child's teacher is a source of evidence rather than a tutoring option.

For whoever you do hire, the regulatory position is checkable in a sentence. Private tuition work permits were introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by MoHRE and granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation and claims none.

process.title: Gather the free evidence first
process.description: A marked paper with per-question marks, a recent data table, the investigation draft with the school's comments, and the term's internal deadlines. Twenty minutes of asking changes the diagnosis often enough to be worth doing before any money is spent.

process.title: Take the free first lesson as a baseline
process.description: The tutor reads the marked work, asks your child what a gradient means and which principle they would write first, and sends a written note naming the leaking component and the single error to be tracked. That note is the baseline everything afterwards is measured against.

process.description: Week four for units and stated principles appearing, week eight for a second timed paper on the same scale, week twelve for a continue, change or stop decision. One sentence at the start, and the month-three conversation never needs to happen.

process.title: Run the cycle and mark everything
process.description: Work set at the end of every session, attempted independently, marked against the published scheme before the next, and the session spent on what the marking showed. Practice that is set and never marked gives repetition without feedback, which is the slowest route to any improvement.

process.title: Decide on the evidence, not the feeling
process.description: Two comparable papers and a tracked error count answer the question. If the marks have moved, continue and consider easing off. If they have not, change the diagnosis, the format or the tutor rather than adding hours to something already not working.

whyPoints.title: Both halves of the first paper are tracked apart
whyPoints.description: The multiple-choice and data-based sections reward opposite habits, and a combined mark hides which one is weak. We mark and report them separately, which is how a timing problem stops being mistaken for a knowledge problem.

whyPoints.title: Every session leaves a written trace
whyPoints.description: Two lines after each lesson: what was covered, what was set, and the one error being tracked. It takes a minute to write and it is the difference between a family who can check what they are buying and a family who is hoping for the best.

whyPoints.title: We say what the school owns
whyPoints.description: The experimental programme, the internal deadlines, the predicted grade and the set comparison all belong to the school, and no tutor substitutes for them. Telling you which door to knock on is part of the job, not a deflection from it.

whyPoints.title: Nothing in an investigation originates with us
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria, teach the physics and the analysis, read drafts and set revisions the student carries out. No part of a submitted report is produced by a tutor. The dated feedback trail is useful evidence that the work is genuinely the candidate's own.

whyPoints.title: No grade is promised, and the reason is stated
whyPoints.description: Boundaries are set per session after marking and are not published in advance, so a specific final grade quoted in advance is invented. What is committed to is the process and the evidence, which is the part anybody can actually be held to.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and limits are both disclosed
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not visit UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. If no Standard Level Physics specialist is free at the hours you need, we say so at the enquiry rather than later.

faqs.question: What evidence should we have after a month of Standard Level Physics sessions?
faqs.answer: Four things. A written baseline from the first lesson naming the weak component and one error to track. Three or four pieces of set work, marked against the published scheme rather than given a percentage. A short note after each session saying what was covered and which error is being tracked. And a date for the next timed paper. You should not expect the overall paper mark to have moved yet; that typically arrives a mock later. What you should see is fewer answers missing units and a principle appearing on more extended questions.

faqs.question: His mock mark went up but the predicted grade did not change. Why not?
faqs.answer: Because the two are different instruments. Grade boundaries are set per session by the IB after marking, they move between sessions and they are not published in advance, so a real gain can sit inside one band. A prediction is separately the school's professional judgement based on all the evidence it holds, not on one mock. Ask the teacher what your son would need to demonstrate, in the school's own assessments, for the prediction to move. That question gets a specific answer; asking for the prediction to be raised does not.

faqs.question: How do we tell a content gap from a technique problem on a Physics script?
faqs.answer: By the shape of the losses. Marks lost thinly across almost every question, one or two at a time, are a technique or presentation problem: missing units, values quoted to a calculator's full display, no principle stated before the algebra. Marks lost in a concentrated block, where a cluster of questions scores nothing at all, are a content gap in a theme. The two need opposite remedies, and a percentage hides which one you have. Ask for the script with per-question marks rather than the summary figure.

faqs.question: Our report says she needs to apply knowledge to unfamiliar contexts. What does that mean in Physics?
faqs.answer: Usually that she has learned question types rather than principles, so a familiar question works and a rephrased one does not. The test for it takes two minutes: ask a prediction question with no numbers in it, such as what happens to the force if the separation doubles. A student who reasons from the relationship is fine. A student who reaches for a formula sheet is pattern-matching, which holds up through early mechanics and collapses in Theme D fields. That is a representation problem and it responds to two or three deliberate sessions rather than to more practice.

faqs.question: What does Standard Level Physics leave out that Higher Level includes?
faqs.answer: Whole subtopics and extensions. The subtopics are rigid body mechanics and Galilean and special relativity in Theme A, thermodynamics in Theme B, induction in Theme D and quantum physics in Theme E. The extensions sit inside shared subtopics such as simple harmonic motion, the gravitational and electric field material, and the radioactive decay law. This matters practically: a Standard Level student revising induction is revising material they will not be examined on, and one given Higher Level practice papers produces scores that mean nothing.

faqs.question: How many drafts should the investigation go through, and what should each one change?
faqs.answer: Four or five passes, each targeting one criterion in dependency order. First, before any data exists, settle the research question and the variables so the method can actually produce enough data over a wide enough range. Then processing and uncertainty propagation. Then the conclusion, compared against accepted physics with the source identified. Then evaluation, with specific quantified weaknesses rather than remarks about human error. A final pass cuts the method to fit the 3,000-word ceiling. A draft that is being retyped rather than restructured is not a pass.

faqs.question: My son's practical work is good but his papers are not. How is that possible?
faqs.answer: Easily, because they test different things. Competent bench work means he can follow a method and take readings carefully. The data-based section of the first paper asks what a gradient means physically, whether a difference between two results is meaningful given the uncertainties, and what is wrong with somebody else's method. Those are interpretive skills, and they are trained on paper rather than at a bench. The useful consequence is that this gap is one of the most improvable things in the course and it lifts the investigation marks at the same time.

faqs.question: Should a tutor be looking at our child's school laboratory record?
faqs.answer: At the data, yes; at the record as a document, no. What helps is a photograph of a recent results table, because it shows whether the student records readings with units, repeats, and sensible precision, which is exactly what the investigation's data analysis criterion rewards. What a tutor should not be doing is working inside the school's assessed practical material or anything the school is supervising. The division is simple: the school owns the experimental programme and the supervision; a tutor helps with design thinking, processing and the written argument.

faqs.question: Is in-home Standard Level Physics tuition available in Abu Dhabi from IB Gram?
faqs.answer: No. We do not send a tutor to any UAE address, and home visits in Abu Dhabi are not a service we sell; that exists only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor each week. For the evidence question this is an advantage rather than a compromise: work set in a session is marked between sessions and returned in writing, so what you hold is a dated record of marked scripts and tracked errors instead of a verbal summary at the door.

faqs.question: Should we move our daughter from Higher Level to Standard Level Physics, and what should decide it?
faqs.answer: Evidence, and the most useful piece is a marked script annotated to separate losses on Higher Level-only content from losses on shared material. If most of the damage is in rigid body mechanics, thermodynamics, induction or quantum physics, stepping down genuinely removes it. If the damage is missing units, unstated principles and unpropagated uncertainty, those habits follow her down and the grade will not move as much as hoped. The decision belongs with the Diploma coordinator, because the school must have a set with space and the registration must be amended.

faqs.question: How often should a timed Physics paper be sat, and which section?
faqs.answer: Fortnightly once the relevant themes are taught, and start with the data-based section because it is short, quick to mark and the most trainable component in the course. Full extended-response papers are worth sitting monthly, under conditions with the phone in another room, with completion time logged next to the mark. Families in outer districts usually do the longer papers on a Saturday morning, because a paper sat at seven in the evening after a bus from the island measures tiredness rather than physics.

faqs.question: What should a written note after a science session actually contain?
faqs.answer: Two or three lines. What was covered, what has been set to do before the next session, and the single error currently being tracked, named the same way each week so it can be counted rather than described. Over six weeks those notes become the clearest record of whether anything is changing. Anything longer turns into a narrative, which reads well and proves nothing. If notes are not arriving, ask for them explicitly; a reluctance to put anything in writing is itself informative.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell us what Physics grade our child will finish with?
faqs.answer: No, and an honest one will explain why rather than hedge. Grade boundaries are set per session after the papers are marked and are not published beforehand, so any specific final grade offered in advance is invented. What a tutor can legitimately tell you is which component is losing marks, how many of those marks are recoverable from habits as against content, and roughly how long that normally takes. Predictions for university applications belong to the school and rest on its own assessment evidence.

faqs.question: Who at the school should we ask, and what exactly should we ask them?
faqs.answer: The Physics teacher first, and the Diploma coordinator if the issue is load or level. Five specific requests get real answers: the marked script with per-question marks, which questions the whole set found hardest, when the experimental hours and investigation deadlines fall, whether any theme was covered at speed because of timetable pressure, and what your child must demonstrate for a predicted grade to move. 'How is she doing' produces a sentence about effort. Those five produce a plan, and they cost nothing.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start Standard Level Physics support?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the marked script shows, which is why the first lesson is a diagnosis rather than a sale. If the content is broadly covered and the marks are going on units, unstated principles and the data-based section, then even six to eight weeks changes the picture, because those are habits and habits move quickly. If two themes were never properly taught, no short block delivers them and we will say so. An honest no at that point saves a family more than a block of hours aimed at an unreachable target.

faqs.question: What does Standard Level Physics support cost in the Abu Dhabi market?
faqs.answer: Published UAE bands put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, while in-home one-to-one work runs about AED 180 to 350 and reaches around 500 at the specialist end. Standard Level Physics generally sits in the middle of the specialist band, below Higher Level. Those figures belong to the sources named rather than to IB Gram, and the first lesson is free precisely so a plan can be priced after a diagnosis instead of before one.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-physics-sl-home-tutor.closingHeading: Collect the evidence, then decide what to buy
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-physics-sl-home-tutor.closingBody: Standard Level Physics is an unusually easy subject to check, because almost everything in it produces something markable. Ask the school for the script with per-question marks, a recent data table, the investigation draft with its comments, and the term's internal deadlines. Send those to us with the level and the theme you think is the problem, and the free first lesson comes back as a written baseline naming the leaking component and the one error to track. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, work is marked against the published schemes between sessions, and at the agreed review we will tell you plainly whether the evidence says continue, change or stop.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-physics-sl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Physics at Standard Level as its own job. That is a different skill from teaching Higher Level: the content is bounded, the student is often not a physicist by inclination, and the fastest route to a better grade usually runs through examination technique rather than through more theory.

intro.heading: Physics SL is usually a means to an end, and that should shape the teaching
paragraphs: Most students sitting Physics at Standard Level in Abu Dhabi did not choose it because they love physics. They chose it because the Diploma requires a Group 4 science, because a target degree mentions a science, because the alternative subjects clashed on the timetable, or because an older sibling said it was the sensible option. That is not a criticism of anyone. It is the single most useful fact about the course, because it changes what good teaching looks like.

A student who intends to study physics benefits from depth, derivation and the pleasure of a hard problem. A student who needs a 5 or a 6 in Physics SL to complete a Diploma aimed at law, design, business or medicine benefits from something else entirely: a bounded map of the 150 hours, a hard focus on the marks that are lost for non-physics reasons, and a revision routine that fits around five other subjects. Teaching the second student as if they were the first is the commonest way a Standard Level physics grade stalls at a 4.

The bounded map matters because Physics SL is finite in a way students rarely realise. The current guide runs five themes — space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; nuclear and quantum physics — and Standard Level sees those themes without the Higher Level extensions. The relativity, rigid body mechanics, induction and quantum extensions that frighten students reading about the course online are not on the Standard Level syllabus at all. Knowing precisely where the boundary sits removes a surprising amount of anxiety in one session.

The marks lost for non-physics reasons are the other half. A large share of Standard Level loss comes from unit conversion, from arithmetic done in a hurry, from an answer given to five significant figures when the data justified two, from a one-line answer to a question whose command term asked for reasons, and from a graph read correctly and interpreted wrongly. None of that is theory. All of it is habit, and habit changes in weeks when someone marks it strictly.

Abu Dhabi's practical constraint is timing rather than distance, because lessons here run over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service available only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one on video with screen sharing of the student's own work. What that buys a Standard Level family is the ability to pick a tutor who teaches this course well rather than one who happens to live near Khalifa City, and to hold a slot at 6pm without anyone driving across Mussafah to reach it.

The rest of this page sets out the content boundary theme by theme, the Higher Level to Standard Level decision and when it can still be made, where Standard Level marks actually go, how the scientific investigation works at this level, a revision plan counted backwards from the May session, and what the Abu Dhabi market charges for a science specialist.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-physics-sl-tutor.programmesIntro: A Physics SL booking in Abu Dhabi is almost always a Diploma booking, but the useful history sits earlier. What a student brings from middle years science or from an IGCSE physics course decides how much of the first term is repair and how much is progress.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every candidate must take a Group 4 science, and Physics SL is one of the standard ways to do it. Assessment is Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the scientific investigation at 20%, with a data booklet supplied in the examinations.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi cohorts the Standard Level physics set is often a mixed group: a few students who moved down from Higher Level, several who need a science and chose this one, and one or two genuine physicists who wanted the timetable space. A whole-class pace cannot serve all three, which is where individual support earns its place.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Integrated sciences assessed against four criteria, including inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating. Those two criteria are the direct ancestors of the Diploma scientific investigation, so students from a strong MYP background usually find the investigation familiar even when the physics content feels new.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Abu Dhabi student has come through the same school's MYP, the old criterion reports are the cheapest diagnostic available. They tend to show clearly whether the difficulty in DP1 will be the arithmetic and algebra or the extended written explanation, and those need different plans.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson International GCSE 4PH1 are the usual routes into the Diploma for Abu Dhabi students. Both cover mechanics, thermal physics, waves, electricity and basic nuclear physics. The Diploma deepens all of it and adds formal uncertainty treatment and much longer written explanation.
programmes.countryNote: The step from 0625 or 4PH1 into Physics SL is manageable and has two predictable sticking points: rearranging a formula rather than substituting into it, and writing a three-step explanation rather than a one-line answer. A term of deliberate work on those two clears most of the gap.

programmes.name: Course certificates and the Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Not every student takes the full Diploma. Some Abu Dhabi schools offer individual course certificates or the Career-related Programme, and a student can sit Physics SL within either. The papers and the investigation are identical; what differs is the surrounding workload and the absence of some core deadlines.
programmes.countryNote: A student taking Physics SL as a certificate course usually has more room in the DP2 calendar, because there is no Extended Essay competing for the same weeks. That often means the investigation can be finished early, which is the single best thing to do with it.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-physics-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Physics SL is usually one piece of a wider Diploma plan, and Abu Dhabi families often book two or three subjects together. These are the courses most frequently requested alongside it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes assessed by Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and one scientific investigation at 20%. Standard Level sees the themes without the Higher Level extensions, so relativity, rigid body mechanics, induction and quantum physics do not appear on the syllabus.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across six organising themes, with its own scientific investigation marked on the same four criteria. The two sciences share the uncertainty and significant-figure conventions, so one data-handling session repairs marks in both.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Four organising themes plus the investigation. Biology carries more terminology and less arithmetic than physics, which is why students who struggle with rearrangement often do better here and should know that before an option form is signed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with technology assumed throughout. The commonest mathematics pairing for a Physics SL student, and the one that leaves rearrangement and trigonometry to be built inside the physics sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic and calculus route, including a paper sat without a calculator. A Physics SL student in AA SL usually finds the formula work routine, because the mathematics course is already drilling exactly that fluency.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary course that can satisfy either Group 3 or Group 4. Students weighing Physics SL against a lighter science route frequently compare the two, and the honest comparison is about assessment style rather than difficulty.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisation, human resources, finance, marketing and operations. A very common Diploma companion for Abu Dhabi students taking Physics SL as their required science rather than as a subject of interest.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Micro, macro, the global economy and development, with internal commentaries on news articles. It competes with physics for DP2 weeks, which makes planning the two timetables together more useful than treating them separately.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: The design cycle, materials, production and a major project. It shares the physics habit of justifying a choice against evidence and rewards the same documentation discipline the investigation needs.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay. A Standard Level physics student has good material here: measurement, uncertainty and the status of scientific models are all usable knowledge questions.

sections.heading: Who takes Physics SL, and why the reason changes the plan
paragraphs: A Standard Level physics set in an Abu Dhabi school usually contains three different students. The first moved down from Higher Level, often during DP1, and carries both relief and a dented confidence. The second needs a Group 4 science, picked physics over biology or chemistry for timetable or preference reasons, and has no intention of studying it further. The third genuinely likes physics but wanted Higher Level space for another subject, and will probably finish with a 7.

Those three students need different tutoring, and the mismatch is the commonest reason a Standard Level grade sticks. The student who moved down from Higher Level does not need more content; they need to be shown how much smaller the syllabus has become, because they are usually still revising as if the extensions applied. The student who needs a grade does not need derivations; they need a bounded map, strict marking and a routine. The student who likes physics needs harder questions than the class is setting.

The practical implication for a parent choosing a tutor is to be explicit about which student their child is, because the honest answer shapes the first month. A family that says 'she needs a 5, she is not going to be an engineer, and she has five other subjects' will get a plan built around marks per hour of effort. A family that says only 'she needs help with physics' will get something generic and will pay for a term of it before noticing.

Being clear about the goal is not lowering ambition; it is choosing where the effort goes. A Standard Level student aiming at a 6 who spends every session on the hardest Paper 2 questions while losing eight marks a paper to unit conversion and command terms is working hard in the wrong place. Sequencing the work by marks recoverable per hour is what a good Standard Level plan actually is.

sections.heading: Standard Level and Higher Level side by side
paragraphs: The difference between the two levels is ninety teaching hours and a set of named extensions that sit inside the five themes, plus longer papers. Standard Level runs 150 hours and Higher Level 240. Both levels are assessed on Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the scientific investigation at 20%, which surprises families who assume the Standard Level investigation must be a smaller piece of work. It is not: same rubric, same four criteria, same twenty-four marks, same 3,000-word limit.

What Standard Level does not include is the content students read about online and panic over. Rigid body mechanics with torque and moment of inertia, Galilean and special relativity, induction with flux and Lenz's law, gravitational and electric potential as extended topics, and quantum physics with the photoelectric effect and the de Broglie relationship are Higher Level material. A Standard Level student encountering those in a video or a revision book is reading something they will not be examined on, and the hours spent are simply gone.

Paper durations differ between the levels, with Higher Level sitting longer papers in both components. The exact timings for a particular session should be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator rather than taken from any third-party page, including this one. What is stable and worth planning around is the weighting, because weighting is what tells a student where to spend revision time, and Paper 2 at 44% deserves more of it than most students give it.

sections.heading: The five themes at Standard Level depth
paragraphs: The current Physics guide organises the course into five themes, and at Standard Level each one is studied without its Higher Level extensions. Theme A, space, time and motion, covers kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, and circular motion. Theme B, the particulate nature of matter, covers thermal energy and specific heat, the gas laws and the kinetic model, and the greenhouse effect and energy transfers. Theme C, wave behaviour, covers simple harmonic motion, wave characteristics, superposition, interference and standing waves.

Theme D, fields, covers gravitational and electric fields at Standard Level depth, electric current and circuits including resistance and power, and magnetic effects of currents. Theme E, nuclear and quantum physics, covers the structure of the atom, radioactive decay and half-life, nuclear fission and fusion, and mass-energy equivalence. Alongside these sit the tools — experimental technique, technology and mathematics — and the inquiry process, which supply the investigation's structure.

Where Standard Level students lose most content marks is predictable by theme rather than random. Circular motion in Theme A causes trouble because it requires recognising that a resultant force points towards a centre even when nothing visible pushes it there. The gas laws in Theme B cause trouble through unit handling, especially temperature in kelvin. Circuits in Theme D cause trouble because series and parallel reasoning has to be done before any formula is used. Half-life in Theme E causes trouble when the question gives a fraction rather than a whole number of half-lives.

The table maps each theme to the mathematics it assumes and the specific topic that most reliably needs a second explanation. A revision plan built on that map is more efficient than one built on the order of the textbook, because it puts the hours where the marks are.

sections.heading: Moving from Higher Level to Standard Level: the decision and the window
paragraphs: Dropping physics from Higher Level to Standard Level is the commonest level change in a science subject, and it is usually a good decision made too late. The school decides, the Diploma coordinator has to agree it, and the practical window is widest in the first term of DP1 and narrows through the second. By DP2 a move is still sometimes possible but the student has already spent a year carrying a heavier course, which is a year of pressure that did not need to be paid.

The mechanics of the move are gentle, which is the part families do not realise. The Standard Level syllabus is contained within the Higher Level course, so a student who moves down does not have to learn anything new. They have to stop learning things, which is psychologically harder and practically easier. The content they were struggling with in the extensions simply ceases to be examinable, and the content they already know becomes a comfortable margin.

The decision should be made on evidence rather than on a single bad assessment. The useful evidence is two or three pieces of marked work and an honest read on where the marks went. A student losing marks across the Higher Level extensions specifically is a good candidate for the move. A student losing marks on unit conversion, command terms and arithmetic is not: those losses will follow them to Standard Level, and dropping a level without fixing them converts a struggling Higher Level student into a struggling Standard Level student.

The thing to check before moving is the university requirement, and it should be checked on the universities' own admissions pages rather than assumed. Some engineering and physical-science programmes specify physics at Higher Level. Many degrees specify a science without naming a level. Where a target course requires Higher Level, the conversation is about course choice and shortlist rather than about tutoring, and it belongs with the school's university counsellor.

sections.heading: Where Standard Level marks actually go
paragraphs: Mark loss at Standard Level has a different profile from Higher Level, and it is more recoverable. The largest single block is unit handling. Prefixes converted wrongly, millimetres treated as metres, temperatures left in degrees Celsius inside a gas-law calculation, kilowatt-hours mixed with joules, and electronvolts left unconverted together account for a startling number of lost marks across a paper. None of that requires understanding more physics, and all of it responds to six weeks of strict marking.

The second block is answer length against command term. A question that says 'explain' wants reasons and the mark scheme awards the steps; a student who writes one correct line collects one mark of three. A question that says 'state' wants one line, and a student who writes a paragraph wastes time they will need later in the paper. Command terms are published, there are not many of them, and matching an answer to the term is a mechanical skill that moves marks within a few weeks of attention.

The third block is graph work. Reading a gradient, saying what the gradient physically represents, giving it units, reading an intercept and interpreting it, and recognising when a relationship needs linearising before a straight line can be drawn are all examined. Students routinely get the number right and the meaning wrong, which scores the calculation mark and loses the interpretation mark. Practising the sentence, not just the calculation, fixes it.

The fourth is arithmetic under pressure, which is where a calculator habit matters. Working to full precision and rounding only at the end, storing intermediate values rather than retyping them, checking an order of magnitude against a sensible expectation, and giving a final answer to a precision the data justifies are habits rather than knowledge. They are also the habits most visibly absent in a hurried Paper 1B.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation at Standard Level
paragraphs: The investigation is worth 20% of the Standard Level grade, is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each, is limited to 3,000 words, and is allocated around ten hours of class time. Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation carry equal weight. None of that is reduced for Standard Level candidates, which makes the investigation proportionally the biggest opportunity on the course for a student who finds examinations difficult.

The single best decision a Standard Level student makes is to choose a boring, measurable experiment. An investigation that produces clean data from a straightforward setup — a pendulum, a spring, a resistance against length, a cooling curve — can score full marks, because the criteria reward design, processing, justified conclusion and honest evaluation, not ambition. An investigation built around an interesting phenomenon that cannot be measured reliably with school equipment loses marks in research design before any data exists and cannot recover them later.

Research design is where the preparation pays. A clearly stated research question, a defined independent and dependent variable, identified controlled variables and a method detailed enough to repeat are what the criterion asks for, and all of it is written before entering the laboratory. That makes it the part of the investigation remote tutoring handles best: it is a conversation about what to vary, what to hold fixed, how many repeats, and over what range.

The limit on tutor involvement should be written down and given to the family before any investigation work begins. A tutor may discuss whether a question is measurable, point at a criterion and say which descriptor a current version meets, comment on uncertainty treatment and presentation conventions, and ask questions that make a student notice a gap. A tutor may not supply text or data, and may not return a rewritten report. The student signs an authenticity declaration and the work must be theirs.

sections.heading: Revision counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Standard Level physics revision fails for a scheduling reason rather than a motivation one. A student with six subjects and three internal assessments plans forwards: today I will revise physics. Three weeks later the themes revised are the ones that were comfortable, the gas laws and circuits have been avoided, and nobody has sat a timed paper. Counting backwards from the examination window fixes this, because it forces every week to have a named job.

The structure that works is simple. The last two weeks before the session are reserved for weaknesses already identified, not for new revision. The six weeks before that are one theme per week, each with a timed section of Paper 1 and a timed Paper 2 question, marked and returned. Before that, the investigation must be finished and submitted, because an unfinished investigation in the final term eats the revision weeks it cannot afford to take.

Mock examinations sit inside this calendar and should be treated as data rather than as a verdict. The useful output of a mock is not the grade but the breakdown: which themes lost marks, how many marks went to units and command terms rather than to physics, and where the clock ran out. A student who takes that breakdown seriously in January finishes the course in a different place from one who reads the grade and feels bad about it.

Ramadan sits inside the DP2 calendar and shifts earlier each year on the Gregorian calendar. School hours shorten and energy patterns change, and Abu Dhabi families commonly move sessions to post-Iftar slots for the month. Because lessons run over video, that is a scheduling change rather than a pause. For examination dates themselves, use the source: the IB publishes session and results dates on ibo.org, and the school's Diploma coordinator will confirm the exact windows for a cohort.

sections.heading: Costs, permits and how lessons are delivered in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Published rates in this market are thin, so the figures here come from providers that publish their own prices and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost survey. They describe the market rather than IB Gram's fee. Qualified online subject tutors run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Bestimate puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. In-home visits in the same survey are AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoted to AED 500, because driving is inside the rate.

Standard Level generally sits below Higher Level across providers that publish a split, which makes a Standard Level booking one of the better-value interventions in a Diploma. The arithmetic a family should do is marks per dirham rather than dirhams per hour: six sessions aimed at unit conversion and command terms will often move a Standard Level grade further than twenty sessions of additional theory, and will cost a quarter as much.

On the legal position, two bodies do different jobs. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain and publishes inspection ratings. Individual tutors are covered federally by the private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to a parent.

Delivery is stated the same way on every UAE page here. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, Al Ain or anywhere in the Emirates; a tutor travelling to a family's address is an India-only service. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video with screen sharing and a recording. For a Standard Level student, the practical gain is choice: a tutor selected for teaching this course well, in a slot that fits the bus timetable, with no travel premium inside the hourly rate.

process.title: Say what the grade is for
process.description: A Standard Level plan depends on the target. 'She needs a 5 and is not going to study physics' and 'he wants a 7 and is applying for architecture' produce different first months, and saying which one applies saves a term of generic sessions.

process.title: Send one marked paper
process.description: A single marked assessment is enough to start. What a tutor reads is where the marks went: unit conversion, command terms, graph interpretation, arithmetic, or genuine content gaps. Those five have five different plans and very different timelines.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One 45-minute lesson over live video with the proposed tutor, no card details, no obligation. It runs on a real question from the student's own work, and it ends with the tutor naming the first three things the plan would change.

process.title: Fix a slot the student can actually use
process.description: Sessions are set on Gulf Standard Time around when the bus arrives and how much attention is left. For Al Reef and Mohammed Bin Zayed City that usually means 6pm; for the island neighbourhoods 4pm often works well.

process.title: Build the calendar backwards
process.description: From the first session there is a written plan counted back from the examination window, with the investigation finished early and the final fortnight reserved for identified weaknesses only. Progress is read from marked returns rather than from impressions.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus boundary drawn clearly
whyPoints.description: Standard Level students are shown precisely which content is not theirs — relativity, rigid bodies, induction, quantum physics — so that no evening is spent revising Higher Level extensions that cannot be examined.

whyPoints.title: Marks per hour, not theory per hour
whyPoints.description: Sessions are sequenced by what is recoverable fastest: units, command terms, graph interpretation and arithmetic discipline before additional content. For a student with five other subjects, that sequencing is the whole value.

whyPoints.title: A written revision calendar
whyPoints.description: The final term is planned backwards from the examination window, with a named job for each period and a marked return as the evidence. Revision that is planned forwards reliably skips the hardest themes.

whyPoints.title: An honest view on dropping a level
whyPoints.description: Where a move from Higher Level is the right call, the evidence for it is laid out: which losses come from extensions and which are habits that would follow a student down. The decision stays with the school.

whyPoints.title: Investigation support with a stated limit
whyPoints.description: Help is discussion, criterion feedback and process coaching on the student's own work. No text and no data are supplied, and the boundary is given to the family in writing before the first investigation session.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider or survey that published it and the year. The market is quoted as the market, and IB Gram's own fee is confirmed in writing after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is Physics SL a sensible choice if my child is not a scientist?
faqs.answer: For many students, yes, and the reason is that Standard Level physics is bounded. It runs 150 teaching hours across five themes without the Higher Level extensions, so finishing the syllabus properly is realistic alongside five other subjects. The honest comparison is with biology and chemistry rather than with a harder physics course: physics carries more arithmetic and rearrangement, biology carries more terminology, chemistry sits between them. A student who dislikes formula manipulation often does better in biology, and that is worth knowing before an option form is signed rather than in DP2.

faqs.question: Can my son move down from Physics HL to Physics SL partway through?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is the commonest level change in a science subject, but the school decides and the Diploma coordinator has to agree it. The window is widest in the first term of DP1 and narrows through the second. Mechanically the move is gentle, because the Standard Level syllabus is contained within the Higher Level course: nothing new has to be learned, content simply stops being examinable. The decision should rest on where his marks are being lost, because losses to units and command terms will follow him down while losses on the extensions will not.

faqs.question: How long are the IB Physics Standard Level papers?
faqs.answer: Standard Level papers are shorter than their Higher Level counterparts in both components, and the exact timings for a given session should be confirmed with the school's Diploma coordinator rather than taken from a third-party page. What is stable is the weighting, and that is what should drive revision: Paper 1 carries 36% and comes in a multiple-choice part and a data-based part, Paper 2 carries 44% and is the extended-response paper, and the scientific investigation carries the remaining 20%. Paper 2 is the largest single component and the most consistently under-revised.

faqs.question: Does Physics SL satisfy the Diploma science requirement on its own?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every Diploma candidate must take a subject from Group 4, the sciences, and Physics at Standard Level satisfies that requirement in full. A student does not need a second science or a Higher Level science to complete the Diploma. What may require more is a specific university course: some programmes ask for two sciences, and some ask for a named science at Higher Level. That is a question about the shortlist rather than about the Diploma, and the answer is on each university's own admissions pages.

faqs.question: Which universities accept Physics SL rather than Physics HL?
faqs.answer: Many accept a science at Standard Level where a science is required at all, but the only reliable method is to read the published entry requirements for each specific course in the year of application. Engineering and physical-science programmes commonly specify physics at Higher Level, often with Analysis and Approaches mathematics alongside it. Architecture, design, business, law and several health-science routes are frequently satisfied by Standard Level or by any science. Nobody should summarise this for a family, because the requirement is stated by the university and varies between two courses at the same institution.

faqs.question: What grade is realistic in Physics SL with one session a week?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the marks are currently going, which is why an honest answer follows a diagnosis rather than preceding it. A student whose content understanding is sound and who loses marks to unit conversion, command terms and the clock has substantial room to move, because those are habits and habits change in weeks. A student who has not learned two of the five themes and has eight weeks left has a different problem, and should be told the number of hours it would actually take rather than sold a weekly slot and an implied outcome.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether the problem is physics or arithmetic?
faqs.answer: Look at a marked paper and read what was crossed out rather than the total. If the setup is right, the correct relationship was selected, and the error appears in the rearrangement, the unit conversion or the final rounding, the problem is arithmetic discipline and it is fixable in weeks. If the student could not choose a relationship, could not say what the question was about, or left the item blank, the problem is content. The two look identical in a grade and need completely different plans, which is why a tutor should ask for marked work before quoting anything.

faqs.question: How much time does the Physics SL investigation really take?
faqs.answer: The course allocates around ten hours of class time, and the report is limited to 3,000 words and marked out of twenty-four across four criteria. In practice most students spend more than ten hours, mostly on processing and writing rather than on measurement. The planning that saves the most time happens before the laboratory: a measurable research question, defined variables, a decided number of repeats and range. Students who improvise the design in the laboratory spend the extra hours twice, and still lose research-design marks they can never recover.

faqs.question: What should a Physics SL student be doing twelve weeks before the exams?
faqs.answer: One theme a week with a timed paper section each week, marked and returned, having already submitted the investigation. Twelve weeks out is too late to start new content and exactly right for structured coverage: five themes plus the data and graph skills gives six weeks of work, then four weeks of full timed papers, then a final fortnight on identified weaknesses only. The investigation should be finished well before this period, because an unfinished report in the final term consumes revision weeks that cannot be replaced.

faqs.question: Is Physics SL much harder than IGCSE 0625 Extended?
faqs.answer: Harder, but in two specific and manageable ways rather than across the board. The content overlaps substantially: mechanics, thermal physics, waves, electricity and basic nuclear physics all appear in both. What changes is the mathematics, which moves from substituting into a formula to rearranging it and resolving vectors, and the writing, which moves from one-line answers to multi-step explanations where the mark scheme awards each link. A student with a strong 0625 or 4PH1 grade has the foundation; a term of work on those two differences usually closes the gap.

faqs.question: Do Standard Level students need to memorise the data booklet?
faqs.answer: No, because it is supplied in the examinations, and that changes what the papers test. The examinable skill is selecting the right relationship for the situation and justifying why it applies, not recalling it. Students who treat the booklet as a safety net rather than a working tool lose marks because they have never practised finding things in it quickly or deciding between two similar-looking relationships. Deliberate practice with the booklet open, under time pressure, is worth several marks and takes very little teaching.

faqs.question: What does an online Physics SL tutor cost for an Abu Dhabi family?
faqs.answer: Market figures from providers that publish them put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour; Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase publishes AED 270, while Bestimate's 2026 Dubai survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. In-home visits in that survey are AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors are quoted to AED 500, because driving is priced inside the hour. Standard Level generally sits below Higher Level. IB Gram confirms its own fee in writing after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a headline rate.

faqs.question: Can sessions be moved around Ramadan and school examination weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning the change in advance works much better than cancelling. School hours shorten during Ramadan and energy patterns shift, so Abu Dhabi families commonly move a weekly slot to a post-Iftar time for the month. Because lessons run over live video, that is a calendar change with no travel consequences. The same applies to school examination weeks: the useful move is usually to keep the slot and change what it is used for, spending the hour on the school's assessment content rather than on the longer plan.

faqs.question: My daughter is at school in Al Ain. Is online really the only option for Physics SL?
faqs.answer: It is the only option that reliably gets a subject specialist. Al Ain sits under the same regulator as Abu Dhabi city and has its own international schools, but the resident pool of tutors who teach Diploma physics on the current guide is very small, so a local search usually returns a general science tutor. A video lesson removes the constraint entirely: the choice becomes who teaches the course best in a slot that works, rather than who lives within reach. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE in any case.

faqs.question: Does Physics SL include relativity, induction or quantum physics?
faqs.answer: No. Those are Higher Level extensions and they are not on the Standard Level syllabus, along with rigid body mechanics and the extended treatment of gravitational and electric potential. This matters practically rather than academically: Standard Level students regularly find these topics in revision videos and second-hand books and spend evenings on material that cannot be examined. Checking the Higher Level markings in the current subject guide through the school, and then deleting the extension chapters from the revision plan, is often the most useful single hour of a first month.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-physics-sl-tutor.closingHeading: One marked paper tells us where the Standard Level marks are going
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-physics-sl-tutor.closingBody: If your child sits Physics at Standard Level in an Abu Dhabi school, the first step is one marked assessment and a short message saying what the grade is for. A free 45-minute trial lesson with the proposed tutor follows, over live video, with no card details taken. What should come back is a clear read on whether the marks are being lost to units and arithmetic, to command terms and answer length, to graph interpretation, or to content that was never learned — and a written plan counted backwards from the May session rather than forwards from today.

intro.heading: The grade is set by the verb, not by the reading
paragraphs: Psychology attracts students who are genuinely interested, and that is why the mark often disappoints. A student reads around the subject, holds strong views about obedience studies and memory models, can talk for twenty minutes about the material, and writes an essay that earns twelve marks out of twenty-two. The content was present. What was missing was the thing the question asked for, and in this subject what the question asks for is encoded in a single verb at the start of it.

The IB uses command terms on a graded scale. The lowest band asks for recall: define, describe, outline, state. The middle band asks for process: explain, apply, analyse, distinguish, compare and contrast. The top band asks for judgement: discuss, evaluate, to what extent, examine. An answer written at the wrong level is capped regardless of quality. A beautifully written description in response to a question beginning discuss has already lost the marks that separate a 5 from a 7, and it will lose them again on the next paper, and the one after that, until somebody points at the verb.

The structure the terms sit inside is worth stating plainly. The first paper examines the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches to behaviour through three short-answer questions worth nine marks each and one extended response worth twenty-two. The second paper draws on the option topic or topics the school has chosen, again through extended responses worth twenty-two marks. Higher Level adds a third paper, built on an unseen description of a study, which tests the methodology and ethics vocabulary of the course rather than its content. The internally assessed experimental report is marked against four criteria totalling twenty-two marks and sits inside a defined word range.

Abu Dhabi contributes two specifics. First, cohorts are small and the option topic is chosen by the department, so two students in neighbouring communities can be sitting materially different second papers; brief any tutor on the option before booking. Second, the ethics of running a replication are tighter here than students assume, because the participants available to a school student are usually classmates who are minors, and consent, debriefing and data handling all have to be properly dealt with. Lessons themselves are delivered online, one to one, over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, because home visits are a service we run only in India.

The order of work on this page follows the order the marks come in. Command terms first, because they cap everything. Then the three approaches as a revision structure rather than a reading list. Then the methodology vocabulary, which supplies the critical-thinking credit in every essay and the whole of the Higher Level methodology paper. Then the report, criterion by criterion, with the ethics settled before any data is collected. Then the regulator, the university routes and the honest position on what a tutor may and may not touch.

Extended responses carry twenty-two marks and are capped by the command term
The second paper is set on the option topic your school chose, not a student choice

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-psychology-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Psychology is a Diploma subject, but students arrive at it from several directions and the gap on arrival differs by route. These are the stages that matter for an Abu Dhabi family and what support is actually for at each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years covering three approaches to behaviour, one or more option topics, research methodology, and an experimental report written against four criteria. Standard and Higher Level share the approaches; Higher Level adds extension content within each approach and a separate methodology paper. The subject sits in the individuals and societies group rather than the sciences.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Psychology cohorts are often taught by a single teacher across both levels, and the option topic is settled at department level. Ask which option the class sits and whether the Higher Level extensions have been taught yet, because in a mixed-level room they are frequently left until late in DP2.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and Societies in the middle years is where command-term discipline is built. The criteria already distinguish between describing and evaluating, and students who learned to separate the two arrive in DP1 able to read a question properly. Those who did not spend DP1 unlearning a habit instead of learning content.
programmes.countryNote: Students moving into Diploma Psychology from a middle years programme in this emirate usually need methodology vocabulary rather than subject content. A short block in the summer before DP1 on sampling, bias and generalisation pays off across both papers and the report.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: IA, EE and TOK
programmes.description: The experimental report, an Extended Essay that many students choose to write in Psychology, and Theory of Knowledge all land together. Psychology is a popular Extended Essay subject and a difficult one, because the ethical constraints on original research push students towards literature-based questions they are not taught how to frame.
programmes.countryNote: Internal deadlines in Abu Dhabi schools cluster before the long weekends and the Eid breaks, and a report that depends on collecting data from classmates has to be scheduled around those breaks rather than through them. abu-dhabi/ib-dp-psychology-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Psychology is chosen alongside a particular set of subjects, and the combination affects both the workload and the university routes that stay open. These are the pairings seen most often in this emirate.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, one or more option topics, research methodology, and an experimental report on four criteria. Marks are lost to command terms and to unevidenced claims far more often than to gaps in content knowledge.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, physiology, genetics and ecology with an internally assessed investigation. Frequently paired with Psychology because several university psychology courses prefer an experimental science alongside it. The two share a weakness in the evaluation sections of their respective reports.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary course spanning the sciences and individuals and societies, often taken to satisfy two group requirements at once. Students choosing it alongside Psychology should confirm how their target universities treat it, because recognition varies by course.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Anatomy, exercise physiology and the psychology of performance, with its own investigation. Overlaps usefully with the biological approach in Psychology, and students often find that revising one strengthens the other rather than doubling the load.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Five content units, two written papers and a research project worth a quarter of the grade. Popular beside Psychology in Abu Dhabi humanities blocks, and the two fail identically: a concept stated correctly and never anchored to specific evidence.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Political concepts examined through a source booklet and extended responses, plus an engagement project. Shares Psychology's dependence on command terms, and students who master the verb ladder in one subject transfer it to the other almost immediately.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A source paper, comparative essays, a Higher Level regional option and a 2,200-word historical investigation. The argument discipline History demands is the same discipline the twenty-two-mark Psychology essay rewards, which makes the pairing efficient rather than heavy.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: Studied works, unseen literary analysis, an individual oral and a Higher Level essay. Relevant to Psychology in a practical way: both reward paragraphs that make a claim, evidence it and weigh it, and neither rewards fluent summary.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and financial mathematics. The statistics content maps directly onto the analysis criterion of the Psychology report, and students taking both should be using one to teach the other rather than treating them separately.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Offered at several levels across Abu Dhabi schools, and a mandatory subject alongside the licensed curriculum for the groups the regulations specify. sections.heading: What this search means, and why wording moves Psychology grades more than reading
paragraphs: A parent searching for an IB DP psychology home tutor in Abu Dhabi usually has a specific grievance: the child is interested, informed and getting a 5. The grievance is reasonable and the cause is almost always structural rather than intellectual. Psychology is marked on whether an answer did the operation the question specified, and students who have never been taught to separate the operations write the same essay for every verb.

Three documents make the diagnosis quick. A marked extended response shows which band the examiner placed the answer in and usually why. A marked short-answer question shows whether the student can produce a complete nine-mark answer or runs out after the description. And the report draft, if one exists, shows whether methodology is understood or borrowed. Twenty minutes with those three is worth more than an hour of conversation about how the subject is going.

What the diagnosis typically finds is one of four things. The student describes when asked to evaluate. The student evaluates without a study to evaluate, so the claims float. The student has studies but cannot name their methodological limitations, which is where most of the critical-thinking credit lives. Or the student can do all of it and cannot do it in the time, which is a technique problem rather than a knowledge one.

Each of those has a different fix and a different cost in hours. Describing instead of evaluating takes four or five marked essay cycles. Floating claims take a study bank, built once and reused. Missing methodological limitations is a vocabulary job and the fastest of the four. Timing is practice under the clock, which a tutor can structure but mostly cannot shortcut. Knowing which of the four you are dealing with is why the first session should produce a diagnosis rather than a lesson.

sections.heading: The command-term ladder, and what each rung is worth
paragraphs: The IB groups its command terms into three levels of demand, and the level sets the maximum an answer can earn. The first level asks the student to reproduce: define, describe, outline, state, identify. The second asks the student to do something with the material: explain, apply, analyse, distinguish, compare, contrast, compare and contrast. The third asks for a judgement that could have gone the other way: discuss, evaluate, examine, to what extent.

An extended response worth twenty-two marks almost always opens with a third-level term, and the credit is distributed accordingly. Knowledge and understanding of the material is necessary but bounded. The marks that lift an answer out of the middle bands come from the critical-thinking strand: methodological limitations of the studies cited, alternative explanations for the findings, the question of whether a result generalises beyond its sample, and a position taken and defended rather than a summary of views.

Students resist this for an understandable reason. Describing is safe, it demonstrates work, and it fills a page. Judgement feels like an invitation to be wrong. The teaching move that fixes it is not an explanation but a constraint: the student is required to finish every paragraph with a sentence that weighs something. Two or three essay cycles under that constraint and the habit sticks, because the band moves and the student can see it move.

Short-answer questions behave differently and are worth drilling separately. Nine marks will not accommodate a judgement, so the structure is tighter: the concept stated accurately, one study used to support it with enough procedural detail to count as evidence, and the link between the two made explicitly rather than implied. Students lose marks here by writing a long description of a famous study and never connecting it to the term in the question.

sections.heading: Three approaches, and what each one is examined on
paragraphs: The first paper is built on three approaches to behaviour, and students who organise their revision by approach rather than by topic find the paper considerably easier to sit. The biological approach deals with the relationship between physiology and behaviour: brain structures, neurotransmission, hormones and pheromones, and the genetic contribution. The cognitive approach deals with models of mental process: memory models, schema, thinking and decision-making, and the reliability of cognitive process including reconstructive memory and the effect of emotion.

The sociocultural approach deals with the social and cultural origins of behaviour: social identity, social cognitive theory, stereotypes, cultural dimensions and the transmission of behaviour. At Higher Level each approach carries an extension, and these are the parts most often taught last and revised least in a mixed-level classroom. In an Abu Dhabi cohort where one teacher runs both levels, the extensions are a reasonable first question for a parent to ask about.

Running underneath all three is research methodology, which is examined in the papers as well as assessed in the report. Students are expected to know which methods suit which questions, what the sampling techniques are and what each one costs in terms of representativeness, how bias enters through the researcher and through the participant, and what ethical obligations apply. This is examinable content in its own right and it is also the source of most critical-thinking marks in essays about any approach.

The practical revision structure that works is a grid: approach down one axis, and for each cell the concept, two studies, each study's method, each study's main methodological limitation, and one ethical consideration. Built once in DP1 and maintained, it answers short-answer questions directly and supplies evidence for extended responses in any of the three approaches. Built in the fortnight before the examination, it is a list of names.
