sections.heading: The methodology paper and the vocabulary Higher Level students skip
paragraphs: Higher Level students sit an additional paper built on an unseen passage describing a piece of research. The questions are short and they are about the research rather than about psychology: what method was used and why, what the sampling approach costs the study, what ethical considerations arise, how credible the findings are, and how far they can be generalised. Students who have treated methodology as background reading find this paper unexpectedly hard, because none of it can be recalled from content revision.

The vocabulary is finite and learnable, which is the good news. Methods: experimental, quasi-experimental, correlational, case study, observation, interview, focus group. Sampling: random, opportunity, purposive, self-selected, snowball, with the trade-off between convenience and representativeness attached to each. Bias: researcher bias, participant expectancy, demand characteristics, social desirability. Credibility, triangulation and the several senses in which a finding may or may not generalise.

The paper rewards precision with those terms rather than general sensible comment. A student who writes that the sample was small and therefore the study is unreliable has said something true and earned little. A student who identifies an opportunity sample drawn from a single institution, explains that this limits generalisation to populations sharing that institution's characteristics, and names what a different sampling approach would have cost in practical terms has answered the question that was asked.

Two or three sessions on this vocabulary move marks on the methodology paper and on every essay in the other two papers, because methodological criticism is where the critical-thinking credit lives throughout the course. It is the highest-leverage content in the subject and the least likely to be covered properly in a small mixed-level class with a crowded year.

sections.heading: Building a study bank that survives a twenty-two-mark question
paragraphs: Most students carry studies as names with a gist attached. That is enough to recognise a question and not enough to answer one. An extended response needs studies used as evidence, which means the student can state the aim, describe enough of the procedure for the reader to see why the finding follows, give the finding accurately, and then say something critical about how it was obtained.

The practical form is a single-page record per study with five fields: aim, participants and how they were obtained, procedure in three sentences, findings, and one methodological limitation with its consequence stated. The fifth field is the one students leave out and the one that earns the marks, because a limitation named without a consequence is a label rather than an evaluation.

How many studies are needed is less than students fear and more than they usually hold properly. Two well-known studies per content area, held to that standard, cover the short-answer questions and supply evidence for extended responses across the paper. Twenty studies held as names is worse than eight held to the five-field standard, and it takes longer to assemble. The economy here is real and it is worth explaining to a student who is trying to read everything.

The bank also does the work on the second paper. Option topics draw on their own studies, but the evaluation moves are the same: sampling, ecological validity, cultural specificity, the gap between a laboratory task and the behaviour it stands in for. A student who has internalised those moves in the context of the three approaches applies them to option material without being taught again.

sections.heading: The experimental report: a replication, four criteria and a word range
paragraphs: The internally assessed component is a report on an experimental study the student has conducted, normally a simple replication or modification of a published experiment. It is marked against four criteria covering the introduction, the exploration of the design, the analysis of the results and the evaluation, totalling twenty-two marks, and it sits inside a defined word range. Confirm the current range and your school's internal deadline with the Diploma coordinator rather than relying on any figure from a tutoring page.

The failure that costs most is choosing a study that cannot be replicated by a school student with classmates as participants. If the original required equipment, clinical populations, deception that would not be permitted, or a timescale longer than a term, the replication will be a distortion and the introduction will struggle to justify it. That decision is made in a single conversation, early, and it is the highest-value hour anyone will spend on this component.

The second failure is the analysis. Students either apply a statistical test they do not understand or avoid statistics entirely and describe the means. The criterion rewards an appropriate test, correctly applied, with the result interpreted in terms of the hypothesis rather than announced. A student taking a mathematics course with statistics in it already has the tools; the job is connecting two subjects they have been taught separately.

The third is the evaluation, which students write as general reflection. The criterion wants the design, the sample and the procedure assessed specifically, with modifications proposed that would address the weaknesses identified, not a paragraph about how the experiment went well other than a few problems. The pattern that earns the band is: this specific feature of the design limited this specific inference, and here is what would have been done differently and why.

sections.heading: Ethics for a student researcher in this emirate: what cannot be run
paragraphs: Students design replications without thinking about who the participants will be, and in practice they will be classmates, which means minors at a school licensed and inspected by ADEK. That changes what is possible. Informed consent has to be obtained properly, with the school's involvement and in the form the school requires. The right to withdraw has to be real and stated before participation rather than mentioned afterwards. Debriefing is not optional. Anonymity has to be designed into the data collection rather than promised in the write-up.

Some study designs are simply unavailable to a school student and it is better to discover that in the first conversation than in the third week. Anything requiring deception beyond the mildest, anything that could cause distress, anything touching on clinical conditions, anything involving data about identifiable individuals that a student would then hold on a personal device. A replication that cannot be run ethically is not a replication worth proposing, and the introduction will be unable to justify it.

Data handling deserves a specific mention because students rarely consider it. The UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs personal data generally, and the sensible student practice is to collect no more than the design needs, to separate any identifying information from the responses at the point of collection, and to have a plan for deleting what was gathered once the report is submitted. Schools increasingly ask about this, and a student who has thought about it looks like a researcher rather than like a candidate.

The useful framing for a tutor session is that ethics is a design constraint rather than a paperwork exercise. Every ethical requirement narrows the design space, and a student who designs inside the constraints from the start produces a study that is both permissible and defensible in the exploration criterion. One that designs freely and then bolts on consent forms produces a report with a visible seam in it.

sections.heading: Diploma Psychology in Abu Dhabi schools, and the option the department chose
paragraphs: ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in this emirate and publishes inspection ratings for them. Those ratings describe schools rather than departments, so they will not tell you whether the Psychology teaching is strong. The questions that will are specific: how many students sit the subject this year, whether both levels share a room, which option topic the department has chosen, how many cohorts have sat that option, and whether anonymised past reports at different mark bands can be seen.

The option question matters more than families expect. The second paper is set entirely on the option or options the school teaches, and the choice is a department decision. A tutor who has taught one option through several cohorts is a specialist for those students and a generalist for everyone else. This is the first thing to establish and it costs one email.

Mandatory UAE subjects sit alongside the Diploma for the groups the regulations specify, and they are a real constraint on a Psychology student's week rather than a footnote. Dubai's regulator requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction. The federal position is that private schools must follow Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their own curriculum. Abu Dhabi families should confirm the local requirement with the school, and should count those hours when planning how many tutoring sessions a week is realistic.

On the national picture, the regulator map is worth knowing because families move. Dubai sits with KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain with ADEK, Sharjah with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any of them, nor from the IB, and claims none; they are named to explain who governs what.

sections.heading: Where Psychology leads after the Diploma, and what to check first
paragraphs: Psychology sits in the individuals and societies group rather than in the sciences, and that single fact causes more admissions confusion than anything else in the subject. Some university psychology courses treat it as a relevant subject and ask for a laboratory science alongside it. Others accept it as the science-adjacent subject in its own right. A few do not count it either way. The variation is at course level rather than institution level, so the only reliable method is to read each course's own entry profile.

For students staying in the region, Khalifa University, New York University Abu Dhabi, Zayed University, United Arab Emirates University and Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi each publish their own requirements, and those requirements change. For overseas applications the pattern to watch is whether a course wants mathematics at a particular level, since psychology degrees are more quantitative than school psychology suggests and several courses specify it.

Certificate equivalency through the Ministry of Education is a separate process from university admission and is often conflated with it. The published British-track rules are specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count of five, plus either one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with at least 450 in SAT Mathematics. No IB points threshold appears in the source we verified, so check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority rather than taking a figure from any tutoring page.

One thing worth saying plainly: tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for progressing through the Diploma. Pages that imply otherwise are inventing urgency about a regulatory process. What tutoring can do is move marks on named components, and the honest sales argument stops there.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and the specific temptation in Psychology coursework
paragraphs: Every subject in this set has an honesty section, and in Psychology the temptation has a recognisable shape. A replication produces a result that does not match the original, the student concludes the experiment failed, and the pressure arrives to adjust the data or to write the discussion as though the expected result had appeared. Both are academic misconduct and both are unnecessary, because a replication that does not reproduce the original finding is entirely normal and the criteria do not reward the result.

What the criteria reward is the quality of the reasoning about the result. A student whose findings diverge and who can explain plausibly why, in terms of the sample, the procedure, the operationalisation or the context, is demonstrating exactly what the evaluation criterion asks for. The student who reports a tidy confirmation with no reflection has produced a weaker report. This is worth telling a student explicitly and early, because the fear of a null result drives a lot of poor decisions in the final fortnight.

The tutor boundary is the same as everywhere else in the Diploma and worth stating in full. A tutor may teach methodology, explain what a criterion asks for, question a design before data is collected, read a student's own draft and say where a claim is unevidenced, explain a statistical test, and ask the questions that make a student revise. A tutor may not supply text, perform the analysis, rewrite a section into its final form, or produce any part of the assessed work. One site in the competitor research sells completed internal assessments outright; the consequence of buying one falls on the student.

Ask any provider for their written position on coursework before booking hours, and read the answer for what it describes rather than for how it sounds. A provider who talks about integrity in general while offering a service that returns completed drafts has answered the question. A provider who states which specific actions they will refuse has given you something useful to compare.

sections.heading: What Psychology support costs in the Abu Dhabi market, and how lessons run
paragraphs: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online across the UAE run roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with IB specialists quoted from about AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards, and in-home visits at roughly AED 180-500 because travel is carried inside the hour. Those bands come from published provider pages and from Bestimate's Dubai rate table, read in October 2026. They describe the market and are not an IB Gram price list.

In this subject the distinction that matters is whether marking is inside the rate. Psychology improves through marked essays, and a provider whose hourly rate covers lesson time only is selling something different from one whose rate includes reading a timed extended response against the published criteria and naming the band. Compare those two quotes as though they were the same product and the cheaper one will look better than it is.

On delivery, the position stated plainly: every UAE lesson is one-to-one and online, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Abu Dhabi, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The practical gain is tutor choice. A family in Al Falah or Al Samha selects from the same pool of specialists in their option topic as a family in Al Khalidiyah, rather than from whoever is prepared to make the drive.

Scheduling in this emirate deserves one note. The useful study window for essay work is narrow, and it moves. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the productive hours shift late, so a standing slot usually moves to after Iftar for that period. Internal coursework deadlines cluster before the long weekends and the Eid breaks. Because there is no travel to rearrange, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation, and a report block timed properly against those dates is worth more than the same hours spread evenly through a term.

process.title: Send three documents, not a description
process.description: One marked extended response, one marked short-answer question and the report draft if it exists. Those three show whether the problem is the command term, the evidence base, the methodology vocabulary or the clock. A description of how the subject is going cannot distinguish between them.

process.title: Confirm the option topic and the level
process.description: The second paper is set on the option the department chose, and the Higher Level extensions may or may not have been taught yet. One email to the Diploma coordinator settles both, and both decide which tutors can actually help. Send the answers with the enquiry.

process.title: Free trial with an essay open
process.description: The trial is held by the tutor who would take the slot, with the student's own marked essay on the screen. It ends by naming the band the work currently sits in and the specific move that reaches the band above. If that statement is general, the honest conclusion is not to book.

process.title: Buy marking cycles, not lessons
process.description: The purchase that moves Psychology marks is a cycle: timed essay before the session, marked against the criteria, session spent on the gap. Agree how many cycles, what is included, and the date on which somebody reports whether the band has moved.

process.title: Report block timed to the internal deadline
process.description: Coursework hours work against the school's internal date rather than anything external, and the design and ethics conversation has to happen before any data is collected. Book the block early; the conversation that saves a report is the first one, not the last.

whyPoints.title: Essays marked against the published criteria
whyPoints.description: Written work is marked with the band named and the specific move to the next band stated. A comment that says the essay was good is not feedback. In a subject where the command term sets the ceiling, naming the band is the only honest way to show whether anything changed.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the option, which is checkable
whyPoints.description: The second paper is set entirely on the option the department chose. We tell you which option the tutor has taught and for how many cohorts, because a Psychology specialist for the wrong option is a well-read generalist. Ask every provider the same question.

whyPoints.title: Ethics treated as part of the teaching
whyPoints.description: Consent, right to withdraw, debriefing, anonymity and data handling are design constraints, and the exploration criterion rewards a student who designed inside them. We raise them in the first coursework conversation rather than after the data has been collected the wrong way.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches method, explains criteria, questions a design and comments on the student's own draft. A tutor does not supply text, run the analysis or produce assessed work. The boundary is published because a market in finished coursework exists alongside this one.

whyPoints.title: No regulator borrowed as a credential
whyPoints.description: ADEK licenses and inspects private schools in this emirate; other emirates sit with KHDA, SPEA, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge or the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of them, nor from the IB, and claims none.

whyPoints.title: Figures that carry a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to a named published source read in October 2026, and no statistic about our own results appears anywhere, because we could not produce the underlying data for one. A number without a source is a number nobody can check.

faqs.question: Which command terms does IB Psychology use, and why do they decide the mark?
faqs.answer: The IB groups command terms into three levels of demand. Define, describe, outline and state ask for reproduction. Explain, apply, analyse and compare and contrast ask the student to do something with the material. Discuss, evaluate, examine and to what extent ask for a judgement. The level sets the ceiling: a description written in answer to a question beginning discuss is capped in the middle bands however well it is written. This is why a student who knows the content can keep receiving a 5, and why the fastest fix is marked essay cycles rather than more reading.

faqs.question: Why does my child score a 5 on essays despite knowing all the studies?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the marks that lift an answer out of the middle bands are in the critical-thinking strand, not in the content. That strand wants methodological limitations of the studies cited, alternative explanations for the findings, a view on whether a result generalises beyond its sample, and a position taken rather than a summary of views. A student who writes accurate content and never weighs it has done the first half of the task. The reliable fix is a constraint: every paragraph must end with a sentence that weighs something. Two or three essay cycles under that rule usually moves the band.

faqs.question: How many psychological studies does my child actually need to know by name?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most students try to carry, held to a higher standard. Two well-known studies per content area is normally enough, provided each one is held with five things: the aim, who the participants were and how they were obtained, three sentences of procedure, the findings, and one methodological limitation with its consequence stated. Twenty studies held as names and gists is worse than eight held that way, because names cannot be used as evidence. The fifth field is the one students omit and the one that earns the critical-thinking marks.

faqs.question: What is the third paper that Higher Level Psychology students sit?
faqs.answer: It is built on an unseen passage describing a piece of research, and the short questions are about the research rather than about psychology: which method was used and why, what the sampling approach costs the study, what ethical issues arise, how credible the findings are and how far they generalise. None of it can be recalled from content revision, which is why students who treated methodology as background reading find it hard. The vocabulary is finite and two or three focused sessions on it also lift the critical-thinking marks on the other papers.

faqs.question: What is the word range for the Psychology internal assessment report?
faqs.answer: The report sits inside a defined range specified in the subject guide, and it is marked against four criteria covering the introduction, the exploration of the design, the analysis of results and the evaluation, totalling twenty-two marks. Confirm the exact current range with your school's Diploma coordinator rather than relying on a figure from any tutoring page, including this one, because guides are revised. The more useful planning number is the school's internal deadline, which normally sits months ahead of anything external and is what the data collection has to be scheduled against.

faqs.question: Can my child run a psychology experiment on classmates at an Abu Dhabi school?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, within real constraints, and those constraints should shape the design from the start. Participants will be minors at a school licensed and inspected by ADEK, so informed consent has to be obtained in the form the school requires, the right to withdraw has to be stated before participation, debriefing is not optional, and anonymity has to be built into the data collection. Designs involving meaningful deception, potential distress, clinical conditions or identifiable personal data held on a student's own device are not available. Settle this in the first conversation, not the third week.

faqs.question: What goes wrong in the analysis section of a Psychology report?
faqs.answer: Two things, in roughly equal measure. Some students apply a statistical test they do not understand, which the criterion does not reward because the interpretation gives it away. Others avoid statistics entirely, describe the means and stop. What earns the band is an appropriate test, correctly applied, with the result interpreted against the hypothesis rather than announced. A student taking a mathematics course with statistics in it already holds the tools and has simply never been shown that the two subjects connect, which is a quick fix in one or two sessions.

faqs.question: Our replication did not produce the original finding. Has the report failed?
faqs.answer: No, and this is worth telling a student early because the fear of it drives poor decisions in the final fortnight. Replications frequently diverge, and the criteria do not reward the result. What they reward is reasoning about the result: a student who can explain plausibly why their findings differ, in terms of the sample, the procedure, the operationalisation or the context, is doing exactly what the evaluation criterion asks. A tidy confirmation with no reflection is the weaker report. Adjusting data to match an expectation is academic misconduct and entirely unnecessary.

faqs.question: Which Psychology option topic has my child's school chosen?
faqs.answer: Ask the department, because it is their decision and it determines the whole second paper. The option is chosen at school level from a small set, and at Higher Level more than one may be taught. This is the single most important question to settle before matching a tutor, since someone who has taught one option through several cohorts may be of limited use for another. A provider who books you in without asking has told you something about how closely they match. One email answers it.

faqs.question: Does Psychology count as a science for university applications?
faqs.answer: It depends on the course rather than on the university, and the variation is wide. In the Diploma, Psychology sits in the individuals and societies group, not the sciences. Some university psychology courses accept it as the relevant subject, others require a laboratory science alongside it, and competitive medicine and health science routes generally expect named sciences at Higher Level with Psychology as an additional subject. Several psychology degrees also specify mathematics, because the discipline is more quantitative than school psychology suggests. Read each course's own entry profile before the level choices lock.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the experimental report without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful help is substantial. A tutor may teach research methods, explain what each criterion asks for in plain language, question the choice of study and the design before any data is collected, explain a statistical test, read the student's own draft and point out where a claim is unevidenced, and ask the questions that prompt a revision. What a tutor may not do is supply text, perform the analysis, rewrite a section into final form, or produce any part of the assessed work. Ask for that boundary in writing before booking.

faqs.question: How do Abu Dhabi school term dates affect Psychology revision planning?
faqs.answer: More than families expect, because this subject improves through written work produced between sessions rather than during them. Internal coursework deadlines in the emirate's schools tend to cluster before the long weekends and the Eid breaks, which means data collection for the report has to be scheduled around those gaps rather than through them. Mandatory UAE subjects sit alongside the Diploma for the groups the regulations specify, and those hours are real; count them when deciding how many essays a week is honestly achievable rather than planning on paper time nobody has.

faqs.question: What does Diploma Psychology tutoring cost in the Abu Dhabi market?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor working online across the UAE is quoted roughly AED 150-300 an hour, IB specialists from about AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards, and in-home visits roughly AED 180-500 because travel is inside the hour. Those bands come from published provider pages and Bestimate's Dubai rate table, read in October 2026, and they are the market rather than our prices. In this subject the question that matters is whether marking is inside the rate, since Psychology improves through marked essays and a lesson-only hour is a different product.

faqs.question: Can Psychology sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families in this emirate ask for it. School hours shorten, the productive study window shifts late, and the 4.30pm slot that worked in January is the worst hour available in March. Because lessons are online there is no travel to rearrange, so moving a standing slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation. The same flexibility applies around the long weekends and the Eid breaks. For a subject whose progress depends on essays written between sessions, protecting the slot at a workable hour matters more than the hour itself.

faqs.question: What happens if no Abu Dhabi-based Psychology specialist is free at our hour?
faqs.answer: We say so, and offer the slot with a tutor based elsewhere who teaches the same specification and the same option topic, at the same rate, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The Diploma Psychology teaching population inside the UAE is small and the option topics divide it further, so in a given week there may be nobody free at 5pm on a Tuesday. Where the option cannot be covered properly, saying the slot is unavailable is a better answer than substituting a generalist at specialist money. No researched competitor in this cluster discloses a coverage limit.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-psychology-home-tutor.closingHeading: Send a marked essay and we will tell you which band it sits in
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-psychology-home-tutor.closingBody: One marked extended response, one marked short answer and the option topic from your school's Diploma coordinator are enough to say whether the problem is the command term, the evidence base, the methodology vocabulary or the clock. Those four need different numbers of hours and different kinds of tutor, so the diagnosis is worth more than a lesson. The trial that follows is free and is held by the tutor who would take the slot, with your child's own work on screen. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one online over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not make home visits in the UAE.

intro.heading: What an Abu Dhabi family is really asking when they ask the price
paragraphs: Almost every Abu Dhabi parent who contacts us about IB Diploma Psychology opens with the same question, phrased as a price. They want to know what an IB DP Psychology tutor in Abu Dhabi costs. Underneath that question sits a harder one: how many hours of somebody's time this actually takes, and whether the number quoted reflects teaching or logistics. The two are routinely confused. A quote of AED 400 an hour for a tutor who drives from Khalifa City to Saadiyat Island contains a fee for Psychology and a fee for the Sheikh Khalifa Bridge at rush hour, and nobody itemises which is which.

This page itemises it. Market rates in the emirate, as read from published provider pages in October 2026, run from about AED 45 an hour for an undergraduate tutor working online to AED 650 an hour for a premium named tutor. Those are other people's published figures, attributed below, not ours. The spread is enormous because the label 'Psychology tutor' covers a first-year undergraduate who finished the course two years ago and a teacher who has marked several hundred Paper 1 short-answer responses against the real mark bands. Those two people are not selling the same hour.

Six things move an Abu Dhabi quote, and only one of them is the subject. Whether the student sits Higher or Standard Level changes the number of examined components from three to four. Whether the internal assessment is at proposal, data-collection or write-up stage changes whether the tutor is teaching content or supervising a 2,200-word report. The distance between the student's community and the tutor's determines whether travel is being billed. The weeks remaining before the May session change availability more than they change price. Group size changes the rate per student. Permit status changes who is legally able to take the booking at all.

Our model removes the travel variable entirely rather than discounting it. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Abu Dhabi, and there are no home visits in the emirate; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Everything for UAE families happens live, one to one, over video, with a shared screen for annotated past-paper responses. The practical consequence for a family in Al Reef or Yas Island is that the pool of available Psychology specialists stops being 'whoever can reach us by 4.30pm' and becomes 'whoever is free at 4.30pm Gulf Standard Time'.

The rest of the page is written to be used rather than skimmed. There is an AED rate table by component, a provider-model comparison showing who carries the permit obligation, a cost-in-context table that puts tuition next to an Abu Dhabi school fee, and a breakdown of where Psychology marks are actually gained and lost across Paper 1, Paper 2, Paper 3 and the IA. Every regulatory statement names its source. Every figure carries the date we read it.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.programmesIntro: Psychology belongs to Group 3 of the Diploma Programme, but Abu Dhabi students arrive at it from several different starting points. The three programmes below are the ones that feed DP Psychology classes in the emirate, and each produces a different gap in the first term.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Psychology sits in the individuals and societies group and is examined by written papers plus one internally assessed experimental report. Standard Level students sit two papers; Higher Level students sit three and study additional content across the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches. The subject looks deceptively readable, which is why so many students arrive in DP2 with good notes and weak command-term discipline.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi DP cohorts are unusually mixed in prior schooling, because families move into the emirate mid-cycle from British, American, CBSE and francophone systems. A student who joins DP1 in October has often never written a 9-mark short-answer response to a command term, and that single skill carries more marks in Paper 1 than any content topic.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP individuals and societies is assessed against four criteria using task-specific clarifications rather than examination mark bands. Students learn to investigate and communicate, which transfers well, and learn to write at length against descriptors, which transfers badly to a timed 22-mark Psychology essay. The MYP to DP step in this subject is mostly a step in assessment literacy.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run MYP through Year 11 and then offer the Diploma, so the transition happens inside one building and parents assume continuity. The first set of DP1 Psychology marks is frequently the moment that assumption breaks. A short block of work on command terms and essay structure in the autumn of DP1 is cheaper than the same work in February of DP2.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. A CP student may take DP Psychology as one of their Diploma courses and sit exactly the same papers, under the same criteria, as a full Diploma candidate. The difference is the surrounding load, not the standard of the subject.
programmes.countryNote: CP is still thin on the ground in Abu Dhabi compared with the full Diploma, which means a CP student taking Psychology often has no classmate on the same pathway and little peer reference for pacing. One-to-one support becomes the comparison point they do not otherwise have, particularly for judging how long a 22-mark essay should take under exam conditions.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.subjectsIntro: Psychology is rarely the only subject in the conversation. These are the Group 3 and adjacent courses Abu Dhabi families most often combine with it, with the specific pressure point each one brings to a Diploma timetable.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Three approaches to behaviour, options chosen by the school, research methods throughout, and one experimental report. Marks are lost on command terms, on using a study without using its findings, and on evaluation that lists limitations instead of weighing them against the claim being made.

subjects.name: Psychology internal assessment
subjects.levels: HL and SL, 20-25% of the grade
subjects.description: A replication of a simple published experiment, written up to a 2,200-word ceiling and marked out of 22 across criteria A to D. The commonest avoidable loss is in criterion C, where students report a statistic without stating what it means for the hypothesis they set.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Shares the biological approach's territory on neurotransmission, hormones and genetics, which helps, and competes for the same revision evenings, which does not. Students taking both often write Psychology answers that are too physiological and skip the behavioural claim the question asked about.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A frequent Group 3 pairing in Abu Dhabi because of family business and finance interests. Both subjects reward applied evidence, but Business rewards a recommendation while Psychology rewards a judgement about evidence quality. Blurring the two costs evaluation marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Taken alongside Psychology by students heading for behavioural economics or management degrees. The diagram-and-definition discipline of Economics transfers usefully to Psychology terminology, though Economics essay structure is looser than a Psychology 22-mark response needs.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Overlaps with the sociocultural approach on identity, conformity and group behaviour. Students who take both have a genuine advantage on sociocultural questions, provided they keep political theory out of a Psychology answer that needs a named study and its findings.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The human sciences are a standing TOK example, and Psychology students have the best material in the cohort for it. Working the two together saves hours: a tutor can use the same methodological critique for a Psychology evaluation paragraph and a TOK exhibition commentary.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Psychology
subjects.description: A popular choice in Abu Dhabi because the reading is accessible, which is exactly why it goes wrong. A good Psychology essay needs a narrow question answerable from published studies. Supervision here is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts, never authorship of any part of the text.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Shares the analytical-paragraph habit Psychology needs, but trains a student to interpret rather than to cite. The transfer is worth making explicit in a session: Psychology wants the study, the finding, and then the inference, in that order.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Carries the statistics that make the Psychology IA tractable. Students on this route generally handle measures of central tendency and a test of significance comfortably; students on Analysis and Approaches often need the applied statistics explained once, properly, before IA data collection.

sections.heading: The six variables that move an Abu Dhabi Psychology quote
paragraphs: Level comes first. Higher Level Psychology adds a third written paper and extra content across all three approaches, so an HL plan usually runs more weeks than an SL plan rather than costing more per hour. Parents often expect the reverse, and then find a quote that looks identical to the SL quote and assume the tutor has misunderstood. They have not. The hourly rate reflects the tutor; the total reflects the number of components.

Stage of the internal assessment comes second, and it is the single biggest swing. A tutor asked to teach content for an hour a week is doing one job. A tutor supervising a replication study, from choosing a simple published experiment through operationalising variables to a 2,200-word write-up, is reading drafts between sessions and returning comments mapped to criteria A to D. Providers that price those the same are either underpricing the second or overpricing the first.

The other four are proximity, timing, group size and permit status. Proximity only has a price if somebody is driving, which is why it disappears from an online quote. Timing changes availability rather than rate: in the eight weeks before the May session, the specialists with free evening slots on Gulf Standard Time are the constraint, not the money. Group size divides attention and the rate with it. Permit status determines who can lawfully take the booking at all, and that belongs in a separate section of this page because it is a legal question rather than a pricing one.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against a tutor in the living room, priced honestly
paragraphs: Home tutoring is a real market in Abu Dhabi and it exists for a real reason: some students concentrate better with another person physically present, and some families prefer a lesson they can see from the kitchen. It is worth saying what it costs and what it gives up, because the honest comparison makes the case better than a sales argument would. Published in-home rates in the emirate run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150 to AED 450 online for a comparable specialist, and the difference is travel rather than teaching.

What in-home buys is presence. What it costs, beyond the surcharge, is the size of the pool. A family in Al Shamkha choosing from tutors willing to drive out there in the late afternoon is choosing from a handful of people, few of whom will have taught DP Psychology options to examination. The same family choosing online is choosing from every specialist free at that hour. For a subject where the marks sit in command-term discipline and evaluation structure rather than in content coverage, specialism is worth more than proximity.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in the UAE, and there are no home visits in Abu Dhabi: in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. That is a limit on what we sell, stated plainly, and it is also why our Abu Dhabi matches are not constrained by a drive time. Lessons run over live video with a shared screen, which has one concrete advantage for this subject: a marked Paper 1 response can be annotated in front of the student and saved, so the same error is not made twice.

sections.heading: Where Psychology marks are gained and lost, component by component
paragraphs: Psychology rewards precision about evidence, and penalises fluent writing that never commits to a claim. Standard Level candidates sit two written papers plus the internal assessment. Higher Level candidates sit three written papers plus the internal assessment, with additional content and a paper built on an unseen description of a study. The weightings in the table below follow the subject guide in force for the current cohort; confirm them with your child's Diploma coordinator, because the IB revises guides on a rolling cycle and a stale weighting is worse than none.

Paper 1 is where the most marks are casually given away. The short-answer questions on the three approaches are command-term exercises: outline wants something different from explain, and describe wants something different again. Students who revise content and ignore command terms write good paragraphs that score in the middle band. The extended response in the second section needs a named study, its actual findings, and then an inference drawn from those findings. Many answers stop at the second step and lose the evaluation marks entirely.

Paper 2 and the Higher Level Paper 3 fail for different reasons. Paper 2 option essays fail on breadth: three studies mentioned in passing score lower than two studies used properly. Paper 3 fails on reading: the questions ask about the research described in the stimulus, not about research in general, and an answer that ignores the method actually used in the passage cannot access the upper bands. Both are coachable in a handful of sessions because both are structural rather than content gaps.

sections.heading: The internal assessment: 22 marks, four criteria, one word ceiling
paragraphs: The Psychology internal assessment is a replication of a simple published experiment, written up as a report with a 2,200-word ceiling and marked out of 22 marks across four criteria. Criterion A covers the introduction, criterion B the exploration of method and design, criterion C the analysis, and criterion D the evaluation. Naming the criteria by letter matters because the mark sheet a teacher completes is organised that way, and a student who has never seen it writes to a structure nobody is marking.

The predictable losses are the same every year. In criterion A, students summarise a study at length and never state a hypothesis in operationalised terms, so the introduction does not justify the investigation that follows. In criterion C, they report a measure of central tendency and a test of significance without saying what either means for the hypothesis. In criterion D, they list limitations as a checklist rather than weighing which of them actually threatens the conclusion. Each of those is a structural habit, and each can be fixed in one session with a draft on the screen.

There is a hard boundary on what any tutor may do here, and we state it to the student in the first session rather than burying it in terms and conditions. A tutor teaches method, explains statistics, asks questions about a draft the student has written, and returns comments mapped to the criterion letters. A tutor does not author any part of the submitted report, does not supply text to paste in, and does not hand over a finished investigation. Providers in this market that sell completed coursework are selling an academic-integrity breach that lands on the student, not on them.

sections.heading: Ethics and consent: what an Abu Dhabi Psychology student may actually run
paragraphs: Psychology is the one Diploma subject where the internal assessment involves other people, and that changes what is permissible. Participants must give informed consent, must be able to withdraw, must be debriefed, and must not be deceived in any way that could cause distress. Replications involving minors, clinical populations or sensitive personal data are generally ruled out before they start. These are IB requirements, applied through the school's own ethics procedure, and the school signs off before data collection begins.

In Abu Dhabi there is a further practical layer. Most students recruit participants from their own school, which means the school's permission is not a formality but the gatekeeper for the whole project. Schools licensed by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, apply their own safeguarding rules on top of the IB's, and those rules vary between institutions. A student who designs a study in October and asks for approval in January has often designed something the school will not allow, and loses weeks replacing it.

The sequence that works is unglamorous: pick a simple, well-documented experiment first, check it against the school's ethics requirements second, and only then write the proposal. A tutor's job in that sequence is to say which experiments replicate cleanly at sixth-form scale, which statistical test the design implies, and where a proposal will meet an obstacle. The approval itself belongs to the school, and no tutoring provider can grant, speed up or guarantee it.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Examination boards work further ahead than families expect, and the deadline that catches people out is never the examination itself. Cambridge International's published key dates for its March 2027 series make the pattern plain: the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, but final entries were due on 27 November 2026 and forecast grades on 27 February 2027. That is a board asking for commitments months before a paper is sat, and the IB operates on the same logic through the school rather than directly with parents.

For IB dates specifically, we publish no exam or results date on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so every date in circulation is second-hand, and a wrong date on a page like this costs a family more than a missing one. The reliable source is your child's Diploma coordinator, who holds the school's own internal deadline calendar: IA submission dates, Extended Essay checkpoints, the mock window and the upload deadlines that sit weeks before anything the IB publishes.

What a tutor can do is work backwards from whatever that calendar says. Internal assessment drafts need to exist well before the school's internal deadline, which itself sits well before the IB's. Timed-paper practice needs to start early enough that there is time to repeat the exercise after marking, which means a minimum of two attempts per component. Revision of Paper 2 options needs to be sequenced around the mock window rather than crammed after it. None of that requires knowing a published examination date; it requires knowing the school's.

sections.heading: Permits, ADEK ethics and who may lawfully tutor your child in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a parent paying for lessons in Abu Dhabi should know what that means. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. According to u.ae, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists the application route through its smart app, website and e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time and no fee.

The consequence for a family is a question worth asking out loud. u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here, and any provider quoting one is guessing. What you can do is ask a prospective tutor whether they hold the permit. Because it costs nothing and takes days, there is no good reason for a working tutor not to have one.

Abu Dhabi adds a layer that Dubai does not. Gulf News has reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students from their own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document here, so verify it against the current ADEK publication before relying on it. The practical point stands either way: 'your child's own teacher, privately' is not a service a family in this emirate should be offered. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and nothing on this page should be read as implying otherwise.

sections.heading: Tuition cost in context, and what equivalency actually requires
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means little without something to compare it to. Dubai's regulator, KHDA, confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in that emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Abu Dhabi's fee regime is set separately by ADEK, so that announcement does not apply here, and the current fee position for any Abu Dhabi school should be read from the school and from adek.gov.ae. The reason the comparison matters is proportion: weekly tuition across a two-year Diploma is a material commitment next to a school fee, and it should be planned as one rather than booked by the hour indefinitely.

The second piece of context is what a Diploma is for locally. Students intending to study at a UAE university generally need their certificate recognised through the Ministry of Education's equivalency process. For the British track, the published requirements are specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with at least 450 in SAT Mathematics.

For the Diploma itself, no points threshold is published here, because none has been read on a Ministry of Education source. One ranking competitor publishes a subject count for IGCSE that contradicts the figure above, which is a useful reminder to check the authority rather than the agency. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs; IB Gram does not perform it, speed it up or guarantee any outcome in it, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae before making any decision that depends on them.

whyPoints.description: Annotated past-paper responses are saved from the shared screen, session notes name the command terms practised, and IA feedback is written by criterion letter. The record is what makes a review conversation about marks rather than about impressions.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP Psychology tutor in Abu Dhabi charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates read from providers' own pages in October 2026 put a qualified DP subject specialist at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour online, rising to about AED 200 to AED 450 for Higher Level and internal assessment supervision. Published in-home rates in the emirate run higher, roughly AED 180 to AED 500, because they include travel. Budget and undergraduate tutors advertise from around AED 45 to AED 150 online. Premium named tutors publish up to AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, attributed and dated. IB Gram quotes its own terms after a free first lesson rather than publishing a tariff.

faqs.question: Why is Psychology IA supervision priced higher than ordinary weekly lessons?
faqs.answer: Because the booked hour is not the only hour. Supervising a replication study means reading a draft before the session, checking whether the hypothesis is operationalised, confirming the statistical test suits the design, and writing comments mapped to criteria A to D afterwards. A content lesson has no work either side of it. Any provider charging the same for both is either underpricing the supervision or overpricing the teaching. Expect an IA block to be four to six sessions spread over six to ten weeks, with the heaviest preparation around the proposal and the first full draft.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Psychology cost more per hour than Standard Level in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Usually not. The hourly figure reflects the tutor's specialism, and that is the same person teaching either level. What changes is the number of components: Higher Level adds a third written paper and extra content across the three approaches, so a Higher Level plan typically runs more weeks. Parents expecting an HL premium sometimes read an identical rate as a mistake. It is not. If you are budgeting, work from total sessions across the Diploma rather than from the hourly figure, and ask the tutor to map sessions to components.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Psychology tutor to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. There are no home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one to one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for annotated past-paper work. The practical gain is the size of the tutor pool: instead of choosing from specialists willing to drive to your community in the late afternoon, you choose from everyone free at that hour. For a subject where marks turn on command-term discipline, that trade favours specialism.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Abu Dhabi need a MoHRE permit, and should I ask for it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by MoHRE. u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, and that individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any figure you see as unverified. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services. Since it costs nothing, a working tutor has no reason not to hold one.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school Psychology teacher tutor them privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: You should not be offered that. Gulf News has reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also prohibits serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it on adek.gov.ae before relying on the exact wording. The safer route is a specialist with no connection to the school, which also removes any conflict over marking internal work.

faqs.question: What is the word limit on the DP Psychology internal assessment?
faqs.answer: The report is written to a 2,200-word ceiling and marked out of 22 marks across four criteria: A for the introduction, B for the exploration of method and design, C for the analysis, and D for the evaluation. Going over the ceiling costs marks without adding any. Most over-length drafts we see are long in the introduction and short in the analysis, which is the wrong way round for the mark allocation. Confirm the current ceiling and criterion marks with your child's teacher, since the IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle.

faqs.question: Where do Abu Dhabi students lose the most marks in Psychology Paper 1?
faqs.answer: On command terms. The short-answer questions reward exactly what the verb asks for, and outline, describe and explain want different things. Students who revise content thoroughly and ignore the verb write competent paragraphs that land in the middle band. The extended response loses marks differently: it needs a named study, the finding that study actually produced, and then an inference from that finding. Many answers stop after the study and never reach the judgement, which is where the evaluation marks live. Both faults are structural, so a handful of marked timed attempts usually moves them.

faqs.question: What exactly may an Abu Dhabi tutor do on a Psychology replication report?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach experimental method, explain which statistical test a design implies, discuss ethics requirements, ask questions about a draft the student has written, and return comments mapped to the criterion letters. A tutor may not author any part of the submitted report, supply text to paste in, or hand over a finished investigation. Providers in this market that sell completed coursework are selling a malpractice risk that falls on the candidate. We state that boundary to the student in the first session rather than in small print.

faqs.question: What ethical approval does a Psychology IA need in an Abu Dhabi school?
faqs.answer: Participants must give informed consent, be able to withdraw, and be debriefed, and they must not be deceived in any way likely to cause distress. Studies involving minors, clinical populations or sensitive personal data are generally refused at proposal stage. On top of the IB's requirements, the school applies its own safeguarding procedure, and schools licensed by ADEK differ in how strictly they interpret it. The sequence that works is to choose a replicable experiment first, check it against the school's rules second, and write the proposal third.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a DP2 Psychology student in Abu Dhabi usually start with?
faqs.answer: Most families start with one weekly slot and add an internal assessment block when the proposal is due. In the final stretch before the May session that often becomes two or three sessions a week for a fixed number of weeks, each producing one timed response marked against the published bands. We would rather agree a fixed block with an end date than sell an open-ended weekly booking. If the marked work stops moving, the right answer is sometimes a different tutor or a different format, and we will say so.

faqs.question: Can Psychology sessions move around Ramadan and Abu Dhabi school mock weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes. Slots are held rather than fixed in stone, so they shift to post-Iftar timings during Ramadan and pause or lighten during school mock weeks and examination periods without losing the booking. That flexibility is easier online than with any travelling arrangement, because nobody is planning a drive around the change. Families who move between Abu Dhabi and abroad during school holidays usually keep the same tutor and the same hour, adjusting only for the time difference, which keeps continuity through the part of the year when most revision slips.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start Psychology tutoring eight weeks before the May session?
faqs.answer: It is late, and it is not pointless, but what changes is the plan rather than the price. Eight weeks is enough for timed-paper technique, command-term discipline and option-essay structure, which is where most retrievable marks in this subject sit. It is not enough to rebuild two years of content coverage, and a provider promising otherwise is selling something it cannot deliver. The constraint at that point is availability: the specialists with free evening slots on Gulf Standard Time are fewer in the weeks before a session than in October.

faqs.question: What does the free first Psychology lesson actually include?
faqs.answer: One 50-minute lesson in one subject, at no charge, with no card details taken and no obligation to continue. The tutor looks at a recent piece of marked work, usually a Paper 1 response or an IA section, and says specifically what is costing marks against the published criteria. You then get a written plan with the number of sessions, what each covers and the rate in AED, and nothing recurring begins until you have agreed it. If the honest answer is that tutoring is not what your child needs, the tutor will say that instead.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have ADEK or IB approval for its Abu Dhabi Psychology tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider claiming it should be asked for the permit or centre number. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and does not operate an office or centre in the UAE. What exists is a permit regime for individual tutors through MoHRE, and a separate KHDA educational services permit for training institutes with premises in Dubai. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is legitimate. Implying its endorsement is not.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one marked Psychology response, not a package
abu-dhabi/ib-dp-psychology-tutor.closingBody: The most useful first step is not a decision about hours. It is putting one marked Paper 1 response or one IA section in front of a DP Psychology specialist and hearing precisely where the marks went. That is what the free 50-minute online lesson is for: one subject, no card details, no obligation. You will come out of it with a written plan, the rate in AED, and an honest view of whether weekly lessons, an internal assessment block or nothing at all is the right call for your child this term. Lessons run live online from any community in Abu Dhabi, held on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-spanish-ab-initio-home-t.tutorsIntro: The tutors below read Spanish for beginners rather than Spanish as a subject. For an ab initio candidate that distinction decides everything: the course rewards a narrow, controlled range used accurately, and a tutor used to Spanish B literature will push a beginner straight past the band they are being marked in.

intro.heading: What an ab initio parent can actually check, week by week
paragraphs: Spanish ab initio is the IB Diploma's beginner language course. It exists for a student who arrives at DP1 with little or no Spanish, and it is offered at Standard Level only. That single fact removes the question most families ask first. There is no Higher Level to aim at and no advantage in treating the course as a cut-down version of Spanish B. The grade comes from how accurately a beginner handles a deliberately limited amount of language, under four separately marked assessments.

The problem in Abu Dhabi is rarely the teaching. It is the absence of evidence. A beginner language is the one subject where a parent has no instinct for progress: you cannot look at a page of Spanish and tell whether it would score 12 or 20. So families end up judging a tutor by how pleasant the hour felt, which is the one signal that has no relationship to the grade. Three months later the school report says 'making steady progress' and the mock says 3.

This page is built around the opposite habit. Before a plan is written, the student sits a short diagnostic that produces numbers: how many of the five prescribed themes they can say anything about, how many words of unprompted Spanish they produce in four minutes, and which error classes repeat. Those numbers go in a file. Every marked piece after that is filed next to them, with the criterion letter the examiner would use written on it. By the end of a term you are not reading an opinion. You are reading a trend line.

That evidence habit also changes what a session is for. A tutor who knows a student loses marks almost entirely on verb endings in the past does not spend the hour on new vocabulary, however enjoyable that would be. They spend it on the four endings that recur, test them cold the following week, and write down whether the error rate fell. If it did not, the method changes rather than the hours increasing.

Delivery in the UAE is online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi, and does not send a tutor to a Khalifa City villa or a Saadiyat apartment; home tutoring at the door is a service we offer only in India. For a beginner language that limitation turns out to be an advantage rather than a compromise, and the comparison table further down sets out why: a screen-shared, recorded, markable session leaves a paper trail that a kitchen-table lesson does not.

Market rates for private tuition in Abu Dhabi are published by comparison sites rather than by tutors. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai and UAE rate table puts a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour and an in-home visit at AED 180 to AED 350, with specialist exam-year support quoted higher. Those are market bands, not IB Gram prices, and they are the number against which any quote you receive should be read.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-spanish-ab-initio-home-t.programmesIntro: Spanish ab initio sits in the Diploma Programme, but the students who take it usually arrive from an MYP or an IGCSE language background that shaped how much Spanish they bring. The three programme notes below explain what each starting point leaves a beginner with in an Abu Dhabi school.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma takes six subjects, one from each group, with Group 2 covering language acquisition. Spanish ab initio is the Group 2 entry point for a genuine beginner and is examined at Standard Level. Candidates sit a written paper, a listening paper, a reading paper and an individual oral, and a Group 2 grade counts towards the Diploma total on the same seven-point scale as every other subject.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts are small and Group 2 timetabling is set early in DP1, often in a single blocked option column. Families at Raha International School, Cranleigh Abu Dhabi and the American Community School of Abu Dhabi report the same pattern: the choice between a B course and an ab initio course is made in the first weeks, on limited evidence, and is difficult to unpick by the second term. A diagnostic before that conversation is worth more than a term of tuition after it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language Acquisition runs in phases rather than year groups, from Phase 1 for a near-beginner to Phase 6 for a confident user. A student finishing MYP in Phase 1 or 2 is the clearest ab initio candidate there is. The phase descriptor is the most useful document a parent can bring to a first session, because it describes what the student could already do rather than what they were taught.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has several IB continuum schools where MYP Spanish runs for only two or three years before the Diploma, so a student can reach DP1 having met Spanish twice a week since Year 9 and still sit comfortably in Phase 2. That is not a failure of the school; it is what a short exposure produces. It does mean the ab initio course is the honest placement, and that saying so early avoids a wasted DP1.

programmes.name: IGCSE and GCSE transfers
programmes.description: Students moving into an Abu Dhabi IB school from a British-curriculum Year 11 may have taken Cambridge or Pearson Spanish as a foreign language, or no Spanish at all. A completed IGCSE in Spanish usually rules out ab initio, because the course is intended for students without prior study of the language. A student who dropped Spanish after Year 9, by contrast, is often an ab initio candidate on paper and an awkward one in practice.
programmes.countryNote: The transfer cases are where Abu Dhabi schools differ most. ADEK licenses a mix of British, American, Indian and IB schools across the emirate, and students move between them mid-phase more often than in most markets. A DP coordinator will want to see what was studied, for how long, and at what level before approving a Group 2 placement, and that conversation goes better with a dated diagnostic script attached to it.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-spanish-ab-initio-home-t.subjectsIntro: A beginner language tutor is rarely hired on their own. The subjects below are the ones Abu Dhabi families most often pair with Spanish ab initio support, and each note says what the pairing usually needs rather than listing the syllabus.

subjects.name: Spanish ab initio
subjects.description: Four assessments split evenly: a written paper of two tasks, a listening paper, a reading paper and an individual oral built on a visual stimulus. Marks are lost on tense accuracy, on text-type conventions, and on answering a reading question with a copied phrase that does not fit the grammar of the answer.

subjects.name: Spanish B
subjects.description: The course for a student with prior Spanish. Assessment looks similar in shape but the texts are longer, the themes less prescribed, and HL adds two literary works. A student placed here by optimism rather than evidence usually shows it first in the listening paper, where no amount of preparation covers an unknown vocabulary gap.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Frequently the paired Group 1 subject in Abu Dhabi IB schools. Students who find the ab initio oral difficult often carry the same weakness here: describing an image without structuring an argument about it. The transferable work is the structure, not the language.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Taught alongside all six subjects and assessed by an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay. Language learners make unusually good TOK candidates because translation gives them a concrete example of knowledge changing shape, and that example is worth planting deliberately.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The common Group 5 choice for students whose strengths are verbal. The scheduling consequence matters for a language plan: an AI internal assessment deadline in the second term of DP1 will eat the Spanish practice window unless the calendar is drawn before it happens.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A popular Group 3 pairing in the emirate. Economics and a beginner language compete for the same kind of memory work, which is why the weekly plan matters more than the number of hours; two short Spanish contacts a week beat one long one for retention.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Taken widely in Abu Dhabi DP cohorts. Biology candidates tend to be comfortable with controlled vocabulary lists, which transfers usefully to ab initio theme vocabulary, and comfortable with precise definition, which transfers badly to open-ended Spanish speaking.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic alongside their licensed curriculum, so most Abu Dhabi Diploma students are learning two languages at once. Sequencing the two matters: a student revising Arabic vocabulary and Spanish vocabulary in the same evening retains less of both than one who separates them by a day.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Can be registered in Group 2, though an ab initio student will almost never have the language to do so. The useful point for a beginner's family is the opposite one: an Extended Essay written in English about a Spanish-speaking context is not a language essay and will not be marked as one.

abu-dhabi/ib-dp-spanish-ab-initio-home-t.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi's Diploma families are spread across the island and three distinct mainland corridors, and the practical constraint on a language plan is almost always the drive home from school rather than the subject itself. Each note below is about when a Spanish session can realistically start.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Short school runs, late finishes. Students from the island's IB and American-curriculum schools are usually home before 16:15, which makes a 16:30 Spanish slot the easiest in the emirate to hold twice a week during DP1.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: The bridge traffic back onto Al Reem between 15:30 and 16:30 adds enough time that a 16:00 start is unreliable. Families here more often take a 17:30 session and keep Saturday mornings for the longer oral rehearsals.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: School buses serving the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor can take over an hour on the return leg. A beginner language does better here with two 45-minute contacts than one 90-minute block landing on a tired student.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Mixed British and IB intake, and a high proportion of students who also attend after-school sport at the same compound. Spanish sessions in this area are most often booked at 18:30, after dinner, which suits listening work better than speaking.

regions.name: Al Bateen and the Corniche
regions.note: Central, well served by schools within a short drive, and the area where families most often ask for a 15:45 start. For an oral-heavy plan that early slot is genuinely better: a student rehearsing a visual stimulus performs differently at 16:00 than at 19:00.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: A newer corridor with longer internal distances than the map suggests. Weekend clustering works well here, with a Friday afternoon block for writing tasks and a short midweek slot to keep vocabulary live.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan
regions.note: Dense, established, and close to several mainland schools, so after-school tutoring demand peaks between 16:00 and 18:00. Booking outside that window usually gets a better tutor match for a minority subject like beginner Spanish.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Falah
regions.note: Furthest from the island schools, with the longest bus journeys in the emirate. Families here are the clearest beneficiaries of online delivery: the hour that would have gone to a tutor's drive becomes a second Spanish contact in the week.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Saadiyat Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's longest-established Diploma cohorts sit here, and Group 2 option blocks are usually narrow. Ask the DP coordinator which Group 2 courses are actually running this year rather than which are listed in the curriculum booklet; a beginner course needs a viable class to exist at all.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas
schoolClusters.note: The mainland corridor where IB continuum provision is concentrated, so more students arrive in DP1 with an MYP phase descriptor on file. That descriptor is the single most useful document for settling an ab initio placement, and it is usually available on request.
