sections.heading: The two Higher Level literary works, and where they are actually examined
paragraphs: Spanish B at Higher Level requires two literary works studied in Spanish. They do not appear on Paper 1 and they do not appear on Paper 2. Their role is in the individual oral, where the starting point is an extract from one of them, and that single fact is misunderstood in both directions by roughly equal numbers of HL families.

The first error is under-preparation. A student reads the two works during DP1, finds them hard, and then spends DP2 revising for the written papers because those are the ones that feel like exams. The oral arrives, a short extract is put in front of them, and they cannot place it in the work or say anything substantial about it. Twenty-five per cent of the grade is decided in fifteen minutes on material they half-remember. Any HL student who can describe each work's situation, main figures and central concerns in a paragraph of Spanish is already in a different position from that.

The second error is over-preparation of the wrong kind. A student treats the works as a literature course, memorises commentary, and arrives able to deliver an analysis of theme and technique. Spanish B is not Spanish A. The oral assesses language, message and interactive skills through the extract; it does not reward literary sophistication. A candidate who can summarise the extract's situation, link it to a concern of the work as a whole, and then hold an unscripted conversation about it will outscore one reciting prepared criticism, because the prepared criticism collapses at the first unexpected question.

What works in sessions is practical. Each work reduced to a page of usable Spanish: situation, main figures, two or three concerns, and the vocabulary those concerns require. Then unseen extracts from each work, with the student placing the extract and talking about it under the real preparation limit, recorded and reviewed. Three sessions of that, with the works to hand, usually moves an HL oral mark more than a term of general conversation practice, because the component is specific and the preparation can be too.

sections.heading: Where Spanish practice actually comes from in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Arabic and French have a visible local presence in this emirate. Spanish does not, in any comparable way, and that changes how practice has to be engineered. A student learning Arabic in Abu Dhabi can read street signs; a student learning Spanish has to arrange every minute of exposure deliberately. Families who understand that build it into the week. Families who assume exposure will happen reach DP2 with a student who has only ever heard one teacher's Spanish.

The good news is that Spanish has more accessible authentic material than almost any other language, and most of it is free. Latin American and Spanish news outlets publish readable short articles in a register close to what Paper 2 uses. Subtitled drama provides natural speech at natural speed with a safety net, and the sequence that works is Spanish audio with Spanish subtitles rather than English ones. Podcasts aimed at learners provide graded listening; podcasts aimed at native speakers provide the harder version once recognition has started to build. None of this costs anything beyond the discipline of scheduling it.

What is genuinely scarce here is unscripted speaking practice with someone who is not being paid to be patient. That is the one thing a weekly session supplies that self-study cannot, and it is why the interactive element of a session is worth protecting even when the component under repair is writing. A student who speaks Spanish only in their school lesson and their tutoring hour is speaking it for perhaps ninety minutes a week, which is enough to maintain and not enough to build.

The table below sets out what each source does and does not provide, with honest notes on cost. The point of laying it out is that Spanish B is a subject where a family can substitute a great deal of paid tutoring with structured free material, provided someone tells them which material and in what order. We would rather say that than sell sessions for work a student can do alone.

sections.heading: What a Spanish B tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: Group 2 courses have fewer academic-honesty pressure points than Group 1 or the Diploma core, because there is no coursework essay. The individual oral is internally conducted and externally moderated, and preparation for it is ordinary teaching. The boundary is still worth stating plainly, partly because this market contains providers selling finished assessed work and partly because the consequences fall on the student rather than on the provider.

A tutor may run full oral rehearsals, including with unseen extracts from the HL literary works. A tutor may review a recording against the criteria with the student. A tutor may mark writing, explain the criterion split, and point out that a paragraph lists rather than develops. A tutor may build vocabulary for a topic, drill a grammatical decision, and set reading and listening between sessions. All of that is teaching and all of it is normal and expected.

A tutor may not script the assessment. Supplying memorised answers to be delivered as the student's own thinking in the oral is not preparation, and it fails on its own terms as well as ethically, because the component includes unscripted conversation and a memorised candidate collapses at the first unexpected question. For any written work that must be the student's own, a tutor gives feedback and asks questions; the sentences are the student's. We put this in writing because the risk lands on your child.

One more boundary concerns materials. We reference and link official syllabus documents, specimen papers and board timetables rather than reproducing or supplying them. Subject guides, past papers and mark schemes belong to the IB and reproducing them is a copyright matter, so the right thing is to point you at the official source and let the school supply what it is entitled to supply.
bullets: Rehearsals, marking, feedback and drilling are ordinary teaching

sections.heading: Permits, availability and how to start
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE operates under a permit regime. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists it as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services, with a two-working-day completion time and no fee shown.

Tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, so we quote none and recommend scepticism towards any page that does. In Abu Dhabi there is a second consideration: reported ADEK professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct runs the same way. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools across the emirate and publishes its own inspection ratings.

On availability, we disclose rather than conceal. Spanish B at Higher Level, with the two literary works prepared, is a narrower specialism than Spanish tutoring generally, and there are weeks when no UAE-based specialist has a slot matching a DP2 student's early-evening need. When that happens the options are stated: a different time with an available specialist, a wait for a named slot, or a specialist outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time. A general Spanish tutor is never substituted for a Spanish B specialist without being named as such.

Starting is deliberately cheap. Send the most recent marked writing task with criterion marks if the school provides them, the Paper 2 result split into listening and reading if available, and the oral mark. We read them and say which of the three diagnoses applies and what the first two sessions would do. There is no charge for that. A trial lesson follows, one per subject, booked before any payment is taken, spent on a real piece of the student's work rather than on introductions.

process.title: Send the marked writing, not the report
process.description: A marked Paper 1 style task with the criterion marks visible tells us in two minutes what a term of reports does not. If the school does not break the mark into language, message and conceptual understanding, send the annotated script anyway — the pattern of corrections is itself the diagnosis.

process.title: Split the Paper 2 score
process.description: Listening and reading separately, if the school provides it. If not, have your child sit one listening section to time at home, audio twice and no pausing. The ratio between the two numbers decides whether the plan is grammar work or a term of recognition building.

process.title: Match on level and on the HL works
process.description: SL and HL orals are different exams, and an HL block needs a tutor who has read the two literary works your child is studying. We name which level the tutor has taught and how recently, confirm the works, and offer a second option where one exists.

process.title: Take the trial on a real task
process.description: One trial per subject, before any payment, spent marking something your child has written. By the end you should know which of the three diagnoses applies and what the first two sessions will target. A trial that was a conversation in Spanish has not told you anything you did not know.

process.title: Book a block against one diagnosis
process.description: A defined number of sessions aimed at one thing: a grammatical decision, listening recognition, the oral. Each session's artefact is agreed in advance — marked writing, a timed listening score, a recorded rehearsal — and marking between sessions is settled before the first invoice.

process.title: Re-mark at the end against the same criteria
process.description: The block closes with the same kind of task marked the same way, placed beside the baseline. Then an explicit decision: move to the next diagnosis, change tutor, or stop. Without that comparison, a block cannot tell you whether the money did anything.

whyPoints.title: The criterion split is shown, not summarised
whyPoints.description: Every marked task comes back with language out of 12, message out of 12 and conceptual understanding out of 6 shown separately. A single total hides which of three different problems a student actually has, and that is the problem the grade is hiding too.

whyPoints.title: Grammatical decisions are drilled to automatic
whyPoints.description: Ser and estar, preterite and imperfect, the subjunctive triggers, por and para: one per session, on the student's own sentences, until the choice stops being a calculation. Understanding these is easy; using them under exam pressure is what the marks measure.

whyPoints.title: Listening practice includes variety on purpose
whyPoints.description: A candidate calibrated to one teacher's accent is relying on the examination choosing that accent. We build in several Spanish varieties across a block, because regional pronunciation is the half of Paper 2 that classroom audio tends to avoid.

whyPoints.title: HL literary works prepared where they are examined
whyPoints.description: The two works feed the oral and never appear on the written papers. Sessions reduce each to a page of usable Spanish and then practise unseen extracts under the real preparation limit, rather than teaching literary criticism the component does not reward.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you what you can do free
whyPoints.description: Spanish has more accessible authentic material than almost any other language, and a good deal of this subject can be built from free sources in the right order. We say which and in what order, even when saying so means fewer booked sessions.

whyPoints.title: Claims limited to what can be evidenced
whyPoints.description: No examiner status without evidence, no grade guarantees, no statistics without a source, and no implied endorsement from ADEK, the IB or any named school. Those four appear constantly in this market and all four are liabilities rather than selling points.

faqs.question: Why does my child speak Spanish confidently and still score 4?
faqs.answer: Because fluency is not a criterion. Paper 1 is marked out of 30 with 12 for language, 12 for message and 6 for conceptual understanding, and the oral uses the same shape. A confident speaker who guesses on Spanish's recurring grammatical decisions — the two verbs meaning 'to be', the split between the preterite and imperfect past, whether a clause triggers the subjunctive, and which word for 'for' belongs here — produces fluent Spanish that drops small language marks in nearly every sentence. The marked script looks like a page of minor corrections rather than one identifiable problem, which is exactly why it goes unaddressed.

faqs.question: Which Spanish grammar points are worth paying a tutor to fix?
faqs.answer: Four, in this order. The preterite and imperfect split, because English has one simple past and a student narrating anything has to choose in every clause. The two verbs meaning 'to be', particularly with adjectives whose meaning changes depending on the choice. The present subjunctive after roughly ten identifiable triggers, which is a finite list and demonstrates range when used once correctly. And the two words for 'for', which is low stakes individually and very high in volume. Together these account for more lost language marks than every other grammatical issue combined.

faqs.question: How is Spanish B Paper 1 marked, and how long should the task be?
faqs.answer: Out of 30: language 12, message 12, conceptual understanding 6. The word range is 250 to 400 at Standard Level and 450 to 600 at Higher Level, and writing outside it costs marks in both directions. Short answers cannot develop a message enough for the 12 available message marks; very long ones lose control of language and overrun. Have your child measure once what their own handwriting looks like at the top and bottom of the range, so length can be judged in the exam without spending minutes counting words.

faqs.question: Which of the three Paper 1 tasks should my child choose?
faqs.answer: The one whose text type they have practised, not the one whose topic feels familiar. That is the opposite of what most candidates do in the ninety seconds they spend deciding. A narrative task lets a student display the past tenses they have drilled; a proposal or a speech invites the subjunctive naturally through recommendations and wishes. An unfamiliar topic in a practised form almost always beats a comfortable topic in a form never attempted. Teaching that comparison takes one session and changes the decision permanently.

faqs.question: What are the six conceptual understanding marks in Spanish B?
faqs.answer: They credit recognising the audience, context and purpose the task sets, choosing a suitable text type and using its conventions. They are the cheapest marks on the paper because they require no better Spanish. A task asking for a blog post, answered with accurate undifferentiated prose and no title, no reader addressed and no closing hook, loses most of them. One page of text-type reference — what a blog post, a formal letter, a speech, an interview and a diary entry each need — plus three timed attempts, is usually enough to stop the leak permanently.

faqs.question: Why is my child's Spanish listening score so much lower than their reading?
faqs.answer: Because Spanish gives readers two advantages that listeners do not get. Spelling maps onto sound transparently, so a reader is never unsure which word they are looking at, and English shares a large Latin-derived vocabulary, so abstract words are often transparent on sight. Natural Spanish is fast, runs words together, drops consonants in several major varieties and uses regional vocabulary classroom material avoids. If listening sits around half of reading, the issue is recognition rather than knowledge, and more vocabulary learning will not close it.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my child learns Latin American or peninsular Spanish?
faqs.answer: The examination accepts any standard variety provided the student is consistent, and consistency is the part that matters. The plural form of address differs between Spain and most of Latin America and affects verb endings. Some regions use a distinct second-person singular with its own forms. Everyday vocabulary varies. None of that costs marks when used consistently; mixing varieties inside one task does. Choose the variety the household or school uses, stay in it, and treat varied listening practice as separate insurance for Paper 2.

faqs.question: Do the two Higher Level literary works appear on the Spanish B papers?
faqs.answer: No. Spanish B at Higher Level requires two literary works studied in Spanish, and they appear on neither Paper 1 nor Paper 2. Their role is in the individual oral, where the starting extract is drawn from one of them. HL students who read the works in DP1 and then revise only for the written papers have left 25% of the grade on half-remembered material. The useful preparation reduces each work to a page of usable Spanish — situation, main figures, two or three concerns — then practises unseen extracts under real timing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor prepare the HL oral without it becoming a script?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a script would fail on its own terms anyway. The oral includes unscripted conversation, so a memorised candidate collapses at the first unexpected question. Legitimate preparation is full rehearsals with unseen extracts from the two works, recorded and reviewed against language, message and interactive skills, plus practice placing an extract in the work and linking it to a concern. What a tutor may not do is supply memorised answers to be delivered as the student's own thinking. The risk of that falls on the student, not the tutor.

faqs.question: Where can a student in Abu Dhabi actually practise Spanish?
faqs.answer: It has to be engineered, because unlike Arabic or French, Spanish has little incidental presence in this emirate. The good news is that accessible material is abundant and mostly free. Short news articles from Spanish-language outlets build reading pace in a register close to Paper 2. Subtitled drama with Spanish rather than English subtitles gives natural speed with a safety net. Graded learner podcasts build recognition, and native-speaker podcasts take over once recognition exists. What is genuinely scarce is unscripted speaking, which is the part a weekly session supplies.

faqs.question: Will a Spanish tutor come to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. Spanish B sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the format suits the work: the script is annotated on a shared screen while both people look at the same sentence, and audio replays from the same window. In-home tuition exists in this market at roughly AED 180-500 an hour by published UAE surveys and listings, with travel inside the rate, and the drive across Abu Dhabi is part of what that pays for.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to move a Spanish B grade?
faqs.answer: It depends which of three diagnoses applies. A confident speaker losing language marks on grammatical decisions shows measurable movement in about six sessions, because each decision can be drilled to automaticity on their own writing. A student whose oral sits well below their written papers usually needs three recorded rehearsals, which is the cheapest intervention available on a component worth 25%. A listening recognition gap takes a term, because recognition is built by volume. We say which one applies before a block is booked rather than at session fifteen.

faqs.question: Is my near-native child in the right course at Spanish B?
faqs.answer: Worth examining in DP1, while a change is still possible. A student scoring 7 in Spanish B with no effort is being assessed well below their level and learning little, and Spanish A: Language and Literature is where that student usually belongs. It is also the route towards a bilingual diploma, which requires two Language A courses rather than a Group 2 course, with conditions set by the IB and worth confirming with your school's coordinator. The evidence to look at is written register and analytical writing in Spanish, not conversational ease.

faqs.question: Can we move down from Spanish B to Spanish ab initio?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the school decides within the IB's framework. Ab initio is for students with little or no previous experience of the language, so a student with three years of MYP Spanish does not qualify however shaky the grades look. If Spanish B genuinely is the wrong level, the realistic options are Standard Level rather than Higher Level, or a different Group 2 language where the student is a true beginner. Either conversation needs to happen early in DP1, because both become impossible once the course is underway.

faqs.question: Do Spanish tutors in Abu Dhabi need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time with no fee. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule of amounts. Abu Dhabi adds that reported ADEK ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of their own enrolled students.

faqs.question: What should we send when asking about Spanish B support?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is a school report. The most recent marked writing task with criterion marks if the school provides them, because the pattern of corrections is the diagnosis. The Paper 2 result split into listening and reading, or a listening section sat to time at home if the school does not split it. And the oral mark, plus the titles of the two literary works if your child is at Higher Level. We read those and say which diagnosis applies and what the first two sessions would target, at no charge.
